*mahādevo vijānāti tasya tīrthasya vaibhavam \|*  
*yāni kāni ca puṇyāni brahmāṇḍāntargatāni vai \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tāni gaṃgāditīrthāni svapāpapariśuddhaye \|*  
*kaṭāhatīrthasevāṃ ca kurvanti dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. Listen ye all sages of great prowess headed by Śaunaka! Who knows the greatness of Kaṭāhatīrtha (adequately) in all the three worlds? Only Mahādeva understands the greatness of that Tīrtha. All those sacred Tīrthas within the Cosmic Egg, Gaṅgā and all the other Tīrthas, resort to the Kaṭāha Tīrtha, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, in order to dispel their own sins.

## \|\| 1.28.12-17 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāḥ kṣattriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāścetarajātayaḥ \|*  
*spṛśanti tajjalamiti na pibedyo vimūḍhadhīḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*sa hi caṇḍālatāṃ prāpya kumbhīpāke patiṣyati \|*  
*brahmacārī gṛhastho vā vānaprastho yatīśvaraḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*sevayā tasya tīrthasya prāpnoti paramaṃ padam \|*  
*śrutismṛtipurāṇeṣu tattīrthasya praśaṃsanam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*bahudhā varṇyate paṃcamahāpātakanāśanam \|*  
*atyadbhutataraṃ viprāḥ sarvalokaikapāvanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*brahmahatyāyutaṃ cāpi surāpānāyutaṃ tathā \|*  
*ayutaṃ gurudārāṇāṃ gamanaṃ pāpakāraṇam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*steyāyutaṃ suvarṇānāṃ tatsaṃsargāśca koṭayaḥ \|*  
*śīghraṃ vilayamāyāṃti tasya tīrthasya sevayā \|\| 17 \|\|*

12-13a. A foolish person may think thus: ‘All people touch this water—Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, Śūdras and people of other castes too.’ Thinking thus he may not drink it. Indeed that foolish one will become a Cāṇḍāla and he will fall in Kuṃbhīpāka hell.

13b-15a. Whether he be a religious student, a householder, a forest-dweller or an eminent ascetic, by serving that Tīrtha he attains the highest state. In Śrutis, Smṛtis and Purāṇas there are many passages praising that Tīrtha which destroys the five major sins.

15b-17. It is exceedingly wonderful, O Brāhmaṇas; it is the only sanctifying thing in all the worlds. By serving and resorting to that Tīrtha ten thousand sins of Brahmin-slaughter, ten thousand sins of liquor-drinking, ten thousand sins of carnally approaching the preceptor’s wife, ten thousand sins of the theft of gold and crores of the sins of associating with the great sinners, immediately become dissolved.

## \|\| 1.28.18 \|\|

*yāni niṣkṛtihīnāni pāpāni vividhāni ca \|*  
*tāni sarvāṇi naśyaṃti tīrthasyāsya niṣevaṇāt \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. By resorting to this Tīrtha all those different kinds of sins which have no means of expiation, perish.

## \|\| 1.28.19-21 \|\|

*idaṃ tīrthaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ bhagavatpādanissṛtam \|*  
*kuṣṭhādirogayukto yaḥ pratyahaṃ ca pibedidam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*atha kaṭāhatīrthamahimaśraddhāśūnyānāṃ mahānarakaprāptiḥ \|*  
*so'pi rogavihīnaḥ sanviṣṇulokaṃ ca gacchati \|*  
*bhagavāñchaṃkaro devo rahasyānubhave purā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*pārvatyai kathayāmāsa tasya tīrthasya vaibhavam \|*  
*ukteṣveteṣu sandeho na kartavyaḥ kadācana \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-20a. This Tīrtha of great merit has issued from the feet of the Lord. If a person suffering from leprosy and other diseases drinks the water of this everyday, he shall get rid of that disease and go to the world of Viṣṇu.

\[Those Who have no Faith in the Greatness of Kaṭāhatīrtha Will Fall into Great Hells\]:—

20b-21. In the course of his (revelation) of secret experiences Lord Śaṅkara formerly spoke to Pārvatī about the greatness of that Tīrtha. No one should entertain any doubt about what has been said before.

## \|\| 1.28.22-24 \|\|

*arthavādo'yamiti ca na vaktavyaṃ kadācana \|*  
*ye'rthavādamidaṃ brūyusteṣāṃ vai nāstikātmanām \|\| 22 \|\|*

*jihvāgre paraśuṃ taptaṃ prakṣipanti ca kiṃkarāḥ \|*  
*tasmātkaṭāhatīrthaṃ tu sevanīyaṃ prayatnataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*sarvaduḥkhapraśamanamapavargaphalapradam \|*  
*yatra pītvā naro bhaktyā sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. It should never be uttered that it is mere laudatory statement. Those who say that this is mere eulogy are atheists in the core of their heart. The servants (of Yama) will place red-hot axe at the tips of their tongues. Hence the Tīrtha called Kaṭāha-tīrtha should be scrupulously served and resorted to. It suppresses all miseries and bestows the benefit of salvation. By drinking (its waters) devoutly a man shall realize all his desires.

## \|\| 1.28.25-27 \|\|

*evamuktvā mahābhāgaḥ kāśīṃ trailokyapāvanīm \|*  
*saṃprāpto nāradaḥ śrīmānsūta paurāṇikottama \|\| 25 \|\|*

*saṃkṣepataśca bhagavānnaimiṣe hyuktavānkhalu \|*  
*idānīṃ śrotumicchāmaḥ kaṭāhasya ca vaibhavam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*suvistareṇa cāsmākaṃ vada sūta kṛpāvaśāt \|\| 27 \|\|*

25-27. O Sūta, the most excellent one among those conversant with the Purāṇas, after saying thus (to us) the glorious Nārada of exalted magnificence went to Kāśī that sanctifies all the three worlds. That holy lord spoke everything briefly in the Naimiṣa forest. Now we wish to know the greatness of Kaṭāha in great detail. Kindly tell it to us, O Sūta.

\[The Procedure of Drinking the Waters of Kaṭāha Tīrtha\]:—

## \|\| 1.28.28 \|\|

*iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīveṃkaṭācalamāhātmye sūtaśaunaka saṃvāde kaṭāhatīrthapraśaṃsanaṃnāmāṣṭāviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

Śrī Sūta said:

28\. O ye all ascetics living in the Naimiṣa forest, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, listen to the greatness of Kaṭāha Tīrtha.

## \|\| 1.28.29 \|\|

*kaṭāhatīrthaṃ bho viprāḥ sarva lokeṣu viśrutam \|*  
*sarvasampatkaraṃ śuddhaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O Brāhmaṇas, Kaṭāha Tīrtha is well-known in all the worlds. It causes all prosperity. It is pure and destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 1.28.30 \|\|

*duḥsvapnanāśanaṃ hyetanmahāpātakanāśanam \|*  
*mahāvighnapraśamanaṃ mahāśāntikaraṃ nṛṇām \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. It annihilates (the effects of) evil dreams. It is destructive of great sins. It suppresses great obstacles and brings about great peace (of mind) to men.

## \|\| 1.28.31-36 \|\|

*smṛtimātreṇa yatpuṃsāṃ sarvapāpaniṣūdanam \|*  
*mantreṇāṣṭākṣareṇaiva pibettīrthaṃ manoharam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*athavā keśavādyaiśca nāmabhirvā pibejjalam \|*  
*yadvā nāmatrayeṇā'pi pibettīrthaṃ śubhapradam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*āhosvidveṃkaṭeśasya mantreṇāṣṭākṣareṇa vai \|*  
*pibetkaṭāhatīrthaṃ tadbhuktimuktipradāyakam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*vinā maṃtreṇa yo vipraḥ saṃpibettīrthamuttamam \|*  
*pāpaṃ me nāśaya kṣipraṃ janmāntarakṛtaṃ mahat \|\| 34 \|\|*

*ityuktvā sa pibennityaṃ mokṣamārgaikasādhanam \|*  
*svāmipuṣkariṇīsnānaṃ varāhaśrīśadarśanam \|\| 35 \|\|*

*kaṭāhatīrthapānaṃ ca trayaṃ trailokyadurlabham \|*  
*bahunā kimihoktena brahmahatyādināśanam \|\| 36 \|\|*

31-36. Merely by being remembered it nullifies all the sins of men. One should drink its enchanting waters after repeating the eight-syllabled Mantra. Or he should mutter the names of Keśava etc. and sip water after each name. Or he should drink the water that bestows auspiciousness after muttering three names (Keśava, Nārāyaṇa, Mādhava) (together). Or he shall repeat the eight-syllabled Mantra of Veṅkaṭeśa and drink (the water of) Kaṭāha Tīrtha. That yields worldly pleasures as well as salvation.

If any Brāhmaṇa wishes to drink at the excellent Tīrtha without a Mantra, he should always say “Destroy quickly all the great sins of mine committed in all the previous births” and drink the water. It is the sole means leading to salvation.

The following three are very rare in all the three worlds: bath in Svāmipuṣkariṇī, vision of Lord of Śrī in the form of Varāha and drinking of (the water of) Kaṭāha Tīrtha.

Of what avail is much talk? It is destructive of all sins like that of slaying a Brāhmaṇa etc.

\[The Episode of a Brāhmaṇa Named Keśava\]:—

## \|\| 1.28.37-38 \|\|

*atha keśavākhyadvijavṛttāntaḥ \|*  
*purā kaściddvijo mohātkeśavākhyo bahuśrutam \|*  
*hatvā khaḍgena durbuddhyā brahmahatyāmavāptavān \|\| 37 \|\|*

*so'pi tasminmahātīrthe pītvā jalamanuttamam \|*  
*keśavākhyo mahāpāpī vimukto brahmahatyayā \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. Formerly, out of delusion, a Brāhmaṇa named Keśava viciously killed Bahuśruta and incurred the sin of Brahmin-slaughter. He drank the excellent water of this great Tīrtha. The great sinner named Keśava was liberated from the sin of Brahmin-slaughter.

The Sages asked:

## \|\| 1.28.39 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kasya putraḥ keśavākhyaḥ kathaṃ prāpto bhayaṃkarīm \|*  
*brahmahatyāmatikrūrāmasmākaṃ vaktumarhasi \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Whose son was this (Brāhmaṇa) named Keśava? How did he incur the terrible and exceedingly formidable sin of Brahmin-slaughter? It behoves you to tell it to us.

Śrī Sūta narrated:

## \|\| 1.28.40 \|\|

*śrīsūta uvāca \|*  
*tuṅgabhadrātaṭe ramye gandharvairupasevite \|*  
*agrahāro mahānāsīdvedāḍhya iti nāmataḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. There was a great Agrahāra (i.e. village donated to Brāhmaṇas) named Vedāḍhya on the beautiful banks of Tuṅgabhadrā resorted to by Gandharvas.

## \|\| 1.28.41-43 \|\|

*tasminvedapure ramye brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ \|*  
*śabdaśāstraparāḥ sarve jyotiḥśāstrapravartakāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*mīmāṃsātarkaśāstrajñāḥ sarve vedāntavādinaḥ \|*  
*dharmaśāstreṣu niratā annadānaparāḥ sadā \|\| 42 \|\|*

*putravantaśca te sarve hyagrahāre mahājanāḥ \|*  
*vedāḍhaye'pyagrahāre vai padmanābha iti śrutaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

41-43. In that beautiful place Vedapura all the Brāhmaṇas were masters of the Vedas. They were devoted to the Science of Words (i.e. Grammar). All of them were promotors of the Science of Astrology. They were conversant with Nyāya and Mīmāṃsā systems of Philosophy. All of them were expounders of Vedānta. They were devoted to the treatises on Ethics and Law Codes. They were always engaged in making gifts of food. All the great residents of the Agrahāra were blessed with sons. (There was a Brāhmaṇa) well-known as Padmanābha in that Agrahāra (named) Vedāḍhya.

\[Keśava, a Brāhmaṇa Hankering after Harlots, Incurs the Sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter\]:—

## \|\| 1.28.44-50 \|\|

*atha gaṇikālaṃpaṭasya keśavadvijasya brahmahatyāprāptikramaḥ \|*  
*tasya putraḥ keśavākhyaḥ sarvakarmabahiṣkṛtaḥ \|*  
*mātaraṃ pitaraṃ tyaktvā bhāryāmapi pativratām \|\| 44 \|\|*

*sarvadā gaṇikāsakto veśyāgāraṃ viveśa ha \|*  
*dinadvaye ca tāṃ veśyāmanubhūya dvijastataḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*niṣkadvayaṃ pradātavyaṃ haste dattvā gataḥ sukham \|*  
*veśyayā cādhanastyaktastatsaṃyogaikatatparaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*itastataścorayitvā bahudravyāṇi santatam \|*  
*dattvā tayā ciraṃ reme tadgṛhe bubhuje ca saḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*ekena caṣakeṇāsau tayā saha surāṃ papau \|*  
*sa kadācitkirātaistu dravyaṃ hartuṃ yayau dvijaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*viprasya kasyacidgehe so'pi kairātaveṣadhṛk \|*  
*keśavo viprabandhurvai sāhasī khaṅgahastavān \|\| 49 \|\|*

*tadgṛhasvāminaṃ vipraṃ hatvā khaḍgena sāhasāt \|*  
*samādāya bahu dravyaṃ veśyāgāraṃ viveśa ha \|\| 50 \|\|*

44-48a. He had a son named Keśava who had been banished from all holy rites. He abandoned his mother, father and his wife also who was a chaste woman. He was attached to harlots and he always visited brothels. The Brāhmaṇa enjoyed the company of a prostitute for two days and handed over to her the two gold coins due to her. Then he went away happily. When he had no money he was discarded by the woman of ill fame. Since he was desirous of sexual union with her, he began to steal much money frequently. He handed over the same to her and sported with her for a long time. He took food in her house. He drank wine with her from the same goblet.

48b-50. Once that Brāhmaṇa assumed the guise of a Kirāta (hunter) and went to the house of a certain Brāhmaṇa along with other Kirātas in order to rob him of his wealth. Keśava, the unworthy Brāhmaṇa, took a sword in his hand. He rashly attacked the Brāhmaṇa who was the master of the house and killed him with his sword. He brought much wealth from there and entered the prostitute’s house.

## \|\| 1.28.51-52 \|\|

*taṃ yāntamanuyāti sma brahmahatyā bhayaṃkarī \|*  
*nīlavastradharā bhīmā bhṛśaṃ raktaśiroruhā \|\| 51 \|\|*

*garjantī sāṭṭahāsaṃ sā kampayantī ca rodasī \|*  
*anudrutastayā vipro babhrāma jagatītale \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. The awful and hideous Brahmahatyā followed him as he went along. She was terrible in her blue robes and very red hair. She roared with boisterous laughter shaking heaven and earth. Being pursued by her the Brāhmaṇa wandered all over the earth.

## \|\| 1.28.53 \|\|

*evaṃ bhramandharāṃ sarvāṃ viprabandhurdurātmavān \|*  
*svagrāmaṃ prayayau bhītyā śaunakādyā mahaujasaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. While wandering all over the earth the vicious, unworthy Brāhmaṇa went to his village with excessive fright, O Śaunaka and other (sages) of great prowess.

## \|\| 1.28.54 \|\|

*anudrutastayā bhītaḥ prayayau svaniketanam \|*  
*brahmahatyāpyanudrutya tena sākaṃ gṛhaṃ yayau \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. He was terrified on being chased by her and went to his own house. Brahmahatyā who pursued him went into the house along with him.

## \|\| 1.28.55 \|\|

*janakaṃ rakṣa rakṣeti keśavaḥ śaraṇaṃ yayau \|*  
*mā bhaiṣīriti sa procya pitā rakṣitumudyataḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Saying, “Save me, save me” Keśava sought refuge in his father. The father said. “Do not be afraid” and attempted to save him.

## \|\| 1.28.56-58 \|\|

*atha svasutarakṣaṇodyukte padmanābhe brahmahatyoktiḥ \|*  
*krūrainaṃ brahmahatyā sā janakaṃ pratyabhāṣata \|\| 56 \|\|*

*brahmahatyovāca \|*  
*mainaṃ tvaṃ pratigṛhṇīṣva padmanābha dvijottama \|*  
*ayaṃ surāpī steyī ca brahmahā cātipātakī \|\| 57 \|\|*

*mātṛdrohī pitṛdrohī bhāryātyāgī ca duṣṭadhīḥ \|*  
*gaṇikāsaktacittaśca hyenaṃ muñca durātmakam \|\| 58 \|\|*

56-58. As Padmanābha endeavoured to protect his son, the cruel demoness Brahmahatyā spoke to the father:

## \|\| 1.28.59-60 \|\|

*gṛhṇāsi cetsutaṃ vipra mahāpātakinaṃ vṛthā \|*  
*tvadbhāryāmasya bhāryāṃ ca tvāṃ ca putramimaṃ dvija \|\| 59 \|\|*

*bhakṣayiṣyāmi vaṃśaṃ ca tasmānmuñca durātmakam \|*  
*imaṃ tyajasi cetputraṃ yuṣmānmuñcāmi sāṃpratam \|\| 60 \|\|*

Brahmahatyā said:

O excellent Brāhmaṇa Padmanābha, do not accept him (and give him shelter). He is addicted to drinking liquor. He is a thief and Brāhmaṇa-slayer. He is a great sinner. He is treacherous to his mother and father. He is vicious in his mind. He has deserted his wife and is over-fond of harlots. Leave off this wicked one.

59-60. O Brāhmaṇa, if you shield in vain your son who is a great sinner, I will swallow your wife, this man’s wife, you, your son and the entire family. Hence leave off this wicked one. If you abandon your son now, I will release you all.

## \|\| 1.28.61 \|\|

*naikasyārthe kulaṃ hantumarhasi tvaṃ mahāmate \|*  
*ityuktaḥ sa tayā tatra padmanābho'bravīcca tām \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O highly intelligent one, it does not behove you to get the whole family destroyed for the sake of one (member).

On being told by her thus Padmanābha spoke to her thus:

## \|\| 1.28.62 \|\|

*padmanābha uvāca \|*  
*bādhate māṃ sutasnehaḥ kathaṃ putraṃ parityaje \|*  
*brahmahatyā tadākarṇya padmanābhaṃ tamabravīt \|\| 62 \|\|*

Padmanābha said:

62\. Affection for my son torments me. How can I forsake my son?

On hearing it Brahmahatyā spoke to the Brāhmaṇa:

## \|\| 1.28.63-64 \|\|

*brahmahatyovāca \|*  
*putro'yaṃ patito'bhūtte varṇāśramabahiṣkṛtaḥ \|*  
*putresminmā kuru snehaṃ niṃditaṃ tasya darśanam \|\| 63 \|\|*

*ityuktvā brahmahatyā sā padmanābhasya paśyataḥ \|*  
*hastena prajahārāsya sutaṃ keśavanāmakam \|\| 64 \|\|*

Brahmahatyā said:

63-64. This son of yours has become fallen. He is excommunicated from the pale of castes and stages of life. Do not love this son. His very sight is despicable.

After saying this Brahmahatyā struck his son named Keśava with her hand even as Padmabābha \[Padmanābha?\] was watching.

## \|\| 1.28.65 \|\|

*ruroda tātatāteti janakaṃ prabruvanmuhuḥ \|*  
*rurudurjanako mātā bhāryā tasya durātmanaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Calling his father frequently he lamented, “O father! O father!” The father, mother and wife of that wicked one, all lamented.

\[The Means of Liberation from Brahmahatyā as Advised by Bharadvāja to Padmanābha\]:—

## \|\| 1.28.66 \|\|

*atha padmanābhaṃ prati bharadvājakathito brahmahatyāvimuktyupāyaḥ \|*  
*tasminkāle mahābhāgo bharadvājo mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*diṣṭyā samāyayau yogī śaunakādyā mahaujasaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. At that time Bharadvāja, the great sage of exalted magnificence, the great Yogin, chanced to come there, O Śaunaka and sages of great prowess.

## \|\| 1.28.67 \|\|

*padmanābho'tha taṃ dṛṣṭvā bharadvājaṃ mahāmunim \|*  
*stutvā praṇamya śaraṇaṃ yayāce putrakāraṇāt \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. On seeing Bharadvāja the great sage Padmanābha bowed down to him and eulogized him. He sought refuge in him for the sake of his son:

## \|\| 1.28.68-74 \|\|

*bharadvāja mahābhāga sākṣādviṣṇvaṃśako bhavān \|*  
*tvaddarśanamapuṇyānāṃ bhavitā na kadācana \|\| 68 \|\|*

*brahmahā ca surāpī ca steyī cābhūtsuto mama \|*  
*putraṃ prahartumā yātā brahmahatyā bhayaṃkarī \|\| 69 \|\|*

*bhūyādyathā me putroyaṃ mahāpātakamocitaḥ \|*  
*ghoreyaṃ brahmahatyā ca yathā śīghraṃ layaṃ vrajet \|\| 70 \|\|*

*tamupāyaṃ vadasvādya mama putre dayāṃ kuru \|*  
*eka eva hi putro me nānyo'sti tanayo mune \|\| 71 \|\|*

*sute mṛte tu vaṃśo me samucchidyeta mūlataḥ \|*  
*tataḥ pitṛbhyaḥ piṇḍānāṃ dātā'pi na bhaveddhruvam \|\| 72 \|\|*

*tataḥ kṛpāṃ kuruṣva tvamasmāsu bhagavanmune \|*  
*ityuktaḥ sa bharadvājaḥ sākṣānnārāyaṇāṃśakaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*dhyātvā tu suciraṃ kālaṃ padmanābhaṃ vaco'bravīt \|\| 74 \|\|*

68-74. “O Bharadvāja of exalted magnificence, you are a part of Viṣṇu himself. Persons without merits will never see you. My son has become murderer of a Brāhmaṇa, liquor-addict and a thief. The terrifying Brahmahatyā has come to strike my son. Advise me the means whereby my son shall become liberated from great sins and this terrible Brahmahatyā shall be destroyed quickly. Take pity on my son. O sage, I have only one son. I have no other son. If this son dies, my family will become extinct. Then there may not be anyone to offer rice-balls to the Pitṛs. Therefore, O sage, be kind to us.”

On being appealed thus Bharadvāja who was a part of Nārāyaṇa himself, meditated for a long time and spoke these words to Padmanābha:

## \|\| 1.28.75-76 \|\|

*bharadvāja uvāca \|*  
*padmanābha kṛtaṃ pāpamatikrūraṃ sutena te \|*  
*nāsya pāpasya śāntiḥ syātprāyaścittāyutairapi \|\| 75 \|\|*

*tathā'pi te sutasyāhamasya pāpasya śāntaye \|*  
*prāyaścittaṃ vadiṣyāmi padmanābha śṛṇu dvija \|\| 76 \|\|*

Bharadvāja said:

75-76. O Padmanābha, very formidable sins have been perpetrated by your son. Even by means of ten thousand atonements his sins will not be quelled. Still I shall recommend some expiation for absolution of the sins of your son. O Brāhmaṇa Padmanābha, listen.

## \|\| 1.28.77-78 \|\|

*gaṅgāyā dakṣiṇe bhāge dviśatīyojane dvija \|*  
*pūrvāmbhodheḥ paścime tu pañcabhiryojanairmite \|\| 77 \|\|*

*suvarṇamukharītīre cottare krośamātrake \|*  
*veṃkaṭādriti khyātaḥ sarvalokanamaskṛtaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

77-78. O Brāhmaṇa, two hundred Yojanas (2400 kms) to the south of Gaṅgā, five Yojanas to the west of the Eastern Sea, on the northern basin of Suvarṇamukharī and only one Krośa from it, there is the mountain well-known as Veṅkaṭādri.

## \|\| 1.28.79-80 \|\|

*meruputro mahāpuṇyaḥ sarvadevābhivanditaḥ \|*  
*vaikuṇṭhalokādānīto viṣṇoḥ krīḍācalo mahān \|\| 79 \|\|*

*garutmatā vegavatā svarṇamukhyāstaṭe śubhe \|*  
*vartate devasaṃghaiśca ṛṣisaṃghaiśca pūjitaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

79-80. It is bowed to by all the worlds. It is the son of Meru. It is of great merit. It is saluted to by all the Devas. It has been brought from Vaikuṇṭha by the fast moving (vehicle) Garuḍa. It is the great mountain of sport of Viṣṇu. Now it is there on the auspicious banks of Svarṇamukhī. It is adored by groups of Devas and groups of sages.

## \|\| 1.28.81-83 \|\|

*tasminveṃkaṭaśailendre sākṣānnārāyaṇaḥ svayam \|*  
*lakṣmīdevyā ca bhūdevyā nīlādevyā samāgataḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*vartate veṃkaṭeśaḥ sa sākṣānmokṣapradāyakaḥ \|*  
*tasya veṃkaṭanāthasya hyālayasya tathottare \|\| 82 \|\|*

*kaṭāhatīrthaṃ viprendra vartate maṅgalapradam \|*  
*brahmahatyādipāpaghnaṃ vāñchitārthapradāyakam \|\| 83 \|\|*

81-83. On that prominent mountain Veṅkaṭa Nārāyaṇa himself dwells along with Goddess Lakṣmī, Goddess Bhū (the Earth) and Goddess Nīlā. Veṅkaṭeśa is the direct bestower of salvation. To the north of the temple of Veṅkaṭanātha, O great Brāhmaṇa, there is the holy spot Kaṭāhatīrtha that bestows auspiciousness. It destroys the sins like that of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter. It yields all desired objects.

## \|\| 1.28.84-85 \|\|

*sutena sākaṃ vipreṃdra piba tīrthaṃ manoharam \|*  
*bharadvājasya vākyaṃ tacchrutvā vai vedasaṃmitam \|\| 84 \|\|*

*śirasā taṃ praṇamyātha yayau veṃkaṭaparvatam \|\| 85 \|\|*

84-85. O eminent Brāhmaṇa, along with your son drink the charming holy water (of that Tīrtha).

On hearing the words of Bharadvāja, which are on a par with the words of Vedas, he bowed down his head to him and went to the Veṅkaṭa mountain.

\[By Drinking the Holy Water from Kaṭāhatīrtha as per Advice of Bharadvāja Keśava is Liberated from the Sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter\]:—

## \|\| 1.28.86 \|\|

*atha bharadvājoktyā kaṭāhatīrthapānena keśavasya brahmahatyāvimuktiḥ \|*  
*taṃ gatvā veṃkaṭaṃ śailaṃ svāmipuṣkariṇījale \|*  
*sutena sākaṃ vipreṃdraḥ sasnau niyamapūrvakam \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. After going to the mountain Veṅkaṭa the eminent Brāhmaṇa took his holy bath with due holy observances in the waters of Svāmipuṣkariṇī along with his soṇ.

## \|\| 1.28.87-88 \|\|

*varāhasvāminaṃ natvā śrīnivāsālayaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*pradakṣiṇaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā vimānaṃ saṃpraṇamya ca \|\| 87 \|\|*

*padmanābho'tha putreṇa keśavena durātmanā \|*  
*papau kaṭāhatīrthaṃ tadbrahmahatyāvināśakam \|\| 88 \|\|*

87-88. He bowed down to Lord Varāha and went to the shrine of Śrīnivāsa. He circumambulated and bowed down to Vimāna (palatial Temple). Along with Keśava, his son of great wickedness, Padmanābha drank (the water of) Kaṭāhatīrtha that is destructive of the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter.

## \|\| 1.28.89-91 \|\|

*tadānīṃ brahmahatyā sā śīghrameva layaṃ gatā \|*  
*anantaraṃ tato gatvā veṃkaṭeśaṃ kṛpānidhim \|\| 89 \|\|*

*putreṇa saha viprendraḥ padmanābho dadarśa saḥ \|*  
*tadā prādurabhūddevo veṅkaṭeśo dayānidhiḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

*kaṭāhatīrthapānena toṣito vākyamabravīt \|\| 91 \|\|*

89-91. Thereat Brahmahatyā was dissolved immediately. Thereafter the leading Brāhmaṇa Padmanābha went to Veṅkaṭeśa, the storehouse of mercy, along with his son and visited the Lord. Then Veṅkaṭeśa, the storehouse of kindness, appeared before them on being delighted by their drinking (the water of) Kaṭāhatīrtha. He spoke these words:

\[The Lord Addresses Padmanābha who was Accompanied by His Son Liberated from Brahmahatyā\]:—

## \|\| 1.28.92-95 \|\|

*atha brahmahatyāvimuktasutena sahitaṃ padmanābhaṃ prati bhagavaduktiḥ \|*  
*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*padmanābha mahābuddhe vedavedāntapāraga \|*  
*bharadvājasya vākyena prāpya veṃkaṭaparvatam \|\| 92 \|\|*

*kaṭāhatīrthaṃ tvaṃ pītvā kṛtārtho'si na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tava putraḥ keśavākhyo vimukto brahmahatyayā \|\| 93 \|\|*

*tasmātkaṭāhatīrthaṃ tu sevanīyaṃ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*tasmiṃstīrthe mahābhāga pītvā jalamanuttamam \|\| 94 \|\|*

*pāpino'pi kṛtārthāḥ syuḥ satyaṃ satyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*māmakaṃ lokamāgatya sukhī bhava mahāmate \|\| 95 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

92-95. O Padmanābha of great wisdom, O master of Vedas and Vedāṅgas, at the instance of Bharadvāja you came to the Veṅkaṭa mountain. After drinking (the water from) Kaṭāhatīrtha you have undoubtedly become blessed with your object achieved. Your son named Keśava has been released from Brahmahatyā. Hence Kaṭāhatīrtha should be resorted to with great effort. O Brāhmaṇa of great fortune, after drinking the excellent water in that Tīrtha even sinners become blessed and contented. It is true. It is (really) true. There is no doubt. Gome to my world and be happy, O highly intelligent one.

## \|\| 1.28.96 \|\|

*ityuktvā veṃkaṭeśo'sāvantardhānaṃ gatastataḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. After saying this Veṅkaṭeśa vanished from there.

## Chapter 29 - Arjuna Proceeds on a Pilgrimage

## \|\| 1.29.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*tīrthānāmiha sarveṣāṃ prabhāvaḥ kathitastvayā \|*  
*nadīnāṃ parvatānāṃ ca kṣetrāṇāṃ sarasāmapi \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: From this chapter begins the sub-section of the glorification of river Suvarṇamukharī (see Supra p. 6, Fnt 2)

The sages said:

1\. The power of all the holy places as also of the rivers, mountains, holy shrines and lakes has been related by you.

## \|\| 1.29.2 \|\|

*nideśātpadmagarbhasya suvarṇamukharī nadī \|*  
*nītā bhuvamagastyena vyākhyātā bhavatānagha \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. It has been described by you, O sinless one, that at the instance of Brahmā the river Suvarṇamukharī was brought to the earth by Agastya.

## \|\| 1.29.3 \|\|

*tadutpattiprabhāvaṃ ca tīrthaughāṃstatsamāśrayān \|*  
*śrotuṃ saṃprītirutpannā tanno vaktuṃ tvamarhasi \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Now a desire has arisen to hear about its origin and power as well as of the groups of Tīrthas depending on it. It behoves you to recount that to us.

## \|\| 1.29.4 \|\|

*praṇamya śambhuṃ nandīśaṃ ṣaḍāsyaṃ vyāsameva ca \|*  
*munibhiḥ prārthitaḥ sūtastadā vaktuṃ pracakrame \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Sūta who was thus requested by the sages, bowed down to Śaṃbhu, the Lord Nandī, the six-faced Lord Skanda and Vyāsa. Then he began to recount.

## \|\| 1.29.5-6 \|\|

*śrīsūta uvāca \|*  
*sādhu pṛṣṭaṃ mahābhāga bhavadbhirmaṃgalāvaham \|*  
*ākhyānametadāmnāya śravaṇodbhūtasiddhidam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*śṛṇutāvahitā divyāṃ kathāṃ kalmaṣanāśinīm \|*  
*bharadvājena kathitāṃ pārthāya kathayāmi vaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

Śrī Sūta said:

5-6. O blessed ones, what has been asked by you is relevant and conducive to the good. This narrative bestows the Siddhi that comes from listening to the Vedas.

Listen attentively. I shall recount to you the divine story that is destructive of sins. It had been narrated by Bharadvāja to Arjuna.

## \|\| 1.29.7 \|\|

*avāpya drupadātprājñādyājñasenīṃ pṛthāsutāḥ \|*  
*dhṛtarāṣṭranideśena jagmuḥ karipuraṃ śubham \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. After getting Yājñasenī (i.e. Draupadī) from the wise king Drupada the sons of Pṛthā went to the splendid city of Hastinā-pura at the bidding of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

## \|\| 1.29.8 \|\|

*bhīṣmeṇa cāṃbikeyena tatra saṃmānitāstadā \|*  
*duryodhanādibhiḥ sārddhaṃ nyavasanpañcavatsarān \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. They were honoured thereby Bhīṣma as well as by the son of Aṃbikā (i.e. Dhṛtarāṣṭra). They lived there for five years along with Duryodhana and others.

## \|\| 1.29.9-10 \|\|

*tato'nuśiṣṭo bhīṣmādyairdhṛtarāṣṭro mahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ kulavṛddhānāṃ vāsudevasya cāgrataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*pradadau pāṃḍuputrebhyastatsevāhṛṣṭamānasaḥ \|*  
*sārdharājyaṃ puravaraṃ khāṇḍavaprasthasaṃjñikam \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. As advised by Bhīṣma and others, Dhṛtarāṣṭra of great fame, who was himself delighted in his mind on account of their services, granted to the sons of Pāṇḍu the excellent city named Khāṇḍavaprastha along with half the kingdom in the preseṇce of Vāsudeva and all the elderly members of the family.

## \|\| 1.29.11 \|\|

*āmaṃtrya pāṇḍutanayā dhṛtarāṣṭrādikānkurūn \|*  
*jagmustatkhāṇḍavaprasthaṃ puraṃ kṛṣṇasamanvitāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. After taking leave of the Kurus headed by Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the sons of Pāṇḍu went to that city of Khāṇḍavaprastha accompanied by Kṛṣṇa.

## \|\| 1.29.12 \|\|

*indraprasthāhvaye tatra rakṣite viśvakarmaṇā \|*  
*vasanpure'śiṣatpṛthvīṃ sānujo dharmanaṃdanaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Residing in that city named Indraprastha which was well guarded by Viśvakarman, Dharmaputra (Yudhiṣṭhira) ruled over the kingdom in the company of his brothers.

## \|\| 1.29.13 \|\|

*gate kṛṣṇe nijapuraṃ nāradasyānuśāsanāt \|*  
*pratijñāṃ cakrire pārthā dharmajñā draupadīṃ prati \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. After Kṛṣṇa had gone back to his city, the sons of Pṛthā, well-conversant with Dharma took a vow (i.e. made an agreement) regarding Draupadī at the advice of Nārada.

\[Prelude to the Pilgrimage of Arjuna\]:—

## \|\| 1.29.14-16 \|\|

*athārjunatīrthayātropoddhātaḥ \|*  
*yathākrameṇa sā kṛṣṇā varṣamekaikamādarāt \|*  
*ekaikasya gṛhe tiṣṭhetpratinirṇayapūrvakam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*yaḥ paśyettāṃ paragṛhe sthitāṃ pāṃcālanaṃdinīm \|*  
*tenaikahāyanamitaṃ vidheyaṃ tīrthasevanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*evaṃ kṛtapratijñāste pāṇḍubhūpālanaṃdanāḥ \|*  
*vyāpārairloṃkasāmānyairninyuḥ kālamataṃdritāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. The agreement was as follows: Kṛṣṇā (i.e. Draupadī) should stay with each one of them (Pāṇḍava-brothers) in due order, with great respect, for one year, with this proviso that if any one of them were to see the daughter of Pāñcāla staying in another brother’s house, he would proceed on a pilgrimage for a period of one year.

Having taken a vow thus, those sons of king Pāṇḍu spent their time carefully in all those activities common to everyone in the world.

## \|\| 1.29.17 \|\|

*atha jānapado vipro rājagehāṃgaṇe sthitaḥ \|*  
*cukrośa bahudhā dhenurhṛtā me taskarairiti \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Once a Brāhmaṇa from the rural areas came and stood in the palace courtyard and lamented loudly many times, “My cow has been taken away by thieves.”

## \|\| 1.29.18 \|\|

*samāśvāsya ca taṃ vipraṃ praviveśa dhanaṃjayaḥ \|*  
*āyudhāni samānetuṃ tvarayā śastramaṃdiram \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. After consoling that Brāhmaṇa Dhanañjaya (Arjuna) hurriedly entered the arsenal to take out his weapons.

## \|\| 1.29.19 \|\|

*tatrāpaśyatsamāsīnau pāṃcālīdharmanandanau \|*  
*jānannapi pratijñāṃ sa dhanurjagrāha seṣudhi \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. There he saw Pāñcālī and Dharmaputra seated (together). Though he was fully aware of the vow, he entered the apartment and took out the bow along with the quiver.

## \|\| 1.29.20 \|\|

*sa gatvā taskarānājau nihatya nṛpanandanaḥ \|*  
*nivartya dhenuṃ tāṃ tasmai dadau viprāya sādaram \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. That Prince went to fight with the thieves, killed them in battle, retrieved the cow and gave it to the Brāhmaṇa with due respect.

## \|\| 1.29.21 \|\|

*atha vijñāpayāmāsa phālguno dharmanandanam \|*  
*tīrthayātrā mayā kāryā samayollaṃghanāditi \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Thereafter Phālguna intimated to Dharmaputra (Yudhiṣṭhira):

“Pilgrimage has to be undertaken by me, because I have broken the stipulations in the vow.”

## \|\| 1.29.22 \|\|

*anujasya vacaḥ śrutvā sarvadharmavidāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ dhīraḥ sādaraṃ dharmanaṃdanaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. On hearing the words of his younger brother the wise king Dharmaputra, the most excellent one among those conversant with righteousness, eagerly spoke thus:

## \|\| 1.29.23 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca \|*  
*gavārthaṃ brāhmaṇārthaṃ ca yadvadedanṛtaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*yadācaredasatkarma tatsatyaṃ tatsamaṃjasam \|\| 23 \|\|*

Yudhiṣṭhira said:

23\. If for the sake of cows and Brāhmaṇas one were to tell a lie, it is truth itself. If for the same purpose one were to commit an evil act, it is appropriate indeed.

## \|\| 1.29.24 \|\|

*brāhmaṇārthaṃ gavārthaṃ ca tvayā karmedṛśaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*tadasadbhāvamāpnoti kathaṃ kathaya suvrata \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. It is for the sake of a Brāhmaṇa as well as for the sake of a cow that you have done like this. How can it become a vile deed? Tell me, O (brother) of good holy rites.

## \|\| 1.29.25 \|\|

*prajāpālanakṛtyasya coropekṣaṇaśikṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*nūnaṃ phalaṃ bhavedrājño brahmahatyāśvamedhajam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The duty of a king is the protection of his subjects. If he is indifferent to thieves, he will incur the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter. If he punishes the thieves, he shall enjoy the benefit of a horse sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.29.26 \|\|

*asādhyānvairiṇo jñātvā'pyavanīśo na bhadrabhāk \|*  
*svadeśopaplavakarāstaskarā yadyaśikṣitāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Even after knowing that they are uncontrollable enemies, if the thieves who oppress the people of his own country are not punished by the king, he will not be entitled to welfare and peace.

## \|\| 1.29.27 \|\|

*asmākaṃ bhūbhujāṃ lokajālasya ca hitaṃ hi yat \|*  
*tvayedṛśaṃ kṛtaṃ karma nāsti doṣo hyatastava \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. What has been done by you is an act conducive to the good and welfare of us, the kings, as well as of all the classes of the public. Therefore there is no fault on your part.

## \|\| 1.29.28 \|\|

*śrīsūta uvāca \|*  
*dharmaputrasya vacanamākarṇya racitāṃjaliḥ \|*  
*punarvijñāpayāmāsa dharmanityo dhanaṃjayaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

Śrī Sūta said:

28\. On hearing the words of Dharmaputra, Dhanañjaya who was always virtuous, joined his palms in reverence and submitted once again:

## \|\| 1.29.29-30 \|\|

*iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīveṃkaṭācalamāhātmye suvarṇamukharīmāhātmye arjunatīrthayātrāgamanavarṇanaṃnāmaikonatriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*kṛtyākṛtyavidā dakṣeṇātmanā prāksamīritā \|*  
*nollaṃghanīyā satataṃ pratijñā puruṣeṇa hi \|\| 30 \|\|*

Arjuna said:

29-30. O King, do not speak like this (to approve) a thing that involves the breaking of one’s own vow.

A vow should never be broken by a person who knows everything about Dharma, who is himself the brilliant Dharma incarnate, who is conversant with what should be done and what should not be done (and especially by one) who is competent. A vow that has been proclaimed before by oneself should never be broken.

## \|\| 1.29.31 \|\|

*aśaktānāṃ gatiḥ seyaṃ yadbaṃdhuguruvākyataḥ \|*  
*dharmaṃ tyajaṃti samayaṃ tyaktāḥ prāksvaṃ samīritam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. It is a way out for weaklings to forsake their duty on being prompted by the words of kinsmen and elders by casting off their own pledges announced by themselves previously.

## \|\| 1.29.32 \|\|

*kṛpayā tīrthagamanādāryo yadi nivartayet \|*  
*hatapratijñaṃ māṃ lokāñjalpataḥ ko nivārayet \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. If out of compassion my noble (brother) were to dissuade me from undertaking the pilgrimage, who can prevent the people from decrying me as one who has broken his vow?

## \|\| 1.29.33 \|\|

*mamāpi tīrthayātrāyāṃ kautukottaralaṃ manaḥ \|*  
*kartavyaṃ ca smṛtaṃ rājannāradādiṣṭaśāsanam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. My mind is extremely eager for going on a pilgrimage. My duty based on the behest of Nārada has been remembered by me.

## \|\| 1.29.34 \|\|

*tatprasīda mahārāja yattīrthagamanodyame \|*  
*saṃmānanīyaḥ prabhubhiḥ samayo hyanujīvinām \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Hence be pleased, O great King, in the matter of undertaking the pilgrimage. The vow of servants should be honoured by masters.

## \|\| 1.29.35 \|\|

*tatheti bhrātṛbhiḥ sārddhaṃ kṛtānumatirarjunaḥ \|*  
*agrajaṃ toṣayāmāsa praṇāmapraśrayādibhiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Arjuna was given permission by saying “So be it”. Along with his brothers he delighted his elder brother by means of his humility, obeisance etc.

## \|\| 1.29.36 \|\|

*yathārhaṃ bhīmasenādīnbhrātṝnāmantrya pāṇḍavaḥ \|*  
*kṛtasvastyayano bhavyairniryayau dharaṇīsuraiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The son of Pāṇḍu took leave of his brothers Bhīmasena and others. Holy rites for his welfare during his travels were performed by excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.29.37-38 \|\|

*paurāṇikā jyautiṣikā bhiṣajo dharaṇīsurāḥ \|*  
*anujagmurbhṛtyagaṇāḥ śilpinaḥ sūtamāgadhāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*yudhiṣṭhirājñayā tasya bhogatyāgakṣamaṃ dhanam \|*  
*gṛhītvānuyayuḥ snigdhāḥ sabhyāḥ kośādhikāriṇaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. At the bidding of Yudhiṣṭhira many persons followed him, viz. Brāhmaṇas conversant with the Purāṇas, astrologers, physicians, artisans, servants, bards and heralds. Affectionate and well-behaved officers of the treasury followed him taking with them sufficient wealth for the sake of Arjuna’s pleasures as well as charitable purposes.

\[Arjuna’s Arrival at Suvarṇamukharī after taking His Holy Bath in Gaṅgā and Other Tīrthas\]:—

## \|\| 1.29.39 \|\|

*atha arjunasya gaṃgāditīrthāvagāhanapūrvaka suvarṇamukharyāgamanam \|*  
*sa rājaputraḥ prathamaṃ prāpya bhāgīrathīṃ nadīm \|*  
*gaṃgādvāraṃ prayāgaṃ ca siṣeve kāśikāmapi \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. At the outset the Prince went to the river Bhāgīrathī. He visited the holy places of Gaṅgādvāra, Prayāga and Kāśī.

## \|\| 1.29.40 \|\|

*paśyaṃstīrthāni jāhnavyāstattīropāntavartmanā \|*  
*āsasāda samuttuṅgakallolaṃ dakṣiṇodadhim \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Visiting various Tīrthas and travelling by the path along the banks of Gaṅgā he reached the southern ocean agitated by high waves.

## \|\| 1.29.41 \|\|

*mahānadīṃ mahāpuṇyāṃ prasiddhaṃ puruṣottamam \|*  
*siṃhācalaṃ ca saṃvīkṣya prāptavānkṛtakṛtyatām \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. After visiting Mahānadī of great merit, the well-known shrine of Puruṣottama (i.e. Jagannātha) and Siṃhācala he attained great contentment (and peace).

## \|\| 1.29.42 \|\|

*tato dadarśa kaunteyaḥ puṇyāṃ godāvarīṃ nadīm \|*  
*samastaduritavrātaśātanottīrṇagauravām \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Thereafter the son of Kuntī saw the holy river Godāvarī whose greatness is increased on account of its power of dispelling all the masses of sins.

## \|\| 1.29.43 \|\|

*kṛtābhiṣekastattoyairvidhivatpāṇḍunandanaḥ \|*  
*pramodaṃ vividhairdānairakarodbhūsuvarṇakaiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. He duly took his bath in its waters. The son of Pāṇḍu delighted others by means of different kinds of charitable gifts such as lands and gold.

## \|\| 1.29.44 \|\|

*nadīṃ malāpahākhyāṃ ca dṛṣṭvā modaṃ yayau śubham \|*  
*tataḥ samāsasādāsau kṛṣṇaveṇīṃ saridvarām \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. After visiting the river named Malāpahā he experienced splendid pleasure. Then he reached Kṛṣṇaveṇī, the excellent river.

## \|\| 1.29.45 \|\|

*śivasya niyatāvāsaṃ caturdvārasamanvitam \|*  
*nānātīrthagaṇākīrṇaṃ śrīparvatamavaikṣata \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. He visited Śrīparvata, the permanent residence of Śiva. It has four entrances and there are many Tīrthas there.

## \|\| 1.29.46 \|\|

*nadīṃ pinākinīṃ tīrtvā gatvā devarṣisevitam \|*  
*nārāyaṇapriyāvāsamapaśyadveṃkaṭācalam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. He crossed the river Pinākinī (modem Pennar) and proceeded ahead. Then he saw Veṅkaṭācala, the favourite abode of Nārāyaṇa, frequented by celestial sages.

## Chapter 30 - Description of the Hermitage of Bharadvāja

## \|\| 1.30.1 \|\|

*atha suvarṇamukharīvarṇanam \|*  
*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tathā sarvāṇi tīrthāni samālokyāgatasya ca \|*  
*mudaṃ praguṇayāñcake sā pārthasya mahāpagā \|\| 1 \|\|*

\[Description of Suvarṇamukharī\]:—

Sūta said:

1\. That great river heightened the pleasure of the son of Pṛthā (Arjuna) who had come there after visiting all the Tīrthas.

## \|\| 1.30.2 \|\|

*yasyāstaṭanikuñjeṣu modante vanitāḥ sukhāḥ \|*  
*siddhāḥ saṃsevitā vātaiḥ śīkarāsāraśītalaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. In the bowers on the banks of that river Siddhas and their women rejoice happily, being served and attended upon by winds cool on account of water-spray.

## \|\| 1.30.3 \|\|

*yā samudyatahasteva gaṅgāmākāśavāhinīm \|*  
*āliṃgituṃ samuttuṃgaiḥ kallolairabhrasaṃgibhiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. With its lofty waves coming into contact with the clouds, it appeared as though the river had flung up its arms to embrace the (heavenly) Gaṅgā flowing through the sky.

## \|\| 1.30.4 \|\|

*dhūmairāhutisaṃbhūtaistaruśākhopalaṃbhibhiḥ \|*  
*valkalaiśca virājante yattaṭāśramabhūmayaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The penance groves on its banks were marked by the columns of smoke rising up from Āhutis (offering of ghee into the Sacred Fire) and the bark garments hanging from the branches of the trees.

## \|\| 1.30.5 \|\|

*munīndraiḥ suravaryaiśca sthāpitāni samantataḥ \|*  
*yattaṭadvitaye bhāṃti divyaliṃgāni śūlinaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The divine Liṅgas of the Trident-bearing Lord installed all round by prominent sages and excellent Suras were seen on the banks of that river.

## \|\| 1.30.6 \|\|

*yadīyasaikatāvāsaviśrāntā mānasaṃ saraḥ \|*  
*na smaraṃti nijāvāsaṃ marālā vihagottamāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Having taken rest in their abodes among the sands on the banks of that river, swans, the most excellent ones among birds, forget the Mānasa lake, their (original) home.

## \|\| 1.30.7 \|\|

*śamitāvagrahātaṃkaiḥ kulyāmukhavinirgataiḥ \|*  
*puṣṇāti toyaiḥ sasyāni lokarakṣākṣamāṇi yā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. That river increases the productivity of grain-bearing plants and is capable of protecting people by its waters flowing through canals, thereby dispelling the anguish due to drought.

## \|\| 1.30.8-10 \|\|

*cakravākakucottuṃgavīcivallīvibhūṣitā \|*  
*āvartanābhivilasatsaikataśroṇi maṇḍalā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*praphullapadmavadanā calanmīnayugekṣaṇā \|*  
*vilasatphenavasanā haṃsayānamanoharā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*jalapakṣiravālāpā nayanānandakāriṇī \|*  
*apūrvakāminīrūpā yā vibhātyambudhipriyā \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. This river, the beloved of the Ocean, shone like a woman of an extraordinarily wonderful form. The Cakravāka (ruddy goose) birds were her protruding breasts. They were adorned with Patravallīs (lines or figures on the body drawn by means of fragrant colourful substances). She shone with the sandy banks as her buttocks and the eddy as her navel. The full-blown lotus was her face. The moving fish were her pair of eyes. She shone with the foams as her garments. She was charming with the gait of swans. The chirping sound of the aquatic birds was her voice and talk. She caused much delight to the eyes.

## \|\| 1.30.11-12 \|\|

*rodhasyantaravāhinyā nadyāḥ prācyāṃ dhanañjayaḥ \|*  
*dadarśa śailamuttuṃgaṃ kālahastisamāhayam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*udagraśikharābhogollikhitākāśamaṇḍalam \|*  
*saptapātālamūlādhorūḍhamūlopalāṃcitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. On the western bank of the river that flows in between, Dhanañjaya (Arjuna) saw a lofty mountain named Kālahastī. Many lofty peaks of this mountain scraped the region of the sky. The bottom rock of this mountain is firmly fixed beneath all the seven Pātālas.

\[Arjuna’s Opportunity of Visiting and Worshipping Kālahastīśvara and Other Deities Stationed on the Banks of the Suvarṇamukharī\]:—

## \|\| 1.30.13 \|\|

*atha arjunasya svarṇamukharītīrasthakālahastīśvarādisevāprāptiḥ \|*  
*snātvā tasyāṃ mahānadyāṃ tasmiñchaile surārcitam \|*  
*apaśyadarjuno devaṃ kālahastīśanāmakam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. After taking his bath in that great river Arjuna visited the deity named Kālahastīśa, worshipped by all the Suras on that mountain.

## \|\| 1.30.14 \|\|

*saṃpūjya ca mahādevaṃ nagendratanayāsakham \|*  
*manasā bhaktiyuktena kṛtārthatvamupeyivān \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. With his mind infused with devotion, he worshipped Mahādeva accompanied by the daughter of the Lord of Mountains. Thereby he derived full contentment.

## \|\| 1.30.15 \|\|

*tato mahāgirau tasminnadbhutaikaniketane \|*  
*cacārābhūtapūrvāṇāṃ viśeṣāṇāṃ didṛkṣayā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. With a desire to see special features that had never existed before (in other places), Arjuna wandered over that great mountain, the sole abode of mysteries.

## \|\| 1.30.16 \|\|

*siddhānālokayāmāsa vasato girisānuṣu \|*  
*gāyato devadevasya caritrāṇyabalāyutān \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He saw Siddhas who accompanied by their womenfolk lived on the peaks and ridges of the mountain and sang the anecdotes of the Lord of Devas.

## \|\| 1.30.17 \|\|

*apsarolalanājuṣṭānpuṣpāsavamadākulān \|*  
*nikuñjeṣu samāsīnāngaṃdharvānaikṣatādarāt \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He looked at the Gandharvas with great respect as they were seated in the bowers of flowers accompanied by the Apsaras-maidens and excited and inebriated on account of the (imbibed) liquor extracted from the flowers.

## \|\| 1.30.18 \|\|

*vivikteṣu pradeśeṣu śivadhyānaparāyaṇān \|*  
*apaśyadyogino divyānādarānandaśālinaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. In secluded spots he saw divine Yogins who were deeply engrossed in meditating on Śiva and full of respect and delight.

## \|\| 1.30.19 \|\|

*praśāntānyāśramapadānyavaikṣata samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*balinīvāravilasaddvārabhūmīśca pāṇḍavaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. All around he saw quiet and peaceful hermitages and penance-groves. The son of Pāṇḍu saw the courtyard at the entrance (to the various abodes) resplendent with the Nīvāra grains offered as oblations.

## \|\| 1.30.20 \|\|

*nirāhārānvāyubhujaḥ parṇādānātapāśanān \|*  
*śāntānālokayāmāsa munīnniyamitendriyān \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He saw the sages abstaining from food, or taking in only air, or eating leaves, or consuming sunlight. All of them were calm with all their sense-organs perfectly controlled.

## \|\| 1.30.21-22 \|\|

*mudaṃ vitenire tasya netrayoḥ kamalākarāḥ \|*  
*phullasaugandhikāmodasaṃvāsitadigantarāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*mṛgayāsaṃbhṛtadhiyaścarato'dhijyakārmukān \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Lotus-ponds that rendered the quarters fragrant with the sweet smell of the full-blown flowers, gave delight to his eyes.

He saw Kirātas (Hunters) accompanied by their womenfolk, searching for deer, engrossed in thoughts of hunting and walking about with well-strung bows.

\[Arjuna Goes to Bharadvāja’s Hermitage Situated on the Banks of Suvarṇamukharī\]:—

## \|\| 1.30.23-28 \|\|

*athā'rjunasya suvarṇamukharītīrasthabharadvājāśramagamanam \|*  
*dadarśānveṣitamṛgānkirātānvanitāyutān \|*  
*tato dakṣiṇadigbhāge carannadrermanohare \|\| 23 \|\|*

*puṇyamāśramamadrākṣīdbharadvājasya kauravaḥ \|*  
*kadalīnārikelāmrakolacaṃpakacaṃdanaiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*takkolāśokahintālatālaketakidāḍimaiḥ \|*  
*jaṃbūkadamvakatakakhadirārjunapāṭalaiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*nāgapunnāgasaraladevadārukarañjakaiḥ \|*  
*lavaṃgaluṃgalavalīpriyaṃgutilakairapi \|\| 26 \|\|*

*bibhītaśrīphalāśvatthamadhūkaplakṣakesaraiḥ \|*  
*pūgajambīranāraṃganimbāmalakakauśikaiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*anyaiśca phalapuṣpāḍhyaiḥ śobhitaṃ dharaṇīruhaiḥ \|*  
*vāsantīkundajātyādilatābhiḥ pariveṣṭitam \|\| 28 \|\|*

23-28a. Walking through the charming southern portion of the mountain, the descendant of Kuru saw the holy hermitage of Bharadvāja. It was rendered splendid by trees laden with fruits and flowers, such as plantains, coconut palms, mango trees, black pepper, Caṃpaka, Sandal trees, Takkola, Aśoka, Hintāla, Tāla, Ketakī, Dāḍima (Pomegranates), Jaṃbū (Rose apple), Kadaṃba, Kaṭaka, Khadira, Arjuna, Pāṭala (Trumpet flower tree), Nāga, Punnāga, Sarala, Devadāru (Cedar), Karañjaka, Lavaṅga (Clove tree), Luṅga (a kind of citron), Lavalī, Priyaṅgu, Tilaka, Vibhīta, Śrīphala (Bilva), holy fig tree, Madhūka, Plakṣa, Kesara, Pūga, Jambīra (a kind of citron), Nāraṅga (Orange), Niṃba (Margosa), Āmalaka (Embylic myrobalan) and Kauśika (coconut?) trees.

28b. It was surrounded by the creepers of Vāsantī, Kunda, Jāti etc. (varieties of Jasmine).

## \|\| 1.30.29-44 \|\|

*apūrvasaurabhākṛṣṭabhramarībhiḥ samantataḥ \|*  
*cakravākabakakrauñcahaṃsakāraṇḍavāśrayaiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīveṃkaṭācalamāhātmye suvarṇamukharīmāhātmyapraśaṃsāyāṃ bharadvājāśramavarṇanaṃnāma triṃśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*samāpāditalakṣmīkaṃ kautukaikaniketanam \|*  
*siṃhadantāvalavyāghratarakṣurururaṅkubhiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*mṛgairanyaiḥ samākīrṇamanyo'nyahitakāribhiḥ \|*  
*jitacaitrarathodyānamadharīkṛtanandanam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*ativāṅmanasodāraṃ paramānandakāraṇam \|*  
*śivāgamānāṃ divyānāmarthajātamanuttamam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*prakāśayanti śāvānāṃ yatra mañjugiraḥ śukāḥ \|*  
*yasminhutāśano dāradhūmaśyāmalitaṃ nabhaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*akālajaladabhrāṃtimātanoti śikhaṇḍinām \|*  
*yasminvihāraśrāntānāṃ siṃhānāṃ svecchayāgatāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*nirvāpayanti gātrāṇi kariṇaḥ karaśīkaraiḥ \|*  
*tadāśramapadaṃ paśyanvismayākrāṃtamānasaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*prabhāvaṃ pāṇḍutanayaḥ praśaśaṃsa tapasvinām \|*  
*nivārya tatra tatraiva sakalānanujīvinaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*athārjunakṛtabharadvājasevākramaḥ \|*  
*mitrairvipravaraiḥ sārdhaṃ praviveśa tamāśramam \|*  
*agre dadarśa kaunteyaḥ sphuratpāvakatejasam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*bharadvājaṃ munivarairanekaiḥ parivāritam \|*  
*bhasmānuliptasarvāṃgaṃ mṛgacarmottarīyakam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*navavāridasaṃvītaṃ kailāsamiva bhāsvaram \|*  
*jaṭābhirlambamānābhirbhāsvantaṃ svarṇakāṃtibhiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*sthiravidyullatākīrṇamiva śāradanīradam \|*  
*śrutismṛti purāṇārthairekībhūya samāgataiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*aṅgīkṛtamivākāraṃ divyajñānaśubhāspadam \|*  
*dhṛtikṣāṃtidayātuṣṭiśāṃtibhirnityasevitam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*priyābhiriva raktābhirakhaṃḍabrahmavarcasam \|*  
*upagamya śanaiḥ pārthastatpādāṃbujayoḥ puraḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*cakre praṇāmaṃ sāṣṭāṃgaṃ samāliṃgitabhūtalam \|\| 44 \|\|*

29-33a. Various lakes and tanks brought glory and magnificence to it. Being attracted by uncommon and unprecedented fragrance, bees hovered all round.

Birds like ruddy geese, cranes, storks, swans, Kāraṇḍava ducks etc. resorted to them. The lakes were marked with various flowers, such as red lotuses, blue lotuses, lilies etc. The lakes and ponds were full of water, sweet like nectar. The hermitage was a unique place of curious things.

It was full of animals of various kinds like lions, elephants, tigers, bears, deer, antelopes etc. All of them were friendly and helpful to one another. The gardens and parks therein far surpassed Nandana, Caitraratha and other divine parks. It was the cause of supreme bliss (to everyone). It was charming beyond the power of thinking of minds and the power of expression through words.

33b-44. Parrots of sweet voice revealed to their young ones the excellent meanings of the divine Śivāgamas.

The sky above the hermitage was rendered dark by means of the thick columns of smoke arising from the sacred fires when the offerings of ghee were poured therein. Seeing the same, peacocks had the erroneous notion of untimely clouds (spreading over the sky).

When the lions got tired after their continuous sport in the forests, the elephants approached them there of their own accord and showered water on them through their trunks to give their bodies some relief from the strain.

Seeing that penance-grove, the son of Pāṇḍu got struck with wonder. He praised the power of the ascetics.

Preventing all his followers from straying here and there, he entered the hermitage along with his friends and excellent Brāhmaṇas.

\[Arjuna Pays His Respects to Bharadvāja\]:—

In front of him the son of Kuntī saw Sage Bharadvāja shining with the refulgence of blazing fire. He was surrounded by many excellent sages. He had smeared the whole of his body with ash. A deerskin constituted his upper garment. He was as resplendent as Kailāsa encircled by a fresh cloud. He was brilliant with his matted hair of golden splendour hanging down like the autumnal cloud with permanent streaks of lightning. He appeared as though the meanings of Śrutis, Smṛtis and Purāṇas had come collectively and adopted his form. He was (as it were) the receptacle of great auspiciousness, of divine knowledge and wisdom. He was permanently attended upon by (virtues like) fortitude, forbearance, kindness, contentment and peace, as though by loving wives. He had unimpaired Brahmanical splendour. The son of Pṛthā (Arjuna) approached him slowly and prostrated before his lotus-like feet with (his) eight limbs touching the ground.

\[Bharadvāja Extends His Hospitality to Arjuna\]:—

## \|\| 1.30.45 \|\|

*athārjunaṃ prati bharadvājakṛtātithyaprakāraḥ \|*  
*tamāgataṃ pṛthāputramutthāpya munipuṅgavaḥ \|*  
*āśīrbhiredhayāñcakre praharṣotphullamānasaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The eminent sage raised up the son of Pṛthā who had come (there and fallen at his feet) and blessed him with his mind extremely delighted.

## \|\| 1.30.46 \|\|

*saṃpūjya ca yathānyāyaṃ tamarghyādyaiḥ priyātithim \|*  
*vinirdiṣṭāsanāsīnaṃ samapṛcchadanāmayam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. After duly honouring him as a beloved guest with Arghya and other materials, he offered him a seat. As he sat thereon, he enquired about his welfare.

## \|\| 1.30.47 \|\|

*saṃmānanamavāpyāsmānmuneḥ pāṇḍavamadhyamaḥ \|*  
*priyairvākyairmunipaterakaronmanaso mudam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. After getting due honour and hospitality from the sage, the middle one among the Pāṇḍava brothers entertained the eminent sage through pleasing words.

## \|\| 1.30.48 \|\|

*sasmārātha bharadvājaḥ svardhenuṃ kāmadohinīm \|*  
*sā vitene'timahatīṃ bhakṣyabhojyādikalpanām \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Then Bharadvāja remembered the Celestial Cow yielding everything one desired. She distributed various kinds of foodstuffs lavishly.

## Chapter 31 - Agastya’s Departure to the South

## \|\| 1.31.1-2 \|\|

*atha suvarṇamukharīprabhāvaśuśrūṣayā bharadvājaṃ pratyarjunapraśraḥ \|*  
*śrīsūta uvāca \|*  
*kṛtasāyantanavidhiṃ hutāśanasamadyutim \|*  
*sukhāsīnaṃ munipatiṃ praṇamya bharatarṣabhaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tadīyaśītalāmodasudhāpūrānumoditaḥ \|*  
*gambhīraṃ praśrayopetamidaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 2 \|\|*

\[Prompted by His Desire to Know the Power of Suvarṇamukharī Arjuna asks Bharadvāja About the Same\]:—

Śrī Sūta said:

1-2. The prominent scion of the family of Bharata (Arjuna) bowed down to the leader of sages who had concluded his evening holy rites. He had a splendour like that of fire and was comfortably seated. He was pleased by his gladdening (words) of nectarine sweetness and cooling fragrance. Then he uttered the following words of decorous gravity full of humility:

## \|\| 1.31.3 \|\|

*arjuna uvāca \|*  
*munipuṃgava loke'smindhanya eko'hameva hi \|*  
*putrāviśeṣaṃ bhavatā yadevaṃ samyagādṛtaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Arjuna said:

3\. O most excellent sage, I am the only blessed one in this world, since I have been enthusiastically honoured by you as though I am not at all different from your own son.

## \|\| 1.31.4 \|\|

*bhavadādarasañjātakautukaṃ mama mānasam \|*  
*bhavadvākyāmṛtaṃ divyaṃ pātuṃ tvarayatīva mām \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. My mind, the curiosity of which has been aroused by your affection and encouragement, strongly urges me to imbibe the divine nectar of your words.

## \|\| 1.31.5 \|\|

*kasmācchailādiyaṃ jātā kenānītā mahānadī \|*  
*kiṃ puṇyaṃ snānadānādyaiḥ kṛtaistatropalabhyate \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. From which mountain has this great river originated? By whom was it brought? What is the merit obtained if the holy rites of bath, charitable gift etc. are performed there?

## \|\| 1.31.6 \|\|

*asyāḥ prabhāvaṃ prabhavaṃ prahvasya mama sanmune \|*  
*vaktumarhasi kāryo hi bhaktānugraha eva te \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. It behoves you, O good sage, to recount to me, your humble (follower), the origin and power of this (river). A devotee has to be blessed by you.

## \|\| 1.31.7 \|\|

*arjunasya vacaḥ śrutvā bharadvājo dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*tadānanaṃ samālokya vākyaṃ vākyavidabravīt \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On hearing the words of Arjuna Bharadvāja, the excellent Brāhmaṇa, a skilled speaker, looked at his face and spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.31.8 \|\|

*bharadvāja uvāca \|*  
*tvamarjuna mahābāho kauravānvayapāvanaḥ \|*  
*viśeṣānmama mānyo'si dharmaputrānujo yataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

Bharadvāja said:

8\. O mighty-armed Arjuna, you are the sanctifier of the family of Kurus. You are specially worthy of my honour because you are the younger brother of Dharmaputra.

## \|\| 1.31.9 \|\|

*aneke bhūmipā dṛṣṭā na te tvamiva phālguna \|*  
*līlārjavadayaudāryadhairyagāmbhīryaśālinaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Many kings have been seen (by me), but, O Phālguna, they are not endowed with grace, rectitude, kindness, liberalmindedness, courage and sagacity like you.

## \|\| 1.31.10 \|\|

*kulaṃ vidyā dhanaṃ caiva balināṃ madakāraṇam \|*  
*bhavādṛśānāṃ bhavyānāṃ tāni praśrayakāraṇam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Nobility (of birth), learning and affluence are (usually) the cause of haughtiness in strong men. But in the case of excellent persons like you they are the cause of (greater) modesty and courteousness.

## \|\| 1.31.11 \|\|

*prājyeṣu rājyabhogeṣu vidyamāneṣu kaurava \|*  
*ṛte bhavantaṃ ko vānyo nopaiti vikṛtervaśam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. In spite of the abundant pleasures and vast kingdom, O descendant of Kura, who else other than you can resist the tendency to deviate from normal decency?

## \|\| 1.31.12 \|\|

*paravānasmi kaunteya guṇailākottaraistava \|*  
*kimastyakathanīyaṃ te kautukopetamānasa \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O son of Kuntī, I am overcome by your extraordinary good qualities. What is it that should not be disclosed to you, O (noble one) with a mind full of such keen curiosity?

## \|\| 1.31.13 \|\|

*śṛṇu rājankathāṃ divyāṃ mayā munimukhācchutām \|*  
*yāṃ śrutvā pātakātaṅkānmucyante sarvajantavaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O king, listen to the divine story heard by me from a sage. On hearing this story all creatures are liberated from the afflictions born of sins.

\[Story of Śaṅkara’s Marriage as Narrated by Bharadvāja\]:—

## \|\| 1.31.14 \|\|

*atha bharadvājakathita śaṃkaravivāhaprakriyā \|*  
*pūrvaṃ dākṣāyaṇī devī janakenāvamānitā \|*  
*tyaktvā tanuṃ tāṃ nīhāragirerabhavadātmajā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Formerly the Goddess, the daughter of Dakṣa, was subjected to insult by her father. After forsaking that body she became the daughter of the Snow-clad Mountain (Himālaya).

## \|\| 1.31.15 \|\|

*saptarṣibhirupāgamya prārthito dharaṇīdharaḥ \|*  
*mṛtyuṃjayāya svāṃ putrīṃ vivāhe dātumudyataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The Mountain (Himālaya) was approached and requested by the Seven Sages. Hence he was ready to give his daughter in marriage to Mṛtyuñjaya (Śiva).

## \|\| 1.31.16 \|\|

*vṛṣabhāṃko jagatsvāmī vivoḍhuṃ sarvamaṃgalām \|*  
*prāpto himavadāvāsamoṣadhīprasthanāmakam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The Bull-emblemed Lord of the universe came to the residence of Himavān, named Oṣadhīprastha, in order to marry Sarvamaṅgalā (Pārvatī).

## \|\| 1.31.17 \|\|

*tacchāsanātsamājagmuḥ sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca \|*  
*bhūtāni bhūtanāthasya kalyāṇamabhinaṃditum \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. At his bidding all the living beings, both mobile and immobile, came there to rejoice in the felicity and prosperity of the Lord of Bhūtas (goblins).

## \|\| 1.31.18 \|\|

*tadbhūribhārasaṃbhagnā bhūmiruttarasaṃśrayā \|*  
*nimnatāmāyayau tāvadyāvatpātālamāsthitā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The earth in the northern region became heavily burdened with their weight and caved in to such an extent that it reached the nether worlds.

## \|\| 1.31.19 \|\|

*nirbhāralāghavādasmādbhṛśaṃ dakṣiṇagāminī \|*  
*ūrdhvaṃ gatā ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā sarveṣāmabhavadbhayam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The southern region became very light because there was no burden on it. Hence it went up, on seeing which everyone became frightened.

## \|\| 1.31.20 \|\|

*jñātvā tāṃ vikṛtiṃ bhūmerdṛṣṭvāgastyaṃmaheśvaraḥ \|*  
*ita ehi mahāprājñetyuktvā vacanamabravīt \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On realising this change in the position of the earth, Maheśvara turned towards Agastya and said, “Come here, O highly intelligent one.” Then he spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.31.21-22 \|\|

*āgateṣu samasteṣu bhūteṣvatra vasundharā \|*  
*tadbhāreṇa samākrāntā vikṛtiṃ samupāgatā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tadbhuvaḥ sāmyakaraṇe tvamarhasi mahāmate \|*  
*ṛte tvāmatra hi tvattaḥ pareṇaitatkathaṃ bhavet \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. “Since all the Bhūtas have come down here, the earth has become over-burdened by their weight. It has undergone a great alteration. Hence it behoves you, O highly intelligent one, to level up the earth. How can this be done by anyone other than you?

## \|\| 1.31.23 \|\|

*mattejaḥsaṃbhavo hi tvaṃ lokasaṃrakṣaṇodyataḥ \|*  
*tasmānmadvacanādvatsa bhuvametāṃ samīkuru \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Indeed you are born of my splendour. You are engaged in the protection of the worlds. Hence, O my dear one, at my instance level up this earth.

## \|\| 1.31.24-26 \|\|

*matpāṇigrahaṇāllokakautukāyattabuddhiṣu \|*  
*āgateṣu samasteṣu sthātavyaṃ bhavatā'pi ca \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tvaṃ na tiṣṭhasi cedatra na kaścidvikṛtiṃ bhuvaḥ \|*  
*apanetuṃ hi śaknoti tadgantavyaṃ tvayānagha \|\| 25 \|\|*

*imāṃ girisutāpāṇigrahakalyāṇabhāsurām \|*  
*mūrtiṃ pradarśayiṣyāmi yatra tiṣṭhasi tatra te \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. You must not stay here among all those persons who have come down here eager to witness my marriage celebration. If you stay here, no one will be competent to set right the change in the level of the earth. Hence, O sinless one, you must go. Wherever you stay, I shall reveal unto you this form of mine resplendent in my marriage with the daughter of the Mountain.”

\[Agastya’s Departure to the South of the Himālaya for the Levelling of the Earth\]:—

## \|\| 1.31.27 \|\|

*atha bhūsāmyakaraṇāyāgastyasya himādrerdakṣiṇadiggamanam \|*  
*ityuktvā taṃ pariṣvajya visasarja maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tatheti praṇamyāsau yayau yāmyāṃ diśaṃ muniḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. After saying this Maheśvara embraced him and bade farewell to him. Saying “So be it”, the sage bowed down to him and went in the direction of South.

## \|\| 1.31.28 \|\|

*vindhyādriṃ samatikramya dakṣiṇāmāgate diśam \|*  
*agastye muniśārdūle mahī sāmyamupāyayau \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. When Agastya, a tiger among sages, went to the southern region after crossing the Vindhya mountain, the earth became level.

## \|\| 1.31.29 \|\|

*bhuvo'panīya vikṛtiṃ sthitaṃ kalaśajaṃ munim \|*  
*tuṣṭuvurharṣataralāḥ suragandharvakinnarāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Suras, Gandharvas and Kinnaras experienced the thrill of delight (at it) and eulogized the Pot-born Sage who stayed on there (even) after removing the imbalance of the earth.

## \|\| 1.31.30 \|\|

*sa dadarśa tato gatvā kaścicchailaṃ samunnatam \|*  
*vitatairdharaṇīṃ pādairdhṛtvā saṃsthitamagrataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. He then proceeded from that place and saw a lofty mountain standing upright in front of him, sustaining the earth by means of its extensive foothills.

## \|\| 1.31.31 \|\|

*iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe veṃkaṭācalamāhātmye suvarṇamukharīmāhātmyapraśaṃsāyāmarjunabharadvājasaṃvāde śaṃkaravivāhāgastyadakṣiṇadiggamanavarṇananāmaikatriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. It appeared like a veritable mine of great medicinal herbs and all types of gems and jewels, all with unimpaired brilliance and created by the Self-born Lord (Brahmā).

## \|\| 1.31.32 \|\|

*samunnatairyaḥ śikharairnipatadvyomabhūtale \|*  
*udāradhārāsaṃpannairdadhātīva nirantaram \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. By means of its lofty peaks having extensive currents of water it appeared to hold up the sky permanently (preventing it from) falling upon the earth.

## \|\| 1.31.33 \|\|

*śanairāruhya taṃ śailamagastyo munipuṃgavaḥ \|*  
*nivāsāya matiṃ cakre ramye tacchikharasthale \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Agastya, the eminent sage, slowly climbed up the mountain and decided to reside in the beautiful region of its summit.

## Chapter 32 - The Birth of Suvarṇamukharī

## \|\| 1.32.1 \|\|

*atha nadyutpādanāyāgastvaṃ prati aśarīryuktiḥ \|*  
*bharadvāja uvāca \|*  
*sa kadācinmunivaraḥ kṛtapaurvāhnikakriyaḥ \|*  
*viveśa devatāgāraṃ samārādhayituṃ śivam \|\| 1 \|\|*

\[An Etherial Voice Urges Agastya to Cause a River to Flow There\]:—

Bharadvāja said:

1\. Once that excellent sage concluded the holy rites of forenoon and entered the temple to propitiate Siva.

## \|\| 1.32.2 \|\|

*adṛśyarūpā vāgdevī tatrāśrāvi mahātmanā \|*  
*tenādbhutopapannena vyaktavarṇasamujjvalā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The Goddess of Speech of invisible form brilliantly revealed herself in clear syllables and it was heard by that noble-souled sage equipped with wonderful (power).

## \|\| 1.32.3-8 \|\|

*ākāśavāṇyuvācainamagastyaṃ japatāṃ varam \|*  
*nadīhīno hyayaṃ deśaḥ prasiddho'pi na śobhate \|\| 3 \|\|*

*jñānavijñānavimukhaḥ sākāra iva bhūsuraḥ \|*  
*dīkṣeva dakṣiṇāhīnā jyotsnāhīneva śarvarī \|\| 4 \|\|*

*na vibhāti nadīhīnā pṛthvīyaṃ bhūsurottama \|*  
*pravartaya nadīṃ kāñcillokānāṃ hitakāmyayā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*agādhaduritodbhūtabhītimocanaśālinīm \|*  
*hitametatsuraughānāmetanmunivarārthitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*bhadrametanmanuṣyāṇāmetadācara suvrata \|*  
*devānāmṛṣivaryāṇāṃ bhūjanānāṃ hitāvahām \|\| 7 \|\|*

*pāpapaṃkapraśamanīṃ pravartaya mahānadīm \|\| 8 \|\|*

3-8. The etherial voice spoke to Agastya, the most excellent one among those who performed Japa:

“Indeed this land devoid of a river does not look nice, although it is famous. (It is) like a Brāhmaṇa who is averse to knowledge and wisdom, though he may have (Brāhmaṇical) features; (or) like the initiation (in a holy rite) without monetary gifts; (or) like the night without moonlight.

O excellent Brāhmaṇa, this piece of land without a river does not appear splendid. With a desire for the welfare of all the worlds, cause a river to flow.

It shall have power to release (everyone) from the fear arising from great sins. This is conducive to the welfare of multitude of Devas. This is what is sought by excellent sages. This is beneficial to human beings. Kindly do this, O sage of good holy rites. Cause a great river to flow—a river that is conducive to the welfare of Devas, excellent sages and people of the earth, a river that will destroy the mire of sins.”

Śrī Bharadvāja continued:

## \|\| 1.32.9 \|\|

*śrībharadvāja uvāca \|*  
*tadākarṇya vaco vipraḥ kṣaṇaṃ cintāparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*samāpya devatāpūjāṃ bahirvedyāmupāviśat \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On hearing those words the Brāhmaṇa became engrossed in thought for a short while. After concluding the worship of the deity he came to the quadrangular spot in the courtyard and sat there.

## \|\| 1.32.10-12 \|\|

*ānāyayāmāsa tadā tadāśramagatānmunīn \|*  
*teṣāmakathayaccāsau divyavāṇīritaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tadadbhutamupaśrutya munayo hṛṣṭamānasāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*abhivandya muniśreṣṭhaṃ maitrāvaruṇimabruvan \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. He then brought together all those sages residing in that hermitage. To them he related the utterance made by the Divine Speech.

On hearing that wonderful utterance the sages became delighted in their minds. After saluting Maitrāvaruṇi (Agastya), the excellent sage, they spoke (these words):

\[The Great Sages Request Agastya to Create Suvarṇamukharī\]:—

## \|\| 1.32.13 \|\|

*atha suvarṇamukharyutpādanāyāgastyaṃ prati maharṣiprārthanā \|*  
*munaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*āścaryāṇāṃ mahāścaryaṃ maṃgalānāṃ ca maṃgalam \|*  
*tavaiva śobhate divyaṃ tvaccaritraṃ kṛpānidhe \|\| 13 \|\|*

The sages said:

13\. O storehouse of mercy, your acts are divine and splendid. Your life is the greatest wonder of all wonderful mysteries. It is the most auspicious of all auspicious things.

## \|\| 1.32.14 \|\|

*tava huṃkāramātreṇa bhraṣṭo devādhirājyataḥ \|*  
*nahuṣaḥ kīṭatāṃ prāpa tataścitraṃ na vidyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Merely by your Huṃkāra (i.e. a noisy grunt of anger) Nahuṣa was brought down from the overlordship of Devas. He then attained the state of a worm. There is nothing more wonderful than that.

## \|\| 1.32.15 \|\|

*samāvṛtadharācakraḥ kallolātāḍitāmbaraḥ \|*  
*kiṃ nvato vidyate citraṃ yadabdhiśculakīkṛtaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Is there anything more wonderful than that (by you) the entire ocean was made a mouthful of water, the ocean that encircles the whole of the earth and strikes the sky with its waves?

## \|\| 1.32.16 \|\|

*sūryamārganirodhārthaṃ pravṛtto vindhyabhūdharaḥ \|*  
*tvayā praśāṃtiṃ gamitaḥ kiṃ nvato vidyate param \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The Vindhya mountain that attempted to obstruct the path of the Sun was subdued by you. What can be greater than this?

## \|\| 1.32.17 \|\|

*tavādbhutāni karmāṇi kaḥ stotuṃ prabhavedbhuvi \|*  
*manmahābhāgyayogāttvaṃ prāpto'sīti śarīritām \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Who is competent to praise adequately your wonderful activities on the earth? It is by my (our?) good luck that you have come here in this embodied form.

## \|\| 1.32.18 \|\|

*vayaṃ kṛtārthāḥ saṃjātāstrailokye yanmahāmune \|*  
*nivasāmo'tra bhavatā sanāthā hyāśramasthale \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. We have become the greatest of all blessed ones in the three worlds, O great sage, that we stay here iṇ the precincts of this hermitage with you as our leader and guide.

## \|\| 1.32.19 \|\|

*varṇyo hi yāmyato dūre viṣayo'yaṃ dvijottama \|*  
*samastavastupūrṇopi nadīhīno na rājate \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. (Defective Text) Though this land is worthy of being praised, it is far from being excellent, O excellent Brāhmaṇa. Though it is full of all (desired) objects, it does not shine, as it is devoid of a river.

## \|\| 1.32.20 \|\|

*kimalabdhanadīsnānenā'munā hatajanmanā \|*  
*anadīke janapade vāsādajananaṃ varam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Of what avail is this damned life that has not obtained the opportunity to bathe in a river? Not being born at all is far better than residing in a land without a river.

## \|\| 1.32.21 \|\|

*paripākastu bhāgyānāmasmākaṃ samupasthitaḥ \|*  
*yadādiṣṭosi vibudhaiḥ pravartaya mahānadīm \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The time of fructification of our fortune is imminent, since you have been directed by Devas to cause the great river to flow.

## \|\| 1.32.22 \|\|

*pravartitāyāṃ deśesminmahānadyāṃ tavānagha \|*  
*kadā nu khalu yāsyāmaḥ kṛtasnānā kṛtārthatām \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. When will we take our holy bath, and be blessed, in the great river caused to flow by you in this land, O sinless one?

## \|\| 1.32.23 \|\|

*kiṃ vitarkeṇa bahunā prayatnaḥ kriyatāṃ dhuvam \|*  
*samānetuṃ jagadvandyāṃ śaraṇyāṃ sariduttamām \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Of what avail is much conjecturing and deliberation? Let the endeavour be made certainly to bring down the excellent river that is worthy of taking refuge in and that should be saluted by the entire universe.

## \|\| 1.32.24 \|\|

*śrībharadvāja uvāca \|*  
*sa teṣāṃ vacanaṃ hṛdyaṃ mānayitvā mahādvijaḥ \|*  
*samāneṣyāmi saritamiti cakre viniścayam \|\| 24 \|\|*

Śrī Bharadvāja said:

24\. That great Brāhmaṇa honoured their sincere words (of request) and made the resolve, ‘I will bring the river’.

\[Agastya’s Penance for Making Suvarṇamukharī Flow Out\]:—

## \|\| 1.32.25-26 \|\|

*atha suvarṇamukharyāvirbhāvāyāgastyakṛtatapaḥprakāraḥ \|*  
*munīśvarairanujñātastānabhyarcya surānapi \|*  
*viśeṣapūjāṃ vidhivadvidhāya puravidviṣaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*aṃgīkṛtya vrataṃ gāḍhaṃ bahulakleśaduḥsaham \|*  
*ananyasulabhaṃ yatnātsa cakāra mahattapaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. He was (formally) accorded permission by the eminent sages. He worshipped Suras after performing a special worship of Śiva. He undertook an intensive observance of holy rites, unbearable on account of the excessive strain involved. With a great effort he performed a very severe penance (which is) not at all easy for anyone else.

## \|\| 1.32.27 \|\|

*ghoreṣu gharmadivaseṣvantarastho havirbhujām \|*  
*caturṇāṃ savitṛnyastadṛṣṭirnāpayayau klamam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. During the hot and fierce days of summer he stayed in the midst of four fires with his eyes fixed on the Sun. Still he did not experience any strain or fatigue.

## \|\| 1.32.28 \|\|

*vārṣikeṣu dineṣūgravāyusampātaduḥsahaiḥ \|*  
*āsāraistāḍyamāno'pi nodvegamagamaddhṛdi \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. During rainy days he was lashed at by torrential downpours of rains accompanied by unbearable violent gusts of wind. Yet he did not feel disturbed in the heart.

## \|\| 1.32.29 \|\|

*hemante samaye tiṣṭhankaṇṭhadaghneṣu vāriṣu \|*  
*japadhyānaparo bhūtvā na kiñcidvikṛtiṃ yayau \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. During early winter he stood in the waters coming up to his neck and proceeded ahead with his Japa and meditation. Yet there was no change in his (steadiness or mental peace).

## \|\| 1.32.30 \|\|

*tataḥ samīhitārthasya vilambamavalokya saḥ \|*  
*punargāḍhatarāṃ niṣṭhāṃ prapede lokabhīṣaṇām \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. On realizing that there was delay in achieving what he desired, he adopted a procedure still more intense, that terrified all the worlds.

## \|\| 1.32.31 \|\|

*nigṛhya mānasīṃ vṛttiṃ nirāhāro jitendriyaḥ \|*  
*avijñātabahirvṛttistasthau pāṣāṇavattadā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. He controlled all his mental activities. He abstained from taking food. He conquered his sense organs. Without being conscious of external (world) he stood like a stone.

## \|\| 1.32.32 \|\|

*iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīveṃkaṭācalamāhātmye śrīsuvarṇamukharīmāhātmyapraśaṃsāyāṃ suvarṇamukharyāvirbhāvavarṇanaṃnāma dvātriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. While he was thus engaged in penance, a terrible fire sprang up from all his limbs. Blazing with furious flames it scraped the sky.

## \|\| 1.32.33 \|\|

*tato'dbhutaśikhājālairāvṛtāḥ sarvato diśaḥ \|*  
*samudagrabhayodvignā janaughāḥ paricukruśuḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. All the quarters were covered with mysteriously wonderful clusters of flames. Greatly tormented by fear multitudes of people cried out.

## \|\| 1.32.34 \|\|

*tadā tathāvidhaṃ ghoraṃ jagatsaṃkṣobhamāgatam \|*  
*devā vijñāpayāmāsurnamaskṛtyābjajanmane \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. After bowing down to him Devas informed the Lotus-born One about such a terribly great agitation of the whole universe that had taken place.

\[Arrival of the Four-Faced Lord to the Hermitage of Agastya\]:—

## \|\| 1.32.35 \|\|

*athāgastyāśramaṃ prati caturmukhāgamanam \|*  
*tānāśvāsya tato brahmā siddhagandharvasevitaḥ \|*  
*prādurāsītkumbhabhuvaḥ purobhāge tapasyataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Brahmā reassured them. He was attended upon by Siddhas and Gandharvas. He appeared in front of the Pot-born Sage who was engaged in penance.

## \|\| 1.32.36 \|\|

*tamāgataṃ samālokya brahmāṇaṃ paramaṃ dvijaḥ \|*  
*praṇamya vividhaiḥ stotraistoṣayāmāsa tanmanāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. On. seeing that Brahmā the great (Lord) had come, the Brāhmaṇa bowed to him. With his mind fixed on him alone he propitiated him with different kinds of hymns and prayers.

## \|\| 1.32.37 \|\|

*tatastaṃ vinayānamramagastyaṃ vīkṣya padmabhūḥ \|*  
*prasādasumukho bhūtvā pūtāṃ giramupādade \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Then looking at Agastya who bowed to him humbly, the Lotus-born Lord, with his countenance beaming with great delight, spoke these sacred words:

## \|\| 1.32.38 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*parituṣṭo'smi tapasā duścareṇa tavānagha \|*  
*vṛṇīṣva yadyadiṣṭaṃ te tattaddāsyāmi suvrata \|\| 38 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

38\. O sinless one, I am highly pleased with your penance (which is) very difficult to be performed. Choose your boon. O (sage) of good holy rites, I shall grant you whatever is desired by you.

## \|\| 1.32.39 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*tava prasādātsakalamupapannaṃ mama prabho \|*  
*saṃprayacchasi cetkāmaṃ yāce niḥśaṃkayā dhiyā \|\| 39 \|\|*

Agastya said:

39\. By your favour, O Lord, everything is readily accomplished by me. If you desire to give me whatever I wish, I beg for this unhesitatingly.

## \|\| 1.32.40 \|\|

*nadīhīnamimaṃ deśaṃ dṛṣṭvā khidyati me manaḥ \|*  
*arthāvavodharahitaṃ śrutipāṭhamivādhikam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. On seeing this region devoid of a river my mind is pained as (it would be) at the repetition of the Vedic passages almost without understanding the meaning.

## \|\| 1.32.41 \|\|

*urvīṃ pāvayituṃ dakṣāṃ rakṣituṃ ca mahānadīm \|*  
*prasādaṃ kuru deveśa mameṣṭamidameva hi \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O Lord of Devas, be pleased to grant a great river that has power to sanctify and protect the earth. This alone is what I desire.

\[At the Request of Agastya the Four-Faced Lord Urges Gaṅgā\]:—

## \|\| 1.32.42 \|\|

*athāgastyaprārthanayā gaṅgāṃ prati caturmukhacodanā \|*  
*śrībharadvāja uvāca \|*  
*agastyasya vacaḥ śrutvā bhūyādevamiti bruvan \|*  
*sasmāra manasā brahmā suravartmāśrayāṃ nadīm \|\| 42 \|\|*

Śrī Bharadvāja said:

42\. On hearing the words of Agastya Brahmā said: “It will so happen.” He then remembered the river flowing through the celestial path (i.e. Gaṅgā).

## \|\| 1.32.43 \|\|

*athopetya viyadgaṃgā purastātparameṣṭhinaḥ \|*  
*atiṣṭhanmukuṭanyastapraśastāñjalibhāsurā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Then the celestial Gaṅgā appeared and stood in front of Brahmā resplendent with her crown and palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 1.32.44 \|\|

*svaśāsanātsamāyātāṃ vinayānatamastakām \|*  
*tāṃ sarvajagatāṃ dhātrīmidaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Brahmā then spoke these words to that mother of all the worlds who had come to him at his bidding and (stood there) with the head bent down in humility.

## \|\| 1.32.45 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*gaṃge mayānuśāsyāsi kārye lokopakārake \|*  
*tavāpi lokarakṣāyāṃ mameva niyatā sthitiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

45\. O Gaṅgā, you have to be directed by me in a matter that is helpful to all the worlds. Like me you too invariably stand ready in all matters concerning the protection of the worlds.

## \|\| 1.32.46 \|\|

*deśe nadīvihīne'tra pravartayitumāpagām \|*  
*hitārthaṃ sarvalokānāṃ kumbhajanmā samīhate \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The Pot-born Sage wishes to cause the flow of a river for the sake of the welfare of all the worlds in this land devoid of rivers.

## \|\| 1.32.47 \|\|

*tasmāttvamavatīryorvīṃ svāṃśenaikena bhūjanān \|*  
*punīhi gaccha vasudhāmetaddarśitavartmanā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Hence you descend down to the earth. Sanctify the people of the earth with a portion of yours. You go to the earth by the path pointed out to you by this (sage).

## \|\| 1.32.48 \|\|

*bhūloke saṃpravṛtte tu pravāhe siddhikāṃkṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*seviṣyante suravarā munivaryāśca saṃtatam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. When the current of water begins to flow in the terrestrial world, all those who desire for spiritual achievement, the excellent Suras and the leading sages will resort to it.

## \|\| 1.32.49 \|\|

*nadīṣūttamatāṃ yāhi trāhi tvatsaṃśrayāñjanān \|*  
*kuru priyamagastyasya gaccha bhadre yathāsukham \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Be the most excellent one among (all) the rivers; protect the people resorting to you; do what is pleasing to Agastya. O gentle one, go ahead happily.

## \|\| 1.32.50 \|\|

*bharadvāja uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvāntardadhe brahmā tayā nadyā ca tena ca \|*  
*praṇāmapūjanastotrairviśeṣairabhinanditaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

Bharadvāja said:

50\. After saying this, Brahmā vanished. He was specially honoured and adored by that river and that (sage) by obeisance, veneration and eulogies.

\[In the Presence of Agastya Gaṅgā Accepts the Responsibility of Causing the Flow of a River as Her own Part\]:—

## \|\| 1.32.51 \|\|

*athāgastyasamīpe svāṃśatvena gaṃgākṛtanadyutpattyabhyupagamaḥ \|*  
*atha gaṃgā munipateḥ purastātsvāṃśasaṃbhavām \|*  
*divyatejomayīṃ mūrtiṃ darśayitvā vaco'bravīt \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Then Gaṅgā revealed in front of the eminent sage a divinely resplendent form born of her own part and spoke these words:

## \|\| 1.32.52 \|\|

*gaṃgovāca \|*  
*madīyāṃśo'yamavanīṃ saṃprāpya munivallabha \|*  
*pūrayiṣyati te'bhīṣṭaṃ nadīrūpaṃ samāśritaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

Gaṅgā said:

52\. O dear sage, a part of mine will come to the earth after assuming the form of a river and will fulfil your desire.

## \|\| 1.32.53 \|\|

*bharadvāja uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā siddhavāhinyāṃ gatāyāṃ tatprayuktayā \|*  
*gantavyaṃ vartmanā kenetyukto muniruvāca tām \|\| 53 \|\|*

Bharadvāja said:

53\. After saying this the heavenly river went away. The river urged by Gaṅgā asked the sage, “Which way should we go?” The sage replied to her:

## Chapter 33 - The Efficacy of Suvarṇamukharī

## \|\| 1.33.1-2 \|\|

*atha suvarṇamukharīṃ prati śakrādistutiḥ \|*  
*bharadvāja uvāca \|*  
*tadā divyavimānasthāḥ śakramukhyā divaukasaḥ \|*  
*agastyamanuyāntīṃ tāmanujagmurmahāpagām \|\| 1 \|\|*

*navāvatārāṃ tāṃ divyāṃ sarve ca munipuṃgavāḥ \|*  
*kṛtāñjalipuṭāḥ stotrairanuyātāḥ siṣevire \|\| 2 \|\|*

\[Śakra and Others Eulogize Suvarṇamukharī\]:—

Bharadvāja said:

1-2. Then the Heaven-dwellers, the chief of whom was Śakra, seated in the divine aerial chariots, followed that great river which followed Agastya. With the palms joined in reverence all the great sages followed that divine river that had newly descended and attended upon her with prayers.

## \|\| 1.33.3-4 \|\|

*siddhacāraṇagandharvāḥ saṃbhṛtāśca sahasraśa \|*  
*tāṃ nadīṃ taṃ munīndraṃ ca praśaśaṃsuḥ śubhaiḥstavaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*sudhopamānamamalaṃ diṣṭyā labdhamidaṃ jalam \|*  
*ityautsukyarasāyattā nanandurdharaṇījanāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Siddhas, Cāraṇas and Gandharvas who had gathered together in thousands, praised that eminent sage and that river with splendid hymns.

## \|\| 1.33.5 \|\|

*tadā nideśāddevasya padmayoneḥ samīraṇaḥ \|*  
*śṛṇvatāṃ sarvadevānāmidaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 5 \|\|*

The people of the earth eagerly said: “Fortunately this water that is free from impurities and comparable to nectar has been obtained.” They expressed their delight and enthusiasm thus.

5\. At the bidding of the Lotus-born Lord, the Wind-god spoke these words within the hearing of all the Devas:

\[The Derivation of the Name Suvarṇamukharī as Explained by the Wind-Goo (Vāyu)\]:—

## \|\| 1.33.6 \|\|

*atha vāyukathitasuvarṇamukharīnāmaniṣpattiḥ \|*
