## \|\| 3.5.60-61 \|\|

*bhikṣukāṇāṃ phalāvāptirviśeṣādiha kīrtyate \|*  
*vedāṃtaśravaṇātpuṇyaṃ daśadhā yatprakīrtitam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*badarī dṛṣṭimātreṇa bhikṣukāṇāṃ tadiṣyate \|*  
*cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa kaivalyaphalabhāginaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

60-61. The acquisition of merits by mendicants here is particularly glorified. Merely by seeing Badarī mendicants acquire ten times the merit usually obtained by listening to the Vedanta. During Cāturmāsya they derive particularly the benefit of salvation.

## \|\| 3.5.62 \|\|

*nyāsino badarīsthāne vināyāsena putraka \|*  
*ye mūrkhā jāḍyamāpannā dambhakāṣāyavāsasaḥ \|*  
*badarīdarśanātteṣāṃ muktiḥ karatale sthitā \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Those who renounce (i.e. become Sannyāsins), O dear son, in the holy place of Badarī, are liberated without strain. Those foolish persons and those who are insentient, those hyprocrites who wear ochre robes—all these can have salvation within their reach.

## \|\| 3.5.63 \|\|

*jñānino'jñānino vāpi nyāsino niyatavratā \|*  
*draṣṭavyā badarī taistu phalāni samabhīpsubhiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Whether they are persons of knowledge or not, whether they are renouncers or men of holy observances, Badarī should be visisted by all those who are desirous of obtaining benefits.

## Chapter 6 - The Greatness of Vasudhārā

## \|\| 3.6.1 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*karādvigalitaṃ yatra kapālaṃ te maheśvara \|*  
*tasya tīrthasya māhātmyaṃ kṛpayā vada me pitaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: \[Vasudhārā is\] a waterfall four miles north of Badrīnāth near the village Manal. It is the source of Alakanandā, a tributary of Gaṅgā. (Dc 3, 26)

Skanda asked:

1\. O my father Maheśvara, kindly recount to me the greatness of that Tīrtha where the skull dropped down from your hand.

## \|\| 3.6.2 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*atiguhyamidaṃ tīrthaṃ surāsuranamaskṛtam \|*  
*brahmahā'pi naro yatra snānamātreṇa śuddhyati \|\| 2 \|\|*

Jaimini said:

2\. This Tīrtha is a great secret. It is bowed down to by Suras and Asuras. Merely by bathing therein even a man guilty of the murder of a Brāhmaṇa becomes purified.

## \|\| 3.6.3 \|\|

*paṃca tīrthāni tiṣṭhaṃti kapāle pāpamocane \|*  
*tatra snānaṃ tapo dānaṃ sarvamakṣayamiṣyate \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. There are five Tīrthas in the holy place named Kapālamocana

which rids one of all the sins. Penance, charitable gifts and holy ablution therein (the merit accrued from) everything is expected to be inexhaustible.

## \|\| 3.6.4 \|\|

*piṃḍaṃ vidhāya vidhivannarakāttārayetpitṝn \|*  
*pitṛtīrthamidaṃ proktaṃ gayāto'ṣṭaguṇādhikam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. By making rice-balls duly (and offering them to Pitṛs) one can redeem the Pitṛs from hell. This is called Pitṛtīrtha, eight times more meritorious than Gayā.

## \|\| 3.6.5 \|\|

*tilatarppaṇato yāṃti pitaraḥ svargamuttamam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. By the libation of water and gingelly seeds, the Pitṛs go to the excellent heaven.

## \|\| 3.6.6 \|\|

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe badarikāśramamāhātmye śivakārttikeyasaṃvāde vasudhārātīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma ṣaṣṭho'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. If the devotee is steadily engaged in Japa day and night with concentration and mental purity, the fulfilment of his desire shall be great and instantaneous.

## \|\| 3.6.7 \|\|

*pāralaukikakarmāṇi sarvāṇyavyāhatāni ca \|*  
*kapālamocane tīrthe nādhikaṃ pitṛkarmaṇi \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. All the holy rites pertaining to the other world are unobstructed in the Tīrtha called Kapālamocana. Nothing more remains to be done about Pitṛs.

## \|\| 3.6.8 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*kutra vā brahmatīrthaṃ vai phalaṃ vā kīdṛśaṃ bhavet \|*  
*ke vā tatra vasaṃtīha kṛpayā vada me pitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

Skanda said:

8\. Where is this Brahmatīrtha? Of what sort is its benefit? Who stay there? Kindly recount this to me, O father.

## \|\| 3.6.9-10 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*ekadā viṣṇunābhyambhoruhasthasya prajāpateḥ \|*  
*vedānmukhāṃbujāddhṛtvā jagmaturmadhukaiṭabhau \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tato hyutthāya śayanātsisṛkṣurabjasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*sraṣṭuṃ vinā'gamaṃ loke na śaśāka hṛtasmṛtiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

Śiva said:

9-10. Once Madhu and Kaiṭabha carried away the Vedas from the lotus-like mouth of Prajāpati who was stationed in the lotus coming out through the navel of Viṣṇu. They went away. Then the Lotus-born Lord got up from his bed and was desirous of creating (the universe). But without the Vedas he could not create the world. His power of memory was affected.

## \|\| 3.6.11 \|\|

*tadā badarikāmetya hariṇā pratipālitām \|*  
*tuṣṭāva praṇato bhūtvā bhagavaṃtaṃ sanātanam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then he came to Badarikā guarded by Han. Bending his head down, he eulogized the eternal Lord.

## \|\| 3.6.12-14 \|\|

*tataḥ kuṃḍātsamudbhūto hayaśīrṣo nijāyudhaḥ \|*  
*pītāṃbaradharaḥ śuklaścaturbāhuḥ sudṛptadṛk \|\| 12 \|\|*

*atyadbhutaḥ prakaṭakaṭhoralocanaścalacchaṭāvicchuritameghaḍaṃbaraḥ \|*  
*svatejasā hatanikhilaprabhākulaḥ kṛpānvito druhiṇapuraḥsaro'bhavat \|\| 13 \|\|*

*nirīkṣya taṃ vidhirapi vismayākulaḥ praṇamya ca stutimakarotprasannadṛk \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. Then, from the holy pit rose up the horse-headed Lord equipped with his own weapons. He was clad in yellow robes. He was white in complexion. He had four arms and very proud eyes. He was very wonderful in his features, with prominently keen eyes. He resembled a cloud tinged with moving lustre. By his own refulgence he had subdued all sorts of lustres. Endowed with mercy he appeared in front of Brahmā. On seeing him Brahmā became agitated with surprise. With his delight evident in his eyes he bowed down and eulogized him.

## \|\| 3.6.15 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*namaḥ kamalanābhāya namaste kamalāśraya \|*  
*namaste kamalāvāsaviśālavanamāline \|\| 15 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

15\. Obeisance to you having the lotus in your navel. Bow to you, O support of Kamalā (Goddess of fortune). Obeisance to you, O abode of Kamalā. Salute to the Lord wearing a large garland of sylvan flowers.

## \|\| 3.6.16 \|\|

*namo vijñānabhātrāya guhāvāsa nivāsine \|*  
*hṛṣīkeśāya śāṃtāya tubhyaṃ bhagavate namaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Obeisance to the Lord of the nature of pure knowledge, to the Lord residing in his abode in the cavity (hearts of all beings); obeisance to you, to Lord Hṛṣīkeśa, the calm one.

## \|\| 3.6.17 \|\|

*svabhaktarakṣaṇakṛte dhṛtadehāya śārṅgiṇe \|*  
*anaṃtakleśanāśāya gadine brahmaṇe namaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Salute to the Lord who have assumed many bodies for the sake of protecting your own devotees, to the wielder of the Śārṅga bow; obeisance to Brahman, to the wielder of the iron club for destroying infinite pain (of devotees).

## \|\| 3.6.18 \|\|

*saṃsāravividhāsāranivṛttikṛtakarmaṇe \|*  
*rakṣitre sarvajaṃtūnāṃ viṣṇave jiṣṇave namaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Obeisance to the victorious Viṣṇu, to the protector of all creatures, to the Lord who engage yourself in various activities to stop the worthless worldly existence(?).

## \|\| 3.6.19 \|\|

*namo viśvaṃbharāśeṣanivṛttaguṇavṛttaye \|*  
*surāsuravarastaṃbhanivṛttisthitikīrtaye \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O Lord supporting the universe, obeisance to you from whom all the activities of the Guṇas have receded, O Lord, the excellent supporting pillar of Suras and Asuras; obeisance to you, the cause of recession, sustenance and renown?

## \|\| 3.6.20 \|\|

*itīritaḥ surapatinā maheśvaro hṛdisthito'khilavidaśeṣakarmabhiḥ \|*  
*tato'ntaraṃ sapadi gato nibadhya tau suradruhau kila nijaghāna līlayā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On being praised thus by the Lord of Suras, the great Īśvara who is stationed in the heart and who knows everything along with all activities, came in between those demons suddenly, bound them and killed them sportingly.

## \|\| 3.6.21 \|\|

*tato nigamamādāya brahmaṇoṃ'tikamāyayau \|*  
*dattvā svanigamaṃ tasmai svastho'bhūtsa samīḍitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Thereafter he took the Nigama (Vedas) and came near Brahmā. After giving his own Nigama unto him, he became happy and composed, and was eulogized.

## \|\| 3.6.22 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti tattīrthaṃ brahmaṇā prakaṭīkṛtam \|*  
*brahmakuṃḍamiti khyātaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Ever since then that Tīrtha which was manifested by Brahmā became well-known as Brahmakuṇḍa. It is famous in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 3.6.23 \|\|

*yasya darśanamātreṇa mahāpātakino janāḥ \|*  
*vimuktakilbiṣāḥ sadyo brahmalokaṃ vrajaṃti te \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Merely by visiting it people of great sins become absolved of their sins. They immediately go to the world of Brahmā.

## \|\| 3.6.24 \|\|

*snānaṃ kurvaṃti ye lokā vratacaryāmathāpi vā \|*  
*brahmalokamatikramya viṣṇulokaṃ vrajaṃti te \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Those people who take their holy bath or perform holy rites there, go beyond the world of Brahmā, to that of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 3.6.25 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*tataḥ kimakaroddhātā labdhvā vedāñjanārddanāt \|*  
*etadanyacca sarvaṃ me kṛpayā vada sāṃpratam \|\| 25 \|\|*

Skanda said:

25\. What did Brahmā do after obtaining the Vedas from Janārdana? Kindly recount this and everything else to me now.

Mahādeva narrated:

## \|\| 3.6.26 \|\|

*mahādeva uvāca \|*  
*caturṇāmapi vedānāṃ dṛṣṭvā badarikāśramam \|*  
*matirna jāyate gaṃtuṃ brahmaṇā saha putraka \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Having seen Badarikāśrama, all the four Vedas were not inclined to go along with Brahmā, O dear son.

## \|\| 3.6.27 \|\|

*tatastu vikalaṃ dṛṣṭvā brahmāṇaṃ janavāsinaḥ \|*  
*siddhāstu vidhivatstutvā praṇipatyedamabruvan \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Thereupon Brahmā became depressed. On seeing him so, Siddhas, the residents of Janaloka, duly eulogized, prostrated and spoke thus:

## \|\| 3.6.28 \|\|

*siddhā ūcuḥ \|*  
*ājñā bhagavataḥ kāryā sarvaiḥ sthāvarajaṃgamaiḥ \|*  
*bhagavānsarvajaṃtūnāṃ karttā hartā pitā guruḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

Siddhas said:

28\. The command of the Lord must be earned out by all the beings, mobile and immobile. The Lord is the maker, the annihilator, the father (protector) and the preceptor unto all the creatures.

## \|\| 3.6.29 \|\|

*sthitirbrahmāṃtike vaśca hariṇaivānukalpitā \|*  
*nivṛttirvartate caiṣā tathāpyetannirāmayam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Your stay (residence) near Brahmā has been commanded by Lord Hari himself. There is a way out, still without much of worry.

## \|\| 3.6.30 \|\|

*ekāṃte dravarūpeṇa mūrtirvo'trāvatiṣṭhatām \|*  
*dvitīyā brahmaṇā sārddhaṃ brahmalokaṃ vrajetpunaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. One form of yours should stay here in the liquid form and let the second form go with Brahmā to his world.

## \|\| 3.6.31 \|\|

*tataḥ sahṛdayā vedā dvaidhīkṛtātmarūpakāḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇā brahmalokaṃ te yayuḥ sārddhaṃ praharṣitāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Thereafter, the Vedas with due consideration assumed two forms. They went to the world of Brahmā along with him with great delight.

## \|\| 3.6.32 \|\|

*tatastrilokaṃ vidhivatsasarja caturānanaḥ \|*  
*dravarūpeṣu vedeṣu snānadānatapaḥkriyāḥ \|*  
*kṛtā viccheditā na syuryāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Thereafter, the Four-faced Lord duly created the three worlds. The holy bath, charitable gifts, penances and other holy rites performed in the liquid forms of the Vedas will not be broken or interrupted until the ultimate annihilation of all living beings.

## \|\| 3.6.33 \|\|

*phalamuddiśya kurvaṃti upavāsatrayaṃ narāḥ \|*  
*caturṇāmapi vedānāṃ vyākhyātāro na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Men who observe fast for three days with some benefit in view become undoubtedly the commentators and expounders of the four Vedas.

## \|\| 3.6.34 \|\|

*anukrameṇa tiṣṭhaṃti vedāścatvāra eva ca \|*  
*ṛgyajuḥsāmātharvākhyā bhagavatpārśvavartinaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. All the four Vedas stand in the proper order at the side of the Lord. They are called Ṛk, Yajus, Sāman and Atharvan.

## \|\| 3.6.35 \|\|

*ye puṇyavaṃto'kaluṣā vedavedāṃgapāragāḥ \|*  
*te vedaghoṣaṃ viralāḥ śṛṇvaṃtyapi kalau yuge \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Even in Kaliyuga there are very few people who are meritorious, devoid of sins and masters of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas. Very few of them hear the chanting of the Vedas even.

## \|\| 3.6.36 \|\|

*caturṇāmapi vedānāmudagasti sarasvatī \|*  
*japtātha sā nṛṇāṃ haṃti jaḍatāṃ jalarūpiṇī \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Sarasvatī is above the four Vedas. If her name is repeated frequently, Sarasvatī in the form of water dispels the inertia of men.

## \|\| 3.6.37 \|\|

*sarasvatyā jale sthitvā japaṃ kṛtvā samāhitaḥ \|*  
*manostasya na vicchedaḥ kadācidapi jāyate \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. If a person stands in the waters of Sarasvatī and performs Japa (of a Mantra) with concentration and mental purity, that Mantra will never be broken.

## \|\| 3.6.38 \|\|

*vedavyāso'pi bhagavānyatprasādādudāradhīḥ \|*  
*purāṇasaṃhitārthajño'bhavadatra na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Even the holy lord, sage Vedavyāsa of a liberal mind, became conversant with the import or contents of the Purāṇa collection, by the favour of Sarasvatī.

## \|\| 3.6.39 \|\|

*trayāṇāmapi lokānāṃ hitāya jagatāṃ patiḥ \|*  
*sthāpayāmāsa vidhinā vāṇīṃ vāgvibhavapradām \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. For the welfare of all the three worlds the Lord of the worlds duly established Vāṇī (Goddess of speech) who bestows the (rich) gift of speech.

## \|\| 3.6.40 \|\|

*darśanasparśanasnānapūjāstutyabhivandanaiḥ \|*  
*sarasvatyā na vicchedaḥ kule tasya kadācana \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. If a person visits, touches, takes bath in it, worships it, eulogizes it or rejoices in it, his family will never have separation from Sarasvatī (Learning).

## \|\| 3.6.41 \|\|

*mantrasiddhirviśeṣeṇa sarasvatyāstaṭe nṛṇām \|*  
*japatāmaciraṇaiva jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. If men perform Japas on the banks of Sarasvatī, they will attain perfection in (the employment of) Mantras ere long. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 3.6.42 \|\|

*bahunā kimihoktena vāṇī vāgvibhavapradā \|*  
*dravarūpadharā nṛṇāṃ darśanātpūtirujjvalā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Of what avail is much talk? Vāṇī, having the liquid form (i.e. River Sarasvatī) bestows the gift of speech on men. (Merely) by seeing it, there shall result brilliant (excellent) purification.

## \|\| 3.6.43 \|\|

*tato'rvāgdakṣiṇe bhāge dravadhāreti viśrutam \|*  
*tīrthamiṃdrapadaṃ yatra tapaścakre puraṃdaraḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Behind it on the southern side there is the Tīrtha Indrapada well-known as Dravadhārā, where Indra had performed penance.

## \|\| 3.6.44 \|\|

*sudāruṇaṃ tapaḥ kṛtvā paritoṣya janārddanam \|*  
*padamaiṃdraṃ samālebhe surāsuranamaskṛtam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. After performing a very severe penance, he propitiated Janārdana. Then he obtained the position of Indra bowed to by Suras and Asuras.

## \|\| 3.6.45 \|\|

*tapo dānaṃ japo homo vratāni niyamā yamāḥ \|*  
*tatrānantaguṇaṃ proktaṃ tattīrthamatidurlabham \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Penance, charitable gifts, Homa, holy rites, pious observances and restraints—all these are said to yield merit, multiplied infinite-fold. That Tīrtha is difficult of access.

## \|\| 3.6.46-47 \|\|

*pratimāse trayodaśyāṃ śuklāyāṃ haritoṣaṇe \|*  
*snātvā sutīrthe sutrāmācchandaṃ copetya saṃgataḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*upavāsadvayaṃ kṛtvā pūjayitvā janārddanam \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ śakraloke mahīyate \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. Every month, on the thirteenth day in the bright half, a devotee should take bath in the excellent Tīrtha (named) Haritoṣaṇa. He should approach Sutrāmācchanda in its company(?) He should then fast for two days and worship Janārdana. He shall thereby be liberated and honoured in the world of (Indra).

## \|\| 3.6.48 \|\|

*tatraiva mānasodbhedaḥ sarvapāpapraṇāśanaḥ \|*  
*durlabhaḥ sarvajaṃtūnāṃ yatra te syurmaharṣayaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. There itself is (the holy spot) Mānasodbheda that is destructive of all sins. It is difficult of access to all creatures. There are great sages in that place.

## \|\| 3.6.49 \|\|

*mānasaṃ cidacidgranthimudgrathnaṃti ca sarvataḥ \|*  
*mānasodbheva ityākhyā ṛṣibhiḥ parigīyate \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. They completely untie the mental knot of Cit and Acit. The name Mānasodbheda is proclaimed everywhere by the sages.

## \|\| 3.6.50 \|\|

*bhiṃdaṃti hṛdayagraṃthīśchiṃdanti bahusaṃśayam \|*  
*karmāṇi kṣapayantyasmānmānasodbheda ityabhūt \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. They split the knots in the heart and clarify many doubts. They destroy Karmas. Therefore (the holy spot) became (known as) Mānasodbheda.

## \|\| 3.6.51 \|\|

*yadi bhāgyavaśādatra biṃdumātraṃ labhennaraḥ \|*  
*tatkṣaṇānmuktimāpnoti kimatastvadhikaṃ bhavet \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. If by chance a man obtains only a drop (from the Tīrtha) here, he attains liberation instantaneously. What can be superior to this?

## \|\| 3.6.52 \|\|

*giridarīnilaye nivasatyamī ṛṣigaṇāḥ phalamūlajalāśanāḥ \|*  
*jitamanoviṣayāḥ śitabuddhayaḥ kalibhayādiva pāpabhayākulāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. These sages live in their abodes in the caves of the mountain. They subsist on the diet of fruits, roots and water. They have conquered their minds and (desire for) objects. They have keen intellect. They are agitated due to their fear of sins as well as that of the Kali Age. (Defective Text)

## \|\| 3.6.53 \|\|

*phalasamīraṇagahvaranirjharāśramabharādupalabdhapaṭottamāḥ \|*  
*triṣavaṇakramanirjitadurjayendriyaparākramaṇā munayastvamī \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. They get good clothes after exertions for (collecting) fruit (and bringing) water from springs in deep caverns. Everyday they take bath three times. Thereby these sages have subdued the onslaughts (strong impulses) of the sense organs.

## \|\| 3.6.54 \|\|

*sādhanāni bahūnyeva kāyakleśakarāṇyaho \|*  
*sulabhaṃ sādhanaṃ loke mānasodbhedadarśanam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. There are many means (to salvation) involving physical strain. But the easiest means in the world is visiting Mānasodbheda.

## \|\| 3.6.55 \|\|

*yasmindine jalaṃ caitallabhate puṇyavāñjanaḥ \|*  
*bhavati vyāsasadṛśo yamapitṛsamaḥ kramāt \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. On the day when a meritorious person obtains the (sacred) waters, he becomes similar to Vyāsa, Yama and the Pitṛs in due course.

## \|\| 3.6.56 \|\|

*kāmyatīrthamidaṃ nṝṇāṃ kāmanāvaśakṛtpunaḥ \|*  
*akāmatastu muktiḥ syādubhayoreṣa niścayaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. This Tīrtha is one worthy of being desired by men. It keeps desires and ambitions under control by fulfilling them. There shall be salvation even if there is no desire. This is certain in both the cases.

## \|\| 3.6.57 \|\|

*yadi kaścitpramādena kāmanāṃ kurute naraḥ \|*  
*phalaṃ bhuktvā punarmuktirbhavatyeva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. If any man, by mistake, were to entertain desires, he will enjoy the fruits and later he will have liberation. There is no doubt about this.

## \|\| 3.6.58 \|\|

*maharādiṣu lokeṣu bhuktvā bhogānyathepsitān \|*  
*bhoge bhukte punaryāti kāmanāvaśato janaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. People will enjoy all the pleasures in the worlds beginning with Maharloka as they desire. After the pleasures have been enjoyed, they go again (to this world) being subject to desires.

## \|\| 3.6.59 \|\|

*puruṣārthasamāvāptyai yatanīyaṃ manīṣibhiḥ \|*  
*mānasodbhedane tīrthe nāpetyatreti me matiḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Learned men should endeavour for the acquisition of the aims of life. In my opinion their endeavour here in the holy spot Mānasodbheda does not go in vain.

## \|\| 3.6.60 \|\|

*mānasodbhedanātpratyagdiśi sarvamanoharam \|*  
*vasudhāreti vikhyātaṃ tīrthaṃ trailokyadurlabham \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. On the western side of Mānasodbhedana there is the famous Tīrtha named Vasudhārā. It is the most fascinating of all. It is the rarest of Tīrthas in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 3.6.61 \|\|

*trilokyāṃ sarvatīrthebhyaḥ śreṣṭho badarikāśramaḥ \|*  
*śrutvā tannāradātsarve vasavaḥ samupāgatāḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. On hearing from Nārada that Badarikāśrama is the most excellent one among all the Tīrthas in the three worlds, all the Vasus came here.

## \|\| 3.6.62 \|\|

*triṃśadvarṣasahasrāṇi tapaḥ paramadāruṇam \|*  
*dalāṃbuprāśanāścakrustataḥ siddhimupāyayuḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. They performed very severe penance for thirty thousand years with leaves and water for their diet. Thereby they attained Siddhi.

## \|\| 3.6.63-64 \|\|

*bhagavaddarśanātprāptānaṃdanirvṛttaviklamāḥ \|*  
*hṛdayānandasaṃdohapraphullitamukhāṃbujāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ varaṃ labdhvā manoramam \|*  
*haribhaktisukhaiśvaryyaṃ paraṃ labdhvā mudaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. Their fatigue has been dispelled by the happiness of seeing the Lord. Their lotus-like faces became full-blown due to the mass of delight in their hearts. After seeing Lord Nārāyaṇa and securing a fine boon, they obtained the happiness, prosperity and devotion to Hari. Thus they became joyous.

## \|\| 3.6.65 \|\|

*atra snātvā jalaṃ pītvā pūjayitvā janārddanam \|*  
*iha loke sukhaṃ bhuktvā yātyaṃte paramaṃ padam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. By taking bath here, drinking the water and worshipping Janārdana, one enjoys happiness in this world and attains the greatest region in the end.

## \|\| 3.6.66 \|\|

*atra puṇyavatāṃ jyotirdṛśyate jalamadhyataḥ \|*  
*yaddṛṣṭvā na punarbhūyo garbhavāsaṃ prapadyate \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. To meritorious persons a fiery refulgence is visible here in the middle of the water. On seeing this one does not stay further within any womb (i.e. gets Mokṣa).

## \|\| 3.6.67 \|\|

*ye'śuddhapitṛjāḥ pāpāḥ pāṣaṃḍamativṛttayaḥ \|*  
*na teṣāṃ śirasi prāyaḥ pataṃtyāpaḥ kadācana \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. If sinners of impure parentage, whose minds and activities are those of heretics, come here, the waters generally do not fall on their heads.

## \|\| 3.6.68 \|\|

*dinatrayaṃ śucirbhūtvā pūjayitvā janārdanam \|*  
*upoṣya bhagavadbhaktyā siddhānpaśyaṃti sādhavaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Good people who remain pure, worship Janārdana and fast for three days with great devotion to the Lord, see the Siddhas.

## \|\| 3.6.69-70 \|\|

*ye tatra capalāstathyaṃ na vadaṃti ca lolupāḥ \|*  
*parihāsaparadravyaparastrīkapaṭāgrahāḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*malacailāvṛtā'śāṃtā'śucayastyaktasatkriyāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ malinacittānāṃ phalamatra na jāyate \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. Those who are fickle-minded and covetous, who do not speak the truth there, who fraudulently take away the wealth and wives of other people and ridicule others, who are clad in dirty clothes, who are not calm, who are not pure, who have abandoned good holy rites and whose minds also are impure, never attain any benefit here.

## \|\| 3.6.71-72 \|\|

*ye tatra sādhakāḥ śāṃtā viralā vidhivartmagāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ japastapohomo dānavratajapakriyāḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*kriyamāṇā yathāśaktyā hyakṣayyaphaladāyakāḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

71-72. The few calm and quiet Sādhakas (aspirants) who take the path enjoined in the Vedas (attain happiness). Their Japas, penances, Homas, charitable gifts, holy rites, pious observances etc. pursued in accordance with their capacity bestow everlasting benefits.

## \|\| 3.6.73 \|\|

*yatkiṃcicchubhakarmāṇi kriyamāṇāni dehinām \|*  
*mahadādiphalaṃ dadyurniḥśreyasamanuttamam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Even the least bit of auspicious rites performed by embodied beings may yield a great result and even excellent salvation.

## \|\| 3.6.74 \|\|

*śrāvaṇīyamiha kiṃ phalādhikaṃ yatra yāṃti vibudhāḥ phalārthinaḥ \|*  
*pūjitādanu hareḥ priyārthinaḥ svargamārganiratāḥ pramodinaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Is it necessary to recount more about the benefits of a place where (even) Devas go seeking benefit? After Hari’s worship those people who sought pleasing things became joyous and are engaged in the path leading to heaven.

## \|\| 3.6.75 \|\|

*yatra saṃti na ca vighnakāriṇaḥ karmaṇāṃ haribhayātsusidhyati \|*  
*nirviśaṃti ca phalaṃ vivekinaḥ karmamārganiratāḥ sudehinaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. (This is a holy spot) where there are no persons who create obstacles to holy rites. Afraid of Hari, they (? holy rites) become fructified. Those who possess the power of discrimination enjoy the benefit. All good souls engaged in the path of duty (enjoy the benefit).

## Chapter 7 - The Greatness of Pañcadhārā and Other Tīrthas

## \|\| 3.7.1 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*tato nairṛtyadigbhāge paṃcadhārāḥ pataṃtyadhaḥ \|*  
*prabhāsaṃ puṣkaraṃ caiva gayāṃ naimiṣameva ca \|*  
*kurukṣetraṃ vijānīhi dravarūpaṃ ṣaḍānana \|\| 1 \|\|*

Śiva said:

1\. On the south-west thereof, five streams of water flow down. Know that they are Prabhāsa, Puṣkara, Gayā, Naimiṣa and Kurukṣetra in liquid (water) form, O Six-faced One.

## \|\| 3.7.2 \|\|

*purā te brahmaṇaḥ sthānaṃ gatā malinarūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*pāpināṃ pāpadoṣeṇa vikṛtāḥ kṛtabuddhayaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Formerly those intelligent ones went to the abode of Brahmā in unclean forms, (because) they had been polluted by the sins of sinners.

## \|\| 3.7.3 \|\|

*tatra gatvā namaskṛtya brahmāṇaṃ lokabhāvanam \|*  
*ūcuḥ prāṃjalayaḥ sarve nijāgamanakāraṇam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. After going there and bowing down to Brahmā, the sanctifier of the worlds, all of them stood there with palms joined in reverence and told the purpose of their arrival.

## \|\| 3.7.4 \|\|

*tacchrutvā dhyānamālaṃbya prahasya jagadīśvaraḥ \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ cāru smṛtvā badarīkāśramam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. On hearing it the Lord of the universe went into a trance. On recollecting Badarikāśrama he smiled and spoke the following sweet words:

## \|\| 3.7.5 \|\|

*mā bhaiṣṭa gacchata kṣipraṃ harerbadarikāśramam \|*  
*yasya nirdeśamātreṇa sadyaḥ puṇyaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. “Do not be afraid. Go quickly to Badarikāśrama of Had by entering which great merit will accrue to you.”

## \|\| 3.7.6 \|\|

*tataste harṣavegena namaskṛtya pitāmaham \|*  
*jagmurutphullanayanā viśālāmamitaprabhām \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Then they bowed down to Brahmā and with their eyes (like) full-blown (lotus) on account of excessive delight, they went to Viśālā of unmeasured lustre.

## \|\| 3.7.7 \|\|

*iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe badarikāśramamāhātmye śivakārttikeyasaṃvāde pañcadhārāditīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma saptamodhyāyaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The moment they entered Viśālā, all their sins were dispelled. Thereafter, they assumed two forms and eagerly went to their own abode.

## \|\| 3.7.8-10 \|\|

*dravarūpeṇa cānyena paṃca tiṣṭhaṃti nirmalāḥ \|*  
*teṣu snātvā vidhānena kṛtvā nityakriyāṃ śuciḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tattattīrthaphalaṃ labdhvā yātyaṃte paramaṃ padam \|*  
*paṃcopavāsa nirataḥ pūjayitvā janārdanam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*iha bhogānbahūnbhuktvā hareḥ sālokyamāpnuyāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. In liquid (water) form as well as in another all those five stand free from the impurities. By taking bath in accordance with the injunctions in those Tīrthas and by performing the daily routine of holy rites with purity, one obtains the merit of the respective Tīrtha and attains the greatest position in the end. One who is engaged in the observance of fasts for five days and then worships Janārdana, enjoys many worldly pleasures here and (after death) attains Sālokya (i.e. residence in the same world as that) of Hari.

## \|\| 3.7.11 \|\|

*tatastu vimalaṃ tīrthaṃ somakuṃḍābhidhaṃ param \|*  
*tapaścakāra bhagavānsomo yatra kalānidhiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Beyond that is the Tīrtha free of impurities, named Somakuṇḍa. It is the place where Soma, the storehouse of digits, performed a penance.

## \|\| 3.7.12 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*somakuṇḍasya māhātmyaṃ vada me vadatāṃ vara \|*  
*tvatprasādādahaṃ śrotumicchāmi parameśvara \|\| 12 \|\|*

Skanda said:

12\. O you the most excellent one among eloquent beings, describe to me the greatness of Somakuṇḍa. O great Lord, I wish to hear about it with your favour.

## \|\| 3.7.13 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*purātritanayaḥ śrīmānsomaḥ saṃprāpya yauvanam \|*  
*śrutvā svarvāsināṃ saukhyaṃ gaṃdharvebhyo muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*tadā svapitaraṃ prāyātpraṣṭuṃ tallabhate katham \|\| 13 \|\|*

Śiva said:

13\. Formerly Soma, the glorious son of Atri, attained youth. From Gandharvas he frequently heard that heaven-dwellers enjoy (perpetual) happiness. Then he went to his father to ask him how it could be obtained.

## \|\| 3.7.14-15 \|\|

*soma uvāca \|*  
*bhagavansarvadharmajña karuṇāmṛtasāgara \|*  
*kathaṃ vā labhyate svargaḥ sarveṣāmuttamottamaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*grahanakṣatratārāṇāmoṣadhīnāṃ patiḥ prabho \|*  
*syāmahaṃ yena taṃ yatnaṃ kṛpayā vada me pitaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

Soma said:

14-15. O holy lord conversant with all pious activities, O ocean of the nectar of mercy, how can heaven that is the most excellent of all, be obtained? Kindly tell me, O father, that (holy) means through which I shall become Lord of Planets, Stars, Constellations and Medicinal Herbs.

## \|\| 3.7.16 \|\|

*atriruvāca \|*  
*tapasārādhya goviṃdaṃ yamairvā niyamaiḥ suta \|*  
*kiṃ durllabhaṃ tu sādhūnāmiha loke paratra ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

Atri said:

16\. O son, if one propitiates Govinda by means of restraints and pious observances, what is difficult of access to him? Nothing is difficult to be obtained by good people in this world and in the other world.

## \|\| 3.7.17 \|\|

*tatastu nāradācchrutvā kṣetraṃ paramanirmalam \|*  
*jagāma badarīṃ natvā pitaraṃ diśamuttarām \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. From Nārada he heard that (Badarī), the holy place, is excellent and free from impurities. After bowing down to his father, he went to the North, to Badarī.

## \|\| 3.7.18 \|\|

*tatra gatvā phalairmedhyairviṣṇoḥ pūjāmakalpayat \|*  
*jajāpa paramaṃ jāpyamaṣṭākṣaraṃ manoharam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. After going there, he performed the worship of Viṣṇu by means of pure and praiseworthy fruits. He performed Japa of the excellent and charming eight-syllabled Mantra (viz. oṃ nārāyaṇāya namaḥ).

## \|\| 3.7.19 \|\|

*aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇi varṣāṇi bhagavatparam \|*  
*tapastepe'tiparamaṃ sarvalokabhayāvaham \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. For eighty thousand years he performed the excessively austere, great penance with the Lord in view. It was the cause of great panic to all the worlds.

## \|\| 3.7.20 \|\|

*tatastuṣṭaḥ samāgatya bhagavānbhaktavatsalaḥ \|*  
*uvāca somaṃ vidhivadvaraṃ varaya suvrata \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then the delighted Lord, fond of his devotees, came there and spoke to Soma duly: “O devotee of excellent holy rites, choose your boon.”

## \|\| 3.7.21 \|\|

*tataḥ somaḥ samutthāya namaskṛtya punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*grahanakṣatratārāṇāmoṣadhīnāmahaṃ patiḥ \|*  
*dvijānāmapi sarveṣāṃ bhūyāsaṃ te prasādataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Then Soma got up, bowed to him again and again and said: “With thy favour I wish to be Lord of Planets, Stars and Constellations as well as all the Brāhmaṇas.”

## \|\| 3.7.22 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*varamanyaṃ vṛṇuṣvāto durllabhaṃ tvaṃ bhavādṛśām \|*  
*varānno varayāmāsa tadā taṃ himajātmaja \|\| 22 \|\|*

Hari said:

22\. Choose another boon that is more difficult to obtain to people like you.

Then he did not choose any boon, O Son of the Daughter of Himavān.

## \|\| 3.7.23 \|\|

*tato'tivimanāḥ somaḥ punastepe tapo mahat \|*  
*triṃśadvarṣasahasrāṇi devamānena putraka \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. With his mind excessively distressed, Soma performed a great penance once again for thirty thousand years by the standard of gods, O dear son.

## \|\| 3.7.24 \|\|

*tadāsau karuṇāpūrṇahṛdayo bhagavānagāt \|*  
*varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te varado'haṃ tavāgrataḥ \|*  
*somastu tādṛśaṃ vavre tacchrutvāntarddadhe hariḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. At that time, with his heart filled with pity, the Lord went there and said, “Welfare unto you. Choose a boon. I am the bestower of boons in front of you.” Soma chose a boon like the one before. On hearing it, Hari vanished.

## \|\| 3.7.25 \|\|

*tato'tivimanāḥ somaḥ punastepe tapo mahat \|*  
*catvāriṃśatsahasrāṇi tapastaptaṃ suduṣkaram \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Thereupon Soma who became more distressed performed a great penance once again. A very difficult penance was performed (by him) for forty thousand years.

## \|\| 3.7.26 \|\|

*tatastuṣṭo hariḥ sākṣācchaṃkhacakragadādharaḥ \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ cāru somaṃ śrāṃtaṃ taponidhim \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Thereupon, the delighted Hari appeared directly before him holding the conch, the discus and the iron club. He spoke these charming words to the exhausted Soma, the storehouse of penance:

## \|\| 3.7.27 \|\|

*uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha bhadraṃ te varaṃ varaya suvrata \|*  
*tapasārādhito nūnaṃ tvayāhaṃ tapasāṃ nidhiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. “Get up, get up; welfare unto you. Choose a boon, O (devotee) of holy rites. I, the storehouse of penances, have been certainly propitiated by you by means of penance.”

## \|\| 3.7.28 \|\|

*soma uvāca \|*  
*yadi tuṣṭo bhavānmahyaṃ bhagavānvaradarṣabhaḥ \|*  
*grahanakṣatratārāṇāmādhipatyaṃ prayaccha me \|*  
*tathauṣadhīnāṃ viprāṇāṃ yāminyāśca jagatpate \|\| 28 \|\|*

Soma said:

28\. If you are delighted with me, O holy Lord, the most prominent bestower of boons, grant unto me the lordship of Planets, Constellations and Stars as well as of Medicinal Herbs, Brāhmaṇas and Night, O Lord of the universe.

## \|\| 3.7.29 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*durllabhaṃ prārthitaṃ vatsa vitarāmi tathāpyaham \|*  
*evamastu tataḥ sarve samāgatya divau kasaḥ \|*  
*abhiṣiktavaṃto vidhivatsomaṃ rājānamādṛtāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

29\. A thing very difficult to obtain has been prayed for, O dear one. Yet I shall grant it. Let it be so.

Thereupon all the heaven-dwellers came there and duly crowned Soma as the king with great respect.

## \|\| 3.7.30 \|\|

*tato vimānamārūḍho rathena śubhravāsasā \|*  
*abhiṣṭutaḥ surairabhūddivaṃ gato niśākaraḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Thereupon the Moon-god came in a chariot covered with fine cloths. He then got into the aerial chariot. Being eulogized by Suras, he rose into the firmament.

## \|\| 3.7.31 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti tīrthaṃ tatsomakuṃḍeti durllabham \|*  
*yaddṛṣṭimātrānmanujā gatadoṣā bhavaṃti hi \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Ever since then that Tīrtha became well-known as Somakuṇḍa. It is a rare sacred place. Merely by seeing it, men become rid of their faults and sins.

## \|\| 3.7.32-34 \|\|

*yadupasparśanādyāṃti somalokaṃ viniṃditāḥ \|*  
*yatra snātvā vidhānena saṃtarpya pitṛdevatāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*somalokaṃ vinirbhidya viṣṇulokaṃ prapadyate \|*  
*upavāsatrayaṃ kṛtvā pūjayitvā janārddanam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*na teṣāṃ punarāvṛttiḥ kalpakoṭiśatairapi \|*  
*trirātreṇa sthito bhūtvā pūjayitvā janārddanam \|*  
*japaṃ kurvanviśeṣeṇa maṃtrasiddhiḥ prajāyate \|\| 34 \|\|*

32-34. Even persons of despicable nature go to Soma’s world by touching it and drinking its waters. By taking the holy bath in it, by propitiating Pitṛs and Devas in accordance with the injunctions, the devotee shall pierce Soma’s world and pass on to the world of Viṣṇu.

If anyone observes fast for three days and worships Janārdana, he never returns to the earth even in the course of hundreds and crores of Kalpas.

If a person stays there for three days, worships Janārdana, performs particular Japas, he can achieves mastery over Mantras.

## \|\| 3.7.35 \|\|

*karmaṇā manasā vācā yatkṛtaṃ pātakaṃ nṛbhiḥ \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ kṣayamāyāti somakuṃḍekṣaṇādiha \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. By visiting Somakuṇḍa, all the sins of men, committed mentally, verbally or physically, shall be destroyed.

## \|\| 3.7.36 \|\|

*tatastu dvādaśādityatīrthaṃ pāpaharaṃ param \|*  
*yatra taptvā punaḥ kṛcchraṃ kāśyapaḥ sūryatāṃ yayau \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Beyond that is the Dvādaśāditya Tīrtha which is a great destroyer of sins. By performing a very difficult penance here a son of Kaśyapa became the Sun-god.

## \|\| 3.7.37 \|\|

*durllabhaṃ triṣu lokeṣu tapaḥsiddhyekakāraṇam \|*  
*ravivāreṣu saptamyāṃ saṃkrātyāṃ vidhivannaraḥ \|*  
*saptajanmakṛtātpāpātsnānamātreṇa śuddhyati \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. It is very difficult to get (a Tīrtha like this) in all the three worlds. It is the sole cause for success of penance. On Sundays, the seventh lunar day and on the days of the transit of the Sun (from one Zodiac to another), one should take his holy bath in accordance with the injunctions. He becomes purified, of all the sins committed in the course of seven births.

## \|\| 3.7.38 \|\|

*pārākaṃ vidhivatkṛtvā pūjanīyo janārddanaḥ \|*  
*sūryaloke sukhaṃ bhuktvā viṣṇuloke mahīyate \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. One shall perform the Pārāka expiatory rites duly and worship Janārdana. He will rejoice in the world of the Sun and will be honoured in the world of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 3.7.39 \|\|

*mahārogābhibhūtastu snātvā pītvā jalaṃ śuciḥ \|*  
*rogamukto'cirādeva nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. One who is afflicted with severe illness should take bath and drink its water with mental and physical purity. Ere long he will be liberated from ailments. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 3.7.40 \|\|

*catuḥsrotaṃ paraṃ tīrthaṃ vilocanamanoharam \|*  
*dharmārthakāmamokṣāste tiṣṭhaṃti dravarūpiṇaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The next Tīrtha is Catuḥsrota. It is very fascinating to the eyes. The four aims of life, Dharma (virtue), Artha (wealth), Kāma (love) and Mokṣa (salvation), stay there in liquid form.

## \|\| 3.7.41 \|\|

*harerājñānusāreṇa kṣetre'sminvaiṣṇave svayam \|*  
*puruṣārthā dravībhūtā bhūtānāṃ muktihetavaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. In compliance of the behest of Hari in this Vaiṣṇava holy place, the Puruṣārthas (aims of life) themselves in liquefied form are the causes of the salvation of all living beings.

## \|\| 3.7.42 \|\|

*pūrvādidikṣu kramasanniviṣṭā dharmapradhānā iva rūpabhājaḥ \|*  
*bhajaṃti ye tānkramasanniviṣṭānprasannataiṣāṃ satataṃ bhaveddhi \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The aims of life with Dharma as the most important one occupy the quarters beginning with the East in due order. They are there as if they have separate bodies. If people worship them as they occupy (the quarters) in due order, indeed people will derive perpetual pleasure.

## \|\| 3.7.43 \|\|

*nānyatra kṣetre militāḥ kathaṃciccatvāra ete tridaśairalabhyāḥ \|*  
*tānagrimaṃ janma javena labdhvā paśyaṃti pūrvārjitapuṇyapuṃjāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. In other holy places these four have not come together like this. They are not obtainable even to gods. Those who have masses of merit acquired before, take birth as Brāhmaṇas and see them.

## \|\| 3.7.44-45 \|\|

*ye durjanā durjanasaṃgabhājaḥ kṣamārjavaprāṇajayapradhānāḥ \|*  
*krīḍāmṛgā grāmyavadhūjanānāṃ na te prapaśyaṃtyacirātpumarthān \|\| 44 \|\|*

*tathaiva paśyaṃtyacireṇa tattvajñānaikahetūnapi tānpumarthān \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. Those who are wicked, those who are in league with vicious people, those who are like only pet short animals of vulgar womenfolk, may give importance to forbearance, straightforwardness, and vital breaths. They do not see the aims of human life even after a long time.

Similarly they find ere long those aims of life that may cause Tattvajñāna (knowledge of the Truth).

## \|\| 3.7.46 \|\|

*atra brahmādayo devā ṛṣayaśca tapodhanāḥ \|*  
*parvaṇi prayatāḥ snātuṃ samāyāṃti ṣaḍānana \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Devas beginning with Brahmā, sages and ascetics come here during Parvan days with great purity, in order to take their holy bath, O Six-faced One.

## \|\| 3.7.47-50 \|\|

*tataḥ satyapadaṃnāma tīrthaṃ sarvamanoharam \|*  
*trikoṇākāramevaitatkuṃḍaṃ kalmaṣanāśanam \|*  
*ekādaśyāṃ haristatra svayamāyāti pāvane \|\| 47 \|\|*

*tatpaścādṛṣayaḥ sarve munayaśca tapodhanāḥ \|*  
*snātumāyāṃti vidhivatkuṃḍe satyapadābhidhe \|\| 48 \|\|*

*gaṃdharvāpsarasāṃ yatra madhyāhne harivāsare \|*  
*gānaṃ śṛṇvaṃti viralāḥ satyavrataparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*darśanādyasya tīrthasya pātakāni mahāṃtyapi \|*  
*palāyaṃte bhayenaiva siṃhaṃ dṛṣṭvā mṛgā iva \|\| 50 \|\|*

47-50. There, beyond that is the Tīrtha named Satyapada. It is charming to all. This Kuṇḍa is in the shape of a triangle. It is destructive of sins. On the eleventh day (in the lunar fortnight) Hari himself comes to that holy spot. After him come all the sages, saints and ascetics, in order to take their bath duly in the Kuṇḍa named Satyapada. A few persons who are devoutly engaged in the practice of truth hear the song of Ganḍharvas and celestial damsels at midday on the eleventh day. On seeing this holy Tīrtha even great sins flee with fright like deer on seeing a lion.

## \|\| 3.7.51 \|\|

*svaśākhoktavidhānena snānaṃ kṛtvā vicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*satyalokamavāpnoti tato naiḥśreyasaṃ padam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. A clever devotee should take holy bath in accordance with the injunctions of one’s own branch (of Vedas). Thereby he attains Satyaloka. Thereafter he attains salvation.

## \|\| 3.7.52 \|\|

*ahorātraṃ śucirbhūtvā upoṣya ca janārddanam \|*  
*pūjayitvā yathāśaktyā sa jīvanmuktibhājanaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. One should be pure (mentally and physically) and observe fast for a day and a night. Then he should worship Janārdana in accordance with his capacity. He shall be worthy of being a liberated soul even while alive.

## \|\| 3.7.53 \|\|

*brahmā viṣṇuśca rudraśca trikoṇasthāḥ samāhitāḥ \|*  
*tapaḥ kurvaṃtyanudinaṃ sarvalokāditoṣaṇam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra are stationed in a triangle. They perform penance with perfect concentration everyday for giving delight to all the worlds.

## \|\| 3.7.54 \|\|

*trikoṇamaṃḍitaṃ tīrthaṃ nāmnā satyapadapradam \|*  
*darśanīyaṃ prayatnena sarvapāpamumukṣubhiḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. This Tīrtha which gives the region of Satya(-loka), named Trikoṇamaṇḍita should be visisted with great effort by those who desire to be rid of all sins.

## \|\| 3.7.55 \|\|

*japaṃ tapo haristotraṃ pūjāṃ stutyabhivaṃdanam \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ kurvatāṃ vaktuṃ brahmaṇāpi na śakyate \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. It is impossible even for Brahmā to express the greatness of those who perform Japa, penance, eulogy of Hari, worship, adoration and salutation to Hari.

## \|\| 3.7.56 \|\|

*tato'tivimalaṃ nāma naranārāyaṇāśramam \|*  
*dvividhaṃ dṛśyate tatra pāthaḥ paramanirmalam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Beyond that is the hermitage of Nara and Nārāyaṇa, named Ativimala. There the pure water is seen in two forms.

## \|\| 3.7.57 \|\|

*ubhābhyāmubhayoḥ prītirbhavatīti viniścitam \|*  
*tatra snātvā prayatnena pūjayitvā janārddanam \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktastatkṣaṇānnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Both of them will be certainly delighted with both of these. One who takes bath there with determination and worships Janārdana shall certainly be liberated from all sins.

## \|\| 3.7.58 \|\|

*tato nārāyaṇāvāsaśikhare vimalākṛti \|*  
*tīrthaṃ pavitramurvaśyā abhivyaktikaraṃ bhavet \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Thereafter, a sacred Tīrtha of fine shape on the summit that is the abode of Nārāyaṇa, is the manifestor of Urvaśī (i.e. her birth place).

## \|\| 3.7.59 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*abhivyaktiḥ kathaṃ tasyā urvaśyāḥ śikhare pitaḥ \|*  
*kiṃ puṇyaṃ kiṃ phalaṃ tatra paraṃ kautūhalaṃ vada \|\| 59 \|\|*

Skanda said:

59\. O father, how did Uravaśī reveal herself on that summit? What is the merit and the benefit of that holy Tīrtha there? I have great curiosity. Recount it to me.

## \|\| 3.7.60 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*dharmasyapatnī mūrtyāsīttasyāṃ jātau ṣaḍānana \|*  
*naranārāyaṇau sākṣādbhagavāneva kevalam \|\| 60 \|\|*

Śiva said:

60\. Mūrti was the wife of Dharma, O Six-faced One. Nara and Nārāyaṇa were born to her. The Lord himself was born (of her).

## \|\| 3.7.61 \|\|

*pitrorājñāmanuprāpya tapo'rdhaṃ kṛtamānasau \|*  
*ubhayornagayostau tu tapomūrtī iva sthitau \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Getting the sanction from their parents, they determined to perform penance. They stationed themselves on the two mountains like personifications of penance itself.

## \|\| 3.7.62-63 \|\|

*tau dṛṣṭvā vismitaḥ śakraḥ preṣayāmāsa manmatham \|*  
*sagaṇaṃ tapaso dhvaṃso yathā syādgandhamādanam \|\| 62 \|\|*

*vikramya vidhivatte tu nārāyaṇabalodayam \|*  
*jñātvā hatamanaskāstānuvāca jagatīpatiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. On seeing them, Śakra was surprised. He sent Manmatha (i.e. the god of love) along with his group, so that the penance might be (disturbed and) destroyed. They went to Gandhamādana with pride in their exploits. Realizing the rise in the strength of Nārāyaṇa duly, they lost their hope and they became dispirited. The Lord of the universe said to them:

## \|\| 3.7.64-66 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*kimarthamāgatā yūyamātithyaṃ gṛhyatāmiti \|\| 64 \|\|*

*ityuktvā phalamūlāni tebhyo dattvorvaśīṃ tathā \|*  
*dattvāntardhimagādeva paśyatāṃ vighnakāriṇīm \|\| 65 \|\|*

*te tu gatvā divaṃ bhīte śakrāyocurbalaṃ hareḥ \|*  
*śakrastāmurvaśīṃ prāpya harṣaṇaikayuto'bhavat \|\| 66 \|\|*

Hari said:

64-66. Why have you come? Let my hospitality be accepted.

After saying this he gave them fruits and roots as well as Urvaśī. Then he vanished even as they stood observing her as one who might cause obstruction to the penance. They became frightened and went to heaven where they mentioned to Śakra about the strength of Hari. On getting Urvaśī Śakra experienced ecstatic delight.

## \|\| 3.7.67-68 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti tattīrthamurvaśī nāmataḥ pṛthak \|*  
*prasiddhaṃ yatra bhagavānsvayamāste tapomayaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā vidhānena upoṣya rajanidvayam \|*  
*pūjayitvā haristatra naro nārāyaṇo bhavet \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. Ever since then, that Tīrtha became famous separately after the name of Urvaśī. In the place where the Lord sits engrossed in penance, a devotee should take his bath in accordance with the injunctions and observe fast for two nights. By worshipping Hari there Nara (Man) becomes Nārāyaṇa himself.

## \|\| 3.7.69 \|\|

*urvaśīkuṇḍamāsādya kāmanāvaśato naraḥ \|*  
*urvaśīlokamāpnoti snānamātreṇa putraka \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. A man who reaches Urvaśīkuṇḍa and takes his bath there with an ardent desire obtains the world of Urvaśī, O dear son.

## \|\| 3.7.70 \|\|

*sadaiva bhagavāṃstatra urvaśīkuṃḍa sannidhau \|*  
*bhūtānāṃ bhāvayanbhavyaṃ tapomūrtirvyavasthitaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Near Urvaśīkuṇḍa the Lord is always present in the (posture of) performing a penance, contemplating on the well-being of all living beings.

## \|\| 3.7.71 \|\|

*āmodaṃ tadupari vai prabhañjano'pi śrībharturvahati padāṃbujaikalabdham \|*  
*yatsaṃgātkaliyugakalmaṣāturāṇāmutsaṃge na bhavati pāpabhārapākaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Above it even wind bears the fragrance obtained solely from the lotus-like feet of the Lord of Śrī. If those who are afflicted by the sins of Kali come into contact with it, they will never suffer due to the mass of sins.

## \|\| 3.7.72 \|\|

*yatsaṃgāddharṣamupāvahatpadaśrīnirviṇṇo girivivarecyutaikasevī \|*  
*śrībhartuścaraṇayugaṃ vahansamantādabhyeti praśamamahastapaḥsamīre \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. (Defective Text) A person who is dejected due to the glory of (his high) office attained delight by the power of the contact with it. He serves Acyuta alone in the cavity of the mountain. Bearing the pair of the feet of the Lord of Śrī all round, he becomes calm in the wind.

## \|\| 3.7.73 \|\|

*gīrvāṇānupahasati svaghena pūrṇaḥ kīṭo'pipraśamitadurnayo nirīhaḥ \|*  
*yatrasthaḥ kusumanivedamātmayogaparyuṣṭaṃ jahadupayāsyate padaṃ tat \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Even a worm which is full of excessive sins laughs at Devas because, stationed in that holy spot, all his evils have been subdued and he has become devoid of desires. Indeed that region is obtained after abandoning the flower which has become sport due to his contact(?).

## \|\| 3.7.74 \|\|

*yatretvā munimatayo bahiḥpadārthānnāpaśyannihitapadāṃbujaikabhājaḥ \|*  
*yatrasthaḥ svayamapi gopatirjanānāmādhatte svapadamanukramāgatānām \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. After going to that place, the minds of sages are not aware of external objects, because they (their minds) are fixed to the lotuslike feet (of the Lord). The Lord of the earth stationed there, allots his own region to the people coining in due order.

## \|\| 3.7.75 \|\|

*bahūni saṃti tīrthāni girau nārāyaṇāśrite \|*  
*sarvapāpaharāṇyāśu tānyahaṃ veda no janaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. There are many Tīrthas on the mountain resorted to by Nārāyaṇa. They are destructive of all sins instantaneously. I know them but the common people do not.

## \|\| 3.7.76 \|\|

*saṃsārakuhare ghore yatra sthagitamātmanaḥ \|*  
*urvaśīkuṇḍamāsādya dinamekaṃ vasennaraḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. In the terrible cave of Saṃsāra where (the existence of) the Ātman is concealed, after reaching Urvaśīkuṇḍa a man should stay there for a day.

## \|\| 3.7.77 \|\|

*urvaśīdakṣiṇe bhāge āyudhāni jagatpateḥ \|*  
*vidyaṃte darśanātteṣāṃ na śastrabhayabhāgbhavet \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. To the southern side of Urvaśīkuṇḍa, there are the weapons of the Lord of the universe. By seeing them one will not meet with any danger from weapons.

## Chapter 8 - The Greatness of Various Tīrthas at Badarī

## \|\| 3.8.1 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*brahmakuṇḍāddakṣiṇato narāvāsagirirmahān \|*  
*yatra bhagavatā meruḥ sthāpito lokasundaraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Śiva said:

1\. To the south of Brahmakuṇḍa is the great mountain Narāvāsa (‘Abode of Nara’). It is there that Meru which is the most beautiful in the world was fixed by the Lord.

## \|\| 3.8.2 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ bhagavatā meruḥ sthāpito narasannidhau \|*  
*mahatkautūhalaṃ tāta kathyatāṃ yadi rocate \|\| 2 \|\|*

Skanda said:

2\. How was Meru fixed by the Lord near Nara? O father, my curiosity is great. Let it be narrated if you like it.

## \|\| 3.8.3-6 \|\|

*mahādeva uvāca \|*  
*yadā bhagavato vāso viśālāyāṃ samāgataḥ \|*  
*devā maharṣayaḥ siddhāḥ savidyādharacāraṇāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*vihāya meruśṛṃgāṇi bhagavaddarśanotsukāḥ \|*  
*bhagavaddarśanāhlādatiraskṛtasurālayāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tadā tu bhagavāṃsteṣāṃ sukhahetoḥ ṣaḍānana \|*  
*utpādya meruśṛṃgāṇi kareṇaikena līlayā \|*  
*sthāpayāmāsa sarveṣāṃ bhagavānprītivarddhanaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tataḥ sarve samālokya giriṃ kāṃcananirmitam \|*  
*prasannāstuṣṭuvuḥ sarve nārāyaṇamanāmayam \|\| 6 \|\|*

Mahādeva said:

3-6. When the Lord himself transferred his residence to Viśālā, Devas, great sages, Siddhas, Vidyādharas and Cāraṇas left the peaks of Meru because they were eager to see the Lord.

On account of the delight caused to them by the sight of the Lord they abandoned heaven. Then, O Six-faced One, for their happiness (and convenience) the Lord uprooted the peaks of Meru with his single hand playfully and placed them (at Viśālā). Thereby the Lord increased the pleasure of all. Then all of them saw the mountain made of gold. They all were delighted; they eulogized Nārāyaṇa who is devoid of ailments.

## \|\| 3.8.7 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*yosmatsukhāya bhavaviśramaṇāya bibhrallīlātanūḥ kanakaśailamihānināya \|*  
*jetā surārddanaśataṃ tridaśaikapakṣastasmai vidhema nama ugratapaḥśriyāya \|\| 7 \|\|*

Devas said:

7\. We pay our obeisance to that Lord of fierce splendour and power of penance, who assumes sportingly many bodies for our happiness as well as for the rest of the world, who brought the golden mountain here, who conquers hundreds of demons, and who solely belongs to the side of Suras.

## \|\| 3.8.8 \|\|

*yadyatkaroti kṛpayā kṛpaṇārtitūlaśailāgnirāśritakṛdekavidāṃ variṣṭhaḥ \|*  
*svenaiva tena karaṇena sa tuṣyatāṃ no yasyānvakāri puruṣeṇa na kenacidvai \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The Lord destroys out of compassion the distress of the miserable like fire reducing to ash even a mountain of cotton. He is the supporter of those who seek refuge in him; he is the most excellent one among those who know the one (and our Lord). Let him be pleased with us by whatever he does out of kindness. Whatever he does has never been imitated by any person.

## \|\| 3.8.9 \|\|

*asmākamunnatadhiyāṃ vidadhāti samyakchikṣāṃ piteva karuṇo nijalābhapūrṇaḥ \|*  
*trailokyarakṣaṇavicakṣaṇadṛṣṭipātapūrṇāmṛtāṃbudhirasau vipadaḥ prapāyāt \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Like a father he gives us perfect training and makes us lofty-minded. He is kind and full of his own acquisition. His glances are efficient in the protection of the three worlds. He is the ocean full of nectar. Let him protect (us) from adversities.

## \|\| 3.8.10 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yenādhyastaṃ bhāti samastaṃ jagadekaṃ krīḍābhāṃḍaṃ satyatayā'jasya vibhūmnaḥ \|*  
*bhānāṃ vṛdaṃ yadvadanepyāśritamūrtistasmai nityaṃ śāśvata tubhyaṃ praṇamāma \|\| 10 \|\|*

The sages said:

10\. The entire universe is superimposed on him. It is only an implement for his sports. It appears to be true. There is a mass of splendour on the face of the unborn Lord of great plenty. He is the Lord whose form is resorted to (by all). We bow down to you, O eternal Being.

## \|\| 3.8.11 \|\|

*siddhā ūcuḥ \|*  
*yatkṛpālavata eva mahāṃtaḥ siddhimīyuritare bhavabhājaḥ \|*  
*te'cireṇa bhavabhīmapayodhiṃ tīrṇavaṃta iti naḥ sumanīṣā \|\| 11 \|\|*

Siddhas said:

11\. Great men have attained Siddhi due to an iota of his kindness. Other men of the world too have crossed the terrible ocean of worldly existence without delay. This is our considered opinion.

## \|\| 3.8.12 \|\|

*vidyādharā ūcuḥ \|*  
*vibho sadguṇagrāma kalyāṇamūrte pareśāna saṃmānasaṃtānaheto \|*  
*bhavatpādapadmāsavasvādamattāḥ kṛtārthā na citraṃ bhavatyatra kiṃcit \|\| 12 \|\|*

Vidyādharas said:

12\. O Lord endowed with a host of good qualities, O Lord with welfare as your form (i.e. whose form is conducive to welfare), O great Lord, O cause.of continuous series of honour, is there any wonder that those who are inebriated with the sweet flavour of the liquor (extracted) from your lotus-feet stay completely satisfied?

## \|\| 3.8.13 \|\|

*tatastuṣṭo'tha bhagavāṃsteṣāmāsīddivaukasām \|*  
*varaṃ vṛṇudhvamityuktāste procurvaradarṣabham \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Thereupon the delighted Lord (appeared) before those heaven-dwellers. On being told “Choose your boons”, they said to (the Lord) who is the most eminent among the bestowers of boons:

## \|\| 3.8.14-16 \|\|

*parituṣṭo bhavānsākṣāddevadevo ramāpatiḥ \|*  
*badarī na tvayā tyājyā na ca meruḥ kadācana \|\| 14 \|\|*

*meruśṛṃgaṃ prapaśyaṃti ye janāḥ puṇyabhāginaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ vai tvatprasādena merau vāsaḥ prajāyatām \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tatra bhuktvā cirādbhogānbhūyādante layastvayi \|*  
*evamastviti cābhāṣya tatraivāṃtarhito hariḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. “If (you) the Lord of Devas, the Lord of Ramā, are really pleased, Badarī should never be abandoned by you, nor should Meru too. Those who see the peak of Meru are meritorious persons. With your favour let their residence be on Meru itself. After enjoying the pleasures there for a long time, let them become merged in you.”

Saying “so be it” Hari vanished there itself.

## \|\| 3.8.17 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti te sarve meruśṛṃgavihāriṇaḥ \|*  
*naranārāyaṇasyāṃte pālyamānā muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Ever since then all of them began to sport about on the peak of Meru. They were being protected repeatedly near Nara and Nārāyaṇa.

## \|\| 3.8.18 \|\|

*kadāciddivi tiṣṭhaṃti kadācinmerumadhyataḥ \|*  
*nirviśaṃkā nirudvegā ṛṣayaśca tapodhanāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. They used to stay in heaven for some time and some time in the middle of Meru. The sages and ascetics were devoid of distress and fear. They were not excited or agitated.

## \|\| 3.8.19 \|\|

*bhagavānapi tatraiva nararūpeṇa tiṣṭhati \|*  
*dhanurbāṇadharaḥ śrīmāṃstapasā pāvakopamaḥ \|*  
*ānaṃdamṛṣivṛṃdasya janayaṃstapa āsthitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The Lord too stays there in the form of (the sage) Nara holding the bow and arrows. The glorious Lord is comparable to fire on account of (the brilliance of) his penance. He resorts to penance and causes bliss to the multitudes of sages.

## \|\| 3.8.20 \|\|

*tatastu paramaṃ tīrthaṃ lokapālābhivaṃditam \|*  
*yatra saṃsthāpayāmāsa lokapālānhariḥ svayam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Beyond that is the excellent Tīrtha saluted by the Guardians of the Quarters. Hari himself established the Guardians of the Quarters there.

## \|\| 3.8.21 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*ekadā merumadhyasthāśrayāniha haranhariḥ \|*  
*devānāmṛṣimukhyānāṃ caritaṃ draṣṭumudyataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

Skanda said:

21\. How were the Guardians of the Quarters established there by the Lord? O dear father, I have great curiosity and eagerness in regard to it. O highly intelligent one, recount it (to me).

## \|\| 3.8.22 \|\|

*null*

Śiva said:

22\. Once, while bringing those who had resorted to the middle of Meru here, Hari was eager to see the activities of Devas and the chief sages.

## \|\| 3.8.23-27 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasotthāya namaskṛtya divaukasaḥ \|*  
*ūcuste vinayātsarve prasīda bhagavanvibho \|\| 23 \|\|*

*kṣaṇaṃ viśrāmya vidhivaddṛṣṭvā tāṃ viralāṃ bhuvam \|*  
*sānnidhyamṛṣidevānāmayuktaṃ bhāvayanmithaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tataḥ prahasya bhagavānuvāca madhusūdanaḥ \|*  
*lokapālānsamāhūya nātra stheyaṃ bhavadvidhaiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*ṛṣayastāpasāḥ siddhāḥ sastrīkā nivasaṃti hi \|*  
*bhavadvidhānāmāsthānaṃ pureva kalpitaṃ mayā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tataḥ sa tvarito gatvā ramye girivare hariḥ \|*  
*lokapālānsamāhūya sthāpayāmāsa tānguha \|\| 27 \|\|*

23-27. On seeing him the heaven-dwellers got up suddenly and bowed down to him. All of them humbly said, “O Lord, be pleased”.

The Lord halted there for a moment and duly surveyed the scanty place there. He thought that the proximity of the sages and the Devas was not proper. Then Lord Madhusūdana called the Guardians of the Quarters and laughingly said to them: “Persons like you should not stay here. Indeed the sages, ascetics and Siddhas stay here along with their womenfolk. The abode of persons like you has already been well-arranged by me.”

Then Hari hurriedly went to the beautiful and excellent mountain. O Guha, he called the Guardians of the Quarters and established them there.

## \|\| 3.8.28 \|\|

*tatraiva śailadaṃḍena hatvāgniṃ jalakāṃkṣayā \|*  
*krīḍāpuṣkaraṇīṃ teṣāṃ nirmame sumanoharāma \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Desirous of water, he hit the mountain with a piece of rock. Thereby he created a charming pond for their sport.

## \|\| 3.8.29-30 \|\|

*sastrīkā yatra gīrvāṇā vicaraṃti nijecchayā \|*  
*gāyaṃti svanumodaṃti gaṃdharvāstridivaukasām \|\| 29 \|\|*

*vanāni kusumāmodaramyāṇi paritoṣataḥ \|*  
*dināni yatra gacchaṃti kṣaṇaprāyāṇi dehinām \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. There Devas roam about as they please along with their wives. Gandharvas sing and rejoice. The forests and parks of heaven-dwellers were fascinating with the fragrance of flowers. All the embodied beings spend the days happily as though they were so many moments.

## \|\| 3.8.31 \|\|

*bhagavānapi tatraiva teṣāmānaṃdamāvahan \|*  
*dvādaśyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ ca svayamāyāti majjane \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Delighting them, the Lord himself comes there to take his holy bath on the twelfth day as well as full-moon day.

## \|\| 3.8.32 \|\|

*tatpaścādṛṣayaḥ sarve munayaśca tapodhanāḥ \|*  
*yatra snātvā vidhānena guha madhyāhnakālataḥ \|*  
*asaṃgaṃ paramaṃ jyotirjale paśyaṃti cakṣuṣā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. After that, all the sages and ascetics take their bath, O Guha, according to the injunctions, at midday. They see with their own eyes the great fiery splendour in the waters moving without any obstruction.

## \|\| 3.8.33 \|\|

*sarvatīrthāvagāhena yatphalaṃ parikīrtitam \|*  
*tatphalaṃ tatkṣaṇādeva daṇḍapuṣkariṇīkṣaṇāt \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. By seeing Daṇḍapuṣkariṇī they obtain instantaneously the merit which is said to be equal to that of taking the holy bath in all the Tīrthas.

## \|\| 3.8.34 \|\|

*yatra kāmyāni karmāṇi saphalāni manīṣiṇām \|*  
*yatra piṃḍapradānena gayāto'ṣṭaguṇaṃ phalam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. All the rites performed for some desired results by the wise become fruitful there. The offering of riceballs there has eight times the benefit than that at Gayā.

## \|\| 3.8.35-36 \|\|

*yajño dānaṃ tapaḥ karma sarvamakṣayamucyate \|*  
*dvādaśyāṃ śuklapakṣasya jyeṣṭhe māsi ṣaḍānana \|\| 35 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā vidhānena kṛtakṛtyo bhavedyataḥ \|*  
*badarītīrthamadhye tu guptametatsurottamaiḥ \|*  
*na vācyaṃ yatra kutrāpi tava prītyā mayoditam \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36 Yajña, charity, penance and holy rite when performed there on the twelfth day in the bright half of the month of Jyeṣṭha, O Six-faced One, are said to be everlasting, since one becomes blessed and contented by taking the holy bath in accordance with the injunctions (there on that day). This secret is well guarded by the excellent Suras in regard to Badarītīrtha. This should not be disclosed to anyone and everyone. It was out of love for you that it has been mentioned to you.

## \|\| 3.8.37 \|\|

*vaktavyaṃ kimiha bahu prabhūtapuṇyāḥ paśyaṃti prathitamidaṃ suraikaguptam \|*  
*nānyeṣāṃ kathamapi cetasi prasaṃgāddevaiḥ syādanudinaciṃtitaṃ guhaitat \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Why should much be spoken about it here? Only those with plenty of merit see this famous holy place well-guarded by Suras. Not others. They will not even think about this. O Guha; Devas think about this everyday.

## \|\| 3.8.38 \|\|

*yeṣāṃ vai bhagavati cetsamagrakarma svādhyāyābhyasanavidhikrameṇa jātam \|*  
*paśyaṃti tribhuvanadurllabhaṃ sutīrthaṃ daṃḍodaṃ na bhavati cānyathā sudṛṣṭam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. If people have performed all holy rites for the Lord in accordance with the religious injunctions and if they have regularly studied the Vedas, they see the rare Tīrtha named Daṇḍoda (i.e. Daṇḍa Puṣkariṇī). Otherswise it is not seen well.

## \|\| 3.8.39 \|\|

*daṃḍodakātparaṃ tīrthaṃ na viṣṇoḥ sadṛśo'maraḥ \|*  
*viśālāsadṛśaṃ kṣetraṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. There has never been and there will never be a Tīrtha greater than Daṇḍodaka, a god like Viṣṇu and a holy spot on a par with Viśālā.

## \|\| 3.8.40 \|\|

*sevanīyā prayatnena viśālā ca vicakṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*ya icchetsatataṃ dhāma bhagavatpārśvavarti vai \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Viśālā should be resorted to by clever devotees with great determination if they wish to be always near the Lord.

## \|\| 3.8.41 \|\|

*skaṃda uvāca \|*  
*gaṃgāmāśritya tīrthāni kāni saṃtīha satpade \|*  
*śreyaskarāṇi bhūrīṇi saṃkṣepāttāni me vada \|\| 41 \|\|*

Skanda said:

41\. What are those Tīrthas which are connected with Gaṅgā and are conducive to welfare in the region of good people? Recount them briefly to me.

## \|\| 3.8.42 \|\|

*mahādeva uvāca \|*  
*gaṃgāyāṃ yatra saṃyogo mānasodbhedasannidhau \|*  
*tattīrthaṃ vimalaṃ puṇyaṃ prayāgādadhikaṃ mahat \|\| 42 \|\|*

Mahādeva said:

42\. The Tīrtha in the vicinity of Mānasodbheda where Gaṅgā comes in contact, is devoid of impurities. It is meritorious. It is, superior to Prayāga.

## \|\| 3.8.43 \|\|

*triṃśadvarṣasahasrāṇi vāyubhojanato bhavet \|*  
*tatphalaṃ snānamātreṇa gaṃgāyāḥ saṃgame nṛṇām \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Merely by talcing there bath at the confluence of Gaṅgā, men obtain as much merit as is obtained by performing penance while taking in only air for thirty thousand years.

## \|\| 3.8.44 \|\|

*saṃgamāddakṣiṇe bhāge dharmakṣetraṃ prakīrtitam \|*  
*yatra mūrtyā śrutau jātau naranārāyaṇāvṛṣī \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The Tīrtha to the south of the confluence is glorified as Dharmakṣetra. It is reported that the sages Nara and Nārāyaṇa were born of Mūrti there.

## \|\| 3.8.45 \|\|

*tatkṣetraṃ pāvanaṃ martye sarveṣāmuttamottamam \|*  
*dharmastatraiva bhagavāṃścatuṣpādavatiṣṭhati \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. That holy spot is very sacred in the human world. It is the most excellent of all excellent holy spots. There alone does the Holy Lord Dharma stand on all his four feet.

## \|\| 3.8.46 \|\|

*yatra yajñāstapo dānaṃ yatkiṃcitkriyate nṛbhiḥ \|*  
*tatpuṇyasya kṣayo nāsti kalpakoṭiśatairapi \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. If Yajña, penance or charity are performed by men there—whatever that may be, the merit thereof is not destroyed even in the course of hundreds and crores of Kalpas.

## \|\| 3.8.47 \|\|

*tato dakṣiṇadigbhāga urvaśī saṃgamābhidham \|*  
*sarvapāpaharaṃ puṃsāṃ snānamātreṇa dehinām \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. To the south of it is the Tīrtha named Urvaśīsaṅgama. Merely by taking holy bath there all the sins of men and embodied beings are destroyed.

## \|\| 3.8.48 \|\|

*kūrmoddhārastataḥ sākṣāddharibhaktyekasādhanam \|*  
*snānamātreṇa bhūtānāṃ sattvaśuddhiḥ prajāyate \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Beyond that is Kūrmoddhāra. It is the sole means for devotion to Hari. By taking bath therein all living beings will gain purity of nature.

## \|\| 3.8.49 \|\|

*brahmāvarttastataḥ sākṣādbrahmalokaikakāraṇam \|*  
*darśanādeva tīrthasya sarvapāpakṣayo bhavet \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Next to it is the holy spot named Brahmāvarta. It is the sole and direct cause (of attaining) the world of Brahmā. Only by visiting the Tīrtha all the sins will be destroyed.

## \|\| 3.8.50 \|\|

*bahūni saṃti tīrthāni durgamyānīha dehinām \|*  
*saṃkṣepātkathitaṃ vatsa tavādaravaśādidam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. There are many Tīrthas here. But they are not easily approachable to embodied beings. O dear one, it has been briefly recounted because of my considerateness for you.

## \|\| 3.8.51 \|\|

*ya idaṃ śṛṇuyānnityaṃ śrāvayedvā samāhitaḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ padaṃ viṣṇoḥ prapadyate \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. He who always listens to this, or he who recites this or reads this with mental purity and concentration shall get rid of all sins. He attains the region of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 3.8.52 \|\|

*rājā vijayamāpnoti sutārthī labhate sutam \|*  
*kanyārthī labhate kanyāṃ kanyā viṃdati satpatim \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. A king gains victory; he who seeks a son gets a son; he who prays for a daughter gets a daughter; a virgin obtains a good husband.

## \|\| 3.8.53 \|\|

*dhanārthī dhanamāpnoti sarvakāmaikasādhanam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. He who seeks wealth gets wealth that is the sole means for the fulfilment of all desires.

## \|\| 3.8.54 \|\|

*māsamātraṃ naro bhaktyā śṛṇuyādyaḥ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*tasyābhīṣṭasamāvāptirdurlabhopi na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. If a man devoutly listens to this for a full month with concentration and purity, there is no doubt that what is wished for by him will be acquired even if it is rare.

## \|\| 3.8.55 \|\|

*ādhivyādhibhayaṃ ghoraṃ dāridrya kalahaṃ tathā \|*  
*yasya geheṣu māhātmyaṃ tatraitāni na karhicit \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Where this (text of) the greatness (of Badarī) is present, there is no danger from mental worry or physical ailment or trouble, poverty or strife. All these are not present at all in the houses where this (text of) greatness (of Badarī) is present.

## \|\| 3.8.56 \|\|

*nāpamṛtyurna sarpādi daurbhāgyaṃ cāpi vartate \|*  
*duḥsvapnagrahapīḍā ca pararāṣṭrabhayaṃ tathā \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. There is no premature death, nor danger from serpents etc. There is no ill-luck or mishap. There is no bad dream or affliction caused by evil spirits. There is no danger (of invasion) from other nations.

## Section 4 - Kārttikamāsa-māhātmya

## Chapter 1 - Praise of Kārttika Vow

## \|\| 4.1.1 \|\|

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe kārtikamāsamāhātmye kārtikavratapraśaṃsāvarṇanaṃnāma prathamo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Obeisance to Śrī Gaṇeśa

1\. One should recite this Purāṇa after bowing down to Nārāyaṇa (i.e. Kṛṣṇa) who abides in the hearts of men, Nara (Man i.e. Arjuna), Narottama (i.e. Sage Vyāsa who enlightens people and enhances their spiritual status) and Goddess Sarasvatī.

## \|\| 4.1.2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*sūta naḥ kathitaṃ puṇyaṃ māhātmyamāśvinasya ca \|*  
*bhūyo'nyacchrotumicchāmaḥ kārtikasya ca vaibhavam \|\| 2 \|\|*

The sages said:

2\. O Sūta, the meritorious greatness of the month of Āśvina has been recounted to us. We wish to hear about another thing (i.e. narration), the greatness of Kārttika (October-November).

## \|\| 4.1.3 \|\|

*kalau kaluṣacittānāṃ narāṇāṃ pāpakarmaṇām \|*  
*saṃsārābdhau nimagnānāmanāyāsena kā gatiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. What is the means of achieving the goal without strain in the Kali age in the case of men of sinful activities, whose minds are defiled by dirty thoughts and are immersed in the ocean of worldly affairs?

## \|\| 4.1.4 \|\|

*ko dharmaḥ sarvadharmāṇāmadhiko mokṣasādhakaḥ \|*  
*ihā'pi muktido nṛṇāmetattvaṃ kathaya prabho \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O holy Sir, please tell us that Dharma among all Dharmas which is the greatest means of achieving salvation, a giver of good results here and salvation (hereafter) to men.

## \|\| 4.1.5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*bhavadbhiryadahaṃ pṛṣṭastadetatpṛṣṭavānmuniḥ \|*  
*nārado brahmaṇaḥ putro brahmāṇaṃ tu jagadgurum \|\| 5 \|\|*

Sūta said:

5\. Nārada, the sage and son of Brahmā, asked Brahmā, the preceptor of the universe, the same question as I have been asked by you all.

## \|\| 4.1.6 \|\|

*tathaiva satyabhāmā ca śrīkṛṣṇaṃ jagadīśvaram \|*  
*apṛcchatkārtikasyaiva vaibhavaṃ śravaṇotsukā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Similarly, Satyabhāmā who was desirous of listening to the greatness of Kārttika asked Śrīkṛṣṇa, the Lord of the universe (the same question).

## \|\| 4.1.7 \|\|

*vālakhilyaiśca ṛṣibhiryaduktamṛṣisaṃsadi \|*  
*śrīsūryāruṇasaṃvādarūpeṇā'timanoharam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The same was recounted by the sages, Vālakhilyas, in the assembly of sages, in the form of a dialogue between the Sun-god and Aruṇa. It is extremely fascinating.

## \|\| 4.1.8 \|\|

*kailāse śaṃkareṇaiva kārtikasya ca vaibhavam \|*  
*varṇitaṃ ṣaṇmukhasyāgre nānākhyānasamanvitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On Kailāsa the greatness of Kārttika was recounted by Śaṅkara to Ṣaṇmukha (Skanda) along with various anecdotes and narratives.

## \|\| 4.1.9 \|\|

*pṛthuṃ prati nāradena kathitaṃ ca mahātmyakam \|*  
*kārtikasya ca vipreṃdrā śrutvā brahmamukhātpurā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. After hearing it in the olden time directly from Brahmā, O eminent Brāhmaṇas, the greatness of Kārttika was recounted to Pṛthu by Nārada.

## \|\| 4.1.10 \|\|

*ekadā nārado yogī satyalokamupāgataḥ \|*  
*papraccha vinayenaiva sarvalokapitāmaham \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Once Nārada, the Yogin, went to Satyalokā and humbly asked the Grandfather of all the worlds:

Śrī Nārada asked:

## \|\| 4.1.11 \|\|

*śrīnārada uvāca \|*  
*pāpeṃdhanasya ghorasya śuṣkārdrasya ca bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*ko vahnirdahate brahmaṃstadbhavānvaktumarhati \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. What is that fire, O Brahmā, that burns the fuel of terrible sins irrespective of its being dry or wet? It behoves you to recount it.

## \|\| 4.1.12 \|\|

*nājñātaṃ triṣu lokeṣu brahmāṃḍāṃtargatasya yat \|*  
*vidyate tava deveśa trividhasya suniścitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O Lord of Devas, surely there is nothing in the three worlds within the Cosmic Egg that is not known to you.

## \|\| 4.1.13 \|\|

*māsānāṃ pravaro māso devānāmuttamottamaḥ \|*  
*tīrthāni tadviśeṣeṇa kathayasva pitāmaha \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O Pitāmaha, name particularly the most excellent month among all the months, the most excellent one among the excellent Devas and (the most excellent Tīrtha among) Tīrthas.

Brahmā replied:

## \|\| 4.1.14 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*māsānāṃ kārtikaḥ śreṣṭho devānāṃ madhusūdanaḥ \|*  
*tīrthaṃ nārāyaṇākhyaṃ hi tritayaṃ durlabhaṃ kalau \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Among the months Kārttika is the most excellent; among Devas the Slayer of Madhu is the most excellent. The most excellent Tīrtha is the one called Nārāyaṇa. All these three are very rare in Kali age.

## \|\| 4.1.15 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*bhagavaṃstava dāso'smi bhakto'smi harivallabha \|*  
*vaiṣṇavānbrūhi me dharmānsarvajño'si pitāmaha \|\| 15 \|\|*

Nārada said:

15\. O Lord, I am your servant. I am your devotee, O favourite of Hari. Tell me (what are) the pious activities of Vaiṣṇavas. You are omniscient, O Pitāmaha.

## \|\| 4.1.16-17 \|\|

*ādau kārtikamāhātmyaṃ vaktumarhasi me prabho \|*  
*dīpadānasya māhātmyaṃ vratināṃ niyamāṃstathā \|\| 16 \|\|*

*gopīcaṃdanamāhātmyaṃ tulasyāśca tathā vibho \|*  
*dhātryāścaiva ca māhātmyaṃ vidhiṃ snānādikasya ca \|*  
*vratāraṃbhaḥ kadā kāryaṃ udyāpanavidhiṃ tathā \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. At the outset it behoves you to recount the greatness of Kārttika to me, O Lord. (Then) describe the greatness of the, gift of lamps, the holy observances of those who observe vows, the greatness of Gopīcandana (a species of white clay found near Dvārakā used for putting the vertical sectarian mark on the forehead) and that of Tulasī (the holy basil plant), the greatness of Dhātrī (Āmalaka—Emblic myrobalan) and the injunction regarding holy bath etc. When is the Vrata to be begun? Describe the procedure of Udyāpana (concluding rites).

## \|\| 4.1.18 \|\|

*yatkiṃcidvaiṣṇavaṃ dharmaṃ tatsarvaṃ vaktumarhasi \|*  
*yenā'haṃ tvatprasādena padaṃ yāsyāmyanāmayam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. It behoves you to recount all of whatever Vaiṣṇava observances there are. Thereby, with your favour, I shall go to the region devoid of ailments.

## \|\| 4.1.19 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iti putravacaḥ śrutvā brahmā harṣasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*rādhādāmodaraṃ smṛtvā provāca tanujaṃ prati \|\| 19 \|\|*

Sūta said:

19\. On hearing these words of his son Brahmā became delighted. After remembering Rādhā and Dāmodara, he spoke to his son:

## \|\| 4.1.20 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*sādhu pṛṣṭaṃ tvayā putra lokoddharaṇahetave \|*  
*kathayāmi na saṃdehaḥ kārtikasya ca vaibhavam \|\| 20 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

20\. What has been asked by you, O son, for the sake of uplifting the worlds, is well-put. There is no doubt. I shall tell you the greatness of Kārttika.

## \|\| 4.1.21 \|\|

*ekataḥ sarvatīrthāni sarve yajñāḥ sadakṣiṇāḥ \|*  
*kārtikasya tu māsasya kalāṃ nārhaṃti ṣoḍaśīm \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. On one side let there be all the Tīrthas and all the Yajñas with adequate monetary gifts (on the other side let there be the month of Kārttika). All those do not deserve (to possess) even a sixteenth part of the (greatness of the) month of Kārttika.

## \|\| 4.1.22 \|\|

*ekataḥ puṣkare vāsaḥ kurukṣetre himālaye \|*  
*ekataḥ kārtikaḥ putra sarvapuṇyādhiko mataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. On one side there is dwelling in Puṣkara or in Kurukṣetra or on the Himālaya mountain. On the other side there is Kārttika, O son, which is considered most meritorious of all.

## \|\| 4.1.23 \|\|

*svarṇāni merutulyāni sarvadānāni caikataḥ \|*  
*ekataḥ kārtiko vatsa sarvadā keśavapriyaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. There is on one side gold equal (in amount) to Meru and all types of charitable gifts and on the other side there is Kārttika, O son, which is always favoured by Keśava.

## \|\| 4.1.24 \|\|

*yatkiṃcitkriyate puṇyaṃ viṣṇumuddiśya kārtike \|*  
*tasya kṣayaṃ na paśyāmi mayoktaṃ tava nārada \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Whatever meritorious rite is performed in the month of Kārttika with Viṣṇu in view—I do not see any end to its merit. It has already been told (to you) by me, O Nārada.

## \|\| 4.1.25 \|\|

*sopānabhūtaṃ svargasya mānuṣyaṃ prāpya durlabham \|*  
*tathātmānaṃ samādadyānna bhraśyeta yathā punaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. On having got an extremely rare chance of being born as a human being which forms the staircase leading to heaven, one should maintain oneself in such a way that one will not fall back (to an inferior birth).

## \|\| 4.1.26 \|\|

*duṣprāpyaṃ prāpya mānuṣyaṃ kārtikoktaṃ carenna yaḥ \|*  
*dharmaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭha sa mātāpitṛghātakaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. After attaining human birth which is very difficult to get, if a man does not perform the holy rites prescribed for the month of Kārttika, O most excellent one among righteous souls, he is (no better than) a murderer of his mother and father.

## \|\| 4.1.27-31 \|\|

*kārtikaḥ khalu vai māsaḥ sarvamāseṣu cottamaḥ \|*  
*puṇyānāṃ paramaṃ puṇyaṃ pāvanānāṃ ca pāvanam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*asminmāse trayastriṃśaddevāḥ sannihitā mune \|*  
*atra snānānidānāni bhojanāni vratāni ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tiladhenuṃ hiraṇyaṃ ca rajataṃ bhūmivāsasī \|*  
*gopradānāni kurvaṃti sarvabhāvena nārada \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tāni dānāni dattāni gṛhṇaṃti vidhivatsurāḥ \|*  
*yatkiṃca dattaṃ vipreṃdra tapaścaiva tathā kṛtam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*tadakṣayyaphalaṃ proktaṃ viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|*  
*pāpānāṃ mokṣaṇaṃ caiva kārtike māsi śasyate \|\| 31 \|\|*

27-31. The month of Kārttika is the most excellent of all months. It is the most meritorious. It sanctifies all sanctifying things.

In this month, thirty-three Devas are present together, O sage. People perform all these rites now, O Nārada, with full devotion: holy baths; charitable gifts; feeding; holy rites; the various gifts of cow made of gingelly seeds, gold, silver, plots of land, garments and cows.

Suras duly accept those gifts made over (to deserving persons). Whatever is given, O eminent Brāhmaṇa, the penance that is performed, is said by Viṣṇu, the powerful one, to give inexhaustible merit. Relief from sins in the month of Kārttika is highly commended.

## \|\| 4.1.32-37 \|\|

*tasmādyatnena vipreṃdra kārtike māsi dīyate \|*  
*yatkiṃcitkārtike dattaṃ viṣṇumuddiśya mānavaiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tadakṣayaṃ hi labhate annadānaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*yathā nadīnāṃ vipreṃdra śailānāṃ caiva nārada \|\| 33 \|\|*

*udadhīnāṃ ca viprarṣe kṣayo naivopapadyate \|*  
*dānaṃ kārtikamāse tu yatkiṃciddīyate mune \|\| 34 \|\|*

*na tasyāsti kṣayo vipra pāpaṃ yāti sahasradhā \|*  
*saṃprāptaṃ kārtikaṃ dṛṣṭvā parānnaṃ yastu varjayet \|\| 35 \|\|*

*dinedine'tikṛcchrasya phalaṃ prāpnotyayatnataḥ \|*  
*na kārtikasamo māso na kṛtena samaṃ yugam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*na vedasadṛśaṃ śāstraṃ na tīrthaṃ gaṃgayā samam \|*  
*na cānnasadṛśaṃ dānaṃ na sukhaṃ bhāryayā samam \|\| 37 \|\|*

32-35a. Hence charitable gift is made with great care and effort, O Brāhmaṇa, in the month of Kārttika. Whatever is given in the month of Kārttika by men with Viṣṇu in view, especially the gift of cooked food, gives inexhaustible merit. Just as, O Nārada, O Brahminical sage, there is no destruction of rivers, mountains and oceans, so also, O sage, the gift that is made in the month of Kārttika has no destruction, O Brāhmaṇa. The sin is split into a thousand.

35b-37. On seeing the arrival of the month of Kārttika, if a man refrains from taking other people’s cooked food, everyday he secures without difficulty the benefit of the holy rite Atikṛcchra.

There is no month on a par with Kārttika. There is no Yuga equal to Kṛta. There is no scripture comparable with the Vedas. There is no Tīrtha on a par with Gaṅgā. There is no charitable gift on a par with that of cooked rice. There is no happiness on a par with that of the wife.

## \|\| 4.1.38 \|\|

*nyāyenopārjitaṃ dravyaṃ durlabhaṃ dānakāriṇām \|*  
*durlabhaṃ martyadharmāṇāṃ tīrthe ca pratipādanam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Wealth acquired by justifiable means is the rarest thing for those who make charitable gifts. Performance of rites by mortals in a Tīrtha is also a rare (chance).

## \|\| 4.1.39 \|\|

*kārtike muniśārdūla śāligrāmaśilārcanam \|*  
*smaraṇaṃ vāsudevasya kartavyaṃ pāpabhīruṇā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O tiger (i.e. prominent one) among sages, worship of Śālāgrāmā stone and remembrance of Vāsudeva are the rites that should be performed in Kārttika by one who is afraid of sins.

## \|\| 4.1.40 \|\|

*etādṛśaṃ kārtikaṃ ca akṛtenaiva yo nayet \|*  
*pūrvaṃ kṛtasya puṇyasya kṣayamāpnotyasaṃśayam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. If a person passes Kārttika of such a nature without doing anything (meritorious), he will certainly see the destruction of the merit acquired before.

## \|\| 4.1.41 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*aśaktena kathaṃ kāryaṃ kārtikavratamuttamam \|*  
*yena tatphalamāpnoti tanme vada pitāmaha \|\| 41 \|\|*

Nārada said:

41\. How is the excellent rite of Kārttika to be performed by a weak person? O Pitāmaha, tell me that whereby he too shall obtain its benefit,

## \|\| 4.1.42-45 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*aśaktastu yadā martyastadaivaṃ vratamācaret \|*  
*anyasmai draviṇaṃ dattvā kārayetkārtikavratam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*tasmātpuṇyaṃ pragṛhṇīta dānasaṃkalpapūrvakam \|*  
*dravyadāne'pyaśaktaścedyadā devarṣisattama \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tadā tena prakartavyaṃ pānaṃ tīrthajalasya ca \|*  
*tatrāpyaśakto yo martyastena nityaṃ harermudā \|\| 44 \|\|*

*smaraṇaṃ ca prakartavyaṃ nāmnā niyamapūrvakam \|*  
*akhaṃḍitaṃ tadā tena kārtikavratajaṃ phalam \|\| 45 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

42-45. If a man is (physically) incapable, he should perform the Vrata in the following manner. He should give money to another person and make him perform the Kārttika Vrata (for himself).

He should take the merit from him by means of the rite of Dana saṅkalpa (i.e. ceremonious pronouncement of religious gift).

If he is incapable of making monetary gifts, O excellent one among the divine sages, he should drink the water from the Tīrtha. If a person is incapable of doing that too, he should joyously remember Hari always and repeat the names with due observances. Then, he will acquire the full benefit of the Kārttika Vrata.

## \|\| 4.1.46-48 \|\|

*viṣṇoḥ śivasya vā kuryādālaye harijāgaram \|*
