## \|\| 4.13.9-11 \|\|

*svasvapuṇya prabhāvena viṣṇulokaṃ gatāvubhau \|*  
*tato guṇavatī śrutvā rakṣasā nihatāvubhau \|\| 9 \|\|*

*pitṛbhartṛjaduḥkhārtā kāruṇyaṃ paryadevayat \|*  
*sā gṛhopaskarā nsarvānvikrīyāśu ca karmaṃ tat \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tayoścakre yathāśakti pāralaukīṃ tataḥ kriyām \|*  
*tasminneva pure cakre vāsaṃ sā mṛtajīvinī \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. Both of them went to the world of Viṣṇu due to the power of their respective merits.

On hearing that both of them had been killed by a Rākṣasa, Guṇavatī became extremely distressed, having been separated from her husband as well as her father. She lamented in a pitiable manner. She quickly sold all the furniture, utensils etc. and performed according to her capacity their obsequies and other holy rites for (their) happiness in the other world. Living like a dead person, she continued to stay in the same city.

## \|\| 4.13.12 \|\|

*vratadvayaṃ tayā samyagājanmamaraṇātkṛtam \|*  
*ekādaśīvrataṃ samyaksevanaṃ kārtikasya ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Two Vratas were perfectly observed by her throughout her life till death, viz. the Vrata of Ekādaśī and the holy rite of Kārttika.

## \|\| 4.13.13-14 \|\|

*itthaṃ guṇavatī samyakpratyabda vratinī hyabhūt \|*  
*kadācitsarujā sā'tha kṛśāṃgī jvarapīḍitā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*snātuṃ gaṃgāṃ gatā kāṃte kathaṃcicchanakaistadā \|*  
*yāvajjalāṃtaragatā kaṃpitā śītapīḍitā \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Thus Guṇavatī performed the Vratas every year. Once that slender-bodied one became afflicted with fever. She was in great physical pain. O my beloved, with great difficulty she went slowly to Gaṅgā for taking her bath. When she entered the water, she became distressed with chillness. She shivered.

## \|\| 4.13.15-17 \|\|

*tāvatsā vihvalā'paśyadvimānaṃ yātamaṃbarāt \|*  
*atha sā tadvimānasthā vaikuṇṭhabhuvanaṃ yayau \|\| 15 \|\|*

*kārtikavratapuṇyena matsānnidhyaṃ gatā'bhavat \|*  
*atha brahmādidevānāṃ yadā prārthanayā bhuvam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*āgato'haṃ gaṇāḥ sarve yātāste'pi mayā saha \|*  
*ete hi yādavāḥ sarve madgaṇā eva bhāmini \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-16a. By that time the lady in distress saw an aerial chariot that had come from the sky. She got into that aerial chariot and went to the world of Vaikuṇṭha. Thanks to the merit of Kārttikavrata, she came to my presence.

16b-17. When I came to the earth at the request of the Devas headed by Brahmā, all those groups (of Devas) also came along with me. O beautiful lady, all these Yādavas are my own attendants.

## \|\| 4.13.18 \|\|

*pitā te devaśarmā'bhūtsatrājidabhidho hyayam \|*  
*yaścaṃdranāmā'so'krūrastvaṃ sā guṇavatī śubhā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Your father Devaśarmā now has the name Satrājit. He who had been called by the name Candra is Akrūra now and you are that splendid Guṇavatī.

## \|\| 4.13.19-23 \|\|

*kārtikavratapuṇyena bahu matprītidāyinī \|*  
*maddvāri yattvayā pūrvaṃ tulasīvāṭikā kṛtā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tasmādayaṃ kalpavṛkṣastavāṃgaṇagataḥ śubhe \|*  
*ājanmamaraṇātpūrvaṃ yatkṛtaṃ kārtikavratam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*kadācidapi tena tvaṃ madviyogaṃ na yāsyasi \|*  
*satyovāca \|*  
*māsānāṃ tu kathaṃ nāma sa māsaḥ kārtiko varaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*priyaste devadeveśa kāraṇaṃ tatra kathyatām \|*  
*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*sādhu pṛṣṭaṃ tvayā kāṃte śṛṇuṣvaikāgramānasā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*pṛthorvainyasya saṃvādaṃ maharṣernāradasya ca \|*  
*evameva purā pṛṣṭo nāradaḥ pṛthunābravīt \|\| 23 \|\|*

19-23. You gave me great delight, thanks to the merit of the Kārttikavrata.

Formerly a grove of Tulasī plants was made by you in front of my doorway. Hence, O splendid lady, the Kalpa tree (i.e. Pārijāta) has come to your courtyard. Since formerly you performed the Kārttika Vrata throughout your life till death, you will never be separated from me.

Satyā asked:

How did the month of Kārttika come to be the most excellent of all the months? O Lord of chiefs of Devas, why is it your favourite? Let the reason thereof be mentioned.

## \|\| 4.13.24 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*śaṃkhanāmā'bhavatpūrvamasuraḥ sāgarātmajaḥ \|*  
*indrādilokapālānāmadhikārāñjahāra ha \|\| 24 \|\|*

Śrīkṛṣṇa said:

O my beloved, you have asked an excellent question. Listen to me with great concentration.

I recount the dialogue between Pṭthu, the son of Vena, and Nārada, the great sage. Nārada was formerly asked in the same way by Pṛthu and he spoke thus:

Nārada said:

24\. Formerly there was an Asura named Śaṅkha. He was the son of Sāgara (Ocean). He usurped the powers of Indra and other Guardians of the Quarters.

## \|\| 4.13.25 \|\|

*suvarṇādriguhādurgasaṃsthitāstridaśādayaḥ \|*  
*tadvīkṣayāṃbabhūvuste tadā daityo vyacārayat \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The Devas and others hid themselves in the forts of the caves of the Golden Mountain (Meru). They watched (the activities of the Asura). Then the Daitya thought thus:

## \|\| 4.13.26 \|\|

*hṛtādhikārāstridaśā mayā yadyapi nirjitāḥ \|*  
*lakṣyaṃte balayuktāste karaṇīyaṃ mayā'tra kim \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. ‘Although the Devas have been vanquished by me and they have been divested of their powers, they appear to be strong. What should I do in this matter?

## \|\| 4.13.27 \|\|

*jñātaṃ tattu mayā devā vedamantrabalānvitāḥ \|*  
*tānhariṣye tataḥ sarve balahīnā bhavaṃti vai \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. I know it now. The Devas have the power due to the Vedic Mantras. I shall take them away. Thereupon all of them will become powerless.’

## \|\| 4.13.28 \|\|

*iti matvā tato daityo viṣṇumālakṣya nidritam \|*  
*satyalokājjahārāśu vedānādisvayaṃbhuvaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The Daitya thought thus and, on seeing Viṣṇu asleep, he took away the Vedas from the primordial self-born Lord Brahmā from Satyaloka.

## \|\| 4.13.29 \|\|

*nītāstu tena te vedāstadbhayātte nirākraman \|*  
*toyāni viviśuryajñamaṃtrabījasamanvitāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. While they were being carried away by him, the Vedas, out of fear of him, escaped and entered the waters along with the seeds of the Yajñamantras.

## \|\| 4.13.30 \|\|

*tānmārgamāṇaḥ śaṃkho'pi samudrāṃtargato bhraman \|*  
*na dadarśa tadā daityaḥ kvacidekatra saṃsthitān \|*  
*atha devaiḥ stuto viṣṇurbodhitastānuvāca ha \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. In search of them, Śaṅkha too entered the ocean. Wandering here and there the Daitya did not find them together anywhere. Then Viṣṇu, eulogized and awakened by the Devas, spoke to them:

## \|\| 4.13.31-32 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*varado'haṃ suragaṇā gītavādyādimaṃgalaiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*ūrjasya śuklaikādaśyāṃ bhavadbhiḥ pratibodhitaḥ \|*  
*ataścaiṣā tithirmānyā sā'tīva prītidā mama \|\| 32 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:

31-32. O groups of Suras, I am the bestower of boons. On the eleventh day in the bright half of the month of Kārttika, I have been awakened by you all through the auspicious sounds of musical instruments and songs. Hence this Tithi (Lunar day) should be honoured much.

It is exceedingly delightful to me.

## \|\| 4.13.33 \|\|

*vedāḥ śaṃkhahṛtāḥ sarve tiṣṭhaṃtyudakasaṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*tānānayāmyahaṃ devā hatvā sāgaranaṃdanam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. All the Vedas carried away by Śaṅkha now lie submerged in the waters. O Devas, I shall bring them all after killing the son of the Ocean.

## \|\| 4.13.34 \|\|

*adyaprabhṛti vedāstu maṃtrabījasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*pratyabdaṃ kārtike māsi viśramaṃtvapsu sarvadā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. From this day onwards forever, let the Vedas along with the mystic seeds of Mantras take rest in the waters in the month of Kārttika every year.

## \|\| 4.13.35 \|\|

*kāle'sminye prakurvaṃti prātaḥsnānaṃ narottamāḥ \|*  
*te sarve yajñā'vabhṛthaiḥ susnātāḥ syurna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. During this period (Kārttika), those excellent men who take the holy bath in the morning, will all be as though they have taken the Avabhṛtha bath (valedictory bath after a sacrifice). There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 4.13.36 \|\|

*adyaprabhṛtyahamapi bhavāmi jalamadhyagaḥ \|*  
*bhavanto'pi mayā sārddhamāyāṃtu samunīśvarāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. From today onwards I shall be in the middle of the waters. All of you along with the leading sages may also come along with me.

## \|\| 4.13.37 \|\|

*kātikavratināṃ ceṃdra rakṣā kāryā tvayā sadā \|*  
*ityuktvā bhagavānviṣṇuḥ śapharītulyarūpadhṛk \|*  
*khātpapāta jale viṃdhyavāsinaḥ kasya paśyataḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O Indra, protection should always be accorded to those who observe Kārttikavrata, by you.

After saying this, Lord Viṣṇu assumed the form of a Śapharī fish and plunged into the water from the sky even as Brahmā staying on Vindhya was watching.

## \|\| 4.13.38 \|\|

*hatvā śaṃkhāsuraṃ viṣṇurbadarīvanamāgamat \|*  
*tatrā'hūya ṛṣīnsarvānidamājñāpayatprabhuḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. After killing Asura Śaṅkha Viṣṇu went to the forest of Badarī. There the Lord called together all the sages and commanded thus:

## \|\| 4.13.39 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*jalāṃtaraviśīrṇāṃstānyūyaṃ vedānpramārgatha \|*  
*ānayadhvaṃ ca tvaritāḥ sāgarasya jalāṃtarāt \|*  
*tāvatprayāgaṃ tiṣṭhāmi devatāgaṇasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:

39\. O you all, do search for the Vedas scattered within the waters. Bring them quickly from the midst of the waters of the sea. Till then I shall remain at Pravāga accompanied by the groups of Devas.

## \|\| 4.13.40-42 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*tatastaissarvamunibhistapobalasamanvitaiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*uddhṛtāśca sabījāste vedā yajñasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*teṣu yāvanmitaṃ yena labdhaṃ tāvaddhi tasya tat \|\| 41 \|\|*

*sa sa eva ṛṣirjātastattatprabhṛti pārthiva \|*  
*atha sarve'pi saṃgamya prayāgaṃ munayo yayuḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

Nārada said:

40-42. Thereafter those Vedas along with their Bījas (seeds) and the Yajñas were redeemed by all those sages endowed with the power of penance. O king, the number of Mantras for each (sage) was as much as he redeemed or found. Since then he came to be regarded as the sage (seer) of those Mantras. Then all the sages joined together and went to Prayāga.

## \|\| 4.13.43 \|\|

*viṣṇave savidhātre te labdhānvedānnyavedayan \|*  
*labdhvā vedānsamagrāṃstu brahmā harṣasamanvitaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. They submitted all the Vedas they recovered to Viṣṇu accompanied by Brahmā. After regaining the entire set of Vedas Brahmā became delighted.

## \|\| 4.13.44 \|\|

*ayajadvājimedhena devarṣigaṇasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*yajñāṃ'te devatāḥ sarve vijñaptiṃ cakruraṃjasā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Accompanied by the groups of Celestial Sages, he performed a horse-sacrifice. At the end of the Yajña all the Devas submitted their requests immediately.

## \|\| 4.13.45 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*devadeva jagannātha vijñaptiṃ śṛṇu naḥ prabho \|*  
*harṣakālo'yamasmākaṃ tasmāttvaṃ varado bhava \|\| 45 \|\|*

The Devas said:

45\. O Lord of Devas, O Lord of the universe, listen to our prayer and submission. This is the period of delight for us. Hence be the bestower of boons.

## \|\| 4.13.46 \|\|

*sthāne'smindruhiṇo vedānnaṣṭānprāpa punastvayam \|*  
*yajñabhāgānvayaṃ prāptāstvatprasādādramāpate \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. With your favour, O Lord of Ramā, Brahmā regained the lost Vedas in this place. We too got back our shares in the Yajñas.

## \|\| 4.13.47 \|\|

*sthānametaddhi naḥ śreṣṭhaṃ pṛthivyāṃ puṇyavardhanam \|*  
*bhuktimuktipradaṃ cā'stu prasādādbhavataḥ sadā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. With your favour let this spot be the bestower of worldly pleasures and salvation and one that increases merits. Let it be the most excellent place for us on the earth.

## \|\| 4.13.48 \|\|

*kālo'pyayaṃ mahāpuṇyo brahmaghnā'diviśuddhikṛt \|*  
*dattā'kṣayakaraṃ cā'stu varamevaṃ dadasva naḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Let this time be highly meritorious. Let it be the sanctifier of even the murderer of a Brāhmaṇa. It should cause the increase of everything given. Let it have everlasting benefit. Grant this boon to us.

## \|\| 4.13.49 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*mamāpyetadvṛtaṃ devā yadbhavadbhirudāhṛtam \|*  
*tathāstu sulabhaṃ tvetadbrahmakṣetramitipratham \|\| 49 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:

49\. O Devas, this (place) has been chosen by me. What you all requested has been accepted by me. Let this spot be easily accessible. Let it be famous by the name Brahmakṣetra.

## \|\| 4.13.50 \|\|

*sūryavaṃśodbhavo rājā gaṃgāmatrānayiṣyati \|*  
*sā sūryakanyayā cātra kāliṃdyā yogameṣyati \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. A king born of the solar race (viz. Bhagīratha) will bring Gaṅgā here. It will be joined by Kālindī, the daughter of the Sun-god, here.

## \|\| 4.13.51 \|\|

*yūyaṃ ca sarve brahmādyā nivasaṃtu mayā saha \|*  
*tīrtharājeti vikhyātaṃ tīrthametadbhaviṣyati \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. All of you including Brahmā should stay with me. This Tīrtha shall become well known as Tīrtharāja.

## \|\| 4.13.52-53 \|\|

*sarvapāpāni naśyaṃti tīrtharājasya darśanāt \|*  
*sūrye makarage prāpte snāyināṃ pāpanāśanaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*kālo'pyeṣa mahāpuṇyaphalado'stu sadā nṛṇām \|*  
*sālokyādiphalaṃ snānairmāghe makarage ravau \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. By mere sight of Tīrtharāja all the sins perish. It destroys the sins of those who take bath there when the Sun is in the Zodiac Capricorn. Let this period be the bestower of great merit unto men always. In the month of Māgha, when the Sun is in Capricorn, it shall grant the type of liberation called Sālokya.

## \|\| 4.13.54 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ devāndevadevastaduktvā tatraivāṃtardhānamāgātsavedhāḥ \|*  
*devāḥ sarvepyaṃśakaiste'pyatiṣṭhaṃścāṃtardhānaṃ prāpuriṃdrādayaste \|\| 54 \|\|*

Nārada said:

54\. After saying this to Devas, the Lord of Devas vanished there itself along with Brahmā. All the Devas remained there partially. Indra and others then vanished.

## Chapter 14 - The Birth of Jalandhara

## \|\| 4.14.1-3 \|\|

*pṛthuruvāca \|*  
*yattvayā kathitaṃ brahmanvratamūrjasya vistarāt \|*  
*tatra yā tulasīmūle viṣṇoḥ pūjā tvayoditā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tenā'haṃ praṣṭumicchāmi māhātmyaṃ tulasībhavam \|*  
*kathaṃ sā'tipriyā tasya devadevasya śārṅgiṇaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kathameṣā samutpannā kasminsthāne ca nārada \|*  
*evaṃ brūhi samāsena sarvajño'si mato mama \|\| 3 \|\|*

Pṛthu said:

1-3. O Brāhmṇa, the Vrata of Kārttika has been recounted in detail by you. But therein the worship of Viṣṇu at the root of Tulasī has also been enjoined by you. I, therefore, wish to ask you about the greatness of Tulasī. How is it that it became a great favourite of the Śārṅga-bearing Lord of Devas? How did it originate? O Nārada, at what place did it originate? Describe this succinctly. You are respected as an omniscient person by me.

## \|\| 4.14.4 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu rājannavahito māhātmyaṃ tulasībhavam \|*  
*setihāsaṃ purāvṛttaṃ tatsarvaṃ kathayāmi te \|\| 4 \|\|*

Nārada said:

4\. O king, listen attentively to the greatness of Tulasī. I shall describe everything along with its legendary story that happened formerly.

## \|\| 4.14.5 \|\|

*purā śakraḥ śivaṃ draṣṭumagātkailāsaparvatam \|*  
*sarvadevaiḥ parivṛto hyapsarogaṇasevitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Formerly Śakra went to the Kailāsa mountain to pay a visit to Siva. He was surrounded by all the Devas and accompanied by groups of celestial damsels.

## \|\| 4.14.6 \|\|

*yāvadgataḥ śivagṛhaṃ tāvattatra sa dṛṣṭavān \|*  
*puruṣaṃ bhīmakarmāṇaṃ daṃṣṭrā'nanavibhīṣaṇam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. When he reached the abode of Śiva, he saw a person of terrible activities there. He was highly terrifying on account of his curved teeth and hideous face.

## \|\| 4.14.7 \|\|

*sa pṛṣṭastena kastvaṃ bhoḥ kva gato jagadīśvaraḥ \|*  
*evaṃ punaḥ punaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ sa tadā noktavānnṛpa \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He was asked by him (Indra): “Who are you? Where has the Lord of the universe gone?” Though asked thus frequently, O king, he did not reply.

## \|\| 4.14.8-9 \|\|

*tataḥ kuddho vajrapāṇistaṃ nirbhartsya vaco'bravīt \|*  
*re mayā pṛcchayamāno'pi nottaraṃ dattavānasi \|\| 8 \|\|*

*atastvāṃ hanmi vajreṇa kaste trātā'sti durmate \|*  
*ityudīrya tato vajrī vajreṇā'bhyahanaddṛḍham \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Then the infuriated Lord with the thunderbolt in his hand rebuked him and spoke these words: “Oh! Though you are being asked by me, you have not replied. Hence I shall kill you with my thunderbolt. O vicious-minded one, who is there to save you?” After saying this, the Thunderbolt-bearing Lord smote him with force with his thunderbolt.

## \|\| 4.14.10 \|\|

*tenāsya kaṇṭho nīlatvamagādvajraṃ ca bhasmatām \|*  
*tato rudraḥ prajajvāla tejasā pradahanniva \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Thereby his throat became blue and the thunderbolt was reduced to ash. Then Rudra blazed with his refulgence as if he would burn (everything).

## \|\| 4.14.11 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā bṛhaspatistūrṇaṃ kṛtāṃjalipuṭo'bhavat \|*  
*indraṃ ca daṃḍavadbhūmau kṛtvā stotuṃ pracakrame \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. On seeing it Bṛhaspati immediately joined his palms in reverence. He made Indra prostrate flat on the ground and began to eulogize.

## \|\| 4.14.12 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*namo devādhipataye tryaṃbakāya kapardine \|*  
*tripuraghnāya śarvāya namo'dhaṃkaniṣūdine \|\| 12 \|\|*

Bṛhaspati said:

12\. Obeisance to the overlord of Devas, to the Three-eyed Lord with matted hair. Obeisance to the slayer of Tripuras, to Śarva, to the destroyer of Andhaka.

## \|\| 4.14.13 \|\|

*virūpāyā'tirūpāya bahurūpāya śaṃbhave \|*  
*yajñavidhvaṃsakartre ca yajñānāṃ phaladāyine \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Bow to the lord with a hideous form, to the lord who is beyond all forms, to Śaṃbhu of many forms. Obeisance to the lord who caused destruction to (Dakṣa’s) Yajña, to the lord who grants the benefit of Yajñas.

## \|\| 4.14.14 \|\|

*iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe kārtikamāsamāhātmye jalaṃdharotpattivarṇanaṃnāma caturdaśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Obeisance to the destroyer of Kāla (Death), to Kāla (Time), to the lord holding black serpents. Salute to the destroyer of Brahmā’s head. Obeisance, obeisance to the Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 4.14.15 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ stutastadā śaṃbhurdhiṣaṇena jagāda tam \|*  
*saṃharannayanajvālāṃ trilokīdahana kṣamām \|\| 15 \|\|*

Nārada said:

15\. On being eulogized thus by Bṛhaspati, Śaṃbhu said to him after withdrawing the flame of fire issuing from the eye—the fire that was capable of burning the three worlds:

## \|\| 4.14.16 \|\|

*varaṃ varaya bho brahmanprītaḥ stutyā'nayā tava \|*  
*indrasya jīvadānena jīveti tvaṃ prathāṃ vajra \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. “O Brāhmaṇa, choose a boon. I am pleased with this eulogy of yours. Since you granted life unto Indra, attain the reputation as Jīva.”

## \|\| 4.14.17 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*yadi tuṣṭo'si deva tvaṃ pāhīṃdraṃ śaraṇāgatam \|*  
*agnireṣa śamaṃ yātu bhālanetrasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

Bṛhaspati said:

17\. If you are pleased, O Lord, you do protect Indra who seeks refuge in you. Let this fire issuing from the eye in the forehead subside.

## \|\| 4.14.18 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*punaḥ praveśamāyāti bhālanetre kathaṃ śikhī \|*  
*enaṃ tyakṣyāmyahaṃ dūre yatheṃdraṃ naiva pīḍayet \|\| 18 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

18\. How can the fire re-enter the eye in the forehead? I shall cast this off very far, so that it will not trouble Indra.

## \|\| 4.14.19 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā taṃ kare dhṛtvā prākṣipallavaṇārṇave \|*  
*so'patatsiṃdhugaṃgāyāḥ sāgarasya ca saṃgame \|\| 19 \|\|*

Nārada said:

19\. After saying thus he took hold of it in his hand and threw it into the briny sea. It fell where the river Sindhu met the ocean.

## \|\| 4.14.20 \|\|

*tāvatsa bālarūpatvamagāttatra ruroda ca \|*  
*rudatastasya śabdena prākaṃpaddharaṇī muhuḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. By that time it assumed the form of a child and began to cry. Due to the noise of his cries the entire earth shook frequently.

## \|\| 4.14.21 \|\|

*svargādyāḥ satyalokāṃtāstatsvanādbadhirīkṛtāḥ \|*  
*śrutvā brahmā yayau tatra kimetaditi vismitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. All the worlds beginning with Svarga (heaven) and ending with Satyaloka became deafened due to that noise. On hearing it Brahmā went there wondering what it was.

## \|\| 4.14.22-23 \|\|

*tāvatsamudrasyotsaṃge taṃ bālaṃ sa dadarśa ha \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā brahmāṇamāyātaṃ samudro'pi kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*praṇamya śirasā bālaṃ tasyotsaṃge nyaveśayat \|*  
*bho brahmansiṃdhugaṃgāyāṃ jāto'yaṃ mama putrakaḥ \|*  
*jātakarmā'disaṃskārānkuruṣvā'dya jagadguro \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. He saw the boy in the lap of the Ocean. On seeing Brahmā coming, the Ocean joined his palms in reverence, bowed down his head and placed the boy on his lap:

“O Brahmā, my son was born in the place where the river Sindhu joins the ocean. O Sire of the universe, perform the post-natal consecratory rites for him.”

## \|\| 4.14.24-25 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*itthaṃ vadati pāthodhau sa bālaḥ sāgarātmajaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*brahmāṇamagrahītkūrce vidhunvaṃstaṃ muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*dhunvatastasya kūrce tu netrābhyāmagamajjalam \|*  
*kathaṃcinmuktakūrco'tha brahmā provāca sāgaram \|\| 25 \|\|*

Nārada said:

24-25. While the Ocean said so, the boy, the son of the Ocean, caught hold of the beard of Brahmā and shook it frequently. As the beard was pulled thus, water flowed from his (Brahmā’s) eyes. Somehow Brahmā extricated his beard and spoke to the Ocean:

## \|\| 4.14.26 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*netrābhyāṃ vidhṛtaṃ yasmādanenaitajjalaṃ mama \|*  
*tasmājjalaṃdhara iti khyāto nāmnā bhaviṣyati \|\| 26 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

26\. Since the water flowing from my eyes was held by him, he will become famous by the name Jalandhara.

## \|\| 4.14.27-28 \|\|

*anenaivaiṣa taruṇaḥ sarvaśastrāstrapāragaḥ \|*  
*avadhyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ vinā rudraṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 27 \|\|*

*yata eṣa samudbhūtastatraivāṃtaṃ gamiṣyati \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. For this very reason, when he becomes a youth, he will become a master of all missiles and weapons. He will be invincible to all living beings, except Rudra. He will attain his end at the place where he was born.

## \|\| 4.14.29 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā śukramāhūya rājye taṃ cābhyaṣecayat \|*  
*āmaṃtrya saritāṃ nāthaṃ brahmāṃtardhānamāgamat \|\| 29 \|\|*

Nārada said:

29\. On saying this, he called Śukra and made him crown him as king in the realm. After taking leave of the Ocean, Brahmā vanished,

## \|\| 4.14.30 \|\|

*atha taddarśanotphullanayanaḥ sāgarastadā \|*  
*kālanemisutāṃ vṛṃdāṃ tadbhāryārthamayācata \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The Ocean had his eyes beaming like full-blown lotus at his sight. He requested Kālanemi for the hand of Vṛndā, his daughter, to be the wife unto his son.

## Chapter 15 - The Victories of Jalandhara

## \|\| 4.15.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*ye devairnirjitāḥ pūrvaṃ daityāḥ pātālasaṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*te'pi bhūmaṃḍalaṃ yātā nirbhayāstamupāśritāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:

1\. Daityas who had been formerly defeated by Devas and who had been staying in the nether worlds came without any fear whatsoever to the earth and resorted to him.

## \|\| 4.15.2 \|\|

*kadācicchinnaśirasaṃ rāhuṃ dṛṣṭvā sa daityarāṭ \|*  
*papraccha bhārgavaṃ tatra tacchiraśchedakāraṇam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Once, on seeing Rāhu with his head cut, that king of Daityas asked Śukra about the cause of his head being cut off.

## \|\| 4.15.3 \|\|

*sa śaśaṃsa samudrasya mathanaṃ devakāritam \|*  
*ratnāpaharaṇaṃ caiva daityānāṃ ca parābhavam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He told him the detailed story of the churning of the Ocean, the fact that all jewels were taken away by Devas and the defeat of the Daityas etc.

## \|\| 4.15.4 \|\|

*sa śrutvā krodharaktākṣaḥ svapiturmathanaṃ tadā \|*  
*dūtaṃ saṃpreṣayāmāsa ghasmaraṃ śakrasannidhau \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. On hearing about the churning of his father (i.e. Ocean), he became furious with eyes turned red. He sent Ghasmara as his messenger to the presence of Śakra.

## \|\| 4.15.5 \|\|

*dūtastriviṣṭapaṃ gatvā sudharmāṃ prāviśadvarām \|*  
*jagādākharvamaulistu deveṃdraṃ vākyamadbhutam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The messenger went to heaven and entered the excellent (Assembly of Indra called) Sudharmā. With his head raised up (with self-respect) the messenger spoke to Devendra the following wonderful words.

## \|\| 4.15.6 \|\|

*ghasmara uvāca \|*  
*jalaṃdharo'bdhitanayaḥ sarvadaityajaneśvaraḥ \|*  
*dūto'haṃpreṣitastena sa yadāha śṛṇuṣva tat \|\| 6 \|\|*

Ghasmara said:

6\. Jalandhara, the son of the Ocean, is the lord of all the Daitya-folks. I am sent by him as his messenger. Hear what he says:

## \|\| 4.15.7 \|\|

*kasmāttvayā mama pitā mathitaḥ sāgaro'driṇā \|*  
*nītāni sarvaratnāni tāni śīghraṃ prayaccha me \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. “Why was my father, the Ocean, churned by you with a mountain? All the jewels had been carried away (by you). Return all those things to me immediately.”

## \|\| 4.15.8 \|\|

*iti dūtavacaḥ śrutvā vismitastridaśādhipaḥ \|*  
*uvāca ghasmaraṃ raudraṃ bhayaroṣasamanvitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On hearing these words of the messenger the Lord of Devas became surprised. Moved by fear as well as anger, he spoke to the terrible Ghasmara:

## \|\| 4.15.9-10 \|\|

*iṃdra uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu dūta mayā pūrvaṃ mathitaḥ sāgaro yathā \|*  
*adrayo madbhayāttrastāḥ svakukṣisthāḥ kṛtāstathā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*anye'pi maddviṣastena rakṣitā ditijāḥ purā \|*  
*tasmādyattatprajātaṃ tu mayā'pyapahṛtaṃ kila \|\| 10 \|\|*

Indra said:

9-10. Listen, O messenger, why the Ocean was churned by me formerly. The Mountains who were afraid of me were kept by him within his bowels. Other enemies too of mine, Daityas, were accorded shelter by him formerly. Hence, what came out of him has been taken away by me.

## \|\| 4.15.11 \|\|

*śaṃkho'pyevaṃ purā devānadviṣatsāgarātmajaḥ \|*  
*mamā'nujena nihataḥ praviṣṭaḥ sāgarodaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Śaṅkha too, a son of the Ocean, became inimical to Devas formerly. He was killed by my younger brother (Viṣṇu) and he entered the bowels of the Ocean for good.

## \|\| 4.15.12 \|\|

*tadgaccha kathayasvā'sya sarvaṃ mathanakāraṇam \|*  
*nārada uvāca \|*  
*itthaṃ visarjito dūtastadeṃdreṇā'gamadbhuvam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12a. Therefore, go and tell him everything about the cause of the churning (of the Ocean).

Nārada said:

12b. Thus the messenger who was sent back by Indra went to the earth.

## \|\| 4.15.13 \|\|

*tadidaṃ vacanaṃ sarvaṃ daityāyākathayattadā \|*  
*tanniśamya tadā daityo roṣātprasphuritā'dharaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then he told the Daitya all these words. On hearing them the Daitya became furious. His lips throbbed due to anger.

## \|\| 4.15.14 \|\|

*daityasenāsamāyukto yayau yoddhuṃ triviṣṭapam \|*  
*tato yuddhe mahāñjāto devadānavasaṃkṣayaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Accompanied by the army of Daityas, he went to heaven in order to fight. Then in that war the destruction of Devas and Dānavas was excessive.

## \|\| 4.15.15 \|\|

*iti śrī skānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe kārtikamāsamāhātmye jalaṃdharavijayaprāptirnāma pañcadaśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Bhārgava (i.e. Śukra) resuscitated all those Daityas who died in the war there by means of his Vidyā (secret formula) named Mṛtajīvanī (‘enlivener of the dead’) and with water drops charged with Mantras.

## \|\| 4.15.16 \|\|

*devānapi tathā yuddhe tatrā'jīvayadaṃgirāḥ \|*  
*divyauṣadhī samānīya droṇādreḥ sa punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Aṅgiras (i.e. Bṛhaspati) acquired divine medicinal herbs from the Droṇa mountain frequently and resuscitated the Devas who were killed in the war.

## \|\| 4.15.17 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā devāṃstathā yuddhe punareva samutthitān \|*  
*jalaṃdharaḥ krodhavaśo bhārgavaṃ vākyamabravīt \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On seeing that the (resuscitated) Devas were coming up again in the battle, Jalandhara became furious and he spoke these words to Bhārgava:

## \|\| 4.15.18 \|\|

*jalaṃdhara uvāca \|*  
*mayā yuddhe hatā devā uttiṣṭhaṃti kathaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*tava saṃjīvinīvidyā na vā'nyatreti viśrutam \|\| 18 \|\|*

Jalandhara said:

18\. How is it that the Devas killed by me in the battle rise up again? It is well-known that your Vidyā named Sañjīvinī is not known to others.

## \|\| 4.15.19 \|\|

*śukra uvāca \|*  
*divyauṣadhīḥ samānīya droṇādreraṃgirāḥ surān \|*  
*jīvayatyeva tacchīghraṃ droṇādriṃ tvamapāhara \|\| 19 \|\|*

Śukra said:

19\. Aṅgiras brings divine herbs from the Droṇa mountain and resuscitates the Suras. Hence you remove the Droṇa mountain quickly.

## \|\| 4.15.20 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*ityuktaḥ sa tu daityeṃdro nītvā droṇācalaṃ tadā \|*  
*prākṣipatsāgare tūrṇaṃ punarāgānmahāhavam \|\| 20 \|\|*

Nārada said:

20\. On being told thus, the Lord of Daityas carried the Droṇa mountain and cast it into the ocean. Then he returned to the battlefield quickly.

## \|\| 4.15.21 \|\|

*atha devānhatāndṛṣṭvā droṇādrimagamadguruḥ \|*  
*tāvattatra girīṃdraṃ tu na dadarśa surārcitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. On seeing the Devas being killed, Guru (i.e. Bṛhaspati) went to the Droṇa mountain but the preceptor who was honoured by the Suras could not find the important mountain there.

## \|\| 4.15.22 \|\|

*jñātvā daityahṛtaṃ droṇaṃ dhiṣaṇo bhayavihvalaḥ \|*  
*āgatya dūrādvyājahre śvāsā'kulitavigrahaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. On coming to know that the Droṇa mountain had been taken away by the Daitya, Dhiṣaṇa (Bṛhaspati) became frightened. He came to the battleground and spoke from a distance with all his body gasping for breath:

## \|\| 4.15.23 \|\|

*palāyadhvaṃ havāddevā nā'yaṃ jetuṃ kṣamo yataḥ \|*  
*rudrāṃśasaṃbhavo hyeṣa smaradhvaṃ śakraceṣṭitam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. “Run away from the battle, O Devas. This (Daitya) cannot be vanquished because he is born of a part of Rudra. Remember the act of Śakra (such as striking the Bhīma Puruṣa with Vajra).”

## \|\| 4.15.24 \|\|

*śrutvā tadvacanaṃ devā bhayavihvalitāstadā \|*  
*daityena vadhyamānāste palāyaṃte diśo daśa \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. On hearing his words the Devas became alarmed. On being killed and hit by the Daitya they ran to all the ten directions.

## \|\| 4.15.25 \|\|

*devānvidrāvitāndṛṣṭvā daityaiḥ sāgaranaṃdanaḥ \|*  
*śaṃkhabherījayaravaiḥ praviveśā'marāvatīm \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. On seeing that the Devas had been routed by the Daityas, the son of the Ocean entered Amarāvatī to the accompaniment of the victorious sounds of conchs and Bherī drums.

## \|\| 4.15.26 \|\|

*praviṣṭe nagarīṃ daitye devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ \|*  
*suvarṇādriguhāṃ prāptā nyavasandaityatāpitāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. When the Daitya entered the city, the Devas with Śakra as their leader went to the cave of the Meru mountain and stayed there. They were excessively harassed by the Daityas.

## Chapter 16 - Nārada Visits Jalandhara

## \|\| 4.16.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*punardaityaṃ samāyāṃtaṃ dṛṣṭvā devāḥ savāsavāḥ \|*  
*bhayaprakaṃpitāḥ sarve viṣṇuṃ stotuṃ pracakramuḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:

1\. On seeing the Daitya coming once again, all the Devas including Indra trembled with fear and they began to eulogize Viṣṇu:

## \|\| 4.16.2 \|\|

*namo matsyakūrmādinānāsvarūpaiḥ sadābhaktakāryodyatāyā'rtihaṃtre \|*  
*vidhātrādisargasthitidhvaṃsakartre gadāśaṃkhapadmārihastāya testu \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. “Obeisance to you who always are prepared to carry out the tasks of your devotees through (assuming) various forms such as that of the Fish, Tortoise and others; to the dispeller of agony, to the lord, the cause of creation, sustenance and annihilation of Brahmā and others, to the lord holding iron club, conch, lotus and discus in the hands.

## \|\| 4.16.3-4 \|\|

*ramā vallabhāyā'surāṇāṃ nihaṃtre bhujaṃgāriyānāya pītāṃbarāya \|*  
*makhādikriyāpākakartre vikartre śaraṇyāya tasmai natāḥ smo natāḥ smaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*namo daityasaṃtāpitāmartyaduḥkhācaladhvaṃsadaṃbholaye viṣṇave te \|*  
*bhujaṃgeśatalpeśayāyārkacaṃdradvinetrāya tasmai natāḥ smo natāḥ smaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Repeatedly we bow to the lover of Ramā, to the slayer of Asuras, to the lord whose vehicle is (Garuḍa) the enemy of serpents, to the yellow-robed lord, to the lord who gives the fruits of yajñas and other holy rites, to the bestower (or to the lord who is the cause of all the created beings), to the lord who is worthy of being sought refuge in. We bow down to him again and again. Like the thunderbolt which destroys mountains, the Lord dispels the (mountains of) miseries of the immortal ones tortured by the Daityas. Obeisance to you, to Viṣṇu, to the Lord who lies on the couch of the Lord of Serpents. We repeatedly salute the Lord whose two eyes are the Sun and the Moon.”

## \|\| 4.16.5 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*saṃkaṣṭanāśanaṃnāma stotrametatpaṭhennaraḥ \|*  
*sa kadācinna saṃkaṣṭaiḥ pīḍyate kṛpayā hareḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Nārada said:

5\. One who reads or recites this prayer named Saṃkaṣṭanāśa (‘Destroyer of distress’) is never afflicted with distresses and troubles due to the mercy of Hari.

## \|\| 4.16.6 \|\|

*iti devāḥ stutiṃ yāvatkurvaṃti danujadviṣaḥ \|*  
*tāvatsurāṇāmāpattirvijñātā viṣṇunā tadā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. By the time the Devas concluded the prayer to the Enemy of the Dānavas, the calamity of the Suras had come to be known to Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 4.16.7 \|\|

*sahasotthāya daityāriḥ sakrodhaḥ khinnamānasaḥ \|*  
*ārūḍho garuḍaṃ vegāllakṣmīṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The Enemy of the Daityas got up suddenly with great fury. He was distressed in his mind. Mounting Garuḍa hurriedly he spoke to Lakṣmī:

## \|\| 4.16.8 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*jalaṃdhareṇa te bhrātrā devānāṃ kadanaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*tairāhūto gamiṣyāmi yuddhāyādya tvarānvitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

8\. Great havoc has been played with the Devas by your brother Jalandhara. Called by them, I shall go hurriedly for fighting (with him).

## \|\| 4.16.9 \|\|

*śrīruvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ te vallabhā nātha bhaktyā ca yadi sarvadā \|*  
*tatkathaṃ te mama bhrātā yuddhe vadhyaḥ kṛpānidhe \|\| 9 \|\|*

Śrī said:

9\. O Lord, if due to my perpetual devotion to you I am your beloved, O storehouse of mercy, how can my brother be worthy of being killed (by you) in battle?

## \|\| 4.16.10 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*rudrāṃśasaṃbhavatvācca brahmaṇo vacanādapi \|*  
*prītyā ca tava naivāyaṃ mama vadhyo jalaṃdharaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

10\. As he is born of a part of Rudra, because of the word (conferring boon) of Brahmā and because of my love to you Jalandhara is not worthy of being killed by me.

## \|\| 4.16.11 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā garuḍārūḍhaḥ śaṃkhacakragadāsibhṛt \|*  
*viṣṇurvegādyayau yoddhuṃ yatra devāḥ stuvaṃti te \|\| 11 \|\|*

Nārada said:

11\. After saying this, Viṣṇu bearing the conch, the discus, the iron club and the sword got on to Garuḍa and rushed to the place where the Devas stood praying to him. He went there in order to fight (with the Demon).

## \|\| 4.16.12 \|\|

*athā'ruṇānujātyugrapakṣavātaprapīḍitāḥ \|*  
*vātyā vimarditā daityā babhramuḥ khe yathā ghanāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Afflicted with the dreadful gusts of wind from the wings of Garuḍa, the Daityas whirled about like clouds in the sky shattered and scattered by violent storms.

## \|\| 4.16.13 \|\|

*tato jalaṃdharo dṛṣṭvā daityānvātyāprapīḍitān \|*  
*udvṛttanayanaḥ krodhāttatoviṣṇuṃ samabhyayāt \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On seeing the Daityas afflicted with the violent gust of wind, Jalandhara rolled his eyes in fury and then rushed at Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 4.16.14 \|\|

*tataḥ samabhavadyuddhaṃ viṣṇudaityeṃdrayormahat \|*  
*ākāśaṃ kurvatorbāṇaistadā niravakāśavat \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Then a fierce fight ensued between Viṣṇu and the king of Daityas. With their arrows they filled up the entire sky leaving no space void.

## \|\| 4.16.15 \|\|

*viṣṇurdaityasya bāṇaughairdhvajaṃ chatraṃ dhanurhayān \|*  
*ciccheda taṃ ca hṛdaye bāṇenaikena tāḍayat \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. With volleys of arrows Viṣṇu cut off the top of the flagstaff, the umbrella, the bow and the horses of the Daitya. With an arrow he hit him in his chest.

## \|\| 4.16.16 \|\|

*iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe kārtikamāsamāhātmye jalaṃdharasabhāyāṃ nāradāgamanaṃnāma ṣoḍaśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then seizing an iron club with his hand, the Daitya leaped up hurriedly. He hit Garuḍa on his head and made him fall on the ground.

## \|\| 4.16.17 \|\|

*viṣṇurgadāṃ svakhaṅgena ciccheda prahasanniva \|*  
*tāvatsa hṛdaye viṣṇuṃ jaghāna dṛḍhamuṣṭinā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Laughingly Viṣṇu split his iron club with his sword. Then the Daitya hit Viṣṇu on his chest with his (iron) firm fist.

## \|\| 4.16.18 \|\|

*tatastau bāhuyuddhena yuyudhāte mahābalau \|*  
*bāhubhirmuṣṭibhiścaiva jānubhirnādayanmahīm \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Then both of the two highly powerful ones had a hand-to-hand fight (like wrestling and boxing). They made the earth reverberate the sounds produced by their arms, fists and knees.

## \|\| 4.16.19 \|\|

*evaṃ tau suciraṃ yuddhaṃ kṛtvā viṣṇuḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*uvāca daityarājānaṃ meghagaṃbhīranisvanaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Thus they fought for a long time. Then Viṣṇu, the valorous one, spoke to the king of Daityas in a voice as grave and majestic as that of rumbling clouds:

## \|\| 4.16.20 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*varaṃ varaya daityeṃdra prīto'smi tava vikramāt \|*  
*adeyamapi te dadmi yatte manasi vartate \|\| 20 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:

20\. Choose a boon, O king of Daityas, I am pleased with your valour. I shall give whatever you wish in your mind, even if it should not be given.

## \|\| 4.16.21 \|\|

*jalaṃdhara uvāca \|*  
*yadi bhāvuka tuṣṭo'si varamenaṃ dadasva me \|*  
*madbhaginyā sahā'dya tvaṃ madgṛhe sagaṇo vasa \|\| 21 \|\|*

Jalandhara said:

21\. O Brother-in-law, if you are pleased, grant me this boon. Stay in my house today along with my sister and your groups of attendants.

## \|\| 4.16.22 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*tathetyuktā sa bhagavānsarvadevagaṇaiḥ saha \|*  
*tadā jalaṃdharapuramagamadramayā saha \|\| 22 \|\|*

Nārada said:

22\. Saying, “So it shall be” the Lord went to the city of Jalandhara along with Ramā and all the groups of the Devas.

## \|\| 4.16.23 \|\|

*jalaṃdharastu devānāmadhikāreṣu dānavān \|*  
*sthāpayitvā mahābāhuḥ punarāgānmahītalam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. After establishing the Dānavas in the offices of the Devas, the mighty-armed Jalandhara came once again to the earth.

## \|\| 4.16.24 \|\|

*devagaṃdharvasiddheṣu yatkiṃcidratnasaṃyutam \|*  
*tadātmavaśagaṃ kṛtvā'tiṣṭhatsāgaranaṃdanaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Whatever there was with the Devas, Gandharvas and Siddhas studded with gems was taken into his possession by the son of the Ocean.

## \|\| 4.16.25 \|\|

*pātālabhuvane daityaṃ niśuṃbhaṃ sa mahābalam \|*  
*sthāpayitvā sa śeṣādīnānayadbhūtalaṃ balī \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. After establishing Niśuṃbha, the exceedingly powerful Daitya, in the Pātāla region, that strong demon brought Śeṣa and others to the earth.

## \|\| 4.16.26 \|\|

*devagaṃdharvasiddhā'dyānsarparākṣasamānuṣān \|*  
*svapure nāgarānkṛtvā śaśāsa bhuvanatrayam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He made the Devas, Gandharvas, Siddhas and others, Serpents, Rākṣasas and human beings citizens of his capital and ruled over the three worlds.

## \|\| 4.16.27 \|\|

*evaṃ jalaṃdharaḥ kṛtvā devānsvavaśavartinaḥ \|*  
*dharmeṇa pālayāmāsa prajāḥ putrānivaurasān \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. After making the Devas subject to his control, Jalandhara protected his subjects righteously as though they were his bosom-born children.

## \|\| 4.16.28 \|\|

*na kaścidvyādhito naiva duḥkhī naiva kṛtastathā \|*  
*na dīno dṛśyate tasmindharmādrājyaṃ praśāsati \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. No one was sick, miserable, or lean. While he was ruling over the kingdom virtuously no poor man was visible therein.

## Chapter 17 - Dialogue between Nārada and Jalandhara

## \|\| 4.17.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*sa māṃ provāca vidhivatsaṃpūjyātīva bhaktimān \|*  
*saṃprahasya tadā vākyaṃ snehapūrvaṃ ca vai nṛpa \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: This chapter reveals the mischievous genius of Nārada, the partisan of Devas. He created enmity between Jalandhara and Śiva by misguiding him to bring the jewel-like consort (Pārvatī) of Śiva.

Nārada said:

1\. He duly and devoutly worshipped me, O king, and laughingly spoke these loving words to me:

## \|\| 4.17.2 \|\|

*kuta āgamyate brahmankiciddṛṣṭaṃ tvayā prabho \|*  
*yadarthamiha cā'yātastadā'jñāpaya māṃ mune \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. “O Brāhmaṇa, where are you coming from? Has anything been seen by you, O Lord, for which you have come over here? Command me (to comply), O sage.”

## \|\| 4.17.3-4 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*gataḥ kailāsaśikharaṃ daityeṃdrāhaṃ yadṛcchayā \|*  
*tatromayā samāsīnaṃ dṛṣṭavānasmi śaṃkaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

*yojanāyutavistīrṇe kalpavṛkṣamahāvane \|*  
*kāmadhenuśatākīrṇe ciṃtāmaṇisudīpite \|\| 4 \|\|*

Nārada said:

3-4. O leader of Daityas, I went to the peak of Kailāsa casually. There I saw Śaṅkara seated with Umā in the great forest of Kalpa-trees, which extends to ten thousand Yojanas, which is illuminated excellently with Cintāmaṇi jewels and is full of hundreds of Kāmadhenus (divine cows).

## \|\| 4.17.5 \|\|

*taddṛṣṭvā mahadāścaryaṃ vismayo me'bhavattadā \|*  
*kvā'pīdṛśī bhavedṛddhistrailokye vā na veti ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. On seeing that great wonderful thing I was surprised. I thought that such a prosperity and glory may or may not be present (anywhere else) in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 4.17.6 \|\|

*tadā tavā'pi daityeṃdra samṛddhiḥ saṃsmṛtā mayā \|*  
*tadvilokanakāmo'smi tvatsānnidhyamihā'gataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. At that time, O king of Daityas, your glory too was remembered by me. I wish to survey the same. Therefore, I have come here to you.

## \|\| 4.17.7 \|\|

*tvatsamṛddhimimāṃ paśyanstrīratnarahitāṃ dhuvam \|*  
*tarkayāmi śivādanyastrilokyāṃ na samṛddhimān \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Well I have seen your glory that is certainly devoid of jewels among women. I conclude that in the three worlds there is no one more prosperous than Śiva.

## \|\| 4.17.8 \|\|

*apsaronāgakanyādyā yadyapi tvadvaśe sthitāḥ \|*  
*tathā'pi tā na pārvatyā rūpeṇa sadṛśā dhruvam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Although the celestial damsels, Nāga maidens and others are within your control, certainly they are not like Pārvatī in beauty.

## \|\| 4.17.9 \|\|

*yasyā lāvaṇyajaladhau nimagnaścaturānanaḥ \|*  
*svadhairyamamucatpūrvaṃ tayā kā'nyopamīyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The Four-faced Lord himself got drowned in the ocean of her beauty and lost his courage once. Who can be compared with her?

## \|\| 4.17.10 \|\|

*vītarāgo'pi hi yathā madanāriḥ svalīlayā \|*  
*sauṃdaryagahane'bhrāmi śapharīrūpayā purā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The enemy of Madana is devoid of sensuous attachment. Still he was whirled formerly in the forest of beauty by her sportingly, in the form of a Śapharī fish(?) \[a Śabarī lass?\]

## \|\| 4.17.11 \|\|

*yasyāḥ punaḥ punaḥ paśyanrūpaṃ dhātā'pi sarjane \|*  
*sasarjā'psarasastāsāṃ tatsamaikā'pi nābhavat \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. At the time of creation, Brahmā frequently looked at her form and then created the celestial damsels. But among them there was none on a par with Pārvatī.

## \|\| 4.17.12 \|\|

*ataḥ strīratnasaṃbhoktuḥ samṛddhistasya sā varā \|*  
*tathā na tava daityeṃdra sarvaratnā'dhipasya ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Hence the prosperity and glory (of Śiva) who enjoys the jewel among women is the most excellent one. Your glory is not like that, O king of Daityas, though you are the possessor of all jewels.

## \|\| 4.17.13 \|\|

*evamuktvā tamāmaṃtrya gate sati sa daityarāṭ \|*  
*tadrūpa śravaṇādāsīdanaṃgajvarapīḍitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. After saying this, I took leave of him and went away. The king of Daityas became afflicted with, the fever of love on hearing about her (Pārvatī’s) beauty.

## \|\| 4.17.14 \|\|

*atha saṃpreṣayāmāsa sa dūtaṃ siṃhikāsutam \|*  
*tryaṃbakāyā'pi ca tadā viṣṇumāyāvimohitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Then, deluded by Viṣṇu’s Māyā, he sent the son of Siṃhikā (Rāhu) as his messenger to the Three-eyed Lord too.

## \|\| 4.17.15 \|\|

*kailāsamagamadrāhuḥ kurvañchukleṃduvarcasam \|*  
*kārṣṇyena kṛṣṇapakṣenduvarcasaṃ svāṃgajena tam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Rāhu went to Kailāsa that has the refulgence of the moon in the bright fortnight but, with the blackness arising from his own body, he made it (appear as though) it had the lustre of the moon in the dark fortnight.

## \|\| 4.17.16 \|\|

*niveditastadeśāya naṃdinā praviveśa saḥ \|*  
*tryaṃbakabhrūlatāsaṃjñā prerito vākyamabravīt \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. On Īśa having been informed by Nandin, Rāhu entered. When he was urged by a gesture of the eyebrows of Śiva, he spoke these words:

## \|\| 4.17.17 \|\|

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe kārtikamāsamāhātmye jalaṃdharopākhyāne dūtavākyakathanaṃnāma saptadaśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

Rāhu said:

17\. O Bull-emblemed One, listen to the command of my lord who is worthy of being served by Devas and Serpents, who is the overlord of all the three worlds and is the possessor of all jewels.

## \|\| 4.17.18 \|\|

*smaśānavāsino nityamasthibhāravahasya ca \|*  
*digaṃbarasya te bhāryā kathaṃ haimavatī śubhā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. “How can you have such a splendid wife as the daughter of Himavān, you who are a resident of cremation ground forever, who always bear the burden of bones and who are always naked?

## \|\| 4.17.19 \|\|

*ahaṃ ratnādhinātho'smi sā ca strīratnasaṃjñikā \|*  
*tasmānmamaiva sā yogyā naiva bhikṣāśinastava \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. I am the overlord of all Ratnas (jewels). She can be designated as a jewel among women. Hence she fits me and not you who beg for your own food.”

## \|\| 4.17.20 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*vadatyevaṃ tadā rāhau bhrūmadhyācchūlapāṇinaḥ \|*  
*abhavatpuruṣo raudrastīvrāśanisamasvanaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

Nārada said:

20\. While Rāhu was saying this, a terrible person issued forth from the middle of the eyebrows of the Trident-bearing Lord. His voice resembled the sound of the powerful thunderbolt.

## \|\| 4.17.21 \|\|

*siṃhāsyaḥ pralalajjihvaḥ sa jvalannayano mahān \|*  
*ūrdhvakeśaḥ śuṣkatanurnṛsiṃha iva cā'paraḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. He had a leonine face with a rolling tongue and blazing eyes. He was huge with hair standing upright and the body dry and rough. He was like another Nṛsiṃha.

## \|\| 4.17.22 \|\|

*sa taṃ khāditumāyāṃtaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāhurbhayāturaḥ \|*  
*adhāvata sa vegena bahiḥ sa ca dadhāra tam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. On seeing that person rushing at him in order to devour him, Rāhu became excessively frightened. He ran out quickly but the person caught hold of him (Rāhu).

## \|\| 4.17.23 \|\|

*sa ca rāhurmahābāho meghagambhīrayā girā \|*  
*uvāca devadeva tvaṃ pāhi māṃ śaraṇāgatam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. With words as resonant and majestic as thunder, O mighty one, Rāhu said: “O lord of Devas, protect me. I have sought refuge in you.

## \|\| 4.17.24 \|\|

*brāhmaṇaṃ māṃ mahādeva khādituṃ samupāgataḥ \|*  
*mahādevo vacaḥ śrutvā brāhmaṇasya tadā'bravīt \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. (This fellow) has come here, O Mahādeva, to devour me, a Brāhmaṇa.” On hearing the words of that Brāhmaṇa, Mahādeva spoke then:

## \|\| 4.17.25 \|\|

*naivā'sau vadhyatāmeti dūto'yaṃ paravānyataḥ \|*  
*muṃceti puruṣaḥ śrutvā rāhuṃ tatyājya soṃ'bare \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. “He does not deserve to be killed because he is (only) a messenger and hence he is dependent. Let him go.” On hearing this, that person set Rāhu free in the open sky.

## \|\| 4.17.26-27 \|\|

*rāhuṃ tyaktvā'tha puruṣastadā rudraṃ vyajijñapat \|*  
*puruṣa uvāca \|*  
*kṣudhā māṃ vādhate'tyaṃtaṃ kṣutkṣāmaścā'smi sarvathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*kiṃ bhakṣayāmi deveśa tadājñāpaya māṃ prabho \|*  
*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*bhakṣayasvātmanaḥ śīghraṃ māṃsaṃ tvaṃ hastapādayoḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

26a. After leaving off Rāhu, the person requested Rudra:

The person said:

26b-27a. Hunger afflicts me much. I am emaciated due to hunger utterly. O Lord, O Lord of Devas, what shall I eat? Command me.

Īśvara said:

27b. Eat the flesh of your own hands and feet. Be quick.

## \|\| 4.17.28 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*sa śivenaivamājñaptaścakhāda puruṣaḥ svakam \|*  
*hastapādodbhavaṃ māṃsaṃ śiraḥśeṣo yathā'bhavat \|\| 28 \|\|*

Nārada said:

28\. On being commanded thus by Śiva, the person devoured the flesh of his own hands and feet till he was left with his head alone.

## \|\| 4.17.29 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā śiro'vaśeṣaṃ taṃ suprasannastadā śivaḥ \|*  
*uvāca bhīmakarmāṇaṃ puruṣaṃ jātavismayaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. On seeing him left with his head alone, Śiva became highly delighted. Himself struck with wonder, he spoke to that person of terrible activities.

## \|\| 4.17.30 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*tvaṃ kīrtimukhasaṃjño hi bhava maddvārigaḥ sadā \|*  
*tvadarcāṃ ye na kurvaṃti naiva te me priyaṃkarāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

30\. You are named Kīrtimukha. Be always present at my doorway. Those who do not worship you, are not liked by me.

## \|\| 4.17.31 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*tadā prabhṛti devasya dvāri kīrtimukhaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*nārcayantīha ye pūrvaṃ teṣāmarcā vṛthā bhavet \|\| 31 \|\|*

Nārada said:

31\. Ever since then Kīrtimukha is stationed at the doorway (of the temple) of the Lord. Those who do not worship (him) here at the outset, will find their worship futile.

## \|\| 4.17.32 \|\|

*rāhurvimukto yastena so'pi tadbarbare sthale \|*  
*ataḥ sa barbarodbhūta iti bhūmau prathāṃ gataḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Since Rāhu was set free by him at that desolate spot (Barbara) he became known on the earth as Barbarodbhūta.

## Chapter 18 - Rudra’s Army Defeated

## \|\| 4.18.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*jalaṃdharastu tacchutvā kopākulitavigrahaḥ \|*  
*nirjagāmā'śu daityānāṃ koṭibhiḥ parivāritaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:

1\. On hearing it, the whole body of Jalandhara became agitated with anger. Surrounded by a crore of Daityas, he quickly marched out (of his abode).

## \|\| 4.18.2 \|\|

*gacchato'syā'grataḥ śukro rāhurdṛṣṭipathe'bhavat \|*  
*mukuṭaścā'patadbhūmau vegātpraskhalitastadā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. As he was going, Śukra and Rāhu came within the range of his vision in front. His crown fell on the ground as he faltered in his steps due to the speed.

## \|\| 4.18.3 \|\|

*daityasainyā'vṛtaistasya vimānānāṃ śataistadā \|*  
*vyarājata nabhaḥpūrṇaṃ prāvṛṣīva yathā ghanaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The sky was completely covered with hundreds of his aerial chariots filled with the army of Daityas. It shone as though covered with clouds during the rainy season.

## \|\| 4.18.4 \|\|

*tasyodyogaṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ \|*  
*alakṣitāstadā jagmuḥ śūlinaṃ taṃ vyajijñapuḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. On seeing his army, Devas with Śakra as their leader went to the Trident-bearing Lord without being noticed by anyone and informed him entreatingly.

## \|\| 4.18.5 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*na jānāsi kathaṃ svāmindevāpattimimāṃ vibho \|*  
*tadasmadrakṣaṇārthāya jahi sāgaranaṃdanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

The Devas said:

5\. How is it that you are not aware of this calamity of the Devas, O Lord? Therefore, kill the son of the Ocean for the sake of protecting

## \|\| 4.18.6 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*iti devavacaḥ śrutvā prahasya vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|*  
*mahāviṣṇuṃ samāhūya vacanaṃ cedamabravīt \|\| 6 \|\|*

Nārada said:

6\. On hearing these words of the Devas, the Bull-emblemed Lord laughed. He called Mahāviṣṇu and spoke these words:

## \|\| 4.18.7 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*jalaṃdharaḥ kathaṃ viṣṇo na hataḥ saṃgare tvayā \|*  
*tadgṛhaṃ cā'pi yāto'si tyaktvā vaikuṃṭhamātmanaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

7\. O Viṣṇu, how is it that Jalandhara was not killed by you in battle? Further you have gone over to his house after leaving off your own Vaikuṇṭha?

## \|\| 4.18.8 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*tavāṃśasaṃbhavatvācca bhrātṛtvācca tathā śriyaḥ \|*  
*na mayā nihataḥ saṃkhye tvamenaṃ jahi dānavam \|\| 8 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:

8\. He is not killed in battle by me because he is born of a part of yours and because he is the brother of Śrī. You do kill this Dānava.

## \|\| 4.18.9 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*nāyamebhirmahātejāḥ śastrāstrairvadhyate mayā \|*  
*devaiḥ saha svatejoṃśaṃ śastrārthaṃ dīyatāṃ mama \|\| 9 \|\|*

Īśvara said:

9\. He is exceedingly refulgent. He cannot be killed by me through these (ordinary) weapons and missiles. Let a part of their splendour be given by the Devas for making my weapon. Let a part of your splendour too be given to me.

## \|\| 4.18.10 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*atha viṣṇumukhā devāḥ svatejāṃsi dadustadā \|*  
*tānyaikyamāgatānīśo dṛṣṭvā svaṃ cāmucanmahaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

Nārada said:

10\. Then the Devas including Viṣṇu gave their respective refulgences. On seeing them united together, Īśa released his own refulgence too.

## \|\| 4.18.11 \|\|

*tenākaronmahādevo mahasā śastramuttamam \|*  
*cakraṃ sudarśanaṃ nāma jvālāmālātibhīṣaṇam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. With that (combined) splendour, Mahādeva created an excellent weapon, a discus named Sudarśana which was extremely terrible with its clusters of flames.

## \|\| 4.18.12 \|\|

*tataḥ śeṣeṇa ca tadā vajraṃ ca kṛtavānhariḥ \|*  
*tāvajjalaṃdharo dṛṣṭaḥ kailāsatalabhūmiṣu \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. With the remaining (splendour), Hari (?Hara) made the thunderbolt. By that time Jalandhara was seen on the grounds at the foot of Kailāsa.

## \|\| 4.18.13 \|\|

*hastyaśvarathapattīnāṃ koṭibhiḥ parivāritaḥ \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā lakṣitā jagmurdevāḥ sarve yathāgatāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He was surrounded by crores of elephants, horses, chariots and foot-soldiers. On seeing him, all the Devas slipped away unobserved in the manner they had come.

## \|\| 4.18.14 \|\|

*gaṇāśca samasajjaṃta yuddhāyā'titvarānvitāḥ \|*  
*nandībhavaktrasenānīmukhāḥ sarve śivājñayā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The Gaṇas (attendants of Śiva) got ready for the battle in a hurry. All of them with, Nandin, Gajānana and Kārttikeya as leaders made preparations for the battle at the behest of Śiva.

## \|\| 4.18.15 \|\|

*avaterurgaṇā vegātkailāsādyuddhadurmadāḥ \|*  
*tataḥ samabhavadyuddhaṃ kailāsopatyakābhuvi \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Proud of their ability to fight, the Gaṇas descended from Kailāsa. Then a fight ensued on the lower slopes of Kaiīāsa between the chieftains of Pramathas and Daityas.

## \|\| 4.18.16-21 \|\|

*pramathādhipadaityānāṃ ghoraśastrāstrasaṃkulam \|*  
*bherīmṛdaṃgaśaṃkhaugha niḥsvanairvīraharṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*gajāśvarathaśabdaiśca nāditā bhūrvyakaṃpata \|*  
*śaktitomarabāṇaughamusalaprāsapaṭṭiśaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe kārtikamāsamāhātmye jalaṃdharopākhyāne rudrasenāparābhavonāmā'ṣṭādaśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*vajrāhatācalaśiraḥśakalairiva saṃvṛtā \|*  
*pramathāhatadaityaughairdaityāhatagaṇaistathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*vasāsṛṅmāṃsapaṃkāḍhyā bhūragamyā'bhavattadā \|*  
*pramathāhatadaityaughānbhārgavaḥ samajīvayat \|\| 20 \|\|*

*yuddhe punaḥ punastatra mṛtasaṃjīvinībalāt \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā vyākulībhūtā gaṇāḥ sarve bhayānvitāḥ \|*  
*śaśaṃsurdevadevāya tatsarvaṃ śukraceṣṭitam \|\| 21 \|\|*

16-18a. The battle was tumultuous with (the sound) of terrible weapons and missiles. The whole of the earth reverberated with the sounds of Bherī and Mṛdaṅga drums, multitudes of conchs, shrill and joyous shouts of heroes and the sounds produced by elephants, horses and chariots. The whole earth shook. The sky filled with javelins, iron clubs, arrows, pestles, spears, lances having sharp edges etc. shone as though with firebrands.

18b-21. With the chariots, elephants, horses and foot-soldiers struck down or killed, the earth shone as though scattered with pieces of the tops of mountains struck by thunderbolts.

The ground became impassable because of the suet, blood and flesh that formed a mass of muddy heap with the groups of Daityas struck down by Pramathas and Gaṇas killed by the Daityas.

Śukra resuscitated the groups of Daityas killed by Pramathas in the battle by the power of the Mṛtasañjīvinī Vidyā. This happened frequently. On seeing this all the Gaṇas became bewildered and frightened. They reported all the activities of Śukra to the Lord of the Devas.

## \|\| 4.18.22-23 \|\|

*atha rudramukhātkṛtyā babhūvā'tīvabhīṣaṇā \|*  
*tālajaṃghā darīvaktrā stanāpīḍitabhūruhā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*sā yuddhabhūmimāsādya bhakṣayaṃtī mahāsurān \|*  
*bhārgavaṃ svabhage dhṛtvā jagāmāṃtarhitā nabhaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Then an extremely terrible Kṛtyā (female Ogress) came out of the mouth of Rudra. Her calves were as huge as palm trees. Her mouth resembled a huge cave. With her breasts she crushed tall trees.

She came to the battleground and began to devour the great Asuras. She put Bhārgava (Śukra) within her vaginal passage and vanished in the sky.

## \|\| 4.18.24 \|\|

*vidhṛtaṃ bhārgavaṃ dṛṣṭvā daityasainyaṃ gaṇāstadā \|*  
*amlānavadanā harṣānnijaghnuryuddhadurmadāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. On seeing that Bhārgava had been abducted, the Gaṇas became delighted. Their faces ceased to be faded and pallid. Proud of their ability to fight, they killed the army of Daityas.

## \|\| 4.18.25 \|\|

*null*

25\. The army of Daityas frightened by the Gaṇas broke lose like a cluster of grasses scattered and tossed about by stormy winds.

## \|\| 4.18.26 \|\|

*athābhajyata daityānāṃ senā gaṇabhayārditā \|*  
*vāyuvegenāhateva prakīrṇā tṛṇasaṃtatiḥ \|*  
*bhagnāṃ gaṇabhayātsenāṃ dṛṣṭvāmarṣayutā yayuḥ \|*  
*niśuṃbhaśuṃbhau senānyau kālanemiśca vīryavān \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. On seeing that their army was being crushed due to the fear of the Gaṇas, Niśuṃbha and Śuṃbha, the generals, and Kālanemi, the powerful one, became furious and rushed (into the battlefield).

## \|\| 4.18.27 \|\|

*trayaste vārayāmāsurgaṇasenāṃ mahābalāḥ \|*  
*muñcataḥ śaravarṣāṇi prāvṛṣīva balāhakāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Showering volleys of arrows like clouds showering heavy rain in the rainy season, those three (Daityas) of great strength thwarted the army of Gaṇas.

## \|\| 4.18.28 \|\|

*tato daityaśaraughāste śalabhānāmiva vrajāḥ \|*  
*rurudhuḥ khaṃ diśaḥ sarvā gaṇasenāmakaṃpayan \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Then the volleys of arrows of the Daityas overcast the sky and enveloped the quarters like swarms of locusts and made the army of Gaṇas tremble.

## \|\| 4.18.29 \|\|

*gaṇāḥ śaraśatairbhinnā rudhirāsāravarṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*vasaṃte kiṃśukābhāsā na prājñāyata kiṃcana \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The Gaṇas were split by hundreds of arrows. Blood began to gush out from their bodies and they resembled Kiṃśukas (Butea frondosa). They were not aware of anything.

## \|\| 4.18.30 \|\|

*patitāḥ pātyamānāśca bhinnāśchinnāstadā gaṇāḥ \|*  
*tyaktvā saṃgrāmabhūmiṃ te sarvepi vimukhā'bhavan \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The Gaṇas who had dropped down or who were being struck down, those who were split and cut—all these abandoned the battlefield and turned their backs.

## Chapter 19 - The Fail of Vīrabhadra

## \|\| 4.19.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*te gaṇādhipatīndṛṣṭvā naṃdībhamukhaṣaṇmukhān \|*  
*amarṣādabhyadhāvaṃta dvaṃdvayuddhāya dānavāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:

1\. On seeing Nandin, Gajānana and Ṣaṇmukha, the leaders of Gaṇas, those Dānavas rushed at them angrily to engage them in duels.

## \|\| 4.19.2 \|\|

*naṃdinaṃ kālanemiśca śumbho laṃbodaraṃ tathā \|*  
*niśumbhaḥ ṣaṇmukhaṃ vegādabhyadhāvata daṃśitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Kālanemi rushed at Nandin, Śuṃbha at Laṃbodara (Gajānana) and Niśuṃbha rushed hurriedly at Ṣaṇmukha. He had his armour on.

## \|\| 4.19.3 \|\|

*niśumbhaḥ kārtikeyasya mayūraṃ paṃcabhiḥ śaraiḥ \|*  
*hṛdi vivyādha vegena mūrcchitaḥ sa papāta ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. With five arrows Niśuṃbha hit with force the peacock of Kārttikeya in its chest and it fell down unconscious.

## \|\| 4.19.4 \|\|

*tataḥ śaktidharaḥ śaktiṃ yāvajjagrāha roṣitaḥ \|*  
*tāvanniśuṃbho vegena svaśaktyā tamapātayat \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. By the time the infuriated lord holding the Śakti (i.e. Kārttikeya) took up his javelin, Niśuṃbha hurriedly made him fall down by means of his own javelin.

## \|\| 4.19.5 \|\|

*naṃdīśvaraḥ śaravrātaiḥ kālanemimavadhyata \|*  
*saptabhiśca hayānketuṃ tribhiḥ sārathimacchinat \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. With volleys of arrows, Nandīśvara struck at Kālanemi. He pierced his horses and cut the flagstaff with seven arrows and the charioteer with three arrows.

## \|\| 4.19.6 \|\|

*kālanemistu saṃkruddho dhanuściccheda naṃdinaḥ \|*  
*tadapāsya sa śūlena taṃ vakṣasyahanadbalī \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Kālanemi became furious and he cut off the bow of Nandin. Discarding it, that powerful one hit him on his chest with his spear.

## \|\| 4.19.7 \|\|

*sa śūlabhinnahṛdayo hatāśvo hatasārathiḥ \|*  
*adreḥ śikharamāmucya śailādiṃ so'pyapātayat \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. With his heart pierced by the spear, with his horses and the charioteer killed, Kālanemi uprooted the peak of a mountain and made Nandin, the son of Śilāda, fall down (with it).

## \|\| 4.19.8 \|\|

*atha śumbho gaṇeśaśca rathamūṣakavāhanau \|*  
*yudhyamānau śaravrātaiḥ parasparamavidhyatām \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Śuṃbha and Gajānana having a chariot and a mouse respectively for their vehicles, fought and hit each other with volleys of arrows.

## \|\| 4.19.9 \|\|

*gaṇeśastu tadā śumbhaṃ hṛdi vivyādha patriṇā \|*  
*sārathiṃ ca tribhirbāṇaiḥ pātayāmāsa bhūtale \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Gajānana pierced the chest of Śuṃbha with an arrow and struck down the charioteer to the ground with three arrows.

## \|\| 4.19.10 \|\|

*tato'tikruddhaḥ śumbho'pi bāṇaṣaṣṭyā gaṇādhipam \|*  
*mūṣakaṃ ca tribhirviddhvā nanāda jaladasvanaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then Śuṃbha became extremely infuriated. He hit Gajānana with sixty arrows and his mouse with three and roared like thunder.

## \|\| 4.19.11 \|\|

*mūṣakaḥ śarabhinnāṃgaścacāla dṛḍhavedanaḥ \|*  
*laṃbodaraśca patitaḥ padātirabhavannṛpa \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. When his body was pierced with arrows, the mouse squirmed and writhed with excessive pain. Laṃbodara (i.e. Gajānana) fell down, O king, and became a pedestrian.

## \|\| 4.19.12 \|\|

*tato laṃbodaraḥ śumbhaṃ hatvā paraśunā hṛdi \|*  
*apātayattadā bhūmau mūṣakaṃ cāruhatpunaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Then Laṃbodara struck Śuṃbha on his chest with his axe and felled him down to the ground and mounted on his mouse once again.

## \|\| 4.19.13 \|\|

*kālanemirniśuṃbhaścā'pyubhau laṃbodaraṃ śaraiḥ \|*  
*yugapajjaghnatuḥ krodhāttotrairiva mahādvipam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Kālanemi and Śuṃbha both simultaneously hit Laṃbodara furiously with arrows as they would a great elephant with goads.

## \|\| 4.19.14 \|\|

*taṃ pīḍayamānamālokya vīrabhadro mahābalaḥ \|*  
*abhyadhāvata vegena bhūtakoṭiyutastadā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. On seeing him harassed, Vīrabhadra of great strength rushed immediately, accompanied by crores of Bhūtas (goblins).

## \|\| 4.19.15 \|\|

*kūṣmāṃḍabhairavāścā'pi vetālā yoginīgaṇāḥ \|*  
*piśācayoginīsaṃghā gaṇāścā'pi tamanvayuḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The spirits such as Kūṣmāṇḍas, Bhairavas, Vetālas, groups of Yoginīs, Piśācas (ghosts) etc. and the Gaṇas followed him.

## \|\| 4.19.16 \|\|

*tataḥ kilakilāśabdaiḥ siṃhanādaiḥ sughargharaiḥ \|*  
*bherītālamṛdaṃgaiśca pṛthivī samakaṃpata \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. With the chattering noises, roarings like thunder, leonine shouts and the sounds of Bherī and Mṛdaṅga drums and cymbals the earth shook and quaked.

## \|\| 4.19.17 \|\|

*tato bhūtānyadhāvaṃta bhakṣayaṃtisma dānavān \|*  
*utpataṃtyāpataṃti sma nanṛtuśca raṇāṃgaṇe \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Then the goblins and spirits rushed at the Dānavas and devoured them. They jumped up and leaped down and began to dance on the battlefield.

## \|\| 4.19.18 \|\|

*nandī ca kārtikeyaśca samāśvasya tvaratvitau \|*  
*nijaghnatū raṇe daityānniraṃtaraśaravrajaiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Nandin and Kārttikeya composed themselves. Regaining confidence, they hurriedly hit and killed the Daityas with uninterrupted volleys of arrows on the battlefield.

## \|\| 4.19.19 \|\|

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe kārtikamāsamāhātmye jalaṃdharopākhyāne vīrabhadrapatananāmaikonaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. With the Daityas killed, fallen or devoured the entire (Daitya) army became broken and scattered. The faces of all turned pale and the whole army became bewildered.

## \|\| 4.19.20 \|\|

*pravidhvastāṃ tadā senāṃ dṛṣṭvā sāgaranaṃdanaḥ \|*  
*rathenā'tipatākena gaṇānabhiyayau balī \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On seeing the army crushed, the powerful son of the Ocean rushed against the Gaṇas in a tall bannered chariot.

## \|\| 4.19.21 \|\|

*hastyaśvarathasaṃhrādāḥ śaṃkhabherīsvanāstathā \|*  
*abhavansiṃhanādāśca senayorubhayostadā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Then a tumultuous sound arose from both the armies inclusive of the trumpeting of elephants, the neighing sounds of horses, the rumblings of chariots, the sounds of conchs and Bherī drums and leonine roars of warriors.

## \|\| 4.19.22 \|\|

*jalaṃdharaśaravrātairnīhārapaṭalairiva \|*  
*dyāvāpṛthivyorācchinnamaṃtaraṃ samapadyata \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The intervening space between heaven and earth became covered by clusters of the arrows of Jalandhara as though with layers of fog and mist.

## \|\| 4.19.23 \|\|

*gaṇeśaṃ paṃcabhirviddhvā śailādiṃ navabhiḥ śaraiḥ \|*  
*vīrabhadraṃ ca viṃśatyā nanāda jaladasvanaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. After hitting Gaṇeśa (Gajānana) with five arrows, Nandin with nine arrows arid Vīrabhadra with twenty, he roared like thundering clouds.

## \|\| 4.19.24 \|\|

*kārtikeyastadā daityaṃ śaktyā vivyādha satvaraḥ \|*  
*yuyudhe śaktinirbhinnaḥ kiṃcidvyākulamānasaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Kārttikeya then hurriedly pierced the Daitya with his Śakti (Javelin). Though split and rent with the Śakti, he fought on. He was only slightly agitated in his mind.

## \|\| 4.19.25 \|\|

*tataḥ krodhaparītākṣaḥ kārtikeyaṃ jalaṃdharaḥ \|*  
*gadayā tāḍayāmāsa sa ca bhūmitale'patat \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. With eyes full of anger, Jalandhara struck Kārttikeya with his iron club and he fell on the ground.

## \|\| 4.19.26 \|\|

*tathaiva naṃdinaṃ vegādapātayata bhūtale \|*  
*tato gaṇeśvaraḥ kruddho gadāṃ paraśunā'hanat \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Similarly he made Nandin too fall on the ground with force. Thereupon Gaṇeśvara became furious and struck his iron club with his axe.

## \|\| 4.19.27 \|\|

*vīrabhadrastribhirbāṇairhṛdi vivyādha dānavam \|*  
*saptabhiśca hayānketuṃ dhanuśchatraṃ ca cicchide \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. With three arrows Vīrabhadra struck and pierced the Dānava in his heart and cut down his horses, flagstaff, bow and umbrella.

## \|\| 4.19.28 \|\|

*tato'tikruddho daityeṃdraḥ śaktimudyamya dāruṇām \|*  
*gaṇeśaṃ pātayāmāsa rathaṃ cā'nyamathā'ruhat \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Then the Daitya king became excessively angry. He raised his terrible Śakti and struck down Gaṇeśa and got into another chariot.

## \|\| 4.19.29 \|\|

*abhyayādatha vegena vīrabhadraṃ ruṣānvitaḥ \|*  
*tatastau sūryasaṃkāśau yuyudhāte parasparam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. He rushed at Vīrabhadra with great force and anger. Then both of them who shone like the Sun fought with each other.

## \|\| 4.19.30 \|\|

*vīrabhadraḥ punastasya hayānbāṇairapātayat \|*  
*dhanuściccheda daityeṃdraḥ pupluve parighāyudhaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Again Vīrabhadra struck down his horses with his arrows and cut down his bow. The Daitya king then leaped (forward).

## Chapter 20 - Fight between Śiva and Jalandhara

## \|\| 4.20.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*patitaṃ vīrabhadraṃ tu dṛṣṭvā rudragaṇā bhayāt \|*  
*agamaṃste raṇaṃ hitvā krośamānā maheśvaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:

1\. On seeing Vīrabhadra fallen, the Gaṇas of Rudra left the battleground in great panic. Crying and lamenting, they went to Maheśvara.

## \|\| 4.20.2 \|\|

*atha kolāhalaṃ śrutvā gaṇānāṃ caṃdraśekharaḥ \|*  
*abhyayādvṛṣabhārūḍhaḥ saṃgrāmaṃ prahasanniva \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. On hearing the tumultuous sound of the Gaṇas, the Moon-crested Lord came to the battleground laughingly riding on his bull.

## \|\| 4.20.3 \|\|

*rudramāyāṃtamālokya siṃhanādairgaṇāḥ punaḥ \|*  
*nivṛttāḥ saṃgare daityānnirjaghnuḥ śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On seeing Rudra coming, the Gaṇas returned to the battlefield with leonine shouts. With showers of arrows they began killing the Daityas.

## \|\| 4.20.4 \|\|

*daityāśca bhīṣaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarve caiva vidudruvuḥ \|*  
*kārtikavratinaṃ dṛṣṭvā pātakānīva tadbhayāt \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Just as sins run away out of fear on seeing a person observing the Kārttika Vrata, so also on seeing the terrible one (Śiva) all the Daityas fled.

## \|\| 4.20.5 \|\|

*jalaṃdharotha tāndaityānnivṛttānprekṣya saṃgare \|*  
*roṣādadhāvaccaṃḍīśaṃ muṃcanbāṇānsahasraśaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. On seeing those Daityas turning away from the battlefield, Jalandhara angrily rushed at the Lord of Caṇḍī discharging thousands of arrows.

## \|\| 4.20.6 \|\|

*śuṃbho niśuṃbho'śvamukhaḥ kālanemirbalāhakaḥ \|*  
*khaḍgaromā pracaṃḍaśca ghasmarādyāḥ śivaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Śuṃbha, Niśuṃbha, Aśvamukha, Kālanemi, Balāhaka, Khaḍgaromā, Pracaṇḍa, Ghasmara and others went to (i.e. attacked) Śiva.

## \|\| 4.20.7 \|\|

*bāṇāṃdhakārasaṃchannaṃ dṛṣṭvā gaṇabalaṃ śivaḥ \|*  
*bāṇajālamavācchidya svabāṇairāvṛṇonnabhaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On seeing the army of Gaṇas enveloped by the darkness caused by arrows, Śiva tore away the net (cluster) of arrows and covered the sky with his own arrows.

## \|\| 4.20.8 \|\|

*daityāṃśca bāṇavātyābhiḥ pīḍitānakarottadā \|*  
*pracaṃḍabāṇajālaughairapātayata bhūtale \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He afflicted the Daityas with stormy winds (in the form) of arrows. He made them fall on the ground by means of volleys of fierce arrows.

## \|\| 4.20.9 \|\|

*khaḍgaromṇaḥ śiraḥ kāyāttadā paraśunā'cchinat \|*  
*balāhakasya ca śiraḥ khaṭvāṃgenā'karoddvidhā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. With his axe he severed the head of Khaḍgaromā from his body. With his Khaṭvāṅga (club with skull-shaped top), he split the head of Balāhaka into two.

## \|\| 4.20.10 \|\|

*baddhvā ca ghasmaraṃ daityaṃ pāśenābhyahanadbhuvi \|*  
*vṛṣabheṇa hatāḥ kecitkecidbāṇairnipātitāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He bound Daitya Ghasmara with noose and dashed him on the ground. Some (of the Daityas) were killed by the bull and some were struck down by means of arrows.

## \|\| 4.20.11-13 \|\|

*na śekurasurāḥ sthātuṃ gajāḥ siṃhārditā iva \|*  
*tataḥ krodhaparītātmā vegādrudraṃ jalaṃdharaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*āhvayāmāsa samare tīvrāśanisamasvanaḥ \|*  
*jalaṃdhara uvāca \|*  
*yudhyasva ca mayā sārddhaṃ kimebhirnihitaistava \|\| 12 \|\|*

*yacca kiṃcidbalaṃ te'sti taddarśaya jaṭādhara \|*  
*ityuktvā bāṇasaptatyā jaghāna vṛṣabhadhvajam \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. Like elephants tormented by a lion, the Asuras were unable, to stand. Thereupon Jalandhara whose anger was aroused, challenged Rudra to fight in the battle in a voice as loud as the terrible thunderbolt.

## \|\| 4.20.14 \|\|

*tānprāptānniśitairbāṇaiściccheda prahasanniva \|*  
*tato hayāndhvajaṃ chatraṃ dhanuściccheda śaktibhiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

Jalandhara said:

Fight with me. What do you get even if these are killed. O one with matted hair, show me what little strength you have.

After saying thus, he struck the Bull-emblemed Lord with seventy arrows.

14\. As those arrows arrived, Śiva laughingly cut them off with sharper arrows. Then with his Śaktis he cut off the horses, flagstaff, umbrella and bow (of Jalandhara).

## \|\| 4.20.15 \|\|

*sa cchinnadhanvā viratho gadāmudyamya vegavān \|*  
*abhyadhāvacchivastāvadgadāṃ bāṇairdvidhā'cchinat \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. With his bow broken and himself deprived of his chariot, he (Jalandhara) speedily raised his iron club and rushed (at Śiva). By that time, Śiva cut off the iron club into two by means of his arrows.

## \|\| 4.20.16 \|\|

*tathā'pi muṣṭimudyamya yayau rudraṃ jighāṃsayā \|*  
*tāvacchivena bāṇaughaiḥ krośamātramapākṛtaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Still he raised his fist and went up to Rudra with a desire to kill him. By that time he was pushed away a Krośa (3 Kms.) by Śiva by means of a volley of arrows.

## \|\| 4.20.17 \|\|

*tato jalaṃdharo daityo matvā rudraṃ balādhikam \|*  
*sasarja māyāṃ gāṃdharvīmadbhutāṃ rudramohinīm \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Thereupon, thinking that Rudra was superior to him in strength. Daitya Jalandhara created his Gāndharvī Māyā, that mysteriously fascinated Rudra.

## \|\| 4.20.18-19 \|\|

*tato jaguśca nanṛturgaṃdharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ \|*  
*tālaveṇumṛdaṃgādyānvādayaṃti sma cā'pare \|\| 18 \|\|*

*taddṛṣṭvā mahadāścaryaṃ rudro nādavimohitaḥ \|*  
*patitānyapi śastrāṇi karebhyo na viveda saḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. In front of him groups of Gandharvas and celestial damsels sang and danced. Others played on various musical instruments such as cymbals, flutes, Mṛdaṅga drums etc. On seeing that wonderful spectacle Rudra became enchanted. He was not even aware that the weapons had dropped down from his hands.

## \|\| 4.20.20 \|\|

*iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ sahitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe kārtikamāsamāhātmye jalaṃdharopākhyāne śivajalaṃdharayuddhavarṇanaṃnāma viṃśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On seeing that Rudra was fully engrossed in it. Daitya Jalandhara who was afflicted with lust, went immediately to the place where Gaurī was present.

## \|\| 4.20.21-30 \|\|

*yuddhe śuṃbhaniśuṃbhākhyau sthāpayitvā mahābalī \|*  
*daśadordaṃḍapacāsyastrinetraśca jaṭādharaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*mahāvṛṣabhamārūḍhaḥ sa babhūva jalaṃdharaḥ \|*  
*atho rudraṃ samāyāṃtamālokya bhavavallabhā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*abhyāyayau sakhīmadhyāttaddarśanapathe'bhavat \|*  
*yāvaddadarśa cārvaṃgī pārvatī danujeśvaraḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tāvatsvavīryaṃ mumuce jaḍāṃgaścā'bhavattadā \|*  
*atha jñātvā tadā gaurī dānavaṃ bhayavihvalā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*jagāmā'ntarhitā vegātsā tadottaramānase \|*  
*tāmadṛṣṭvā tato daityaḥ kṣaṇādvidyullatāmiva \|\| 25 \|\|*

*javenā'gātpunaryuddhaṃ yatra devo vṛṣadhvajaḥ \|*  
*pārvatyapi bhayādviṣṇuṃ sasmāra manasā tadā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tāvaddadarśa taṃ devaṃ sūpaviṣṭaṃ samīpagam \|*  
*pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*viṣṇo jalaṃdharo daityaḥ kṛtavānparamādbhutam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tatkiṃ na viditaṃ te'sti ceṣṭitaṃ tasya durmateḥ \|*  
*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*tenaiva darśitaḥ paṃthā vayamapyanvayāmahe \|\| 28 \|\|*

*nā'nyathā sa bhavedvadhyaḥ pātivratyasurakṣitḥ \|*  
*nārada uvāca \|*  
*jagāma viṣṇurityuktvā punarjālaṃdharaṃ puram \|\| 29 \|\|*

*atha rudraśca gaṃdharvā'nugataḥ saṃgare sthitaḥ \|*  
*aṃtardhānaṃ gatāṃ māyāṃ dṛṣṭvā sa bubudhe tadā \|\| 30 \|\|*

21 -22a. Jalandhara had employed the two powerful Daityas named Śuṃbha and Niśuṃbha to continue the fight. He had then assumed the form of Śiva with three eyes, five faces and ten mighty arms and matted hair. He rode on a great bull.

22b-24a. On seeing Rudra coming the beloved one of Bhava came forward from the middle of her friends and chaperons and stood within the range of his vision.

No sooner did the lord of the Dānavas see Pārvatī of beautiful limbs, than he discharged his semen virile and all his limbs became stiff and benumbed.

24b-27a. On realizing that he was a Dānava, Gaurī became agitated with fear. She immediately vanished and went to Northern Mānasa. On seeing her vanished in a moment like the streak of lightning, the Daitya speedily returned to the battleground where the Bull-emblemed Lord was still present. Out of fear, Pārvatī mentally remembered Viṣṇu. Presently she saw that Lord firmly seated nearby.

Pārvatī said:

27b-28a. O Viṣṇu, Jalandhara the Daitya, has created something wonderfully mysterious. Was it not known to you? Were you not aware of the evil designs of that vicious fellow?

Viṣṇu said:

28b-29a. We too shall follow the path that has been pointed out by him. Otherwise he cannot be killed. He is protected by the chastity (of his wife).

Nārada said:

29b-30. After saying this Viṣṇu went once again to the city of Jalandhara. Rudra who was stationed in the battleground and followed the Gandharvas saw the Māyā vanish. Then he understood (everything).

## Chapter 21 - Vṛndā’s Self-immolation

## \|\| 4.21.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*viṣṇurjalaṃdharaṃ gatvā taddaityapuṭabhedanam \|*  
*pātivratyasya bhaṃgāya vṛṃdāyāścā'karonmatim \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:

1\. Viṣṇu went to Jalandhara, the city of that Daitya. He resolved to violate the chastity of Vṛndā.

## \|\| 4.21.2 \|\|

*atha vṛṃdārakā devī svapnamadhye dadarśa ha \|*  
*bhartāraṃ mahiṣā'rūḍhaṃ tailābhyaktaṃ digaṃmbaram \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. In the meantime, the queen Vṛndārakā (Vṛndā) saw in a dream her husband seated on a buffalo. He was anointed with oil. He was stark naked.

## \|\| 4.21.3-6 \|\|

*kṛṣṇaprasūnabhūṣāḍhyaṃ kravyādagaṇasevitam \|*  
*dakṣiṇāśāgataṃ muṇḍaṃ tamasāpyā'vṛtaṃ tadā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*svapuraṃ sāgare magnaṃ sahasaivā'tmanā saha \|*  
*tataḥ prabuddhā sā bālā tatsvapnaṃ pravicinvatī \|\| 4 \|\|*

*dadarśoditamādityaṃ sacchidraṃ niṣprabhaṃ muhuḥ \|*  
*tadaniṣṭamiti jñātvā rudatī bhayavihvalā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*kutracinnā'labhaccharma gopurāṭṭālabhūmiṣu \|*  
*tataḥ sakhīdvayayutā nagarodyānamāgamat \|\| 6 \|\|*

3-6. He wore black flowers and ornaments. He was attended upon by carnivorous animals and demons. His head was completely shaven and he was proceeding towards the southern direction. She saw her own city enveloped in darkness and immersed in the sea suddenly along with herself. Then that young woman woke up pondering over that dream. She saw the rising sun with a hole in the middle without any lustre and saw this frequently.

Thinking that it foreboded evil, she began to cry. She was excessively frightened. She did not get happiness or mental peace anywhere in the ornamental arched gateways, attics, terraces etc. Then, accompanied by two friends, she went to the city park.

## \|\| 4.21.7 \|\|

*tatrā'pi sā'bhramadbālā nā'labhatkutracitsukham \|*  
*vanādvanāṃtaraṃ yātā naiva vedātmanastadā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. There also the young woman wandered but did not get happiness anywhere. She went from forest to forest without being aware of it herself.

## \|\| 4.21.8 \|\|

*tataḥ sā bhramatī bālā dadarśā'tīvabhīṣaṇau \|*  
*rākṣasau siṃhavadanau daṃṣṭrā'nanavibhīṣaṇau \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. While wandering thus she saw two Rākṣasas who were extremely terrifying. They had leonine faces, extremely terrible on account of the curved teeth.

## \|\| 4.21.9 \|\|

*tau dṛṣṭvā vihvalā'tīva palāyanaparā'bhavat \|*  
*dadarśa tāpasaṃ śāṃtaṃ saśiṣyaṃ maunamāsthitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On seeing them she became much afflicted and ready to flee from there. She then saw a calm and tranquil ascetic who had resorted to the vow of silence. He had a disciple too.

## \|\| 4.21.10 \|\|

*tatastatkaṇṭhamāvṛtya nijāṃ bāhulatāṃ bhayāt \|*  
*mune māṃ rakṣa śaraṇamāgatā'smītyabhāṣata \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Out of fear she put her tender arms round his neck and said: “O sage, protect me. I have sought refuge in you.”

## \|\| 4.21.11 \|\|

*munistāṃ vihvalāṃ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasā'nugatāṃ tadā \|*  
*huṃkāreṇaiva tau ghorau cakāra vimukhau ruṣā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. On seeing her agitated and closely pursued by the Rākṣasas, he angrily made a loud hum sound whereby he turned back those terrible demons.

## \|\| 4.21.12 \|\|

*tau huṃkārabhayatrastau dṛṣṭvā ca vimukhau gatau \|*  
*praṇamya daṃḍavadbhūmau vṛndā vacanamabravīt \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On seeing them turned and gone due to the fear of that hum sound, Vṛndā prostrated before the sage like a rod on the ground and spoke these words:

## \|\| 4.21.13-14 \|\|

*vṛndovāca \|*  
*rakṣitāhaṃ tvayā ghorādbhayādasmātkṛpānidhe \|*  
*kiṃcidviptumicchāmi kṛpayā tanniśāmaya \|\| 13 \|\|*

*jalaṃdharo hi madbhartā rudraṃ yoddhuṃ gataḥ prabho \|*  
*sa tatrā'ste kathaṃ yuddhe tanme kathaya suvrata \|\| 14 \|\|*

Vṛndā said:

13-14. O holy one, storehouse of mercy, I have been protected by you from this terrible fear. I wish to submit to you something. Kindly listen to it.

Jalandhara is my husband. O holy lord, he has gone to fight with Rudra. How does he fare in that battle? O holy lord of good holy rites, tell me.

## \|\| 4.21.15 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*munistadvākyamākarṇya kṛpayordhvamavaikṣata \|*  
*tāvatkapī samāyātau praṇamya cāgrataḥ sthitau \|\| 15 \|\|*

Nārada said:

15\. On hearing her words, the sage kindly looked up. By that time two monkeys came there, bowed down to him and stood by.

## \|\| 4.21.16 \|\|

*tatastadbhrūlatāsaṃjñāniyuktau gaganaṃ gatau \|*  
*gatvā kṣaṇārddhādāgatya praṇatāvagrataḥ sthitau \|*  
*śiraḥkabandhe hastau ca gṛhītvā samupasthitau \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Directed by the gesture from his eyebrows they went up into the sky. Within half a moment they came back, bowed to him and stood in front of him. They were holding a pair of hands, a head and a headless trunk.

## \|\| 4.21.17 \|\|

*śiraḥkabaṃdhe hastau ca dṛṣṭvā'bdhitanayasya sā \|*  
*papāta mūrchitā bhūmau bhartṛvyasanaduḥkhitā \|\| 17 \|\|*
