17\. On noticing that the head, the trunk and the hands were those of the son of the Ocean (Jalandhara), she fell on the ground unconscious, miserable due to the distress of her husband.

## \|\| 4.21.18 \|\|

*kamaṃḍalūdakaiḥ siktvā muninā'śvāsitā tadā \|*  
*svabhartṛbhāle sā bhālaṃ kṛtvā dīnā ruroda ha \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. After sprinkling her with the waters from his water pot the sage consoled her. Placing her forehead upon the forehead of her husband, she cried piteously.

## \|\| 4.21.19 \|\|

*vṛndovāca \|*  
*yaḥ purā sukhasaṃvāde vinodayasi māṃ prabho \|*  
*sa kathaṃ na vadasyadya vallabhā māmanāgasam \|\| 19 \|\|*

Vṛndā said:

19\. O my lord, formerly during our happy dialogue you used to humour me and delight me. I am your beloved and innocent wife. Why don’t you speak to me now?

## \|\| 4.21.20 \|\|

*yena devāḥ sagaṃdharvā nirjitā viṣṇunā saha \|*  
*sa kathaṃ tāpasenā'dya trailokyavijayī hataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. You were the conqueror of the three worlds. Devas and Gandharvas along with Viṣṇu have been defeated by you. How did it happen that you have now been killed by a mere ascetic?

## \|\| 4.21.21-22 \|\|

*iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe kārtikamāsamāhātmye jalaṃdharopākhyāne vṛndāgnipraveśavarṇanaṃnāmaikaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tvamevāsya mune śakto jīvanāya mato mama \|*  
*nārada uvāca \|*  
*iti tadvākyamākarṇya prahasanmunirabravīt \|\| 22 \|\|*

Nārada said:

21-22. After lamenting thus, Vṛndā spoke these words to the sage:

## \|\| 4.21.23 \|\|

*muniruvāca \|*  
*nā'yaṃ jīvayituṃ śakto rudreṇa nihato yudhi \|*  
*tathā'pi tvatkṛpāviṣṭa enaṃ saṃjīvayāmyaham \|\| 23 \|\|*

Vṛndā said:

O excellent sage, O storehouse of mercy, resuscitate this my lover and lord. You alone are capable of bringing him back to life, O sage, I believe.

Nārada said:

On hearing these words of hers, the sage said with a smile:

The sage said:

23\. He has been killed in battle by Rudra. He cannot be made alive once again. Still, out of sympathy for you, I shall make him alive.

## \|\| 4.21.24 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvāṃtardadhe viprastāvatsāgaranaṃdanaḥ \|*  
*vṛṃdāmāliṃgya tadvaktraṃ cucuṃba prītamānasaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

Nārada said:

24\. After saying this, the Brāhmaṇa vanished. By that time, the son of the Ocean embraced Vṛndā and kissed her face with great mental pleasure and satisfaction.

## \|\| 4.21.25 \|\|

*atha vṛndā'pi bhartāraṃ dṛṣṭvā harṣitamānasā \|*  
*reme tadvanamadhyasthā tadyuktā bahuvāsaram \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Vṛndā too was extremely delighted in her mind on seeing her husband once again. Staying within the forest in his company for many days, she sported about.

## \|\| 4.21.26 \|\|

*kadācitsuratasyāṃte dṛṣṭvā viṣṇuṃ tameva ca \|*  
*nirbhartsya krodhasaṃyuktā vṛndā vacanamabravīt \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Once at the conclusion of the sexual intercourse, she saw him in the form of Viṣṇu. Rebuking him angrily Vṛndā spoke these words:

## \|\| 4.21.27 \|\|

*vṛṃdovāca \|*  
*dhiktvadīyaṃ hare śīlaṃ paradārābhigāminaḥ \|*  
*jñāto'si tvaṃ mayā samyaṅmāyāpracchannatāpasaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

Vṛndā said:

27\. Fie upon your conduct, O Hari, you commit adultery! I know now well that you are a fake ascetic.

## \|\| 4.21.28 \|\|

*yau tvayā māyayā dvāḥsthau svakīyau darśitau mama \|*  
*tāveva rākṣasau bhūtvā bhāryāṃ tava hariṣyataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The two, your own gatekeepers, who were shown to me by you by means of Māyā will be born as Rākṣasas. They will abduct your wife.

## \|\| 4.21.29 \|\|

*tvaṃ cā'pi bhāryāduḥkhārto vane kapisahāyavān \|*  
*bhrama sarpeśvareṇā'yaṃ yaste śiṣyatvamāgataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. You will wander in forest, miserable due to the separation from your wife. Do wander along with this Lord of serpents, who has now been your disciple.

## \|\| 4.21.30 \|\|

*ityuktvā sā tadā vṛndā prāviśaddhavyavāhanam \|*  
*viṣṇunā vāryamāṇā'pi tasyāmāsaktacetasā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. After saying this, Vṛndā entered fire, though Viṣṇu whose mind was attached to her, tried to prevent her.

## Chapter 22 - Jalandhara Attains Salvation

## \|\| 4.22.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*tato jalaṃdharo dṛṣṭvā rudramadbhutavikramam \|*  
*cakāra māyayā gaurīṃ tryaṃbakaṃ mohayanniva \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:

1\. On seeing Rudra with wonderful exploits, Jalandhara created (an illusory) Gaurī by means of his Māyā, as though to delude the Three-eyed Lord.

## \|\| 4.22.2 \|\|

*rathopari ca tāṃ baddhāṃ rudantīṃ pārvatīṃ śivaḥ \|*  
*niśuṃbhapramukhādyaiśca vadhyamānāṃ dadarśa saḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Śiva saw that Pārvatī was crying. She was bound above the chariot and was being struck and hit by Niśuṃbha and others.

## \|\| 4.22.3 \|\|

*gaurīṃ tathāvidhāṃ dṛṣṭvā śivo'pyudvignamānasaḥ \|*  
*avāṅmukhaḥ sthitastūṣṇīṃ vismṛtya svaparākramam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On seeing Gaurī in that plight, Śiva too became agonized in his mind. With his face bent down, he stood motionless forgetting his own valour.

## \|\| 4.22.4 \|\|

*tato jalaṃdharo vegāttribhirvivyādha sāyakaiḥ \|*  
*āpuṃkhamagraistaṃ rudraṃ śirasyurasi codare \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Then with great rapidity, Jalandhara pierced Rudra with three arrows which went deep into his head, chest and belly up to their tail-feathers.

## \|\| 4.22.5 \|\|

*tato jajñe sa tāṃ māyāṃ viṣṇunā ca prabodhitaḥ \|*  
*raudrarūpadharo jāto jvālāmālā'tibhīṣaṇaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Then enlightened by Viṣṇu, he (Śiva) understood that it was all Māyā (trickery). Thereupon he adopted a very terrific form, dreadful on account of the clusters of flames.

## \|\| 4.22.6 \|\|

*tasyā'tīva mahāraudraṃ rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahāsurāḥ \|*  
*na śekuḥ saṃmukhe sthātuṃ bhejire te diśo daśa \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On seeing his excessively terrifying form, the great Asuras being incapable of standing in front of him (fled) and resorted to all the ten quarters.

## \|\| 4.22.7 \|\|

*tataḥ śāpaṃ dadau rudrastayoḥ śuṃbhaniśuṃbhayoḥ \|*  
*mama yuddhādapakrāṃtau gauryā badhyau bhaviṣyathaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Then Rudra cursed the two Rākṣasas Śuṃbha and Niśuṃbha thus: “You who fled away from the battle with me, shall be killed by Gaurī.”

## \|\| 4.22.8 \|\|

*punarjalaṃdharo vegādvavarṣa niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ \|*  
*bāṇāṃdhakāraiḥ saṃchannaṃ tadā bhūmitalaṃ mahat \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Again Jalandhara showered sharp arrows in quick succession. At that time the vast surface of the earth was covered by darkness due to the (numerous) arrows (so discharged).

## \|\| 4.22.9 \|\|

*yāvadrudraśca ciccheda tasya bāṇagaṇaṃ javāt \|*  
*tāvatsa parigheṇā'śu jaghāna vṛṣabhaṃ balī \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. By the time Rudra quickly cut off the mass of his arrows, that powerful demon immediately hit the bull with an iron club.

## \|\| 4.22.10 \|\|

*vṛṣastena prahāreṇa parāvṛtto raṇāṃgaṇāt \|*  
*rudreṇā'kṛṣyamāṇo'pi na tasthau raṇabhūmiṣu \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. On account of that blow, the bull turned away from the battlefield. Though it was dragged and pulled by Rudra, it did not stay on the battlegrounds.

## \|\| 4.22.11 \|\|

*tataḥ paramasaṃkuddho rudro raudravapurdharaḥ \|*  
*cakraṃ sudarśanaṃ vegāccikṣepā'dityavarcasam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thereupon Rudra became excessively infuriated. He adopted a highly dreadful physical form. With great velocity he hurled the discus Sudaraśana that had the refulgence of the Sun.

## \|\| 4.22.12 \|\|

*pradahadrodasī vegātpapāta vasudhātale \|*  
*jahāra tacchiraḥ kāyānmahadāyatalocanam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Burning heaven and earth, it rapidly descended on the earth and severed his (Jalandhara’s) head with huge large eyes from his body.

## \|\| 4.22.13-16 \|\|

*rathātkāyaḥ papātā'sya nādayanvasudhātalam \|*  
*tejaśca nirgataṃ dehāttadrudre layamāgamat \|\| 13 \|\|*

*vṛndādehodbhavaṃ tejastadgauryāṃ vilayaṃ gatam \|*  
*atha brahmādayo devā harṣādutphullalocanāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*praṇamya śirasā rudraṃ śaśaṃsurviṣṇuceṣṭitam \|*  
*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*mahādeva tvayā devā rakṣitāḥ śatrujādbhayāt \|\| 15 \|\|*

*kiṃcidanyatsamudbhūtaṃ tatra kiṃ karavāmahe \|*  
*vṛndālāvaṇyasaṃbhrāṃto viṣṇustiṣṭhati mohitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

13-14a. His body came with a thudding sound upon the surface of the earth when it fell from the chariot. A refulgence issued forth from his body and it merged in Rudra. The refulgence that had issued forth from the body of Vṛndā got merged into Gaurī.

14b-16. Then the Devas beginning with Brahmā, with eyes beaming like full-blown lotuses due to delight, bowed down their heads before Rudra and spoke of the action of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 4.22.17 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*gacchadhvaṃ śaraṇaṃ devā viṣṇormohāpanuttaye \|*  
*śaraṇyāṃ mohinīṃ māyāṃ sā vaḥ kāryaṃ kariṣyati \|\| 17 \|\|*

Devas said:

O Mahādeva, Devas have been rescued from the fear arising from the enemies. But a new development has taken place. What shall we do in that respect? Viṣṇu has become deluded by the beauty of Vṛndā, He stands enchanted.

Īśvara said:

17\. O Devas, in order to dispel the delusion of Viṣṇu, go and seek refuge in Māyā, the Mohinī (Enchantress) worthy of being sought shelter in. She will do your work.

## \|\| 4.22.18 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvāṃtardadhe devaḥ sarvabhūtagaṇaistadā \|*  
*devāśca tuṣṭuvurmūlaprakṛtiṃ bhaktavatsalām \|\| 18 \|\|*

Nārada said:

18\. After saying this the Lord vanished along with all the Bhūtas and the Gaṇas. The Devas then eulogized Mūlaprakṛti (Primordial Prakṛti) fond of her devotees.

## \|\| 4.22.19 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*yadudbhavāḥ sattvarajastamoguṇāḥ sargasthitidhvaṃsanidānakāriṇaḥ \|*  
*yadicchayā viśvamidaṃ bhavā'bhavau tanoti mūlaprakṛtiṃ natāḥ sma tām \|\| 19 \|\|*

Devas said:

19\. We bow down to that Mūlaprakṛti from whom the guṇas, Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas, originate and then cause the creation, sustenance and annihilation (of the universe) and at whose will this universe extends and causes its existence and non-existence.

## \|\| 4.22.20 \|\|

*yā hi trayoviṃśatibhedaśabditā jagatyaśeṣe samadhiṣṭhitā parā \|*  
*yadrūpakarmāṇi jaḍāstrayo'pi devā na vidyuḥ prakṛtiṃ natāḥ sma tām \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. We bow down to that Prakṛti which has been said to have twenty-three different manifestations (evolutes or Tattvas?), which is the greatest being that is established in the entire universe, and whose form and activities are not known to even the three foolish Devas.

## \|\| 4.22.21 \|\|

*yadbhaktiyuktāḥ puruṣāstu nityaṃ dāridryabhīmohaparābhavādīn \|*  
*na prāpnuvaṃtyeva hi bhaktavatsalāṃ sadaiva mūlaprakṛtiṃ natāḥ sma tām \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. We bow down to that Mūlaprakṛti who is fond of her devotees. Those Puruṣas who have devotion to her do not meet with poverty, fear, delusion, defeat etc.

## \|\| 4.22.22 \|\|

*iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe kārtikamāsamāhātmye jalaṃdharamuktikathanaṃ nāma dvāviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

Nārada said:

22\. Poverty, delusion and misery never touch that person who reads and recites this prayer with fully concentrated mind during the three junctions (i.e. morning, noon and at dusk).

## \|\| 4.22.23 \|\|

*itthaṃ stuvaṃtaste devāstejomaṇḍalamāsthitam \|*  
*dadṛśurgaganaṃ tatra jvālāvyāptadigaṃtaram \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Even as those Devas were eulogizing thus, they saw a mass of splendour spreading in the firmament. Flames spread in all the quarters and the intervening spaces.

## \|\| 4.22.24-25 \|\|

*tanmadhyādbhāratīṃ sarve śuśruvurvyomacāriṇīm \|*  
*śaktiruvāca \|*  
*ahameva tridhā bhinnā tiṣṭhāmi trividhairguṇaiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*gaurī lakṣmī svarā ceti rajaḥsattvatamoguṇaiḥ \|*  
*tatra gacchata tāḥ kāryaṃ vidhāsyati ca vaḥ surāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. From its middle all of them heard the speech spreading in (i.e. emanating from) the firmament.

## \|\| 4.22.26 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇvatāmiti tāṃ vācamaṃtardhānamagānmahaḥ \|*  
*devānāṃ vismayotphullanetrāṇāṃ tattadā nṛpa \|\| 26 \|\|*

Śakti said:

I alone stand in three different forms characterized by the three Guṇas. I am Gaurī, Lakṣmī and Svarā characterized by the Guṇas of Rajas, Sattva and Tamas respectively. Therefore go to them, O Suras, they will do your work.

Nārada said:

26\. Even as the Devas stood listening to this, with surprise evident in their beaming eyes, that refulgence vanished, O king.

## \|\| 4.22.27 \|\|

*tataḥ sarve'pi te devā gatvā tadvākyanoditāḥ \|*  
*gaurīṃ lakṣmīṃ svarāṃ caiva praṇemurbhaktitatparāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. On being urged by those words (of Śakti), all those Devas went to Gaurī, Lakṣmī and Svarā and bowed down with great devotion.

## \|\| 4.22.28 \|\|

*tatastāstānsurāndṛṣṭvā praṇatānbhaktavatsalāḥ \|*  
*bījāni pradadustebhyo vākyānyūcuśca bhūmipa \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. On seeing the Suras bowing down, those deities, fond of devotees, gave them the seeds and spoke these words, O king.

## \|\| 4.22.29 \|\|

*devya ūcuḥ \|*  
*imāni tatra bījāni viṣṇuryatrā'vatiṣṭhate \|*  
*nirvapadhvaṃ tataḥ kāryaṃ bhavatāṃ siddhimeṣyati \|\| 29 \|\|*

The Devīs said:

29\. Sow these seeds in the place where Viṣṇu is present. Then you will succeed in your work.

## Chapter 23 - The Origin of Dhātrī and Tulasī

## \|\| 4.23.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*kṣiptebhyastatra bījebhyo vanaspatyastrayo'bhavan \|*  
*dhātrī ca mālatī caiva tulasī ca nṛpottama \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:

1\. From the seeds sown there three plants grew up, viz. Dhātrī, Mālatī (Jasmine) and Tulasī.

## \|\| 4.23.2 \|\|

*dhātryudbhavā smṛtā dhātrī mābhavā mālatī smṛtā \|*  
*gaurībhavā ca tulasī tamaḥsattvarajoguṇāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Dhātrī is remembered as having been born of Dhātrī (the Earth); Mālatī is remembered as born of Mā (Lakṣmī) and Tulasī is born of Gaurī. These have the Guṇas—Tamas, Sattva and Rajas (respectively).

## \|\| 4.23.3 \|\|

*strīrūpiṇyau vanaspatyau dṛṣṭvā viṣṇustadā nṛpa \|*  
*uttasthau saṃbhramādvṛṃdā rūpātiśayavibhramaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On seeing the plants in the form of women, O king, Viṣṇu got up with great excitement. His flurry and perturbation was mainly due to the excessive beauty of Vṛndā.

## \|\| 4.23.4 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā ca yācate mohātkāmāsaktena cetasā \|*  
*taṃ cā'pi tulasīdhātryau rāgeṇaiva vyalokatām \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. On seeing them he began to solicit due to fascination with a passionate mind. Tulasī and Dhātrī looked at him with sincere love and attachment.

## \|\| 4.23.5 \|\|

*yacca lakṣmyā purā bījamīrṣyayaiva samarpitam \|*  
*tasmāttadudbhavā nārī tasminnīrṣyāparā'bhavat \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Since the seed was offered formerly by Lakṣmī with malice and jealousy, the woman originating therefrom became malicious and jealous with him.

## \|\| 4.23.6 \|\|

*ataḥ sā barbarītyākhyāmavāpā'dha vigarhitām \|*  
*dhātrītulasyau tadrāgāttasya prītiprade sadā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Hence she (it) later received the despicable name Barbarī. But Dhātrī and Tulasī accorded great pleasure and delight to him always due to their attachment and love for him.

## \|\| 4.23.7 \|\|

*tato vismṛtaduḥkho'sau viṣṇustābhyāṃ sahaiva tu \|*  
*vaikuṇṭhamagamaddhṛṣṭaḥ sarvadeva namaskṛtaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Then Viṣṇu forgot all his misery. Becoming delighted, he went to Vaikuṇṭha along with them. He was then bowed to by all the Devas.

## \|\| 4.23.8 \|\|

*kārtikodyāpane viṣṇostasmātpūjā vidhīyate \|*  
*tulasīmūladeśe'sya prītidā sā yataḥ smṛtā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Hence while concluding the Kārttika Vrata, Viṣṇu is worshipped at the root of the Tulasī plant, since it is remembered as very pleasant to him.

## \|\| 4.23.9 \|\|

*tulasīkānanaṃ rājangṛhe yasyā'vatiṣṭhate \|*  
*tadgṛhaṃ tīrtharūpaṃ tu nā'yāṃti yamakiṃkarāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The house in which there is a grove of Tulasī plants is a Tīrtha, O king. The servants of Yama do not come there.

## \|\| 4.23.10 \|\|

*sarvapāpaharaṃ nityaṃ kāmadaṃ tulasīvanam \|*  
*ropayaṃti narāḥ śreṣṭhāste na paśyaṃti bhāskarim \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Those excellent men who grow the Tulasī grove that is destructive of all sins and always grants all desired objects, never see the son of the Sun-god (Yama, the god of Death).

## \|\| 4.23.11 \|\|

*darśanaṃ narmadāyāstu gaṃgāsnānaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*tulasīvanasaṃsargaḥ samameva trayaṃ smṛtam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. These three are said to be equal (in efficacy): seeing Narmada, taking a holy bath in Gaṅgā and association with the grove of Tulasī plants.

## \|\| 4.23.12 \|\|

*ropaṇātpālanātsekāddarśanātsparśanānnṛṇām \|*  
*tulasī dahate pāpaṃ vāṅmanaḥkāyasaṃcitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. If it is planted, guarded, watered, seen and touched, Tulasī burns down the sins of men accumulated through words, thoughts and physical activities.

## \|\| 4.23.13 \|\|

*tulasīmaṃjarībhiryaḥ kuryāddhariharā'rcanam \|*  
*na sa garbhagṛhaṃ yāti muktibhāgī na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He who worships Hari and Hara with bunches of Tulasī, is not reborn in any other womb. He shall certainly attain salvation.

## \|\| 4.23.14 \|\|

*puṣkarādyāni tīrthāni gaṃgādyāḥ saritastathā \|*  
*vāsudevādayo devāstiṣṭhaṃti tulasīdale \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Tīrthas including Puṣkara, rivers including Gaṅgā and Devas including Vāsudeva dwell on the leaf of the Tulasī plant.

## \|\| 4.23.15 \|\|

*tulasīmaṃjarīyukto yastu prāṇānvimuṃcati \|*  
*yamo'pi nekṣituṃ śakto yuktaṃ pāpaśatairapi \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Even Yama is incapable of looking at the person who gives up his life with a bunch of Tulasī (on his person), though he may have committed hundreds of sins.

## \|\| 4.23.16-18 \|\|

*viṣṇoḥ sāyujyamāpnoti satyaṃ satyaṃ nṛpottama \|*  
*tulasīkāṣṭhajaṃ yastu caṃdanaṃ dhārayennaraḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*taddehaṃ na spṛśetpāpaṃ kriyamāṇamapīha yat \|*  
*tulasīvipinacchāyā yatrayatra bhavennṛpa \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tatra śrāddhaṃ prakartavyaṃ pitṝṇāṃ dattamakṣayam \|*  
*dhātrīphalavimiśraiśca tulasīpatramiśritaiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

16-18. He attains Sāyujya with Viṣṇu. O excellent king, this is certainly true. One who wears a twig of the Tulasī plant with sandal paste is never contaminated with sins even if they are committed. Wherever there is the shade of Tulasī grove, Śrāddha should be performed unto the Manes there. The Śrāddha thus offered is of everlasting benefit.

## \|\| 4.23.19-22 \|\|

*jalaiḥ snāti narastasya gaṃgāsnānaphalaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*devārcanaṃ naraḥ kuryāddhātrīpatraiḥ phalaistathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*suvarṇamaṇimuktaughairarcanasyāpnuyātphalam \|*  
*tīrthāni munayo devā yajñāḥ sarve'pi kārtike \|\| 20 \|\|*

*nityaṃ dhātrīṃ samāśritya tiṣṭhaṃtyarke tulāsthite \|*  
*dvādaśyāṃ tulasīpatraṃ dhātrīpatraṃ tu kārtike \|\| 21 \|\|*

*lunāti sa naro gacchennirayānatigarhitān \|*  
*dhātrītulasyormāhātmyamapi devaścaturmukhaḥ \|*  
*na samartho bhavedvaktuṃ yathā devasya śārṅgiṇaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

19-21a. One who takes his holy bath with the waters mingled with fruits of Dhātrī and with leaves of Tulasī attains the benefit of holy bath in Gaṅgā.

If a man performs the worship of the Lord with leaves and fruits of Dhātrī, he shall attain the benefit of a worship with gold, jewels and multitudes of pearls.

In the month of Kārttika, when the Sun is in the Zodiac Libra, all the Tīrthas, sages, Devas and Yajñas perpetually resort to Dhātrī.

21b-22. One who plucks the leaves of Tulasī on the twelfth day and those of Dhātrī in the month of Kārttika falls into the most despicable of all the hells.

Even the Four-faced Lord is not capable of recounting the greatness of Dhātrī and Tulasī as that of the Śārṅga-bearing Lord (Viṣṇu).

## Chapter 24 - The Legend of Dharmadatta

## \|\| 4.24.1 \|\|

*pṛthuruvāca \|*  
*yadūrjavratinaḥ puṃsaḥ phalaṃ mahadudādṛtam \|*  
*tatpunarbrūhi māhātmyaṃ kena cīrṇamidaṃ śubham \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: The legend of Dharmadatta is mentioned in 12.86 supra. The detailed legend is given in this chapter. This is obviously a later addition.

Pṛthu said:

1\. The great benefit of the person of observing the Kārttika Vrata has been mentioned. Describe once again its efficacy. By whom was this observed? By whom has this splendid Vrata been performed?

## \|\| 4.24.2 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*āsītsahyādriviṣaye karavīrapure purā \|*  
*brāhmaṇo dharmavitkaściddharmadatteti viśrutaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Nārada said:

2\. Formerly, in the city of Karavīra, in the country (around) Sahya mountain, there was a certain Brāhmaṇa well known by the name Dharmadatta.

## \|\| 4.24.3-7 \|\|

*viṣṇuvratakaraḥ samyagviṣṇupūjārataḥ sadā \|*  
*kadācitkārtike māsi harijāgaraṇāya saḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*rātryāṃ turyāvaśeṣāyāṃ jagāma harimadiram \|*  
*haripūjopakaraṇānpragṛhya vrajatā tadā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tena dṛṣṭā samāyātā rākṣasī bhīmadarśanā \|*  
*tāṃ dṛṣṭvā bhayavitrastaḥ kaṃpitāvayavastadā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*pūjopakaraṇaiḥ sarvaiḥ payobhiścāhanadbhayāt \|*  
*saṃsmṛtya taddharernāma tulasīyuktavāriṇā \|*  
*tena vai hatamātre tu pāpaṃ tasyā hyagāllayam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*atha saṃsmṛtya sā pūrvajanmakarmavipākajām \|*  
*svāṃ daśāmabravīdvipraṃ daṃḍavacca praṇamya vai \|\| 7 \|\|*

3-7. He performed (all) Viṣṇu Vratas. He was always engaged in the proper worship of Viṣṇu.

Once, in the month of Kārttika, he went to the temple of Hari when a fourth of the night yet remained, for the purpose of Hari Jāgaraṇa (keeping awake at night along with prayers to Hari).

As he went along taking all the materials of worship of Hari with him, a Rākṣasī (demoness) of dreadful appearance was seen coming by him. On seeing her, he became extremely frightened. All his limbs began to tremble. Out of fear he threw all the materials of worship and the holy waters upon her. The moment she was hit by that water which contained a Tulasī leaf after remembering Hari’s names her sins perished. She remembered that her state was the result of her Karmas of the previous birth. She prostrated in front of the Brāhmaṇa and spoke these words:

## \|\| 4.24.8 \|\|

*kalahovāca \|*  
*pūrvakarmavipākena daśāmetāṃ gatāsmyaham \|*  
*tatkathaṃ nu punarvipra prayāsyāmyuttamāṃ gatim \|\| 8 \|\|*

Kalahā said:

8\. I have attained this plight (of being an ogress) as a result of my own previous Karmas. How can I once again, O Brāhmaṇa, attain the excellent goal?

## \|\| 4.24.9 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*tāṃ dṛṣṭvā praṇatāṃ samyagvadamānāṃ svakarma tat \|*  
*atīva vismito viprastadā vacanamabravīt \|\| 9 \|\|*

Nārada said:

9\. On seeing her bowing down and clearly speaking about her own Karmas, the Brāhmaṇa was exceedingly surprised. Then he spoke these words:

## \|\| 4.24.10 \|\|

*dharmadatta uvāca \|*  
*kena karmavipākena tvaṃ daśāmīdṛśīṃ gatā \|*  
*kutratyā kā ca kiṃ śīlā tatsarvaṃ kathayasva me \|\| 10 \|\|*

Dharmadatta said:

10\. What is that Karma as a result of which you have attained such a plight as this? Who are you? To which place do you belong? What had been your conduct? Tell me everything.

## \|\| 4.24.11 \|\|

*kalahovāca \|*  
*saurāṣṭranagare brahmanbhikṣurnāmā'bhavaddvijaḥ \|*  
*tasyāhaṃ gṛhiṇī pūrvaṃ kalahākhyā'tiniṣṭhurā \|\| 11 \|\|*

Kalahā said:

11\. O Brāhmaṇa, formerly there was a Brāhmaṇa named Bhikṣu in a city in Saurāṣṭra. I was his wife Kalahā by name. I was extremely cruel.

## \|\| 4.24.12-16 \|\|

*na kadācinmayā bharturvacasā'pi śubhaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*nā'rpitaṃ tasya miṣṭānnaṃ bharturvacanaśīlayā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*kalahapriyayā nityaṃ mayodvignamanā yadā \|*  
*pariṇetuṃ yadā'nyāṃ sa matiṃ cakre patirmama \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tato garaṃ samādāya prāṇāstyaktā mayā dvija \|*  
*atha baddhvā badhyamānāṃ māṃ ninyuryamakiṃkarāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*yamaśca māṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā citraguptamapṛcchata \|\| 15 \|\|*

*yama uvāca \|*  
*anayā kiṃ kṛtaṃ karma citragupta vilokaya \|*  
*prāpnotveṣā ca tatkarma śubhaṃ vā yadi vā'śubham \|\| 16 \|\|*

12-16. No auspicious rite was performed by me even at the instance of my husband. Nor did I ever offer him sweet food. He became dejected because I was fond of quarrel and habituated to speak (harsh) words to my husband. So my husband became inclined to marry another woman. Therefore, I took poison and gave up my life, O Brāhmaṇa. Then the servants of Yama bound me and carried me away even as I was being tortured. On seeing me Yama asked Citragupta:

## \|\| 4.24.17 \|\|

*kalahovāca \|*  
*citraguptastadā vākyaṃ bhartsayanmāmuvāca saḥ \|*  
*citragupta uvāca \|*  
*anayā tu kṛtaṃ karma śubhaṃ kiṃcinna vidyate \|\| 17 \|\|*

Yama said:

O Citragupta, see what acts have been performed by this woman. Let her experience the fruit thereof, food or otherwise.

Kalahā said:

17\. Then Citragupta rebuked me and spoke these words: Citragupta said:

No good act was done at all by this woman.

## \|\| 4.24.18 \|\|

*miṣṭānnaṃ bhuṃjamāneyaṃ na bhartari tadarpitam \|*  
*ataśca valgulīyonyāṃ svaviṣṭhādā'vatiṣṭhatu \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. She used to eat sweet food but nothing was given to her husband. Hence let her be born of a Valgulī (a kind of bat or a species of nocturnal birds) and let her remain feeding herself on her own faeces.

## \|\| 4.24.19 \|\|

*bharturdveṣāttadāpyeṣā nityaṃ kalahakāriṇī \|*  
*viṣṭhādāṃ sūkarīṃ yoniṃ tasmāttiṣṭhatviyaṃ hare \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. She used to despise her own husband and regularly quarrelled with him. Hence, O Yama, let her be born in the womb of a Sūkarī (a sow, a female pig).

## \|\| 4.24.20 \|\|

*pākabhāṃḍe sadā bhuṃkte bhuṃkte caikā yatastataḥ \|*  
*tasmādeṣā biḍālyastu svajātā'patyabhakṣiṇī \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. She used to eat straight from the vessel in which food was cooked. She was further in the habit of taking food by herself. Hence let her be born as a cat that devours her own young one.

## \|\| 4.24.21 \|\|

*bhartāramapi coddiśya hyātmaghātaḥ kṛto'nayā \|*  
*tasmātpretaśarīre'pi tiṣṭhatvekā'tiniṃditā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. With her husband in view, she had committed suicide. Hence she is highly despicable. So, let her remain as a ghost in the dead body, all alone.

## \|\| 4.24.22 \|\|

*ataścaiṣā maruddeśaṃ prāpitavyā bhaṭairiyam \|*  
*tatra pretaśarīrasthā ciraṃ tiṣṭhatviyaṃ tataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Therefore, she has to be taken to a desert place by the soldiers (of Yama). Let her be a ghost there and remain there for a long time.

## \|\| 4.24.23 \|\|

*ūrdhvaṃ yonitrayaṃ caiṣā bhunaktvaśubhakāriṇī \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. After that let her be born (as mentioned before) in the three wombs (species) as she had been a doer of evil acts.

## \|\| 4.24.24 \|\|

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ sahitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe kārtikamāsamāhātmye dharmadattetihāsakathanaṃnāma caturviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

Kalahā said:

24\. I remained as a ghost in a dead body for five hundred years. Being afflicted with hunger and thirst I permeated the body of a merchant. Then I came to the southern land to the confluence where Kṛṣṇā and Veṇī meet.

## \|\| 4.24.25 \|\|

*tattīraṃ saṃśritā yāvattāvattasya śarīrataḥ \|*  
*śivaviṣṇugaṇairdūramapakṛṣṭā balādaham \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. As soon as I came to the banks of that river, I was dragged out of the body of that merchant by the attendants of Śiva and Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 4.24.26 \|\|

*tataḥ kṣutkṣāmayā dṛṣṭo mayā hi tvaṃ dvijottama \|*  
*tvaddhastatulasīvārisaṃsargagatapāpayā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Then, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, you were seen by me even as my body has become emaciated. Thanks to the contact with the Tulasī water sprinkled with your hand, all my sins have disappeared.

## \|\| 4.24.27 \|\|

*tatkṛtyaṃ kuru vipreṃdra kathaṃ muktimiyāmyaham \|*  
*yonitrayādagrabhavādasmācca pretadehataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O eminent Brāhmaṇa, perform that holy rite whereby I shall attain liberation from this ghostly nature, as well as the three types of births destined to happen later.

## Chapter 25 - Kalahā Attains Liberation

## \|\| 4.25.1 \|\|

*dharmadatta uvāca \|*  
*vilayaṃ yāṃti pāpāni tīrthe dānavratādibhiḥ \|*  
*pretadehasthitāyāste teṣu naivā'dhikāritā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Dharmadatta said:

1\. By performing charitable gifts and holy rites etc. in a Tīrtha, all the sins perish. But you are not authorized for it because you are a ghost in a dead body.

## \|\| 4.25.2 \|\|

*tvadglānidarśanādasmātkhinnaṃ ca mama mānasam \|*  
*na vai nirvṛtimāyāti tvāmanuddhṛtya duḥkhitām \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. My mind is distressed on seeing your misery. Without redeeming you from the misery my mind will not be at ease.

## \|\| 4.25.3 \|\|

*tasmādājanmacaritaṃ yanmayā kārtikavratam \|*  
*tatpuṇyasyārddhabhāgena sadgatiṃ tvamavāpnuhi \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Hence you do attain the good goal by means of half the merit that I have earned throughout my life from Kārttika Vrata.

## \|\| 4.25.4 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā dharmadatto'sau yāvattāmabhyaṣecayat \|*  
*tulasīmiśratoyena śrāvayandvādaśākṣaram \|\| 4 \|\|*

Nārada said:

4\. After saying thus, Dharmadatta sprinkled on her water mixed with Tulasī and repeated the twelve-syllabled Mantra (oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya):

## \|\| 4.25.5 \|\|

*tāvatpretatvanirmuktā jvaladagniśikhopamā \|*  
*divyarūpadharā jātā lāvaṇyena yatheṃdirā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Immediately she became liberated from ghosthood. She assumed a divine form comparable to the flames of blazing fire. In beauty she appeared like Indirā.

## \|\| 4.25.6 \|\|

*tataḥ sā daṃḍavadbhūmau praṇanāmātha taṃ dvijam \|*  
*uvāca sā tadā vākyairharṣagadgadabhāṣiṇī \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Then she prostrated flat on the ground like a rod and bowed down to that Brāhmaṇa. Then with words choked with delight, she spoke thus:

## \|\| 4.25.7 \|\|

*kalahovāca \|*  
*tvatprasādāddvijaśreṣṭha vimuktā nirayādaham \|*  
*pāpābdhau majjamānāyāstvaṃ naubhūto'si me dhruvam \|\| 7 \|\|*

Kalahā said:

7\. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, with your favour I have been redeemed from hell. Certainly you have been like a boat unto me, as I was about to be drowned in the ocean of sin.

## \|\| 4.25.8 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*itthaṃ vadantī sā vipraṃ dadarśā'yātamaṃbarāt \|*  
*vimānaṃ bhāsvaraṃ yuktaṃ viṣṇurūpadharairgaṇaiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

Nārada said:

8\. As she was speaking thus to the Brāhmaṇa, she saw a sparkling aerial chariot coming from the sky accompanied by attendants who had assumed the form of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 4.25.9 \|\|

*atha sā tadvimānā'gryaṃ dvāḥsthābhyāmavaropitā \|*  
*puṇyaśīlasuśīlābhyāmapsarogaṇasevitā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The gatekeepers Puṇyaśīla and Suśīla made her get into that excellent aerial chariot. She was (there) served by groups of celestial damsels.

## \|\| 4.25.10 \|\|

*tadvimānaṃ tadā'paśyaddharmadattaḥ savismayaḥ \|*  
*papāta daṇḍavadbhūmau dṛṣṭvā tau viṣṇurūpiṇau \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Dharmadatta gazed at that aerial chariot with great wonder. On seeing those two in the form of Viṣṇu he prostrated flat on the ground.

## \|\| 4.25.11 \|\|

*puṇyaśīlasuśīlau ca tamutthāpyā'nataṃ dvijam \|*  
*abhinandya tato vākyamūcaturdharmasaṃyutam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Puṇyaśīla and Suśīla raised the Brāhmaṇa who was bowing down. After congratulating him, they spoke these righteous words:

## \|\| 4.25.12 \|\|

*gaṇāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*sādhusādhu dvijaśreṣṭha yastvaṃ viṣṇurataḥ sadā \|*  
*dīnā'nukampī sarvajño viṣṇuvrataparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

The Attendants said:

12\. Well done, well done, O excellent Brāhmaṇa. You are omniscient. You are merciful to the distressed. You are engaged in the holy rites of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 4.25.13 \|\|

*ā bālatvācchubhaṃ tvetadyattvayā kārtikavratam \|*  
*kṛtaṃ tasyā'rddhadānena puṇyaṃ dvaiguṇyamāgamat \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Ever since your childhood you have been performing the excellent Kārttikavrata. Half of the merit thereof you have donated. Hence your merit has become doubled.

## \|\| 4.25.14 \|\|

*janmāṃtaraśatodbhūtaṃ pāpaṃ tadvilayaṃ gatam \|*  
*snānaireva gataṃ pāpaṃ yadasyāḥ pūrvakarmajam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. All the sins of yours that had accumulated in the course of hundreds of births have perished. The sin of this woman arising out of her previous Karmas has been destroyed through the holy baths (of yours, transferred to her).

## \|\| 4.25.15 \|\|

*harijāgaraṇādyaiśca vimānamidamāsthitā \|*  
*vaikuṇṭhe nīyate sādho nānābhogayutā tviyam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Through the meritorious deeds of Hari Jāgaraṇa (vigil on the Ekādaśī day) etc. she has got into this aerial chariot and is being taken to Vaikuṇṭha. O gentle Sir, she will enjoy different kinds of pleasures.

## \|\| 4.25.16 \|\|

*dīpadānabhavaiḥ puṇyaistejaḥsārūpyamāsthitā \|*  
*tulasīpūjanādyaiśca kārtikavratakaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|*  
*viṣṇusānnidhyagā jātā tvayā dattaiḥ kṛpānidhe \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. By means of the merit of offering lamps she has attained the Sārūpya of the (Supreme) Refulgence. She has come to the presence of Viṣṇu through the auspicious worships of Tulasī and Kārttika Vratas, all given by you, O storehouse of mercy.

## \|\| 4.25.17 \|\|

*tvamapyasya bhavasyāṃte bhāryābhyāṃ saha yāsyasi \|*  
*vaikuṇṭha bhuvanaṃ viṣṇoḥ sānnidhyaṃ ca sarūpatām \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. At the end of this birth you along with your two wives will go to the world of Vaikuṇṭha, reach the presence of Viṣṇu and attain Sārūpya (indentity of form with Viṣṇu).

## \|\| 4.25.18 \|\|

*te dhanyāḥ kṛtakṛtyāste teṣāṃ ca saphalo bhavaḥ \|*  
*yairbhaktyārādhito viṣṇurdharmadatta yathā tvayā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O Dharmadatta, those people by whom Viṣṇu has been devoutly propitiated like you, are blessed and contented. They have accomplished their object. Their birth is fruitful.

## \|\| 4.25.19 \|\|

*samyagārādhito viṣṇuḥ kiṃ na yacchati dehinām \|*  
*auttānacaraṇiryena dhruvatve sthāpitaḥ purā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. What is it that Viṣṇu does not give to the embodied beings when (he is) perfectly propitiate? The son of Uttānapāda (Dhruva) had been established as Dhruva formerly by him.

## \|\| 4.25.20 \|\|

*yannāmasmaraṇādeva dehino yāṃti sadgatim \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Merely by remembering his name all the embodied beings attain beatitude.

## \|\| 4.25.21 \|\|

*grāhagrasto hi nāgeṃdro yannāmasmaraṇātpurā \|*  
*vimuktaḥ saṃnidhiṃ prāpto jāto'yaṃ jayasaṃjñakaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The great elephant who had been caught in the jaws of a crocodile, became liberated formerly by remembering his name. He reached the presence of Viṣṇu and has become (the attendant) named Jaya.

## \|\| 4.25.22 \|\|

*yatastvayā'rcito viṣṇustatsānnidhyaṃ prayāsyasi \|*  
*bahūnyabdasahasrāṇi bhāryādvayayutaḥ kila \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Since Viṣṇu has been worshipped by you, you will go to his presence accompanied by both the wives. You will stay there for thousands of years.

## \|\| 4.25.23-24 \|\|

*tataḥ puṇyakṣayejāte yadā yāsyasi bhūtalam \|*  
*sūryavaṃśodbhavo rājā vikhyātastvaṃ bhaviṣyasi \|\| 23 \|\|*

*nāmnā daśarathastatra bhāryādvayayutaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*tṛtīyayā'nayā cā'pi yā te puṇyārddhabhāginī \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. Then as the merits dwindle, you will go to the earth. Then you will become a famous king named Daśaratha in the solar race. These two wives will be born as your wives then also. This woman who secured half of your merits will be your third wife then.

## \|\| 4.25.25 \|\|

*iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe kārtikamāsamāhātmye dharmadattopākhyāne kalahāmokṣakathanaṃnāma pañcaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. There also Viṣṇu will come to your presence on the earth for carrying out the task of Devas. He will be born as your son.

## \|\| 4.25.26 \|\|

*tava janmavratādasmādviṣṇusaṃtuṣṭikārakāt \|*  
*na yajñā na ca dānāni na tīrthānyadhikāni vai \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Neither Yajñas nor charitable gifts, nor Tīrthas are superior to the Vratas performed by you ever since your birth, as the Vratas give satisfaction to Viṣṇu.

## Chapter 26 - Dialogue between King Cola and Viṣṇudāsa

## \|\| 4.26.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*itthaṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā dharmadattaḥ savismayaḥ \|*  
*praṇamya daṇḍavadbhūmau vākyametaduvāca ha \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: Vide PdP VI (Uttara Khaṇḍa, Pūrvārdha, Chs. 108, 109).

Nārada said:

1\. On hearing their words thus with great wonder Dharmadatta prostrated flat on the ground and spoke these words:

## \|\| 4.26.2-3 \|\|

*dharmadatta uvāca \|*  
*ārādhayaṃti sarve'pi viṣṇuṃ bhaktā'rtināśanam \|*  
*yajñairdānairvrataistīrthaistapobhiśca yathāvidhi \|\| 2 \|\|*

*viṣṇuprītikaraṃ teṣāṃ kiṃcitsānnidhyakārakam \|*  
*yatkṛtvā tāni cīrṇāni sarvāṇyapi bhavaṃti hi \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. All people worship Viṣṇu, the destroyer of the distress of devotees, by means of Yajñas, charitable gifts, Vratas, Tīrthas and penances in accordance with the injunctions. Is there anything which causes pleasure to Viṣṇu, which takes (the devotees) to his presence and by performing which all the (other) holy rites would have been performed?

The Attendants replied:

## \|\| 4.26.4 \|\|

*gaṇāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*sādhu pṛṣṭaṃ tvayā vipra śṛṇuṣvaikāgramānasaḥ \|*  
*setihāsakathāṃ puṇyāṃ kathyamānāṃ purābhavām \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Well asked by you, O Brāhmaṇa. Listen with concentration of mind to the meritorious story that happened formerly.

## \|\| 4.26.5 \|\|

*kāṃcipuryāṃ purā colaścakravartī nṛpo'bhavat \|*  
*yasyākhyayaiva te deśāścolā iti prathāṃ gatāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Formerly Emperor Cola ruled over his kingdom in the city of Kāñcī. The land also was famous by the name Colas after the name of the king.

## \|\| 4.26.6 \|\|

*sa kadācidagādrājā hyanaṃtaśayanaṃ dvija \|*  
*yatrā'sau jagatāṃ nātho yoganidrāmupāśritaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. While he was ruling over the earth no man was poor, miserable, sick or wicked in his mind.

## \|\| 4.26.7 \|\|

*yasyāpyunnatayajñasya tāmraparṇyāstaṭāvubhau \|*  
*suvarṇayūpaiḥ śobhāḍhyāvāstāṃ caitrarathopamau \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He performed many big Yajñas on the banks of Tāmraparṇī where golden sacrificial posts were fixed. This heightened the beauty of the banks and made them resemble the garden Caitraratha (of Kubera).

## \|\| 4.26.8 \|\|

*null*

8\. Once, O Brāhmaṇa, that king went to Anantaśayana (modern Trivandrum, capital of Kerala) where the Lord of the worlds has resorted to Yogic slumber.

## \|\| 4.26.9 \|\|

*tatra śrīramaṇaṃ devaṃ saṃpūjya vidhivannṛpaḥ \|*  
*maṇimuktāphalairdivyaiḥ svarṇapuṣpaiśca śobhanaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. There the king duly worshipped the Lord Śrīramaṇa (Lord of Śrī) with jewels and pearls of divine (lustre) and splendid golden flowers.

## \|\| 4.26.10 \|\|

*praṇamya daṇḍavadbhūmāvupaviṣṭaḥ sa tatra vai \|*  
*tāvadbrāhmaṇamāyāṃtamapaśyaddevasannidhau \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After prostrating before the Lord he sat on the ground. By then he saw that a Brāhmaṇa had also come to the presence of the Lord.

## \|\| 4.26.11 \|\|

*devārcanārthaṃ pāṇau tu tulasyudakadhāriṇam \|*  
*svapurīvāsinaṃ tatra viṣṇudāsāhvayaṃ dvijam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. For the purpose of the worship of the Lord he held in his hand Tulasī leaves and water. He was a Brāhmaṇa named Viṣṇudāsa, a resident of his own city.

## \|\| 4.26.12 \|\|

*sa tatrābhyetya viprarṣirdevadevamapūjayat \|*  
*viṣṇusūktena saṃsnāpya tulasīmaṃjarīdalaiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. That saintly Brāhmaṇa approached the Lord of Devas, bathed him with water mixed with bunches of Tulasī and worshipped repeating Viṣṇusūkta.

## \|\| 4.26.13 \|\|

*tulasīpūjayā tasya ratnapūjāṃ purā kṛtām \|*  
*ācchāditāṃ samālokya rājā kuddho'bravīdidam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On seeing that his worship performed with jewels earlier, had been covered by the worship with Tulasī leaves, the king became furious and spoke thus:

## \|\| 4.26.14 \|\|

*cola uvāca \|*  
*māṇikyasvarṇapūjā'tra śobhāḍhyā yā kṛtā mayā \|*  
*viṣṇudāsa kathaṃ seyamācchannā tulasīdalaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

Cola said:

14\. The worship that I had performed with rubies and gold was splendid. O Viṣṇudāsa, how is it that it has been covered up by Tulasī leaves?

## \|\| 4.26.15 \|\|

*viṣṇubhaktiṃ na jānāsi varāko'si mato mama \|*  
*yastvimāmatiśobhāḍhyāṃ pūjāmācchādayasyaho \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. You do not know (real) devotion unto Viṣṇu. You are, I think, very poor. Alas! You have covered up my excessively refulgent worship.

## \|\| 4.26.16 \|\|

*iti tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sakrodhaḥ sa dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*rājño gauravamullaṃghya jagāda vacanaṃ tadā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. On hearing the king’s words thus, the excellent Brāhmaṇa also became furious. Violating the majesty of the king he then spoke these words:

## \|\| 4.26.17 \|\|

*viṣṇudāsa uvāca \|*  
*rājanbhaktiṃ na jānāsi garvito'si nṛpaśriyā \|*  
*kiyadviṣṇuvrataṃ pūrvaṃ tvayā cīrṇaṃ vadasva tat \|\| 17 \|\|*

Viṣṇudāsa said:

17\. O king, you do not know what is devotion. You are proud of your royal glory. How many Viṣṇuvratas have been performed by you earlier? Tell me.

## \|\| 4.26.18 \|\|

*gaṇāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*tadbrāhmaṇavacaḥ śrutvā prahasya sa nṛpottamaḥ \|*  
*viṣṇudāsaṃ tadā garvāduvāca vacanaṃ dvijam \|\| 18 \|\|*

The Attendants said:

18\. On hearing the words of that Brāhmaṇa the excellent king laughed and haughtily spoke these words to Viṣṇudāsa, the Brāhmaṇa:

## \|\| 4.26.19 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*itthaṃ cedvadase vipra viṣṇubhaktyā'tigarvitaḥ \|*  
*bhaktiste kiyatī viṣṇordaridrasyā'dhanasya ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

The king said:

19\. If you say thus, O Brāhmaṇa, because you are too proud on account of your devotion to Viṣṇu, how much can your devotion be? You are an indigent fellow without wealth.

## \|\| 4.26.20 \|\|

*yajñadānādikaṃ naiva viṣṇostuṣṭikaraṃ kṛtam \|*  
*nā'pi devālayaṃ pūrvaṃ kṛtaṃ vipra tvayā kvacit \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Yajñas, charitable gifts etc. which give satisfaction to Viṣṇu have not been performed by you. Nor has any temple been built by you anywhere, O Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 4.26.21 \|\|

*īdṛśasyā'pi te garva eṣa tiṣṭhati bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*tacchṛṇvaṃtu vaco me'dya sarve'pyete dvijātayaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. In spite of being like this you are proud on account of your devotion. Therefore, let all the Brāhmaṇas listen to my words now.

## \|\| 4.26.22 \|\|

*sākṣātkāramahaṃ viṣṇoreṣa vādo gamiṣyati \|*  
*paśyaṃtu sarve'pi tato bhaktiṃ jñāsyaṃti cāvayoḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Who will directly perceive Viṣṇu first, this fellow or I? May all of you see. Thereupon you will come to know about our devotion.

## \|\| 4.26.23 \|\|

*gaṇāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*ityuktvā sa nṛpo'gacchannijarājagṛhaṃ tadā \|*  
*ārabhadvaiṣṇavaṃ satraṃ kṛtvā'cāryaṃ tu mudgalam \|\| 23 \|\|*

The Attendants said:

23\. After saying ṃus the king went back to his palace. He began a Vaiṣṇava Satra (sacrifice) after inviting Mudgala to be his preceptor.

## \|\| 4.26.24 \|\|

*ṛṣisaṃghasamājuṣṭaṃ bahvannaṃ bahudakṣiṇam \|*  
*yacca brahmakṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ gayākṣetre samṛddhimat \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. It was the same Satra as was formerly performed elaborately by Brahmā at Gayākṣetra. It was graced with their presence by groups of sages. Much food was distributed and many monetary gifts were given.

## \|\| 4.26.25 \|\|

*viṣṇudāso'pi tatraiva tasthau devālaye vratī \|*  
*yathoktaniyamānkurvanviṣṇostuṣṭikarānsadā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Viṣṇudāsa continued to stay in the temple performing the Vratas. He performed all the austerities as laid down—those which cause satisfaction to Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 4.26.26 \|\|

*iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe kārtikamāsamāhātmye colarājaviṣṇudāsabrāhmaṇavivādakathanaṃnāma ṣaḍviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He observed the Māgha Vrata and Kārttika Vrata. He planted Tulasī groves and nourished them. On Ekādaśī (eleventh) days he performed the Japa of Hari repeating the twelve-syllabled Mantra.

## \|\| 4.26.27 \|\|

*upacāraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhirnṛtyagītādimaṃgalaiḥ \|*  
*nityaṃ viṣṇostathā pūjāṃ vratānyetāni so'karot \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. All the sixteen services \[see notes below\] were performed by him. There were auspicious songs and dances. He performed the worship of Viṣṇu regularly. He observed these Vratas.

## \|\| 4.26.28 \|\|

*nityaṃ saṃsmaraṇaṃ viṣṇorgacchanbhuvi svapannapi \|*  
*sarvabhūtasthitaṃ viṣṇumapaśyatsamadarśanaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Even as he walked about he remembered Viṣṇu. He used to sleep on the ground. He viewed all impartially. He saw Viṣṇu dwelling in all living beings.

## \|\| 4.26.29 \|\|

*māghakārtikayornityaṃ viśeṣaniyamānapi \|*  
*akarodviṣṇutuṣṭyarthaṃ sodyāpanavidhiṃ tathā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. During the months of Māgha and Kārttika he performed all special austerities for the propitiation of Viṣṇu and also the respective concluding rites.

## Chapter 27 - King Cola and Viṣṇudāsa Liberated

## \|\| 4.27.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*kadācidviṣṇudāso'tha kṛtvā nityavidhiṃ dvija \|*  
*sa pākamakarottāvadaharatko'pyalakṣitaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:

1\. Once, O Brāhmaṇa, Viṣṇudāsa performed all his daily rites and then cooked his food. But someone stealthily took it away.

## \|\| 4.27.2 \|\|

*tamadṛṣṭvā'pyasau pākaṃ punarnaivā'karottadā \|*  
*sāyaṃkālā'rcanasyā'sau vratabhaṃgabhayāddvijaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Although he could not see cooked food, he did not prepare it once again, because he was afraid that it would create obstacles to his evening worship and thereby his Vrata would be broken.

## \|\| 4.27.3 \|\|

*dvitīye'hni punaḥ pākaṃ kṛtvā yāvatsa viṣṇave \|*  
*upahārārpaṇaṃ kartuṃ gataḥ ko'pyaharatpunaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On the second day also he cooked his food. By the time he went (to the temple) to dedicate the offerings, someone stole it once again.

## \|\| 4.27.4 \|\|

*evaṃ saptadinaṃ tasya pākaṃ ko'pyaharannṛpa \|*  
*tataḥ savismayaścātha manasyevamadhārayat \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. In this way for seven days someone stole away his cooked food. He was struck with wonder and thought thus:

## \|\| 4.27.5 \|\|

*aho nityaṃ samabhyetya kaḥ pākaṃ harate mama \|*  
*kṣetrasaṃnyāsinaḥ sthānaṃ na tyājyaṃ mama sarvathā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. ‘Oh! Who comes here everyday and takes away my food? This abode should not at all be abandoned by me who am a Sannyāsin (recluse). It is a holy spot.

## \|\| 4.27.6 \|\|

*punaḥ pākaṃ vidhāyā'tra bhujyate yadi cenmayā \|*  
*sāyaṃkālā'rcanaṃ caiva parityājyaṃ kathaṃ bhavet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. If the food is to be cooked once again and eaten by me, the worship in the evening will have to be abandoned. How can it be?

## \|\| 4.27.7 \|\|

*yadi pākaṃ vidhāyaivaṃ bhoktavyaṃ tu mayā na tat \|*  
*anivedya harau sarvaṃ vaiṣṇavairnaiva bhujyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Even if I cook again it cannot be eaten because, without offering to Han nothing is to be eaten by Vaiṣṇavas.

## \|\| 4.27.8 \|\|

*upoṣito'haṃ saptā'haṃ tiṣṭhāmyatra vratasthitaḥ \|*  
*adyasaṃrakṣaṇaṃ samyakpākasyā'tra karomyaham \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. I have observed fast for seven days. I shall remain here and maintan the Vrata. To-day let me protect the cooked food carefully.’

## \|\| 4.27.9 \|\|

*iti pākaṃ vidhāyā'sau tatraivā'lakṣitaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*tāvaddadarśa caṃḍālaṃ pākānnaharaṇe sthitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Thinking thus, he remained there itself hidden after cooking the food. Presently he saw a Cāṇḍāla stealing the cooked food.

## \|\| 4.27.10 \|\|

*kṣutkṣāmaṃ dīnavadanamasthicarmā'vaśeṣitam \|*  
*tamālokya dvijāgryo'bhūtkṛpayā'nvitamānasaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He was emaciated due to hunger. His face was pale and gloomy. Only bones and skin remained (on his body). On seeing him the eminent Brāhmaṇa was moved with pity.

## \|\| 4.27.11 \|\|

*vilokyā'nnaharaṃ viprastiṣṭhatiṣṭhetyabhāṣata \|*  
*kathamaśnāsi tadrūkṣaṃ ghṛtametadgṛhāṇa bhoḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. On seeiag the thief of the cooked food the Brāhmaṇa said:

“Stop, stop. How can you eat that dry food without ghee? Take this ghee too.”

## \|\| 4.27.12 \|\|

*itthaṃ vadaṃtaṃ viprāgryamāyāṃtaṃ sa vilokya ca \|*  
*vegādadhāvattadbhītyā mṛrcchitaśca papāta ha \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Saying this the Brāhmaṇa hastened towards him. On seeing the Brāhmaṇa coming, (the thief) ran quickly due to fear. He fell down unconscious.

## \|\| 4.27.13 \|\|

*bhītaṃ saṃmūrcchitaṃ dṛṣṭvā caṃḍālaṃ sa dvijāgraṇīḥ \|*  
*vegādabhyetya kṛpayā svavastrāṃtairavījayat \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On seeing the frightened and unconscious Cāṇḍāla that eminent Brāhmaṇa rushed towards him compassionately and fanned him with the end of his cloth.

## \|\| 4.27.14 \|\|

*athotthitaṃ tamevāsau viṣṇudāso vyalokayat \|*  
*sākṣānnārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ śaṃkhacakragadādharam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. As he rose up Viṣṇudāsa saw that it was Lord Nārāyaṇa himself holding the conch, the discus and the iron club.

## \|\| 4.27.15 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā sāttvikairbhāvairāvṛto dvijasattamaḥ \|*  
*stotuṃ caiva namaskartuṃ tadā nā'laṃ babhūva saḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. On seeing him, the excellent Brāhmaṇa had all the Sāttvika Bhāvas (the emotions and feelings along with horripilation, perspiration etc.). He became incapable of eulogizing or bowing down.

## \|\| 4.27.16 \|\|

*atha śakrādayo devāstatraivābhyāyayustadā \|*  
*gaṃdharvāpsarasaścā'pi jaguśca nanṛturmudā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then the Devas including Śakra came there. Gandharvas and celestial damsels sang and danced joyously.

## \|\| 4.27.17 \|\|

*vimānaśatasaṃkīrṇaṃ devarṣiśatasaṃkulam \|*  
*gītavāditranirghoṣaṃ sthānaṃ tadabhavattadā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The whole place became crowded with hundreds of aerial chariots and celestial sages. The place was full of the sound of songs and instrumental music.

## \|\| 4.27.18 \|\|

*tato viṣṇuḥ samāliṃgya svabhaktaṃ sāttvikavratam \|*  
*sārūpyamātmano dattvā'nayadvaikuṇṭhamaṃdiram \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Viṣṇu embraced his devotee of excellent holy rites. Granting him Sārūpya (identity of form), he took him to his abode in Vaikuṇṭha.

## \|\| 4.27.19 \|\|

*vimānavarasaṃsthaṃ taṃ gacchaṃtaṃ viṣṇusannidhim \|*  
*dīkṣitaścolanṛpatirviṣṇudāsaṃ dadarśa saḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. King Cola who was under initiation (for sacrifice) saw Viṣṇudāsa seated in an excellent aerial chariot and going to the presence of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 4.27.20 \|\|

*vaikuṇṭhabhuvanaṃ yāṃtaṃ viṣṇudāsaṃ vilokya saḥ \|*  
*svaguruṃ mudgalaṃ vegādāhūyetthaṃ vaco'bravīt \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On Seeing Viṣṇudāsa going to the world of Vaikuṇṭha, he hurriedly called his preceptor Mudgala and spoke these words:

## \|\| 4.27.21 \|\|

*cola uvāca \|*  
*yatsparddhayā mayā caiva yajñadānādikaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*sa viṣṇurūpadhṛgvipro yāti vaikuṇṭhamaṃdiram \|\| 21 \|\|*

Cola said:

21\. Yajñas and Dānas were performed by me in order to compete with Viṣṇudāsa. That Brāhmaṇa has now assumed the form of Viṣṇu. He is going to the abode of Vaikuṇṭha.

## \|\| 4.27.22 \|\|

*dīkṣitena mayā samyaksatre'sminvaiṣṇave tvayā \|*  
*hutamagnau kṛtā viprā dānādyaiḥ pūrṇamānasāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. In this Satra I have been initiated by you perfectly. In this Vaiṣṇava sacrifice Homa was performed in the sacred fire. With charitable gifts etc. Brāhmaṇas have been fully satisfied mentally.

## \|\| 4.27.23 \|\|

*naivā'dyāpi sa me devaḥ prasanno jāyate dhruvam \|*  
*viṣṇudāsasya bhaktyaiva sākṣātkāraṃ dadau hariḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. But that Lord is not pleased with me till now. It is certain. It was due to the devotion of Viṣṇudāsa that Hari granted him direct vision.

## \|\| 4.27.24 \|\|

*tasmāddānaiśca yajñaiśca naiva viṣṇuḥ prasīdati \|*  
*bhaktireva paraṃ tasya nidānaṃ darśane vibhoḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Hence, Viṣṇu is never pleased with charitable gifts and Yajñas. Devotion alone is the greatest cause of the perception of the Lord.

## \|\| 4.27.25-26 \|\|

*gaṇāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*ityuktvā bhāgineyaṃ svamabhyaṣiṃcannṛpāsane \|*  
*ābālyāddīkṣito yajñe hyaputratvamagādyataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tasmādadyā'pi taddeśe sadā rājyāṃ'śabhāginaḥ \|*  
*svasreyā eva jāyaṃte tatkṛtāvadhivartinaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

The Attendants said:

25-26. After saying this he crowned his nephew as the king and made him sit on the throne. Ever since his childhood he was engaged in Yajñas and so he had no son.

Hence even today in that land (Tamil Nadu or rather Kerala?) the sons of sisters are the successors to the throne. They share the kingdom. They remain within the bounds and limitations imposed by him (i.e. the reigning king).

## \|\| 4.27.27 \|\|

*iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe kārtikamāsamāhātmye colaviṣṇudāsamuktikathanaṃnāma saptaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Then he went to the sacrificial chamber and stood in front of the sacrificial pit. Addressing Viṣṇu, he called thrice in a loud voice:

## \|\| 4.27.28 \|\|

*viṣṇo bhaktiṃ sthirāṃ dehi manovākkāya karmabhiḥ \|*  
*ityuktvā so'patadvahnau sarveṣāmeva paśyatām \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. “O Viṣṇu, grant me steady devotion permeating my mind, speech and action.” After saying this he threw himself into the fire even as everyone was watching.

## \|\| 4.27.29 \|\|

*mudgalastu tadā krodhācchikhāmutpāṭayatsvakām \|*  
*tatastvadyāpi tadgotre mudgalā viśikhā babhuḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Out of anger Mudgala plucked out his tuft of hair. Ever since then the Mudgalas belonging to his Gotra have remained tuftless.

## \|\| 4.27.30 \|\|

*tāvadāvirabhūdviṣṇuḥ kuṇḍāgnau bhaktavatsalaḥ \|*  
*tamāliṃgya vimānāgryaṃ samārohayadacyutaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. In the meantime Viṣṇu, fond of his devotees, appeared in the fire in the pit. Acyuta embraced him and got him into an excellent aerial chariot.

## \|\| 4.27.31 \|\|

*tamāliṃgyā'tmasārūpyaṃ dattvā vaikuṇṭhamaṃdiram \|*  
*tenaiva saha deveśo jagāma tridaśairvṛtaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. After embracing him and granting him his own form (Sārūpya), the Lord of Devas went to his abode in Vaikuṇṭha along with him surrounded by Devas.

## Chapter 28 - Dharmadatta Attains Salvation

## \|\| 4.28.1 \|\|

*dharmadatta uvāca \|*  
*jayaśca vijayaścaiva viṣṇordvāsthau śrutau mayā \|*  
*kiṃ nu tābhyāṃ purā cīrṇaṃ tasmāttadrūpadhāriṇau \|\| 1 \|\|*

Dharmadatta said:

1\. I have heard that Jaya and Vijaya are the gatekeepers of Viṣṇu. What holy rites have been performed by them, whereby they have assumed his (Lord’s) form?

## \|\| 4.28.2 \|\|

*gaṇāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*tṛṇabiṃdostu kanyāyāṃ devahūtyāṃ purā dvija \|*  
*kardamasya tu dṛṣṭyaiva putrau dvau saṃbabhūvatuḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

The Attendants said:

2\. Two sons were born of Devahūtī, the daughter of Tṛṇabindu, O Brāhmaṇa, through Kardama’s vision alone.

## \|\| 4.28.3 \|\|

*jyeṣṭho jayaḥ kaniṣṭho'bhūdvijayaścaiva nāmataḥ \|*  
*tasyāmevā'bhavatpaścātkapilo yogadharmavit \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The elder was Jaya and the younger Vijaya by name. Afterwards, Kapila, the knower of Yogic rites, was also born to her.

## \|\| 4.28.4 \|\|

*jayaśca vijayaścaiva viṣṇubhaktiratau sadā \|*  
*tau tanniṣṭhendriyagrāmau dharmaśīlau babhūvatuḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Jaya and Vijaya were always engaged in devotion to Viṣṇu. They were virtuous in conduct and all their sense-organs were concentrated in him (Viṣṇu).

## \|\| 4.28.5 \|\|

*nityamaṣṭākṣarījāpyau viṣṇuvratakarāvubhau \|*  
*sākṣātkāraṃ dadau viṣṇustayornityārcane sadā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. They used to perform the Japa of the eight-syllabled Mantra regularly. Both of them observed the vow of Viṣṇu. During their daily worship, Viṣṇu always granted them his vision.

## \|\| 4.28.6 \|\|

*maruttena kadācittāvāhūtau yajñakarmaṇi \|*  
*jagmaturyajñakuśalau devarṣigaṇapūjitau \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Once they were invited by (King) Marutta to his Yajña. Those two who were experts in the performance of Yajñas, went there. They were honoured by the celestial sages.

## \|\| 4.28.7 \|\|

*jayastatrābhavadbrahmāyājako vijayo'bhavat \|*  
*tato yajñavidhiṃ kṛtsnaṃ paripūrṇaṃ ca cakratuḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Jaya was the Brahmā (Presiding Priest) there and Vijaya was the Yājaka (one who actually performs the rites). Then they completely performed the Yajña.

## \|\| 4.28.8 \|\|

*marutto'vabhṛthasnātastābhyāṃ vittaṃ dadau bahu \|*  
*tatsamādāya tau vittaṃ jagmatuḥ svāśramaṃ prati \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. After taking his A vabhṛtha bath (valedictory bath after a sacrifice) Marutta gave them plenty of wealth. Taking that wealth, they went to their hermitage.

## \|\| 4.28.9 \|\|

*yajanāya pṛthagviṣṇostuṣṭyarthaṃ tau tato munī \|*  
*taddhanaṃ vibhajaṃtau tu paspardhāte parasparam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. They wanted to worship Viṣṇu separately. For the purpose of propitiating Viṣṇu, they wanted to perform sacrifice individually. While sharing that money those sages quarrelled with each other.

## \|\| 4.28.10 \|\|

*jayo'bravītsamo bhāgaḥ kriyatāmiti tatra saḥ \|*  
*vijayaścābravīnnaitadyallabdhaṃ yena tasya tat \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Jaya said: “Let the amount be shared equally”. Vijaya said: “It shall not be so. The sum belongs to him who obtained it.”

## \|\| 4.28.11 \|\|

*tato'śapajjayaḥ krodhādvijayaṃ lubdhamānasam \|*  
*gṛhītvā na dadāsyetattasmādgrāho bhaveti tam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thereupon Jaya cursed Vijaya who was covetous-minded: “You have taken the money but do not give. Hence be a crocodile.”

## \|\| 4.28.12 \|\|

*vijayastasya taṃ śāpaṃ śrutvā sopyaśapacca tam \|*  
*madabhrāṃto'śapastvaṃ māṃ tasmānmātaṃgatāṃ vraja \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On hearing his curse Vijaya too cursed him: “You have gone astray due to arrogance and cursed me. Hence be an elephant.”

## \|\| 4.28.13 \|\|

*tattadācakhyaturviṣṇuṃ dṛṣṭvā nityārcane vibhum \|*  
*śāpayośca nivṛttiṃ tau yayācāte ramāpatim \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On seeing Lord Viṣṇu at the time of their daily worship, they told him what had happened. They requested the Lord of Ramā for the termination of the curses.

## \|\| 4.28.14 \|\|

*jayavijayāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*bhaktāvāvāṃ kathaṃ deva grāhamātaṃgayonigau \|*  
*bhaviṣyāvaḥ kṛpāsiṃdho tacchāpo vinivartyatām \|\| 14 \|\|*

Jaya and Vijaya said:

14\. O Lord, we are your devotees. How can we become a crocodile and an elephant, O ocean of mercy? Let that curse be terminated.

## \|\| 4.28.15 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*madbhaktayorvaco'satyaṃ na kadācidbhaviṣyati \|*  
*mayā'pi nānyathā kartuṃ śakyate tatkadācana \|\| 15 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

15\. The words of my devotees should never be false. I too can never alter them.

## \|\| 4.28.16 \|\|

*prahlādavacasā staṃbhe'pyāvirbhūto hyahaṃ purā \|*  
*tathāṃ'barīṣavākyena jāto garbhe svayaṃ kila \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Formerly I manifested myself through a pillar too due to the words of Prahlāda. Similarly at the instance of Aṃbarīṣa I myself was born of a womb (i.e. had to take birth).

## \|\| 4.28.17 \|\|

*tasmādyuvāmimau śāpāvanu'bhūya svayaṃkṛtau \|*  
*labhethāṃ matpadaṃ nityamityuktvāṃ'tardadhe hariḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Hence suffer the consequences of these curses uttered by yourselves. Then regain my region.

After saying this Hari vanished.

## \|\| 4.28.18 \|\|

*gaṇāvūcatuḥ \|*  
*tatastau grāhamātaṃgāvabhūtāṃ gaṃḍakītaṭe \|*  
*jātismarau tu tadyonyāmapi viṣṇuvrate sthitau \|\| 18 \|\|*

The Attendants said:

18\. Then they were born as a crocodile and an elephant on the banks of Gaṇḍakī. Even then they could remember what happened in their previous birth. They remained steady in observing the vow of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 4.28.19 \|\|

*kadācitsa gajaḥ snātuṃ kārtike gaṃḍakīṃ gataḥ \|*  
*tāvajjagrāha taṃ grāhaḥ saṃsmarañcchāpakāraṇam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Once in the month of Kārttika that elephant went to Gaṇḍakī for bathing. Suddenly that crocodile remembering the cause of the curse caught hold of him.

## \|\| 4.28.20 \|\|

*grāhagrasto hyasau nāgaḥ sasmāra śrīpatiṃ tadā \|*  
*tāvadāvirabhūdviṣṇuścakraśaṃkhagadādharaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The elephant held by the crocodile remembered Śrīpati. Then Viṣṇu appeared before them with the discus, conch and iron club in his hands.

## \|\| 4.28.21 \|\|

*tatastau grāhamātaṃgau cakraṃ kṣiptvā samuddhṛtau \|*  
*dattvaiva nijasārūpyaṃ vaikuṇṭhamanayadvibhuḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Hurling his discus he redeemed the crocodile and the elephant. The Lord granted them his own form (Sārūpya) and took them to Vaikuṇṭha.

## \|\| 4.28.22 \|\|

*tataḥprabhṛti tatsthānaṃ harikṣetramitismṛtam \|*  
*cakrasaṃgharṣaṇādyasmingrāvāṇo'pi hi lāṃchitāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Ever since then that spot is known as Harikṣetra. Due to having been rubbed by the discus the pebbles too had been marked with circular lines.

## \|\| 4.28.23 \|\|

*tāvubhau viśrutau loke jayaśca vijayastathā \|*  
*nityaṃ viṣṇupriyau dvāḥsthau pṛṣṭau yau hi tvayā dvija \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Those two are well-known in the world as Jaya and Vijaya. Those perpetual favourites of Viṣṇu became his gatekeepers, about whom you asked, O Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 4.28.24 \|\|

*atastvamapi dharmajña nityaṃ viṣṇuvrate sthitaḥ \|*  
*tyaktamātsaryadaṃbho'pi bhavasva samadarśanaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Hence, O Brāhmaṇa conversant with Dharma, be stable in holy rites forever. Avoid malicious rivalry and hypocrisy. Be impartial in viewing others.

## \|\| 4.28.25 \|\|

*tulāmakarameṣeṣu prātaḥsnāyī sadā bhava \|*  
*ekādaśīvrate tiṣṭha tulasīvanapālakaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. During the months of Tūlā, Makara and Meṣa take early morning bath regularly. Perform the holy rite of Ekādaśī. Keep a grove of Tulasī plants.

## \|\| 4.28.26 \|\|

*brāhmaṇānatha gāścā'pi vaiṣṇavāṃśca sadā bhaja \|*  
*masūrikāmāranālaṃ vṛṃtākānyapi khāda mā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Always adore Brāhmaṇas, cows and Vaiṣṇavas. Do not consume Masūra pulse, Āranāla (gruel from fermented boiled rice) and brinjals.

## \|\| 4.28.27 \|\|

*evaṃ tvamapi dehāṃte tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam \|*  
*prāpnoṣi dharmadatta tvaṃ tadbhaktyaiva yathā vayam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Due to your devotion to him, O Dharmadatta, you will attain the greatest region of Viṣṇu like us after death.

## \|\| 4.28.28 \|\|

*iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe kārtikamāsamāhātmye dharmadattamokṣaprāptikathanaṃnāmā'ṣṭāviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Your stay in the world will be only till then. Neither Yajñas nor charitable gifts nor Tīrthas are superior to the Vrata that causes satisfaction to Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 4.28.29 \|\|

*dhanyo'si viprāgrya yatastvayaitadvrataṃ kṛtaṃ tuṣṭikaraṃ jagadguroḥ \|*  
*yadardhabhāgā'ptaphalā murāreḥ praṇīyate'smābhiriyaṃ salokatām \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O eminent Brāhmaṇa, you are blessed because this Vrata which causes satisfaction and delight to the sire of the universe, has been performed by you. This woman has attained half of the benefit thereof and hence is being taken to the world of Murāri by us.

## \|\| 4.28.30 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*itthaṃ tau dharmadattaṃ tamupadiśya vimānagau \|*  
*tayā kalahayā sārddhaṃ vaikuṇṭhabhavanaṃ gatau \|\| 30 \|\|*

Nārada said:

30\. Advising Dharmadatta thus those two went to the abode of Vaikuṇṭha by means of the aerial chariot along with Kalahā.

## \|\| 4.28.31 \|\|

*dharmadatto hyasau jātapratyayastadvrate sthitaḥ \|*  
*dehāṃ'te tadvibhoḥ sthānaṃ bhāryābhyāṃ saṃyuto'bhyayāt \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Dharmadatta became convinced (of the efficacy of the Vrata) and observed it regularly. After death he went to the region of the Lord accompanied by his two wives.

## Chapter 29 - The Story of Dhaneśvara

## \|\| 4.29.1 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*iti tadvacanaṃ śrutvā pṛthurvismitamānasaḥ \|*  
*saṃpūjya nāradaṃ samyagvisasarja tadā priye \|\| 1 \|\|*

Śrīkṛṣṇa said:

1\. On hearing Nārada’s words thus, Pṛthu became surprised in his mind. Then, O beloved, he worshipped him duly and bade farewell to him.

## \|\| 4.29.2 \|\|

*purā'vaṃtīpure kaścidvipra āsīddhaneśvaraḥ \|*  
*brahmakarmaparibhraṣṭaḥ pāpakarmā sudurmatiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Formerly there was a certain Brāhmaṇa named Dhaneśvara in the city of Avantī. He had deviated from all Brahminical rites. He was wicked-minded and sinful in activities.

## \|\| 4.29.3 \|\|

*deśāddeśātaraṃ gacchankrayavikrayakāraṇāt \|*  
*māhiṣmatīpurīmāgātkadācitsa dhaneśvaraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. For the purpose of buying and selling things he used to go from one country to another.

Thus once that Dhaneśvara went to the city of Māhiṣmatī.

## \|\| 4.29.4 \|\|

*mahiṣeṇa kṛtā pūrvaṃ tasmānmāhiṣmatīti sā \|*  
*yasyā vapragatā bhāti narmadā pāpanāśinī \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Formerly, this city had been built by Mahiṣa. Hence it is well-known as Māhiṣmatī. The river Narmadā, the destroyer of sins, forms a defensive ditch to this city.

## \|\| 4.29.5 \|\|

*kārtikavratinastatra nānādeśā'gatānnarān \|*  
*sa dṛṣṭvā vikrayaṃ kurvanmāsamekamuvāsa saḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Men who observed Kārttika Vrata had come there from different lands. He attended to them selling things (that they required). Thus he stayed there for a month.

## \|\| 4.29.6 \|\|

*sa nityaṃ narmadātīre bhramanvikrayakāraṇāt \|*  
*dadarśa brāhmaṇānsnānajapadevārcane sthitān \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. For the purpose of selling things he used to move frequently on the banks of Narmadā everyday. On those occasions he saw Brāhmaṇas engaged in holy baths, Japas or worships of the Lord.

## \|\| 4.29.7 \|\|

*kāṃścitpurāṇaṃ paṭhataḥ kāṃścicca śravaṇe ratān \|*  
*nṛtyagāyanavāditraviṣṇuśravaṇatatparān \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He saw some of them reading the Purāṇas, some engaged in listening to them, some eagerly interested in watching (religious) dances or hearing (devotional) songs and instrumental music or stories of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 4.29.8 \|\|

*udyāpanavidhau saktānkāṃścijjāgaraṇe ratān \|*  
*vipragopūjanaratāndīpadānaratāṃstathā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Some were engaged in the concluding rites of the Vratas; some were enthusiastic about keeping awake; engaged in the worship of the Brāhmaṇas and cows, some were ardently offering lamps.

## \|\| 4.29.9 \|\|

*dadarśa kautukāviṣṭastatratatra dhaneśvaraḥ \|*  
*nityaṃ paribhramaṃstatra darśanasparśabhāṣaṇāt \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Dhaneśvara saw these in different places very enthusiastically. As he moved in the region regularly he was fortunate enough to contact Vaiṣṇavas, seeing them, talking to them, touching them etc.

## \|\| 4.29.10-13 \|\|

*vaiṣṇavānāṃ tathā viṣṇornāmaśrāvādi so'labhat \|*  
*evaṃ māsaṃ sthitastasyā narmadāyāstaṭe dvijaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tāvatkṛṣṇā'hinā daṣṭo vihvalaḥ sa papāta ha \|*  
*atha dehaparityaktaṃ taṃ vaddhvā yamakiṃkarāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*yamājñayā kuṃbhipāke cikṣipustaṃ dhaneśvaram \|*  
*yāvatkṣiptaśca tatrāsau tāvacchītalatāṃ yayau \|\| 12 \|\|*

*kuṃbhīpāko yathā vahniḥ prahlādakṣepaṇātpurā \|*  
*yamastu kautukaṃ dṛṣṭvā papracchānīya taṃ tataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

10-13. He listened to the names of Viṣṇu frequently uttered by them. Thus that Brāhmaṇa stayed on the banks of Narmada for a month. (One day) he was bitten by a black serpent. Afflicted much he fell down (dead). After death the servants of Yama bound him and at the bidding of Yama threw that Brāhmaṇa Dhaneśvara into the hell Kumbhīpāka. But as soon as he was thrown into that place Kumbhīpāka became very cool like the fire into which Prahlāda was thrown formerly. On seeing this wonder Yama brought him out and questioned him.

## \|\| 4.29.14-16 \|\|

*tāvadabhyāgatastatra nāradaḥ prāha satvaram \|*  
*nārada uvāca \|*  
*naivā'yaṃ nirayānbhoktumarho hyaruṇanaṃdana \|\| 14 \|\|*

*yasmādaṃte'sya saṃjātaṃ karma yannirayāpaham \|*  
*yaḥ puṇyakarmiṇāṃ kuryāddarśanasparśabhāṣaṇam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tataḥ ṣaḍaṃśamāpnoti puṇyasya niyataṃ naraḥ \|*  
*sakhyaṃ tu taistu saṃsargaṃ kṛtavānvai dhaneśvaraḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

14a. Presently Nārada who came there told him:

Nārada said:

14b-16. O son of the Sun-god, this (Brāhmaṇa) does not deserve to suffer in hells, since at the end of his life there occurred certain acts (done by him) that dispel hells.

If a person were to meet, touch or speak to persons of meritorious deeds, he gets one-sixth of their merits invariably. This Dhaneśvara not only contacted them but became their friend too.

## \|\| 4.29.17 \|\|

*kārtikavratibhirmāsaṃ teṣāṃ puṇyāṃśabhāgayam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He had contacted the Kārttikavrata-observers for a month. Hence he must get a share of their merit.

## \|\| 4.29.18 \|\|

*tasmādakāmapuṇyo hi yakṣayonisthito hyayam \|*  
*vilokya nirayānsarvānpāpabhogapradarśakān \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Since he has acquired merits unintentionally, let him be born in Yakṣa womb (species) after surveying all the hells that show how sinners fare there.

## \|\| 4.29.19 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā gatavati nārade sa sauristadvākyaśravaṇavibuddhatatsukarmā \|*  
*taṃ vipraṃ punaranayatsvakiṃkareṇa tānsarvānnirayagaṇānpradarśayiṣyan \|\| 19 \|\|*

Śrīkṛṣṇa said:

19\. When Nārada went away after saying this, Yama who came to know his meritorious deeds on hearing his words, desired to show him all the hells and asked a servant to take him round.

## \|\| 4.29.20 \|\|

*tato dhaneśvaraṃ nītvā nirayānpretapo'bravīt \|*  
*darśayiṣyaṃstu tānsarvānyamānujñākarastadā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then the servant of Yama took Dhaneśvara to those hells, desirous of showing him all. Then Pretapa (Head of the departed spirits) said:

## \|\| 4.29.21 \|\|

*pretapa uvāca \|*  
*paśyemānnirayānghorāndhaneśvara mahābhayān \|*  
*eṣu pāpakarā nityaṃ pacyaṃte yamakiṃkaraiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

Pretapa said:

21\. O Dhaneśvara, see these terrible hells that instil fear (in everyone). In these the sinners are cooked and tortured continuously by the servants of Yama.

## \|\| 4.29.22 \|\|

*akāmātpātakaṃ śuṣkaṃ kāmādārdramudāhṛtam \|*  
*ārdraśuṣkādibhiḥ pāpairdviprakārānavasthitān \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. A sin that is committed without any intention is called Śuṣka (dry) and what which is committed with intention is known as Ārdra (wet). On the basis of Ārdra and Śuṣka sins, the hells are divided into two groups.

## \|\| 4.29.23-24 \|\|

*caturāśītisaṃkhyākaiḥ pṛthagbhedairavasthitān \|*  
*yatprakīrṇamapāṃkteyaṃ malinīkaraṇaṃ tathā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*jātibhraṃśakaraṃ tadvadupapātakasaṃjñakam \|*  
*atipāpaṃ mahāpāpaṃ saptadhā pātakaṃ smṛtam \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. They are eighty-four in number, with separate locations. It is declared that sins are of seven varieties: (1) Prakīrṇa, (2) Apāṅkteya, (3) Malinīkaraṇa, (4) Jātibhraṃśakara, (5) Upapātaka, (6) Atipāpa and (7) Mahāpāpa.

## \|\| 4.29.25-27 \|\|

*ebhiḥ saptasu pacyaṃte nirayeṣu yathākramam \|*  
*kārtikavratibhiryasmātsaṃsargo hyabhavattava \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tatpuṇyopacayādete nirhṛtā nirayāḥ khalu \|*  
*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*darśayitveti nirayānpretapastamathāharat \|\| 26 \|\|*

*dhaneśvaraṃ yakṣalokaṃ yakṣaścā'bhūtsa tatra hi \|*  
*dhanadasyā'nugaḥ so'yaṃ dhanayakṣeti viśrutaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

25-26a. These sinners are cooked in these seven hells in order. Since you came into contact with those who had observed Kārttika Vrata, you acquired (a share in) their merits. Due to that you have been spared suffering in these hells.

Śrīkṛṣṇa said:

26b-27. After showing the hells to him thus, Pretapa took Dhaneśvara

to the world of Yakṣas. There he became a Yakṣa and an attendant of Kubera. He became well-known as Dhana-Yakṣa.

## \|\| 4.29.28-29 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā vāsudevo'sau satyabhāmāmatipriyam \|*  
*sāyaṃsaṃdhyāvidhiṃ kartuṃ jagāma jananīgṛham \|\| 28 \|\|*

*iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe kārtikamāsamāhātmye dhaneśvarayakṣajanmaprāptivarṇanaṃnāmaikonatriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

Sūta said:

28-29. After saying this to his great beloved Satyabhāmā, Vāsudeva went to his mother’s house to perform the evening Sandhyā rites.

## Chapter 30 - Fasts and Austerities of the Month

## \|\| 4.30.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*adbhuto'yaṃ tvayā prokto mahimā kārtikasya tu \|*  
*svasya kartumasāmarthyaṃ kathametatkṛtaṃ bhavet \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:

1\. Wonderful indeed is the efficacy of the Kārttika Vrata described by you. If one has no capacity to perform it, what shall one do about it?

## \|\| 4.30.2-3 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*nāsti kartuṃ svasāmarthyamupāyātprāpyate phalam \|*  
*dravyaṃ dattvā brāhmaṇāya gṛhṇīyātphalamuttamam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*śiṣyādvā bhṛtyavargādvā strībhyo vā'ptācca kārayet \|*  
*tasmādapi phalaṃ gṛhṇanphalabhāgjāyate naraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

2-3. If one has no capacity, the benefit is attained by certain (other) means. He can give some money to a Brāhmaṇa and get the excellent benefit. He can secure the same (fruit) from a disciple, servants or women. Or he can make some relative (or trustworthy person) perform the Vrata on his behalf. From him also he can take the benefit. Thus that man can be its beneficiary.

## \|\| 4.30.4 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*adattānyapi puṇyāni prāpyaṃte kenacitkvacit \|*  
*etadicchāmyahaṃ śrotuṃ kautukaṃ mama vartate \|\| 4 \|\|*

Nārada said:

4\. Are merits obtained by anyone anywhere though not given? I wish to hear about this as I am very eager.

## \|\| 4.30.5 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*adattānyapi puṇyāni labhaṃte pātakānyapi \|*  
*yenopāyena tadvacmi śṛṇuṣvaikamanā dvija \|\| 5 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

5\. Though not given, merits as well as sins are obtained. To know by what means it happens, listen with concentration, O Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 4.30.6-8 \|\|

*sukṛtaṃ vā duṣkṛtaṃ vā kṛtamekena yatkṛte \|*  
*jāyate tasya tadrāṣṭre tretāyāṃ tu puro bhavet \|\| 6 \|\|*

*dvāpare vaṃśamadhye tu kalau kartaiva kevalam \|*  
*ājñānādyatkṛtaṃ karma bālye svapne tu tatphalam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*ajñānādyacca tāruṇye bālye tasya phalaṃ bhavet \|*  
*jñānapūrvaṃ kṛtaṃ karma ājanmāṃtaṃ ca tatphalam \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. Whether a good deed or an evil one, if one does it in Kṛta Yuga, the whole kingdom reaps the fruit thereof. If one does it in Tretā Yuga, the whole city gets it. If one does it in Dvāpara Yuga, the consequence extends to the whole family. And if one does it in Kali Yuga, only the doer is affected or benefited by it. If an action is performed unwittingly during childhood, the result thereof is experienced in dream; if it is committed unwittingly during youth, the result thereof is had as in childhood(?); if any action is performed knowingly, the result thereof lasts till the end of that life.

## \|\| 4.30.9-10 \|\|

*ṣaṇmāsaṃ pāpisaṃgena naraḥ pāpī prajāyate \|*  
*pāpināṃ vā dharmiṇāṃ vā saṃsargāddaśamāsikam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*bhojanādekapaṃktau ca viṃśāṃśaḥ puṇyapāpayoḥ \|*  
*ekāsane dvayorvāsātsahasrāṃśena lipyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. If a man is in close contact with a sinner for six months, he himelf becomes a sinner. If a man is in close contact with sinners or righteous men for ten months and if he takes food with them in the same row, the share of sin and merit is a twentieth part. If two men sit on the same seat, they get a thousandth of each other’s (sin or merit).

## \|\| 4.30.11-12 \|\|

*yo vai yasyānnamaśnāti sa bhuṃkte tasya kilbiṣam \|*  
*japādau pāpisaṃsargātṣoḍaśāṃ'śo vinaśyati \|\| 11 \|\|*

*parasya stavanādyānādekapātrasthabhojanāt \|*  
*ekaśayyāprāvaraṇātṣaṣṭhāṃśaḥ puṇyapāpayoḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. If a man eats another man’s cooked food, he gets a share in the latter’s sin. Should a person come into contact with a sinner while performing Japa etc., a sixteenth (part) of his merit perishes. By eulogizing another man, by going in his vehicle, by taking food along with him from the same pot, by lying with him on the same bed, or by covering oneself with his shawl, one incurs a sixth of his sins or merits.

## \|\| 4.30.13 \|\|

*puruṣo harate sarvaṃ bhāryāyā aurasasya ca \|*  
*arddhaṃ śiṣyāccaturthāṃśaṃ pāpaṃ puṇyaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The husband takes away everything (i.e. sin as well as merit) from his wife and the father from his bosom-born son takes away half of his sins and merits and a fourth from his disciple.

## \|\| 4.30.14 \|\|

*bharturājñākarī nārī bharturarddhaṃ vṛṣaṃ haret \|*  
*yaddhastapakvaṃ bhujīyāddaśāṃśaṃ tadaghaṃ haret \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. A woman obedient and faithful to her husband takes away half his merit. A man takes away a tenth of the sin of another man, if he takes the food cooked by him.

## \|\| 4.30.15 \|\|

*varṣā'śanaṃ tu yo datte tadarddhāghasya bhāgayam \|*  
*varṣāśanārddhaṃ puṇyaṃ tu bhuṃkte varṣāśanī naraḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. If a man gives food to another man for a whole year, that man gets half the sin of the former (defective text) and the man who partakes of the food for one year, gets half the merits by eating food for one year (?) (Rather the former i.e. partaker of food should get half the sin of the latter.)

## \|\| 4.30.16 \|\|

*purohitasya ṣaṣṭhāṃśaṃ pāpaṃ vā puṇyameva vā \|*  
*yajamāno bhunaktyeva taddaśāṃśaṃ purohitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The sponsor of a sacrifice gets a sixth of the sin or merit of his priest and the priest gets a tenth of the former’s sin or merit.

## \|\| 4.30.17 \|\|

*udyogī cānumantā ca yaścopakaraṇapradaḥ \|*  
*ṣaṣṭhāṃśaṃ puṇyapāpānāmupadraṣṭā daśāṃśakam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. (Whatever may be the deed) the person actively engaged in it, the person who permitted or sanctioned it and the person who supplied the instruments thereof acquire a sixth of the result whether sin or merit and the onlooker a tenth of it.

## \|\| 4.30.18 \|\|

*yaddhastātkāryate karma nānnamasmai prayacchati \|*  
*vinā bhṛtakaśiṣyābhyāṃ ṣaṣṭhāṃśaṃ puṇyamāharet \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. If a person engages another person in a job, that person being other than a person hired by him or his disciple, and does not give him food, the person engaged so will take away a sixth of the merit of the employer.

## \|\| 4.30.19 \|\|

*vyavahārāttathā prītyā nityaṃ saṃbhāṣaṇādibhiḥ \|*  
*daśāṃśaṃ puṇyapāpānāṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. By means of social dealings or by regular loving talks with another, one gets a tenth of the sins and merits of the other. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 4.30.20 \|\|

*saṃsargapuṇyayogena ekadanto dvijādhamaḥ \|*  
*narakānvividhāndṛṣṭvā svargaṃ prāpa tadaiva hi \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Due to the merit of close association a base Brāhmaṇa Ekadanta saw different types of hells and ultimately attained heaven.

## \|\| 4.30.21 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*īdṛśaṃ kārtikavratamalpāyāsaṃ mahatphalam \|*  
*na kurvaṃti janāḥ kecitkimarthaṃ vai pitāmaha \|\| 21 \|\|*

Nārada said:

21\. The Kārttika Vrata of this type involves only a little effort, but its benefit is enormous. Still some people do not perform it. Why is it so, O Pitāmaha?

## \|\| 4.30.22 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*svasṛṣṭivṛddhaye vedhā dharmā'dharmau sasarja ha \|*  
*dharmamevā'nutiṣṭhaṃtaḥ prāpnuvaṃti śubhāṃ gatim \|\| 22 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

22\. It is to make his own creation flourish that the creator created Dharma and Adharma. Those who practise Dharma (Virtue) alone attain excellent goal.

## \|\| 4.30.23 \|\|

*adharmamanutiṣṭhaṃto yāṃti te'dhogatiṃ narāḥ \|*  
*puṇyakarmaphalaṃ nāko narakastadviparyayaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Those men who resort to Adharma (evil) go deep down (to hell). Heaven is the fruit of meritorious deeds and the opposite thereof is hell.

## \|\| 4.30.24 \|\|

*tayoḥ pālanakartārau dvāveva vidhinā kṛtau \|*  
*śatakratuyamau tau ca puṇyapāpānusāriṇau \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Two persons were engaged by the creator to guard these two, viz. Indra and Yama. They attend to merits and sins (of the doers) respectively.

## \|\| 4.30.25 \|\|

*gurutalpādayaḥ putrāḥ kāmasya prathitā bhuvi \|*  
*krodhasya pitṛghātādyā lobhasya tanayāñchṛṇu \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The sins of defiling the bed of the preceptor etc. are reputed on the earth as the sons of Kāma (Lust). Patricide etc. are the sons of Krodha (Anger). Listen to the sons of Lobha (Greed).

## \|\| 4.30.26-29 \|\|

*brahmasvaharaṇādyāśca ete narakanāyakāḥ \|*  
*kṛtā yamena tairvyāptā manujā na hi kurvate \|\| 26 \|\|*

*vratādidharmakṛtyaṃ yaistairmuktāste hi kurvate \|\| 27 \|\|*

*śraddhā medhā vighātinyau vartete bhuvi sarvadā \|*  
*tābhyāṃ vyāptastu manujaḥ śrīviṣṇoḥ śravaṇādikam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*na karoti sudurmedhā yenāṃdhaṃ yāti vai tamaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇena satyabhāmāyai yaduktaṃ tadvadāmi te \|\| 29 \|\|*

26-29. They are Brahmasvaharaṇa (Misappropriation of a Brahmin’s wealth) etc. These are what lead to Narakas (Hells) at the instance of Yama. Men who are permeated by them do not perform Vratas and other holy rites. Those who are rid of them, do indeed perform.

Faith and intellect (of sinners) are always destructive on the earth. A man influenced by these two does not listen to (the stories) of Śrī Viṣṇu. He is a person of extremely wicked intellect. Thereby he falls into blinding darkness. I shall relate to you what was recounted to Satyabhāmā by Kṛṣṇa.

## \|\| 4.30.30 \|\|

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe kārtikamāsamāhātmye dattapuṇyapāpaphalaprāptivarṇanapūrvaka māsopavāsavratavidhikathanaṃnāma triṃśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. A man indirectly obtains a fourth of the merits and sins of another by teaching him, by performing Yajñas on his behalf or by taking food with him.

## \|\| 4.30.31 \|\|

*ekāsanādekayānānniśvāsasyāṃgasaṃgataḥ \|*
