*sarvasaṃśayasaṃchettā'nalaso gururādṛtaḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇaḥ sarvakālajñaḥ kuryātsarveṣvanugraham \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. He must be capable of dispelling all doubts. He must not be lazy. Such a preceptor is a respected Brāhmaṇa. He knows what happens at different times. He should bless all.

## \|\| 5.16.28 \|\|

*pūrvoktalakṣaṇairyuktaḥ śiṣya īdṛgvidhādguroḥ \|*  
*gṛhṇīyātputra tanmaṃtraṃ mārgaśīrṣe madāyane \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The disciple having the characteristics mentioned before should receive that Mantra, O son, from a preceptor of this type, in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa which is my resort.

## \|\| 5.16.29 \|\|

*vaiṣṇavānāṃ vratānāṃ ca kuryātsvīkaraṇaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*matpriyaṃ śṛṇuyācchaśvacchrīmadbhāgavataṃ param \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. A wise man should perform all the Vaiṣṇava Vratas. He should always listen to the great (holy scripture) Śrīmadbhāgavata that is my favourite.

## \|\| 5.16.30 \|\|

*śrīmadbhāgavataṃnāma purāṇaṃ lokaviśrutam \|*  
*śṛṇuyācchraddhayā yukto mama santoṣakāraṇam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The Purāṇa named Śrīmadbhāgavata is renowned throughout the world. The devotee should listen to it with faith. It causes my satisfaction and pleasure.

## \|\| 5.16.31 \|\|

*nityaṃ bhāgavataṃ yastu purāṇaṃ paṭhate naraḥ \|*  
*pratyakṣaraṃ bhavettasya kapilādānajaṃ phalam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. A man who reads the Bhāgavata Purāṇa continuously gets the merit of gifting a tawny-coloured cow for every syllable (so read).

## \|\| 5.16.32 \|\|

*ślokārdhaṃ ślokapādaṃ vā nityaṃ bhāgavatodbhavam \|*  
*paṭhate śṛṇuyādyastu gosahasraphalaṃ labhet \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. He who reads or listens to half or even one-fourth of a verse quoted from Bhāgavata everyday, shall obtain the merit of (the gift of) a thousand cows.

## \|\| 5.16.33 \|\|

*yaḥ paṭhetprayato nityaṃ ślokaṃ bhāgavataṃ suta \|*  
*aṣṭādaśapurāṇānāṃ phalamāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. O son, a man who reads with (mental and physical) purity a verse from Bhāgavata everyday, attains the merit of (reading) all the eighteen Purāṇas.

## \|\| 5.16.34 \|\|

*nityaṃ mama kathā yatra tatra tiṣṭhanti vaiṣṇavāḥ \|*  
*kalibāhyā narāste vai ye'rcayanti sadā mama \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Vaiṣṇavas stay there where my story is continuously (told). Those men are unaffected by Kali, who always honour my (favourite Purāṇa).

## \|\| 5.16.35 \|\|

*vaiṣṇavānāṃ tu śāstrāṇi ye'rcayanti gṛhe narāḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktā bhavaṃti suravanditāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Those men who honour in their abode the scriptures of Vaiṣṇavas become rid of all their sins and they are saluted by Suras.

## \|\| 5.16.36 \|\|

*ye'rcayanti gṛhe nityaṃ śāstraṃ bhāgavataṃ kalau \|*  
*āsphoṭayaṃti valganti teṣāṃ prīto bhavāmyaham \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. If people always honour the scripture Bhāgavata in their houses in the Kali Age, if they clap their hands (in praise thereof) and if they shout in joy, I become delighted with them.

## \|\| 5.16.37 \|\|

*yāvaddināni he putra śāstraṃ bhāgavataṃ gṛhe \|*  
*tāvatpibaṃti pitaraḥ kṣīraṃ sarpirmadhūdakam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The Manes drink milk, ghee, honey and water for as many days, O son, as their descendants keep the Bhāgavata text in their abodes.

## \|\| 5.16.38 \|\|

*yacchaṃti vaiṣṇave bhaktyā śāstraṃ bhāgavataṃ hi ye \|*  
*kalpakoṭisahasrāṇi mama loke vasaṃti te \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Those who devoutly present the Bhāgavata scripture to a Vaiṣṇava, reside in my world for thousands and crores of Kalpas.

## \|\| 5.16.39 \|\|

*ye'rcayanti sadā gehe śāstraṃ bhāgavataṃ narāḥ \|*  
*prīṇitāstaiśca vibudhā yāvadā'bhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Devas are propitiated till the universal annihilation of all living beings by the men who honour the Bhāgavata scripture in their abodes always.

## \|\| 5.16.40 \|\|

*ślokārdhaṃ ślokapādaṃ vā varaṃ bhāgavataṃ gṛhe \|*  
*śataśo'tha sahasraiśca kimanyaiḥ śāstrasaṃgrahaiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. If one has in one’s abode half of a verse or even one-fourth of it from the excellent Bhāgavata, of what use are the collection of hundreds and thousands of other scriptural texts?

## \|\| 5.16.41 \|\|

*na yasya tiṣṭhate śāstraṃ gṛhe bhāgavataṃ kalau \|*  
*na tasya punarāvṛttiryāmyapāśātkadācana \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. If, in Kali Age, anyone has no Bhāgavata text in his abode, he will never return from the noose of Yama.

## \|\| 5.16.42 \|\|

*kathaṃ sa vaiṣṇavo jñeyaḥ śāstraṃ bhāgavataṃ kalau \|*  
*gṛhe na tiṣṭhate yasya śvapacādadhiko hi saḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. If there is no Bhāgavata text in anyone’s house in Kali Age, how can he be known as a Vaiṣṇava? He is worse than a Cāṇḍāla.

## \|\| 5.16.43 \|\|

*sarvasvenā'pi lokeśa kartavyaḥ śāstrasaṃgrahaḥ \|*  
*vaiṣṇavastu sadā bhaktyā tuṣṭyarthaṃ mama putraka \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. O Lord of the worlds, scriptural texts must be collected even at the cost of all that one possesses. For the sake of propitiating me, O my son, a Vaiṣṇava must do so always.

## \|\| 5.16.44 \|\|

*yatra yatra bhavetpuṇyaṃ śāstraṃ bhāgavataṃ kalau \|*  
*tatra tatra sadaivā'haṃ bhavāmi tridaśaiḥ saha \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Wherever there is Bhāgavata, the holy scripture, in Kali Age, I always stay there along with Devas.

## \|\| 5.16.45 \|\|

*tatra sarvāṇi tīrthāni nadīnadasarāṃsi ca \|*  
*yajñāḥ saptapurī nityaṃ puṇyāḥ sarve śiloccayāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. All the Tīrthas, (West-flowing and East-flowing) rivers and lakes, Yajñas, the seven cities and all the meritorious mountains are present there.

## \|\| 5.16.46 \|\|

*śrotavyaṃ mama śāstraṃ hi yaśodharmajayārthinā \|*  
*pāpakṣayārthaṃ lokeśa mokṣārthaṃ dharmabuddhinā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O Lord of the worlds, my scripture should be listened to by one who seeks fame, virtue and victory, for the sake of dispelling sins and by the pious-minded one for the sake of salvation.

## \|\| 5.16.47 \|\|

*śrīmadbhāgavataṃ puṇyamāyurārogyapuṣṭidam \|*  
*paṭhanācchravaṇādvā'pi sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Śrīmadbhāgavata is meritorious. It yields longevity, health and nourishment. By reading or listening to it, one is liberated from all sins.

## \|\| 5.16.48 \|\|

*na śṛṇvaṃti na hṛṣyaṃti śrīmadbhāgavataṃ param \|*  
*satyaṃsatyaṃ hi lokeśa teṣāṃ svāmī sadā yamaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. If people do not listen to the great (scripture.) Śrīmadbhāgavata, O Lord of the worlds, their perpetual master is Yama. It is indeed the truth, the truth (positively).

## \|\| 5.16.49 \|\|

*na gacchati yadā martyaḥ śrotuṃ bhāgavataṃ suta \|*  
*ekādaśyāṃ viśeṣeṇa nā'sti pāparatastataḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. If a man does not go to listen to Bhāgavata, O son, particularly on the Ekādaśī day, there is no greater sinner than he.

## \|\| 5.16.50 \|\|

*ślokaṃ bhāgavataṃ cā'pi ślokārdhaṃ pādameva vā \|*  
*likhitaṃ tiṣṭhate yasya gṛhe tasya vasāmyaham \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. I stay in that house where a verse from Bhāgavata, or half of it or even a quarter of it is kept written.

## \|\| 5.16.51 \|\|

*sarvā'śramā'bhigamanaṃ sarvatīrthā'vagāhanam \|*  
*na tathā pāvanaṃ nṝṇāṃ śrīmadbhāgavataṃ yathā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Approaching all the hermitages and taking a holy plunge in all the rivers is not as sanctifying unto men as Śrīmadbhāgavata.

## \|\| 5.16.52 \|\|

*yatra yatra caturvaktra śrīmadbhāgavataṃ bhavet \|*  
*gacchāmi tatratatrā'haṃ gauryathā sutavatsalā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Wherever there is Śrīmadbhāgavata, O Four-faced One, I go to that place like a cow fond of her calf.

## \|\| 5.16.53 \|\|

*matkathāvācakaṃ nityaṃ matkathāśravaṇe ratam \|*  
*matkathāprītamanasaṃ nā'haṃ tyakṣyāmi taṃ naram \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. I never abandon that man who is a reader and expounder of my stories, who is always engaged in listening to my stories and who is delighted in his mind (on hearing) my stories.

## \|\| 5.16.54 \|\|

*śrīmadbhāgavataṃ puṇyaṃ dṛṣṭvā nottiṣṭhate hi yaḥ \|*  
*sāṃvatsaraṃ tasya puṇyaṃ vilayaṃ yāti putraka \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. If a man does not stand up on seeing Śrīmadbhāgavata, the meritorious scripture, O son, his merit for the whole year perishes.

## \|\| 5.16.55 \|\|

*śrīmadbhāgavataṃ dṛṣṭvā pratyutthānābhivādanaiḥ \|*  
*sanmānayeta taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhavetprītirmamā'tulā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. If a man honours Śrīmadbhāgavata on seeing it by standing up and bowing down to it, by seeing him I derive matchless pleasure.

## \|\| 5.16.56 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā bhāgavataṃ dūrātprakrametsaṃmukhaṃ hi yaḥ \|*  
*padepade'śvamedhasya phalaṃ prāpnotyasaṃśayam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. If on seeing Bhāgavata from a distance a person (gladly) proceeds towards it, he shall undoubtedly attain the merit of a horse-sacrifice for every such step.

## \|\| 5.16.57 \|\|

*utthāya praṇamedyo vai śrīmadbhāgavataṃ naraḥ \|*  
*dhanaṃ putrāṃstathā dārānbhaktiṃ ca pradadāmyaham \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. If a man gets up and bows down to Śrīmadbhāgavata, I grant to him wealth, sons, wives and devotion.

## \|\| 5.16.58 \|\|

*mahārājopacāraistu śrīmadbhāgavataṃ suta \|*  
*śṛṇvaṃti ye narā bhaktyā teṣāṃ vaśyo bhavāmyaham \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. If men devoutly listen to Śrīmadbhāgavata offering royal reception and reverence to it, I am won over by them (easily).

## \|\| 5.16.59 \|\|

*mamotsaveṣu sarvepu śrīmadbhāgavataṃ param \|*  
*śṛṇvaṃti ye narā bhaktyā mama prītyai ca suvrata \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. O righteous one, men who listen devoutly to the great Śrīmadbhāgavata during all my festivals give me great delight.

## Chapter 17 - The Greatness of Mathura

## \|\| 5.17.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*kasminkṣetre hi deveśa mārgaśīrṣo'dhikaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*kiṃ phalaṃ ca bhavettasminnetatsarvaṃ vada prabho \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: This Sthala-purāṇa of Mathurā has a tenuous relation with this Māhātmya—only that the month of Mārgaśīrṣa is favourite with Viṣṇu and Viṣṇu-Kṛṣṇa happened to live in Mathurā region in the early part of his life.

Brahmā said:

1\. O Lord of Devas, which is that holy place in which the month of Mārgaśīrṣa is most celebrated? What is the benefit thereof? O Lord, state everything.

## \|\| 5.17.2 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*madhureti suvikhyātamasti kṣetraṃ paraṃ mama \|*  
*suramyā ca praśastā ca janmabhūmiḥ priyā mama \|\| 2 \|\|*

Śrī Bhagavān said:

2\. There is a great sacred place of mine well-known as Mathurā. It is very beautiful and well-honoured. It is the place of my birth and is very much loved by me.

## \|\| 5.17.3 \|\|

*padepade tīrthaphalaṃ madhurāyāṃ caturmukha \|*  
*yatrayatra naraḥ snāto mucyate ghorakilbiṣāt \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. At Mathurā, O Four-faced One, a devotee obtains the merit of a Tīrtha at every step. Wherever the man may take his holy bath, he is liberated from terrible sins.

## \|\| 5.17.4 \|\|

*sarvadharmavihīnānāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ durātmanām \|*  
*narakārtiharā putra madhurā pāpanāśinī \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O son, Mathurā is destructive of sins. It dispels the agony suffered in hells by men of wicked souls devoid of all piety and virtue.

## \|\| 5.17.5 \|\|

*kṛtaghnaśca surāpaśca cauro bhagnavratastathā \|*  
*madhurāṃ prāpya manujo mucyate ghorapātakāt \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. An ungrateful one, a drink-addict, a thief and a man whose holy vow is interrupted in the middle and broken, is liberated from terrible sins on reaching Mathurā.

## \|\| 5.17.6-7 \|\|

*sūryaudaye tamo naśyedyathā vajrabhayānnagāḥ \|*  
*tārkṣyaṃ dṛṣṭvā yathā sarpā meghā vātahatā yathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tattvajñānādyathā duḥkhaṃ hariṃ dṛṣṭvā yathā gajāḥ \|*  
*tathā pāpāni naśyaṃti mathurādarśanātsuta \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Just as darkness disappears at sunrise, just as mountains run away out of fear of the thunderbolt, just as serpents perish on seeing Garuḍa, just as clouds are scattered on being tossed by wind, just as (worldly) misery is dispelled by the knowledge of reality, just as elephants run away on seeing a lion, so also sins perish at the sight of Mathurā, O son.

## \|\| 5.17.8 \|\|

*śraddhayā bhaktiyuktastu dṛṣṭvā madhupurīṃ naraḥ \|*  
*brahmahā'pi viśudhyeta kiṃ punastvanyapātakī \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On seeing Madhupurī a man endowed with faith and devotion becomes purified even if he is a slayer of a Brāhmaṇa. What need one say of other sinners?

## \|\| 5.17.9 \|\|

*mathurāṃ snātukāmasya gacchatastu padepade \|*  
*nirāśāni vrajaṃtyeva pāpāni ca śarīrataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Sins become desperate and go away from the body of one who is desirous of taking his holy bath in Mathurā and goes there step by step.

## \|\| 5.17.10 \|\|

*anuṣaṃgeṇa gacchaṃti vāṇijyenā'pi sevayā \|*  
*madhurāsnānamātreṇa divaṃ yāṃti gatāṃhasaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Even if people go to Mathurā casually or for any business dealings or for service, they rid themselves of sins merely due to their holy bath in Mathurā and go to heaven.

## \|\| 5.17.11 \|\|

*nāmā'pi gṛhṇatāmasyāḥ sadā muktirna saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*sadā kṛtayugaṃ tatra sadā caivottarāyaṇam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Even those who utter the name of this (city) shall undoubtedly attain salvation. There is perpetual Kṛtayuga there; there is Uttarāyaṇa (period of the northern transit of the Sun) there always.

## \|\| 5.17.12 \|\|

*yaḥ śṛṇoti caturvaktra mādhuraṃ mama maṃdiram \|*  
*anyenoccārite sadyaḥ so'pi pāpātpramucyate \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He who hears about my temple at Mathurā on being mentioned by another, is liberated from sins.

## \|\| 5.17.13 \|\|

*trirātramapi ye tatra vasaṃti manujāḥ suta \|*  
*teṣāṃ punaṃti sahṛṣṭāḥ spṛṣṭāścaraṇareṇavaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On being seen or touched the particles from the feet of those men who stay there for three nights, O son, sanctify (everything).

## \|\| 5.17.14 \|\|

*yathā tṛṇasamūhaṃ tu jvalayaṃti sphuliṃgakāḥ \|*  
*tathā mahāṃti pāpāni dahate mathurā purī \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Just as flames of fire burn clusters of grass, so also the city of Mathurā burns great sins,

## \|\| 5.17.15 \|\|

*snānena sarvatīrthānāṃ yaḥ syātsukṛtasaṃcayaḥ \|*  
*tato'dhikataraṃ proktā mathurā sarvamaṃḍale \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. It is said that the holy bath in all the zones of Mathurā is more efficacious than, and the merit thereof is superior to, the merit earned by bath in all the Tīrthas.

## \|\| 5.17.16 \|\|

*caturṇāmapi vedānāṃ puṇyamadhyayanācca yat \|*  
*tatpuṇyaṃ jāyate tatra mathurāṃ smaratāṃ nṛṇām \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Men who remember Mathurā acquire that merit which accrues from a study of the four Vedas.

## \|\| 5.17.17 \|\|

*iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe brahmaviṣṇusaṃvāde mārgaśīrṣamāsamāhātmye mathurāmāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma saptadaśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. A sin committed elsewhere perishes on approaching a Tīrtha; a sin committed in Tīrthas becomes permanent like adamantine cement.

## \|\| 5.17.18 \|\|

*mathurāyāṃ kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ mathurāyāṃ praṇaśyati \|*  
*dharmārthakāmamokṣākhyaṃ sthitvā tatra labhennaraḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. A sin committed at Mathurā perishes at Mathurā itself. By staying there a man obtains (all the aims of life) namely virtue, wealth, love and salvation.

## \|\| 5.17.19 \|\|

*anyatra daśabhirvarṣaiḥ prārabdhaṃ bhujyate hi yat \|*  
*kilviṣaṃ ca caturvaktra māthure daśabhirdinaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Sin that takes ten years elsewhere to be consumed completely, O Four-faced One, takes only ten days in the holy spot of Mathurā.

## \|\| 5.17.20 \|\|

*divi naiva na pātāle nāṃtarikṣe na mānuṣe \|*  
*samaṃ tu mathurāyāṃ hi priyaṃ mama sadaiva hi \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. There is nothing in heaven, in nether worlds, in firmament or in the mortal world as dear to me always as Mathurā.

## \|\| 5.17.21-23 \|\|

*sarveṣāmeva tīrthānāṃ māthuraṃ paramaṃ mahat \|*  
*bālakrīḍanarūpāṇi kṛtāni saha gopakaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*triṃśadvarṣasahasrāṇi triṃśadvarṣaśatāni ca \|*  
*yatphalaṃ bhārate varṣe tatphalaṃ mathurāṃ smaran \|\| 22 \|\|*

*sannihatyāṃ tu yatpuṇyaṃ rāhugraste divākare \|*  
*tatodhikaṃ labhetputra mathurāyāṃ dinedine \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. The holy spot of Mathurā is greater than all other Tīrthas (taken together). It is the place where thirty-three thousand years were spent (by me) in sports in childhood with the cowherds. By remembering Mathurā one attains the same merit as in the whole of the Bhārata sub-continent.

O son, everyday, one attains in Mathurā more merit than that obtained at the river Sannihatī when there is a solar eclipse.

## \|\| 5.17.24 \|\|

*pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu tīrtharāje tu yatphalam \|*  
*tatphalaṃ labhate putra sahomāse madhoḥ pure \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. In the city of Madhu, O son, one obtains in the Mārgaśīrṣa month that merit which is obtained in Tīrtharāja Prayāga in the course of a full thousand years.

## \|\| 5.17.25 \|\|

*pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu vārāṇasyāṃ ca yatphalam \|*  
*tatphalaṃ labhate putra mathurāyāṃ saho dine \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. In the course of a day in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, O son, one obtains in Mathurā that merit which is obtained at Vārāṇasī in the course of a full millennium.

## \|\| 5.17.26 \|\|

*godāvarīdvārakayornaro yaḥ kṣetre kurūṇāṃ kṣitidāyako yaḥ \|*  
*ṣaṇmāsakātsādhayate gayāyāṃ samaṃ bhavenno dinamekamāthuram \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. By (spending) a day in Mathurā one obtains the same merit as is obtained by a man who gifts a plot of land near Godāvarī, in Dvārakā or in Kurukṣetra or who spends six months at Gayā.

## \|\| 5.17.27 \|\|

*na dvārakā kāśikāṃcī na māyā gadādharo yasya samaṃ na tīrtham \|*  
*saṃtarpitā yadyamunājalena vāṃchaṃti no vai pitaraḥ piṃḍadānam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Neither Dvārakā, nor Kāśī nor Kāñcī can be a Tīrtha (like Mathurā) where Māyāgadādhara (i.e. Viṣṇu) is the deity. If libations are offered to them by means of Yamunā-water, Pitṛs do not desire the offerings of balls of rice.

## \|\| 5.17.28 \|\|

*mathurāyāṃ prakurvaṃti purīsādhāraṇīdṛśam \|*  
*ye narāste'pi vijñeyāḥ pāparāśibhiranvitāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Those men who view Mathurā as though it is an ordinary city should be known as those contaminated with masses of sins.

## \|\| 5.17.29 \|\|

*na dṛṣṭā mathurā yena didṛkṣā yasya jāyate \|*  
*yatra tatra mṛtasyā'pi māthure janma jāyate \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. If Mathurā is not seen by one, but one had the desire to visit it, one is reborn in Mathurā wherever one dies.

## \|\| 5.17.30 \|\|

*bhūme rajāṃsi gaṇayetkālenā'pi caturmukha \|*  
*māthure yāni tīrthāni teṣāṃ saṃkhyā na vidyate \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O Four-faced One, one may even count the dust particles of the earth in course of time. But there is no limit to the number of Tīrthas in Mathurā.

## \|\| 5.17.31 \|\|

*kuru bhoḥ kuru bho vāsaṃ mathurākhyāṃ purīṃ prati \|*  
*vasāmi satataṃ tasyāṃ gopakanyābhirāvṛtaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Oh, do stay! Oh, do stay in the city of Mathurā! I stay there continuously surrounded by cowherd lasses.

## \|\| 5.17.32 \|\|

*rere saṃsāramagnāśca śiṣyā me śṛṇutā'pare \|*  
*yadīcchatha sukhaṃ sāṃdraṃ vāsaṃ kuruta matpurīm \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O ye who are immersed in the ocean of worldly existence, O my other disciples, listen. If you desire for intense and excellent happiness, stay in my city.

## \|\| 5.17.33 \|\|

*aho loko mahānaṃdo netrayukto na paśyati \|*  
*māthure vidyamāne'pi saṃsṛtiṃ bhajate sadā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Alas! People of the world are exceedingly blind; though they have eyes they do not see. Although the holy place of Mathurā is present, they undergo the ordeal of births and deaths.

## \|\| 5.17.34 \|\|

*mānuṣīṃ yonimatulāṃ labdhvā bhāgyasya yogataḥ \|*  
*vṛthaivāyurgataṃ teṣāṃ na dṛṣṭā mathurāpurī \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Despite the fact that by good luck they have obtained the incomparable birth in human womb (species), their life has gone in vain. The city of Mathurā was not seen by them.

## \|\| 5.17.35 \|\|

*aho mateḥ sudaurbalyamaho bhāgyasya durvidhiḥ \|*  
*aho mohasya mahimā mathurā naiva sevyate \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Alas, the weakness of the intellect! Alas, adverse fate and bad luck! Alas, the powerful influence of delusion! Mathurā is not resorted to.

## \|\| 5.17.36 \|\|

*mathurāṃ tu parityajya yo'nyatra kurute matim \|*  
*mūḍho bhramati saṃsāre mohito mama māyayā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. He who is inclined towards anoṃer place after ignoring Mathurā is deluded by my Māyā. He is stupid and he wanders in the vast expanse of worldly existence.

## \|\| 5.17.37 \|\|

*mathurāmapi saṃprāpya yo'nyatra kurute spṛhām \|*  
*durbuddhestasya kiṃ jñānaṃ so'jñānena vijṛṃbhitaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. If even after reaching Mathurā anyone craves for any other place, how can that evil-minded one acquire perfect knowledge? He displays his ignorance!

## \|\| 5.17.38 \|\|

*mātrā pitrā parityaktā ye tyaktā nijabaṃdhubhiḥ \|*  
*yeṣāṃ kvāpi gatirnāsti teṣāṃ mama purī gatiḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. My city is the goal and refuge unto those who are abandoned by their parents and kinsmen and who have no other go.

## \|\| 5.17.39 \|\|

*pāparāśibhirākrāṃtā ye dāridrya parājitāḥ \|*  
*yeṣāṃ kvāpi gatirnāsti teṣāṃ mama purī gatiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. My city is the goal and refuge unto those who have been overwhelmed by masses of sins, those who have been vanquished by poverty and those who have no other place of resort.

## \|\| 5.17.40 \|\|

*sārātsārataraṃ sthānaṃ guhyādguhyataraṃ param \|*  
*gatimanveṣamāṇānāṃ mathurā paramā gatiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. It is the most excellent of all spots. It is the greatest secret. Mathurā is the greatest goal unto those who are in search of a worthy goal and refuge.

## \|\| 5.17.41 \|\|

*na tatpuṇyairna taddānairna tapobhirna tu stavaiḥ \|*  
*na labhyaṃ vividhairyogairlabhyaṃ madanubhāvataḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. That cannot be obtained through merits; that cannot be acquired through charitable gifts. That cannot be obtained through austerities nor through eulogies. It cannot be secured by means of different kinds of Yogic exercises. It can be obtained only through my grace.

## \|\| 5.17.42 \|\|

*mayi yeṣāṃ sthirā bhaktirbhūyasī yeṣu matkṛpā \|*  
*teṣāmeva hi dhanyānāṃ mathurāyāṃ bhavedgatiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. At Mathurā, good status can be achieved only by those blessed ones who have steadfast devotion to me, and on whom I have ample favour.

## \|\| 5.17.43 \|\|

*yā gatiryogayuktasya brahmajñasya manīṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*sā gatistyajataḥ prāṇānmathurāyāṃ narasya ca \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. One who gives up his life at Mathurā attains that goal which a learned man endowed with Yogic power, who has realized Brahman, attains.

## \|\| 5.17.44 \|\|

*kāśyādipuryo yadi saṃti loke tāsāṃ tu madhye mathuraiva dhanyā \|*  
*yā janmamauṃjīvratamuktidānairnṛṇāṃ caturdhā vidadhāti muktim \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. There are cities like Kāśī etc. But the most blessed one is Mathurā alone which yields the fourfold salvation (Sālokya etc.) through four ways (viz.) of taking birth there, performing the rite of sacred thread-ceremony, observing many vows, and making charitable gifts.

## \|\| 5.17.45 \|\|

*na yogairyā gatirlabhyā manvaṃtaraśatairapi \|*  
*anyatra helayā sā'tra labhyate matprasādataḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. With my favour good goal is easily attained here, the goal which cannot be attained even in the course of hundreds of Manvantaras by means of Yogic exercises.

## \|\| 5.17.46 \|\|

*na pāpebhyo bhayaṃ yatra na bhayaṃ yatra vai yamāt \|*  
*na garbhavāsabhīryatra tatkṣetraṃ ko na saṃśrayet \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Who will not resort to that holy place where there is no fear from sins, where one need not be afraid of Yama and where the fear of stay in a womb (i.e. rebirth) ceases to exist

## \|\| 5.17.47-49 \|\|

*mathurāyāṃ ca yatpuṇyaṃ tatpuṇyasya phalaṃ śṛṇu \|*  
*mathurāyāṃ samāsādya mathurāyāṃ mṛtā hi ye \|\| 47 \|\|*

*api kīṭapataṃgādyā jāyaṃte te caturbhujāḥ \|*  
*kūlātpataṃti ye vṛkṣāste'pi yāṃti parāṃ gatim \|\| 48 \|\|*

*mūkā jaḍāṃdhabadhirāstaponiyamavarjitāḥ \|*  
*kālenaiva mṛtā ye ca mama lokaṃ vrajaṃti te \|\| 49 \|\|*

47-49. Listen to the merit acquired from Mathurā and the fruit thereof. Those worms, locusts, moths etc. which come to Mathurā and die there become four-armed ones (i.e. having the same form as that of Viṣṇu i.e. Sārūpya type of liberation). Those trees which fall from the banks attain the greatest goal. Dumb, sluggish, blind and deaf people devoid of penance and holy observances and those who die in course of time go to my world.

## \|\| 5.17.50 \|\|

*sarpadaṣṭāḥ paśuhatāḥ pāvakāṃbuvināśitāḥ \|*  
*labdhā'pamṛtyavo ye ca māthure mama lokagāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Those who are bitten by serpents, who are killed by animals, those who perish in fire and water and those who die prematurely or accidentally in Mathurā go to my world.

## \|\| 5.17.51 \|\|

*null*

51\. Truth! It is the truth, O excellent sage, that I say on my honour. There is nothing else like Mathurā anywhere yielding all that one desires.

## \|\| 5.17.52 \|\|

*trivargadā kāmināṃ yā mumukṣūṇāṃ ca muktidā \|*  
*bhaktīcchorbhaktidā kastāṃ mathurāṃ nā'śrayedbudhaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Which learned man will not resort to Mathurā which bestows on persons who desire the three aims of life (Virtue, Wealth and Love)? It bestows salvation on those who are desirous of salvation and it bestows devotion on one who desires for devotion.

## \|\| 5.17.53 \|\|

*etādṛśī madhupurī karttavyā mārgaśīrṣake \|*  
*tadabhāve puṣkaraṃ hi kartavyaṃ vidhipūrvakam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The city of Madhu of all these characteristics and good features should be resorted to in the month of Mārgaśīrṣaka. If that is not available, Puṣkara is to be resorted to in accordance with the injunctions.

## \|\| 5.17.54 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhaṃ hi brahmaṇaḥ kuṇḍaṃ madhyaṃ kuṇḍaṃ ca vaiṣṇavam \|*  
*kaniṣṭhaṃ rudradaivatyamiti jānīhi buddhiman \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The oldest Kuṇḍa (well) is that of Brahmā, the middle Kuṇḍa is that of Viṣṇu and the youngest one is that having Rudra for its deity. O intelligent one, know this.

## \|\| 5.17.55 \|\|

*eṣu snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca śrāddhaṃ ca vidhipūrvakam \|*  
*pūjā ca mahatī kāryā mama prītikarā suta \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. In all these, O son, one should perform all these rites—holy ablution, charitable gift and Śrāddha in accordance with the injunctions. A splendid worship shall be performed. It is conducive to my delight.

## \|\| 5.17.56 \|\|

*pūrṇā yā tu bhavetputra sahomāse mama priyā \|*  
*tasyāṃ yatkriyate puṇyaṃ mama prītikaraṃ bhavet \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The full-moon day, O son, in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa is a great favourite of mine. Whatever meritorious rite is performed on that day shall be pleasing to me.

## \|\| 5.17.57 \|\|

*godānamannadānaṃ ca hemadānaṃ ca putraka \|*  
*dharādānaṃ ca kartavyaṃ pūrṇāyāṃ vidhipūrvakam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. On the full-moon day, O son, one shall perform all these rites of charitable gifts, viz. gift of cows, gift of food, gift of gold and gift of land.

## \|\| 5.17.58 \|\|

*sahomāse hi pūrṇāyāṃ sadmadānaṃ ca kārayet \|*  
*yatkiṃcitkriyate pūrṇaṃ tadakṣayyaphalaṃ bhavet \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. On the full-moon day in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa one should make gift of a house. Whatever is done shall be perfect, yielding everlasting merit.

## \|\| 5.17.59 \|\|

*brahmabhojyaṃ hi kartavyaṃ yathāvibhavasārataḥ \|*  
*pūrṇāyāmeva kartavya utsavo vratapūrttaye \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Feeding of Brāhmaṇas should be done in accordance with one’s affluence. Festival on the completion of a religious observation should be celebrated on the full-moon day itself.

## \|\| 5.17.60 \|\|

*yādṛśī mathurā putra sahomāse mama priyā \|*  
*na tathā tīrtharājādyāstadabhāve ca puṣkaram \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. O son, Tīrtharāja etc. are not as pleasing to me in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa as Mathurā. If it is not available, Puṣkara (is to be resorted to).

## \|\| 5.17.61 \|\|

*puṣkare mathurāyāṃ vai pūrṇā kāryā vicakṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*yatra kutrāpi vā kāryā vidhiyuktā ca pūrṇimā \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. At Puṣkara and Mathurā the full-moon day is to be celebrated by intelligent devotees. Wherever it is celebrated it shall be celebrated in accordance with the injunctions.

## \|\| 5.17.62 \|\|

*snānaṃ dānaṃ tathā pūjāṃ pūrṇāyāṃ na karoti yaḥ \|*  
*ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi pacyate rauravādiṣu \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. He who does not take holy bath, make charitable gifts and perform worship on the full-moon day is cooked (tortured) in Raurava and other hells for sixty thousand years.

## \|\| 5.17.63 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena mānyā pūrṇā vicakṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*mārgaśīrṣeṇa saṃyuktā anaṃtaphaladāyinī \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Hence by all means, the full-moon day should be honoured by intelligent people. That in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa bestows infinite merit.

## \|\| 5.17.64 \|\|

*yathā te kathitaṃ vatsa mārgaśīrṣaṃ mama priyam \|*  
*karoti yo naro bhaktyā tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Listen to the fruit of the merit of that man who devoutly performs all the rites as mentioned by me in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, of which I am fond.

## \|\| 5.17.65 \|\|

*tīrthāyuteṣu yatpuṇyaṃ yatpuṇyaṃ vratakoṭibhiḥ \|*  
*sarvayajñeṣu yatpuṇyaṃ tatpuṇyaṃ samavāpnuyāt \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. He shall attain that merit which is obtained in ten thousand Tīrthas or by means of crores of holy rites or all the Yajñas.

## \|\| 5.17.66 \|\|

*aputro labhate putraṃ nirdhano dhanameva ca \|*  
*vidyārthī ca tathā vidyāṃ rūpārthī rūpamāpnuyāt \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. A man without a son obtains a son; a poor man obtains wealth; one who seeks learning shall get learning and one who seeks beauty shall become beautiful.

## \|\| 5.17.67 \|\|

*brāhmaṇo brahmavarcasvī kṣatriyo vijayī bhavet \|*  
*vaiśyo nidhipatitvaṃ ca śūdraḥ śuddhyeta pātakāt \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. A Brāhmaṇa shall get all Brahminical splendour; a Kṣatriya shall be victorious; a Vaiśya shall acquire lordship over wealth; and a Śūdra shall become purified of all his sins.

## \|\| 5.17.68 \|\|

*yaddurlabhaṃ ca duṣprāpyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu mānada \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ prāpnuyānmartyaḥ sahomāse na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. A man shall attain in the Mārgaśīrṣa month whatever is very difficult to get or inaccessible in the three worlds, O bestower of honour. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 5.17.69 \|\|

*yadyapyeteṣu kāmeṣu saktā ye mānavāḥ suta \|*  
*tuṣṭā hyaṃte caturvaktra na kāmārhā mahābhuja \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Although men who are attracted by these desires, O son, are satisfied in the end, O Four-faced One, they do not deserve(?) those desires, O mighty-armed one.

## Section 6 - Bhāgavata-māhātmya

## Chapter 1 - The Greatness of Vrajabhūmi

## \|\| 6.1.1 \|\|

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīmadbhāgavatamāhātmye śāḍilyopadiṣṭavrajabhūmimāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma prathamo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Obeisance to Śrī Gaṇeśa

Now begins the glorification of Śrīmadbhāgavata.

Vyāsa said:

1\. For the perpetual attainment of the bliss of devotion we bow to Kṛṣṇa whose form (accompanied by Śrī Rādhā) is constituted of existence, knowledge and bliss; who incessantly showers infinite happiness and who is the cause of the origin, sustenance and annihilation of the universe.

## \|\| 6.1.2 \|\|

*naimiṣe sūtamāsīnamabhivādya mahāmatim \|*  
*kathāmṛtarasāsvādakuśalā ṛṣayo'bruvan \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. After bowing down to the highly intelligent Sūta who was seated in Naimiṣa forest, sages who were experts in enjoying the nectarine juice of narratives said:

The sages enquired:

## \|\| 6.1.3 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*vajraṃ śrīmāthure deśe svapautraṃ hastināpure \|*  
*abhiṣicya gate rājñi tau kathaṃ kiṃ ca cakratuḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The king (Yudhiṣṭhira) went away (abdicating his throne) after crowning Vajra (nābha) in the glorious country of Mathurā and his grandson (Parīkṣit) at Hastināpura. What did those two (kings) do?

Sūta replied:

## \|\| 6.1.4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*nārāyaṇaṃ namaskṛtya naraṃ caiva narottamam \|*  
*devīṃ sarasvatīṃ vyāsaṃ tato jayamudīrayet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. After bowing down to Nārāyaṇa, Nara, Narottama the most excellent among men (i.e. Arjuna), Goddess Sarasvatī and Vyāsa, one should uttter (recite) the Purāṇa.

## \|\| 6.1.5 \|\|

*mahāpathaṃ gate rājñi parīkṣitpṛthivīpatiḥ \|*  
*jagāma mathurāṃ viprā vajranābhadidṛkṣayā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. When the king (Yudhiṣṭhira) went along the great path (the northern direction), Parīkṣit, the king, went to Mathurā, O Brāhmaṇas, with a desire to see Vajraṇābha.

## \|\| 6.1.6 \|\|

*pitṛvyamāgataṃ jñātvā vajraḥ premapariplutaḥ \|*  
*abhigamyābhivādyātha nināya nijamandiram \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On knowing that his uncle had come, Vajra was overwhelmed with affection. He approached (to receive) and saluted him and took him to his mansion.

## \|\| 6.1.7 \|\|

*pariṣvajya sa taṃ vīraḥ kṛṣṇaikagatamānasaḥ \|*  
*rohiṇyādyā hareḥ patnīrvavandāyatanāgataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. That hero whose mind was solely devoted to Kṛṣṇa embraced him. He went inside the abode and bowed down to Hari’s wives, Rohiṇī and others.

## \|\| 6.1.8 \|\|

*tābhiḥ sammānito'tyarthaṃ parīkṣitpṛthivīpatiḥ \|*  
*viśrāntaḥ sukhamāsīno vajranābhamuvāca ha \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Parīkṣit, the king, was ardently honoured by them. He took rest and after seating himself comfortably said to Vajraṇābha:

## \|\| 6.1.9 \|\|

*śrīparīkṣiduvāca \|*  
*tāta tvatpitṛbhirnūnamasmatpitṛpitāmahāḥ \|*  
*uddhṛtā bhūriduḥkhaughādahaṃ ca parirakṣitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

Śrī Parīkṣit said:

9\. O dear one, our father and grandfathers were redeemed from great mass of miseries by your predecessors. I too was protected.

## \|\| 6.1.10-11 \|\|

*na pārayāmyahaṃ tāta sādhu kṛtvopakārataḥ \|*  
*tvāmataḥ prārthayāmyaṅga sukhaṃ rājye'nuyujyatām \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kośasainyādijā cintā tathāridamanādijā \|*  
*manāgapi na kāryā te susevyāḥ kintu mātaraḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. I cannot adequately repay (help) you in return, O dear one. Hence I request you to be engaged happily in (enjoying your) kingdom. You need not have any worries about finance (treasury) and defence (army). Nor need you have any anxiety regarding suppression of enemies. None of these worries should bother you at all. Only the mothers (elderly relatives) should be served well.

## \|\| 6.1.12 \|\|

*nivedya mayi kartavyaṃ sarvādhiparivarjjanam \|*  
*śrutvaitatparamaprīto vajrastaṃ pratyuvāca ha \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Avoid all anxieties after leaving them to me.

On hearing this, Vajra was exceedingly pleased. He replied to him:

## \|\| 6.1.13 \|\|

*śrīvajranābha uvāca \|*  
*rājannucitametatte yadasmāsu prabhāṣate \|*  
*tvatpitropakṛtaścāhaṃ dhanurvidyāpradānataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

Śrī Vajranābha said:

13\. O king, what you say to me is but proper. I have been obliged by your father by imparting to me the science of archery.

## \|\| 6.1.14 \|\|

*tasmānnālpāpi me cintā kṣātraṃ dṛḍhamupeyuṣaḥ \|*  
*kintvekā paramā cintā tatra kiñcidvicāryyatām \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Hence I have not the least worry at all, as I firmly uphold my Kṣatriyahood (military expertise). But I have a great worry. Give some thought to it.

## \|\| 6.1.15 \|\|

*māthure tvabhiṣikto'pi sthito'haṃ nirjane vane \|*  
*kva gatā vai prajā'tratyā yatra rājyaṃ prarocate \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. I have been crowned in Mathurā, yet I am staying in a desolate forest. Where have the subjects of this place gone? I like a kingdom inhabited by subjects.

## \|\| 6.1.16 \|\|

*ityukto viṣṇurātastu nandādīnāṃ purohitam \|*  
*śāṃḍilyamājuhāvāśu vajrasaṃdehanuttaye \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. On being told thus, Viṣṇurāta (i.e. Parīkṣit) invited Śāṇḍilya, the priest of Nanda, and others in order to dispel the doubt of Vajra.

## \|\| 6.1.17 \|\|

*athoṭajaṃ vihāyāśu śāṃḍilyaḥ samupāgataḥ \|*  
*pūjito vajranābhena niṣasādāsanottame \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Śāṇḍilya immediately left his cottage and came there. Duly honoured by Vajranābha, he occupied an excellent seat.

## \|\| 6.1.18 \|\|

*upodghātaṃ viṣṇurātaścakārāśu tatastvasau \|*  
*uvāca paramaprītastāvubhau parisāntvayan \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Parīkṣit made some introductory remarks. Then (the sage) who was exceedingly delighted, said thus consoling both of them:

## \|\| 6.1.19 \|\|

*śrīśāṃḍilya uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇutaṃ dattacittau me rahasyaṃ vrajabhūmijam \|*  
*vrajanaṃ vyāptirityuktyā vyāpanādvraja ucyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

Śrī Śāṇḍilya said:

19\. Listen attentively to me (as I recount) the secret of the land called Vraja. The root ^vraj means ‘to spread’. As the land spread extensively, it is called Vraja.

## \|\| 6.1.20 \|\|

*guṇātītaṃ paraṃ brahma vyāpakaṃ vraja ucyate \|*  
*sadānandaṃ paraṃ jyotirmuktānāṃ padamavyayam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Supreme Brahman is beyond Guṇas. It is pervasive and is called Vraja. It is the greatest splendour and of the nature of perpetual bliss. It is the immutable region of the liberated ones.

## \|\| 6.1.21 \|\|

*tasminnandātmajaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sadānandāṃgavigrahaḥ \|*  
*ātmārāmaścāptakāmaḥ premāktairanubhūyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. In that (land) Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda, is seen by the people immersed in love, as one whose form is of perpetual bliss. He is one who has realized all his desires. He sports within his Ātman. He is seen by those full of love (devotees like Nārada).

## \|\| 6.1.22 \|\|

*ātmā tu rādhikā tasya tayaiva ramaṇādasau \|*  
*ātmārāmatayā prājñaiḥ procyate gūḍhavedibhiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. His Ātman is Rādhikā. Since he sports with her, he is said to be ‘one sporting and rejoicing in the soul’, by learned men who know mysterious things.

## \|\| 6.1.23 \|\|

*kāmāstu vāñchitāstasya gāvo gopāśca gopikāḥ \|*  
*nityāḥ sarve vihārādyā āptakāmastatastvayam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. His desired ones are the cows, the cowherds and the cowherd-esses. They are always present near him for sport. Therefore, he is Āptakāma (‘one who has realized his desires’).

## \|\| 6.1.24 \|\|

*rahasyaṃ tvidametasya prakṛteḥ paramucyate \|*  
*prakṛtyā khelatastasya līlā'nyairanubhūyate \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. This is his secret. He is said to be beyond Prakṛti. As he sports with Prakṛti, his sport (with Prakṛti) is experienced by others.

## \|\| 6.1.25 \|\|

*sargasthityapyayā yatra rajaḥsattvatamoguṇaiḥ \|*  
*līlaivaṃ dvividhā tasya vāstavī vyāvahārikī \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. His sport consists of creation, sustenance and annihilation by means of Rajas, Sattva and Tamas Guṇas. This sport is of two kinds: the real and the ordinary or customary.

## \|\| 6.1.26 \|\|

*vāstavī tatsvasaṃvedyā jīvānāṃ vyāvahārikī \|*  
*ādyāṃ vinā dvitīyā na dvitīyā nādyagā kvacit \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The real sport is worthy of being known by Himself alone (with the experience of bliss along with his devotees—Commentary). The customary one is that which is understood by the individual souls. The second one cannot take place without the first and the second one does not reach as far as the first anywhere.

## \|\| 6.1.27-30 \|\|

*āvayorgocareyaṃ tu tallīlā vyāvahārikī \|*  
*yatra bhūrādayo lokā bhuvi māthuramaṇḍalam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*atraiva vrajabhūmiḥ sā yatra tattvaṃ sugopitam \|*  
*bhāsate premapūrṇānāṃ kadācidapi sarvataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*kadāciddvāparasyānte raholīlādhikāriṇaḥ \|*  
*samavetā yadā'tra syuryathedānīṃ tadā hariḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*svaiḥ sahāvataretsveṣu samāveśārthamīpsitāḥ \|*  
*tadā devādayo'pyanye'vataranti samantataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

27-30. His Vyāvahārikī Līlā (ordinary sport) is within the range of our experience where the worlds, Bhūmi etc. exist. The region of Mathurā is on this earth and it is here that the land of Vraja too exists. It is there that the truth is well concealed. At times it is revealed to those who are full of love (for him). It is wholly revealed to them.

Some time at the end of Dvāpara, those who are knowers of the secret sports (of the Lord) gather together as now. At that time Hari shall incarnate along with his (folk) in order to assimilate his desired ones into himself and his (folk). Then the Devas and others too incarnate all round (him).

## \|\| 6.1.31-34 \|\|

*sarveṣāṃ vāñchitaṃ kṛtvā harirantarhito'bhavat \|*  
*tenātra trividhā lokāḥ sthitāḥ pūrvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*nityāstallipsavaścaiva devādyāśceti bhedataḥ \|*  
*devādyāsteṣu kṛṣṇena dvārikāṃ prāpitāḥ purā \|\| 32 \|\|*

*punarmauśalamārgeṇa svādhikāreṣu cāpitāḥ \|*  
*tallipsūṃśca sadā kṛṣṇaḥ premānandaikarūpiṇaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*vidhāya svīyanityeṣu samāveśitavāṃstadā \|*  
*nityāḥ sarve'pyayogyeṣu darśanābhāvatāṃ gatāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

31-34. After fulfilling the desires of everyone, Hari vanished. Therefore, three types of people remained here undoubtedly. They are Nityas (permanent folk). Tallipsus (those who desire to obtain him) and Devādyas (Devas and others). Devādyas were formerly taken to Dvārakā by Kṛṣṇa. Again through the means of the Muśala (Pestle used in the fratricidal fight among the Yādavas) they were assimilated into himself.

Tallipsus who are always in the form of love and bliss were converted into Nityas belonging to himself and merged within them. All the Nityas being undeserved to be seen by ordinary unworthy people attained invisibility.

## \|\| 6.1.35 \|\|

*vyāvahārikalīlāsthāstatra yannādhikāriṇaḥ \|*  
*paśyantyatrāgatāstasmānnirjjanatvaṃ samantataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Ordinary people (lit. people in the ordinary sport of the Lord) who came to see the people authorized (to participate in the secret sports of the Lord) did (could) not see them. Hence they departed rendering Vraja desolate all round.

## \|\| 6.1.36 \|\|

*tasmāccintā na te kāryā vajranābha madājñayā \|*  
*vāsayātra bahūngrāmānsaṃsiddhiste bhaviṣyati \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Hence, O Vajranābha, you need not worry at all. At my behest colonize many villages here. You will achieve Siddhi (success in the undertaking).

## \|\| 6.1.37 \|\|

*kṛṣṇalīlānusāreṇa kṛtvā nāmāni sarvataḥ \|*  
*tvayā vāsaya tā grāmānsaṃsevyā bhūriyaṃ parā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. In accordance with the sports of Kṛṣṇa, you should name the villages you establish. Thereby you shall serve this great earth.

## \|\| 6.1.38 \|\|

*govarddhane dīrghapure mathurāyāṃ mahāvane \|*  
*nandigrāme bṛhatsānau kāryā rājyasthitistvayā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. You must establish your realm in Govardhana, Dīrghapura, Mathurā, Mahāvana (Great Forest), Nandigrāma and Bṛhatsānu.

## Chapter 2 - Parīkṣit and Others Meet Uddhava

## \|\| 6.2.1 \|\|

*śrīṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*śāṃḍilye tau samādiśya parāvṛtte svamāśramam \|*  
*ki kathaṃ cakratustau tu rājānau sūta tadvada \|\| 1 \|\|*

The glorious sages asked:

1\. When Śāṇḍilya returned to his hermitage after instructing them thus, O Sūta, how and what did those two kings do? Narrate it.

## \|\| 6.2.2 \|\|

*iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīmadbhāgavatamāhātmye govarddhanaparvatasamīpe parīkṣidādīnāmuddhavadarśanavarṇanonāma dvitīyo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Śrī Sūta said:

2\. Thereafter thousands of Śreṇimukhyas (leaders of the guilds of traders, artisans etc.) were brought to Mathurā from Indraprastha by Viṣṇurāta.

## \|\| 6.2.3 \|\|

*māthurānbrāhmaṇāṃstatra vānarāṃśca purātanān \|*  
*vijñāya mānanīyatvaṃ teṣu sthāpitavānsvarādaṭ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. After knowing (from scriptural texts) that the Mathurā Brāhmaṇas were monkeys (? of Rāma) formerly, the Emperor conferred on them special honour and respectability.

## \|\| 6.2.4-6 \|\|

*vajrastu tatsahāyena śāṇḍilyasyā'pyanugrahāt \|*  
*govindagopagopīnāṃ līlāsthānānyanukramāt \|\| 4 \|\|*

*vijñāyā'bhidhayā'sthāpya grāmānāvāsayadbahūn \|*  
*kuṇḍakūpādipūrtena śivādisthāpanena ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

*govindaharidevādisvarūpā'ropaṇena ca \|*  
*kṛṣṇaikabhaktiṃ sve rājyaṃ tatāna ca mumoda ha \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. With his help and the blessings of Śāṇḍilya, Vajra came to know the various spots of the sports of Govinda, the cowherdesses and cowherds. He named them duly and established them. He made many village settlements and colonies. Ponds, wells, lakes and other amenities for the public were constructed. Idols (and Liṅgas) of Śiva and other deities were installed. The images of Govinda, Hari (? Indra) and other Devas were installed. He propagated exclusive devotion to Kṛṣṇa in his realm and rejoiced.

## \|\| 6.2.7 \|\|

*prajāstu muditāstasya kṛṣṇakīrtanatatparāḥ \|*  
*paramānandasampannā rājyaṃ tasyaiva tuṣṭuvuḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The subjects were joyous. His subjects were eagerly engrossed in glorifying Kṛṣṇa. They were endued richly with the greatest bliss. They eulogized his kingdom.

## \|\| 6.2.8 \|\|

*ekadā kṛṣṇapatnyastu śrīkṛṣṇavirahāturāḥ \|*  
*kālindīṃ muditā vīkṣya papracchurgatamatsarāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Once the wives of Kṛṣṇa who were distressed due to separation from him, saw Kālindī rejoicing. Without any jealousy or malice they asked her:

Śrīkṛṣṇa’s wives asked:

## \|\| 6.2.9 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇapatnya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yathā vayaṃ kṛṣṇapatnyastathā tvamapi śobhane \|*  
*vayaṃ virahaduḥkhārtāstvaṃ na kālindi tadvada \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Just as we were the wives of Kṛṣṇa, so you too were, O splendid lady. We are agitated and distressed due to the separation from him, while you are not. Tell (us the reason thereof).

## \|\| 6.2.10 \|\|

*tacchrutvā smayamānā sā kālindī vākyamabravīt \|*  
*sāpatnyaṃ vīkṣya tattāsāṃ karuṇāparamānasā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. On hearing those words and noticing their jealousy, Kālindī mentally pitied them. She smilingly spoke these words:

## \|\| 6.2.11 \|\|

*śrīkālindyuvāca \|*  
*ātmārāmasya kṛṣṇasya dhruvamātmāsti rādhikā \|*  
*tasyā dāsyaprabhāveṇa viraho'smānna saṃspṛśet \|\| 11 \|\|*

Śrī Kālindī said:

11\. Kṛṣṇa is Ātmārāma (i.e. one who rejoices in the Ātman). Certainly Rādhikā is his Ātman. As a result of being her servant, the pangs of separation will not afflict us.

## \|\| 6.2.12 \|\|

*tasyā evāṃśavistārāḥ sarvāḥ śrīkṛṣṇanāyikāḥ \|*  
*nityasaṃbhoga evāsti tasyāḥ sāmmukhyayogataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. All the heroines (beloved ones) of Śrīkṛṣṇa are the extensions of her own parts. There is perpetual union (with Kṛṣṇa) due to our perpetual presence (attendance) near her.

## \|\| 6.2.13 \|\|

*sa eva sā sa saivāsti vaśī tatpremarūpikā \|*  
*śrīkṛṣṇanakhacandrālisaṃgāccandrāvalī smṛtā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. She is he (Kṛṣṇa) himself. He is she (Rādhā) herself. The Vaṃśī (flute) is the form of their love. It is known as Candrāvalī, because it has contact with the moon-like nails of Śrīkṛṣṇa.

## \|\| 6.2.14 \|\|

*rūpāntaraṃ ca gṛhṇānā tayoḥ sevātilālasā \|*  
*rukmiṇyādisamāveśo mayātraiva vilokitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Being ardently desirous of serving them (Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa) both, Rukmiṇī (and other chief queens) assumed another form and entered and got identified with it (the flute, the symbol of the love of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa). I have been witness to it.

\[Or\]:—

(Rukmiṇī and other chief queens were the parts of Rādhā. Where have they gone?) The queens being extremely desirous of serving them (Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa) assumed another form and merged themselves in Rādhā. I have witnessed their merger.

## \|\| 6.2.15 \|\|

*yuṣmākamapi kṛṣṇena viraho naiva sarvataḥ \|*  
*kintu evaṃ na jānītha tasmādvyākulatāmitāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. In your case too there is absolutely no separation from Kṛṣṇa at all. But you do not realize it. Hence, you have become agitated and distressed.

## \|\| 6.2.16 \|\|

*evamevātra gopīnāmakrūrāvasare purā \|*  
*virahābhāsa evāsīduddhavena samāhitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Formerly, at the time of the arrival of Akrūra the cowherdesses too experienced an apparent separation. But it was dispelled (and the Gopīs) were pacified by Uddhava.

## \|\| 6.2.17 \|\|

*tenaiva bhavatīnāṃ cedbhavedatra samāgamaḥ \|*  
*tarhi nityaṃ svakāntena vihāramapi lapsyatha \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. If you come into contact with him alone here, you can have perpetual sport with your lover.

## \|\| 6.2.18 \|\|

*śrīsūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktāstu tāḥ patnyaḥ prasannāṃ punarabruvan \|*  
*uddhavālokanenātmapreṣṭhasaṃgamalālasāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

Śrī Sūta said:

18\. On being told thus, those wives (of Śrīkṛṣṇa) became eager to come into contact with their lover after seeing Uddhava. They spoke again (to Kālindī) who was delighted.

## \|\| 6.2.19 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇapatnya ūcuḥ \|*  
*dhanyāsi sakhi kāntena yasyā naivāsti vicyutiḥ \|*  
*yataste svārthasaṃsiddhistasyā dāsyo babhūvima \|\| 19 \|\|*

Śrīkṛṣṇa’s wives said:

19\. Blessed are you, O friend, since you have no separation from your lover. We would have become the servants of (that lady) through whom you have achieved your purpose.

## \|\| 6.2.20 \|\|

*parantūddhavalābhe syādasmatsarvārthasādhanam \|*  
*tathā vadasva kālindi tallābho'pi yathā bhavet \|\| 20 \|\|*

Śrī Sūta said:

20\. But, should we meet Uddhava, all our objects will be realized. Hence, O Kālindī, tell that means whereby we can meet him (Uddhava).

## \|\| 6.2.21 \|\|

*śrīsūta uvāca \|*  
*evamuktā tu kālindī pratyuvācātha tāstathā \|*  
*smarantī kṛṣṇacandrasya kalāṣoḍaśarūpiṇī \|\| 21 \|\|*

Śrī Sūta said:

21\. On being told thus, Kālindī remembered the sixteen Kalās of Kṛṣṇa resembling the Moon and then replied to them:

## \|\| 6.2.22 \|\|

*sādhanabhūmirbadarī vrajatā kṛṣṇena maṃtriṇe proktā \|*  
*tatrāste sa tu sākṣāttadvayunaṃ grāhayaṃllokān \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. “While going (to Vaikuṇṭha) Kṛṣṇa said to his minister (Uddhava) that Badarī (Badarikāśrama) was the land of preparation (penance) for obtaining an object. He stays there in the visible form imparting knowledge (about Kṛṣṇa).

## \|\| 6.2.23 \|\|

*phalabhūmirvrajabhūmirdattā tasmai puraiva sarahasyam \|*  
*phalamiha tirohitaṃ sattadihedānīṃ sa uddhavo'lakṣyaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The land of Vraja is the land of fruition (enjoying fruits) of the penance. It has been formerly given to him along with its secrets. The fruit (i.e. Kṛṣṇa) is invisible (regarding place of Rāsa etc.). So Uddhava stays here invisible now.

## \|\| 6.2.24 \|\|

*govarddhanagirinikaṭe sakhīsthale tadrajaḥkāmaḥ \|*  
*tatratyāṅkuravallīrūpeṇāste sa uddhavo nūnam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Near the Govardhana mountain, in the Sakhīsthala (? in the spot of Kṛṣṇa’s friends—Gopīs) Uddhava is indeed present in the form of sprouts and creepers, because he is desirous of their dust particles.

## \|\| 6.2.25-27 \|\|

*ātmotsavarūpatvaṃ hariṇā tasmai samarpitaṃ niyatam \|*  
*tasmāttatra sthitvā kusumasaraḥparisare savajrābhiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*vīṇāveṇumṛdaṃgaiḥ kīrtanakāvyādisarasasaṃgītaiḥ \|*  
*utsava ārabdhavyo hariratalokānsamānāyya \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tatroddhavāvaloko bhavitā niyataṃ mahotsave vitate \|*  
*yauṣmākīṇāmabhimatasiddhiṃ savitā sa eva savitānām \|\| 27 \|\|*

25-27. The form of his own festival has been definitely transferred to him by Hari. Hence all of you, along with Vajra should stay in the neighbourhood of Kusumasaras (Flower-Lake). You must bring together all the persons ardently attached to Hari and the festival should be begun (celebrated), with recitation (of Hari’s glory), sweet songs and musical instruments like lute, flute and Mṛdaṅga drums.

When the great festival is being elaborately celebrated, you will definitely meet Uddhava. That meeting will surely result in the complete attainment of your desired objects.”

## \|\| 6.2.28 \|\|

*śrīsūta uvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā prasannāstāḥ kālindīmabhivandya tat \|*  
*kathayāmāsurāgatya vajraṃ prati parīkṣitam \|\| 28 \|\|*

Śrī Sūta said:

28\. On hearing this they became delighted. They saluted Kālindī and returned. They reported everything to Vajra and Parīkṣit.

## \|\| 6.2.29 \|\|

*viṣṇurātastu tacchrutvā prasannastadyutastadā \|*  
*tatraivāgatya tatsarvaṃ kārayāmāsa satvaram \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. On hearing it, Viṣṇurāta (i.e. Parīkṣit) became pleased. Accompanied by them he went to that place and got everything performed immediately.

## \|\| 6.2.30 \|\|

*govardhanādadūreṇa vṛndāraṇye sakhīsthale \|*  
*pravṛttaḥ kusumāmbhodhau kṛṣṇasaṃkīrtanotsavaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The festival of the glorification of Kṛṣṇa began at the Flower-Lake in the spot Sakhīsthala in the Vṛndāvana forest not far from Govardhana.

## \|\| 6.2.31 \|\|

*vṛṣabhānusutākāntavihāre kīrtanaśriyā \|*  
*sākṣādiva samāvṛtte sarve'nanyadṛśo'bhavan \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. When the actual dance (and other sports) of the lover of the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu revived once again on account of the power of Kṛṣṇa (glorification of Kṛṣṇa), all had their eyes (fixed on him only) turned to nothing else.

## \|\| 6.2.32 \|\|

*tataḥ paśyatsu sarveṣu tṛṇagulmalatācayāt \|*  
*ājagāmoddhavaḥ sragvī śyāmaḥ pītāmbarāvṛtaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Then, even as all of them were watching, Uddhava emerged from the cluster of grasses, creepers and hedges. He was dark in complexion with garlands (round his neck) and was clad in yellow robes.

## \|\| 6.2.33-34 \|\|

*guñjāmālādharo gāyanballavīvallabhaṃ muhuḥ \|*  
*tadāgamanato reje bhṛśaṃ saṃkīrtanotsavaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*candrikāgamato yadvatsphāṭikāṭṭālabhūmaṇiḥ \|*  
*atha sarve sukhāmbhodhau magnāḥ sarvaṃ visasmaruḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. He had garlands of Guñjā (a red and black berry). He was repeatedly singing the glory of the lover of the cowherd lasses. When he came, the festival of glorification became very much graceful like the crystals on the attics and terraces when the moon rises. AH of them were immersed in the ocean of bliss. All of them forgot (everything else).

## Chapter 3 - Dialogue between Parīkṣit and Uddhava

## \|\| 6.3.1 \|\|

*śrīsūta uvāca \|*  
*athoddhavastu tāndṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇakīrtanatatparān \|*  
*satkṛtyātha pariṣvajya parīkṣitamuvāca ha \|\| 1 \|\|*

Śrī Sūta said:

1\. On observing them eagerly engaged in glorifying Kṛṣṇa, Uddhava received them ardently, embraced Parīkṣit and said:

## \|\| 6.3.2 \|\|

*uddhava uvāca \|*  
*dhanyo'si rājankṛṣṇaikabhaktyā pūrṇo'si nityadā \|*  
*yastvaṃ nimagnacitto'si kṛṣṇasaṃkīrtanotsave \|\| 2 \|\|*

Uddhava said:

2\. O king, you are full of devotion solely to Kṛṣṇa. You are continuously engrossed in the festival of the glorification of Śrīkṛṣṇa. Indeed you are blessed!

## \|\| 6.3.3 \|\|

*iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe parīkṣiduddhavasaṃvāde śrībhāgavatamāhātmye tṛtīyo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O dear one, the power of your limbs was granted to you by Kṛṣṇa (Kṛṣṇa resuscitated your life). Hence this is befitting unto you. Fortunately you have evinced your affection for the wives of Kṛṣṇa and also for Vajra.

## \|\| 6.3.4 \|\|

*dvārakāstheṣu sarveṣu dhanyā ete na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*yeṣāṃ vrajanivāsāya pārthamādiṣṭavānprabhuḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Among all those residents of Dvārakā, blessed are all those who were asked to migrate to Vraja by the Lord by instructing Pārtha (to settle them there).

## \|\| 6.3.5 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇasya manaścaṃdro rādhāsyaprabhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*tadvihāravanaṃ gobhirmaṇḍayanrocate sadā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Like the moon, the mind of Śrīkṛṣṇa, accompanied by the refulgence of the face of Rādhā, always shines, beautifying that forest of sports by means of its rays.

## \|\| 6.3.6 \|\|

*kṛṣṇacandraḥ sadā pūrṇastasya ṣoḍaśa yāḥ kalāḥ \|*  
*citsahasraprabhābhinnā atrāste tatsvarūpatā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Moon, is always full. His sixteen digits are non-different from the refulgence of thousands of Cits (Gopīs or Kṛṣṇa’s queens). Here his form and likeness exist.

## \|\| 6.3.7 \|\|

*evaṃ vajrastu rājendra prapannabhayabhañjakaḥ \|*  
*śrīkṛṣṇadakṣiṇe pāde sthānametasya vartate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thus, O eminent king, Vajra is the dispeller of the fear of those who resort to him. His place is at the right foot of Śrīkṛṣṇa. (This suggests the Vajra mark on Kṛṣṇa’s sole.).

## \|\| 6.3.8 \|\|

*avatāre'tra kṛṣṇena yogamāyā'ti bhāvitā \|*  
*tadbalenātmavismṛtyā sīdantyete na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In this incarnation, the Yogic Māyā was very much displayed by Kṛṣṇa. O n account of its power all these are undoubtedly languishing with self-oblivion (forgetting their own nature).

## \|\| 6.3.9 \|\|

*ṛte kṛṣṇaprakāśaṃ tu svātmabodho na kasyacit \|*  
*tatprakāśastu jīvānāṃ māyayā pihitaḥ sadā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Without the light of Kṛṣṇa no one shall have self-enlightenment. That light is always hidden by Māyā in the case of the individual souls.

## \|\| 6.3.10 \|\|

*aṣṭāviṃśe dvāparānte svayameva yadā hariḥ \|*  
*utsārayennijāṃ māyāṃ tatprakāśo bhavettadā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Towards the end of the twenty-eighth Dvāpara, when Hari himself would remove his own Māyā, that light could be manifested.

## \|\| 6.3.11 \|\|

*sa tu kālo vyatikrāṃtastenedamaparaṃ śṛṇu \|*  
*anyadā tatprakāśastu śrīmadbhāgavatādbhavet \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. That time has passed off. Therefore, listen to this other suggestion. On other occasions, that light can issue forth from Śrīmadbhāgavata.

## \|\| 6.3.12 \|\|

*śrīmadbhāgavataṃ śāstraṃ yatra bhāgavatairyadā \|*  
*kīrtyate śrūyate cāpi śrīkṛṣṇastatra niścitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Certainly Śrīkṛṣṇa is present at that place and time where! and when the scripture Śrīmadbhāgavata is expounded and listened to by Bhāgavatas (devotees, followers of the Lord).

## \|\| 6.3.13 \|\|

*śrīmadbhāgavataṃ yatra ślokaṃ ślokārddhameva ca \|*  
*tatrāpi bhagavānkṛṣṇo ballavībhirvirājate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Lord Kṛṣṇa graces that place also along with the cowherd lasses—the place where a verse of Śrīmadbhāgavata or half of it is present.

## \|\| 6.3.14 \|\|

*bhārate mānavaṃ janma prāpya bhāgavataṃ na yaiḥ \|*  
*śrutaṃ pāpaparādhīnairātmaghātastu taiḥ kṛtaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. If, after being born as human beings in Bhārata, people have not heard about Bhāgavata, self-murder has been committed by them.

## \|\| 6.3.15 \|\|

*śrīmadbhāgavataṃ śāstraṃ nityaṃ yaiḥ parisevitam \|*  
*piturmātuśca bhāryāyāḥ kulapaṃktiḥ sutāritā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The lines of families of their father, mother and wife have been redeemed by the people who have continuously resorted to the (study, recitation of or listening to) the scripture Śrīmadbhāgavata.

## \|\| 6.3.16 \|\|

*vidyāprakāśo viprāṇāṃ rājāṃ śatrujayo viśām \|*  
*dhanaṃ svāsthyaṃ ca śūdrāṇāṃ śrīmadbhāgavatādbhavet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. From Śrīmadbhāgavata Brāhmaṇas will derive the enlightenment of learning, kings victory over their enemies, Vaiśyas plenty of wealth and Śūdras good health.

## \|\| 6.3.17 \|\|

*yoṣitāmapareṣāṃ ca sarvavāṃchitapūraṇam \|*  
*ato bhāgavataṃ nityaṃ ko na seveta bhāgyavān \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Women and other people shall obtain the realization of their desires. So which fortunate man will not continuously resort to Bhāgavata?

## \|\| 6.3.18 \|\|

*anekajanmasaṃsiddhaḥ śrīmadbhāgavataṃ labhet \|*  
*prakāśo bhagavadbhakterudbhavastatra jāyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. It iṣ only after fruition of the merits of many births that a person can obtain Śrīmadbhāgavata. Enlightenment and devotion to God result herefrom.

## \|\| 6.3.19 \|\|

*sāṃkhyāyanaprasādāptaṃ śrīmadbhāgavataṃ purā \|*  
*bṛhaspatirdattavānme tenāhaṃ kṛṣṇavallabhaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Formerly Śrīmadbhāgavata was obtained by Bṛhaspati through the grace of Sāṃkhyāyana. Bṛhaspati imparted it to me. Therefore, I am a lover of Kṛṣṇa.

## \|\| 6.3.20 \|\|

*ākhyāyikā ca tenoktā viṣṇurāta nibodha tām \|*  
*jñāyate saṃpradāyo'pi yatra bhāgavataśruteḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O Viṣṇurāta, know the anecdote told by him. In it the traditional (mode) of listening to Bhāgavata (is also obtained).

## \|\| 6.3.21-24 \|\|

*śrībṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*īkṣāṃcakre yadā kṛṣṇo māyāpuruṣarūpadhṛk \|*  
*brahmā viṣṇuḥ śivaścāpi rajaḥsattvatamoguṇaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*puruṣāstraya uttasthuradhikārāṃstadādiśat \|*  
*utpattau pālane caiva saṃhāre prakrameṇa tān \|\| 22 \|\|*

*brahmā tu nābhikamalādutpannastaṃ vyajijñapat \|*  
*śrībrahmovāca \|*  
*nārāyaṇādipuruṣa paramātmannamo'stu te \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tvayā sarge niyukto'smi pāpīyānmāṃ rajoguṇaḥ \|*  
*tvatsmṛtau naiva bādheta tathaiva kṛpayā prabho \|\| 24 \|\|*

Śrī Bṛhaspati said:

21 -23a. When Kṛṣṇa who had assumed the form of Māyāpuruṣa was beholding, three Puruṣas, viz. Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva rose up with the Guṇas Rajas, Sattva and Tamas. (The Lord) then employed them in the work of creation, sustenance and annihilation respectively. Brahmā who was born of the lotus at his navel, submitted to him:

Brahmā said:

23b-24. O Nārāyaṇa, O Primordial Being, O Supreme Ātman, I offer obeisance to you. I have been engaged in the work of creation by you. Take pity on me lest the evil Rajas Guṇa should obstruct me while remembering you.

## \|\| 6.3.25-27 \|\|

*śrībṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*yadā tu bhagavāṃstasmai śrīmadbhāgavataṃ purā \|*  
*upadiśyābravīdbrahmansevasvainatsvasiddhaye \|\| 25 \|\|*

*brahmā tu paramaprītastena kṛṣṇāptaye'niśam \|*  
*saptāvaraṇabhaṃgāya saptāhaṃ samavartayat \|\| 26 \|\|*

*śrībhāgavatasaptāhasevanāptamanorathaḥ \|*  
*sṛṣṭiṃ vitanute nityaṃ sasaptāhaḥ punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

Śrī Bṛhaspati said:

25-27. Formerly the Lord imparted Śrīmadbhāgavata to him and

advised him in the following words: “O Brahmā, resort to this for the sake of your Siddhi.” Thereupon, Brahmā became exceedingly pleased. Therefore, in order to attain Kṛṣṇa permanently and to break through the seven Āvaraṇas (coverings) (viz. two of auspicious and inauspicious Karmas plus five of Avidyā), he spent seven days. By resorting to (reading) Śrīmadbhāgavata for seven days he realized his desire. He continues to create again and again resorting to the Saptāha (i.e. study/reading/expounding spread over seven days) of Bhāgavata.

## \|\| 6.3.28 \|\|

*viṣṇurapyarthayāmāsa pumāṃsaṃ svārthasiddhaye \|*  
*prajānāṃ pālane puṃsā yadanenāpi kalpitaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Viṣṇu too requested the Puruṣa for the accomplishment of his purpose, since the work of protecting the subjects had been allotted to him by the Puruṣa.

## \|\| 6.3.29-32 \|\|

*śrīviṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*prajānāṃ pālanaṃ deva kariṣyāmi yathocitam \|*  
*pravṛttyā ca nivṛttyā ca karmajñānaprayojanāt \|\| 29 \|\|*

*yadāyadaiva kālena dharmaglānirbhaviṣyati \|*  
*dharmaṃ saṃsthāpayiṣyāmi hyavatāraistadā tadā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*bhogārthibhyastu yajñādiphalaṃ dāsyāmi niścitam \|*  
*mokṣārthibhyo viraktebhyo muktiṃ pañcavidhāṃ tathā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*ye'pi mokṣaṃ na vāñchanti tānkathaṃ pālayāmyaham \|*  
*ātmānaṃ ca śriyaṃ cāpi pālayāmi kathaṃ vada \|\| 32 \|\|*

Śrī Viṣṇu said:

29-32. O Lord, I shall carry on the protection of the subjects in a suitable manner by means of Pravṛtti (active engagement) and Nivṛtti (renunciation) of Karma as well as Jñāna (perfect knowledge).

In course of time, whenever there is decline of Dharma, I shall reestablish it by means of incarnations (such as Divine Fish, Tortoise). I shall certainly grant the benefit of Yajñas to those who seek worldly pleasures. To those who are devoid of attachment and who seek salvation, I shall accord salvation of five types, viz. (1) stay in the same region, (2) similarity of power, (3) vicinity to God, (4) similarity of form, (5) identity with God. But, how shall I protect those people who do not desire salvation too? How shall I protect myself and Śrī (goddess Lakṣmī)? Tell me.

## \|\| 6.3.33 \|\|

*tasmā api pumānādyaḥ śrībhāgavatamādiśat \|*  
*uvāca ca paṭhasvainattava sarvārthasiddhaye \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The primordial Being imparted Śrīmadbhāgavata to him too and said: “Read this for the sake of realizing all your objectives.”

## \|\| 6.3.34-35 \|\|

*tato viṣṇuḥ prasannātmā paramārthakapālane \|*  
*samartho'bhūcchriyā māsimāsi bhāgavataṃ smaran \|\| 34 \|\|*

*yadā viṣṇuḥ svayaṃ vaktā lakṣmīśca śravaṇe ratā \|*  
*tadā bhāgavataśrāvo māsenaiva punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. Thereupon, Viṣṇu became delighted in his mind. Remembering Bhāgavata every month (i.e. reading fully once) along with Śrī, he became capable of protecting (the subjects) genuinely.

When Viṣṇu himself is the expounder and Lakṣmī is engaged in listening, the duration of the process is one month.

## \|\| 6.3.36 \|\|

*yadā lakṣmīḥ svayaṃ vaktrī viṣṇuśca śravaṇe rataḥ \|*  
*māsadvayaṃ rasāsvādastadātīva suśobhate \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. When Lakṣmī herself expounds and Viṣṇu is engaged in listening, the duration of enjoying its contents is two months.

## \|\| 6.3.37 \|\|

*adhikāre sthito viṣṇurlakṣmīrniścintamānasā \|*  
*tena bhāgavatāsvādastasyā bhūri prakāśate \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Viṣṇu is officially engaged in his duty; but Lakṣmī is mentally carefree. Hence her exposition of Bhāgavata is better.

## \|\| 6.3.38 \|\|

*atha rudro'pi taṃ devaṃ saṃhārādhikṛtaḥ purā \|*  
*pumāṃsaṃ prārthayāmāsa svasāmarthyavivṛddhaye \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Rudra too who was formerly engaged in the duty of annihilation, requested that Lord Puruṣa for the sake of enhancing his ability.

## \|\| 6.3.39-40 \|\|

*śrīrudra uvāca \|*  
*nitye naimittike caiva saṃhāre prākṛte tathā \|*  
*śaktayo mama vidyante devadeva mama prabho \|\| 39 \|\|*

*ātyaṃtike tu saṃhāre mama śaktirna vidyate \|*  
*mahadduḥkhaṃ mamaitattu tena tvāṃ prārthayāmyaham \|\| 40 \|\|*

Śrī Rudra said:

39-40. O Lord of Devas, O my Lord, I have ample power in the case of the annihilation of Nitya (daily), Naimittika (occasional) and Prākṛta (pertaining to Prakṛti) types. But I do not have any power in regard to Ātyantika (ultimate) annihilation. On account of this, I am very unhappy; therefore, I request you.

## \|\| 6.3.41 \|\|

*śrībṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*śrīmadbhāgavataṃ tasmā api nārāyaṇo dadau \|*  
*sa tu saṃsevanādasya jigye cāpi tamoguṇam \|\| 41 \|\|*

Śrī Bṛhaspati said:

41\. Nārāyaṇa imparted Śrīmadbhāgavata to him also. By resorting to it, he conquered the Tamas Guṇa.

## \|\| 6.3.42 \|\|

*kathā bhāgavatī tena sevitā varṣamātrataḥ \|*  
*laye tvātyaṃtike tenāvāpa śaktiṃ sadāśivaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The story of Bhāgavata was resorted to (read) by him for a period of one year. Thereby Sadāśiva obtained the power (to manage) the ultimate annihilation as well.

## \|\| 6.3.43-44 \|\|

*uddhava uvāca \|*  
*śrībhāgavatamāhātmya imāmākhyāyikāṃ guroḥ \|*  
*śrutvā bhāgavataṃ labdhvā mumude'haṃ praṇamya tam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tatastu vaiṣṇavīṃ rītiṃ gṛhītvā māsamātrataḥ \|*  
*śrīmadbhāgavatāsvādo mayā samyaṅniṣevitaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

Uddhava said:

43-44. On hearing this narrative in regard to the greatness of Śrīmadbhāgavata from my preceptor (from Bṛhaspati) and on getting the Bhāgavata text, I rejoiced much and I bowed down to him. Therefore, I adopted the procedure of the Vaiṣṇavas and for full one month Śrīmadbhāgavata was ardently resorted to by me.

## \|\| 6.3.45-46 \|\|

*tāvataiva babhūvāhaṃ kṛṣṇasya dayitaḥ sakhā \|*  
*kṛṣṇenātha niyukto'haṃ vraje svapreyasīgaṇe \|\| 45 \|\|*

*virahārttāsu gopīṣu svayaṃ nityavihāriṇā \|*  
*śrībhāgavatasaṃdeśo manmukhena prayojitaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. By that alone I became the beloved companion of Kṛṣṇa. Then I was sent with an errand to Vraja to the group of his beloved ones.

The Lord continued to be perpetually sporting even while the cowherd lasses were in agony due to the separation. The message of Śrīmadbhāgavata was sent over to them through me.

## \|\| 6.3.47 \|\|

*taṃ yathāmati labdhvā tā āsanvirahavarjjitāḥ \|*  
*nājñāsiṣaṃ rahasyaṃ taccamatkārastu lokitaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. After receiving it in accordance with their intellectual capacity, they became free from the pangs of separation. I could not know the secret thereof. But the miracle was seen.

## \|\| 6.3.48 \|\|

*svarvāsaṃ prārthya kṛṣṇaṃ ca brahmādyeṣu gateṣu me \|*  
*śrīmadbhāgavate kṛṣṇastadrahasyaṃ svayaṃ dadau \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. After requesting Kṛṣṇa for his stay in heaven, Brahmā and others went away. Then Śrīkṛṣṇa himself gave me that secret in Bhāgavata.

## \|\| 6.3.49 \|\|

*purato'śvatthamūlasya cakāra mayi taddṛḍham \|*  
*tenātra vrajavallīṣu vasāmi badarīṃ gataḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. In front of the root of Aśvattha (Pippla tree) he made it firmly fixed in me. Therefore, having gone to Badarī I stay here in the creepers of Vraja.

## \|\| 6.3.50 \|\|

*tasmānnāradakuṇḍe'tra tiṣṭhāmi svecchayā sadā \|*  
*kṛṣṇaprakāśo bhaktānāṃ śrīmadbhāgavatādbhavet \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. So I stay always as I please in the Nārada Kuṇḍa here. Devotees will get the knowledge of Kṛṣṇa from Śrīmadbhāgavata.

## \|\| 6.3.51 \|\|

*tadeṣāmapi kāryyārthaṃ śrīmadbhāgavataṃ tvaham \|*  
*pravakṣyāmi sahāyo'tra tvayaivānuṣṭhito bhavet \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Therefore, for the sake of these, I shall expound Śrīmadbhāgavata. In this matter you should assist me.

## \|\| 6.3.52-53 \|\|

*śrīsūta uvāca \|*  
*viṣṇurātastu śrutvā taduddhavaṃ praṇato'bravīt \|*  
*śrīparīkṣiduvāca \|*  
*haridāsa tvayā kāryyaṃ śrībhāgavatakīrtanam \|\| 52 \|\|*

*ājñāpyo'haṃ yathākāryyaṃ sahāyo'tra mayā tathā \|*  
*śrīsūta uvāca \|*  
*śrutvaitaduddhavo vākyamuvāca prītamānasaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

Śrī Sūta said:

52a. On hearing it, Viṣṇurāta bowed down to Uddhava and said:

Śrī Parīkṣit said:

52b-53a. O servant of Hari, Śrīmadbhāgavata must be glorified by you (expounded by you). I may be commanded to assist you in any task that can be done by me.

Śrī Sūta said:

53b. On hearing this Uddhava was delighted in his mind. He spoke these words:

## \|\| 6.3.54-56 \|\|

*uddhava uvāca \|*  
*śrīkṛṣṇena parityakte bhūtale balavānkaliḥ \|*  
*kariṣyati paraṃ vighnaṃ satkārye samupasthite \|\| 54 \|\|*

*tasmāddigvijayaṃ yāhi kalinigrahamācara \|*  
*ahaṃ tu māsamātreṇa vaiṣṇavīṃ rītimāsthitaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*śrīmadbhāgavatāsvādaṃ pracārya tvatsahāyataḥ \|*  
*etānsamprāpayiṣyāmi nityadhāmni madhudviṣaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

Uddhava said:

54-56. When the earth is left behind by Śrīkṛṣṇa, the powerful Kali will create great obstacles whenever any good work is started. Hence proceed on a campaign of conquest of the quarters. Restrain and subdue Kali. I shall adopt the procedure of the Vaiṣṇavas and in the course of a month spread the gospel of Śrīmadbhāgavata with your assistance. Thereby, I shall enable these to attain the permanent abode of the Slayer of Madhu.

## \|\| 6.3.57 \|\|

*śrīsūta uvāca \|*  
*śrutvaivaṃ tadvaco rājā muditaścintayāturaḥ \|*  
*tadā vijñāpayāmāsa svābhiprāyaṃ tamuddhavam \|\| 57 \|\|*

Śrī Sūta said:

57\. On hearing his words, the king was joyous as well as worried (a little). Then he intimated to Uddhava his own opinion.

## \|\| 6.3.58-59 \|\|

*śrīparīkṣiduvāca \|*  
*kaliṃ tu nigrahīṣyāmi tāta te vacasi sthitaḥ \|*  
*śrībhāgavatasaṃprāptiḥ kathaṃ mama bhaviṣyati \|\| 58 \|\|*

*ahaṃ tu samanugrāhyastava pādatale śritaḥ \|*  
*śrīsūta uvāca \|*  
*śrutvaitadvacanaṃ bhūyo'pyuddhavastamuvāca ha \|\| 59 \|\|*

Śrī Parīkṣit said:

58-59. O dear one, at your behest I shall restrain and subdue Kali. But how will I attain (the benefit) of Śrībhāgavata? I have resorted to your feet. I am to be blessed.

## \|\| 6.3.60 \|\|

*uddhava uvāca \|*  
*rājaṃścintā tu te kā'pi naiva kāryyā kathaṃcana \|*  
*tavaiva bhagavacchāstre yato mukhyādhikāritā \|\| 60 \|\|*

Śrī Sūta said:

On heari ng these words Uddhava said to him once again:

Uddhava said:

60\. O king, no anxiety or worry need to entertained by you at all, since the most important person authorized in the scripture of the Lord is you yourself.

## \|\| 6.3.61 \|\|

*etāvatkālaparyyantaṃ prāyo bhāgavataśruteḥ \|*  
*vārtāmapi na jānanti manuṣyāḥ karmatatparāḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Till this time men devoted to Karma have not even news whatsoever of the holy text of Bhāgavata.

## \|\| 6.3.62 \|\|

*tvatprasādena bahavo manuṣyā bhāratājire \|*  
*śrīmadbhāgavataprāptau sukhaṃ prāpsyanti śāśvatam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. With your favour in the region of Bhārata many men will attain permanent happiness after the acquisition of (hearing) Śrīmadbhāgavata.

## \|\| 6.3.63 \|\|

*nandanandanarūpastu śrīśuko bhagavānṛṣiḥ \|*  
*śrīmadbhāgavataṃ tubhyaṃ śrāvayiṣyatyasaṃśayaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. The great holy sage Śrīśuka who is in the form of Lord Kṛṣṇa himself will undoubtedly recount to you Śrīmadbhāgavata.

## \|\| 6.3.64 \|\|

*tena prāpsyasi rājaṃstvaṃ nityaṃ dhāma vrajeśituḥ \|*  
*śrībhāgavatasaṃcārastato bhuvi bhaviṣyati \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Thereby, O king, you will attain the eternal abode of the Lord of Vraja. Thereafter, Śrīmadbhāgavata will begin to spread on the earth.

## \|\| 6.3.65 \|\|

*tasmāttvaṃ gaccha rājendra kalinigrahamācara \|*  
*śrīsūta uvāca \|*  
*ityuktastaṃ parikramya gato rājā diśāṃ jaye \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Hence, O great king, go. Restrain and subdue Kali.

## \|\| 6.3.66 \|\|

*vajrastu nijarājyeśaṃ pratibāhuṃ vidhāya ca \|*  
*tatraiva mātṛbhiḥ sākaṃ tasthau bhāgavatāśayā \|\| 66 \|\|*

Śrī Sūta said:

On being told thus, the king circumambulated him and went for the conquest of the quarters.

66\. Vajra made Pratibāhu the lord of his own kingdom. Hoping to secure Bhāgavata, he remained there itself along with the mothers.

## \|\| 6.3.67 \|\|

*atha vṛndāvane māsaṃ govarddhanasamīpataḥ \|*  
*śrīmadbhāgavatāsvādastūddhavena pravartitaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Then in Vṛndāvana near Govardhana the joyful exposition of Śrīmadbhāgavata lasting for a month was inaugurated by Uddhava.

## \|\| 6.3.68-71 \|\|

*tasminnāsvādyamāne tu saccidānandarūpiṇī \|*  
*pracakāśe harerlīlā sarvataḥ kṛṣṇa eva ca \|\| 68 \|\|*

*ātmānaṃ ca tadantaḥsthaṃ sarve'pi dadṛśustadā \|*  
*vajrastu dakṣiṇe dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇapādasaroruhe \|\| 69 \|\|*

*svātmānaṃ kṛṣṇavaidhuryyānmuktastadbhuvyaśobhata \|*  
*tāśca tanmātaraḥ kṛṣṇe rāsarātriprakāśini \|\| 70 \|\|*

*caṃdre kalāprabhārūpamātmānaṃ vīkṣya vismitāḥ \|*  
*svapreṣṭha virahavyādhivimuktāḥ svapadaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

68-71. While the gospel (of Bhāgavata) was being enjoyed, Hari’s Līlā (sport) in the form of existence, knowledge and bliss manifested everywhere. So also Kṛṣṇa. All people saw themselves stationed within him. On seeing himself in the lotus-like right foot of Kṛṣṇa, Vajra was rid of the pangs of separation from Kṛṣṇa. He shone on that ground. The mothers were amazed on seeing themselves as refulgence of the digits in Kṛṣṇa, the moon shining on the night of Rāsa dance. Liberated from the ailment of separation from their dearest beloved, they went over to their own region.

## \|\| 6.3.72-73 \|\|

*ye'nye ca tatra te sarve nityalīlāntaraṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*vyāvahārikalokebhyaḥ sadyo'darśanamāgatāḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*govarddhananikuñjeṣu goṣu vṛndāvanādiṣu \|*  
*nityaṃ kṛṣṇena modante dṛśyante prematatparaiḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

72-73. Others too who were there entered the eternal Līlā (graceful sports). Immediately they became invisible to the ordinary world of everyday life.

They rejoice continuously with Kṛṣṇa in the bowers of Govardhana, in the (middle of the) cows, in Vṛndāvana etc. They are seen by persons who love and who are devoted to them.

## Chapter 4 - The Recitation of Bhāgavata

## \|\| 6.4.1-2 \|\|

*śrīṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*sādhu sūta ciraṃ jīva ciramevaṃ praśādhi naḥ \|*  
*śrībhāgavatamāhātmyamapūrvaṃ tvansukhācchrutam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tatsvarūpapramāṇaṃ ca vidhiṃ ca śravaṇe vada \|*  
*tadvakturlakṣaṇaṃ sūta śrotuścāpi vadādhunā \|\| 2 \|\|*

The glorious sages said:

1-2. Well done! O Sūta, live long! Guide us like this for a long time. The unprecedented greatness of Śrībhāgavata has been heard directly from your mouth.

Tell us its form, its extent and the mode of listening to it. O Sūta, tell us the qualification of its expounder as well as of the listener now.

## \|\| 6.4.3 \|\|

*śrīsūta uvāca \|*  
*śrīmadbhāgavatasyātha śrīmadbhagavataḥ sadā \|*  
*svarūpamekamevāsti saccidānandalakṣaṇam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Śrī Sūta said:

3\. Identical is the form of Śrīmadbhāgavata as well as of the glorious Lord. It is characterized by existence, knowledge and bliss.

## \|\| 6.4.4 \|\|

*iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīmadbhāgavatamāhātmye caturtho'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Know that Bhāgavata is that statement which spreads out and expands, manifesting to the devotees of Śrīkṛṣṇa the sweetness of (the devotion to or the life of) Śrīkṛṣṇa.

## \|\| 6.4.5 \|\|

*jñānavijñānabhaktyaṅgacatuṣṭayaparaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*māyāmardana dakṣaṃ ca viddhi bhāgavataṃ ca tat \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Know that statement to be Bhāgavata which treats of the four (topics), viz. (scriptural) knowledge, experience or realization thereof, devotion (characterised by Love of God) and its auxiliaries (viz. Śravaṇa-hearing, Kīrtana-glorification of God etc.) and is capable of suppressing Māyā.

## \|\| 6.4.6 \|\|

*pramāṇaṃ tasya ko veda hyanaṃtasyākṣarātmanaḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇe hariṇā taddikcatuḥślokyā pradarśitā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Who can know the extent of Bhāgavata, the form of which is characterised by infinity and imperishability? Its direction was shown to God Brahmā in four verses by Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 6.4.7 \|\|

*tadānaṃtyāvagāhena svepsitāvahanakṣamāḥ \|*  
*ta eva saṃti bho viprā brahmaviṣṇuśivādayaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O Brāhmaṇa, only those, i.e. Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva etc. are

capable of realizing their desires by plunging deeply into his infinite nature (and not people like us).

## \|\| 6.4.8-9 \|\|

*mitabuddhyādivṛttīnāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ hitāya ca \|*  
*parīkṣicchukasaṃvādo yo'sau vyāsena kīrtitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*grantho'ṣṭādaśasāhasro yo'sau bhāgavatābhidhaḥ \|*  
*kaligrāhagṛhītānāṃ sa eva paramāśrayaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. In the case of human beings of limited intellectual and other capacities, the dialogue between Śuka and Parīkṣit, as described by Vyāsa, is conducive to their welfare. It is a sacred text of eighteen thousand verses as composed by Vyāsa. It alone is the greatest support to those who are caught by the crocodile in the form of Kali.

## \|\| 6.4.10 \|\|

*śrotāro 'tha nirūpyante śrīmadviṣṇukathāśrayāḥ \|*  
*pravarā avarāścati śrotāro dvividhā matāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The listeners of the holy anecdotes of Viṣṇu are now ascertained. The listeners are considered to be of two types: the Pravaras (the superior ones) and the Avaras (the inferior ones).

## \|\| 6.4.11 \|\|

*pravarāścātako haṃsaḥ śuko mīnādayastathā \|*  
*avarā vṛkabhūruṇḍavṛṣoṣṭrādyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The Pravaras are Cātakas (ruddy geese), swans, parrots, fish etc. Wolves, Bhūruṇḍa birds, bulls, camels etc. are said to be Avaras.

## \|\| 6.4.12 \|\|

*akhilopekṣayā yastu kṛṣṇaśāstraśrutau vratī \|*  
*sa cātako yathāmbhodamukte pāthasi cātakaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. If a person discards all other sacred works and takes to the vow of listening to Kṛṣṇa Śāstra (scriptural texts belonging to Kṛṣṇa), he is Cātaka (like the ruddy goose) which is solely dependent on the water released by clouds.

## \|\| 6.4.13 \|\|

*haṃsaḥ syātsāramādatte yaḥ śrotā vividhācchrutāt \|*  
*dugdhenaikyaṃ gatāttoyādyathā haṃso'malaṃ payaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The Haṃsa (Swan) variety of listener is he who takes the essence from the different kinds of (scriptures) heard by him, just like a swan which takes up pure milk from a mixture of water and milk.

## \|\| 6.4.14 \|\|

*śukaḥ suṣṭu mitaṃ vakti vyāsaṃ śrotṛṃśca harṣayan \|*  
*supāṭhitaḥ śuko yadvacchikṣakaṃ pārśvagānapi \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. A well-trained parrot delights the trainer as well as the bystanders. In the same manner, the Śuka type of listener speaks very well and in limited words also and delights the expounder (of Bhāgavata etc.) as well as other listeners.

## \|\| 6.4.15 \|\|

*śabdaṃ nānimiṣo jātu karotyāsvādayanrasam \|*  
*śrotā snigdho bhavenmīno mīnaḥ kṣīranidhau yathā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The listener of the Mīna (fish) type never makes any sound. He is winkless and he appreciates the excellence of the exposition. He is affectionate also. He is like the glossy fish in the ocean of milk.

## \|\| 6.4.16 \|\|

*yastudanrasikāñcchrotṝnvirautyajño vṛko hi saḥ \|*  
*veṇusvanarasāsaktānvṛko'raṇye mṛgānyathā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The listener who shouts and inflicts pain on Rasikas (those who have good taste and who appreciate excellence or beauty in literature etc.) and other listeners and who is also very ignorant is the Vṛka type. He is like the wolf which inflicts pain on deer in the forest eagerly listening to the sound of the flute.

## \|\| 6.4.17 \|\|

*bhūruṇḍaḥ śikṣayedanyāñcchrutvā na svayamācaret \|*  
*yathā himavataḥ śṛṃge bhūruṇḍākhyo vihaṃgamaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The bird named Bhūruṇḍa is found on the peeks of the Himālaya mountain. The listener of the Bhūruṇḍa type may teach others but he himself does not act according to (the advices) heard by him.

## \|\| 6.4.18 \|\|

*sarvaṃ śrutamupādatte sārāsārāndhadhīrvṛṣaḥ \|*  
*svādu drākṣāṃ khaliṃ cāpi nirviśeṣaṃ yathā vṛṣaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The listener of the Vṛṣa (Bull) type is intellectually blind to both the essential and the inessential. He takes in everything heard by him just like the bull which indiscriminately swallows the tasty grapes as well as the oil cake.
