*pravṛttaṃ tattu sakalamaśāntikṛdudīritam \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. (Karmas under Pravṛtta category are as follows:)

Marrying a woman suitable to oneself by procedure prescribed in Tantra and/or Veda; earning of wealth in a just way; sacrifices involving expenditure of money, but performed with a desired objective; stay in a village or a town; works of personal piety and works of public utility,—all this is Pravṛtta, which is said to be not contributory to peace.

## \|\| 9.3.13-14 \|\|

*strīdravyayoḥ parityāgaḥ kāmalobhakrudhāṃ tathā \|*  
*vanavāsaśca vairāgyaṃ tapaḥ kṣāntiḥ śamo damaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*brahmayajñā yogayajñā jñānayajñāśca sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*japayajñāśceti mune nivṛttaṃ karma kīrtitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. (Karmas under the Nivṛtta category are as follows:)

Renuciation of wife, wealth, sex, greed and anger; stay in a forest; indifference to worldly objects; penance; forbearance; equanimity; self-control; recitation of the Vedas; Yoga-yajña; Jñāna-yajña; muttering a mantra or prayer as sacrifice—all this has been mentioned as Nivṛtta Karma.

## \|\| 9.3.15 \|\|

*trilokyāṃ gatayo dharmaṃ pravṛttamanutiṣṭhatām \|*  
*svargalokāvadhi mune manuṣyāṇāṃ bhavanti vai \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The movement of the souls of men who perform the Pravṛtta dharma is up to heaven in the three worlds.

## \|\| 9.3.16 \|\|

*indracandrāgnilokādau svasvapuṇyaphalaṃ ca te \|*  
*bhogaiśvaryaṃ vahuvidhamabhīṣṭaṃ bhuñjate khalu \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. As a fruit of their respective merits, they certainly enjoy various kinds of coveted lordly pleasures in the abodes of Indra, Candra, Agni and others.

## \|\| 9.3.17 \|\|

*yāvatpuṇyaṃ tāvadeva bhuktvā tatte surā'stataḥ \|*  
*kṣīṇe tu sukṛte bhūyaḥ patanti vivaśā bhuvi \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Having enjoyed pleasures so long as the (balance of) merits lasts, those gods helplessly fall down to the earth again, when (the store of) their merit is exhausted.

## \|\| 9.3.18 \|\|

*bhogaiśvaryādināśo hi kālavegena jāyate \|*  
*anicchatāmapi mune teṣāṃ puṇyakṣaye sati \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O sage, when their (stock of) merit is exhausted, their enjoyment and prosperity dwindle fast with the passage of time, even if they are unwilling.

## \|\| 9.3.19 \|\|

*ādhikārikadevānāmapi brahmadine muhuḥ \|*  
*iṣṭabhogaiśvaryanāśo jāyate kālaraṃhasā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Even in the case of Devas who are established there as authority, the destruction of their desired enjoyment and lordship frequently takes place with the speed of Time during Brahmā’s day.

## \|\| 9.3.20 \|\|

*nivṛttadharmaniṣṭhā ye yoginaśca tapasvinaḥ \|*  
*janādīnyānti lokāṃstrīṃste tu trailokyato bahiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Yogins, the performers of penance who have firm devotion in Nivṛtta Dharma go to Jana and other three worlds beyond (our) three worlds (viz. the earth, the nether world and heaven).

## \|\| 9.3.21 \|\|

*tattallokaiśvaryabhogānbhuñjate te nijepsitān \|*  
*dainandinepi pralaye varttante te yathāsukham \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. As desired by them, they enjoy the pleasures and lordship afforded in those respective worlds. They live equally in happiness, during the daily type of Pralaya (world destruction).

## \|\| 9.3.22 \|\|

*brahmaṇo dviparārddhānte tadbhogaiśvaryasaṃpadaḥ \|*  
*naśyanti kālaśaktyaiva lokāsteṣāṃ ca nārada \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. At the end of two Parārdhas (i.e. one hundred) years of God Brahmā, their worlds as well as their prosperity, pleasures and lordliness, perish with the speed of Time, O Nārada.

## \|\| 9.3.23 \|\|

*athaitadvividhaṃ karma guṇātmakamapi dvija \|*  
*kṛtaṃ cedviṣṇusaṃbaddhaṃ nirguṇaṃ syāttadā tu tat \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Now this two-fold Karma, though possessed of Guṇas, becomes devoid of Guṇas, if performed with reference to (i.e. dedicating it to) Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 9.3.24 \|\|

*tatphalaṃ cākṣayaṃ syāddhi sveṣṭādapyadhikaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*bhaktāste bhagavaddhāma yāntyaṣṭāvṛttitaḥ param \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Its fruit is imperishable. It is much more than what is desired by men. Those devotees go to the supreme abode of the Lord from eight (various) modes of life.

## \|\| 9.3.25 \|\|

*ato vivekino nityaṃ viṣṇubhaktyanvitāḥ kriyāḥ \|*  
*pravṛttā vā nivṛttā vā kurvate sakalā api \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Hence people with (right) discrimination always do all the acts, whether of the Pravṛtta or Nivṛtta type, (remaining imbued) always with devotion to Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 9.3.26-28 \|\|

*brahmā sthāṇurmanurddakṣo bhṛgurddharmastathā yamaḥ \|*  
*marīciraṅgirāścātriḥ pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*vaibhrājaśca vasiṣṭhaśca vivasvānsoma eva ca \|*  
*kaśyapaḥ karddamādyāśca prajānāṃ patayo mune \|\| 27 \|\|*

*devāśca ṛṣayaḥ sarve sarve varṇāstathāśramāḥ \|*  
*pūjayanti tameveśaṃ pravṛttaṃ dharmamāsthitāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. O sage, Brahmā, Śiva, Manu, Dakṣa, Bhṛgu, Dharma, Yama, Marīci, Aṅgiras, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Vaibhrāja, Vasiṣṭha, Sun-god, Moon-god, Patriarchs like Kaśyapa, Kardama and others, all gods, sages, all castes, and (persons belonging to) all stages of life—all those who have resorted to Pravṛtta Dharma (should) worship that very Lord.

## \|\| 9.3.29-30 \|\|

*sanaḥ sanatsujātaśca sanakaḥ sa sanandanaḥ \|*  
*sanatkumāraḥ kapila āruṇiśca sanātanaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*ṛbhuryatiśca haṃsādyā munayo naiṣṭhikavratāḥ \|*  
*tameva pūjayantīśaṃ nivṛttaṃ dharmamāsthitāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. Sana, Sanatsujāta, Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatkumāra, Kapila, Āruṇi, Sanātana, Ṛbhu, Yati and sages like Haṃsa who are steady performers of vows—all these who arc established in Nivṛtta Dharma, worship that very Lord.

## \|\| 9.3.31 \|\|

*vāsudevasyāṅgatayā bhāvayitvā surānpitṝn \|*  
*ahiṃsapūjāvidhinā yajante cānvahaṃ hi te \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Considering gods and ancestors as parts of the person of Vāsudeva, they everyday worship them with the mode of worship free from injury to beings.

## \|\| 9.3.32 \|\|

*yathādhikāramete hi tena yatra niyojitāḥ \|*  
*pravṛtte vā nivṛtte vā dharme te pālayanti tam \|*  
*tasya devasya maryādāṃ na krāmantyubhayepi te \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Wherever these are posted by him according to their powers, whether it is Pravṛtta type of Dharma or Nivṛtta type, they abide by it. In both the cases they never transgress the bounds of morality and propriety set by the Lord.

## \|\| 9.3.33 \|\|

*caturvarge teṣu yasya yadyadiṣṭatamaṃ bhavet \|*  
*tattatsaṃpūrayatyeva sarva śaktipatiḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. That Almighty Lord fully supplies whatever is most desired by any of them in the four classes.

## \|\| 9.3.34 \|\|

*bhaktyā kṛtasyāpyalpasya bhagavānpuṇyakarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*prīto dadātyeva phalaṃ mahadakṣayamīpsitam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The Lord, being pleased, gives the great, cherished imperishable fruit (i.e. Mokṣa), for even a slight meritorious act done (unto him) with devotion.

## \|\| 9.3.35-36 \|\|

*teṣu tadbhaktito loke ye tvekāntitvamāsthitāḥ \|*  
*vāsudevaṃ vinānyatra saṃkṣīṇāśeṣavāsanāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*dehānte te tu saṃprāpya tasya dhāma tamaḥparam \|*  
*dehairaprākṛtaireva premṇā paricaranti tam \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. Out of them, those who, out of devotion to him in the world, are established in devotion solely unto him, and all whose longings for objects other than Vāsudeva are thoroughly exhausted, at the end of their life attain to his domain which is beyond darkness. With their divine bodies they wait upon him with love.

## \|\| 9.3.37 \|\|

*anye tu bhaktāḥ kālena tadupāsanadārḍhyataḥ \|*  
*vāsanānāṃ kṣaye jāte yāntyekāntikavaddhi tam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Other devotees whose longings and false notions come to an end in due course, by firmness of devotional service also go to him like Ekāntika devotees (i.e. devotees who are exclusively attached to a single deity, Viṣṇu).

## \|\| 9.3.38 \|\|

*yena kenāpi bhāvena tena saṃbadhyate tu yaḥ \|*  
*saṃsṛtiṃ na prayātyeva sa tu kvāpyanyajīvavat \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. He who is associated with him in whatever manner or capacity, never returns to Saṃsāra anywhere like other living beings.

## \|\| 9.3.39 \|\|

*karmayogasya saṃsiddhirjñānayogasya cepsitā \|*  
*tasyāśrayādeva nṛṇāṃ nirvighnaṃ bhavati drutam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. It is due solely to taking resort to him that the attainment of the fruit of Karma Yoga or Jñāna Yoga is quickly accomplished without any impediment.

## \|\| 9.3.40 \|\|

*tasmātsa eva bhagavānsavarraipi janairiha \|*  
*svābhīṣṭaphalasiddhyarthaṃ prītyopāsyo yathāvidhi \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Hence, that very Lord should be propitiated with love and devotion as per proper procedure by all people for the accomplishment of the fruit desired by oneself.

## \|\| 9.3.41 \|\|

*brahmaikyamāptā nirvighnā api brahmaśivādayaḥ \|*  
*śrīviṣṇoḥ kurvate bhaktiṃ santītthaṃ tanmahāguṇāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Gods Brahmā, Śiva and others attained oneness (and merger) with Brahman without any impediment. The great virtues of the Lord accrue unto him who performs worship of Śrī Viṣṇu.

## Chapter 4 - Śveta-Dvīpa

## \|\| 9.4.1 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*sa evamuktotmavidāṃ variṣṭho nārāyaṇenottamapūruṣeṇa \|*  
*jagāda vākyaṃ jagatāṃ gariṣṭhaṃ tamacyutaṃ lokahitādhivāsam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Skanda said:

1\. He (Nārada) who was the greatest one among persons possessing knowledge of the soul, and who was thus spoken to by the Superme Person Nārāyaṇa, addressed the following words to that Acyuta, the greatest one among the worlds, the very abode of the welfare of the world.

## \|\| 9.4.2 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*śrutaṃ mayā deva samaṃ tvayoktamṛṣyākṛticchāditabhūridhāmnā \|*  
*tavaiva līlā sakaleyamīśa sarveśvarasyeti vidāmi citte \|\| 2 \|\|*

Nārada said:

2\. O Lord, whatever has been spoken by you, who have concealed your immense lustre within the form of a sage, has been heard by me completely. But I know in my mind that all this is the sport of you only, who are the Lord of all.

## \|\| 9.4.3 \|\|

*tvaddarśanenaiva hi pūrṇakāmo bhavāmi bhūmansvahṛdīpsitena \|*  
*tathāpyahaṃ tattava pūrvarūpaṃ prabho didṛkṣāmi hi kautukaṃ me \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O Bhūman (Viṣṇu), I shall have all my wishes fulfilled by your sight only, which is earnestly desired by my heart. I, however, have a strong desire to see your previous (original) form. O Lord, I am curious (to see it),

## \|\| 9.4.4 \|\|

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye śvetadvīpamuktavarṇanaṃ nāma caturtho'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:

4\. That form of mine is not possible to be seen by acts of charity or religious gifts, performance of sacrifices, or practice of Yoga, or by study or recitation of the Vedas, or performance of penance, O Nārada. It can be seen only by complete, undivided devotion unto me, by excellent devotees exclusively attached to me.

## \|\| 9.4.5 \|\|

*bhaktistava tvasti mayi hyananyā jñānaṃ ca vairāgyayutaṃ svadharmaḥ \|*  
*ataśca taddarśanamāpsyasi tvaṃ sureśvarādyairapi yaddurāpam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Your devotion unto me is undivided; your knowledge is strengthened with disinterestedness to worldly pleasures. That is your Dharma. Hence, you will have that vision which is very difficult to have even by deities including the Lord of gods.

## \|\| 9.4.6 \|\|

*tvadīyabhaktyā'titarā prasannastvājñāpayāmyadya tadīkṣaṇāya \|*  
*sitāntarīpaṃ vraja tatra te'yaṃ manorathaḥ setsyati vipravarya \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. I am extremely pleased with your devotion. Today, I assure you that vision. Go to Śveta-Dvīpa (lit. White Island). This desire of yours will be accomplished there, O excellent Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 9.4.7 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*śrutveti vācaṃ parameṣṭhiputraḥ sopyarccayitvā tamṛṣiṃ purāṇam \|*  
*khamutpapātottamayogayuktastatodhimerau sahasā nipete \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Having heard the words, Nārada, the son of Brahmā, worshipped that ancient sage (Nārāyaṇa). On an excellent auspicious astrological yoga (astral combination), he flew up in the sky. He at once descended on (a peak of) Meru.

## \|\| 9.4.8 \|\|

*tasyāvatasthe ca munirmuhūrttamekāntamāsādya gireḥ sa śṛṃge \|*  
*ālokayannuttarapaścimena dadarśa cātyadbhutamantarīpam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Finding a quiet solitary place, the sage stayed for a while on the peak of the mountain. While looking in the north-western direction, he saw an extremely wonderful island.

## \|\| 9.4.9 \|\|

*kṣīrodadheruttarato hi dvīpaḥ śvetaḥ sa nāmnā prathito viśālaḥ \|*  
*dedīpyamāno vitatena sarvato jyotiścayenātisi tena nityam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. To the northern side of the Milk Ocean (Kṣīrodadhi), there is a famous vast island known as White Island (Śveta-Dvīpa). It is ever-refulgent, radiating very bright, white mass of light spread all over its extent.

## \|\| 9.4.10-11 \|\|

*āmrairanekairasanairaśokairāmrātakairnimbakadambanīpaiḥ \|*  
*bilvairmadhūkaiḥ suradārubhiśca plakṣairvaṭaiḥ kiṃśukacandanaiśca \|\| 10 \|\|*

*sarjjaiśca śālaiḥ panasaistamālairmunidrumaiḥ ketakacampakaiśca \|*  
*kundaiśca jātīsuramallikābhidrumairvṛtaḥ puṣpaphalāvanamraiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. It was surrounded and covered over with innumerable mango trees, Terminalia tomentosa trees, Hogplumes (Spondias mangifera), Neem, Nauclea cadamba, Ixora Bandhucca (Species of Aśoka) Bilva (Bassia latifolia), divine trees, Ficus infectoria, Banyan trees, Kiṃśuka and sandal trees, Vatica robusta, Sāla trees, Bread-fruit trees, Tamāla (Agati grandiflora), Ketakas, Caṃpaka, Kunda trees, Jasmine trees, divine Jasminutn zambac trees—all of which were bent down with (the weight of) flowers and fruits.

## \|\| 9.4.12 \|\|

*kalpadrumāṇāṃ bahubhiśca vṛndaiḥ suvarṇarambhākramukālibhiśca \|*  
*mahadbhirudyānavarairanekaiḥ saritsarobhirvikacāmbujaiśca \|*  
*haṃsādibhiḥ pakṣivaraiḥ suśabdairgaṇairmṛgāṇāṃ ruciraiścaladbhiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. It was covered with many clusters of wish-yielding trees, and with rows of golden banana trees and betel-nut trees. It was full of innumerable great and excellent parks and gardens, rivers and lakes, full of blooming lotuses and sweetly warbling excellent birds like swans and others, and with excellent fleeing deer.

## \|\| 9.4.13 \|\|

*sarvepi jīvāḥ kila yatra muktā vasanti ca sthāvarajaṅgamāśca \|*  
*taṃ vīkṣamāṇena ca tena dṛṣṭā bhaktottamāḥ śrīpuruṣottamasya \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. There all living beings, both movable and immovable, lead a liberated life.

While he was observing, excellent devotees of the Supreme Lord were seen by him.

## \|\| 9.4.14-16 \|\|

*atīndriyā nirgatasarvapāpā niṣyandahīnāśca sugandhinaśca \|*  
*dvibāhavaḥ kepi caturbhujāśca śvetāśca kecinnavanīradābhāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*padmacchadākṣāḥ samamānagātrāḥ surūpadivyāvayavāḥ susārāḥ \|*  
*vikīrṇakeśāśca sadā kiśorā sadbhiśca cihnairnnikhilairupetāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sarojarekhāṅkitapāṇipādāḥ ṣaḍūrmihīnā mihirātitejasaḥ \|*  
*sitāṃśukā dhyānaparāśca saumyāḥ kālopi yebhyo bhayameti nityam \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. They were beyond the ken of sense-organs. They were devoid of all sins and (bodily) discharges. They were sweet-smelling. They were two-handed and some of them were four-handed. Some were white, while others were like new clouds in complexion. Their eyes were like petals of lotuses. Their limbs were symmetrical. They were extremely powerful with beautiful heavenly limbs. Their hair were scattered. They were ever youthful and were characterised with all auspicious marks. Their palms and soles were marked with (the outlines of) lotus. They were devoid of six defects of life (hunger, thirst, decay, death, grief and illusion). They surpassed the Sun in lustre. They were clad in white. They were gentle and absorbed in meditation. Even the god of Death was always afraid of them.

## \|\| 9.4.17 \|\|

*sāvarṇiruvāca \|*  
*atīndriyā nirātaṅkā aniṣyandāḥ sugandhinaḥ \|\| ke te narāḥ kathaṃ jātāstādṛśāḥ kā ca tadgatiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

Sāvarṇi said:

17\. Who are those men who are beyond the range of sense-organs, free from diseases and discharges of the body, full of sweet fragrance? How are persons of such category born? What is their destiny?

## \|\| 9.4.18 \|\|

*śvetadvīpaḥ payombhodhau varttate hi dharātale \|\| tadvāsināmapi kathaṃ proktā'tīndriyatā tvayā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Śveta-dvīpa is on the surface of this earth, (though) in an ocean of waters. How did you proclaim the state of being beyond the (ken of) sense-organs, in case of the inhabitants of Śveta-dvīpa?

## \|\| 9.4.19 \|\|

*ye brahmaṇyakṣare dhāmni saccidānandarūpiṇi \|\| sthitāḥ syuścinmayā muktāste tathā syurnnahītare \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Only those who are established in the imperishable Brahman of the form of existence, consciousness and bliss, full of (identical with) pure thought (Brahman), are the liberated ones and not others.

## \|\| 9.4.20 \|\|

*etaṃ me saṃśayaṃ chindhi paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me \|\| tvaṃ hi sarvakathābhijñastatastvāmāśritosmayaham \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Be pleased to remove this doubt of mine. I have got great eagerness (to know). As you are expert in all sorts of discourses, I have resorted to you.

Skanda replied:

## \|\| 9.4.21-22 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*ekāntopāsanenaiva prākkalpeṣu ramāpateḥ \|\| ye brahmabhāvaṃ saṃprāptā ajarāmaratāṃ gatāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*akṣarākhyāḥ pumāṃsaste śvetadvīpe'tra dhāmani \|\| sevituṃ vāsudevaṃ taṃ sthitā devarṣiṇekṣitāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Those persons called imperishable ones (Akṣara) who, through their undivided propitiation solely of the consort of Ramā (i.e. Viṣṇu) during previous Kalpas, attained the state of Brahman and have attained agelessness and immortality, stay in this domain of Śvetadvīpa for serving Vāsudeva and are being watched by gods and sages.

## \|\| 9.4.23 \|\|

*prāpte pralayakāle tu punaścākṣaradhāmani \|\| sthāsyanti te svatantrāśca kālamāyābhayojjhitāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. When the time of world-destruction arrives, they will stay as independent beings in the eternal domain (Akṣara-dhāman), free from the fear of Kāla (Death, Time) and Māyā.

## \|\| 9.4.24 \|\|

*atrāpi puruṣā ye tu māyājātā ataḥ kṣarāḥ \|\| tepi sadbhiḥ sādhanairvai jāyante tādṛśāḥ kila \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Even here, those persons as well, who are born of Māyā and hence are perishable, verily become similar to those (Akṣara Puruṣas) through pious adorations.

## \|\| 9.4.25-27 \|\|

*ahiṃsayā ca tapasā svadharmeṇa virāgataḥ \|\| vāsudevasya māhātmyajñānenaivātmaniṣṭhayā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*bhaktyā paramayā nityaṃ prasaṅgena mahātmanām \|\| harisevāvihīnānāṃ muktīnāmapyanicchayā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*siddhīnāmaṇimādīnāṃ sarvāsāṃ cāpyakāṃkṣayā \|\| anyonyaṃ śrutikīrtibhyāṃ śrīharerjanmakarmaṇām \|*  
*bhavanti tādṛśā nūnaṃ puruṣā munisattama \|\| 27 \|\|*

25-27. O excellent sage, persons really become like those (Akṣara Puruṣas) through (practice of) non-violence, penance, (by abiding) by one’s specific duties, through non-attachment to worldly objects, knowledge of the glory of Vāsudeva and steadiness in (devotion to) the Ātman, supreme devotion (to the Lord), and contacts with the noble-souled ones, even though (originally) they are devoid of service to Hari, have no desire for liberation, and are covetous of all super-natural powers like Aṇimā, but by hearing and describing to each other the birth and great deeds of Śrī Hari (they become so).

## \|\| 9.4.28 \|\|

*jagatsarge jāyamānepyete kālavaśātkvacit \|\| na jāyante svataṃtratvānna naśyanti laye'nyavat \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Even when the creation of the universe is under way, these are not born through the force of Time anywhere. Due to their independence they do not perish like others at the time of world-destruction.

## \|\| 9.4.29 \|\|

*atra te kathayiṣyāmi kathāṃ paurāṇikīṃ mune \|\| yathātratyopi manujastathā bhāvamupeyivān \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Now, I shall narrate to you an ancient legend, O sage, whereby a person belonging to this world, reached that stage.

## Chapter 5 - Uparicara Vasu, a Pious King

## \|\| 9.5.1 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*āsīdrājoparicaro vasunāmā purā mune \|*  
*bhūbhartturāyostanayaḥ khyātaścāsāvamāvasuḥ \|*  
*ākhaṇḍalasakho bhaktiṃ prāpto nārāyaṇe prabhau \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note:Uparicara Vasu was a pious king of Cedi, a great devotee of Viṣṇu. Indra was so intimate with him that he shared his seat and bed with him (Mbh, Śānti 335.17-26). Indra gave him his unfading Vaijayantī garland and a heavenly car and so he always moved in the sky and hence came to be known as Upari-cara (Mbh, Ādi 63.13-17). Other details of his life are given in this and the subsequent chapters.

Skanda said:

1\. O sage, formerly there was a king called Uparicara Vasu (lit. ‘Vasu who always moved in higher regions’). He was the son of King Āyu and was well-known as Amāvasu. He was a friend of Indra. He got (interested in) devotion unto Lord Nārāyaṇa.

## \|\| 9.5.2 \|\|

*dhārmikaḥ pitṛbhaktaśca pitṝndevāṃśca tarpayan \|*  
*sadācārarato dakṣaḥ kṣamāvānanasūyakaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. He was religious, devoted to his father and propitiated gods and manes. He was engaged in pious conduct, alert and diligent. He was tolerant and envious of none.

## \|\| 9.5.3 \|\|

*sarvopakārakaḥ śānto brahmacaryarataḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*akrodhanaśca mitabhuṅmṛdurnirvyasano muniḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He rendered assistance to all. He was quiescent, interested in the study of the Vedas (or celibacy), pure, not irascible, moderate in his meals, gentle, free from bad habits, an ascetic.

## \|\| 9.5.4 \|\|

*nirdvandvo nirvikāraśca nirmāno dhīra ātmavit \|*  
*nirddambho mānado yogī tapasvī vijitendriyaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He was unaffacted by pleasure-pain etc., free from passion, bereft of pride, resolute (and self-possessed), and knower of the Self. He was devoid of hypocrisy, gave respect to others. (He was) a Yogī, a performer of penance. He had completely subdued his sense-organs.

## \|\| 9.5.5 \|\|

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmya uparicaravasusadguṇavarṇanaṃ nāma paṃcamo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He was unattached to wealth, sons, wife and other relatives. The king everyday performed devoutly the Japa of Nārāyaṇa.

## \|\| 9.5.6 \|\|

*tasmai tuṣṭo'tha bhagavānvāsudevaḥ svayaṃ dadau \|*  
*sāmrājyaṃ so'tha nāsaktastatra bheje tamādarāt \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Being pleased with him, Lord Vāsudeva offered him an empire, but he was not interested in it, but propitiated him (Vāsudeva) only respectfully.

## \|\| 9.5.7-8 \|\|

*tatroktena vidhānena pañcakālasamāhitaḥ \|*  
*pūjayāmāsa deveśaṃ taccheṣeṇa surānpitṝn \|\| 7 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ śeṣeṇa viprāśca saṃvibhajyāśritāṃśca saḥ \|*  
*śeṣānnabhuksatyaparaḥ sarvabhūteṣvahiṃsakaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. With due attention he used to perform five times the worship of the Lord, according to procedure prescribed in the (Vaiṣṇava) Tantra (prob. Pāñcarātra Āgama). He worshipped gods and manes. He shared what remained (of the previous worship) with Brāhmaṇas and his dependents. And he subsisted on the remaining food. He was devoted to truth and was non-violent towards all living beings.

## \|\| 9.5.9 \|\|

*bhakṣaṇe doṣamavidatprāṇimātrāmiṣasya tu \|*  
*mahāpātakavadrājā svaprajāśca tathā'vadat \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The king knew that consuming flesh of animals was a great sin, and declared so to his subjects.

## \|\| 9.5.10 \|\|

*sarvabhāvena bheje'sau devadevaṃ janārdanam \|*  
*anādimadhyanidhanaṃ lokakarttāramavyayam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He resorted with all heart to Janārdana, god of goḍs, who has no beginning, middle and end, the imperishable creator of the world.

## \|\| 9.5.11-15 \|\|

*śrīvāsudevapadayoḥ sa cakāra manaḥ sthiram \|*  
*śrotre ca nityaṃ bhagavatkathāyāḥ śravaṇe nṛpaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*nayane sve mukundasya tadbhaktānāṃ ca darśane \|*  
*guṇagāne harervāṇīṃ cakre bhūmipatiḥ sa tu \|\| 12 \|\|*

*nārāyaṇāṃghrisaṃspṛṣṭa tulasīpuṣpasaurabhe \|*  
*prāṇaṃ cakāra ca nṛpo nānyagandheṣu karhicit \|\| 13 \|\|*

*śrīśopabhuktavastrādi sparśane ca tvacaṃ nijām \|*  
*cakāra rasanāmanne nārāyaṇanivedite \|\| 14 \|\|*

*bhagavanmandirakṣetrasadantikagatautathā \|*  
*cakāra caraṇau rājā sevāyāṃ ca karau hareḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

11-15. The king always concentrated his mind at the feet of Śrī Vāsudeva, and his ears in listening to the story of the Lord. He (devoted) his eyes to the vision of Mukunda, as well as of his devotees. The Lord of the land (king) devoted his speech in praising the qualities of Hari. The king used his nose in smelling the fragrance of Tulasī leaves and flowers, which had touched the feet of Nārāyaṇa, and not any other kind of perfume. He (concentrated) on the touch of the garments enjoyed (used) by the Lord of Śrī (Viṣṇu) to his skin (body). He used his tongue (to take in and enjoy) the food offered to Nārāyaṇa. The king used his feet to go to the sacred precincts of the temple of the Lord, and his hands for th service of Hari.

## \|\| 9.5.16 \|\|

*uttamāṃgaṃ ca cakre'sau viṣṇupādābhivandane \|*  
*sakhyaṃ cakāra paramaṃ mahābhāgavateṣu saḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He used his head (the best part of the body) for paying obeisance to the feet of Viṣṇu. He formed intimate friendship with great devotees of the Lord.

## \|\| 9.5.17 \|\|

*ekopi na kṣaṇastasya vinā bhaktiṃ ramāpateḥ \|*  
*jagāma kila rājarṣestadīya vratacāriṇaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Not a single moment of the royal sage, who observed the vow of devotion to Viṣṇu, was wasted without (performance of) devotion to the Lord of Ramā.

## \|\| 9.5.18 \|\|

*mahadbhireva saṃbhārairviṣṇorjjanmadinotsavān \|*  
*cakre tadarthamudyānamaṃdiropavanāni ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He celebrated with great preparations (and pomp), the festivals of the birth etc. of Viṣṇu. He constructed for this purpose temples, gardens and parks.

## \|\| 9.5.19 \|\|

*itthaṃ nārāyaṇe bhaktiṃ vahato brāhmaṇottama \|*  
*ekaśayyāsanaṃ tasya dattavāndevarāṭ svayam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O excellent Brāhmaṇa, while he was carrying on with such devotion unto Nārāyaṇa, the king of gods (Indra) offered him, of his own accord, participation in his own bed and seat.

## \|\| 9.5.20 \|\|

*vaijayantīṃ dadau mālāṃ tasmā indro'tiśobhanām \|*  
*amlānapaṅkajamayīṃ tathā ratnāni bhūriśaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Indra gave him the most beautiful garland known as Vaijayantī, made of unfading lotuses. Hé also gave him precious stones and jewels in abundance.

## \|\| 9.5.21 \|\|

*ātmā rājyaṃ dhanaṃ caiva kalatraṃ vāhanādi ca \|*  
*yattadbhagavataḥ sarvamiti tatprekṣitaṃ sadā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Everything, his own self, kingdom, wealth, queen, vehicles, were always looked upon by him as belonging to the Lord.

## \|\| 9.5.22 \|\|

*kāmyā naimittikājasraṃ yajñiyāḥ paramāḥ kriyāḥ \|*  
*sarvāḥ sātvatamāsthāya vidhiṃ cakre samāhitaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. With full concentration of mind and devoutly he resorted to the Sātvata form of procedure, and regularly performed all great sacrificial acts, both with desired objects in view, and as demanded by the occasion.

## \|\| 9.5.23 \|\|

*pañcarātravido mukhyāstasya gehe mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*prāyaṇaṃ bhagavatprattaṃ bhuñjatesmāgrato dvijāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. In the mansion of that noble soul, prominent Brāhmaṇas, experts in the Pāñcarātra doctrine, generally used to enjoy food offered to the Lord.

## \|\| 9.5.24 \|\|

*tasya praśāsato rājyaṃ dharmeṇā'mitraghātinaḥ \|*  
*nānṛtā vāksamabhavanmano duṣṭaṃ na cā'bhavat \|*  
*na ca kāyena kṛtavānsa pāpaṃ paramaṇvapi \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. While the destroyer of enemies ruled in the righteous way, no untruth was uttered (by him), nor did (his) mind get corrupt, not did he commit the slightest sin physically.

## \|\| 9.5.25 \|\|

*pañcarātraṃ mahātantraṃ bhagavadbhaktipuṣṭaye \|*  
*śuśrāvānudinaṃ rājā bhagavadbhaktavaktrataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. For the sake of enhancing his devotion unto the Lord the king daily heard the great Tantra called Pāñcarātra from the mouth of devotees of the Lord.

## \|\| 9.5.26 \|\|

*dharmaṃ saṃsthāpayañchuddhaṃ rañjayansakalāḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*pālayāmāsa pṛthivīṃ divamākhaṇḍalo yathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Establishing pure religion and gratifying his subjects, the king protected the earth like Indra taking care of heaven.

## \|\| 9.5.27 \|\|

*api saptavidhastasya rājye palalabhakṣakaḥ \|*  
*pumānkopyabhavannaiva na ca pāṣaṇḍaveṣiṇaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. In his kingdom there was no person of the seven varieties of flesh-eaters (Rākṣasas) nor were there any wearing the garb of atheists.

## \|\| 9.5.28 \|\|

*asādhyo yoṣitaścaiva puruṣāḥ pāradārikāḥ \|*  
*na śrutāstasya rājye ca dharmasaṃkarakāriṇaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. In his kingdom adulterous women and men seducing the wives of others, or perpetrators of promiscuous, irreligious acts (such as intercaste marriages) were not even heard of.

## \|\| 9.5.29 \|\|

*ekādaśavidhaṃ madyaṃ trividhāṃ ca surāmapi \|*  
*nājighradapi kopīha tasminrājyaṃ praśāsati \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. While he ruled his kingdom, nobody even smelt the fragrance of eleven kinds of madya (inebriating drinks)\[4\], nor three kinds of Surā (spirituous liquors) (a kind of beer—MW).

## \|\| 9.5.30 \|\|

*evaṃguṇaḥ sa tu kvāpi pakṣapātāddivaukasām \|*  
*mithyālāpāddivo bhraṣṭaḥ praviveśa mahītalam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Though he was endowed with these qualities, on a certain occasion he fell down from heaven and entered the bowels of the earth for speaking an untruth out of partiality for the heaven-dwellers (gods).

## \|\| 9.5.31 \|\|

*antarbhūmigataścāsau satataṃ dharmavatsalaḥ \|*  
*nārāyaṇaparo bhūtvā tanmaṃtramajapatsthiraḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Even while he was within the bowels of the earth, the king, a lover of piety, remained devoted to Nārāyaṇa and was steady in performing the Japa (muttering the name) of the Lord.

## \|\| 9.5.32 \|\|

*tasyaiva ca prasādena punarevotthitastu saḥ \|*  
*divaṃ prāpya sukhaṃ tatra manobhīṣṭaṃ samanvabhūt \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Through His grace, he was lifted up again (elevated), from the place. After having attained heaven, he enjoyed pleasures as desired by his mind.

## \|\| 9.5.33 \|\|

*punaścedipatirbhūtvā bhuvyasau pitṛśāpataḥ \|*  
*pañcarātroktavidhinā bheje harimatandritaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Through the curse of his manes, he became the king of Cedi (Bundelkhand and a part of Madhya Pradesh in India) on the earth. He performed devotion unto Hari delightfully and alertly in the Pāñcarātra way.

## Chapter 6 - Fall of Uparicara Vasu

## \|\| 9.6.1 \|\|

*sāvarṇiruvāca \|*  
*sa hi bhakto bhagavata āsīdrājā mahānvasuḥ \|*  
*kiṃ mithyā'bhyavadadyena divo bhūvivaraṃ gataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sāvarṇi said:

1\. That King Vasu was a great devotee of the Lord. What lie (deceitful statement) did he utter, whereby he went down from heaven to the bowels of the earth?

## \|\| 9.6.2 \|\|

*kenoddhṛtaḥ punarbhūmeḥ śapto'sau pitṛbhiḥ kutaḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ muktastato bhūpa ityetatskanda me vad \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Who lifted him up again on the earth? Why was he cursed by his faṃers. How was the king redeemed then? O Skanda, please narrate it to me.

Skanda replied:

## \|\| 9.6.3 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu brahmankathāmetāṃ vasorvāsa varociṣaḥ \|*  
*yasyāḥ śravaṇataḥ sadyaḥ sarvapāpakṣayo bhavet \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O Brāhmaṇa, listen to the story of Vasu who had the brilliance of God Indra. By hearing it, there will be instantaneous destruction of all sins.

## \|\| 9.6.4 \|\|

*svāyambhuvāntare pūrvamindro viśvajidāhvayaḥ \|*  
*ārarambhe mahāyajñamaśvamedhābhidhaṃ mune \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Formerly, in the Svāyaṃbhuva Manvantara, Indra, by name Viśvajit, began a great sacrifice called Aśvamedha, O sage.

## \|\| 9.6.5 \|\|

*nibaddhāḥ paśavo'jādyāḥ krośantastatra bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*sarve devagaṇāścāpi rasalubdhāstadāsata \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Beasts like goats and others were tied there and they were bleating frequently. All the multitudes of Devas were desirous of the taste (of their flesh).

## \|\| 9.6.6 \|\|

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇava khaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye vedasyahiṃsāparatvoktyā uparicaravasoradhaḥpātavarṇanaṃ nāma ṣaṣṭho'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. By a lucky chance great sages having the refulgence of the sun, came there in the course of their touring of the world for the welfare of the people.

## \|\| 9.6.7 \|\|

*saṃmānitā suragaṇaiḥ pādyārghyasvāgatādibhiḥ \|*  
*te bṛhanmunayo'paśyanmedhyāṃstānkrośataḥ paśūn \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. They were respectfully received with Pādya, Arghya and other items of (formal) welcome. Those sages saw the multitude of bleating sacrificial beasts.

## \|\| 9.6.8 \|\|

*sāttvikānāmapi ca taṃ devānāṃ yajñavistaram \|*  
*hiṃsāmayaṃ samālokya te'tyāścaryaṃ hi lebhire \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Seeing the violence involved in the paraphernalia of the sacrifice to gods who were of Sāttvika nature, they were extremely wonder-struck.

## \|\| 9.6.9 \|\|

*dharmavyatikramaṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛpayā te dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*mahendrapramukhānūcurdevāndharmadhiyastataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Observing the travesty of Dharma, those paraphernalia, the Brāhmaṇas of virtuous mind, out of compassion, asked the Devas, among whom Mahendra was prominent:

## \|\| 9.6.10 \|\|

*maharṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*devaiśca ṛṣibhiḥ sākaṃ mahendrā'smadvacaḥ śṛṇu \|*  
*yathāsthitaṃ dharmatattvaṃ vadāmo hi sanātanam \|\| 10 \|\|*

The great sages said:

10\. O Mahendra, listen to our speech along with Devas and sages. We declare the essence of the eternal Dhrama as it stands.

## \|\| 9.6.11 \|\|

*yūyaṃ jagatsargakāle brahmaṇā parameṣṭhinā \|*  
*sattvena nirmitāḥ stho vai catuṣpāddharmadhārakāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. At the time of the creation of the world, you were created by the great god Brahmā out of Sattva, and you are the upholders of Dharma standing on all the four feet.

## \|\| 9.6.12 \|\|

*rajasā tamasā cāsau manūṃścaiva narādhipān \|*  
*asurāṇāṃ cādhipatīnasṛjaddharmadhāriṇaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. By means of Rajas and Tamas, he created Manus, kings, rulers of Asuras, the supporters of Dharma.

## \|\| 9.6.13 \|\|

*sarveṣāmatha yuṣmākaṃ yajñādividhibodhakam \|*  
*sasarja śreyase vedaṃ sarvābhīṣṭaphalapradam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. For the guidance of you all regarding the procedure of performance of sacrifice etc., he created the Veda, the conferer of all the desired fruits for the welfare of all.

## \|\| 9.6.14 \|\|

*ahiṃsaiva paro dharmastatra vede'sti kīrttitaḥ \|*  
*sākṣātpaśuvadho yajñe nahi vedasya saṃmataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. There, in the Veda, Ahiṃsā (non-violence) alone has been glorified as the supreme Dharma. The direct killing of a beast is not definitely approved by the Veda.

## \|\| 9.6.15 \|\|

*catuṣpādasya dharmasya sthāpane hyeva sarvathā \|*  
*tātparyamasti vedasya na tu nāśe'sya hiṃsayā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The Veda has the aim of establishing the Dharma of four feet, and not of the destruction of Dharma by committing violence.

## \|\| 9.6.16 \|\|

*rajastamodoṣavaśāttathāpyasurapā nṛpāḥ \|*  
*medhyenājena yaṣṭavyamityādau matijāḍyataḥ \|*  
*chāgādimarthaṃ bubudhurvrīhyādiṃ tu na te viduḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Kings, rulers of Asuras, however, due to the fault of Rajas and Tamas, and dullness of intellect, take ‘a he-goat’ etc. as the meaning of “Aja” in the injunction “sacrifice should be performed with a sacrificial Aja.” They did not know Vrīhi (rice) etc. (which is its meaning).

## \|\| 9.6.17 \|\|

*sāttvikānāṃ tu yuṣmākaṃ vedasyārtho yathā sthitaḥ \|*  
*grahītavyonyathā naiva tādṛśī ca kriyocitā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. In your case, who are created out of Sattvaguṇa, the true meaning of the Vedas should be accepted. Otherwise, that kind of performance (involving violence) is not at all proper.

## \|\| 9.6.18 \|\|

*yādṛśo hi guṇo yasya svabhāvastasya tādṛśaḥ \|*  
*svasvabhāvānusāreṇa pravṛttiḥ syācca karmaṇi \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The nature of a person conforms to his Guṇa. One’s attitude in the performance of a ritual conforms to one’s own nature.

## \|\| 9.6.19 \|\|

*sāttvikānāṃ hi vo devaḥ sākṣādviṣṇū ramāpatiḥ \|*  
*ahiṃsayajñe'sti tato'dhikārastasya tuṣṭaye \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. To you who are Sāttvikas the god is directly Viṣṇu, the consort of Ramā. For his gratification one is authorised to perform a Yajña which does not involve any violence.

## \|\| 9.6.20 \|\|

*pratyakṣapaśumālabhya yajñasyācaraṇaṃ tu yat \|*  
*dharmaḥ sa viparīto vai yuṣmākaṃ surasattamāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The performance of a sacrifice by actually killing a beast, is contrary to Dharma in your case, O excellent Suras.

## \|\| 9.6.21 \|\|

*rajastamoguṇavaśādāsurīṃ saṃpadaṃ śritāḥ \|*  
*yuṣmākaṃ yājakā hyete santyavedavido yathā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. These performers of sacrifice on your behalf have resorted to Asura type of performance due to their being subjected to Rajas and Tamas Guṇas. They are ignorant of Vedas.

## \|\| 9.6.22 \|\|

*tatsaṅgādeva yuṣmākaṃ sāmprataṃ vyatyayo mateḥ \|*  
*jātastenedṛśaṃ karma prārabdhamiti niścitam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. It is due to your association with them that such perversity has token place just now. Certainly, it is due to this, that ṃis performance has been commenced by you.

## \|\| 9.6.23 \|\|

*rājasānāṃ tāmasānāmāsurāṇāṃ tathā nṛṇām \|*  
*yathāguṇaṃ bhairavādyā upāsyāḥ santi devatāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. For Asuras and human beings, characterised by Rajas and Tamas Guṇas, there are deities like Bhairava and oṃers, worthy of being propitiated according to the Guṇas (of the devotees).

## \|\| 9.6.24 \|\|

*svaguṇānuguṇātmīyadevatātuṣṭaye bhuvi \|*  
*hiṃsrayajñavidhānaṃ yatteṣāmevocitaṃ hi tat \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. In this world, for the gratification of one’s deity of suitable guṇa, conforming to one’s own (i.e. devotee’s) guṇa, the performance of sacrifice involving violence is enjoined for them.

## \|\| 9.6.25 \|\|

*tatrāpi viṣṇubhaktā ye daityarakṣonarādayaḥ \|*  
*teṣāmapyucito nāsti hiṃsrayajñaḥ kutastu vaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Even out of them, for the Daityas, Rākṣasas and human beings who are devotees of Viṣṇu, Yajña involving violence is not proper. How can it be so, in your case?

## \|\| 9.6.26 \|\|

*yajñaśeṣo hi sarveṣāṃ yajñakarmānutiṣṭhatām \|*  
*anujñāto bhakṣaṇārthaṃ nigamenaiva vartate \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. It is only in accordance with (the injunction of) the Veda that the remnants of the sacrifice are permitted to be eaten by all who have performed the sacrifice.

## \|\| 9.6.27 \|\|

*sāttvikānāṃ devatānāṃ surāmāṃsāśanaṃ kvacit \|*  
*asmābhistvīkṣitaṃ naiva na śrutaṃ ca satāṃ mukhāt \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Consumption of liquor and eating of flesh by Sāttvika deities is neither seen by us nor heard from the mouths of saintly people anywhere.

## \|\| 9.6.28 \|\|

*tasmādvrīhibhirevāsau yajñaḥ kṣīreṇa sarpiṣā \|*  
*medhyairannarasaiścā'nyaiḥ kāryo na paśuhiṃsayā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Hence this sacrifice should be performed with rice, milk, ghee and other foodstuffs fit for being used in sacrifices, and not with the killing of beasts.

## \|\| 9.6.29 \|\|

*tatrāpi bījairyaṣṭavyamajasaṃjñāmupāgataiḥ \|*  
*trivarṣakālamuṣitairnna yeṣāṃ punarudgamaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Even out of them (the grain of rice etc.), (sacrifices should be performed) with seeds which have attained the state of A-ja by their being ṃree years old and from which there occur no germination again.

## \|\| 9.6.30-31 \|\|

*adrohaścāyalobhaśca damo bhūtadayā tapaḥ \|*  
*brahmacaryaṃ tathā satyamadambhaśca kṣamā dhṛtiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*sanātanasya dharmasya rūpametadudīritam \|*  
*tadatikramya yo varteddharmaghnaḥ sa patatyadhaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. It has been proclaimed that non-injury, non-covetousness, self-control, mercifulness to beings, penance, celibacy, truth, non-hypocrisy, forbearance and courage, constitute the form (and content) of the eternal Dharma. He who transgress it, is the destroyer of Dharma and falls.

## \|\| 9.6.32 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*itthaṃ vedarahasyajñairmahāmunibhirādarāt \|*  
*bodhitā api sannītyā svapratijñāvighātataḥ \|*  
*tadvākyaṃ jagṛhurnaiva tatprāmāṇyavidopi te \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Though they were thus respectfully advised in good moral conduct by the great sages, the knowers of the secrets of the Veda, they (Devas), though acknowledging their authority, did not accept their advice due to its being against their avowed declaration.

## \|\| 9.6.33 \|\|

*mahadvyatikramāttarhi mānakrodhamadādayaḥ \|*  
*viviśusteṣvadharmasya vaṃśyāśchidragaveṣiṇaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Self-conceit, wrath, arrogance and other ‘descendants’ of Adharma, keen to find out (moral) deficiences, entered into them, due to their disregard for the great (sages).

## \|\| 9.6.34-35 \|\|

*ajaśchāgo na bījānītyādi vādiṣu teṣvatha \|*  
*vimanassvṛṣivaryeṣu punastānbodhayatsu ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

*rājoparicaraḥ śrīmāṃstatraivāgādyadṛcchayā \|*  
*tejasā dyotayannāśā indrasya paramaḥ sakhā \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. Now, while they (Devas) were arguing that the term ‘Aja’ means ‘a goat’ and not ‘seeds’, and while the disconsolate great sages were again admonishing them, the glorious King Uparicara (Vasu) came there by chance. That intimate friend of Indra was illuminating the quarters by his brilliance.

## \|\| 9.6.36 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasāyāntaṃ vasuṃ te tvantarikṣagam \|*  
*ūcurdvijātayo devāneṣa cchetsyati saṃśayam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Having seen Vasu passing through the atmosphere coming there all of a sudden, the Brāhmaṇas told the Devas: “He will remove your doubts”.

## \|\| 9.6.37-40 \|\|

*eṣa bhūmipatiḥ pūrvaṃ mahāyajñānsahasraśaḥ \|*  
*cakre sātvatatantroktavidhināraṇyakena ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

*yeṣu sākṣātpaśuvadhaḥ kasmiṃścidapi nā'bhavat \|*  
*na dakṣiṇānukalpaśca nāpratyakṣasurārccanam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*ahiṃsādharmarakṣābhyāṃ khyātosau sarvato nṛpaḥ \|*  
*agraṇīrviṣṇubhaktānāmekapatnīmahāvrataḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*īdṛśo dhārmikavaraḥ satyasandhaśca vedavit \|*  
*kathaṃcinnānyathā brūyādvākyameṣa mahānvasuḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

37-40. “This lord of the earth formerly performed ṃousands of great sacrifices according to the procedure laid down in the Sātvata Tantra and in Āraṇyakas, in any of which (sacrifice) killing of (sacrificial) beasts never took place. There was no adoption of a substitute for sacrificial fees. Nor was there even indirect homage paid to spirituous liquor. The king is known everywhere for his protection of Ahiṃsā (non-violence) and Dharma. He is the leader (i.e. most prominent one) among the devotees of Viṣṇu. He is an observer of the vow of having one wife only. How will this great Vasu, who is such a great religious person, speaker of the truth and expert in the knowledge of the Vedas, speak a word other than the truth?”

## \|\| 9.6.41 \|\|

*evaṃ te saṃvidaṃ kṛtvā vibudhā ṛṣayastathā \|*  
*apṛcchansahasā'bhyetya vasuṃ rājānamutsukāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Having reached such an agreement in opinion (about Vasu), Devas and sages who were eager, immediately approached King Vasu and asked him:

Devas and great sages asked:

## \|\| 9.6.42 \|\|

*devamaharṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*bho rājankena yaṣṭavyaṃ paśunā hosvidauṣadhaiḥ \|*  
*etaṃ naḥ saṃśayaṃ chindhi pramāṇaṃ no bhavānmataḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O king, with what should a sacrifice be performed—with a (sacrificial) beast or with plants, herbs (their products such as grains)? Since Your Honour have been regarded as an authority, please completely remove this doubt of ours.

## \|\| 9.6.43 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*sa tānkṛtāñjalirbhūtvā paripapraccha vai vasuḥ \|*  
*kasya vaḥ ko mataḥ pakṣo brūta satyaṃ samāhitāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

Skanda said:

43\. Vasu folded his palms in reverence and enquired: “Tell me with due deliberation, the truth as to what view is approved by whom.”

## \|\| 9.6.44 \|\|

*maharṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*dhānyairyaṣṭavyamityeva pakṣo'smākaṃ narādhipa \|*  
*devānāṃ tu paśuḥ pakṣo mataṃ rājanvadātmanaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

The great sages said:

44\. O ruler of peoples, our view is that a sacrifice is to be performed with grains. But the opinion of Devas is (that it should be performed) with a beast. O king, please tell us your view (in the matter).

## \|\| 9.6.45 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*devānāṃ tu mataṃ jñātvā vasustatpakṣasaṃśrayāt \|*  
*chāgādipaśunaivejyamityuvāca vacastadā \|\| 45 \|\|*

Skanda said:

45\. Having known the opinion of Devas, Vasu due to his support of their views then told that sacrifices are to be performed with beasts like goats.

## \|\| 9.6.46 \|\|

*evaṃ hi mānināṃ pakṣamasantaṃ sa upāśritaḥ \|*  
*dharmajñopyavadanmithyā vedaṃ hiṃsāparaṃ nṛpaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. He ṃus supported the view of those who believed in the wrong and evil. Though he was the knower of Dharma, the king spoke the untruth, which was violatory to the Veda.

## \|\| 9.6.47 \|\|

*null*

47\. At that very moment the king fell down from the sky due to his faulty (untrue) speech, and immediately entered the earth.

## \|\| 9.6.48 \|\|

*tasminnaiva kṣaṇe rājā vāgdoṣādantarikṣataḥ \|*  
*adhaḥ papāta sahasā bhūmiṃ ca praviveśa saḥ \|*  
*mahatīṃ vipadaṃ prāpa bhūmimadhyagato nṛpaḥ \|*  
*smṛtistvenaṃ na prajahau tadā nārāyaṇāśrayāt \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The king lying in the bowels of the earth experienced great distress. But due to his refuge in Nārāyaṇa, his memory did not fail (abandon) him.

## Chapter 7 - Uparicara Vasu Attains Liberation

## \|\| 9.7.1 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*bhūmadhyagaḥ sa rājā'tha svakṛtaṃ karma garhayan \|*  
*anutapyamānaśca bhṛśaṃ mānayaṃstābṛhanmunīn \|*  
*jajāpa bhagavanmantraṃ tryakṣaraṃ manasā sadā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Skanda said:

1\. Then the king who was in the bowels of the earth, censured his own act (of giving a false judgement). He deeply repented and paid respect to those great sages. In his mind he muttered the three-syllabled Mantra of the Lord.

## \|\| 9.7.2 \|\|

*tatrāpi parayā bhaktyā pañcakālaṃ svacetasā \|*  
*ayajaddhariṃ surapatiṃ bhūmervivara ādarāt \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. There, even in the chasm of the earth, the king respectfully and with great devotion, mentally worshipped Hari, the Lord of Devas, five times a day.

## \|\| 9.7.3 \|\|

*tato'sya tuṣṭo bhagavānvāsudevo jagatpatiḥ \|\| āpadyapi yathākālaṃ yathāśāstraṃ svamarcataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Then, Lord Vāsudeva, the protector of the world, was pleased with him (Vasu) who, even in adverse circumstances, worshipped him at the proper time and in accordance with the Śāstric injunctions.

## \|\| 9.7.4 \|\|

*varado bhagavānviṣṇuḥ samīpasthaṃ dvijottamam \|\| garutmantaṃ mahāvegamābabhāṣe svayaṃ tataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Lord Viṣṇu, the conferer of boons, spoke of his own accord to Garuḍa, the best of birds, and of great velocity, who was standing near him.

## \|\| 9.7.5-7 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*dvijottama mahābhāga gamyatāṃ vacanānmama \|*  
*samrāḍrājā vasurnāma dharmātmā māṃ samāśritaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*brahmātikramadoṣeṇa praviṣṭo vasudhātalam \|*  
*tanmānanā kṛtā tena tadgacchādya tadantikam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmya upīracaravasumokṣanirūpaṇaṃ nāma saptamo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

The Lord said:

5-7. O highly fortunate, excellent bird, go by my order. King Vasu, the paramount sovereign of men, a pious soul who has resorted to me, has entered the nether worlds due to his fault of transgressing the Veda (Vedic injunction regarding sacrifices). Respectful prayer has been made by him. Therefore, approach him today, O Garuḍa. By my order make the king capable of moving through the sky—the king who is concealed in the chasm of the earth and is able only to move beneath (the earth). Don’t delay.

## \|\| 9.7.8 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*garutmānatha vikṣipya pakṣau mārutavegavān \|*  
*viveśa vivaraṃ bhūmyā yatrāste vāgyato vasuḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

Skanda said:

8\. Then Garuḍa, of the speed of wind, spread out his wings and entered the chasm of the earth, where Vasu of controlled speech was staying.

## \|\| 9.7.9 \|\|

*tata enaṃ samutkṣipya svacañcvā vinatā sutaḥ \|*  
*utpapāta nabhastūrṇaṃ tatra cainamamuñcata \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The son of Vinatā (Garuḍa) lifted him up with his beak and immediately flew up in the sky and left him there.

## \|\| 9.7.10 \|\|

*tasminmuhūrtte saṃjajñe rājoparicaraḥ punaḥ \|*  
*saśarīro gataḥ svargaṃ paramaṃ sukhamāptavān \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. At that very moment, the king regained consciousness and again became one moving in higher regions. Along with his (physical) body he went to Svarga and got the supreme bliss.

## \|\| 9.7.11 \|\|

*evaṃ tenāpi brahmarṣe vāgdoṣātsadavajñayā \|*  
*prāptā gatirayajvārhā dharmajñena mahātmanā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O Brāhmaṇa-sage, in this way, on account of his disrespect for the truth (or saintly people), by his sinful transgressive speech, a state undeserving to performers of sacrifices was attained by that noble-souled knower of Dharma.

## \|\| 9.7.12 \|\|

*kevalaṃ puruṣastena sevito harirīśvaraḥ \|*  
*tataḥ śīghraṃ jahau pāpaṃ svargalokamavāpa ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Only Lord Hari, the Supreme Man, was served by him (through devotion). Thereby, he got absolved of sins quickly, and obtained (stay in) Svarga.

## \|\| 9.7.13 \|\|

*bhuñjāno vividhaṃ saukhyaṃ manobhīṣṭaṃ ca tatra saḥ \|*  
*uvāsānyo yathā śakro gīyamānayaśāḥ suraiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. There, he enjoyed different kinds of pleasures as desired by him. He lived there like another Indra, with his praises sung by Suras.

## \|\| 9.7.14 \|\|

*tamekadā vimānena carantaṃ sūryasannibham \|*  
*adrikāpsarasā yuktamacchodā samavaikṣata \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. On one occasion, Acchodā saw him moving in an aerial car, bright like the sun, accompanied by a divine damsel called Adrikā.

## \|\| 9.7.15 \|\|

*sā hi somapadasthānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ mānasī sutā \|*  
*agniṣvāttābhidhānānāmamūrttānāṃ mahātmanām \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. She was the mental daughter of the noble-souled, formless manes called Agniśvātta, who dwell in the domain of Soma.

## \|\| 9.7.16 \|\|

*amūrttatvātpitṝnsvānsā na jānantī śucismitā \|*  
*taṃ vasuṃ pitaraṃ mene sa ca tāmātmajāmiva \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The lady of pure smiles did not know her own ancestors due to their formlessness. She thought (king) Vasu as being her father. He too regarded her as his own daughter.

## \|\| 9.7.17-18 \|\|

*tau tataḥ pitaraḥ śepurbhāvaṃ dṛṣṭvedṛśaṃ tayoḥ \|*  
*kanye tvamasya nṛpaterbhuvi kanyā bhaviṣyasi \|\| 17 \|\|*

*vaso tvaṃ mānuṣo bhūtvā sutāmenāṃ svayoṣiti \|*  
*asyāmevāpsarāyāṃ tvaṃ janayiṣyasi niścitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Seeing their mutual feelings of such (filial) nature, the manes cursed them: “O daughter, you will be the veritable daughter of this king on the earth.

O Vasu, it is definite that you will be (born as) a human being on the earth and give birth to this (daughter of ours) as your daughter from this very divine lady as your wife.

## \|\| 9.7.19 \|\|

*itthaṃ tau pitṛbhiḥ śaptau śāpamokṣāya tāstataḥ \|*  
*prārthayāmāsaturnnatvā tadocuste kṛpālavaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Both of them who were thus cursed by the manes (Pitṛs), bowed down to them, and prayed to them for absolving them from the curse. Then those compassionate ones spoke:

## \|\| 9.7.20 \|\|

*avaśyamitthaṃ bhāvitvādyuvābhyāmupalambhitaḥ \|*  
*śāpo'yaṃ tatra yuvayoḥ śreya eva bhaviṣyati \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. “It was due to the inevitability of such events that this curse was incurred by you. But that will contribute to welfare of you both.

## \|\| 9.7.21 \|\|

*aṣṭāviṃśe dvāpare tu vaso tvaṃ bhuvi bhūpateḥ \|*  
*kṛtayajñasya tanayo bhavitāsi mahātmanaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O Vasu, in the twenty-eighth Dvāpara Yuga, you will be the son of noble-souled King Kṛtayajña on the earth.

## \|\| 9.7.22 \|\|

*tatrāpi ca yathedānīṃ tathā tvaṃ sakalairguṇaiḥ \|*  
*juṣṭaśca khacaro bhāvyo mahābhāgavatāgraṇīḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Even there (on the earth), you will be endowed with all your present qualities, capable of moving in the sky, a leader of the great devotees of the Lord.

## \|\| 9.7.23 \|\|

*pañcarātroktavidhinā viṣṇumabhyarcya bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*taccheṣeṇa surāṃścāsmānarcayiṣyasi saprajaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Having devoutly worshipped Viṣṇu as per procedure of the Pāñcarātra, you, along with your progeny, will worship Devas and us (Pitṛs) with the remnants (of Viṣṇu worship).

## \|\| 9.7.24 \|\|

*tatastvaṃ divyadehena svargalokamavāpsyasi \|*  
*divyānbhogāṃstatra bhuktvā prāpsyase vaiṣṇavaṃ padam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then you will attain Svarga with a divine body. Having enjoyed heavenly pleasures, you will get to the domain of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 9.7.25 \|\|

*acchode tvamapi kṣoṇyāṃ nāmnā kālīti viśrutā \|*  
*svāṃśena matsyadehāyāmadrikāyāṃ janiṣyase \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O Acchodā, you too will be born with a part of yours from Adrikā in the form of a (female) fish. You will be well-known on the earth as Kālī.

## \|\| 9.7.26 \|\|

*parāśarāttatra sutaṃ kanyeva prāpsyase harim \|*  
*prasādādeva tasya tvaṃ bhuktiṃ muktiṃ ca lapsyase \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. There, in your girlhood (in an unmarried state), you will have Hari as your son from Parāśara. Through his grace alone you will get enjoyment in life and liberation (after death).”

## \|\| 9.7.27 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*itthaṃ sa pitṛbhiḥ śapto'nugṛhītaśca bhūpatiḥ \|*  
*kṛtayajñādiha janiṃ prāpyā'bhūdviśruto guṇaiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

Skanda said:

27\. The king who was both imprecated and blessed by the Pitṛs, having been born of Kṛtayajña on the earth, became famous on account of his virtues.

## \|\| 9.7.28 \|\|

*yathā pūrvaṃ kṛṣṇabhakto daivapitryavidhānavit \|*  
*sakhye tasmai mahendraśca prādātpracurasaṃpadaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. As before (in his previous life), that knower of the procedure of worship of Devas and Pitṛs was a devotee of Kṛṣṇa. The great Indra gave his friend (Vasu) abundant wealth.

## \|\| 9.7.29 \|\|

*śvetadvīpe vāsudevātprāpto yo vijayadhvajaḥ \|*  
*purā svenārināśārthaṃ tasmā indrastamapyadāt \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Indra gave him even the Flag of Victory (Vijayadhvaja) which was formerly obtained by him from Vāsudeva in Śveta-dvīpa, for destroying his enemies.

## \|\| 9.7.30 \|\|

*antarikṣagatī rājā bhaumānbhogānsudurlabhān \|*  
*bhuktvānte svargalokaṃ ca divyadehena labdhavān \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The king who could move about in the sky enjoyed very rare earthly pleasures. In the end he attained the celestial world (endowed) with a heavenly body.

## \|\| 9.7.31 \|\|

*prākpuṇyaśeṣasya phalaṃ bhuñjansvamanasepsitān \|*  
*tatra bhogānbahuvidhāṃstīvraṃ vairāgyamāptavān \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Asa fruit of the balance of his meritorious acts in his previous birth, he enjoyed various kinds of pleasures as desired by his mind. He (then) developed intense aversion to worldly pleasures.

## \|\| 9.7.32 \|\|

*meroḥ śṛṅge'tha vijane śuciḥ kṛtadṛḍhāsanaḥ \|*  
*dadhyau svahṛdayāmbhoje sveṣṭadevaṃ ramāpatim \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. In a solitary place, on a peak of Meru, being pure, and sitting firmly on his seat, he meditated in the lotus of his heart on the consort of Ramā, the god worshipped by him with sacrifices.

## \|\| 9.7.33 \|\|

*tyaktvā devavapuḥ so'tha yogadhāraṇayā muniḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sūkṣmaśarīreṇa prāpa bhāskaramaṇḍalam \|*  
*yadāhurnaiṣṭhikānāṃ ca muktidvāraṃ hi yoginām \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Abandoning that celestial body, the sage, by his Yogic concentration of the mind, reached the disc of the Sun with his subtle body—the disc which is called the gate to salvation to perfectly firm Yogins.

## \|\| 9.7.34 \|\|

*tattejodagdhasūkṣmāṅgaḥ saccidūpo'tinirmalaḥ \|*  
*sa babhūva mahābhāgaḥ saṃkṣīṇāśeṣavāsanaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. His subtle body was burnt down by solar heat and lustre. He became extremely pure and of (i.e. endowed with) a body consisting of existence and consciousness. That blessed one became one whose ail residual traces of actions were wiped out.

## \|\| 9.7.35 \|\|

*tatastanmaṇḍalagatairātivāhikadaivataiḥ \|*  
*sa ninye vaiṣṇavaṃ dhāma śvetadvīpākhyamadbhutam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Then by deities faster than wind, who are in the disc (of the sun), he was taken to the wonderful abode of Viṣṇu, called Śveta-dvīpa.

## \|\| 9.7.3637 \|\|

*null*

36 37. O sage, though the island is on the earth, it is extraordinary. After having reached this residence of the devotees of Hari by exclusive devotion to the Lord, it serves as a gateway to Goloka, Brahmapura, Vaikuṇṭha to those noble-souled devotees desiring to get to them.

## \|\| 9.7.38 \|\|

*yasya yaddhāmna icchā syādbhajatastaṃ tadeva hi \|*  
*prāpayanti śvetamuktā mune prāguktalakṣaṇāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O sage, those released from Śveta-dvīpa whose characteristics have been described before, resort to that particular domain for which they cherish a desire.

## \|\| 9.7.39 \|\|

*divyadeho'bhavattatra dhāmnya'sau śvetamuktavat \|*  
*prāpya golokadhāmā'tha paramānandamāptavān \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. He became endowed with a divine body in that domain when released from Śveta-dvīpa. After reaching the world called Goloka, he obtained supreme delight.

## \|\| 9.7.40 \|\|

*itthamekāntikenaiva dharmeṇārādhayanti ye \|*  
*nārāyaṇaṃ paraṃ brahma śvetamuktā bhavaṃti te \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. In ṃis way, those who propitiate Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Brahman, by the Ekāntika Dharma (undivided devotion solely to Viṣṇu) become the liberated ones from Śveta.

## Chapter 8 - Curse to Devendra

## \|\| 9.8.1 \|\|

*sāvarṇiruvāca \|*  
*maharṣivāritairddevaistyakte hiṃsāmaye makhe \|*  
*punaḥ kathaṃ saṃpravṛttā makhāḥ sarvatra tādṛśāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: In this chapter also the curse-motif is used to explain Indra’s loss of fortune. The episode is mentioned in BhP and Brahmāṇḍa P. (Purāṇa Index II.106). The object here is to explain why Yajñas involving Hiṃsā came in vogue even after that punishment to Uparicara Vasu.

Sāvarṇi enquired:

1\. How is it that sacrifices (involving Hiṃsā) became prevalent again after sacrifices involving injury to animals were given up by Devas at the request of great sages?

## \|\| 9.8.2 \|\|

*deveṣvṛṣiṣu bhūpeṣu prācīnādhunikeṣu ca \|*  
*sanātanaḥ śuddhadharmo viparyāsaṃ kathaṃ gataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2 How is it that the eternal pure Dharma became perverse among ancient and modern Devas, sages and kings?

## \|\| 9.8.3 \|\|

*atra me saṃśayo bhūyānsaṃjāto'dya ṣaḍānana \|*  
*tvaṃ sarvaśāstratattvajñastamapākarttumarhasi \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O Six-faced God! A great doubt has been engendered today in me. You are a knower of the truth of all Śāstras. It behoves you to remove that doubt.

Skanda replied:

## \|\| 9.8.4 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*kālo balīyānbalināṃ bhidyante tena buddhayaḥ \|*  
*kāmakrodharasāsvādalobhamānavatāṃ mune \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Time (Kāla) is mighty. The minds of the powerful ones who are possessed of desire, anger, taste for liquor, avarice, pride are penetrated by Kāla.

## \|\| 9.8.5 \|\|

*atikrameṇa mahatāṃ yathārthahitabhāṣiṇām \|*  
*krodhamānavaśātpuṃsāṃ naśyantyeva ca saddhiyaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Good ideas of men become spoiled by being subjected to anger and pride owing to the transgression of (the advice of) the great ones who speak true and beneficial (words).

## \|\| 9.8.6 \|\|

*akāryamapi te kartuṃ tadānīṃ tu budhā api \|*  
*pravarttante'nutapyante bambhramyante'tha saṃsṛtau \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Even ṃough they are wise, they are intent on doing a criminal act, repent and continuously wander in Saṃsāra.

## \|\| 9.8.7 \|\|

*kāmādibhirvihīnā ye sātvatāḥ kṣīṇavāsanāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ tu buddhibhedāya kvāpi kālo na śaknute \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. But even Kāla (god of Death, Time) is not able to create aberrations in the mind of those who are devotees of Kṛṣṇa and are devoid of (illicit) desire for pleasure etc., and whose instinctive tendencies have all ceased.

## \|\| 9.8.8 \|\|

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye devendraśāpo nāmā'ṣṭamo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. I speak the truth that any person who does not resort to proper Dharma (path of virtue), shall never be liberated from Saṃsāra.

## \|\| 9.8.9 \|\|

*pravṛttiṃ hiṃsrayajñāderatha te dvijasattama \|*  
*kathayāmi yathā pūrvaṃ mayā'śrāvi piturmukhāt \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O most excellent Brāhmaṇa! I shall now narrate to you, the beginning of sacrifices involving violence, as I have heard it from the mouth of my father (Śiva).

## \|\| 9.8.10 \|\|

*atrāpyudāharantīmamitihāsaṃ purātanam \|*  
*nārāyaṇasya māhātmyaṃ yatra lakṣmyāśca kīrtitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Here they cite as an illustration this ancient legend in which Nārāyaṇa and Lakṣmī are glorified.

## \|\| 9.8.11 \|\|

*munīnāṃ bṛhatāṃ teṣāmatikramaṇadoṣataḥ \|*  
*indrasyāsīdviśvajitaḥ sadbuddhivilayo mune \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Due to his fault of transgressing great sages, the power of mentally perceiving rightly what is good, was lost by Indra called Viśvajit, O sage.

## \|\| 9.8.12 \|\|

*durvāsāḥ śaṃkarasyāṃśastapasvī munirekadā \|*  
*caranyadṛcchayā lokānpuṣpabhadrāṃ nadīṃ yayau \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Sage Durvāsas, a part of god Śaṅkara, a performer of penance, once happened to go to the river Puṣpabhadrā during his course of wanderings in the worlds.

## \|\| 9.8.13 \|\|

*jalakrīḍārthamāyāṃtīṃ svargāttatra sakhīvṛtām \|*  
*vidyādharasya sumateraṅganāṃ sa samaikṣata \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. There he saw the wife of a Vidyādhara named Sumati surrounded by her friends. She came down from heaven for water sports.

## \|\| 9.8.14 \|\|

*svargaṅgāhemakamalairgrathitāmatisaurabhām \|*  
*dadhatīṃ dakṣiṇe pāṇau srajaṃ madakalābhidhām \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. She was called Madakalā (‘one singing softly as if intoxicated’). She was holding in her right hand a very fragrant garland of golden lotuses from the Heavenly Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 9.8.15 \|\|

*tāmavekṣya munistasyāḥ samīpamupagamya saḥ \|*  
*unmattavadyayāce tāṃ srajaṃ vidyādharīdhṛtām \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Seeing her, the sage approached her. Like an intoxicated person, he requested for the garland held by the Vidyādhara lady.

## \|\| 9.8.16 \|\|

*sāpi praṇamya taṃ sadyo māhātmyaṃ tasya jānatī \|*  
*tatkaṃṭhe dhārayāmāsa mālāṃ tāṃ paramādarāt \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Knowing his greatness, she immediately bowed down to him, and out of great respect, she made him wear the garland round his neck.

## \|\| 9.8.17 \|\|

*tataḥ prītamanā gacchangāyannunmattavanmuniḥ \|*  
*dadarśa pathi devendramāyāntaṃ tāṃ mahānadīm \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Being highly pleased in mind, the sage went away singing like an inebriated person. On his way, he saw Devendra coming to the great river.

## \|\| 9.8.18 \|\|

*apsarobhiśca gandharvaiḥ satālaṃ madhurasvaram \|*  
*upagīyamānavijayamadhirūḍhaṃ gajādhipam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. His victories were being praised in sweet musical voice by divine damsels and musicians (Gandharvas). He was riding a royal elephant.

## \|\| 9.8.19 \|\|

*rambhāmadhurasaṃgītaśravaṇānandanirvṛtam \|*  
*tanmukhābjasthiradṛśaṃ chatracāmaraśobhitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He saw Indra who was lost in the ecstasy of hearing the sweet (vocal) music of Raṃbhā, whose eyes were fixed on her lotus-like face and looked splendid, embellished as he was with (royal) umbrella and chowries, but he was not looking at him (Durvāsas).

## \|\| 9.8.20 \|\|

*anavekṣamāṇamātmānaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā so'trinandanaḥ \|*  
*svakaṇṭhasthāṃ srajaṃ tasmiṃścikṣeponmattavaddhasan \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Seeing him, the son of Atri (i.e Durvāsas), laughing like an intoxicated person, hurled at him the garland he was wearing round his neck.

## \|\| 9.8.21 \|\|

*indropyadharmasargeṇa samāviṣṭaḥ puraiva yat \|*  
*tatastadā kāmavaśastāṃ nyadhādgajakumbhayoḥ \|*  
*tatsaurabhākṛṣṭacetāḥ karīndraḥ śuṇḍayā'kṛṣat \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Indra who was already possessed (as it were), due to his contact with Adharma (unrighteousness), was then overcome with passion, placed it on the temples of the elephant. The royal elephant, with his mind attracted by the fragrance, pulled it down with his trunk.

## \|\| 9.8.22 \|\|

*karātsā patitā bhūmau tāṃ ca gacchankarī padā \|*  
*mamardda paśyatastasya maharṣestapasāṃ nidheḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. From his trank it fell down on the ground. The elephant crushed it under his feet while he was walking—all this happened while the great sage, a storehouse of penance, was looking on.

## \|\| 9.8.23-26 \|\|

*tataḥ kruddhaḥ sa durvāsāḥ pralayāgnyaruṇekṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*prāhendraṃ matta duṣṭātmanstabdhosi kāmalampaṭa \|\| 23 \|\|*

*śriyo dhāma srajaṃ prītyā maddattāṃ nābhinandasi \|*  
*praṇāmamapi re mūḍha na karoṣi tvamunmadaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*na vīkṣase māmapi tvaṃ tvādṛṅmattaikaśikṣakam \|*  
*trailokyarājyaprāptāndhyaḥ samyaktvāṃ śikṣaye'dhunā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*yasyāḥ prasādāttrailokyarājyasaukhyaṃ tvamāptavān \|*  
*saiva śrīḥ satrilokaṃ tvāṃ hitvā līnā'stu sāgare \|\| 26 \|\|*

23-26. Then the infuriated Durvāsas, with his eyes red like the fire appearing at the time of world-destruction, spoke to Indra:

“O intoxicated wicked-souled one, addicted to licentious pleasures, you are arrogant. You do not welcome the garland, the abode of Goddess Śrī, given by me out of love (for you). You intoxicated fellow do not pay me obeisance, O fool. You do not take cognizance even of me who am the only person who (can) teach a lesson to an arrogant and inebriated fellow like you. You have become blind by getting the kingdom of the three worlds. Now I shall teach you properly. Goddess Śrī, with whose favour you are enjoying the kingdom of the three worlds, has abandoned you along with the three worlds and is submerged in the sea.”

## \|\| 9.8.27 \|\|

*vajrapātopamaṃ vākyaṃ tanniśamyaiva tatkṣaṇam \|*  
*gajādutplutya vimadastadaṃghryornyapataddhari \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. As soon as he heard his (Durvāsas’) words terrible like a stroke of thunderbolt, he at once jumped down from the elephant. With his pride humbled, Hari (Indra) fell at his feet.

## \|\| 9.8.28 \|\|

*prārthayāmāsa ca muhuḥ praṇamaṃstaṃ savepathuḥ \|*  
*prasādaṃ mayi dāse tvaṃ kṛpālo kartumarhasi \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Trembling and bowing down again and again, he prayed: “Compassionate as you are, it behoves you to show favour unto me.”

## Chapter 9 - Genesis of Yajñas involving Hiṃsā

## \|\| 9.9.1 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*bhāvidharmaviparyāsakālavegavaśo'tha saḥ \|*  
*nāhaṃ kṣamiṣya ityuktvā kailāsaṃ prayayau mune \|\| 1 \|\|*

Skanda said:

1\. O sage, under the influence of Time leading to the perversity of Dharma in future, he (Durvāsas) said, “I will not forgive” and went to Kailāsa.

## \|\| 9.9.2 \|\|

*trailokyācchrīrapi tadā samudrentarddhimāyayau \|*  
*indraṃ vihāyāpsarasaḥ sarvaśaḥ śriyamanvayuḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Goddess Śrī also then disappeared from the three worlds into the sea. All the celestial damsels in a body left Indra and followed Śrī.

## \|\| 9.9.3 \|\|

*tapaḥ śaucaṃ dayā satyaṃ pādaḥ saddharmaṛddhayaḥ \|*  
*siddhayaśca balaṃ sattvaṃ sarvataḥ śriyamanvayuḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Penance, Purity, Mercy, Truth, Pāda (?), True Dharma, Prosperity, Supernatural Powers, Strength, Sattva (quality of goodness)—all of them followed Śrī.

## \|\| 9.9.4 \|\|

*gajādīni ca yānāni svarṇādyābhūṣaṇāni ca \|*  
*cikṣipurmaṇiratnāni dhātūpakaraṇāni ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Vehicles, elephants and others, ornaments of gold etc., precious stones etc. and metal implements decreased.

## \|\| 9.9.5 \|\|

*annānyauṣadhayaḥ snehāḥ kālenālpena cikṣiyuḥ \|*  
*na kṣīraṃ dhenumahiṣīpramukhānāṃ staneṣva'bhūt \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Within a short time foods, plants, herbs, oils, greasy substances became scanty. No milk was generated in the udders of milk-giving beasts of which cows, she-buffaloes were prominent.

## \|\| 9.9.6 \|\|

*navāpi nidhayo naṣṭāḥ kuberasyāpi mandirāta \|*  
*indraḥ sahāmaragaṇairāsīttāpasasannibhaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. From the mansion of Kubera, even the nine treasures disappeared. Indra along with multitudes of Devas became like ascetics.

## \|\| 9.9.7 \|\|

*sarvāṇi bhogadravyāṇi nāśamīyustrilokataḥ \|*  
*devā daityā manuṣyāśca sarve dāridyapīḍitāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. All materials of enjoyment came to an end in all the three worlds. Devas, Daityas and human beings were afflicted with poverty.

## \|\| 9.9.8 \|\|

*kāntyā hīnastataścandraḥ prāpāmbutvaṃ mahodadhau \|*  
*anāvṛṣṭirmahatyāsīddhānyabījakṣayaṃkarī \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The moon became devoid of its lovely brightness, and became like water in the ocean. There was a terrific drought which ruined completely seeds and grains of corn.

## \|\| 9.9.9 \|\|

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye hiṃsrayajñapravṛttihetunirūpaṇaṃ nāma navamo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Repeatedly crying out ‘Where is food,?’ men emaciated with hunger and bereft of strength, left villages and towns and resorted to forests and mountains.

## \|\| 9.9.10 \|\|

*kṣudhārttāste paśūnhatvā grāmyānāraṇyakāṃstathā \|*  
*paktvā'paktvāpi vā kecitteṣāṃ māṃsānyabhuñjata \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Being overwhelmed with hunger, some of them killed animals, both wild and domesticated, and ate their flesh, either cooked or uncooked.

## \|\| 9.9.11 \|\|

*vidvāṃso munayaścā'tha ye vai saddharmacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*mriyamāṇāḥ kṣudhā'thāpi nāśnanta palalāni tu \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Learned men and sages who followed the true Dharma did not eat flesh, even though they were being starved to death.

## \|\| 9.9.12 \|\|

*tadā tu vṛddhā ṛṣayastāndṛṣṭvā'naśanādṛtān \|*  
*manubhiḥ saha vedoktamāpaddharmamabodhayan \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Seeing them taking to fasting and starvation, old sages along with Manu taught them Dharma to be followed in adversity as proclaimed by the Vedas.

Most of the sages whose sense-organs had become confused due to hunger gave perverse interpretation of the Vedas.

## \|\| 9.9.13-15 \|\|

*munayaḥ prāyaśastatra kṣudhā vyākulitendriyāḥ \|*  
*parokṣavādavedārthānviparītānprapedire \|\| 13 \|\|*

*arthaṃ cājādiśabdānāṃ mukhyaṃ chāgādimeva te \|*  
*bubudhuścā'tha te prāhuryajñān kuruta bho dvijāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*yā vedavihitā hiṃsā na sā hiṃsāsti doṣadā \|*  
*uddiśya devānpitṝṃśca tato ghnata paśūñchubhān \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. They took a word like Aja to means as a goat and exhorted, “O Brāhmaṇas, perform (animal) sacrifices. The violence (Hiṃsā) prescribed by the Vedas is not a fault or violence resulting in sin. Therefore, kill auspicious (sacrificial) beasts in the name of Devas and Pitṛs. Enjoy the flesh (of any animal) desired by you after it is consecrated with sprinkling of water and dedicated to deities and manes as Naivedya. But do not kill animals for your own sake.”

## \|\| 9.9.16 \|\|

*prokṣitaṃ devatābhyaśca pitṛbhyaśca niveditam \|*  
*bhuñjata svepsitaṃ māṃsaṃ svārthaṃ tu ghnata mā paśūn \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then Devas, sages, kings and men who were thus taught by them performed according to their capacities sacrifices, except those who were solely devoted to Hari.

## \|\| 9.9.17-18 \|\|

*tato devarṣibhūpālā narāśca svasvaśaktitaḥ \|*  
*cakrustairbodhitā yajñānṛte hyekāntikānhareḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*gomedhamaśvamedhaṃ ca naramedhamukhānmakhān \|*  
*cakruryajñāvaśiṣṭāni māṃsāni bubhujuśca te \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. They performed sacrifices like Go-medha (bull-sacrifice), Aśvamedha (horse-sacrifice) and sacrifices of which human-sacrifice was prominent and enjoyed the flesh that was left over after the sacrifice.

## \|\| 9.9.19 \|\|

*vinaṣṭāyāḥ śriyaḥ prāptyai kecidyajñāṃśca cakrire \|*  
*strīputramaṃdirādyarthaṃ kecicca svīyavṛttaye \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Some performed sacrifices for wealth that is lost. Some performed for obtaining women (wives), sons and house and some for (the prosperity of) their profession.

## \|\| 9.9.20 \|\|

*mahāyajñeṣvaśaktāstu pitṝnudiśya bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*nihatya śrāddheṣu paśūnmāṃsānyādaṃstathā'dayan \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Those who were unable to perform great sacrifices, killed on various occasions animals intending them for their Pitṛs (manes) in Śrāddhas and ate them and made others do so.

## \|\| 9.9.21 \|\|

*kecitsaritsamudrāṇāṃ tīreṣvevāvasañjanāḥ \|*  
*matsyāñjālairupādāya tadāhārā babhūvire \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Some people living on the shores of seas or banks of rivers, caught fishes with nets and became eaters of them (fish).

## \|\| 9.9.22 \|\|

*svagṛhāgataśiṣṭebhyaḥ paśūneva nihatya ca \|*  
*nivedayāmāsurete gochāgapramukhānmune \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O sage, by killing animals of which cows (bulls) and goats were prominent for the sake of distinguished guests, they served it to them.

## \|\| 9.9.23 \|\|

*sajātīyavivāhānāṃ niyamaśca tadā kvacit \|*  
*nābhavaddharmasāṃkaryādvittaveśmādyabhāvataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. At that time, in the absence of wealth, houses etc., and due to promiscuous mixture of Dharmas, no rule of marriage between individuals belonging to the same caste was observed.

## \|\| 9.9.24 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyādīnāṃ kṣatrādyā brahmaṇāṃ sutāḥ \|*  
*upayemire kālagatyā svasvavaṃśavivṛddhaye \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. In accordance with the damands \[demands?\] of times (and new trends), for the sake of enlargement and continuity of one’s race, Brāhmaṇas married daughters of Kṣatriyas (and oṃer castes) and Kṣatriyas and others married daughters of Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 9.9.25 \|\|

*itthaṃ hiṃsāmayā yajñāḥ saṃpravṛttā mahāpadi \|*  
*dharmastvābhāsamātro'sthātsvayaṃ tu śriyamanvagāt \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Thus in that great calamity, sacrifices involving Hiṃsā were commenced. Dharma itself followed Goddess Śrī (to the bottom of the sea), while a semblance of Dharma remained.

## \|\| 9.9.26 \|\|

*adharmaḥ sānvayo lokāṃstrīnapi vyāpya sarvataḥ \|*  
*avarddhatā'lpakālena durnivāryo budhairapi \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Adharma along with its consequents pervaded all the three worlds and thrived within a short time. It was extremely difficult to be checked by the wise and learned people.

## \|\| 9.9.27 \|\|

*daridrāṇāmathaiteṣāmapatyāni tu bhūriśaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ ca vaṃśavistāro mahāṃllokeṣvavarddhata \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. There were numerous children produced by those poverty-stricken people and the extensions of their families increased greatly in the world.

## \|\| 9.9.28 \|\|

*vidvāṃsastatra ye jātāste tu dharmaṃ tameva hi \|*  
*menire mukhyamevā'tha granthāṃścakruśca tādṛśān \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Those who became learned among them regarded it (i.e. Adharma, the then prevalent practices) as the real Dharma, and wrote treatises accordingly.

## \|\| 9.9.29 \|\|

*te paramparayā granthāḥ prāmāṇyaṃ pratipedire \|*  
*ādye tretāyuge hītthamāsīddharmasya viplavaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Those treatises became authoritative in due course by the power of tradition. In the first Tretā Yuga Dharma took such an evil turn.

## \|\| 9.9.30 \|\|

*tataḥprabhṛti lokeṣu yajñādau paśuhiṃsanam \|*  
*babhūva satye tu yuge dharma āsītsanātanaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Then onwards, killing of animals in Yajña (sacrifices) and on other (religious) occasions gained currency. It was only in Satya (Kṛta) Yuga that there prevailed the eternal Dharma.

## \|\| 9.9.31 \|\|

*kālena mahatā sopi saha devaiḥ surādhipaḥ \|*  
*ārādhya saṃpadaṃ prāpa vāsudevaṃ prabhuṃ mune \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. After a long time, Indra, the Lord of Devas, along with Devas, propitiated Lord Vāsudeva and regained his prosperity, O sage.

## \|\| 9.9.32 \|\|

*tato dharmaniketasya śrīpateḥ kṛpayā hareḥ \|*  
*yathāpūrvaṃ ca saddharmastrilokyāṃ saṃpravarttata \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Then through the grace of Hari, the Lord of Śrī and the seat (refuge) of Dharma, the real Dharma spread about in the three worlds.

## \|\| 9.9.33 \|\|

*tatrāpi kecinmunayo nṛpā devāśca mānuṣāḥ \|*  
*kāmakrodharasāsvādalobhopahatasaddhiyaḥ \|*  
*tamāpaddharmamadyāpi prādhānyenaiva manvate \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Still there are some Devas, sages, and men whose good minds are adversely affected by sex, anger, greed and relish for (non-vegetarian) taste, who regard the Āpad-dharma (i.e. practices allowable in time of distress) as the main Dharma.

## \|\| 9.9.34 \|\|

*ekāntino bhāgavatā jitakāmādayastu ye \|*  
*āpadyapi na te'gṛhṇaṃstaṃ tadā kimutā'nyadā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Devotees of the Lord, who have conquered their passions, and who are solely devoted to the Lord, do not take to them (those practices) even while under duress. What to say of other occasions!

## Chapter 10 - The Grace of Śrī Vāsudeva

## \|\| 9.10.1 \|\|

*sāvarṇiruvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ prāptā punaḥ skanda śrīrindreṇa gatāmbudhim \|\| etāṃ kathaya me sarvāṃ kathāṃ nārāyaṇāśrayām \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sāvarṇi said:

1\. O Skanda, how was Goddess Śrī, who was submerged in the sea, regained by Indra? Tell me the whole episode associated with Nārāyaṇa.

## \|\| 9.10.2 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*śriyā vihīno devendraḥ śrīhīnairapi dānavaiḥ \|*  
*parājito hṛtasthāno naṣṭāśeṣaparicchadaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Skanda said:

2\. Devendra who was devoid of Śrī was defeated by Dānavas who themselves were bereft of Śrī. He was deprived of his position and all the retinue.

## \|\| 9.10.3 \|\|

*girigahvarakuñjeṣu kānaneṣu tatastataḥ \|*  
*paribabhrāma sahito digīśairvaruṇādibhiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Along with the Lords of (different) quarters like Varuṇa and others he wandered in different mountains, valleys, places overgrown with creepers and forests.

## \|\| 9.10.4 \|\|

*valkalājina vastrāśca paśupakṣyāmiṣāśanāḥ \|*  
*devā daityā narā nāgāstulyācāraparicchadāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. They wore garments made of barks and skins. They consumed the flesh of animals and birds. The behaviour and garments of Devas, Daityas, men and reptiles (Nāgas) were all alike.

## \|\| 9.10.5 \|\|

*pātrāṇi mṛnmayānyeva sarveṣāmapi veśmasu \|*  
*āsanvarākāḥ sarvepi piśācya iva ca striyaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. In all their homes the utensils were made of earth only. Women (wives) of all of them were wretched and miserable like female Piśācas (ogresses).

## \|\| 9.10.6 \|\|

*ādāvabhūdanāvṛṣṭirbhuvi dvādaśavārṣikī \|*  
*tato varṣe kvacidvṛṣṭirāsītsvalpā kvacinna ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. At first there was total absence of rainfall for twelve years on the earth. Then during the course of a year there were few showers at some places, while there was none elsewhere.

## \|\| 9.10.7 \|\|

*itthaṃ dāridryaduḥkhānāṃ teṣāṃ varṣaśataṃ gatam \|*  
*baliṣṭhārabdhakarmāṇaste'tiduḥkhepi no mṛtāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. In this way they passed one hundred years in poverty and suffering. But due to their powerful destiny they did not die even in extreme misery.

## \|\| 9.10.8 \|\|

*ajīvanta mṛtaprāyā narakeṣviva nārakāḥ \|*  
*yatantopi śriyaḥ prāptyai yajñādyairnnā'labhanta tām \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. They lived like hellish beings in hells but were almost dead. Even though they tried to gain Śrī by performing sacrifice etc., they did not succeed.

## \|\| 9.10.9 \|\|

*tataḥ sahasravarṣānte merau śaraṇamāyayuḥ \|*  
*śāpāddurvāsaso devāḥ sarve durvāsaso vidhim \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then at the end of one thousand years Devas who were beggarly-attired due to the curse of Durvāsas, sought refuge in God Brahmā.

## \|\| 9.10.10 \|\|

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇava khaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye śrīvāsudevaprasādanirūpaṇaṃ nāma daśamo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Devas including Indra and others, paid obeisance to him and narrated the tale of their misery. But due to his omniscience he already knew the plight of the Suras.

## \|\| 9.10.11 \|\|

*upālabhya tataścendraṃ viriñcaḥ sahaśaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*tadduḥkhavāraṇā kalpo viṣṇumaicchatprasāditum \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. God Brahmā, along with Śaṅkara who was capable of warding off his misery, censured Indra and expressed the desire (to Indra) to propitiate Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 9.10.12 \|\|

*ārādhayiṣyaṃstapasā tato'sau taṃ tapaḥpriyam \|*  
*sarvadevagaṇopeta upāyātkṣīrasāgaram \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. By his penance he (Indra) propitiated him, to whom penance was dear. Then he, accompanied with all categories of Devas, went to the Milk-Ocean.

## \|\| 9.10.13 \|\|

*tasyottare taṭe ramye sarve te'naśanavratāḥ \|*  
*ekapādasthitā ūrddhvabāhavaścakrire tapaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On the beautiful northern shore of that ocean, they who had taken the vow of fasting, performed penance, standing on one leg with arms raised up.

## \|\| 9.10.14 \|\|

*keśavaṃ hṛdi te dadhyuḥ sarvakleśavināśanam \|*  
*lakṣmīpatiṃ vāsudevamekāgrakṛtamānasāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. With their minds concentrated, they meditated in their heart on Keśava, Vāsudeva, the consort of Lakṣmī, the destroyer of all troubles and miseries.

## \|\| 9.10.15 \|\|

*śatābdānte tato viṣṇuḥ śrīkṛṣṇo bhagavānsvayam \|*  
*atyāpanneṣu dīneṣu kṛpāṃ deveṣu so'karot \|\| 15 \|\|*
