15\. At the end of a hundred years Lord Viṣṇu, Śrī Kṛṣṇa himself, showed favour unto the poor Devas who were extremely miserable.

## \|\| 9.10.16 \|\|

*adṛśyamūrtirātmajñairapi bhūritapasvibhiḥ \|*  
*tatrāvirāsītkṛpayā niyutāhaskaradyutiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He whose form was invisible even to self-knowing performers of great penance, manifested himself out of grace with the brilliance of a million suns.

## \|\| 9.10.17 \|\|

*tejomaṇḍalamevādau sahasā sphuritaṃ mahat \|*  
*dadṛśurvibudhāḥ sarve sitaṃ ghanamanaupamam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. At first, a very brilliant disc of refulgence suddenly flashed forth. All the Devas saw that unparalleled white cloud.

## \|\| 9.10.18 \|\|

*brahmā śivaśca tanmadhye dadṛśāte ramāpatim \|*  
*ghanaśyāmaṃ caturbāhuṃ gadābjābjāridhāriṇam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. God Brahmā and Śiva espied within it the Four-armed Lord of Ramā, of bluish-dark complexion like a cloud, holding in his hands a mace, a conch, a lotus and a discus.

## \|\| 9.10.19 \|\|

*kirīṭakāñcīkaṭakakuṇḍalādivibhūṣitam \|*  
*pītakauśeyavasanaṃ divyasundaravigraham \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He was adorned with a crown, a girdle, bracelets of gold, earrings etc. He was wearing yellow silken garment and his person was divinely beautiful.

## \|\| 9.10.20 \|\|

*harṣavihvalitānmānau daṇḍavattau praṇematuḥ \|*  
*tadicchayā'tha devāśca dṛṣṭvā taṃ ca mudā'naman \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. With their minds overwhelmed with ecstasy, both of them prostrated themselves like a staff. Devas seeing him through his desire (to be seen by them), bowed down to him with joy.

## \|\| 9.10.21 \|\|

*babhūvuratihṛṣṭāste nidhiṃ prāpyā'dhanā iva \|*  
*baddhāñjalipuṭāḥ sarve bhaktyā taṃ tuṣṭuvuḥ surāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Like a penniless person getting a treasure-trove, they became overjoyed. With their palms folded in reverence, all the Devas devoutly praised him.

Devas prayed:

## \|\| 9.10.22 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*oṃnamo bhagavate tubhyaṃ vāsudevāya dhīmahi \|*  
*pradyumnāyāniruddhāya namaḥ saṃkarṣaṇāya ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Oṃ, obeisance to you, O venerable Lord Vāsudeva. We meditate upon you. Bow to you, Pradyumna, Aniruddha, Saṅkarṣaṇa (i.e. all the Vyūhas of Vāsudeva).

## \|\| 9.10.23 \|\|

*oṃkārabrahmarūpāya tredhāviṣkṛtamūrtaye \|*  
*brahmāṇḍasargasthityantahetave nirguṇāya ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. (Obeisance to you) of the form of Oṃkāra, Brahman who have manifested your threefold form, the cause of the creation, maintenance and destruction of the Cosmic Egg, one devoid of (three) Guṇas.

## \|\| 9.10.24 \|\|

*nayanānandarūpāya praṇatakleśanāśine \|*  
*keśavāya namastubhyaṃ svataṃtreśvaramūrtaye \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. (Bow to you) whose form gives delight to the eyes, the destroyer of the troubles of those who how down to you; obeisance to you Keśava, the form of the supreme being.

## \|\| 9.10.25 \|\|

*moditāśeṣabhaktāya kālamāyādimohine \|*  
*sadānaṃdāya kṛṣṇāya namaḥ saddharmavarttine \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Bow to (you) Kṛṣṇa who give delight to all his devotees, the fascinator (deluder) of Kāla, Māyā and others, who are forever delightful, who abide by the proper Dharma.

## \|\| 9.10.26 \|\|

*bhavāmbudhinimagrānāmuddhṛtikṣamakīrtaye \|*  
*darśanīyasvarūpāya ghanaśyāmāya te namaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Obeisance to you who are famous as being capable of saving persons who are submerged in the ocean of worldly existence, to one of beautiful form, dark like a cloud.

## \|\| 9.10.27 \|\|

*gadābjadaracakrāṇi bibhrate dīrghabāhubhiḥ \|*  
*suragovipradharmāṇāṃ goptre tubhyaṃ namonamaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Repeated obeisance to the wielder of the mace, lotus, conchshell and discus with your long arms, the protector of Devas, cows, Brāhmaṇas and of Dharma.

## \|\| 9.10.28 \|\|

*vareṇyāya prapannānāmabhīṣṭavaradāyine \|*  
*nigamāgamavedyāya vedagarbhāya te namaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Bow to the most excellent one, the bestower of desired boons to those who seek refuge, one worthy of being known through Vedas and Āgamas, and who are the essence of all Vedas.

## \|\| 9.10.29 \|\|

*tejomaṇḍalamadhyastha divyasundaramūrtaye \|*  
*namāmo viṣṇave tubhyaṃ parātparatarāya ca \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. We pay obeisance to you, O Viṣṇu, whose resplendent, beautiful form exists within a halo of light, who are greater than the greatest.

## \|\| 9.10.30 \|\|

*vāṇīmanoviprakṛṣṭamahimne'kṣararūpiṇe \|*  
*sarvāntaryāmiṇe tubhyaṃ bṛhate ca namonamaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Repeated obeisance to you, the great one, whose greatness is far beyond the ken of speech and mind, who are of imperishable form, who abide within the hearts of all.

## \|\| 9.10.31 \|\|

*sukhadosi tvamevaikaḥ svāśritānāmato vayam \|*  
*mahāpadadhikakliṣṭāḥ śaraṇaṃ tvāmupāgatāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. You alone are the one who give happiness to those who resort to you. Hence we who are deeply troubled by great adversity, have sought refuge in you.

## \|\| 9.10.32 \|\|

*devādhidevabhaktasya tava durvāsaso vayam \|*  
*atikramācchriyā hīnāḥ prāptāḥ smo durdaśāmimām \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Due to our offensive behaviour towards Durvāsas, a devotee of the God of Gods, we became bereft of Śrī and have been reduced to this wretched plight.

## \|\| 9.10.33 \|\|

*vāsonnapānasthānādihīnāndharmopi naḥ prabho \|*  
*tyaktvā saha śriyā yātastānpātuṃ tvamasīśvaraḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. O Lord, abandoning us who are devoid of clothes, food, drink, residence etc., even Dharma went away along with Śrī. You are the Supreme Lord to protect us.

## \|\| 9.10.34 \|\|

*yato vayaṃ ca dharmaśca tvadīyā iti viśrutāḥ \|*  
*yathāpūrvaṃ sukhīkarttuṃ tvamevārhasyato hi naḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Inasmuch as it is well-known that we as well as Dharma are yours, it behoves you to restore us to happiness as before.

## \|\| 9.10.35 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*iti saṃprārthito devairbhagavānsa dayānidhiḥ \|*  
*uvācānandayanvācā meghagambhīrayā surān \|\| 35 \|\|*

Skanda said:

35\. The Lord, the store of mercy, who was thus implored by Devas, addressed the Suras, delighting them with a voice deep like the rumbling of a cloud.

## \|\| 9.10.36 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*viditaṃ me surāḥ sarvaṃ kaṣṭaṃ vaḥ sadatikramāt \|*  
*upāyaṃ kurutādyaiva vacmi yattannivṛttaye \|\| 36 \|\|*

The Lord said:

36\. All the misery suffered by you on account of your offensive behaviour towards the good (sage Durvāsas) is known to me. I shall advise you a remedy for removing it, upon which you act this very day.

## \|\| 9.10.37 \|\|

*oṣadhīrambudhau sarvāḥ kṣiptvā mandarabhūbhṛtā \|*  
*nāgarājavaratreṇa maṃthadhvamasuraiḥ saha \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. After throwing all medicinal plants in the sea, you, along with Asuras, churn it with Mount Mandara (as the churning rod) and (Vāsuki), the king of cobras, as the strap (to churn it).

## \|\| 9.10.38 \|\|

*ādau saṃdhāya danujaiḥ kurutāmbudhimanthanam \|*  
*sāhāyaṃ vaḥ kariṣyāmi khedaḥ kāryo na tatra vaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. First enter into an agreement with Dānavas, and then begin the churning of the ocean. I shall help you. You need not get depressed.

## \|\| 9.10.39 \|\|

*amṛtaṃ ca śriyo dṛṣṭiṃ prāpya pūrvādhikaujasaḥ \|*  
*bhavitāro madvimukhā daityāstu kleśabhāginaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. After getting the Nectar and the (favourable) glance of Śrī, you wilt be much more brilliant than before. Daityas who are averse to me, will be the sufferers.

## Chapter 11 - Churning for the Nectar: Birth of the Poison Kālakūṭa

## \|\| 9.11.1 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*brahmarudrau mahendrādīnsaṃdhānāyā'suraiḥ saha \|*  
*ājñāpya jagmatuḥ svaṃsvaṃ dhāma devā rasāṃ mune \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: The belief in the existence of an immortality-giving liquid medicine and how it was churned out of the sea by Devas and Asuras and how the Asuras were cheated by Viṣṇu in a female form is found in most Purāṇas and Mbh.

Skanda said:

1\. Having ordered Mahendra and others ot have consultation with Asuras, Gods Brahmā and Rudra went to their respective residence. And Devas went to the earth.

## \|\| 9.11.2 \|\|

*samayocitabhāṣāvidvāsavo nītiyuktibhiḥ \|*  
*pralobhya phalabhāgena sandhiṃ cakre'suraiḥ saha \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Indra who was expert in making speech suitable for bringing about an understanding, tempted them (i.e. Asuras) with the offer of a share in the fruit (of the joint effort) with (arguments of) skilful stratagems of policy and entered into an agreement with the Asuras.

## \|\| 9.11.3 \|\|

*tato devāsuragaṇā militā vāridhestaṭe \|*  
*mahauṣadhīrupānīya bahuśo nidadhurdrutam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Then multitudes of Devas and Asuras gathered on the shore of the sea. Bringing huge quantities of medicinal plants of great potency they quickly deposited them in the sea.

## \|\| 9.11.4 \|\|

*mandarādrimupetyā'tha nānauṣadhivirājitam \|*  
*mūlādutpāṭya te sarve netumabdhiṃ samudyatāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Then they approached Mount Mandara which looked splendid with various kinds of medicinal plants. All of them got eagerly engaged in uprooting it from its bottom.

## \|\| 9.11.5 \|\|

*ekādaśasahasrāṇi yojanānāṃ bhuvi sthitam \|*  
*noddhartumaśakaṃste taṃ tadānīṃ tuṣṭuvurharim \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. As they could not uproot it, since it had roots eleven thousand Yojanas deep in the earth, they praised Hari.

## \|\| 9.11.6 \|\|

*etadviditvā bhagavānsaṃkarṣaṇamahīśvaram \|*  
*ajijñapattamuddhartuṃ baddhamūlaṃ mahīdharam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Knowing it, the Lord ordered Saṅkarṣaṇa, the Lord of the earth, to extract the mountain which was firmly rooted.

## \|\| 9.11.7 \|\|

*phūtkāramātreṇaikena sa tu sadyastamīśvaraḥ \|*  
*bahiścikṣepa tatsthānādyojanadvitayāntare \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Immediately with one hissing only, the Lord hurled it from that place to a distance of two Yojanas.

## \|\| 9.11.8 \|\|

*atyāścaryaṃ tadālokya hṛṣṭāḥ sarve surāsurāḥ \|*  
*tadantikamupājagmurddhāvantaśca kṛtāravāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Seeing the extremely wonderous feat, all Suras and Asuras were highly delighted. Shouting loudly, they went a-running and reached near it.

## \|\| 9.11.9 \|\|

*balino yatnavantopi parighopamabāhavaḥ \|*  
*uddhṛtya netuṃ no śekurviṣaṇṇā viphalaśramāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Powerful and endowed with arms like iron bars for locking doors, they could not lift it up to carry, though they tried their best. Due to the fruitlessness of their labour, they became sad.

## \|\| 9.11.10 \|\|

*jñātvā suragaṇānkhinnānbhagavānsarvadarśanaḥ \|*  
*tārkṣyamājñāpayāmāsa netuṃ tamudadhiṃ drutam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The Lord who sees everything, knew that all the multitudes of Devas were dejected. He ordered Garuḍa to take it immediately to the sea.

## \|\| 9.11.11 \|\|

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye'mṛtamanthane viṣotpattirnāmaikādaśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He (Garuḍa) who was powerful enough to hold (lift) the Cosmic Egg along with its sheaths, and whose speed was like that of mind, came there and with his beak he lifted the mountain, deposited it near the sea and returned to Hari.

## \|\| 9.11.12 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃhṛṣṭamanasaḥ sarve kaśyapanandanāḥ \|*  
*vāsukiṃ cāhvayāmāsuḥ sudhābhāgapratijñayā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Then all the sons of Kaśyapa (i.e. Suras and Asuras) with delighted minds visited Vāsuki with a solemn promise to give share in the Nectar.

## \|\| 9.11.13 \|\|

*sa tatrāgādatho sarve te'bdhiṃ manthitumudyatāḥ \|*  
*tānapānnidhirāgatya mūrttimānabravīdvacaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then all of them went to the sea. They became ready to churn it, when the sea presented himself in person and spoke as follows:

## \|\| 9.11.14 \|\|

*yadi dāsyatha me yūyamamṛtāṃśaṃ surāsurāḥ \|*  
*soḍhāsmi vipulaṃ tarhi mandarabhramaṇārddanam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. “O Suras and Asuras! If you will give me some share of the Nectar I shall bear the torments of the churning with Mandara.”

## \|\| 9.11.15 \|\|

*tatheti te pratijñāya kṣiptvādāvoṣadhīlatāḥ \|*  
*parivivyurnnāgarājaṃ tasminkāñcanaparvate \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Promising him to do so, they first ṃrew in it medicinal plants and creepers, and wound the king of Nāgas (Cobras) round that golden mountain.

## \|\| 9.11.16 \|\|

*tato devā hṛdi hariṃ sasmaruḥ kāryasiddhaye \|*  
*smṛtamātraḥ sa tatrā'gādacyutaḥ sarvadarśanaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then Devas remembered Hari in their hearts for (getting) success in the undertaking. Acyuta who sees everything came there the moment they remembered him.

## \|\| 9.11.17 \|\|

*tamālokyāmaragaṇā muditāḥ phaṇināṃ pateḥ \|*  
*purobhāgaṃ gṛhītvaiva tasthustenānumoditāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The multitude of Devas became glad at his sight. They stood there holding the front part (i.e. mouth) of the Lord of snakes, with the Lord’s approval.

## \|\| 9.11.18-19 \|\|

*devatāpakṣapātitvaṃ sūcayansvasya ca prabhuḥ \|*  
*yatra devāstatra tasthau tato daityāstu cukrudhuḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tapovidyāvayojyeṣṭhā adhobhāgamamaṅgalam \|*  
*kathaṃ tiraśco gṛhṇīmo nedṛṅmūrkhā vayaṃ tviti \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Showing his partiality to Devas, the Lord stood where the Devas were standing. But then the Daityas became enraged. “We are senior in penance, learning and age (to Devas). How should we hold the inauspicious (dirty) lower part of this (i.e. serpent)? We are not such fools.”

## \|\| 9.11.20 \|\|

*saha devaistato viṣṇuḥ svayaṃ tānmānayanniva \|*  
*prahasya dattvā prāgbhāgaṃ surānpucchamajigrahat \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. (As if) showing respect to them, Viṣṇu, along with Devas laughed loudly and giving the front part (mouṃ, to Asuras), made Suras hold the tail (of Vāsuki).

## \|\| 9.11.21 \|\|

*mahāhiviṣaphūtkāradāhādamararakṣaṇam \|*  
*caritrametacchrībharturiti daityā na te viduḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The Daityas did not know that his act of the Lord of Śrī was (for) the protection of the immortal ones (Devas) from the heat of the poisonous hissing of the great snake.

## \|\| 9.11.22 \|\|

*tata uttolayāmāsuḥ svarṇasānvālibhāsvaram \|*  
*mandaraṃ kāśyapeyāste carmikābaddhakacchakāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Then, the sons of Kaśyapa (Devas and Asuras) with their ends of lower garments tucked into the waistband and fastened with leather straps, raised up the golden-peaked Mandara resplendently dark like a big black bee.

## \|\| 9.11.23 \|\|

*dvāviṃśatisahasrāṇi yojanānāṃ tamucchritam \|*  
*ambhonidhau nidadhire krośantotyarthamutsukāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Shouting loudly and extremely eager, they placed that mountain of twenty-two thousand Yojanas in height, into the sea.

## \|\| 9.11.24 \|\|

*dhāryamāṇopyanādhārastairadriratigauravāt \|*  
*yayāvadhastalaṃ sadyastadāsaṃste'tivihvalāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The mountain, though held up by them, had no support below. Due to its extremely heavy weight, it went down to the bottom (of the sea). And they were greatly agitated.

## \|\| 9.11.25 \|\|

*tadā sa bhagavānsākṣātsarvathā bhaktakāryakṛt \|*  
*stūyamānomarairadrimuddaghre kamaṭhākṛtiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Then the Lord himself who always carries out the tasks of his devotees, was praised by Devas. The Lord in the form of a tortoise lifted it (the mountain) from below.

## \|\| 9.11.26 \|\|

*utthitaṃ tamavekṣyāśu sarve phullahṛdānanāḥ \|*  
*babhūvuśca sthiraḥ so'bhūtkūrmapṛṣṭhetivistṛte \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. As soon as they saw it lifted up, the hearts and faces of them all bloomed with joy. The mountain became stable on the very extensive back of the tortoise.

## \|\| 9.11.27 \|\|

*tato mamanthustarasā yāvadbalamapāṃnidhim \|*  
*śramaphūtkāravadanā devādayo'dayam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Then the Devas and others with all their power, churned the ocean very fast with incessant hissing sound of exhaustion coming out of their mouth.

## \|\| 9.11.28 \|\|

*bhrāmyamāṇāttatastvadrerbahavonyapatandumāḥ \|*  
*ūrddhvadrugharṣajo vahnistatstha siṃhādimādahat \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. While the mountain was being whirled (round and round), many trees fell down and the fire generated from their friction burnt down lions and oṃers.

## \|\| 9.11.29 \|\|

*tatra nānā jalacarā vinipiṣṭā mahādriṇā \|*  
*vilayaṃ samupājagmuḥ śataśaḥ kṣīravāridhau \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Many aquatic animals were pounded down by the great mountain and met death by hundreds in the Milk-Ocean.

## \|\| 9.11.30 \|\|

*sāṃvarttakamahāmeghasaṅghagarjjitavanmahān \|*  
*āsīnmaṃthananādaśca pratidhvanivivarddhitaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The roaring sound of the churning was loud like deep ṃunder-ing sound of a multitude of Saṃvartaka clouds (appearing at the destruction of the world). And it (i.e. roaring sound) was intensified with its echo.

## \|\| 9.11.31 \|\|

*atyākarṣaṇakhinnāṅgavāsukarmmukhakṛtkṛtaiḥ \|*  
*hataujaso'tikhinnāśca daityā niṅgālavadbabhuḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. By hissing and puffing out of the mouth of Vāsuki, whose body was distressed and exhausted by powerful pulling, the Daityas became bereft of power and extremely exhausted and shone like burning coals.

## \|\| 9.11.32 \|\|

*aviṣahyaṃ viṣāgniṃ ca marṣanti bahudhā muhuḥ \|*  
*lambante smāhirājasya sahasraṃ vadanānyadhaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. They constantly suffered (from) the unbearable poisonous fire. The thousand mouths of the king of serpents dropped down through fatigue.

## \|\| 9.11.33 \|\|

*dadhāra sahasā tāni bhagavanprerito vibhuḥ \|*  
*saṃkarṣaṇo mahātejāḥ sahamāno viṣānalam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Lord Saṅkarṣaṇa (Śeṣa) of great lustre bore the poisonous fire and at once held them (i.e. the mouths of Vāsuki) up as directed by the Lord (Viṣṇu).

## \|\| 9.11.34 \|\|

*sahasramekaṃ varṣāṇāṃ mathyamānātpayonidheḥ \|*  
*hālāhalaṃ viṣamabhūdutsarpadvidiśo diśaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. From the ocean that was being churned for one thousand years, there came out the poison Halāhala spreading to all the quarters and sub-quarters.

## \|\| 9.11.35 \|\|

*yadāhuḥ kālakūṭākhyaṃ sarvalokātidāhakam \|*  
*tena dandahyamānāṅgāste tu cakruḥ palāyanam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. They (Suras and Asuras) whose bodies were constantly scorched by the poison called Kālakūṭa which burns down the three worlds, ran, away.

## \|\| 9.11.36 \|\|

*tato brahmā prajeśāśca devāḥ sarvepyumāpatim \|*  
*prārthayaṃstasya pānārthaṃ stuvantaḥ stutibhirmune \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Then God Brahmā, Devas, Protectors of Prajās, all of them praised Śiva, the consort of Umā, praying to him for drinking up the poison.

## \|\| 9.11.37 \|\|

*bhagavānatha taṃ prāha surāṇāmagrajo bhavān \|*  
*bhavatītyagrajaṃ vārddhergṛhāṇedaṃ viṣaṃ śiva \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The Lord told him, “you were born first and are the senior-most of the Devas. This poison is born first out of the ocean. Hence you take it.”

## \|\| 9.11.38 \|\|

*devānāṃ sa bhayaṃ dṛṣṭvā karuṇaścājñayā hareḥ \|*  
*ākarṣadyogakalayā viṣaṃ pāṇitale'khilam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The merciful Śiva, seeing the fright of Devas and due to the order of Hari, sucked up, by his yogic power, the whole of the poison on his palm.

## \|\| 9.11.39 \|\|

*papau tatkaṇṭhamadhye ca śoṣayāmāsa tatkṣaṇam \|*  
*nīlakaṇṭha iti khyātaḥ śaṃkarākhyaśca pa'bhavat \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. He drank it up and absorbed it in his throat. Hence he became known as blue-throated and a beneficent god.

## Chapter 12 - Churning of the Ocean: Birth of Fourteen Precious Jewels

## \|\| 9.12.1 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*tato hṛṣṭāḥ kāśyapeyā manthasthānamupetya te \|*  
*punarvarṣasahasraṃ ca manthanti sma payonidhim \|\| 1 \|\|*

Skanda said:

1\. Then the sons of Kaśyapa became delighted (as the poison was drunk up). They gaṃered at the place of churning. They again went on churning the Ocean for a thousand years.

## \|\| 9.12.2 \|\|

*mathyamānāttathā sindhoḥ sarvestairapi kiñcana \|*  
*nāsīcca śithilā āsanmaṃthitāraḥ śvasanmukhāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. While the Ocean was being churned by all of them, there emerged nothing. The participants in churning gasping for breath with their mouths, became slack (through fatigue).

## \|\| 9.12.3 \|\|

*vāsukiśca mahāsarpaḥ prāṇavaiklavyamāptavān \|*  
*manthakāle mandaropi naikatrāsītsthirasthitiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The great serpent Vāsuki experienced feebleness and frailty of life. At the time of churning Mandara also could not keep up a stable condition.

## \|\| 9.12.4 \|\|

*sarvāndṛṣṭvā nirutsāhānpradyumno viṇvanujñayā \|*  
*devāsurāhirājeṣu praviśya balamādadhau \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Seeing them all bereft of strength, Pradyumna, authorized by Viṣṇu, entered the Devas, Asuras and the king of serpents (Vāsuki) and infused strength in them.

## \|\| 9.12.5 \|\|

*aniruddhopi tarhyeva tamākramya nagādhipam \|*  
*sahasrabāhubhistasthau mahācala ivā'paraḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Even Aniruddha approached the king of mountains and with his thousand arms, stood like another big mountain.

## \|\| 9.12.6 \|\|

*tato mamanthustarasā saṃprāptaparamojasaḥ \|*  
*savismayā mahābdhiṃ te surāsuragaṇā mudā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Being wonder-struck at the restoration of extreme energy, the multitude of Suras and Asuras joyously and energetically churned the great Ocean.

## \|\| 9.12.7 \|\|

*nārāyaṇānubhāvena nāpurddevādayaḥ śramam \|*  
*śuśubhe manthanaṃ tacca samamākarṣaṇāttadā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. At the gesture of Nārāyaṇa, Devas and others did not experience any fatigue. With the rhythmic pulling the churning (operation) looked splendid.

## \|\| 9.12.8 \|\|

*mathyamāne mahāmbhodhau susruvuḥ paritastadā \|*  
*mahādrumāṇāṃ niryāsā bahavaścauṣadhīrasāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. While the big Ocean was ṃus stirred and shaken up, the exudation and extracts of medicinal plants flowed into it all round.

## \|\| 9.12.9 \|\|

*tathābhūtādambunidherāvirāsītkalānidhiḥ \|*  
*kāntyauṣadhīnāmadhyakṣaḥ sarvāsāṃ ya udīryate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. From the reservoir of water which was in that stage (of being churned), there emerged the Moon who is called the presiding deity of loveliness and medicinal herbs.

## \|\| 9.12.10 \|\|

*tato gavāmadhiṣṭhātrī sarvāsāmapi kāmadhuk \|*  
*havirddhānyabhavaddhenuḥ śītāṃśusadṛśadyutiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then the Cow Havirdhānī, the presiding deity of all cows, the yielder of the wishes of all, with a lustre like the moon, emerged.

## \|\| 9.12.11 \|\|

*aśvaḥ śveto'thāvirāsīddhayānāmadhidevatā \|*  
*airāvataśca nāgendraścaturddantaḥ śaśiprabhaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then a white horse, the presiding deity of all horses, manifested. Airāvata, the king of elephants, endowed with four tusks and of moon-like lustre came out.

## \|\| 9.12.12 \|\|

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye'mṛtamanthane caturdaśaratnotpattirnāma dvādaśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Then came out the heavenly tree Pārijāta, the king of all trees. Then the excellent gem, the lotus-hued ruby called Kaustubha, emerged.

## \|\| 9.12.13 \|\|

*tato'bhavannapsaraso rūpalāvaṇyabhūmayaḥ \|*  
*surā devī tato jajñe sarvamādakadevatā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then were born (i.e. came out) Apsaras (i.e. celestial damsels) who were the receptacles of beauty. Then was born Goddess Wine, the goddess that inebriates all.

## \|\| 9.12.14 \|\|

*āsīdatha dhanuḥ śārṅgaṃ sarvaśastrādhidaivatam \|*  
*vādyādhidaivataṃ śaṃkhaḥ pāñcajanyastato'bhavat \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Then came out the Śārṅga bow, the presiding deity of all weapons. Then emerged Pāñcajanya, the conch, the supreme deity of all musical instruments.

## \|\| 9.12.15 \|\|

*tatra candraḥ pārijātastathaivāpsarasāṃ gaṇaḥ \|*  
*ādityapathamāśritya tasthurete tu tatkṣaṇam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Then the Moon-god, Pārijāta as well as the bevy of celestial damsels resorting to the solar path, stood there instantaneously.

## \|\| 9.12.16 \|\|

*vāruṇīmaśvarājaṃ ca daityeśā jagṛhurdrutam \|*  
*airāvataṃ devarājo jagrāhānumatāddhareḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The leaders of Daityas immediately took hold of the king of horses and Vāruṇī, while Indra, the king of Devas took Airāvata with the consent of Hari.

## \|\| 9.12.17 \|\|

*kaustubhaśca dhanuḥ śaṃkho viṣṇumeva prapedire \|*  
*havirddhānīṃ tu te sarve tāpasebhyo dadustadā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The (gem) Kaustubha, the (Śārṅga) bow and the conch (Pāñcajanya) went over to Viṣṇu only. All of them gave Havirdhānī (cow) to sages.

## \|\| 9.12.18 \|\|

*mathyamānātpunaḥ sindhoḥ sākṣācchrīrabhavatsvayam \|*  
*ānandayantī svadṛśā trilokīṃ hatavarcasam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. While the Ocean was being churned again, Śrī herself directly manifested herself delighting with her glance the three worlds, surpassing the splendour of all.

## \|\| 9.12.19 \|\|

*tāṃ grahītuṃ tu sarvepi surāsuranarādayaḥ \|*  
*aicchaṃstasyāḥ pratāpāttu śekentyetuṃ na kaścana \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. All Suras, Asuras, men desired to get hold of her but nobody could approach her brilliance and power.

## \|\| 9.12.20 \|\|

*tatastāṃ padmahastatvācchrīṃ viditvaiva vāsavaḥ \|*  
*ānandaṃ paramaṃ prāpa brahmādyā ye ca tadvidaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Knowing her to be Śrī, by her holding a lotus in her hand, Vāsava and God Brahmā and others, who knew her, were highly delighted.

## \|\| 9.12.21 \|\|

*tāvattatrāmbudhiḥ sākṣādetya tāṃ haima āsane \|*  
*kanyā mameyamityuktvā gṛhītvāṅka upāviśat \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The Ocean himself in person immediately came there and saying ‘This is my daughter’, took her in his lap, and occupied a golden seat.

## \|\| 9.12.22 \|\|

*punarabdhermathyamānādadhikaṃ balibhiśca taiḥ \|*  
*sudhārthibhirddhairyavadbhirapi naivābhavatsudhā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. While the Ocean was being churned by those powerful and firm (determined) seekers of the Nectar, the Nectar did not come out.

## \|\| 9.12.23 \|\|

*tadā śithilayatnāste nirāśā amṛtodbhave \|*  
*pramlānavaktrāḥ khinnāśca babhūvuḥ kāśyapā mune \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Then being disappointed regarding the emergence of the Nectar, they became slack in their efforts. O sage, the sons of Kaśyapa (i.e. Devas and Daityas) of faded faces became dejected.

## \|\| 9.12.24 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā tathāvidhāṃstāṃśca bhagavānkaruṇānidhiḥ \|*  
*udyuktobhūtsvayaṃ brahmanmanthanāya hasanvibhuḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Seeing them in that state, the Lord, the storehouse of compassion, the all-pervading Lord laughed and himself became ready to churn.

## \|\| 9.12.25 \|\|

*ratnakāñcīdṛḍhābaddhakakṣapītāmbaradyutiḥ \|*  
*dvābhyāṃ dvābhyāmahiṃ madhye dorbhyāmubhayatograhīt \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. He was resplendent with the yellow garment, the end knot of which was tightly fastened with a jewelled girdle. He caught hold of the serpent in the middle by his (two pairs) of hands.

## \|\| 9.12.26 \|\|

*dhṛtāhivadanā daityāstasthurekata eva te \|*  
*ekato dhṛtatatpucchā devāstasthustadākhilāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Daityas who caught hold of the mouth of the serpent stood on one side and all the Devas who held the tail of the serpent stood on the other side.

## \|\| 9.12.27 \|\|

*tanmadhyagaśca bhagavānmamanthābdhiṃ sa līlayā \|*  
*dadāno nayanānanda cañcatkaravibhūṣaṇaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The Lord who stood between them sportively churned the Ocean, giving delight to the eyes (of all) with ornaments of his hands becoming (brightly) visible.

## \|\| 9.12.28 \|\|

*brahmā saharṣipravarairantarikṣasthitastadā \|*  
*avākirattaṃ kusumaiḥ kurvañjayajayadhvanim \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. God Brahmā staying in the firmament along with prominent sages, showered him with flowers, uttering the sound (words) “Be victorious; be victorious.”

## \|\| 9.12.29 \|\|

*mathyamānāttataḥ sindhorjjajñe dhanvantariḥ pumān \|*  
*viṣṇoraṃśena gaurāṃgaḥ sudhākumbhaṃ kare dadhat \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Then, from the Ocean that was churned was born a man Dhanvantari with a part of Viṣṇu. He was fair in complexion, was holding in his hand a pitcher containing Sudhā (Nectar).

## Chapter 13 - Gods Drink the Nectar

## \|\| 9.13.1 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*utprekṣanto jāyamānaṃ maṃthitāro'tha te'khilāḥ \|*  
*āyāṃtaṃ dadṛśurddūrādanti dhanvantariṃ śriyaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Skaṇḍa said:

1\. All the participants in churning who were seeing the emergence of Dhanvantari (with the pitcher of Amṛta), saw from a distance Dhanvantari coming near Śrī.

## \|\| 9.13.2 \|\|

*sudhābhṛtaṃ hemakumbhaṃ dṛṣṭvā cā'sya kare dhṛtam \|*  
*asurāḥ sahasā brahmannutplutya jagṛhuśca tam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Seeing the gold pitcher containing Nectar being held in his hand, the Asuras suddenly pounced on it, and snatched it away, O Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 9.13.3 \|\|

*tatrāpi balino ye te gṛhītvā dudruvustataḥ \|*  
*tāndurbalā nyaṣedhanta nītivākyairanudrutāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Out of them, those who were powerful (enough) seized it, and ran off with it. The weaker ones, running after them, protested in the name of decorum and manner of proper behaviours (as follows):

## \|\| 9.13.4 \|\|

*aho naivamadharmo vaḥ kāryo dharmaparāyaṇaiḥ \|*  
*samaśramebhyo devebhyo dattvā peyaṃ na cānyathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. “Oh! Such unrighteous and wicked deed should not be committed by righteous-mided persons. It (the Nectar) should be drunk after giving it to Devas, the equal partners in the labour (of churning out Nectar) and not otherwise.”

## \|\| 9.13.5 \|\|

*anādṛtyeti tadvākyaṃ yayurdūraṃ tvarānvitāḥ \|*  
*tatrāpi teṣāmanyonyaṃ karākṛṣṭirmahatyabhūt \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Disregarding that speech (appeal), they quickly ran far away. Even there, they were forcibly pulling each other’s hands (for securing the Nectar).

## \|\| 9.13.6 \|\|

*ahaṃ pūrvamahaṃ pūrvaṃ na tvaṃ na tvaṃ pibāmyaham \|*  
*itthaṃ vivadamānāste nāpustatprāśanakṣaṇam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. While they were proclaiming and crying about “I am the first and not you”, “I am the first, not you”, “I shall drink it (first)”, they did not get the opportunity to drink.

## \|\| 9.13.7 \|\|

*atha devā mlānavaktrā dṛṣṭvā daityairhṛtā sudhām \|*  
*aśaktāstatpratīkāre śaraṇaṃ prāpuracyutam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Then, on seeing the Nectar snatched away by the Daityas, Devas became pale-faced. Being incapable of preventing them, they sought refuge in Acyuta.

## \|\| 9.13.8-9 \|\|

*pāhipāhi jagannātha naṣṭaṃ sarvasvameva naḥ \|*  
*daityairhṛtā sudhā sarvā kā gatirnno bhaviṣyati \|\| 8 \|\|*

*sudhāpānādṛtepyete hantumasmānalaṃ kṣamāḥ \|*  
*pīte'mṛte tu tairadya kiṃ kariṣyāmahe vayam \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. “Protect us, O Lord of the world; do protect us. All our possessions are destroyed. AH the Nectar has been taken away by Daityas. What shall be our fate? Even without imbibing Nectar, they are sufficiently capable of killing us. If the Nectar is drunk by them today, what shall we do?”

## \|\| 9.13.10 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*niśamya dainyaṃ devānāṃ bhagavānbhaktakāryakṛt \|*  
*mā bhaiṣṭeti surānuktvā sudhāmāditsadāsurāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

Skanda said:

10\. Having heard the pitiable condition of the Devas, the Lord who performs the tasks of his devotees, told the Suras, “Don’t be afraid” and was intent to take back the Nectar from Asuras.

## \|\| 9.13.11 \|\|

*strīrūpamadbhutaṃ dhṛtvā sarvalokavimohanam \|*  
*daityāntikamupāgatya cakre kandukakhelanam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. After assuming a marvellously beautiful feminine form that enchanted all the world, he approached the Daityas and played with a ball.

## \|\| 9.13.12 \|\|

*te tu tadrūpamālokya mohitāḥ kāmavihvalāḥ \|*  
*tyaktvā parasparonmarddaṃ tāmupetyābruvanvacaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Seeing that beautiful form, they were fascinated and were overwhelmed with the passion of love. Giving up their mutual struggle, they approached and spoke:

## \|\| 9.13.13 \|\|

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye devatāmṛtapānavarṇanaṃ nāma trayodaśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. “O blessed lady! Take this pitcher of Nectar and distribute it amongst us. We are the sons of Kaśyapa; O lady with beautiful buttocks, make us all drink it (Nectar).”

## \|\| 9.13.14-15 \|\|

*ityuktvā taṃ dadustasmai te'nicchantyā api striyai \|*  
*sā prāha mama viśrambho na kāryaḥ svairiṇī hyaham \|\| 14 \|\|*

*akāryaṃ vaḥ kṛtaṃ hyetadvibhajiṣye nijecchayā \|*  
*ityuktā api te mūḍhā yatheṣṭaṃ kurviti bruvan \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. Requesting her thus, they handed it over to the lady who was reluctant. She spoke, “No faith should be entertained in me, as I am a self-willed (i.e. wanton) woman. You have done an improper act. I shall, however, distribute it as per my will.” Though she told them so, those stupid ones said, “Do as you please”.

## \|\| 9.13.16 \|\|

*tatastadājñayā sarve devā daityāśca vāsukiḥ \|*  
*niṣeduḥ paṃktiśastatra svasvamaṇḍalamāśritāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then in compliance of her order, Devas, Daityas, Vāsuki sat there in rows, each keeping with his particular group.

## \|\| 9.13.17 \|\|

*paṃktibaṃdhodyateṣveṣu mohinī sā tu dūrataḥ \|*  
*sammukhaṃ devapaṃktīnāṃ hemāsana upāviśat \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. While they were arranging themselves into groups, Mohinī sat on a golden seat at a distance, facing the rows of gods.

## \|\| 9.13.18 \|\|

*svāṃtike cāmṛtaghaṭaṃ nidhāya straiṇalīlayā \|*  
*itastato vīkṣamāṇā tasthau niḥspṛhavatkṣaṇam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Keeping the pitcher of Nectar near her, she, casting her glances here and there in a woman’s sportive way, sat for a moment like an indifferent, impartial person.

## \|\| 9.13.19 \|\|

*vipracittimukhāstarhi ye vai dānavayūthapāḥ \|*  
*saṃdigdhacittā mohinyāmāsandevāṃtikasthiteḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The leaders of Dānava group, of whom Vipracitti was prominent, were suspicious in their minds about Mohinī and hence they seated themselves near the Devas.

## \|\| 9.13.20 \|\|

*śanairupetya taddṛṣṭiṃ vañcayitvā sudhāghaṭam \|*  
*jahruḥ punardurātmāno raho gatvā pipāsavaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Approaching quietly and evading deceitfully her glance, the wicked-souled ones carried away the pitcher of Nectar again and were desirous of drinking it in a secret place.

## \|\| 9.13.21 \|\|

*naranārāyaṇau tatra munibhiḥ saha cāgatau \|*  
*āstāṃ tau dadṛśāte tāndānavānharato'mṛtam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Nara and Nārāyaṇa came there accompanied by sages. Both of them saw the Dānavas stealing away the Nectar.

## \|\| 9.13.22 \|\|

*nārāyaṇenerito'tha narastānsahasāruṇat \|*  
*balādācchidya tatkumbhaṃ mohinyai sa dadau drutam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Instructed by Nārāyaṇa, Nara at once stopped them. Snatching away per force that pitcher, he quickly handed it over to Mohinī.

## \|\| 9.13.23 \|\|

*tato naraṃ hantukāmā āttaśastrāstu dānavāḥ \|*  
*āpatanpaṃktivikṣepo hyasurāṇāmabhūnmahān \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Then with a desire to kill Nara, Dānavas took up their arms and attacked him. There was thus a great disorder in the ranks of Asuras.

## \|\| 9.13.24 \|\|

*tadā naropi bhagavāndevadaityanarairapi \|*  
*ajeyo nirbhayo hyekaḥ sākaṃ tairyuyudhe balī \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Thereupon, the powerful Lord Nara, the fearless one, unconquerable by Devas, Daityas and human beings, single-handedly fought with them.

## \|\| 9.13.25 \|\|

*etasminnantare devānpaṃktisthānmohinīvapuḥ \|*  
*apāyayatsudhāṃ viṣṇuḥ sarvaśo laghucaṅkramaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. In the meanwhile Viṣṇu who had assumed the form of Mohinī went about quickly and made all the Devas who were sitting in rows, drink the Nectar.

## \|\| 9.13.26 \|\|

*tatrāpi dānavo rāhuḥ sūryācandramasāntare \|*  
*praviśya devatāpaṃktāvupāviśadalakṣitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Even then Rāhu, a Dānava, entered (the unoccupied place) in between the Sun and the Moon and sat in the row of the Devas, without being noticed by anyone.

## \|\| 9.13.27 \|\|

*tatrāgatāyāṃ mohinyāṃ siñcantyāṃ tanmukhe sudhām \|*  
*dṛśā'sūsucatāṃ tasyai puṣpavantāvubhau ca tam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. When Mohinī came sprinkling the Nectar in his (Rāhu’s) mouth, both the Sun and the Moon indicated it to her by the glance of their eyes.

## \|\| 9.13.28 \|\|

*smṛtyāgatena cakreṇa tarhyevā'sya ca sāmṛtam \|*  
*śiraścicchedātimahanmāyāyoṣidvapuḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Therefore, the Lord who had assumed the highly illusory form of a woman, cut down his head containing Nectar (within his mouth) by his discus, which came there as soon as remembered.

## \|\| 9.13.29 \|\|

*tacchailaśṛṅgapratimaṃ grasallokānnadadbhṛśam \|*  
*grahatve sthāpayāmāsa lokānāṃ śāntaye hariḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Hari established it (Rāhu’s head) in the planetary position, for the peace of the people, as that mountain-like head was swallowing people while shouting loudly.

## \|\| 9.13.30 \|\|

*devānsudhāṃ pāyayitvā jagṛhe pauruṣīṃ tanum \|*  
*bhagavānatha devāstu yuyudhuḥ saha dānavaiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. After having made Suras drink the Necṭar, he assumed his male body. The Lord and the Devas fought with Dānavas.

## \|\| 9.13.31 \|\|

*udanvatastaṭe yuddhaṃ devānāmasuraiḥ saha \|*  
*sudhāpānātibalināmāsīdviṣṇusahāyinām \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. On the shore of the Ocean there took place the battle of Devas who grew extremely powerful by imbibing Nectar, and were helped by Viṣṇu, with Asuras.

## \|\| 9.13.32 \|\|

*tasmiṃstu tumule yuddhe nareṇendrādibhiśca te \|*  
*nihanyamānā asurāḥ palāyya viviśū rasām \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. In that tumultuous battle, the Asuras who were being killed by Nara, Indra and others, fled away and entered the earth (nether world).

## Chapter 14 - The Marriage Festival of Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa

## \|\| 9.14.1-8 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*brahmā prajeśvarāḥ śambhurmanavaśca maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*ādityavasurudrāśca siddhagandharvacāraṇāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sādhyāśca marutaścaiva viśvedevā digīśvarāḥ \|*  
*dasrau vahniścandramāśca svayaṃ dharmaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*suparṇaḥ kinnarāścaiva ye cānye gaṇadevatāḥ \|*  
*śepādyā vaiṣṇavā nāgā devapatnyaśca sarvaśaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*sāvitrī pārvatī caiva pṛthivī ca sarasvatī \|*  
*śacī gaurī śivā saṃjñā ṛddhiḥ svāhā ca rohiṇī \|*  
*dhūmorṇā cāditirddharmapatnyo mūrtidayādayaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*arundhatī śāṇḍilī ca lopāmudrā tathaiva ca \|*  
*anasūyādayaḥ sādhvya ṛpipatnyaśca sarvaśaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*gaṅgā sarasvatī revā yamunā tapatī tathā \|*  
*candrabhāgā vipāśā ca śatadrurdevikā tathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*godāvarī ca sarayūḥ kāverī kauśikī tathā \|*  
*kṛṣṇā veṇī bhīmarathā tāmraparṇī mahānadī \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kṛtamālā vitastā ca nirvindhyā surasā tathā \|*  
*carmaṇvatī payoṣṇī ca viśvādyā nadya āyayuḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

Skanda said:

1-8. There came (for the marriage-ceremony of Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa) the following:

God Brahmā; the Lords of created being; Śambhu; Manus; great sages; (twelve) Ādityas; (eight) Vasus; (eleven) Rudras; Siddhas; Gandharvas; Cāraṇas; Sādhyas; (forty-nine) Maruts; (the group of ten gods called) Viśvedevas; presiding deities of quarters; the two Aśvins; the Fire-god; the Moon; Dharma; the Prajāpati himself; Garuḍa; Kinnaras and other groups of gods; serpent-devotees of Viṣṇu; of whom Śeṣa was the first, wives of all the Devas (such as) Sāvitrī, Pārvatī, Pṛthivī, Sarasvatī, Śacī, Gaurī, Śivā, Saṃjñā, Ṛddhi, Svāhā, Rohiṇī, Dhūmorṇā (wife of Yama), Aditi and the lawful wives like Mūrti, Dayā and others; Arundhatī, Śāṇḍilī, Lopāmudrā, Anasūyā and other pious wives of sages; (Rivers like) Gaṅgā, Sarasvatī, Revā, Yamuna, Tapatī (Tapti in north Maharashtra), Candrabhāgā (Chinab), Vipāśā (Bias), Śatadru (Sutlej), Devikā (Devā? or Gogrā), Godāvarī, Kāverī, Kauśikī (Kosī), Kṛṣṇā, Veṇī, Bhīmarathī, the great river Tāmraparṇī, Kṛtamālā (Vaiga near Madura, Tamil Nadu), Vitastā (Jhelum), Nirvindhyā (Kālī-Sindh in Mālvā), Surasā, Carmaṇvatī (Chambal), Payoṣṇī (Pain Gaṅgā), Viśvā and others.

## \|\| 9.14.9 \|\|

*rambhā ghṛtācī viśvācī menakā ca tilottamā \|*  
*urvaśīpramukhāstatra sarvāpsarasa āyayuḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. All celestial damsels, of whom Raṃbhā, Ghṛtācī, Viśvācī, Menakā, Tilottamā, and Urvaśī were prominent ones came there.

## \|\| 9.14.10 \|\|

*vaikuṇṭhavāsinaḥ sarve tathā golokavāsinaḥ \|*  
*pārṣadapravarā viṣṇostatrājagmuḥ praharṣitāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. All the residents of Vaikuṇṭha as well as all the inhabitants of Goloka and important attendants of Viṣṇu came there with great delight.

## \|\| 9.14.11 \|\|

*aṇimādyāḥ siddhayo'ṣṭau śaṃkhapadmādayo nava \|*  
*nidhayo mūrtimantaśca samājagmuḥ śriyontike \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. All the eight supernatural powers beginning with Aṇimā (Levitation), and nine treasures beginning with Śaṅkha, Padma in their corporal forms came near Śrī.

## \|\| 9.14.12 \|\|

*pūrṇaḥ śāradacandropi tadānīṃ prītaye śriyāḥ \|*  
*naiśaṃ tamo'haratsarvaṃ babhūvurnirmalā diśaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. At that time, for the pleasure of Śrī, full autumnal moon removed all the darkness of the night and the quarters became resplendent.

## \|\| 9.14.13 \|\|

*tato'bhiṣekamārebhe tasyā brahmājñayā vṛṣā \|*  
*maṇḍapaṃ racayāmāsa sadyastvaṣṭātiśobhanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. In compliance of the order of God Brahmā, Indra began (the preparations for) her ablution. Tvaṣṭā immediately constructed a very beautiful hall (created for the ceremonial occasion).

## \|\| 9.14.14-15 \|\|

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye lakṣmīnārāyaṇavivāhotsavanirūpaṇaṃ nāma caturdaśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*sugandhipuṣpanamrābhirdivyakalpadrumālibhiḥ \|*  
*juṣṭaṃ nānāvidhairaṅgairdarśanīyaṃ manoharam \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. It was furnished with long rows of thousands of pillars decked with jewels. It was beautified with innumerable wonderful canopies and with plantain trees. It was adorned with rows of heavenly wish-yielding trees bent down with sweet fragrant flowers. It was beautiful and fascinating in its various parts.

## \|\| 9.14.16 \|\|

*koṭiśo ratnadīpānāṃ paṃktibhiḥ śuddharociṣām \|*  
*bhrājamānaṃ toraṇaiśca muktāhāraiśca lambibhiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. It was shining brilliantly with crores of rows of bejewelled lamps of resplendent light. It appeared bright with arches (beautified) with suspended pearl-laces.

## \|\| 9.14.17 \|\|

*ratnasiṃhāsane tatra gītavādyapurassaram \|*  
*upāveśya śriyaṃ cakrurabhiṣekaṃ maharṣayaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Seating Śrī on a bejewelled throne there, great sages performed her ablution, preceded by vocal and instrumental music.

## \|\| 9.14.18-19 \|\|

*airāvataḥ puṇḍarīko vāmanaḥ kumudoñjanaḥ \|*  
*puṣpadantaḥ sārvabhaumaḥ supratīkaśca diggajāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*kurvanto bṛṃhitānyete hemakumbhoddhṛtaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|*  
*catuḥsindhusamānītairabhyaṣiñcanta vāribhiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Airāvata, Puṇḍarīka, Vāmana, Kumuda, Añjana, Puṣpadanta, Sārvabhauma, Supratīka—these elephants presiding over eight cardinal points, making a roaring sound, raised up auspicious gold pitchers and showered her with waters brought from seas in four quarters.

## \|\| 9.14.20 \|\|

*mūrtimatyo mahānadyastatrājahurjalāni ca \|*  
*maṃtrānuccārayaṃti sma mūrtā vedāḥ saharṣibhiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Great rivers in their embodied forms brought waters. Vedas, assuming personal forms, recited Mantras along with sages.

## \|\| 9.14.21 \|\|

*jaguḥ sukaṇṭhā gaṃdharvā nanṛtuścāpsarogaṇāḥ \|*  
*vādyāni vādayāmāsuranye devagaṇāstadā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Sweet-voiced Gandharvas sang. Bevies of the celestial damsels danced. Other groups of Devas played on musical instruments.

## \|\| 9.14.22 \|\|

*mahānabhūttadānaṃdastrilokyāṃ sarvadehinām \|*  
*śrīsūktādi dvijāḥ peṭhurjagurgītāni ca striyaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. There was a great joy all over the three worlds to all embodied beings. Brāhmaṇas recited Vedic Sūktas of which Śrīsūkta (i.e. RV 1.165) was the first. Ladies sang songs.

## \|\| 9.14.23 \|\|

*kāṃsyatālamṛdaṅgāṃśca paṇavānakagomukhān \|*  
*vādayāmāsurambhodā divi duṃdubhayo'nadan \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Clouds played upon musical instruments such as instruments of bell metal for beating time. Tabors (Mṛdaṅga drums), instruments called Gomukha, Paṇava, large military drums called Ānaka, Dundubhi drums resounded in heaven.

## \|\| 9.14.24 \|\|

*āsītkusumavṛṣṭiśca sākaṃ jayaravaistadā \|*  
*āsaṃstatparicaryāyāṃ dharmapatnyaśca siddhayaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. There was a shower of saffron accompanied with shouts of victory. For her personal service were the lawful wives (of sages) and supernatural powers (in person).

## \|\| 9.14.25 \|\|

*susnātāyai tatastasyai kauśeye pītavāsasī \|*  
*dadāvanarghye jaladhī ratnabhūṣāśca bhūriśaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The Ocean gave two yellow-coloured silken garments and abundant invaluable bejewelled ornaments to her who had taken that auspicious bath.

## \|\| 9.14.26 \|\|

*upaveśocitaṃ tasyā iṃdra āsanamāharat \|*  
*viśvakarmā kaṅkaṇāni dadau sadratnamudrikāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Indra brought to her a seat worthy of being occupied by her. Viśvakarmā gave her bangles and rings set with excellent jewels.

## \|\| 9.14.27 \|\|

*sudhākarastu tadbhrātā nāsābhūṣaṇamuttamam \|*  
*dadau tasyai keśabhūṣā sadratnanicitā tathā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The Moon, her brother, offered her an excellent ornament for the nose (nose ring), and also gave her ornaments set with excellent jewels for her hair.

## \|\| 9.14.28 \|\|

*padmajanmā dadau padmaṃ muktāhāraṃ sarasvatī \|*  
*nāgāśca śeṣapramukhāstasyai ratneṃdrakuṇḍale \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The Lotus-born (God Brahmā) gave her a lotus and Sarasvatī presented her a pearl necklace. Nāgas of whom Śeṣa was prominent bestowed on her two ear-rings set with the best of jewels.

## \|\| 9.14.29 \|\|

*añjanaṃ kuṅkumaṃ cādāddurgā sobhāgyalakṣaṇam \|*  
*lalāṭikāṃ ca sāvitrī śacī tāmbūlapātrikām \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Durgā gave her collyrium and saffron symbolic of good fortune (securing the favour, firm devotion and long life of the husband). Sāvitrī gave her an ornament to be worn on the forehead, Śacī gave her a betel-box.

## \|\| 9.14.30 \|\|

*vasaṃtaḥ kausumānhārānkaṇṭhasūtraṃ ca śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*vaijayaṃtīṃ srajaṃ pāśī kubero ratnadarpaṇam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The season Spring presented her a flower-garland. Śaṅkara gave her a necklace. God Varuṇa gave her the garland Vaijayantī. Kubera bestowed upon her a bejewelled mirror.

## \|\| 9.14.31 \|\|

*anarghyāṃ kaṃcukīṃ vahniryamo'dādvyajanaṃ śubham \|*  
*dadustasyai cāparepi bhūṣāstatsamayocitāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The Fire-god gave her an invaluable bodice, while Yama bestowed an auspicious umbrella. Others presented her ornaments suitable for the occasion.

## \|\| 9.14.32 \|\|

*tataḥ svalaṃkṛtāṃ kanyāṃ kasmai dadyāmimāmiti \|*  
*siṃdhuḥ papraccha brahmāṇaṃ tadovāca sa sarvavit \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Then the Ocean asked God Brahmā, “To whom should I offer this daughter endowed with excellent ornaments?” The omniscient Lord then replied:

## \|\| 9.14.33-37 \|\|

*kanyā taveyamambhodhe mātā mama śivasya ca \|*  
*devānāmatha sarveṣāṃ lokānāmasti niścitam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*nārāyaṇaṃ vāsudevaṃ paraṃ brahmākhileśvaram \|*  
*puruṣottamamevaikaṃ vināsyā nāparaḥ patiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*ataḥ sākṣādbhagavate trailokyasukhahetave \|*  
*āgatāyopaviṣṭāya dehyasmai vidhināmbudhe \|\| 35 \|\|*

*kuruṣva janmasāphalyaṃ pāvayitvā nijaṃ kulam \|*  
*samuddhara bhavāmbhodherdattvemāṃ paramātmane \|\| 36 \|\|*

*ekastvaṃ saptabhī rūpaiḥ saptadvīpa vibhāgataḥ \|*  
*viśruto'tha vidhāyaitanmahatīṃ kīrttimāpsyasi \|\| 37 \|\|*

33-37. “O storehouse of waters! This your daughter is the mother of mine as well as that of Śiva. It is definite that she is the mother of all Devas and the worlds. She has no other husband than Nārāyaṇa, Vāsudeva, the Supreme Brahman, the Lord of all, the excellent Puruṣa. Therefore, O Ocean, for the felicity of the three worlds give her in marriage with proper (religious) procedure to the Lord who has arrived here in person and taken his seat. By giving her (in marriage) to the Supreme Soul, make your life successful by making your family pure and lift it up from the ocean of Saṃsāra. (Though) you are one, you are known in the world by your seven forms due to the division by seven Dvīpas (continents). By doing this (i.e. offering in marriage), you will obtain great fame.”

## \|\| 9.14.38 \|\|

*ityukto brahmaṇā hṛṣṭaḥ samudraḥ pulakāñcitaḥ \|*  
*manyamāno nijaṃ dhanyamaditsadviṣṇave sutām \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Addressed thus by God Brahmā, the Ocean who was delighted and had the hair standing on end, regarded himself as blessed and gave his daughter to Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 9.14.39 \|\|

*tataḥ sahaiva vidhinā sa saṃprārthya tamīśvaram \|*  
*vāgdānādi vidhāyaiva cakre vaivāhikaṃ vidhim \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Then after requesting the Lord as per procedure, he performed betrothal (Vāgdāna) and other details. He thus completed the sacred precepts pertaining to marriage-ceremony.

## \|\| 9.14.40 \|\|

*dhanvaṃtariścandramāśca vāsavādyāśca devatāḥ \|*  
*āsansamudrasya pakṣe tatra vaivāhikotsave \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. In the marriage celebrations, Dhanvantari, the Moon-god, Indra and other deities were on the side of the Ocean-god there.

## \|\| 9.14.41 \|\|

*vastrābharaṇayānādi dāne bhojanakarmaṇi \|*  
*sanmānane ca janyānāṃ mukhyā āsaṃsta eva hi \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. They were the chief ones in bestowing (things like) clothes, ornaments, vehicles, serving of meals and rendering honours to the relatives of the bridegroom.

## \|\| 9.14.42-43 \|\|

*lakṣmyāśca māṃgalyavidhau mukhyāstatra tu yoṣitaḥ \|*  
*āsangaṃgādayo nadyaḥ śacyādyāśca surāṃganāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*menādyā nagapatnyaśca siddhayaścāṇimādayaḥ \|*  
*candrapatnī tathā kāntiḥ sarvāścāpsaraso mune \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. In the auspicious rite of the marriage-ceremony of Lakṣmī, the following were the prominent ladies: river-goddesses of which Gaṅgā was the first; spouses of Devas beginning with Śacī; wives of Mountain(-gods) like Menā (the wife of Himālaya); Supernatural powers beginning with Aṇimā; Kānti, the lovely wife the Moon-god; and all celestial nymphs, O sage.

## \|\| 9.14.44 \|\|

*nārāyaṇasyātha vibhorlīlāṃ vaivāhikīṃ vidhiḥ \|*  
*śobhayanpitarau cakre mūrtidharmau vicārya ca \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Then God Brahmā performed the sportive marriage-ceremony of Nārāyaṇa suitable to and in consideration of his parents Dharma and Mūrti.

## \|\| 9.14.45-46 \|\|

*dharmo'sau jagadādhāra pūjyaścākhiladehinām \|*  
*pitā'sya bhavituṃ yogyo hyasmiṃśca prītimānbhṛśam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*iyaṃ ca mūrttiḥ prakhyātā sarvasadguṇajanmabhūḥ \|*  
*dākṣāyaṇī dharmapatnī mātā bhavitumarhati \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. “This Dharma is the support of the world. He is adorable to all embodied beings. He is worthy of being his father. He is excessively in love with him.

This Mūrti who is well-known as the source of origin of all virtues, this daughter of Dakṣa, the lawful wife (of Dharma) deserves to be (Nārāyaṇa’s) mother.”

## \|\| 9.14.47-48 \|\|

*tato dharmasyāpi pakṣe mukhyāḥ kāryeṣvime'bhavan \|*  
*nandīśvaragaṇeśābhyāṃ sahitaḥ śaṃkaro mune \|\| 47 \|\|*

*maharṣayo marīcyādyāḥ prajeśā nārado muniḥ \|*  
*vainateyaśca nandādyāḥ śrīdāmādyāśca pārṣadāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. Then, even on the side of Dharma, participating in the marriage duties these were the prominent ones, O sage: (ṃey were) God Śaṅkara accompanied by Nandīśvara and Gaṇeśa, great sages including Marīci, the lords of subjects (Prajāpatis), the sage Nārada, Vainateya (Garuḍa) and attendants including Nanda and Śrīdāmā.

## \|\| 9.14.49 \|\|

*durgā ca vedasūrvāṇī strīṣu mukhyā babhūvire \|*  
*ṛṣipatnyo'nasūyādyā dharmapatnyaśca sarvaśaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Durgā, the deity of speech (Vāṇī) who is the mother of Vedas, wives of sages including Anasūyā and all Dharmapatnīs (lawful wives) were the prominent ones among the ladies.

## \|\| 9.14.50 \|\|

*saha vedādibhirbrahmā tvāsīdubhayapakṣayoḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇā vaidikā ye ca vivāhavidhikovidāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. God Brahmā along with Vedas and others, and Brāhmaṇas who were expert in the Vedas and the procedures of the marriage-ceremony, were on both the sides.

## \|\| 9.14.51 \|\|

*athābdhiḥ sarvasaṃbhārāñchriyā eva prasādataḥ \|*  
*sadyaḥ saṃpādayāmāsa janayandevavismayam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Then, the Ocean, with the favour of Śrī, immediately procured all the requisites, causing wonderment to Devas.

## \|\| 9.14.52 \|\|

*yadyatsaṃkalpayāmāsa hṛdi tattadupāhṛtam \|*  
*sadyaḥ svāṃtika evaikṣattatobhūdatiharṣitaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. He saw that whatever he intended (to have) in his mind, it was instantaneously brought near him. He was, therefore, highly delighted.

## \|\| 9.14.53 \|\|

*madhye tu maṇḍapasyāsāvagnisthāpanavedikām \|*  
*kārayāmāsa vidhivadbrāhmaṇairvedavedibhiḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. In the middle of that (marriage) hall, he caused (the construction of) the altar for establishing the (holy) fire (in it) by Brāhmaṇas learned in the Vedas.

## \|\| 9.14.54 \|\|

*alaṃcakāra tāṃ vediṃ gandhapuṣpākṣatādibhiḥ \|*  
*nānāvidhaiḥ śubhai raṅgaiḥ sāṅkuraiḥ karakaistathā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. He decorated the altar with sandal-paste, flowers, (unbroken) grains of rice etc., and with auspicious colours and water-pots containing sprouts.

## \|\| 9.14.55 \|\|

*tato mahāmaṅgalavādyaghoṣaiḥ samantrakaṃ saṃsnapito munīndraiḥ \|*  
*anarghyavāsāṃsi ca ratnabhūṣā dadhāra viṣṇurmukuṭaṃ ca divyam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Then Viṣṇu who was bathed by prominent sages chanting Mantras accompanied by the loud tumultuous sound of auspicious musical instruments, wore invaluable clothes, bejewelled ornaments and a splendid celestial crown.

## \|\| 9.14.56 \|\|

*vāditranidhvānanināditāśaṃ nṛtyatsurastrīkalagītaśobhanam \|*  
*taṃ maṇḍapaṃ so'tha suraiḥ stuvadbhiḥ sahetya haime niṣasāda pīṭhe \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. With all the quarters reverberating with the sound of the musical instruments and the sweet songs of dancing celestial ladies he came along with eulogizing Suras to the ceremonial hall and sat on a seat of gold.

## \|\| 9.14.57 \|\|

*prakṣālayāmāsa tadaṅghripaṅkajaṃ svapreṣṭhapatnyā jaladhiḥ sagaṃgayā \|*  
*bhṛṅgārasiktottamavāridhārayā tadambu śīrṣṇā ca dadhāra sānvayaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The Ocean along with his dearest wife Gaṅgā washed his (i.e. Viṣṇu’s) lotus-feet with the stream of excellent water flowing from the spout of a golden pitcher (of a particular shape), and carried that water over his head along with (the heads of) those of the members of his family (by sprinkling it over them).

## \|\| 9.14.58 \|\|

*tataḥ paṭhanmaṃgalamuccakaiḥ śriyaṃ prādāpayaccāmbudhinā'cyutāya \|*  
*prajvālya vahniṃ vidhinā vidhātā sākaṃ bṛhadbhirmunibhirjuhāva \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Then reciting loudly the auspicious verses (relevant to the occasion), God Brahmā made the Ocean-god give (in marriage) Śrī to Acyuta. Enkindling the sacred fire as per injunctions, he offered oblations (to the marital fire) along with sages.

## \|\| 9.14.59 \|\|

*pradāya tasmai tanayāṃ manojñāṃ tatpādapadmaikanibaddhadṛṣṭim \|*  
*vāsāṃsi ratnābharaṇāni cādādbhūyāṃsi bhūmne sa samaṃ duhitrā \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. After giving him his beautiful daughter who had fixed her sight only on his lotus-feet, he presented the great being numerous rich garments and bejewelled ornaments along with the daughter.

## \|\| 9.14.60 \|\|

*hutasya tasyā'tha hutāśanasya pradakṣiṇāṃ cāpi saha śriyaiva \|*  
*cakāra cetāṃsi nijekṣakāṇāṃ strīṇāṃ ca puṃsāṃ ca haranhariḥ saḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Then Hari circumambulated the duly oblated sacrificial fire along with Śrī, attracting awhile the minds of men and women onlookers.

## \|\| 9.14.61 \|\|

*ekāsane tau saha sanniviṣṭau brahmāṇḍamātāpitarau manojñau \|*  
*saṃpūjayāmāsuranarghyavastravibhūṣaṇairdevagaṇāḥ sayoṣāḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The multitudes of gods, along with their wives, worshipped with reverence, the beautiful parents of the universe occupying the same seat, presenting to them invaluable garments and ornaments.

## \|\| 9.14.62 \|\|

*tadā ca gītāni sumaṃgalāni śriyaśca viṣṇorguṇavarṇanāni \|*  
*durgādayaścā'tha pulomajādyā devyo jaguḥ sasmitacāruvaktrāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Goddesses including Durgā and others and wives of Devas including Śacī, whose beautiful faces were beaming with smiles, sang auspicious songs describing the excellences of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 9.14.63-64 \|\|

*dvidhā vibhaktāni surāṃganānāṃ vṛndānyupāviśya ca sammukhāni \|*  
*taddampatiprekṣaṇakautukāni tathā jaguḥ premabhareṇa tāni \|\| 63 \|\|*

*yathā tadākarṇya surāḥ samastā maharṣayaścā'khilayoṣitopi \|*  
*svāṃtastamaikṣaṃta saha śriyeśaṃ sphuraṃtamāsannanu citravacca \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. The multitudes of the wives of Devas seated in two groups facing each other, sang with great love and devotion, festive nuptial songs at the sight of the couple in such a way as on hearing them all Suras, great sages, all womenfolk saw the Lord along with Śrī shining within themselves, and they sat (still and motionless) as if drawn in a picture.

## Chapter 15 - Eulogy of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa

## \|\| 9.15.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*vicāryyā'haṃ vedānmuhurupagato niścayamimaṃ ramārāme bhaktistvayi dṛḍhatarā yarhyasubhṛtām \|*  
*bhavettarhyevaiṣāṃ kṣayavirahitā bhoganikarāstathā syurlokā vai paramapuruṣātyaṃtikagatiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

1\. After having constantly meditated upon the Vedas, I have arrived at the decision that, if living beings entertain firmer devotion unto you, the delight of Ramā, they will enjoy an unending and never decreasing multitude of pleasures, and that they attain to worlds, the ultimate destination of which is the Supreme Person.

## \|\| 9.15.2 \|\|

*ajānantastvitthaṃ bhṛtarajatamaskānapi hare bhajantyasmāndevānbahuvidhataporccāsaraṇibhiḥ \|*  
*ta evoktā mūḍhāḥ kṣayarahitasaukhyaṃ na kuhacillabhante'tastvāṃ vai nijahṛdi dadhe keśavamaham \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Not knowing this, they propitiate us, Devas, through various kinds of penances, worships, even though we are (ourselves) possessed of the qualities of Rajas and Tamas. Hence they are called stupid, O Keśava. I, therefore, cherish you in my heart.

## \|\| 9.15.3 \|\|

*śaṃkara uvāca \|*  
*trayī sāṃkhyavedāṃtayogāḥ purāṇaṃ tathā pañcarātraṃ prabho dharmaśāstram \|*  
*tavaivātimāhātmyamekasya nityaṃ prakārairanekairhi gāyaṃti bhaktyā \|\| 3 \|\|*

Śaṅkara said:

3\. O Lord! The Three Vedas, Sāṅkhya, Vedānta, Yoga, Purāṇa, Pāñcarātra as well as Dharmaśāstra—all these devoutly sing in various ways the supreme majestic glory of yours alone.

## \|\| 9.15.4 \|\|

*tvadeveśa śāstrāṇi caitāni bhūmno babhūvustvadekāśrayāṇyādikalpe \|*  
*ramāsevyapādāmbujaṃ śāstrayoniṃ tamādyaṃ bhavantaṃ bhaje vāsudevam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. In the first Kalpa (Ādi-Kalpa), it is from you, the great one, alone that these Śāstras were born and they have you as their only resort, O Sovereign Lord. I betake myself to you and worship you, the Primordial One whose lotus-feet are served by Ramā, who are the source of the origin of Śāstras.

## \|\| 9.15.5 \|\|

*dharma uvāca \|*  
*kathā tvadīyā bhavapāśamocanī sudhaiva tāpatrayataptadehinām \|*  
*anekajanmāghacayāpahāriṇī tanoti bhaktiṃ vayunaṃ tavāñjasā \|\| 5 \|\|*

Dharma said:

5\. A talk about you is a releaser from the bonds of Saṃsāra. It is like nectar to embodied beings who are tormented by the three kinds of miseries (namely, Ādhibhautika, Ādhidaivika, Ādhyātmika). It is a destroyer of sins accumulated during innumerable births. Devotion unto you instantly enhances knowledge.

## \|\| 9.15.6 \|\|

*sadaiva sā karṇapathena hṛddarī viśatvanantābhidha sammukhodgatā \|*  
*mama tvadanyā haratācca vāsanā dayābdhaye te prabhaviṣṇave namaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O Lord of innumerable names! May it (i.e. a talk about you) issued from the mouths of saintly persons, forever enter into the valley (in the form) of my heart, through (my) ear. It should remove every (other) wish except the one for you. Salute unto you, the ocean of mercy, the mighty one.

## \|\| 9.15.7 \|\|

*prajāpataya ūcuḥ \|*  
*dhanyā ete kalpavṛkṣā yadīyāṃ chāyāmetāmāśritastvaṃ sahaśrīḥ \|*  
*dhanyaḥ kartā maṇḍapasyāsya te vai dhanyaiṣā bhūryatra pīṭhaṃ taveśa \|\| 7 \|\|*

Prajāpati said:

7\. Blessed are these wish-yielding trees, the shade of which has been resorted to by you along with Śrī. Blissful is the creator (builder) of this hall (of your marriage-ceremony). Beatified \[Beautified?\] is this earth where your seat stands, O Lord.

## \|\| 9.15.8 \|\|

*dhanyo loke nūnameṣomburāśiḥ sākṣāttubhyaṃ yena dattā svakanyā \|*  
*dhanyāścaite tvāṃ vayaṃ vīkṣamāṇā dhanyeśānaṃ śrīpatiṃ tvāṃ natāḥ smaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Verily this Ocean is blessed in this world, (inasmuch as) his own daughter was given unto you directly by him. Blessed are these—we—who behold you. We have paid our obeisance to you, the blessed Lord, the consort of Śrī.

## \|\| 9.15.9 \|\|

*manava ūcuḥ \|*  
*dharmaḥ khalu sa hi paramo dharmebhyo mādhava sakalebhyopi \|*  
*bhaktirbhavati yato vai dharmabhuvi tvayi hi niravadyā \|\| 9 \|\|*

Manus said:

9\. O Lord of Lakṣmī! That Dharma certainly is superior to all (oṃers), the Dharma wherefrom pure devotion unto you, the support of Dharma, is engendered.

## \|\| 9.15.10 \|\|

*dharmātmānaṃ bhagavandharmadhurīṇaṃ ca dharmapātāram \|*  
*sarvātipriyadharmaṃ numastvāṃ dharmasaṃbhūtim \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. We praise you, the soul of Dharma, the leader and protector of Dharma, the source of Dharma, to whom Dharma is dearest, O Lord.

## \|\| 9.15.11 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*bhaktyā hīnastvadvimukho vayunārthī śrāmyanbhūyopyasya na siddhiṃ samupaiti \|*  
*tarhyāsaktaḥ karmaṇi kāmye tu kutosau saukhyaṃ yāyādakṣayamānandamahābdhe \|\| 11 \|\|*

Sages said:

11\. He who is devoid of devotion is averse to you; (being) desirous of knowledge he exerts, yet does not achieve success. He is, therefore, attached to Karmas for a desired object. How can he attain imperishable joy, O ocean of bliss?

## \|\| 9.15.12 \|\|

*bhaktyā nityaṃ tvāmata eva vayaṃ vai śraddhāyuktā dharmataponigamādyaiḥ \|*  
*māyātītaṃ kālaniyantāramudāraṃ dhyāyāmaḥ śrīkāntaparātparamekam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Hence, we, filled with faith and devotion, (practising) Dharma, penance and Vedas (Vedic studies), meditate upon you who are beyond Māyā, the controller of Kāla (Death or Time), the noble one, the Lord of Śrī, senior to the senior ones.

## \|\| 9.15.13 \|\|

*indra uvāca \|*  
*bhagavannuruduḥkhitā vayaṃ nanu durvāsasa eva helanāt \|*  
*na bhavantamṛte'vituṃ hi no vidhirudrapramukhā ime'śakan \|\| 13 \|\|*

Indra said:

13\. Really, due to our insulting behaviour towards Durvāsas we became extremely miserable. With your exception, none of these gods like Brahmā, Rudra and others were able to protect us, O Lord.

## \|\| 9.15.14 \|\|

*vigatākhilasaṃpado nirannāḥ samabhāvaṃ bhuvi pāmarairupetāḥ \|*  
*bhavataiva vayaṃ hṛtāpadaḥ smaḥ sapadi śrīharaye namostu tubhyam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Devoid of all wealth and wanting in food we were reduced to a condition on par with destitutes on the earth. By you only we had our miseries removed instantly. Obeisance to you, O Śrī Hari.

## \|\| 9.15.15 \|\|

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye lakṣmīnārāyaṇastutinirūpaṇaṃ nāma pañcadaśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

Fire-god said:

15\. The food that is the means of subsistence to Devas, Dānavas and human beings, is created by you only. Therewith learned men offer oblations in sacrifices to you, and the remnant is carried (offered) to other inhabitants of heaven.

## \|\| 9.15.16 \|\|

*kāmyeṣu karmasu ratā api yājñikāste tatkarmabandhanata āśu vimucya yānti \|*  
*brāhmīṃ gatiṃ taditare tu bhavanti caurāḥ śrīyajñapūruṣamahaṃ praṇamāmi taṃ tvām \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Those performers of sacrifices, though interestedly engaged in acts for realization of desires, get quickly freed from the bondage of Karmas and attain to the Brāhmī state. The others (i.e. non-sacrificers) are thieves. I bow down to you, Śrī-Yajña-Puruṣa (Viṣṇu).

## \|\| 9.15.17 \|\|

*maruta ūcuḥ \|*  
*bhaktā ekāntikāste'kṣaraparamapade sevayā te tu hīnaṃ vāsaiśvaryādi necchantyatiśayitasukhaṃ nāpi kaivalyamokṣam \|*  
*tadyuktaṃ tvātmanopi śvapacakulajanurmānayantyuttamaṃ vai taṃ tvāmekāntadharmāśrayaṇamupagatāḥ śrīmahāpūruṣaṃ smaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

Maruts said:

17\. By rendering service to you, the imperishable, supreme station, devotees exclusively attached to you, do not crave for houses, prosperity etc. (regarding them) as low, nor do they desire for the final emancipation full of excessive happiness. It is proper that they regard their birth in a family of Cāṇḍālas as the excellent one. We have approached you, the great person, the refuge of devotees, who are exclusively attached to you.

## \|\| 9.15.18 \|\|

*siddhā ūcuḥ \|*  
*naikabrahmāṇḍasargādikāraṇaṃ tvāmakāraṇam \|*  
*tatsthaṃ tadvyatiriktaṃ ca niyantāraṃ namāmahe \|\| 18 \|\|*

Siddhas said:

18\. We pay obeisance to you who alone, though causeless, are the cause of creation (sustenance and destruction) of innumerable Cosmic Eggs (Brahmāṇḍas), to you who are immanent in them yet transcendent and their controller.

## \|\| 9.15.19 \|\|

*rudrā ūcuḥ \|\| māyāyāḥ sarvamohinyā mohanaṃ mohavarjitam \|*  
*mahākālasyāpi kālaṃ tvāṃ namaḥ puruṣottamam \|\| 19 \|\|*

Rudras said:

19\. Obeisance to you, the Supreme Person, who, though yourself free from delusion, are the enchanter of Māyā, the deluder of all and who are Kāla (i.e. destroyer) even of Mahākāla (the great destroyer of the universe).

## \|\| 9.15.20 \|\|

*ādityā ūcuḥ \|*  
*prakāśitā yena vayaṃ jaganti prakāśayāmo bhavatā rameśa \|*  
*svayaṃprakāśaṃ tamuruprakāśaṃ prakāśamūrttiṃ praṇatā bhavantam \|\| 20 \|\|*

Sun said:

20\. O Lord of Ramā! Illuminated by you, we lighten the worlds. We have bowed down to you who are self-luminous, of great refulgence, the very light incarnate.

## \|\| 9.15.21 \|\|

*sādhyā ūcuḥ \|*  
*śāstā nṛpāṇāṃ ca mahoragāṇāṃ daityādhipānāṃ ca surādhipānām \|*  
*tvaṃ vai manūnāṃ ca prajāpatīnāṃ rājādhirājāya namostu tubhyam \|\| 21 \|\|*

Sādhyas said:

21\. You are the ruler (and controller) of kings, great serpents, kings of Daityas, of Devas, of Manus, Prajāpatis. We repeatedly salute you, the Supreme King of Kings.

## \|\| 9.15.22 \|\|

*vasava ūcuḥ \|*  
*bhavati bhuvi yadāyadā'surāṃśaiḥ prathitasanātanadharmadhārmikāṇām \|*  
*kadanamuru tadātadā svayaṃ te hyavatarate praṇamāma dharmagoptre \|\| 22 \|\|*

Vasus said:

22\. Whenever there is a destruction of the proclaimed eternal Dharma and its followers by persons (born) with Asura portions, then, every time, you incarnate of your own accord. We bow down to the protector of Dharma.

## \|\| 9.15.23 \|\|

*cāraṇā ūcuḥ \|*  
*caritraṃ śubhaṃ te dhṛtānekamūrtteḥ prabandhairanekairhi gāyanti bhaktāḥ \|*  
*yadu śrotṛvaktṝnpunātyeva sadyo vayaṃ taṃ natāḥ puṇyakīrttiṃ bhavantam \|\| 23 \|\|*

Cāraṇas said:

23\. Devotees sing (the praise) of the auspicious deeds of you who have assumed innumerable forms in various poetical compositions. It (the poetic composition) instantly purifies the hearer as well as the speaker. We have bowed down to you of auspicious fame.

## \|\| 9.15.24 \|\|

*gandharvāpsarasa ūcuḥ \|*  
*ye kathāste vihāyānyagāthāḥ prabho kīrttayante'tha śṛṇvanti vā te janāḥ \|*  
*duḥkhitāḥ syuśca saṃsārapāśaiḥ sitāstaṃ natāḥ smaḥ śaraṇyaṃ bhavantaṃ vayam \|\| 24 \|\|*

Gandharvas and celestial damsels said:

24\. O Lord! Those who, leaving aside your episodes, describe or listen to the laudatory verses about others, become miserable and get sewn (bound) with the bonds of Saṃsāra. We salute you, a worthy resort.

## \|\| 9.15.25 \|\|

*samudra uvāca \|*  
*ajita tavā'tha tāvakajanasya mudā'lpamapi draviṇa jalānnavastranamanānyatamena sakṛt \|*  
*carati ha sevanaṃ sa padavīṃ mahatīṃ mahatāṃ vrajati janolpakopi tamahaṃ praṇataḥ karuṇam \|\| 25 \|\|*

The Ocean said:

25\. O unconquerable Lord! If anyone serves with delight your people (devotees) even once with a little of wealth, water, food, garments, bows, he attains a high position, even if he be of a low status. I salute that merciful one.

## \|\| 9.15.26 \|\|

*pārṣadā ūcuḥ \|*  
*pitaro tvamasi svajanastvamasi tvamasīṣṭaguruḥ suhṛdātmapatiḥ \|*  
*tvamasīśvara eva ca naḥ paramastvamasi draviṇaṃ sakalaṃ tvamasi \|\| 26 \|\|*

Pārṣadas (Viṣṇu’s attendānts) said:

26\. You are our parents; you are (our) relative; you are our beloved teacher, friend and protector; you alone are our ruler; you are the highest (to us); you are our entire wealth.

## \|\| 9.15.27 \|\|

*mūrttiruvāca \|*  
*yatsaṃbandhata eva yānti padavīmuccāṃ mahadbhirnnutāṃ strīśūdrāsuranīcapakṣipaśavaḥ pāpātmajīvā api \|*  
*yaddhīnā vibudheśvarā api bhavantyarccojjhitāstatkṣaṇaṃ golokādhipatiṃ tameva hṛdaye nityaṃ bhaje tvāmaham \|\| 27 \|\|*

Mūrti (Nārāyaṇa’s mother) said:

27\. I always adore in my heart you, the ruler of Goloka, you, through association with whom, women, Śūdras, Asuras, birds and beasts of low categories and even wicked-souled beings attain to a high status praised even by the great ones and abandoned by whom even the lords of Devas immediately become bereft of worship (unfit to be worshipped).

## \|\| 9.15.28 \|\|

*sāvitryuvāca \|*  
*tvaṃ sargakāle prakṛtiṃ ca pūruṣaṃ dṛṣṭyā svayotthāpya tatastadātmanā \|*  
*tattvāni sṛṣṭvā mahadādimānitairnnaikānvirājo bahudhā sasarjitha \|\| 28 \|\|*

Sāvitrī said:

28\. At the time of the creation of the universe, you have created by your glance Prakṛti and Puruṣa, creating through them, these Tattvas, (primary) substances or principles beginning with Mahat; you created many Virājs.

## \|\| 9.15.29 \|\|

*vairājarūpeṇa jagadvidhātṛtāṃ svīkṛtya devāsuramānuṣoragān \|*  
*tvaṃ sthāvaraṃ jaṃgamamīśa nirmame tvāmādikartāramupāśritāsmyaham \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Assuming the creatorship of the world in the form of Vairāja (Brahmā), you created Devas, Asuras, human beings, serpents, movables and immovable beings, O Lord. I seek refuge in you, the first creator.

## \|\| 9.15.30 \|\|

*durgovāca \|*  
*priyatayā'dhikayā hṛdi cintanaṃ vidadhate tava ye bhuvi te vibho \|*  
*na parameṣṭhisukhaṃ na divaḥ sukhaṃ na kamayanti dharaikanareśatām \|\| 30 \|\|*

Durgā said:

30\. O omnipresent Lord! In this world those who perform your meditation in their hearts with excessive love and devotion do not desire for the happiness of Brahmā (or of Brahmā’s post), or the pleasure in heaven or the position of being the sole sovereign lord of the earth.

## \|\| 9.15.31 \|\|

*prasabhamarpitamapyatulaṃ tvayā sukhamidaṃ samavāpya ca tatra te \|*  
*tadapahāya na śaktikṛtaḥ kṣaṇaṃ tamu namāmi ca sātvatanāyakam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Having obtained this incomparable bliss conferred per force by you (upon them), they, the powerful ones, do not give it up even for a moment. I bow down to such a Lord of Sātvatas.

## \|\| 9.15.32 \|\|

*nadya ūcuḥ \|*  
*varada namanamātraṃ nāmasaṃkīrtanaṃ vā vidadhati tava ye vai jñānato'jñānato vā \|*  
*janimṛtiyamabhītestānapi trāyamāṇaṃ narasakhamupayātāḥ smo'dya nārāyaṇaṃ tvām \|\| 32 \|\|*

Rivers said:

32\. O grantor of boons! Today we have approached you, Nārāyaṇa who protect from the fear of birth, death and Yama, people who, knowingly or unknowingly, perform a mere bow unto you or the glorification (or recitation) of your name, O friend of Nara.

## \|\| 9.15.33 \|\|

*devapatnya ūcuḥ \|*  
*bhuvi dhṛtākṛterjanma maṅgalaṃ caritamadbhutaṃ lokapāvanam \|*  
*bhavati nirguṇaṃ sarvameva te bhavasi nirguṇabrahma yatparam \|\| 33 \|\|*

Wives of Devas said:

33\. The birth of you who have assumed a body on this earth, is auspicious. Your deeds are wonderful and sanctifying to the world. As you are the attributeless Brahman, everything pertaining to you becomes devoid of all attributes.

## \|\| 9.15.34 \|\|

*tava samāśrayāttāmasā janā api ca rājasāḥ sāttvikāśca ye \|*  
*nanu bhavanti te nirguṇāstato vayamupāsmahe tvāṃ hi nirguṇam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. By resorting to you, people who are characterised even by Tamas, Rajas and Sattva attributes, become attribute less. Hence we worship (you) who are devoid of attributes.

## \|\| 9.15.35 \|\|

*ṛṣipatnya ūcuḥ \|*  
*ārtānāmuruvṛjinaistridhā ca tāpaiḥ sarvāpatpraśamanamekameva viṣṇoḥ \|*  
*pādābjaṃ tava bhavatīti tadvayaṃ vai prāptāḥ smaḥ śaraṇamananta devadeva \|\| 35 \|\|*

Wives of sages said:

35\. The lotus-feet of Viṣṇu, that is of yours, are the only pacifiers of all difficulties of people afflicted with extremely calamitous torments of three types. Hence, we have approached you as refugees, O infinite God of gods.

## \|\| 9.15.36 \|\|

*pṛthivyuvāca \|*  
*pūrṇaśāradasudhākarānanaṃ śāradābjadaladīrghalocanam \|*  
*śrīviyogabahudhārtimocanaṃ vā'sudevamahamekamāśraye \|\| 36 \|\|*

Pṛthivī said:

36\. I seek refuge only in Vāsudeva whose face is like the full autumnal moon, whose eyes are long like lotus-petals in autumn, who relieves immense sufferings due to separation from Śrī (wealth).

## \|\| 9.15.37 \|\|

*sarasvatyuvāca \|*  
*nayane mamācyuta tavātisundare mukhaśītarociṣi cakoratāṃ gate \|*  
*na hi gacchato'nyata itīyameva me hṛdi mūrtirastu satataṃ nahītarā \|\| 37 \|\|*

Sarasvatī said:

37\. My eyes have been (as if) transformed into Cakora birds with reference to your extremely beautiful moon-like face. They do not go elsewhere. May this form of yours abide in my heart and no other!

## \|\| 9.15.38 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*iti stuto'khilairdevaiḥ sobhinandya dṛśaiva tān \|*  
*prāha śriyaṃ śubhe paśya devādīṃstvamimāniti \|\| 38 \|\|*

Skanda said:

38\. Thus praised by all gods, he welcomed them by his glance only. He spoke to Śrī, “O auspicious lady, give a (favourable) look to these gods.”

## \|\| 9.15.39 \|\|

*tataḥ samīkṣitāḥ prītyā tayā madhurayā dṛśā \|*  
*trilokīvāsinaḥ sarve ṛddhā āsanyathā purā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. With a pleasing look all the residents of the three worlds were glanced with favour by her. They became prosperous as before.

## \|\| 9.15.40 \|\|

*lebhire svasvaṛddhiṃ te gṛhiṇastyāginopi ca \|*  
*dharmādayaśca sānandaṃ pracaranti sma pūrvavat \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Householders as well as renouncers, all got back their own (previous) prosperity. Dharma and others began to move with delight as before.

## \|\| 9.15.41 \|\|

*tasyāḥ śriyaśca bhagavāndadau sthānamuraḥ svakam \|*  
*tatra sthitvaiva sā vyāpattrailokyaṃ saṃpadātmanā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The Lord offered his chest as the place to Śrī. Stationing herself there, she pervaded the three worlds with her affluence.

## \|\| 9.15.42 \|\|

*tato ratnākaraḥ svasmācchrījaneranubhāvataḥ \|*  
*babhūvānvarthasaṃjño vai saṃpūrṇakṣayaratnavān \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Then the Ocean (lit. ‘the mine of jewels’) as a consequence of being the progenitor of Śrī, became true to the meaning of his name by becoming the abode (Kṣaya) of all jewels.

## \|\| 9.15.43 \|\|

*caturvidhairbahurasaiḥ sadannairamṛtopamaiḥ \|*  
*sarvānsamāgatāṃstatra tarpayāmāsa sādaram \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. There he respectfully satisfied all the guests with nectar-like excellent food of four varieties of very good flavour.

## \|\| 9.15.44 \|\|

*anarghyāṇi ca vastrāṇi ratnabhūṣāḥ paricchadān \|*  
*devādibhyo dadau prītyā sarvebhyopi pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. With great pleasure, he presented to all (guests) including Devas individually valuable garments, bejewelled ornaments and other paraphernalia.

## \|\| 9.15.45 \|\|

*jāmātustuṣṭaye svasya tadīyebhyastadāmbudheḥ \|*  
*nāsītkimapyadeyaṃ vai ghanavaddhanavarṣiṇaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. At that time, for the satisfaction of his son-in-law, there was nothing that could not be given to his relatives, in the case of the Ocean who was showering wealth like a cloud.

## \|\| 9.15.46 \|\|

*bhagavānapi taddattaṃ yautakaṃ ca dhanaṃ bahu \|*  
*brāhmaṇebhyaḥ pradāyaiva śriyā saha tirodadhe \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The Lord also distributed among Brāhmaṇas all the abundant wealth given to him as dowry, and vanished along with Śrī.

## \|\| 9.15.47 \|\|

*lakṣmīnārāyaṇābhyāṃ te bhṛśamānanditāḥ surāḥ \|*  
*indrādayo divaṃ jagmuḥ svaṃsvaṃ dhāmā'pare yayuḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Suras were excessively delighted by Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa. Gods including Indra, went to heaven and others went to their respective homes.

## \|\| 9.15.48 \|\|

*adhikāraṃ ca saṃprāpya yathāpūrvaṃ nijaṃnijam \|*  
*sarvepi sukhino jātāḥ prasādātkamalāpateḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Getting back their respective powers as before, all of them became happy through the grace of the Lord of Kamalā (Lakṣmī).

## \|\| 9.15.49 \|\|

*mandaraṃ ca giriṃ tārkṣyaḥ punarbhagavadājñayā \|*  
*svasthānaṃ samupānīya sthāpayāmāsa līlayā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. By the order of the Lord Garuḍa again took back Mount Mandara to his place and fixed him there sportively.

## \|\| 9.15.50 \|\|

*evamindreṇa brahmarṣe naṣṭā brāhmaṇaśāpataḥ \|*  
*upalabdhā punaḥ saṃpannārāyaṇaprasādataḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. O Brāhmaṇa-sage! In this way the prosperity which was lost through the curse of a Brāhmaṇa, was got back by Indra through the grace of Nārāyaṇa.

## \|\| 9.15.51 \|\|

*ya etāṃ śṛṇuyātpuṇyāṃ kathāṃ bhagavato mune \|*  
*kīrtayetprayato vāpi saṃpadaṃ prāpnuto hi tau \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O sage! He who hears this holy story of the Lord and who extols it observing religious restraints, both of them will get riches.

## \|\| 9.15.52 \|\|

*gṛhiṇāṃ dhanasiddhiḥ syāttyāgināṃ ca yathepsitā \|*  
*bhaktijñānavirāgāderbhavetsiddhiranena vai \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. By (listening) to this there will be attainment of wealth to householders. To the recluses there will be attainment of devotion, spiritual knowledge, disaffection from worldly pleasures and others, as desired by them.

## \|\| 9.15.53 \|\|

*iti te kathitaṃ brahmanyathendraḥ prāpa saṃpadam \|*  
*nāradopi yathā śvetaṃ dvīpaṃ sa gatavānṛṣiḥ \|*  
*tatte sarvaṃ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇuṣvaikena caitasā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. In this way I have narrated to you, O Brāhmaṇa, how Indra got back his prosperity. I shall tell you everything as to how Sage Nārada went to Śveta Dvīpa. Listen with concentrated mind.

## \|\| 9.15.54 \|\|

*gṛhiṇāṃ dhanasiddhiḥ syāttyāgināṃ ca yathepsitā \|*  
*bhaktijñānavirāgāderbhavetsiddhiranena vai \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. By (listening) to this there will be attainment of wealth to householders. To the recluses there will be attainment of devotion, spiritual knowledge, disaffection from worldly pleasures and others, as desired by them.

## Chapter 16 - Description of Goloka

## \|\| 9.16.1 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*meruśṛṃgaṃ samārūḍho nārado divyayā dṛśā \|*  
*śvetadvīpaṃ ca tatrasthānpaśyanmuktānsahasraśaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: Goloka is the uppermost of the divine worlds. It is regarded as the upper lip of Viṣṇu, the lower lip being Brahma-loka (Mahābhārata, Śanti 347.52). The description of Goloka in Mahābhārata, Anuśāsana 83.37-44 is somewhat different from what is given here. This Goloka is the replica of the Vṛndāvana region where Kṛṣṇa spent his boyhood in the cowherd community. The same persons—cowherdess Rādhā, her companions, Kṛṣṇa’s playmates, his Rāsa dance, cows etc., are super-divine in the Goloka of this Purāṇa.

Skanda said:

1\. Ascending the peak of Meru, Nārada with his divine vision saw Śveta Dvīpa and thousands of liberated souls thereof.

## \|\| 9.16.2 \|\|

*vāsudeve bhagavati dṛṣṭimābadhya tatkṣaṇam \|*  
*utpapāta mahāyogī sadyaḥ prāpa ca dhāma tat \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Concentrating his sight on Lord Vāsudeva, the great Yogī soared up that very moment and immediately arrived at that place.

## \|\| 9.16.3 \|\|

*prāpya śvetaṃ mahādvīpaṃ nārado hṛṣṭamānasaḥ \|*  
*dadarśa bhaktāṃstāneva śvetāṃścandraprabhāñchubhān \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Reaching the great Dvīpa (continent) Śveta, Nārada was delighted in his mind. He saw those very auspicious devotees who were white-complexioned and had the lustre of the moon.

## \|\| 9.16.4 \|\|

*pūjayāmāsa śirasā manasā taiśca pūjitaḥ \|*  
*didṛkṣurbrahma paramaṃ sa ca kṛcchraparaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He worshipped them with his head (bowed down), and was mentally adored by them. Being desirous of seeing the Supreme Brahman, he stood there embarrassed (lit. in a difficult situation).

## \|\| 9.16.5 \|\|

*bhaktamekāntikaṃ viṣṇorbuddhvā bhāgavatāstu te \|*  
*tamūcustuṣṭamanaso japantaṃ dvādaśākṣaram \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Knowing that he (Nārada) was a devotee exclusively of Viṣṇu, those Bhāgavatas (‘followers of the Lord’) were delighted (i.e. satisfied) in their minds. While muttering the twelve-syllabled (Mantra of the Lord), they spoke to him:

## \|\| 9.16.6 \|\|

*śvetamuktā ūcuḥ \|*  
*munivarya bhavānbhaktaḥ kṛṣṇasyā'sti yato'tra naḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭavāndevadurdṛśyānkimicchannatha tapyati \|\| 6 \|\|*

The Śveta-muktas (‘Liberated Svetas’) said:

6\. O prominent sage! You are a devotee of Kṛṣṇa. Hence you (are able to) see us who are difficult to be seen even by Devas. What desire torments you?

## \|\| 9.16.7 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*
