*bhagavantaṃ paraṃ brahma sākṣātkṛṣṇamahaṃ prabhum \|*  
*draṣṭumutko'smi bhaktendrāstaṃ darśayata tatpriyāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

Nārada said:

7\. I am very eager to see Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Brahman himself, the ruler (of the universe). O great devotees who are dear to him, show him (to me).

## \|\| 9.16.8 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*tadaikaḥ śvetamuktastu kṛṣṇena prerito hṛdi \|*  
*ehi te darśaye kṛṣṇamityuktvā puratobhavat \|\| 8 \|\|*

Skanda said:

8\. Then one white liberated soul, being directed by Kṛṣṇa in his heart, said, “Come, I shall show you Kṛṣṇa”. Saying ṃis, he proceeded ahead.

## \|\| 9.16.9 \|\|

*prahṛṣṭo nāradastena sākamākāśavartmanā \|*  
*paśyandhāmāni devānāṃ tata ūrddhvaṃ yayau muniḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then the highly delighted Sage Nārada went up with him by the path in the firmament, seeing the dwelling places of Devas.

## \|\| 9.16.10 \|\|

*saptarṣīṃśca dhruvaṃ dṛṣṭvā'nāsaktaḥ kutracitsa ca \|*  
*maharjanatapolokānvyatīyāya dvijottama \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Seeing the Seven Sages (Ursa Major) and the Polar Star, he was not attached anywhere there. He crossed the regions known as Maharloka, Janaloka, Tapoloka, O excellent Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 9.16.11 \|\|

*brahmalokaṃ tato dṛṣṭvā śvetamuktānugo muniḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇasyaivecchayā'dhvānaṃ prāpāṣṭāvaraṇeṣvapi \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then, after seeing the region of god Brahmā, the sage who followed the Śveta-mukta. found his way even through the eight sheaths (of the universe) due to the wish of Kṛṣṇa.

## \|\| 9.16.12 \|\|

*bhūmyaptejonilākāśāhammahatprakṛtīḥ kramāt \|*  
*krāntvā daśottaraguṇāḥ prāpa golokamadbhutam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Having successively crossed (the sheaths of) the elements, viz. earth, water, fire, wind, and ether, Ego (Ahaṃ), Mahat and Prakṛti, each of which is ten times (larger) than the previous one, he arrived at the wonderful Goloka.

## \|\| 9.16.13 \|\|

*dhāma tejomayaṃ taddhi prāpyamekāntikairhareḥ \|*  
*gacchandadarśa vitatāmagādhāṃ virajāṃ nadīm \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. It was the glorious abode, accessible only to those exclusively devoted to Had. While going he saw the extensively wide and fathomless river Virajā.

## \|\| 9.16.14 \|\|

*gopīgopagaṇasnānadhautacandanasaurabhām \|*  
*puṇḍarīkaiḥ kokanadai ramyāmindīvarairapi \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. It has the fragrance of sandal due to the bath taken by multitudes of cowherds and cowherdesses. It appeared beautiful with lotuses white, ted and blue in colour.

## \|\| 9.16.15 \|\|

*tasyāstaṭaṃ manohāri sphaṭikāśmamayaṃ mahat \|*  
*prāpa śvetaharidraktapītasanmaṇirājitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He arrived at its bank which was extensive, attractive to the mind, full of crystal-stones. It was beautified with excellent precious stones of white, green, red and yellow colour.

## \|\| 9.16.16 \|\|

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye golokavarṇanaṃ nāma ṣoḍaśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. It was full of rows of wish-yielding trees. It was beautified with coral-sprouts. It was adorned with mines of precious stones, like syamantaka, sapphire and others.

## \|\| 9.16.17 \|\|

*nānāmaṇīndranicitasopānatatiśobhanam \|*  
*kūjadbhirmadhuraṃ juṣṭaṃ haṃsakāraṇḍavādibhiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. It was extremely beautiful with steps (of the ghats) studded with excellent gems of various kinds. It was occupied by swans, Kāraṇḍava ducks (and other aquatic birds) warbling sweetly.

## \|\| 9.16.18-19 \|\|

*vṛndaiḥ kāmadughānāṃ ca gajendrāṇāṃ ca vājinām \|*  
*pibadbhirnnirmalaṃ toyaṃ rājitaṃ sa vyatikramat \|\| 18 \|\|*

*uttīryā'tha dhunī divyāṃ tatkṣaṇādīśvarecchayā \|*  
*taddhāmaparikhābhūtāṃ śataśṛṅgāgamāpa saḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Its splendid, translucent water was being drunk up by multitudes of wish-yielding cows, excellent elephants and horses. He crossed it. Having crossed in a moment the heavenly river which formed a moat round the Lord’s residence, through the will of the Lord, he arrived at Mount Śataśṛṅga (‘having a hundred peaks’).

## \|\| 9.16.20 \|\|

*hiraṇmayaṃ darśanīyaṃ koṭiyojanamucchritam \|*  
*vistāre daśakoṭyastu yojanānāṃ manoharam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. It was of gold and beautiful. It was ten million Yojanas in height. Its extent was hundred million Yojanas and was attractive to the mind.

## \|\| 9.16.21-22 \|\|

*sahasraśaḥ kalpavṛkṣaiḥ pārijātādibhirdrumaiḥ \|*  
*mallikāyūthikābhiśca lavaṅgailālatādibhiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*svarṇarambhādibhiścānyaiḥ śobhamānaṃ mahīruhaiḥ \|*  
*divyairmṛgagaṇairnnāgaiḥ pakṣibhiśca sukūjitaiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. It was adorned with (the growth of) thousands of wish-yielding trees and trees like Pārijāta and others, and creepers like Mallikā, Yūthikā (varieties of jasmine), cloves and cardamoms. It was beautified with trees such as golden plantain trees, and also multitudes of heavenly deer, elephants and sweet-warbling birds.

## \|\| 9.16.23 \|\|

*durgāyitasya taddhāmnastasya ramyeṣu sānuṣu \|*  
*manojñānvitatānaikṣadbhagavadrāsamaṇḍapān \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. In his castle-like abode on the beautiful peaks, he saw mind-attracting Rāsa-maṇḍapas (i.e. halls for dance called Rāsa) of the Lord spread out.

## \|\| 9.16.24 \|\|

*vṛtānudyānatatibhiḥ phullapuṣpasugandhibhiḥ \|*  
*kapāṭai ratnanicitaiścaturdvārasuśobhanān \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. They were surrounded by series of gardens, fragrant with flowers in full bloom. They looked beautiful with gem-set panelled doors in four directions.

## \|\| 9.16.25 \|\|

*citratoraṇasaṃpannai ratnastambhaiḥ sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*juṣṭāṃśca kadalīstambhairmuktālambairvitānakaiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. They were furnished with wonderful arched doorways, and with thousands of pillars studded with jewels. They were provided with pillars of plantain trees and windows with wreaths of pearls suspended thereon.

## \|\| 9.16.26 \|\|

*dūrvālājākṣataphalairyuktānmāṅgalikairapi \|*  
*candanāgurukastūrīkeśarokṣita catvarān \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. They were provided with auspicious Dūrvā grass, fried grains, unbroken rice grains and fruits. The quadrangular places therein were sprinkled with sandal, agallochum, musk and saffron.

## \|\| 9.16.27 \|\|

*suśrāvyavādyaninadairhṛdyānbahuvidhairapi \|*  
*teṣu yūthāni gopīnāṃ koṭiśaḥ sa dadarśa ha \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. They were appealing to the heart, with various kinds of sweet sounds of musical instruments pleasing to the ears (and hence worth listening). He saw there crores of multitudes of cowherdesses.

## \|\| 9.16.28-30 \|\|

*anarghyavāsobhūṣābhiḥ sadratnamaṇikaṅkaṇaiḥ \|*  
*kāñcīnūpurakeyūraiḥ śobhitānyaṅgulīyakaiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tāruṇyarūpalāvaṇyaiḥ svaraiścā'pratimāni hi \|*  
*rādhālakṣmīsavarṇāni śṛṅgārikakarāṇi ca \|\| 29 \|\|*

*bhogadravyairbahuvidhairmaṇḍapeṣu yuteṣu ca \|*  
*vilasanti ca gāyanti manojñāḥ kṛṣṇagītikāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

28-30. They were adorned with invaluable garments and ornaments, with bangles studded with excellent jewels, girdles, anklets, armlets and rings. They were endowed with youth and loveliness of form and features, and with incomparably sweet voice. Their complexion was like that of Rādhā and Lakṣmī and (had) amorous hands. In the hall provided with various articles of enjoyment, they were amusing themselves and singing pleasing songs about Kṛṣṇa.

## \|\| 9.16.31 \|\|

*upatyakāsu tasyādreratha vṛndāvanābhidham \|*  
*vanaṃ mahattadadrākṣītsāvarṇe nārado muniḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Sage Nārada saw a great forest called Vṛndāvana at the foot of that mountain, O Sāvarṇi.

## \|\| 9.16.32 \|\|

*kṛṣṇasya rādhikāyāśca priyaṃ tatkrīḍanasthalam \|*  
*kalpadrumālibhī ramyaṃ sarobhiśca sapaṅkajaiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. It was the playground favourite with Kṛṣṇa and Rādhā. It was beautiful on account of the rows of wish-yielding trees and lakes with blooming lotuses.

## \|\| 9.16.33-37 \|\|

*āmrairāmrātakairnīpairbadarībhiśca dāḍimaiḥ \|*  
*kharjūrīpūganāraṃgairnnālikeraiśca candanaiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*jambūjambīrapanasairakṣodaiḥ suradārubhiḥ \|*  
*kadalībhiścampakaiśca drākṣābhiḥ svarṇaketakaiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*phalapuṣpabharānamrairnnānāvṛkṣairvirājitam \|*  
*mallikā mādhavīkundairllavaṃgairyūthikādibhiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*mandaśītasugandhena sevitaṃ mātariśvanā \|*  
*śataśṛṅgasnutairārdraṃ nirjharaiśca samantataḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*sadā vasanta śobhāḍhyaṃ ratnadīpālimaṇḍitaiḥ \|*  
*śṛṅgārikadravyayutaiḥ kuñjairjuṣṭamanekaśaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

33-37. It was beautified (lit. illuminated) with trees like mango, hog-plum, Kadamba, jujube trees, pomegranates, date-palms, betelnut trees, orange trees, coconut palms, sandal trees, rose-apples, citron trees, bread-fruit trees, walnut trees, plantain trees, Caṃpaka trees, grape-vines, golden Ketakas. All these trees were bending down with the weight of fruits and flowers.

It was served by a gentle wind, wafting the cool and sweet fragrance of (flowers of) Mallikā, Mādhavī, Kunda, cloves, and jasmine. All around, it was wet with spring-water issuing from Śataśṛṅga. It was richly endowed with the beauty of the spring season. It was endowed with innumerable bowers, beautified with rows of lamps studded with gems and provided with materials suitable for amorous sports.

## \|\| 9.16.38 \|\|

*gopānāṃ gopikānāṃ ca kṛṣṇasaṃkīrttanairmuhuḥ \|*  
*govatsa pakṣininadairnnānābhūṣaṇanisvanaiḥ \|*  
*dadhimanthanaśabdaiśca sarvato nāditaṃ mune \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O sage, it was resonant with the sound of glorifications (or repetitions of the name) of Kṛṣṇa by cowherds and cowherdesses, with the lowing of cows and calves, the warbling of birds and jingling sound of various ornaments and the sound of the churning of curds.

## \|\| 9.16.39 \|\|

*phullapuṣpaphalānamranānādrumasuśobhanaiḥ \|*  
*dvātriṃśatavanairanyairyuktaṃ paśyamanoharaiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. It had thirty-two other forests, extremely beautiful with various kinds of trees, bending down with (the weight of) fully blossomed flowers and fruits, attracting the minds of spectators.

## \|\| 9.16.40-43 \|\|

*tadvīkṣya hṛṣṭaḥ sa prāpa golokapuramujvalam \|*  
*vartulaṃ ratnadurgaṃ ca rājamārgopaśobhitam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*rājitaṃ kṛṣṇabhaktānāṃ vimānaiḥ koṭibhistathā \|*  
*rathai ratnendrakhacitaiḥ kiṃkiṇījālaśobhitaiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*mahāmaṇīndranikarai ratnastambhālimaṇḍitaiḥ \|*  
*adbhutaiḥ koṭiśaḥ saudhaiḥ paṃktisaṃsthairmanoharam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*vilāsamaṇḍapai ramyai ratnasāravinirmitaḥ \|*  
*ratnendradīpatatibhiḥ śobhanaṃ ratnavedibhiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

40-43. He was greatly delighted to see it. He arrived at the resplendent city (capital) of Goloka. It was a circular citadel (full) of jewels. It was beautified with royal roads. It appeared splendid with crores of mansions of devotees of Kṛṣṇa, with chariots studded with excellent jewels and decorated with a number of small tinkling bells. It was beautiful on account of crores of wonderful mansions, full of treasures of excellent precious stones, adorned with pillars of precious stones—all arranged in rows.

It appeared splendid with beautiful halls of sports. It was built with excellent precious stones and was furnished with gem-set altars or quadrangles (lighted with) rows of lamps studded with excellent gems.

## \|\| 9.16.44 \|\|

*kesarāgurukastūrīkuṃkumadravacarcitam \|*  
*dadhidūrvālājapūgai rambhābhiḥ śobhitāṅgaṇam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Its courtyard was sprinkled with liquid (mixed) with filaments of flowers, agallochum, musk and saffron and with heaps of (vessels containing) curds, Dūrvā grass, fried grains and plantain trees.

## \|\| 9.16.45 \|\|

*vāripūrṇairhemaghaṭaistoraṇaiḥ kṛtamaṃgalam \|*  
*maṇikuṭṭimarājādhvacaladbhūrigajāśvakam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Auspiciousness was caused by gold pitchers full of water and arches constructed. In it a considerable number of elephants and horses were treading the royal roads paved with precious stones.

## \|\| 9.16.46 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇadarśanāyātairnnaikabrahmāṇḍanāyakaiḥ \|*  
*viriñciśaṃkarādyaiśca balihastaiḥ susaṃkulam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. It was crowded with a number of lords of cosmoses who had come to have a sight of Śrīkṛṣṇa and with great gods such as Brahmā and Śaṅkara having articles of worship in their hands.

## \|\| 9.16.47 \|\|

*vrajadbhiḥ kṛṣṇavīkṣātha gopagopīkadambakaiḥ \|*  
*susaṃkulamahāmārgaṃ mumodālokya tanmuniḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. It was full of multitudes of cowherds and cowherdesses who were going to have a look of Kṛṣṇa. The sage was delighted to see that great road so crowded (with these).

## \|\| 9.16.48 \|\|

*kṛṣṇamandiramāpā'tha sarvāścaryaṃ manoharam \|*  
*nandādivṛṣabhānvādigopasaudhālibhirvṛtam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Then, he reached the mansion of Kṛṣṇa which was beautiful and appeared marvellous to all. It was surrounded by rows of mansions of cowherds including Nanda and of Vṛṣabhānu and others.

## \|\| 9.16.49 \|\|

*caturdvāraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhirdurgaiḥ saparikhairyutam \|*  
*koṭigopavṛtaikaikadvārapālasurakṣitaiḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. It was provided with four gates and consisted of sixteen citadels with moats around them. Each gate of it was guarded by a crore of cowherds as gatekeepers surrounding it.

## \|\| 9.16.50 \|\|

*ratnastambhakapāṭeṣu dvārṣu svāgrasthiteṣu saḥ \|*  
*upaviṣṭānkrameṇaiva dvārapālāndadarśa ha \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. At the doors with jewelled pillars and panels in front of him, he saw successively the doorkeepers who were sitting there (on duty).

## Chapter 17 - Manifestation of Vāsudeva

## \|\| 9.17.1 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*tattvekakālasaṃbhūtakoṭikoṭyarkasannibham \|*  
*sa vyacaṣṭa mahattejo divyaṃ sitataraṃ mune \|\| 1 \|\|*

Skanda said:

1\. O sage, he saw a more brilliant, heavenly splendour, similar to crores of crores of suns arisen (and shining) simultaneously.

## \|\| 9.17.2 \|\|

*diśaśca vidiśaḥ sarvā ūrddhvādho vyāpnuvacca yat \|*  
*akṣaraṃ brahma kathitaṃ saccidānandalakṣaṇam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. It completely pervaded all the quarters, intermediate cardinal points, above and below. It is said to be imperishable Brahman, characterised by existence, knowledge and bliss.

## \|\| 9.17.3 \|\|

*prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ cobhau tatkāryāṇyapi sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*vyāptaṃ yadyogasaṃsiddhāḥ ṣaṭcakrāṇi nijāntare \|*  
*vyatītya mūrdhni paśyanti vāsudevaprasādataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. It permeated both Prakṛti and Puruṣa and their evolutes. It was that brilliance which persons accomplished in Yoga, crossing (in ascendance) all the six Cakras (plexuses) within (their body), see in their heads (in the Sahasrāra-Kamala) with the grace of Vāsudeva.

## \|\| 9.17.4 \|\|

*yadbhāsā bhāsitaḥ sūryo vahnirinduśca tārakāḥ \|*  
*bhāsayanti jagatsarvaṃ svaprakāśaṃ tathāmṛtam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. It is by his brilliance that the sun, the moon, fire and stars are illuminated. They irradiate the whole world by their imperishable light.

## \|\| 9.17.5 \|\|

*yadbrahmapuramityāhurbhagavaddhāma sātvatāḥ \|*  
*yasyāntikeṣu paritastiṣṭhantyarcakakoṭayaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Sātvatas called it Brahma-pura, the residence of the Lord, near which and around which crores of worshippers are standing.

## \|\| 9.17.6-7 \|\|

*brahmaśaṃkara vṛndāni hyuparyupari saṃbhramāt \|*  
*patanti balihastāni gopagopīvrajāśca yat \|\| 6 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇasyānugraho yasminsa tejasi tamīkṣate \|*  
*kevalaṃ teja evānye paśyanti na tu taṃ mune \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Multitudes of Brahmās ana Śaṅkaras with (materials of) worship in their hands, fall over it due to confusion. Cowherds and cowherdesses on whom there is the grace of Kṛṣṇa, see (the Lord) in that brilliance. Others see only the bright splendour but not him, O. sage.

## \|\| 9.17.8 \|\|

*tasmindadarśādbhutadivyamandiraṃ vicitraratnendramayaṃ manojñam \|*  
*ratnojjvalastambhasahasrakāntaṃ mahāsabhā maṇḍapadarśanīyam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He (Nārada) saw therein a wonderful, lustrous, celestial, beautiful palace, consisting of excellent precious stones of various kinds, with thousands of pillars shining with jewels, beautiful with a big assembly hall.

## \|\| 9.17.9 \|\|

*saudhālibhirbhūribhirujjvalābhiḥ svopāsakānāṃ parito virājitam \|*  
*vicitrasūkṣmāmbararatnabhūṣāvibhūṣitānāṃ hi nṛṇāṃ ca yoṣitām \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. It was illuminated all round with numerous rows of brilliant mansions of his devotees, both men and women, who were adorned with ornaments studded with jewels and with very fine garments of various kinds.

## \|\| 9.17.10 \|\|

*siṃhāsanaṃ tatra maṇīndrasārai ratnendrasāraiśca vinirmitaṃ saḥ \|*  
*āścaryakṛnprekṣakamānasānāṃ divya muniḥ praikṣata bhūriharṣaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The sage, with ecstatic delight, saw there a brilliant throne, created out of the quintessence of excellent precious stones, which caused wonder in the minds of spectators.

## \|\| 9.17.11-12 \|\|

*tatrā'tha kṛṣṇaṃ bhagavantamaikṣannārāyaṇaṃ nirguṇamāsthitaṃ saḥ \|*  
*sarvajñamīśaṃ puruṣottamaṃ ca yaṃ vāsudevaṃ ca vadanti sātvatāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*yaṃ kecidāhuḥ paramātmasaṃjñaṃ kecitparaṃ brahma parātparaṃ ca \|*  
*brahmeti kecidbhagavantameke viṣṇuṃ ca bhaktāḥ parameśvaraṃ ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Theṛe he saw seated (on the throne) Lord Kṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa, the attributeless (Brahman), the omniscient ruler (of the universe), the excellent (supreme) Puruṣa whom Sātvatas (i.e. devotees of Kṛṣṇa) call Vāsudeva. Him some devotees call the ‘Supreme Soul’, some call ‘Supreme Brahman’, others, ‘Brahman greater than the greatest’, some, ‘Lord Viṣṇu’ while others call the ‘Supreme Lord’.

## \|\| 9.17.13 \|\|

*kandarpasāhasramanoharāṅgaṃ sadā kiśoraṃ karuṇānidhānam \|*  
*atipraśāṃtākṛtidarśanīyaṃ kṣarākṣarebhyaśca paraṃ svatantram \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. (He saw) him, whose body was beautiful like a thousand gods of love (combined), who was always youthful (lit. a boy below 15 years of age), who, a receptacle of mercy, was graceful due to his extremely quiescent form, was superior to all the perishables and imperishables and (forever) independent.

## \|\| 9.17.14 \|\|

*naikāṇḍasargasthitināśalīlāvidhāyakāpāṃganirīkṣaṇaṃ ca \|*  
*anekakoṭyaṇḍamahādhirājaṃ viśvaikavandyaṃ naṭavaryaveṣam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. (He saw him) whose side-glance causes the sport (as it were) of creation, sustenance and destruction of a number of Brahmāṇḍas (Cosmoses), who is the supreme ruler of innumerable crores of Brahmāṇḍas, who is the sole (deity) worthy of being saluted by all, who has assumed the garb of a great actor.

## \|\| 9.17.15 \|\|

*anarghyadivyottamapītavāsasamanekasadratnavibhūṣaṇāḍhyam \|*  
*navīnajīmūtasamānavarṇaṃ karṇollasatsanmakarābhakuṇḍalam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. (He saw him) who was wearing excellent, yellow, priceless, resplendent garment, who appeared rich with ornaments of innumerable excellent jewels, whose complexion was (dark) like a newly formed cloud, and in whose ears excellent ear-rings of the shape of crocodile were shining.

## \|\| 9.17.16 \|\|

*nijāṃganiryatsitabhūritejaścayāvṛtatvātsitavarṇamuktam \|*  
*sadratnasārojjvalasatkirīṭaṃ śaratsarojacchadacārunetram \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. (He) is called white in complexion as he was enveloped in a highly brilliant mass of refulgence that was radiated from his person. His excellent crown was radiant with the wealth of excellent jewels. His eyes were charming like the petals of an autumnal lotus.

## \|\| 9.17.17 \|\|

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye śrīvāsudevadarśanaṃ nāma saptadaśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. His person was besmeared with excellent fragrant sandal (paste). One (panel-like) side of his chest was marked with Śrīvatsa. He was sweetly playing on a flute put to his mouth with his lotus-like beautiful arms.

## \|\| 9.17.18 \|\|

*jayāsuśīlālalitāmukhānāṃ vṛndaiḥ sakhīnāṃ saha rādhayā ca \|*  
*samarcyamānaṃ ramayā ca bhāmā kalindajā jāmbavatīmukhānām \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He was being worshipped by Rādhā, with multitudes of her friends, of whom Jayā, Suśīlā, Lalitā were prominent, and by Ramā and his consorts including Satyabhāmā, Kālindī (Yamunā) and Jāmbavatī.

## \|\| 9.17.19 \|\|

*dharmeṇa vedairakhilairbhagaiśca jñānādibhiḥ saṃyatapāṇiyugmaiḥ \|*  
*niṣevyamāṇaṃ ca sudarśanādyairnijāyudhairmūrtidharairanekaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He was being served by Dharma, Vedas, all the Suns and by Knowledge and others with their pairs of hands restrained (i.e. folded with reverence), and by his many weapons like Sudarśana who had assumed a personal form.

## \|\| 9.17.20 \|\|

*masāramāṇikyasuvarṇavarṇaiḥ sitaiśca kaiścinnijapārṣadāgryaiḥ \|*  
*upāsitaṃ cakragadābjaśaṅkhalasadbhujairnandasunandamukhyaiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He was waited upon by his prominent attendants who were like emerald, ruby and gold in complexion, and some of whom were white (in colour), and whose arms were shining with the discus, mace, lotus and conch held (by them), and of whom Nanda and Sunanda were prominent.

## \|\| 9.17.21 \|\|

*śrīdāmamukhyairatha gopaveṣairbhaktyāvanamrairdvibhujairanekaiḥ \|*  
*upāsyamānaṃ garuḍena cāgrato vibhūtibhiścāṣṭabhirānatābhiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. He was being worshipped by many two-handed persons in the garb of cowherds, of whom Śrīdāmā was the chief. They bent down (to bow) with devotion. He was adored by Garuḍa, and by eight supernatural powers who bowed down to him.

## \|\| 9.17.22 \|\|

*mūrtyā ca śāntyā dayayā ca sevitaṃ puṣṭyā ca tuṣṭyā hyatha medhayā ca \|*  
*śraddhākriyā hyunnatibhiśca maitryā tathā titikṣāsmṛtibuddhibhiśca \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Assuming personal forms, he was served by Quiescence, Mercy, Magnificence (Nourishment?), Contentment, Intelligence, Faith, Action, Prosperity, and by Friendliness, Forbearance, Memory and Intellect as well.

## \|\| 9.17.23 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā tamatyadbhutadivyamūrtti tadrūpasaurabhyahṛtākhilendriyaḥ \|*  
*ānandavāripratiruddhadṛṣṭiḥ premṇorddhvaromā sukhasaṃbhṛto'bhūt \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. On seeing that marvellous, refulgent form, all his sense-organs were captivated by the pleasing fragrance of his form. His sight was obstructed due to the tears of joy; his hair stood on end out of love for him and he was filled with pleasure.

## \|\| 9.17.24 \|\|

*daṇḍavattaṃ namaskṛtya nāradaḥ premavihvalaḥ \|*  
*baddhāñjalipuṭastasthau vīkṣamāṇastadānanam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Overwhelmed with love, Nārada prostrated himself like a staff before him; with his hands folded in reverence, he stood before him, looking at his face.

## \|\| 9.17.25 \|\|

*taṃ mānayāmāsa hariḥ pṛṣṭvā svāgatamādarāt \|*  
*bhaktamekāntikaṃ svasya svenaiva ca didṛkṣitam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Hari honoured him who was devoted to him exclusively, and whom he desired to see, by respectfully welcoming him (lit. by enquiring about his happy arrival).

## \|\| 9.17.26 \|\|

*bhagavadvākyapīyūṣāsvādaprāptātmasaṃsmṛtiḥ \|*  
*taddarśanamahānando bhaktyā tuṣṭāva taṃ muniḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The sage who came to himself by the taste of the nectar (in the form) of the Lord’s speech, and who was extremely delighted by his sight, praised him devoutly.

## \|\| 9.17.27 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*jaya śrīkṛṣṇa bhagavannārāyaṇa jagatprabho \|*  
*vāsudevā'khilāvāsa sadaikāntikavallabha \|\| 27 \|\|*

Nārada said:

27\. Be victorious, O Śrīkṛṣṇa, Lord Nārāyaṇa, the master of the world, Vāsudeva, who abide in all, and are always dear to your exclusive devotees.

## \|\| 9.17.28 \|\|

*apyāścaryārcanīyāṅghre rādhikākamalādibhiḥ \|*  
*tvamevātyantikaṃ śreyo'bhīpsatāṃ paramā gatiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Your very wonderful feet are worthy of being worshipped by Rādhikā and Kamalā. You are the highest beatitude, and the supreme resort to those who aspire to it.

## \|\| 9.17.29 \|\|

*nityānāmātmanāṃ nitya ātmā cetanacetanaḥ \|*  
*kṣarākṣarebhyaśca parastvaṃ brahma paramaṃ hare \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. You are the eternal (element) of eternal souls; the soul, the sentience of sentient beings; beyond the perishables and imperishables. You are the Supreme Brahman, O Hari.

## \|\| 9.17.30 \|\|

*yathā viśuddhiḥ siddhiśca bhaktyā paramayā tava \|*  
*tathā na syānnṛṇāmanyaiḥ sādhanaistapa ādibhiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The extreme purity and supernatural power as is obtained by highest devotion to you, is not achieved by men with other means including penance.

## \|\| 9.17.31 \|\|

*tvadaṅghridivyajyotsnaikā mumukṣūṇāṃ hṛdi sthitam \|*  
*mahatsantamasaṃhartuṃ sadyaḥ śaktāsti satpate \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Only the divine moonlight of your feet is capable of immediately destroying the thick darkness that abides in the hearts of people desirous of final liberation, O noble master.

## \|\| 9.17.32 \|\|

*sarvairvedaistvamevejya upāsyo jñeya eva ca \|*  
*nirūpitosi bhagavansarvakāraṇakāraṇam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O venerable Lord, the cause of all causes, you are proclaimed as the only one who should be worshipped, propitiated and realized by the Vedas.

## \|\| 9.17.33 \|\|

*ekaikasminromakūpe yattavāsti sitaṃ mahaḥ \|*  
*śāntamānaṃdarūpaṃ ca tatkoṭīnduprabhādhikam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The auspicious, blissful, bright refulgence that abides in each and every pore (of your skin), is more brilliant than the light of a crore of moons.

## \|\| 9.17.34 \|\|

*asmiṃstvamakṣare dhāmni nirguṇe'mṛtasañjñake \|*  
*mahaḥpuñje sadaivāsse nirguṇaḥ puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. (You) the supreme attributeless person, always dwell in this imperishable, attributeless, residence called Amṛta, which is a mass of lustre.

## \|\| 9.17.35 \|\|

*brahmāṇḍabhayadātkālānmāyāyāśca mahābhayāt \|*  
*muktā bhaktā bhavantyeva tvadīyopāsanābalāt \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. By the power of your propitiation your devotees become free from Kāla who strikes terror into the universe, and from the great fear of Māyā.

## \|\| 9.17.36 \|\|

*taṃ tvāmahamupetosmi śaraṇaṃ jagadīśvaram \|*  
*sarvātmānaṃ vibhuṃ brahma mahāpuruṣamacyutam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. For a resort I have approached you who are the master of the universe, and the soul abiding in all, the all-pervading Brahman, the great imperishable Puruṣa.

## \|\| 9.17.37 \|\|

*yathā tvaccaraṇāmbhoje bhaktirme niścalā sadā \|*  
*bhavettathaiva deveśa karttumarhasyanugraham \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O Lord of Devas, it behoves you to confer that favour whereby my devotion unto your lotus-feet will always be firm.

## Chapter 18 - Incarnations of Vāsudeva

## \|\| 9.18.1 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*darśanaṃ mama yajjātaṃ tava tattu mahāmune \|*  
*nityaikāntikabhaktatvānnirdambhatvānmadicchayā \|\| 1 \|\|*

The Lord said:

1\. My audience (vision) that you got, O great sage, is due to your being an ever-exclusive devotee of mine, absence of hypocrisy (in you), and my will (to grant you the audience).

## \|\| 9.18.2 \|\|

*ahiṃsā brahmacaryaṃ ca tvayi nityaṃ ca taddvayam \|*  
*svadharmopaśamau caiva vairāgyaṃ cātmavedanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. In you there is always (observance of) both non-violence and celibacy, abidance by personal (religious) duties, quiescence, disaffection to worldly (objects of) enjoyment, and perception and knowledge of the soul.

## \|\| 9.18.3 \|\|

*satsaṅgo'ṣṭāṅgayogaśca sarvathendriyanigrahaḥ \|*  
*munyannavṛttiśca tapaḥ sarvavyasanahīnatā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. (You always have) association with saintly persons, (practice of) Yoga with all its eight parts, absolute sense-control, subsistence on food (prescribed) for sages, penance and freedom from all vices.

## \|\| 9.18.4 \|\|

*madekāntikabhaktiśca mahātmyajñānapūrvikā \|*  
*varttate tena māmatra paśyasi tvaṃ hi suvrata \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Absolute devotion exclusively to me, preceded by the knowledge of my greatness, is in you. Hence you (can) see me here, O firm observer of religious vows.

## \|\| 9.18.5 \|\|

*īdṛglakṣaṇasaṃpannā ye syuranyepi mānavāḥ \|*  
*tepi māmīdṛśaṃ vipra paśyantyekāntikapriyam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. If there be ever other men who are endowed with these characteristics, they also (can) see me in such a form—me who am dear to devotees exclusively attached to me, O Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 9.18.6 \|\|

*asāvahamiha brahmannasminnakṣaradhāmani \|*  
*rādhālakṣmīyuto nityaṃ vasāmi svāśritaiḥ saha \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O Brāhmaṇa, I, who am such (as described above) accompanied by Rādhā and Lakṣmī always stay in this imperishable residence along with my dependents.

## \|\| 9.18.7 \|\|

*vāsudevasvarūpohaṃ sarvakarmaphalapradaḥ \|*  
*antaryāmitayā vartte svatantraḥ sarvadehinām \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. I, who am of the form of Vāsudeva, am the giver of the fruits of all actions. By my immanence in all embodied beings, I always act as an independent one.

## \|\| 9.18.8 \|\|

*vaikuṇṭhākhyaṃ mahādhāmni lakṣmyā saha caturbhujaḥ \|*  
*vasāmi nandagaruḍamukhyaiḥ sākaṃ ca pārṣadaiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In the great abode called Vaikuṇṭha, I, a four-armed one, live with (my consort) Lakṣmī and along with my attendants of whom Nanda and Garuḍa are the chief ones.

## \|\| 9.18.9 \|\|

*dhāmni tejomaye divye śvetadvīpe'nvahaṃ bhuvi \|*  
*dadāmi śvetamuktebhyaḥ pañcakālaṃ svadarśanam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On the earth, in the divine refulgent residence, Śveta-Dvīpa, I grant my audience five times a day, to the Śveta-muktas (i.e. liberated souls of that Dvīpa).

## \|\| 9.18.10 \|\|

*kurve'niruddhapradyumnasaṃkarṣaṇasamāhvayaiḥ \|*  
*svarūpairnaikakoṭyaṇḍasargasthityapyayānaham \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. With my personal forms called Aniruddha, Pradyumna and Saṅkarṣaṇa I carry out the creation, sustenance and destruction of innumerable crores of Brahmāṇḍas (Cosmoses).

## \|\| 9.18.11 \|\|

*sargārambhe mayā brahmā sṛṣṭo nābhisaroruhāt \|*  
*tapasārādhayāmāsa sa māṃ yajñaiśca nārada \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. At the beginning of creation Brahmā was created by me from the lotus in my navel. He propitiated me with penance and sacrifices, O Nārada.

## \|\| 9.18.12-20 \|\|

*tatastasmai prasanno'haṃ prādadāmīpsitānvarān \|*  
*brahmanprāsyasi sāmarthyaṃ prajānāṃ tvaṃ visarjane \|\| 12 \|\|*

*ājñāyāmeva tāḥ sarvāstava sthāsyanti madvarāt \|*  
*vedāścāpi sphuriṣyanti tava buddhau sanātanāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*jñānaṃ ca matsvarūpasya yathāvatte bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tvayā kṛtāṃ ca maryādāṃ nātikraṃsyati kaścana \|\| 14 \|\|*

*surāsuragaṇānāṃ ca munīnāṃ ca mahātmanām \|*  
*tvameva varado brahmanvarepsūnāṃ bhaviṣyasi \|\| 15 \|\|*

*asādhye yatra kārye ca mohameṣyasi tattvaham \|*  
*prādurbhūya kariṣyami smṛtamātrastvayā vidhe \|\| 16 \|\|*

*sṛjyamāne tvayā viśve naṣṭāṃ pṛthvīṃ mahārṇave \|*  
*ānayiṣyāmi svaṃ sthānaṃ vārāhaṃ rūpamāsthitaḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyākṣaṃ nihatyaiva daiteyaṃ balagarvitam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye śrīvāsudevāvatārādikathanaṃnāmā'ṣṭādaśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*sudhāyai mathnatāmabdhiṃ kāśyapānāṃ nirāśrayam \|*  
*manthānaṃ kūrmarūpohaṃ dhāsye pṛṣṭhe ca mandaram \|\| 19 \|\|*

*nārasiṃhaṃ vapuḥ kṛtvā hiraṇyakaśipuṃ vidhe \|*  
*surakārye haniṣyāmi yajñaghnaṃ ditinandanam \|\| 20 \|\|*

12-20. Then being pleased with him, I granted the boons desired by him: (saying) “O Brahman, you will get the necessary (competence) for creation of subjects. By virtue of my boon all of them will abide by your command. The eternal Vedas will manifest themselves in your intelligence. You will have a correct knowledge of my own form. None shall cross the bounds of morality and propriety laid down by you. You alone will be the bestower of boons to multitudes of Suras and Asuras and noble-souled sages, who are desirous of obtaining boons, O Brahman. O Vidhi (Brahman), when, in a task which cannot be accomplished, you get embarrassed or deluded, I shall manifest myself as soon as I am remembered by you, and accomplish that task for you. While the universe is being created by you, I shall assume the form of a boar and bring the earth which is submerged and lost in the great ocean, and establish it in its own place after killing the Daitya Hiraṇyākṣa proud of his strength. When your day ends, I shall become a fish and shall support (floating) like a boat, the earth along with its medicinal plants, Manus and others, during the period of your night. When the sons of Kaśyapa (i.e. Devas and Asuras) will churn the ocean for (obtaining) nectar, I, assuming the form of a tortoise, will bear on my back Mount Mandara used as the churning rod. Assuming the form of a Man-Lion, I shall kill Hiraṇyakaśipu, the son of Diti, the destroyer of sacrifices, for accomplishing the task of Suras, O Vidhi.

## \|\| 9.18.21-23 \|\|

*virocanasya balavānbaliḥ putro mahāsuraḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyati sa śakraṃ ca svārājyāccyāvayiṣyati \|\| 21 \|\|*

*trailokye'pahṛte tena vimukhe ca śacīpatau \|*  
*adityāṃ dvādaśaḥ putraḥ saṃbhaviṣyāmi kaśyapāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tato rājyaṃ pradāsyāmi devendrāya divaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*devatāḥ sthāpayiṣyāmi sveṣu sthāneṣvahaṃ vidhe \|*  
*baliṃ caiva kariṣyāmi pātālatalavāsinam \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. There will be (born) Bali, the son of Virocana, a powerful great Asura. He will dislodge Śakra from his kingdom. When the three worlds are taken away (i.e. conquered) by him, and the husband of Śacī (Indra) is disappointed and downcast, I shall be the twelfth son of Aditi from Kaśyapa. Then, I shall give again the kingdom of heaven to Devendra. I shall re-establish the deities in their respective places, O Brahmā. And I shall make Bali an inhabitant of the nethermost subterranean world.

## \|\| 9.18.24 \|\|

*kardamāddevahūtyāṃ ca bhūtvā'tha kapilābhidhaḥ \|*  
*pravartayiṣye kālena naṣṭaṃ sāṃkhyaṃ virāgayuk \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Becoming (a son) named Kapila from Kardama and Devahūtī, I, endowed with indifference to the world, shall proclaim the Sāṅkhya philosophy that was lost (forgotten) during the course of time.

## \|\| 9.18.25 \|\|

*datto bhūtyā'nasūyayāmatrerānvikṣikīṃ tataḥ \|*  
*prahlādāyopadekṣyāmi vidyāṃ ca yadave vidhe \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Becoming (incarnating as) Datta, the son of Anasūyā and Atri, I shall teach the science called Ānvīkṣikī (i.e. Nyāya) to Prahlāda and to Yadu (Sahasrārjuna?), O Vidhi.

## \|\| 9.18.26 \|\|

*merudevyāṃ suto nābherbhūtvāhamṛṣabho bhuvi \|*  
*dharmaṃ pāramahaṃsyākhyaṃ vartayiṣye sanātanam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Incarnating (with the name) Vṛṣabha, the son of Merudevī and Nābhi, I shall propagate the ancient Dharma called Pāramahaṃsya (i.e. pertaining to Paramahaṃsas—the highest sect of recluses).

## \|\| 9.18.27 \|\|

*tretāyuge bhaviṣyāmi rāmo bhṛgukulodvahaḥ \|*  
*kṣatraṃ cotsādayiṣyāmi bhagnasetukadadhvagam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. In Tretā, I shall become Rāma, a scion of Bhṛgu family. I shall annihilate Kṣatriyas who have transgressed the limits (of morality etc.) and have taken to bad ways.

## \|\| 9.18.28-31 \|\|

*sandhau tu samanuprāpte tretāyā dvāparasya ca \|*  
*kauśalyāyāṃ bhaviṣyāmi rāmo daśarathādaham \|\| 28 \|\|*

*sītābhidhānā lakṣmīśca bhavitrī janakātmajā \|*  
*udvahiṣyāmi tāmaiśaṃ bhaṃktvā dhanurahaṃ mahat \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tato rakṣaḥpatiṃ ghoraṃ devarṣidrohakāriṇam \|*  
*sītāpahāriṇaṃ saṃkhye haniṣyāmi sahānujam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*tasya me tu caritrāṇi vālmīkyādyā maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*tadā gāsyanti bahudhā yacchruteḥ syādaghakṣayaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

28-31. When the period of junction between Tretā and Dvāpara (i.e. Tretā coming to an end and Dvāpara about to start) arrives, I shall become Rāma, son of Daśaratha and Kauśalyā. Lakṣmī, with the name Sītā, will be the daughter of Janaka. I shall marry her after breaking the big bow of Śiva. I shall then kill in battle along with his brothers the terrible king of Rākṣasas (Rāvaṇa), enemy of Devas and sages and abductor of Sītā. Then great sages including Vālmīki will sing variously of his (that is my) exploits, on hearing which there will be destruction of sins.

## \|\| 9.18.32-33 \|\|

*dvāparasya kaleścaiva sandhau paryavasānike \|*  
*bhūbhārāsuranāśārthaṃ pātuṃ dharmaṃ ca dhārmikān \|*  
*vasudevādbhaviṣyāmi devakyāṃ mathurāpure \|\| 32 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇohaṃ vāsudevākhyastathā saṃkarṣaṇo balaḥ \|*  
*pradyumnaścā'niruddhaśca bhaviṣyanti yadoḥ kule \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. When the junction of Dvāpara and Kali comes to a close, for the sake of annihilation of Asuras who become burden to the earth, and for protecting righteous people, I, Kṛṣṇa, called Vāsudeva, will be born of Vasudeva and Devakī in the city of Mathurā. Similarly Saṅkarṣaṇa alias Balarāma, Pradyumna and Aniruddha (i.e. all the Vyūhas of the Pāñcarātras) will be born in the family of Yadu.

## \|\| 9.18.34 \|\|

*gopasya vṛṣabhānostu sutā rādhā bhaviṣyati \|*  
*vṛndāvane tayā sākaṃ vihariṣyāmi padmaja \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Rādhā will be the daughter of the cowherd Vṛṣabhānu and I shall sport with her in Vṛndāvana, O Lotus-born One (Brahmā).

## \|\| 9.18.35 \|\|

*lakṣmīśca bhīṣmakasutā rukmiṇyākhyā bhaviṣyati \|*  
*udvahiṣyāmi rājanyānyuddhe nirjitya tāmaham \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Lakṣmī will be born as the daughter of Bhīṣmaka by name Rukmiṇī. After defeating kings in a battle, I shall many her.

## \|\| 9.18.36 \|\|

*dharmadruho'surānhatvā tadāviṣṭāṃśca bhūpatīn \|*  
*dharmaṃ saṃsthāpayanneva kariṣye nirbharāṃ bhuvam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. After killing Asuras, the enemies of Dharma and of kings who were haunted by them, and by establishing Dharma, I shall make the earth free from burden.

## \|\| 9.18.37 \|\|

*yena kenāpi bhāvena yasya kasyāpi mānasam \|*  
*mayi saṃyokṣyate taṃtaṃ neṣye brahmagatiṃ parām \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. If the mind of a person is in any way devoted to me, I shall take him to the supreme position of Brahman.

## \|\| 9.18.38 \|\|

*dharmaṃ bhuvi sthāpayitvā kṛtvā yadukulakṣayam \|*  
*paśyatāṃ sarvadevānāmantarddhāsye bhuvastataḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. After establishing righteousness on the earth, and bringing about the annihilation of Yadu’s race, I shall then vanish from the earth, while Devas look on.

## \|\| 9.18.39 \|\|

*kṛṣṇasya mama vīryāṇi kṛṣṇadvaipāyanādayaḥ \|*  
*gāsyanti bahudhā brahmansadyaḥ pāpaharāṇi hi \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Kṛṣṇa-Dvaipāyana and others will extol variously the heroic exploits of me as Kṛṣṇa. They will be instant destroyers of sins.

## \|\| 9.18.40 \|\|

*kṛṣṇadvaipāyano bhūtvā parāśaramuneḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*śākhāvibhāgaṃ vedasya kariṣyāmi taroriva \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. After incarnating as Kṛṣṇa-Dvaipāyana, the son of Parāśara, I shall divide the Veda into different branches like a tree.

## \|\| 9.18.41 \|\|

*vaidikaṃ vidhimāśritya trilokīparipīḍakān \|*  
*chalena mohayiṣyāmi bhūtvā buddho'surānaham \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. By becoming Buddha, I shall delude by the use of fallacious reasoning and deceit the Asuras who adopting Vedic practices will harass the three worlds.

## \|\| 9.18.42-43 \|\|

*mayā kṛṣṇena nihatāḥ sārjunena raṇeṣu ye \|*  
*pravartayiṣyantyasurāste tvadharmaṃ yadā kṣitau \|\| 42 \|\|*

*dharmadevāttadā bhaktādahaṃ nārāyaṇo muniḥ \|*  
*janiṣye kośale deśe bhūmau hi sāmago dvijaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. When the Asuras killed by me (as) Kṛṣṇa and by Arjuna in the battles, will promote and establish Adharma (unrighteous practices) on the earth, I, sage Nārāyaṇa, shall be born on the earth from my devotee Dharmadeva in the land of Kośala, as a Brāhmaṇa-singer of Sāman hymns.

## \|\| 9.18.44 \|\|

*muniśāpānnṛtāṃ prāptānṛṣīṃstāta tathoddhavam \|*  
*tato'vitāsurebhyo'haṃ saddharmaṃ sthāpayannaja \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. O Aja (Brahma), establishing the holy Dharma I shall be the protector of sages who will be born as men by the curse of Munis (other sages) as well as Uddhava, O child.

## \|\| 9.18.45 \|\|

*janānmlecchamayānbhūmau kalerante mahainasaḥ \|*  
*kalkī bhūtvā haniṣyāmi vicarandivyavājinā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. At the end of Kali I shall incarnate as Kalki. Riding a divine horse, I shall kill highly sinful people of Mleccha origin.

## \|\| 9.18.46 \|\|

*yadā yadā ca vedokto dharmo nāśiṣyate'suraiḥ \|*  
*prādurbhāvo bhaviṣyo me tadrakṣāyai tadā tadā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Whenever the Dharma promulgated in the Vedas is being destroyed by Asuras, at that time my manifestation shall take place for its protection.

## \|\| 9.18.47 \|\|

*tasmāccintāṃ vihāyaiva prajāḥ sṛja yathā purā \|*  
*etāndattvā varāṃstasmā ahamantarhito'bhavam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Therefore, completely giving up anxiety, create subjects as before.”

After conferring these boons upon him I became invisible.

## \|\| 9.18.48 \|\|

*yathā tasmai varā dattāstathaiva ca mayā kṛtam \|*  
*kurve kariṣye ca mune nijaśaktibhirañjasā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. I did, do, shall do easily by means of my powers what all the boons given to him imply.

## \|\| 9.18.49-50 \|\|

*evaṃvidhasya me brahmannīśituḥ sarvadehinām \|*  
*darśanaṃ durlabhaṃ jātaṃ tavaikāntikabhaktitaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*varaṃ varaya mattastvaṃ svābhīṣṭaṃ munisattama \|*  
*prasannosmi bhṛśaṃ tubhyaṃ nāphalaṃ mama darśanam \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. O Brāhmaṇa, the vision of mine, who am the controller of all embodied beings in this way, has become very difficult to obtain. (It was possible for you) due to your single-minded devotion unto me.

O excellent sage, seek any boon desired by you from me. I am highly pleased with you. My audience shall not be fruitless.

## \|\| 9.18.51 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*śrutveti bhagavadvākyaṃ nārado munisattamaḥ \|*  
*manyamāno nijaṃ dhanyaṃ tamuvāca prabhuṃ mune \|\| 51 \|\|*

Skanda said:

51\. On hearing the speech of the Lord, the excellent sage Nārada, regarded himself as blessed, and addressed the Lord, O sage.

## \|\| 9.18.52 \|\|

*darśanādeva te svāminsaṃpūrṇo me manorathaḥ \|*  
*idaṃ hi durlabhaṃ manye sarveṣāmapi dehinām \|\| 52 \|\|*

(Nārada said:)

52\. 0 Master, by your very vision all my desire is fulfilled. I regard this (i.e. your audience) as extremely difficult to get for all embodied beings.

## \|\| 9.18.53 \|\|

*ataste ca tvadīyānāṃ tvaddhāmnosyā'mṛtasya ca \|*  
*sākṣātsamīkṣaṇādanyatprāpyaṃ me nāsti vāṃchitam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Hence nothing except directly seeing you, your devotee and this your residence (called) Amṛta, is desired by me as worth obtaining.

## \|\| 9.18.54 \|\|

*itonyaddurlabhaṃ kvāpi nāsti brahmāṇḍagolake \|*  
*yadahaṃ parituṣṭātte prārthayeyamihācyuta \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Compared with this, there is nothing else anywhere in this Brahmāṇḍa that is difficult to be obtained, and this I can request of you who are pleased with me here.

## \|\| 9.18.55 \|\|

*lokāntarasukhaṃ yattadvaidikaireva karmabhiḥ \|*  
*daivaiḥ pitryaiśca labhyeta taccāpyasti hi naśvaram \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The happiness in the other world, which is obtained by performance of Vedic rituals pertaining to Devas and ancestors, is also perishable.

## \|\| 9.18.56 \|\|

*necchāmi tadahaṃ kiñcitsukhaṃ tvattaḥ paraṃ prabho \|*  
*varamekaṃ tu yāce tvatsvepsitaṃ varadarṣabhāt \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. I do not wish that insignificant happiness to be greater than you, O Lord. I beg only one boon desired by me from you who are the most prominent among bestowers of boons.

## \|\| 9.18.57 \|\|

*tavā'tha tava bhaktānāṃ sadaiva guṇagāyane \|*  
*atyutsukāstu me buddhistvayi prītivivarddhinī \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. May my intellect be always eager for singing the excellences of you, as well as that of your devotees, and may it have ever-increasing love and devotion unto you.

## \|\| 9.18.58 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*tathāstviti pratiśrutya kṛṣṇasteneti yācitam \|*  
*gānopayuktāṃ mahatīṃ vīṇāṃ dattvā'bravītpunaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

Skanda said:

58\. Promising him ‘so be it’ to what was requested by him, Kṛṣṇa gave him a great lute useful in singing and spoke to him again.

## \|\| 9.18.59 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*adhunā gaccha devarṣe viśālāṃ badarīmitaḥ \|*  
*tatra dharmātmajaṃ bhaktyā māmārādhaya suvrata \|\| 59 \|\|*

The Lord said:

59\. O divine sage, go from this place to Viśālā Badarī (i.e. Badarikāśrama). There propitiate devoutly me, Nārāyaṇa, the son of Dharma.

## \|\| 9.18.60 \|\|

*tvaṃ hyekāntikabhaktosi mama niṣkapaṭāntaraḥ \|*  
*tena tvāmadhikaṃ manye vidherapi pitustava \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. You are a devotee exclusively attached to me. Your heart is free from deceit. Hence I esteem you better that God Brahmā, your faṃer.

## \|\| 9.18.61 \|\|

*yādṛśo'haṃ ca yadrūpo yāvāṃśca mahimā mama \|*  
*vidustatsarvamapi me bhaktā ekāntikā mune \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O sage, devotees exclusively attached to me, know everything about me, of my nature and form, and the extent of my greatness.

## \|\| 9.18.62 \|\|

*hṛdi cintyohamevāsmi satāṃ teṣāṃ ca te mama \|*  
*teṣāmiṣṭaṃ na matto'nyanmama tebhyo na kiñcana \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. In their hearts I am the only object of thought and contemplation, and they are so in mine. Their desired object is no other than I, and I too have none other but they.

## \|\| 9.18.63 \|\|

*yathā pativratā nāryo vaśīkurvanti satpatim \|*  
*nijairguṇaistathā bhaktā vaśīkurvanti māmapi \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Just as devoted, chaste wives bring good husbands under their power by their virtuous qualities, in the same way my devotees bring me under their power.

## \|\| 9.18.64 \|\|

*anuyāmi śriyā sākaṃ tānahaṃ paravāniva \|*  
*yatrayatra ca te santi tatratatrāhamasmi hi \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. I follow them along with Śrī, as if I am subservient to them. Wherever they are, I am present there.

## \|\| 9.18.65 \|\|

*satsaṃgādeva matprāptirbhavedbhuvi mumukṣatām \|*  
*nānyopāyena devarṣe satyamityavadhāraya \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. O divine sage, know the truth that to those who desire liberation, I can be attained in this world only through association with saintly persons, and by no other means.

## \|\| 9.18.66 \|\|

*māmeva yarhi śaraṇaṃ mānuṣāḥ prāpnuvanti ye \|*  
*tarhyeva te vimucyante māyāyā jīvabandhanāt \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Whenever men resort to me, they are immediately liberated from bondage to Māyā and the state of being a Jīva (i.e. a soul subject to Saṃsāra).

## \|\| 9.18.67 \|\|

*māṃ prapannastu puruṣo yena kenāpi bhāvataḥ \|*  
*yatheṣṭaṃ sukhamāpnoti na tu saṃsṛtimanyavat \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. With whatever feeling or inclination of mind a man seeks refuge in me, he gets the happiness as desired by him, but he does not revert to Saṃsāra, as in the case of others.

## \|\| 9.18.68 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*evamukto bhagavatā prāpto'nugrahamīpsitam \|*  
*praṇamya sāśrunayanaḥ paryāvartata nāradaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

Skanda said:

68\. Thus addressed by the Lord, Nārada who had obtained the desired favour, bowed down to him and returned with his eyes full of tears.

## \|\| 9.18.69 \|\|

*tameva vīṇayā gāyañchvetamuktamapaśyata \|*  
*prāgvatsvāgre calantaṃ tamanvagacchad dvijarṣabha \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. While singing with the lute, he saw the Śveta-Mukta (the liberated soul from Śveta-Dvīpa, his guide) going in front of him as before, and he (Nārada) followed him, O eminent Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 9.18.70 \|\|

*sadyaḥ śvetaṃ mahādvīpaṃ prāpya śvetānpraṇamya tān \|*  
*nivṛtto nārado brahmaṃstarasā merumāgamat \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Immediately after arriving at Śveta-dvīpa, he bowed down to them (all) and returned. Then Nārada arrived quickly at Meru.

## Chapter 19 - Nārada Meets Nara and Nārāyaṇa

## \|\| 9.19.1-4 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*tataḥ sa dadṛśe devau purāṇāvṛṣisattamau \|*  
*tapaścarantau sumahadātmaniṣṭhau mahāvratau \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tejasāpyadhikau sūryātsarvalokavirocanāt \|*  
*śrīvatsalakṣaṇau pūjyau jaṭāmaṇḍaladhāriṇau \|\| 2 \|\|*

*padmacihnabhujau tau ca pādayoścakralakṣaṇau \|*  
*vyūḍhoraskau dīrghabhujau sitasūkṣmaghanāṃśukau \|\| 3 \|\|*

*svāsyau pṛthulalāṭau ca subhruvau śubhanāsikau \|*  
*śubhalakṣaṇasaṃpannau divyamūrttī ghanaprabhau \|\| 4 \|\|*

Skanda said:

1-4. Then he saw the two divine, ancient, excellent sages performing a great penance. They were established in their Ātmans and were great performers of religious observances. By their refulgence they superseded the Sun who illuminates all the world. They were characterised by Śrīvatsa and were worthy of worship. They had circular mass of matted hair. Their arms (palms?) were characterised by lotus. They had discus-sign on (the soles of) their feet. Their chests were broad (and well developed). They had long arms and wore white, fine, compact silken garment. They had excellent faces with high foreheads, excellent eyelashes and beautiful nose. They were endowed with auspicious characteristics, divine form with excessively brilliant lustre.

## \|\| 9.19.5 \|\|

*vinayenāntikaṃ prāpya tayoḥ kṛtvā pradakṣiṇām \|*  
*bhaktyā praṇamya sāṣṭāṅgaṃ tasthau prāñjaliragrataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Approaching them with humility, he circumambulated them. He devoutly prostrated himself before them (touching the ground). He stood before them with palms folded in reverence.

## \|\| 9.19.6-7 \|\|

*tatastau tapasāṃ vāsau yaśasāṃ tejasāmapi \|*  
*ṛṣī paurvāhṇikasyānte vidhermaunaṃ vihāya ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

*prītyā nāradamavyagrau pādyārghyābhyāṃ samārcatām \|*  
*pīṭhayorupaviṣṭau tau kauśayornāradaśca saḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Then, both of the sages, the abodes of penance, glory and lustre, broke their silence at the end of the rituals perfomed in the first part of the day. They worshipped (received) Nārada by offering Pādya and Arghya in a quiet manner. They sat on their seats and Nārada on one of Kuśa grass.

## \|\| 9.19.8 \|\|

*teṣu tatropaviṣṭeṣu sa deśobhivyarājata \|*  
*ājyāhutimahājvālairyajñavāṭognibhiryathā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. When they were seated there, the place shone like an enclosure of sacrifice illuminated by fires having huge flames after receiving oblation of ghee.

## \|\| 9.19.9 \|\|

*atha nārāyaṇastatra nāradaṃ vākyamabravīt \|*  
*sukhopaviṣṭaṃ viśrāntaṃ kṛtātithyaṃ susatkṛtam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then Nārāyaṇa addressed Nārada who had taken rest, was received with hospitality and respect and was seated comfortably there.

## \|\| 9.19.10 \|\|

*śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*api brahmansa bhagavānparamātmā sanātanaḥ \|*  
*brahmadhāmni tvayā dṛṣṭa āvayo kāraṇaṃ param \|\| 10 \|\|*

Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:

10\. O Brāhmaṇa, was eternal Lord, the Supreme Soul, the great cause (source) of both of us seen by you in the Brahmadhāma (residence of Brahman)?

## \|\| 9.19.11 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*bhagavaṃstvatprasādena tamahaṃ parameśvaram \|*  
*vāsudevaṃ samāloke sthitamakṣaradhāmani \|\| 11 \|\|*

Nārada said:

11\. Venerable Sir! It is through your favour that I saw the Supreme Lord Vāsudeva staying in his imperishable residence.

## \|\| 9.19.12 \|\|

*iha caivāgatastena visṛṣṭo vāṃ niṣevitum \|*  
*āsiṣye tatparo bhūtvā yuvābhyāṃ saha nityaśaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Being sent by him to serve you both, I have come here only. I shall always stay with you remaining exclusively devoted to him.

## \|\| 9.19.13 \|\|

*śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*dhanyosyanugṛhītosi yatte dṛṣṭaḥ svayaṃ prabhuḥ \|*  
*nahi taṃ dṛṣṭavānbrahmankaściddevopi vā ṛṣiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:

13\. You are blessed; you are favoured (by God) that the Lord Himself was seen by you. Neither a Deva not a sage has ever seen him, O Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 9.19.14 \|\|

*bhaktyaikāntikayā tasya prāptā akṣarasāmyatām \|*  
*ye hi bhaktāsta evainaṃ paśyantyakhilakāraṇam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Those devotees only who by exclusive devotion unto him have attained imperishable equality with him, (can) see him who is the cause of everything.

## \|\| 9.19.15 \|\|

*sa divyamūrttirbhagavāndurddarśaḥ puruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*nāradaitaddhi me satyaṃ vacanaṃ samudāhṛtam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. That the Supreme Person, the Lord of divine form, is very difficult to be seen, is the purport of a true statement of mine, O Nārada.

## \|\| 9.19.16 \|\|

*nānyo bhaktātpriyataro loke tasyāsti kaścana \|*  
*tataḥ svayaṃ darśitavāṃstavātmānaṃ dvijottama \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. None other than his devotee is more dear to him in this world. Hence he manifested himself to you, O excellent Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 9.19.17 \|\|

*tejaḥpuñjābhiruddhāṃgo guṇātītādbhutākṛtiḥ \|*  
*akhaṇḍānandarūpaśca sadā śuddho'cyutosti saḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. His person is enveloped by a mass of lustre. His mysterious form transcends Guṇas. Complete bliss constitutes his form. He is forever pure and imperishable.

## \|\| 9.19.18 \|\|

*rūpavarṇavayovasthāḥ prākṛtā naiva tasya hi \|*  
*sarvaṃ tasyāsti taddivyaṃ sarvopakaraṇāni ca \|*  
*ekāntikānāṃ bhaktānāṃ sa eva paramā gatiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He does not have a form, complexion, age of the ordinary type (or derived from Prakṛti). Whatever he has is divine including his weapons. He alone is the highest resort of devotees exclusively attached to him.

## \|\| 9.19.19 \|\|

*iti śrīskande mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsu'devamāhātmye nāradanaranārāyaṇasamāgamo nāmaikonaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Devotion to Vāsudeva is performed by persons who have realized the one-ness of Ātman and Brahman and who have desisted from Guṇas. He is endowed with such qualities.

## \|\| 9.19.20 \|\|

*māhātmyamasya ko vaktuṃ śaknuyātparamātmanaḥ \|*  
*acintyānantaśaktīnāmadhipasya mahāmune \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Who is capable of describing the greatness of this Supreme Soul, who is the master of incomprehensible, infinite powers, O great sage?

## \|\| 9.19.21-22 \|\|

*ātmātmā cākṣarātmā ca hyeṣa ākāśanirmalaḥ \|*  
*divyadṛgīkṣyaḥ sanmātraḥ puruṣo vasudevajaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*samastakalyāṇaguṇo nirguṇaśceśvareśvaraḥ \|*  
*parayā vidyayā vedya upāsyo brahmavitprabhuḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. He is the Soul of souls, imperishable Soul, unsoiled and pure like the firmament, visible only to persons endowed with divine vision, who is pure existence, the Puruṣa born of Vasudeva. He is endowed with all auspicious qualities, attributeless, the master of all rulers. He, the knower of Brahman, the master is knowable through superior knowledge. He should be propitiated.

## \|\| 9.19.23 \|\|

*divyamūrttiṃ tamīśānaṃ tapasaikāntikena ca \|*  
*yaḥ prīṇayati dharmeṇa sa dhanyatama ucyate \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. He who pleases that Lord of divine form with penance solely devoted to him, and pious devotion, is the most blessed.

## \|\| 9.19.24 \|\|

*tasmāttvamapi devarṣe dharmeṇaikāntikena tam \|*  
*ārādhayannihaivāṃga kaṃcitkālaṃ tapaḥ kuru \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Therefore, O divine sage, you also propitiate him with exclusive pious devotion, and perform penance here for some time, O dear one.

## \|\| 9.19.25 \|\|

*tapasaivā'tiśuddhātmā māhātmyaṃ tasya satpateḥ \|*  
*yathāvajjñāsyati bhavānprocyamānaṃ mayā'khilam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. With your soul extremely purified with penance, you will (be in a position to) know truly all the glory of the Lord, the great soul, as will be described by me.

## \|\| 9.19.26 \|\|

*sarvārthasādhanaṃ viddhi tapastaddhṛdayaṃ mune \|*  
*nātaptabhūritapasā sa vaśīkriyate prabhuḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Know that penance is the means of attaining all objectives (and) his heart, O sage. The Lord is not won over by a person who has not performed extreme penance.

## Chapter 20 - The Duties of the Four Varṇas

## \|\| 9.20.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*bhagavanbrūhi me dharmamekāntaṃ tava saṃmatam \|*  
*prīyate yena viśvātmā vāsudevaḥ sa sarvadā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Nārada said:

1\. O Lord! Expound to me the Ekānta Dharma as approved by you, whereby the Universal Soul, Vāsudeva, gets always pleased.

Śrī Nārāyaṇa replied:

## \|\| 9.20.2 \|\|

*śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*sādhu pṛṣṭaṃ tvayā brahmanmatiste vimalā kila \|*  
*mayi snigdhāya bhaktāya tubhyaṃ guhyamapi bruve \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O Brāhmaṇa, you have asked very well. Certainly your intellect is pure. I shall tell even a secret to you, a devotee who are attached to me.

## \|\| 9.20.3 \|\|

*dharma eṣa mayā proktaḥ kalpasyādau vivasvate \|*  
*tameva kathaye tubhyaṃ sanātanamahaṃ mune \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. At the beginning of the Kalpa this Dharma was proclaimed by me to Vivasvān. I shall communicate that very ancient Dharma to you, O sage.

## \|\| 9.20.4 \|\|

*svadharmajñānavairāgyaiḥ saha lakṣmīvadīśvare \|*  
*tasminnananyā bhaktiryā dharma ekāntikaḥ sa vai \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. That is verily the Ekāntika Dharma which is undivided devotion exclusively to the Lord as it is to Lakṣmī and is accompanied by the knowledge of one’s own Dharma and disaffection to objects of worldly enjoyment.

## \|\| 9.20.5 \|\|

*tenaivātiprasannaḥ syādgolokādhipatiḥ svayam \|*  
*jāyate sa ca bhaktopi paripūrṇamanorathaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Thereby the ruler of Goloka himself becomes extremely pleased, and even the devotee has all his wishes fully accomplished.

Nārada asked:

## \|\| 9.20.6 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*lakṣaṇāni bubhutsāmi svadharmādeḥ pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*śāstrayonerahaṃ tvatto vaktuṃ tāni tvamarhasi \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. I have a desire to know separately the characteristics of Svadharma (personal duties) from you who are the source of Śāstras. It behoves you to relate them to me.

## \|\| 9.20.7 \|\|

*nigamāgamaśāstrāṇāṃ sarveṣāmapi satpate \|*  
*mūlaṃ tvameka evāsi yeṣu dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. You alone are the root (source of origin) of all Vedas, Āgamas and Śāstras including the eternal Dharma, O good Lord.

## \|\| 9.20.8 \|\|

*tvameva sākṣādbhagavānvāsudevo'kṣarātparaḥ \|*  
*śreyase sarvabhūtānāṃ vartase'tra dayānidhiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. You alone are the Lord Vāsudeva incarnate, who is beyond the perishable (objects). You, a store of mercy, stay here for the welfare of all beings.

## \|\| 9.20.9 \|\|

*tvatto'nye tu svasvabhāvaguṇatantrā hyajādayaḥ \|*  
*yathāvanna vijānīyurddharmādīṃstvamato vada \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. God Brahmā and others who are other than you, are controlled by their respective natural Guṇas. They do not know Dharma and oṃer (related things) as they truly are. Hence narrate it (to me).

## \|\| 9.20.10 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*iti devarṣiṇā pṛṣṭo bhagavāndharmanandanaḥ \|*  
*svadharmādīnkrameṇaiva kathayāmāsa sarvavit \|\| 10 \|\|*

Skanda said:

10\. Lord Nārāyaṇa, the omniscient son of Dharma, who was thus asked by the Divine sages (Narada), narrated to him in due order, the personal Dharma etc.

## \|\| 9.20.11 \|\|

*śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*varṇānāmāśramāṇāṃ ca sadācāraḥ pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*sāmānyaḥ saviśeṣaśca svadharmaḥ sa udīryate \|\| 11 \|\|*

Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:

11\. The moral conduct is different for (different) Varṇas (castes) and stages of life. That is called Svadharma and is general as well as special.

## \|\| 9.20.12 \|\|

*nṛṇāṃ sādhāraṇaṃ dharmaṃ sarveṣāmāditaḥ śṛṇu \|*  
*ahiṃsā paramo dharmastatrādima udāhṛtaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. At first listen to the Dharma (duty) common to all men. Noninjury (Ahiṃsā) is proclaimed to be the first supreme duty.

## \|\| 9.20.13 \|\|

*svamukhyadharmavṛtyorapyadroho manasāpi yaḥ \|*  
*sati gatyantare prāṇimātrasyāpīti sā matā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. (Obscure) Among one’s main moral inclinations what is called absence of ill will even of the mental type, in a provocative situation, towards any living being, is known as Ahiṃsā or non-injury.

## \|\| 9.20.14 \|\|

*satyā vāgbhūtamātrasya droho na syādyayā tathā \|*  
*tapaśca śāstravihitabhogasaṃkocalakṣaṇam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Truth is that speech whereby no injury is caused to living beings. Penance is characterised by the diminution (reduction in) of the enjoyment (of objects) permitted by the scriptures.

## \|\| 9.20.15 \|\|

*bāhyamābhyantaraṃ ceti dvividhaṃ śaucakarma ca \|*  
*anādānaṃ parasvasya parokṣaṃ vā chalena ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Purification is of two types, external and internal. Non-taking of what belongs to others either in his absence or by deceit (is nonstealth).

## \|\| 9.20.16-21 \|\|

*yathocitaṃ brahmacaryakāmalobhakrudhāṃ jayaḥ \|*  
*mudā vittārpaṇaṃ pātre tuṣṭirlabdhena daivataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tīrthe kṣetre ca yajñādau caturvargāptayepi vā \|*  
*ātmano vā parasyāpi sarvathā ghātavarjanam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*jātibhraṃśakarāṇāṃ ca karmaṇāṃ parivarjanam \|*  
*pāṇipādodaropasthavācāṃ saṃyamanaṃ tathā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*sarveṣāṃ vyasanānāṃ ca varjanaṃ madyamāṃsayoḥ \|*  
*vyabhicārānnivṛttiśca kulasaddharmapālanam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye cāturvarṇyadharmanirūpaṇaṃ nāma viṃśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*ārjavaṃ sādhusevā ca vibhajyā'nnādibhojanam \|*  
*bhaktirbhagavataśceti dharmāḥ sādhāraṇā nṛṇām \|\| 21 \|\|*

16-21. Proper celibacy; restraint of the passions or desires, greed and anger; gladly donating wealth to a suitable person; satisfaction with what one gets through luck; total renunciation of injury at holy places or in sacrifices and other religious acts or for obtaining the four ends of human life either for one’s self or for others; avoidance of acts which cause fall from one’s caste; restraint of (movement of) hands and fed, stomach (i.e. eating), the organ of generation (sex) and speech; avoidance of wine and meat and all vices; abstaining from adultery; observance of the traditional good practices of one’s family; observance of fast along with the (prescribed ten restraints) on the eleventh day of the dark and bright half of the month; proper observance of the specific Vrata of the birthday of Hari; straightforwardness; service of saints; taking food after its distribution (as per prescribed rules); acts of devotion unto the Lord—These are duties common to all men.

## \|\| 9.20.22 \|\|

*brahmakṣatraviśaḥ śūdrā varṇāścatvāra īritāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ pṛthakpṛthagdharmānviśeṣānvacmi te mune \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Brāhamaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas and Śūdras—These are spoken as the four Varṇas (Castes). I shall now narrate the specific duties of each to you, O sage.

## \|\| 9.20.23 \|\|

*śamo damaḥ kṣamā śaucamāstikyaṃ bhaktirīśituḥ \|*  
*tapo jñānaṃ ca vijñānaṃ vipradharmaḥ svabhāvajaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The natural duties of a Brāhmaṇa are quiescence, self-control, forgiveness, purity, faith in Vedas, devotion to the Lord, penance, knowledge of Brahman and worldly knowledge.

## \|\| 9.20.24 \|\|

*śūratvaṃ dhairyamaudārya balaṃ tejaḥ śaraṇyatā \|*  
*goviprasādhurakṣejyā dharmāḥ kṣatrasya kīrttitāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The following are declared as the duties of Kṣatriyas: Bravery (i.e. performance of acts of bravery); courage; generosity; strength; dignity; fitness to be a refuge; protection of cows, Brāhmaṇas and saints; performance of sacrifices.

## \|\| 9.20.25 \|\|

*rājñastvete'tha nītyaiva prajānāṃ paripālanam \|*  
*dharmasaṃsthāpanaṃ bhūmau dharmā daṇḍārhadaṇḍanam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The duties of a king are as follows: Protecting the subjects; establishing Dharma on the earth; and administering punishment to those who deserve it.

## \|\| 9.20.26 \|\|

*āstikyaṃ dānaniṣṭhā ca sādhubrāhmaṇasevanam \|*  
*atuṣṭirarthopacaye dharmā vaiśyasya codyamaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The duties of a Vaiśya are: faith in the Vedas; doing acts of charity; rendering service to saintly persons and Brāhmaṇas; non-satisfaction in acquisition of wealth; and assiduous efforts.

## \|\| 9.20.27 \|\|

*dvijātīnāṃ ca devānāṃ sevā niṣkapaṭaṃ gavām \|*  
*viśeṣadharmaḥ kathitaḥ śūdrasya munisattama \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O excellent sages, the specific duty of a Śūdra as proclaimed is: faithful (without any fraud or deceit) service of twice-born castes, Devas and cows.

## \|\| 9.20.28 \|\|

*adhyāpanaṃ yājanaṃ ca viśuddhācca pratigrahaḥ \|*  
*viprasya jīvikā proktā tatrāntyā tvāpadi smṛtā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The means of livelihood prescribed for a Brāhmaṇa are: teaching, performance of sacrifices, acceptance of a gift from a pure person. Out of these, the last is laid down in case of adversity.

## \|\| 9.20.29-30 \|\|

*yājane'dhyāpane vāpi doṣadarśī dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*yastasyā'nyāpi vihitā vṛttirasti caturvidhā \|\| 29 \|\|*

*śiloñcha nityayācñā ca śālīnaṃ cocitā kṛṣiḥ \|*  
*śreyasī pūrvapūrvā'tra jñātavyā dvijasattamaiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. Four types of other means of livelihood are prescribed for an excellent Brāhmaṇa who finds fault with performance of sacrifice and teaching (as means of livehood). (They are) gleaning ears of com, constant mendicancy, settled householdership and proper agriculture. It should be noted by excellent Brāhmaṇas that herein the preceding one (i.e. mode of livelihood) is more conducive to welfare than the succeeding one.

## \|\| 9.20.31 \|\|

*vipro jīvedvaiśyavṛttyā satyāmāpadi nārada \|*  
*atha vā kṣatravṛttyāpi śvavṛttyā na tu karhicit \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. In case of an emergency a Brāmaṇa should maintain himself by adopting the mode of livelihood of a Vaiśya or that of a Kṣatriya but never the mode of a dog (Cāṇḍāla?).

## \|\| 9.20.32 \|\|

*śastreṇa jīvetkṣatraṃ tu sarvato dharmarakṣayā \|*  
*āpanno vaiśyavṛttyaiva viprarūpeṇa vā caret \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. A Kṣatriya should earn his living by weapons (military profession) while protecting Dharma. In emergency he should follow the means of livelihood of a Vaiśya or should move about in the guise of a Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 9.20.33 \|\|

*karādānādinṛpateraviprādvṛttirīritā \|*  
*deśakālānusāreṇa rañjayitvā'khilāḥ prajāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The means of living for a king is declared to be collection of taxes, except from Brāhmaṇas, and from other sources, after keeping contented all the subjects according to the exigencies of time and place.

## \|\| 9.20.34 \|\|

*āpatkālepi kṣatrasya brāhmaṇasyeva sarvathā \|*  
*vigarhitā nīcasevā svatejaḥkṣayakāriṇī \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Even in emergency, the service of a low person is totally prohibited to Kṣatriyas and Brāhmaṇas, as that reduces one’s lustre.

## \|\| 9.20.35 \|\|

*kṛṣivāṇijyagorakṣā turīyā vṛddhijīvanam \|*  
*vaiśyasya jīvikā proktā śūdravṛttistathāpadi \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. In the case of a Vaiśya the mode of livelihood is spoken (as consisting of) agriculture, trade and commerce and tending of cows and lending money on interest as the fourth, but in emergency he may follow the Śūdra mode of livelihood.

## \|\| 9.20.36 \|\|

*śūdro jīveddvijātīnāṃ sevālabdhadhanena ca \|*  
*āpatkāle tu kārvāderjīvikāvṛttimāśrayet \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. A Śudra should maintain himself on the money earned by service rendered to twice-born castes. In emergency he should follow the mode of livelihood of artisans etc.

## \|\| 9.20.37 \|\|

*āpanmuktastu sarvopi prāyaścittaṃ yathocitam \|*  
*vidhāya svasvavṛttyaiva punarvartteta mukhyayā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. When all of them become free after averting the emergency, they should perform the expiation proper for them and again take up their respective main vocations as means of livelihood.

## \|\| 9.20.38 \|\|

*cāturvarṇyaṃ satāṃ saṃgaṃ kuryānna tvasatāṃ kvacit \|*  
*muktipradosti satsaṃgaḥ kusaṃgo nirayapradaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. (Persons belonging to) the four castes should associate themselves with saintly people and never with bad people. Association with the good leads to liberation, while company with evil persons leads to hell.

## \|\| 9.20.39 \|\|

*kāmaṃ krodhaṃ rasāsvādaṃ jitvā mānaṃ ca matsaram \|*  
*nirdambhaṃ viṣṇubhaktā ye te santaḥ sādhavo matāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Those who, having subdued erotic passion, anger, taste for flavours, pride, jealousy, hypocrisy, are the devotees of Viṣṇu, are regarded as saintly persons.

## \|\| 9.20.40 \|\|

*striyāṃ straiṇe rasāsvāde saktāśca dhanagṛdhnavaḥ \|*  
*hiṃsrā dambhakṛtāṭopā bhaktābhāsā hyasādhavaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Those who are addicted to sexual pleasure in the company of women, greedy after wealth, murderous, self-conceited through hyprocrisy and who pose to be devotees, are bad people.

## \|\| 9.20.41 \|\|

*asādhuṣvāsurī saṃpaddaivī saṃpattu sādhuṣu \|*  
*sahajāstīti niścitya sevyā santaḥ sukhepsubhiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Having ascertained that by nature Asura type of prosperity is (found) among bad people and the Deva type of affluence is (seen) among the good, good and saintly persons should be resorted to and served by those desirous of happiness.

## \|\| 9.20.42 \|\|

*yādṛśāṃ yasya saṃgaḥ syācchāstrāṇāṃ vā nṛṇāmapi \|*  
*buddhiḥ syāttādṛśī tasya kāryo'to nāsatāṃ hi saḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The intellect (of a person) assumes a shape in accordance with the kind of Śāstras (scriptures) and people he associates with. Hence no association should be had with bad people (and heretic scriptures).

## \|\| 9.20.43 \|\|

*ye sādhusevārucayaḥ puruṣā nijaśaktitaḥ \|*  
*aprāpyaṃ nāsti teṣāṃ vai kimapyaiśvaryamūrjitam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. To persons who like to render service to saintly persons, any type of superior affluence or excellent power or divine faculties are not unobtainable through dint of their power.

## \|\| 9.20.44 \|\|

*svadharmasthā api satāṃ drohiṇo ye tu mānavāḥ \|*  
*sadgatiṃ naiva te yānti kvāpi kenāpi karmaṇā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Men who, though established in their Dharma, bear malice to saintly persons, shall never attain a happy state or beatitude anywhere by performing any act.

## \|\| 9.20.45 \|\|

*mahāpūjāratā viṣṇorbhaktā api satāṃ yadi \|*  
*drohaṃ kuryustadā teṣu na prasīdati sa kvacit \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. If devotees of Viṣṇu who are devoted to the great worship (of the god) bear hatred towards saintly persons, he (Viṣṇu) will never be propitious unto them.

## \|\| 9.20.46 \|\|

*saddrohiṇastu dehānte yāṃyāṃ yoniṃ brajanti ca \|*  
*tatratatra kṣudhārogaiḥ pīḍyante jīvitāvadhi \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. In whatever species the haters of saintly people are born after death, they will be harassed with hunger and disease throughout their life (up to death).

## \|\| 9.20.47 \|\|

*satāmatikramādeva puṇyānāṃ mahatāmapi \|*  
*sadyaḥ kṣayaḥ syātsarveṣāmāyuṣaḥ saṃpadāmapi \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Merely by doing disrespect to good (saintly) people, there is an instantaneous annihilation even of a mass of merit, (span of) life and wealth of all people.

## \|\| 9.20.48 \|\|

*tasmātsevā satāṃ kāryā sarvairapi sukhepsubhiḥ \|*  
*puṇyatīrthāni sevyāni pūjyā viprāśca dhenavaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Therefore, service should be rendered to saintly persons by all those who desire happiness. Sacred places should be resorted to Brāhmaṇas and cows should be worshipped.

## \|\| 9.20.49 \|\|

*tīrthāni devapratimā nindeyurye kubuddhayaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ tu jārajātānāṃ vaṃśocchedo bhaveddhruvam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Those evil-minded people who denigrate holy places and idols of gods, are bastards and will certainly have exinction of their family line.

## \|\| 9.20.50 \|\|

*ekasmiṃstarpite vipre sadbhojyairdakṣiṇādibhiḥ \|*  
*tarpitaṃ syājjagatsarvaṃ haristuṣyati ca svayam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. If one Brāhmaṇa is satisfied by receiving excellent meal, Dakṣiṇā and other things, the whole world is satisfied. Hari himself is pleased with him.

## \|\| 9.20.51 \|\|

*ekasminbrāhmaṇe drugdhe drugdhaṃ syātsakalaṃ jagat \|*  
*tasmācchaktyā pūjanīyā brāhmaṇā viṣṇurūpiṇaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. If one Brāhmaṇa is harmed (it is as good as) the whole world is hurt. Therefore, Brāhmaṇas who are (this-worldly) forms of Viṣṇu shall be worshipped and honoured according to one’s capacity.

## \|\| 9.20.52 \|\|

*gavāmaṃgeṣu tiṣṭhanti sarve devagaṇā api \|*  
*tathā sarvāṇi tīrthāni tāsu tiṣṭhanti sarvadā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Even all multitudes of Devas abide in the limbs (body) of cows. All holy places exist in them.

## \|\| 9.20.53 \|\|

*gavyarccitāyāmekasyāṃ sarve devāḥ samarccitāḥ \|*  
*kṛtāni syuśca sarvāṇi tīrthānyapi ca nārada \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. When one cow is worshipped, all Devas get worshipped and all sacred places get visited, O Nārada.

## \|\| 9.20.54 \|\|

*ekasyā api gordrohe kṛte kvāpi pramādataḥ \|*  
*drugdhāḥ syurdevatāḥ sarvāstīrthānyapi ca kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. If out of mistake or negligence, hurt or injury is caused to one cow anywhere, all the deities are hurt and holy places are damaged.

## \|\| 9.20.55 \|\|

*tasmāccāturvarṇya janairyathoktavidhisaṃsthitaiḥ \|*  
*bhavitavyaṃ prayatnena tretavyaṃ ca niṣedhataḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Therefore, people born in the four Varṇas should behave as per injunctions and should abstain from what is prohibited.

## \|\| 9.20.56 \|\|

*cāturvarṇyetare ye tu teṣāṃ vṛttiḥ kulocitā \|*  
*cauryahiṃsādyadharmeṇa rahitaiva hitāvahā \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Those who are beyond the pale of four Varṇas, their conduct conforming to their family requirements will be conducive to their welfare if it is devoid of unrighteousness like stealing, violence etc.

## Chapter 21 - Duties of the Celibate student (Brahmacārī)

## \|\| 9.21.1 \|\|

*śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*brahmacārī gṛhasthaśca vānaprastho yatistathā \|*  
*eta āśramiṇaḥ proktāścatvāro munisattama \|\| 1 \|\|*

Śrī Nārayaṇa said:

1\. Brahmacārī (celibate student), Gṛhastha (householder), Vānaprastha (forest-hermit) and Yati (ascetic)—these four belong to the four periods of religious life.

## \|\| 9.21.2 \|\|

*saṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛto yastu śuddhayonirdvijātitām \|*  
*prāptaḥ sa hi brahmacārī taddharmānādito bruve \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. He who is born of a pure family, is consecrated by sacred rites, and ṃus has attained the status of a twice-born is called a Brahmacārī (a celibate student). I shall narrate his duties from the beginning.

## \|\| 9.21.3 \|\|

*varṇī vedamadhīyīta vasangurugṛhe śuciḥ \|*  
*jitendriyo jitakrodho vinītastathyabhāṣaṇaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Residing in the house of a preceptor, a religious student should study the Vedas. He should be pure, have subdued his senses, have control over his anger, be disciplined and be a speaker of truth.

## \|\| 9.21.4 \|\|

*sāyaṃ prātaścareddhomaṃ bhikṣācaryāṃ ca saṃyataḥ \|*  
*kuryāttrikālaṃ saṃdhyāṃ ca viṣṇupūjāṃ tathānvaham \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He should perform fire-worship in the morning and in the evening. Remaining self-controlled, he should go out to beg alms. He should perform the Sandhyā prayer thrice a day and worship God Viṣṇu everyday.

## \|\| 9.21.5 \|\|

*gurvājñayaiva bhuñjīta mitamannamanākulaḥ \|*  
*gurusevāparo nityaṃ bhavedvyasanavarjitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Remaining calm and collected, he should partake of a limited quantity of food with the permission of the preceptor. He should always be solely devoted to the service of the preceptor and be free from evil habits.

## \|\| 9.21.6 \|\|

*snāne ca bhojane home jape maunamupāśrayet \|*  
*chindyānna nakharomāṇi dantānnaivātidhāvayet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He should observe silence at the time of bath, taking meals, performing fire-worship and muttering prayers. He should not pare the nails or cut his hair and should not over-cleanse his teeth.

## \|\| 9.21.7 \|\|

*nātidhāvecca vāsāṃsi bhavenniṣkapaṭo gurau \|*  
*āhūtodhyayanaṃ kuryādādāvante ca taṃ namet \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He should not over-cleanse his garments and should be sincere to his preceptor. When called, he should study (learn) and should bow down at the beginning of and after the completion of the lesson.

## \|\| 9.21.8 \|\|

*aspṛśyānna spṛśeccāsau nā'saṃbhāṣyāṃśca bhāṣayet \|*  
*abhakṣyaṃ bhakṣayennaiva nā'peyaṃ ca pibetkvacit \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He should not touch the untouchable, nor speak with persons undeserved for verbal exchange. He should not eat prohibited articles of food, and never drink forbidden drinks.

## \|\| 9.21.9 \|\|

*mekhalāmajinaṃ daṇḍaṃ bibhṛyācca kamaṇḍalum \|*  
*site dve vāsasī brahmasūtraṃ ca japamālikām \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He should wear and possess a waistband, a deer-skin, a staff, a Kamaṇḍalu (pot of gourd as a water-bottle), two white cloths, the sacred thread and a rosary of beads (for muttering mantras).

## \|\| 9.21.10 \|\|

*darbhapāṇiśca jaṭilaḥ keśasaṃskāravarjitaḥ \|*  
*aṅgarāgaṃ puṣpahārānbhūṣaṇāni ca varjayet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He should have Darbha grass in his hands and should have matted hair without combing and other embellishments. He should abstain from application of perfumed unguents to the body, garland of flowers and ornaments.

## \|\| 9.21.11 \|\|

*tailābhyaṅgaṃ na kurvīta kajjale nāñjanaṃ tathā \|*  
*varjayecca prayatnena saṃsargaṃ madyamāṃsayoḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He should not smear his body with oil, and should not use a cosmetic ointment like collyrium. He should assiduously avoid contact with, (abstain) from, liquor and meat.

## \|\| 9.21.12 \|\|

*strīṇāṃ nirīkṣaṇaṃ sparśaṃ bhāṣaṇaṃ krīḍanādi ca \|*  
*varjayetsarvathā varṇī striyāścāpyavalekhanam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. A celibate should totally abstain from eying, touching, speaking, playing with women and combing (the hair) of a woman.

## \|\| 9.21.13 \|\|

*vinā ca devapratimāṃ kāṣṭhacitrādiyoṣitam \|*  
*api naiva spṛśeddhīmānna ca buddhyāvalokayet \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. With the exception of idols of gods, an intelligent student should never touch even a woman-figure of wood or a woman’s picture etc. Nor should he look at them intently.

## \|\| 9.21.14 \|\|

*prāṇimātraṃ ca mithunībhūtaṃ nekṣeta karhicit \|*  
*strīṇāṃ guṇāścāpyaguṇāñchṛṇuyānnaiva no vadet \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He should never see the sexual intercourse of animals. He should not listen to, nor should speak of, the good or bad qualities of women.

## \|\| 9.21.15 \|\|

*aspṛśanneva vandeta gurupatnīmapi svakām \|*  
*jananyāpi na tiṣṭheta rahaḥsthāne tu karhicit \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Without touching (the person of) one’s own preceptor’s wife, he should pay obeisance. Even with one’s mother, he should not sit in a secret or solitary place.

## \|\| 9.21.16 \|\|

*evaṃvṛtto vasettatra yāvadvidyāsamāpanam \|*  
*tato virakto nyāsī syādvarṇī vā naiṣṭhiko bhavet \|*  
*anadhikāritā proktā naiṣṭhikavratināṃ kalau \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Behaving thus, he should stay there (in preceptor’s house) till the completion of education. Then, if free from worldly attachment, the celibate student should be either a recluse (Sannyāsin) or Naiṣṭhika

i.e. a perpetual religious student who continues with his preceptor, vowing life-long abstinence and chastity. But it is proclaimed that in the Kali Age, eligibility for adopting the vow of a Naiṣṭhika is prohibited.

## \|\| 9.21.17 \|\|

*na saṃdhāviti vijñeyaṃ kalīti śabdasaṃgrahāt \|*  
*vanī syādatha vā brahmannavirakto bhavedgṛhī \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. By the term Kali one should understand ‘not in the junction of Kali-age’. He should be either a forest-hermit or, if he is not averse to worldly life, he should be a householder.

## Chapter 22 - Duties of Householders (Gṛhin or Gṛhastha)

## \|\| 9.22.1 \|\|

*śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*gṛhī bubhūṣurgurave dakṣiṇāṃ svasya śaktitaḥ \|*  
*dattvā tadājñayaivā'sau samāvarttanamācaret \|\| 1 \|\|*

Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:

1\. One who desires to become a householder (gṛhin) should (first) pay his tuition-fees according to his capacity. After paying the fees, and with his (preceptor’s) permission, he should perform the Samāvartana ceremony (for pupil’s homecoming after finishing the course of holy study).

## \|\| 9.22.2 \|\|

*tataḥ kulocitāṃ yoṣāṃ vayasonāmarogiṇīm \|*  
*puṃllakṣaṇena rahitāmapāpāṃ vidhinodvahet \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. He should then marry with due formalities, a girl suitable to his family, junior to him in age, healthy, devoid of masculine characteristics (e.g. hair on the upper lip) and sinless.

## \|\| 9.22.3 \|\|

*svādhikārānusāreṇa kṛṣṇasaṃprītaye'nvaham \|*  
*devarṣipitṛbhūtāni yajeta vidhinā tataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Then for the favour and delight of Lord Kṛṣṇa, he should, according to his eligibility and authority, perform daily worship (by performing the Tarpaṇa of Devas, Sages, Manes and living beings) as per injunctions.

## \|\| 9.22.4 \|\|

*snānaṃ saṃdhyāṃ japaṃ homaṃ svādhyāyaṃ viṣṇupūjanam \|*  
*tarpaṇaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ ca kuryāccātithyamanvaham \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Everyday he should perform (holy) baṃ, twilight prayers, muttering of Mantras, Fire-worship (Homa), recitation of Vedas, worship of Viṣṇu, Tarpaṇa (offering of libations of water to deceased parents etc.), Vaiśvadeva (offering to all deities by offering oblations to fire before meals), reception of guests.

## \|\| 9.22.5 \|\|

*kuryātpuṇyaṃ yathāśakti nyāyārjitadhanena ca \|*  
*anāsaktaḥ poṣyavargaṃ puṣṇīyānna tu pīḍayet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. With wealth earned by righteous means one should perform meritorious acts, according to one’s capacity. He should be unattached. He should feed his dependents, and should not harass them.

## \|\| 9.22.6 \|\|

*dehaṃ ca daihikānvāsāvuddiśya paśuvatparaiḥ \|*  
*vairaṃ na kuryāddehādāvahantāṃ mamatāṃ tyajet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. With reference to a body or bodily limbs, one should not entertain enmity like a brute against others (i.e. one should not inflict injury on the body or limbs of others). One should give up the sense of ‘I’ and ‘mine’ with reference to one’s body etc.

## \|\| 9.22.7 \|\|

*kuryādbhāgavatānāṃ ca satāṃ saṃgamatandritaḥ \|*  
*na straiṇānāṃ vyasanināṃ saṃgaṃ kuryānna lobhinām \|\| 7 \|\|*
