7\. He should carefully form association with devotees of the Lord and saintly persons. He should not keep company of lewd, vicious people and greedy persons.

## \|\| 9.22.8 \|\|

*kāmabhāvena nekṣeta parayoṣāṃ tu karhicit \|*  
*śrāddhaparvavratāhādau nopeyācca svayoṣitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He should never look at the wives of others with sexual desire. He should not approach his wife (carnally) during Śrāddha, Parvan days and observance of religious vows.

## \|\| 9.22.9 \|\|

*prāptopi puruṣaḥ sāṃkhye yoge ca paripakvatām \|*  
*putryā api prasaṃgena rahaḥsthāne tu muhyati \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Even though a man has attained maturity in Sāṅkhya (philosophy) and Yogic (practice), he gets infatuated even with his daughter in a lonely place.

## \|\| 9.22.10 \|\|

*ato mātrā bhaginyā vā duhitrāpi rahaḥsthale \|*  
*saha nāsīta matimānyuvatyā kimutā'nyayā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Hence an intelligent person should not sit with his mother, sister or daughter in privacy. No need to say about sitting in such places with other young women (unrelated to him).

## \|\| 9.22.11 \|\|

*amaṅgalānāṃ sarveṣāṃ vidhavā hyatyamaṃgalam \|*  
*taddarśanaṃ ca tatsparśo nṝṇāṃ sukṛtahṛttataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Of all inauspicious things, a widow is the most inauspicious one. Her sight or touch destroys the merits of men.

## \|\| 9.22.12 \|\|

*prayāṇakāle vidhavādarśanaṃ sanmukhe yadi \|*  
*syāttadā naiva gantavyamanyathā maraṇaṃ dhuvam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. If at the time of starting on a journey one sees a widow in front, one should not go at that time. Otherwise death is certain.

## \|\| 9.22.13 \|\|

*āśiṣo vidhavāstrīṇāṃ samāḥ kālāhiphūtkṛtaiḥ \|*  
*tataśca bibhiyāttābhyo rākṣasībhyo yathā gṛhī \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The blessings of widowed women are similar to the hissing of black serpents. A householder should be afraid of them as of ogresses.

## \|\| 9.22.14 \|\|

*madyaṃ māṃsaṃ mādakaṃ ca dyūtādīndūratastyajet \|*  
*na drohaṃ prāṇimātrasya kuryādvācāpi karhicit \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. One should avoid from a distance liquor, meat, intoxicants (narcotics), gambling etc. One should not entertain malice against living beings, even by speech anywhere.

## \|\| 9.22.15 \|\|

*avatāracaritrāṇi śṛṇuyādanvahaṃ hareḥ \|*  
*sarvā api kriyāḥ kuryādvāsudevārthamāstikaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Everyday one should listen to the stories and exploits of the incarnations of Hari. A believer should perform all acts for the sake of Vāsudeva.

## \|\| 9.22.16 \|\|

*ūrje māghe ca vaiśākhe cāturmāsye malimluce \|*  
*anyeṣu puṇyakāleṣu viśeṣaniyamāṃścaret \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. One should undertake some self-imposed religious observances in the month of Kārttika, Māgha, Vaiśākha, the period of four months from Āṣāḍha to Kārttika and intercalated thirteenth month (called ‘adhika’, extra, additional month).

## \|\| 9.22.17 \|\|

*puṇyadeśe puṇyakāle satpātre vidhinā gṛhī \|*  
*dadyāddānaṃ yathāśakti dayāṃ kurvīta jantuṣu \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. A householder should make religious gifts according to his capacity, to a virtuous recipient in a sacred place, at an auspicious time, as per injunctions. He should be merciful to all beings.

## \|\| 9.22.18 \|\|

*puṇyāndeśānpuṇyakālānpuṇyapātrāṇi cānagha \|*  
*kathayāmi viśeṣeṇa dharmavṛddhikarāṇi te \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O sinless one, I shall now mention to you sacred lands and places, auspicious times, meritorious worthy recipients which specially enhance the merit (of the act).

## \|\| 9.22.19 \|\|

*deśaḥ sarvottamastveṣa bhuvi yo madadhiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*mahāmunigaṇā yatra tapasyanti mahāvratāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. On this earth that land which is presided over by me is the best of all—ṃe land where multitudes of great sages, great observers of religious vows, perform penance.

## \|\| 9.22.20-25 \|\|

*haritadbhaktamāhātmyāddeśānāmasti puṇyatā \|*  
*gaṃgādvāraṃ madhupurī naimiṣāraṇyameva ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

*kurukṣetramayodhyā ca prayāgaśca gayāśiraḥ \|*  
*purī vārāṇasī caiva puṇyaśca pulahāśramaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye gṛhasthadharmanirūpaṇaṃ nāma dvāviṃśodhyāyaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*krīḍāsthānaṃ bhagavataḥ saśriyo raivatācalaḥ \|*  
*tathā govarddhanagiriḥ puṇyaṃ vṛndāvanaṃ vanam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*mahendramalayādyāśca saptāpi kulaparvatāḥ \|*  
*bhāgīrathī mahāpuṇyā yamunā ca sarasvatī \|\| 24 \|\|*

*godāvarī ca sarayūḥ kāverī gomatīmukhāḥ \|*  
*purāṇaprathitāḥ puṇyā mahānadyo nadāstathā \|\| 25 \|\|*

20-25. The sanctity of places is due to the greatness of Lord Hari and his devotees. They are as follows: Gaṅgādvāra, Mathurā, Naimiṣāraṇya, Kurukṣetra, Ayodhyā, Prayāga, Gayāśiras, (Jagannātha) purī, Varāṇasī, the sacred hermitage of Pulaha (Śālagrāma), the hermitage of Kapila (Siddhapur in Gujarat), Śrīraṅga, Prabhāsa, Kuśasthalī (Dvārakā), the holy Siddhapada, and the great lake Puṣkara, the Raivata mountain (Mount Girnār), the place of sports of the Lord along with Śrī, so also the Govardhana mountain and the sacred forest Vṛndāvana, seven Kulaparvatas (principal mountain ranges) including Mahendra, Malaya and others, sacred great rivers famous in Purāṇas like Bhāgīrathī, highly holy river Yamunā and Sarasvatī, Godāvan, Sarayū, Kāverī, Gomatī and others and Nadas (great rivers like the Indus).

## \|\| 9.22.26 \|\|

*mahotsavairbhavedyatra bhagavatpratimārcanam \|*  
*prabhorananyabhaktāśca bhaveyuryatrayatra ca \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Wherever the worship of the idol of the Lord is performed with great celebrations, and wherever devotees exclusively attached to the Lord live (that place is sacred).

## \|\| 9.22.27 \|\|

*ahiṃsrāśca svadharmasthā yatra syurbrāhmaṇottamāḥ \|*  
*mṛgādyāḥ paśavo yatra vicareyuśca nirbhayāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Where excellent Brāhmaṇas commit no violence (in sacrifices and Śrāddha) and are established in their (routine of) duties, where animals including deer move about without any fear (they are the holy places).

## \|\| 9.22.28 \|\|

*yatrayatrāvatārāśca harervāsaśca yatra vā \|*  
*ete puṇyatamā deśā bhuvi santi viśeṣataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Wherever incarnations and stay of Hari have taken place, they are specially the most sacred places on the earth.

## \|\| 9.22.29-32 \|\|

*alpopyeṣu kṛto dharmaḥ syātsahasraguṇo nṛṇām \|*  
*puṇyavṛddhikarānkālāñchṛṇvatho vacmi nārada \|\| 29 \|\|*

*ayane dve ca viṣuvaṃ grahaṇaṃ sūryasomayoḥ \|*  
*dinakṣayo vyatīpātaḥ śravaṇarkṣāṇi sarvaśaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*dvādaśya ekādaśyaśca manvādyāśca yugādayaḥ \|*  
*puṇyāḥ syustithayaḥ sarvā amāvāsyā ca vaidhṛtiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*māsarkṣayukpaurṇamāsyaścatasropyaṣṭakāstathā \|*  
*svajanmarkṣāṇi ca harerjanmotsavadināni ca \|\| 32 \|\|*

29a. Even if an insignificant religious act is performed at these places, it gives a thousand times more merit.

29b-32. I shall now narrate to you the times which enhance the merit (of the act done), Listen to it, O Nārada:

Two Ayanas (the period of Sun’s transition from one solstice to another), Viṣuva (the first point of Aries or Libra into which the Sun enters at the vernal or autumnal equinox), the eclipse of the Sun and the Moon, the days without a tithi, Vyatīpāta and all constellations from Śravaṇa, all the twelfth and eleventh days (Tithis), the first days of Manvantaras and Yugas—All these are auspicious days. Also the new-moon day, Vaidhṛti, the full-moon days accompanied by the constellation of the month and four Aṣṭakā days, the day with the constellation under which one is born and days of celebration of the birth of Hari (the eighth day in the dark half of Śrāvaṇa).

## \|\| 9.22.33 \|\|

*svasya striyāścārbhakāṇāṃ saṃskārobhyudayastathā \|*  
*satpātralabdhiśca yadā kālāḥ puṇyatamā ime \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Those times are auspicious when there take place the sacred ceremonies and consecration of wife and children or times of getting prosperity and of finding a person worthy of receiving gifts.

## \|\| 9.22.34 \|\|

*devapitṛdvijasatāmeṣāṃ śaktyā samarcanam \|*  
*snānadānajapādīni syuranantaphalāni hi \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Worship of Devas, manes, Brāhmaṇas and saintly persons according to one’s capacity, sacred bath, religious gifts, muttering of Mantras, yield infinite fruits.

## \|\| 9.22.35 \|\|

*satpātraṃ tu svayaṃ sākṣādbhagavāneva nārada \|*  
*śākhānāmiva mūlāmbu yaddattaṃ sarvatuṣṭikṛt \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Just as water supplied to roots reaches all branches, so the Lord himself is the worthy recipient, giving satisfaction to all, O Nārada.

## \|\| 9.22.36 \|\|

*ahiṃsā vedavidyābhistuṣṭiḥ saddharmabhaktibhiḥ \|*  
*hṛdi viṣṇuṃ dadhīranye te satpātrāṇi vai dvijāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Those Brāhmaṇas are worthy of receiving (religious gifts) who are satisfied by non-violence and Vedic learning, who hold in their heart Viṣṇu with proper religious devotion.

## \|\| 9.22.37 \|\|

*ekāntikāśca bhagavadbhaktā baddhavimocakāḥ \|*  
*satpātrāṇīti jānīhi yeṣvāste bhagavānsvayam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Know that the devotees of the Lord who are exclusively attached to him and release those who are bound (in Saṃsāra), are worthy recipients and the Lord himself abides in them.

## \|\| 9.22.38 \|\|

*āḍhyastu kārayedviṣṇormandirāṇi dṛḍhāni ca \|*  
*pūjāpravāhasiddhyarthaṃ tadvṛttīścāpi kārayet \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. A rich person should get constructed massive temples of Viṣṇu. He should also provide means of subsistence for the unbroken continuity of the worship (of God).

## \|\| 9.22.39 \|\|

*jalāśayānvāṭikāśca viṣṇvarthamupakalpayet \|*  
*sadannaiḥ surasaiḥ sādhūnbrāhmaṇāṃścaiva tarpayet \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. He should prepare reservoirs of water and gardens for the sake of Viṣṇu. He should satisfy saints and Brāhmaṇas with rich food of good flavour.

## \|\| 9.22.40 \|\|

*ahiṃsānvaiṣṇavānyajñānkuryācchaktyā yathāvidhi \|*  
*vratajanmotsavānviṣṇoḥ saṃbhāreṇa ca bhūyasā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. He should according to his capacity perform Vaiṣṇava type of sacrifices involving no violence as per injunctions. He should celebrate the birth-anniversary festivals of Viṣṇu with greatly affluent preparations.

## \|\| 9.22.41 \|\|

*prauṣṭhapadāsitepakṣe kṣayāhe tīrthaparvasu \|*  
*pitroḥ śrāddhaṃ prakurvīta tadbandhūnāṃ ca śaktitaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. In the dark half of Bhādrapada, on Kṣaya-days, in holy places and on the parvan days, one should perform the Śrāddha of one’s parents and of their relatives as per one’s capacity.

## \|\| 9.22.42 \|\|

*daive karmaṇi pitrye ca bhaktānbhagavato dvijān \|*  
*pūjayeta svadharmasthānbhojayedbhagavaddhiyā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. In ritualistic acts pertaining to Devas and to the manes, one should worship the devotees of the Lord and Brāhmaṇas who are well-established in their specific religious duties and should feed them as if one was feeding the Lord.

## \|\| 9.22.43 \|\|

*daive dvau bhojayedviprau trīṃśca pitrye yathāvidhi \|*  
*ekaikaṃ vobhayatrāpi naiva śrāddhe tu vistaret \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. In rituals pertaining to Devas two Brāmaṇas and in ritualistic acts about Pitṛs (e.g. Śrāddha) three Brāhmaṇas should be fed as per prescribed procedure, or one should feed only one (per Daiva and Pitṛ rituals), but one should not enlarge (the number of Brāhmaṇas) during Śrāddha.

## \|\| 9.22.44 \|\|

*deśakāladravyapātrapūjopakaraṇāni ca \|*  
*vistareṇa yathāśāstraṃ na syādeveti niścitam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. It is definite that Śāstric injunctions do not demand enlargement of place, time, provisions, worthy recipients, utensils of worship etc.

## \|\| 9.22.45 \|\|

*na śrāddhe kvāpi māṃsaṃ tu dadyānnā'dyācca mānavaḥ \|*  
*munyannaiḥ kṣīrasarpirbhyāṃ tṛpyanti pitaro bhṛśam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. A man should never serve non-vegetarian diet anywhere in a Śrāddha nor he should eat it. The ancestors are highly pleased (by partaking) food suitable to sages and with milk and ghee.

## \|\| 9.22.46 \|\|

*ahiṃsā prāṇimātrasya manovāktanubhistu yā \|*  
*tayaiva pitaraḥ sarve tṛpyantyatidayālavaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. All the ancestors who are extremely merciful are satisfied by non-injury to all beings through thoughts, words and physical acts.

## \|\| 9.22.47 \|\|

*tasmātkusaṅgataḥ kvāpi śāstrahārdamabudhya ca \|*  
*śrāddhe māṃsaṃ naiva dadyādvāsudevaparaḥ pumān \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Therefore, a man who is devoted to Vāsudeva should not serve meat in Śrāddha anywhere, either out of evil company or out of ignorance of the meaning of the scripture.

## \|\| 9.22.48 \|\|

*vratāni kuryādviṣṇośca brahmacaryādibhiryamaiḥ \|*  
*sahaiva tatparo nānyatkāryaṃ kuyācca taddine \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. He should observe vows and perform rites pertaining to Viṣṇu, along with restraints including celibacy. He should be devoted to him (Viṣṇu) and should do no other work on that day.

## \|\| 9.22.49 \|\|

*svasaṃbandhijanānāṃ cāpyāśaucaṃ janināśayoḥ \|*  
*yathāśāstraṃ pālayeta grahaṇe cārkacandrayoḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. One should shun auspicious rites during the defilement caused by child-birth or death of one’s relatives as well as at the time of the solar and lunar eclipses, as prescribed in the scriptures.

## \|\| 9.22.50 \|\|

*vyāvahārikakāryāṇāṃ vivāde nirṇayepi ca \|*  
*gṛhītarāstyāgino ye te na kāryā na cādhavāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. In disputes and even in taking decision, in transaction of business, non-householders, including renouncers and widows are not to be employed.

## \|\| 9.22.51 \|\|

*yatraite syurnna tatkāryaṃ sidhyetkvāpi dvijottama \|*  
*sarvasvanāśastatra syādityevaṃ tvasti nirṇayaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Where such persons are present no work can be successful. It will lead to destruction. This is the decision, O excellent Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 9.22.52 \|\|

*dharmā ete gṛhasthānāṃ mayā saṃkṣepatoditāḥ \|*  
*yadanuṣṭhānato nṝṇāṃ syātsveṣṭasukhamakṣayam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. These are the duties of householders narrated in brief by me. After performing these, people will enjoy imperishable happiness as desired by them.

## \|\| 9.22.53 \|\|

*śilādijīvikāvṛttibhedena gṛhiṇo dvijāḥ \|*  
*caturvidhāḥ prakīrtyante tattannāmnā ca nārada \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Householders of twice-born castes are declared as fourfold according to the means of livelihood and known by those various names (of their ways of livelihood), such as maintaining themselves by picking up grains when corn is taken to the thrashing floor.

## \|\| 9.22.54 \|\|

*strīṇāmatha pravakṣyāmi dharmānrdharmavatāṃ vara \|*  
*yeṣu sthitāḥ striyaḥ sarvāḥ prāpnuvantīpsitaṃ sukham \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. I shall now proclaim to you the duties of women abiding by which women will get their desired happiness, O excellent one among the virtuous ones.

## \|\| 9.22.55 \|\|

*suvāsinībhirnnārībhiḥ svapatirdevavatsadā \|*  
*sevanīyo'nuvarttyaśca jaranrugṇo'dhanopi vā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. By women whose husbands are alive, their own husband should always be served as a god, and is to be obeyed even if he be old, diseased or indigent.

## \|\| 9.22.56 \|\|

*tadbandhavaścānuvartyāḥ sevanena yathocitam \|*  
*ujjvalāni vidheyāni gṛhopakaraṇāni ca \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. His relatives also should be obeyed by serving them as is due to them. Utensils in the house should be kept clean and bright.

## \|\| 9.22.57 \|\|

*gṛhaṃ mārjanasekādyaiḥ svacchaṃ kāryaṃ dinedine \|*  
*priyaṃ satyaṃ ca vaktavyaṃ stheyaṃ śucitayā sadā \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Everyday the house should be kept clean by sweeping, sprinkling of water etc. What is true yet agreeable, should be spoken and they should always remain in a pure state.

## \|\| 9.22.58 \|\|

*cāñcalyamatilobhaśca krodhaḥ steyaṃ ca hiṃsanam \|*  
*adhārmikāṇāṃ saṅgaśca varjyaḥ strīṇāṃ tathā nṛṇām \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Fickleness, overgreediness, anger, stealing, violence and association with the irreligious—all these should be avoided boṃ by women as well as by men.

## \|\| 9.22.59 \|\|

*bhavitavyaṃ tatparābhirddharmakāryeṣu sarvadā \|*  
*tyaktvauddhatyaṃ vinītābhiḥ stheyaṃ jitvendriyāṇi ca \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. In religious rituals they should always be exclusively devoted to them. Giving up arrogance and subduing sense-organs, they should live with modesty.

## \|\| 9.22.60 \|\|

*pātivratye sthitābhiśca dharme tābhī ramāpateḥ \|*  
*bhaktiḥ kāryā svatantrābhirbhavitavyaṃ na kutracit \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Worship to the Lord of Ramā should be performed by those women who are established in the virtuous duty of exclusive devotion to the husband. They should never (try to) be independent and self-willed.

## \|\| 9.22.61 \|\|

*vidhavā tu sadā viṣṇuṃ seveta patibhāvataḥ \|*  
*kāmasaṃbandhinīrvārttā na śṛṇvīta na kīrtayet \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. A widow should always serve Viṣṇu, regarding him to be her husband. She should never listen to, nor speak about, sexual matters.

## \|\| 9.22.62 \|\|

*āsannasaṃbandhavato vinānyānpuruṣānkvacit \|*  
*anāpadi spṛśennaiva paśyennaiva ca kāmataḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. If there is no emergency, she should never touch a man unless he is a very close relative. She should never look at a man with carnal intention.

## \|\| 9.22.63 \|\|

*stanapasya tu nuḥ sparśādvṛddhasya ca na duṣyati \|*  
*kārya āvaśyake tābhyāṃ bhāṣaṇe ca vibhartṛkā \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. A widow does not get spoilt by the touch of her male child or of an old man, or by speaking with them in unavoidable situations.

## \|\| 9.22.64 \|\|

*vyāvahārikakārye ca vivādamadhikaṃ naraiḥ \|*  
*na kurvītāvaśyakārye tairbhāṣeta vinā rahaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. She should not enter into inordinate controversy in matters pertaining to practical life, In essential matters she may speak with them (in open places).

## \|\| 9.22.65 \|\|

*nekṣeta midhunībhūtaṃ budyā paśvādyapi kvacit \|*  
*tyajecca sakalānbhogānsyātsakṛnmitabhuktathā \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. She should never intently see the sexual union even of animals. She should give up all objects of pleasure and should be moderate in taking meal once a day.

## \|\| 9.22.66 \|\|

*sadhātusūkṣmavāsāṃsi nālaṃkārāṃśca dhārayet \|*  
*na divā śayanaṃ kuryānna khaṭvāyāmanāpadi \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. She should not put on fine cloth woven with metal (threads like those of gold or silver) and should not wear ornaments. She should never sleep at day time or on bedsteads, except in emergency.

## \|\| 9.22.67 \|\|

*tāmbūlabhakṣaṇaṃ naiva kuryānnābhyaṅgamañjanam \|*  
*pumprasaṃgācca bibhiyātkṛṣṇāheriva nityadā \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. She should never eat betel-leaves, smear the body with oil or unguents and use collyrium. She should always be afraid of association with men like that with a black serpent.

## \|\| 9.22.68 \|\|

*samīkṣya puruṣaṃ nārī yā na mohamupāvrajet \|*  
*tādṛśī tu vinā lakṣmīmekāṃ nānyāsti kutracit \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. With the exception of Goddess Lakṣmī only there is no woman who is not subject to infatuation after seeing a man.

## \|\| 9.22.69 \|\|

*dharmaniṣṭhā tato nārī svaniḥśreyasamicchatī \|*  
*nekṣeta puruṣākāraṃ buddhipūrvaṃ ca na spṛśet \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Hence a woman, established in religious duties and desirous of one’s beatitude, should not look at a male form or touch him intently.

## \|\| 9.22.70 \|\|

*kṛcchracāndrāyaṇādīni nairantaryeṇa bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*vratāni kuryācca sadā bhavenniyamatatparā \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. She should perform religious observance, like Kṛcchra, Cāndrāyaṇa and others regularly. She should be always engaged in observing restraints.

## \|\| 9.22.71 \|\|

*pitrā putrādinā vāpi taruṇī taruṇena ca \|*  
*saha tiṣṭhenna rahasi kusaṅgaṃ sarvathā tyajet \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. A young woman should not stay in a solitary place even with father, sons etc. or with a young man. She should absolutely dissociate herself from bad company.

## \|\| 9.22.72 \|\|

*sadhavā vidhavā vā strī svarajodarśanaṃ kvacit \|*  
*na gopayettrirātraṃ tu manuṣyādīṃśca na spṛśet \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. A woman whether a widow or one with her husband alive, should never conceal her period of menstruation. For ṃree nights (during this period) she should not touch a human being and other (objects etc.).

## \|\| 9.22.73 \|\|

*prathame'hani caṇḍālī dvitīye brahmaghātinī \|*  
*tṛtīye rajakī proktā sā caturthe'hni śuddhyati \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. On the first day of menstruation, she is called (i.e. is equated with) a Cāṇḍāla woman, on the second day, a Brāhmaṇa-killer, on the third day, a washer-women. On the fourth day, she becomes purified.

## Chapter 23 - Duties of Forest-Hermits (Vānaprastha) and Recluses (Saṃnyāsa)

## \|\| 9.23.1 \|\|

*śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*vānaprasthasya vakṣyāmi niyamānatha te mune \|*  
*tṛtīya āyuṣo bhāge tṛtīyāśrama īritaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:

1\. O sage, I shall now narrate to you the religious restraints to be observed by forest-hermits (Vānaprastha). The third part of life is known as the third Āśrama.

## \|\| 9.23.2 \|\|

*nityaṃ kuryādviṣṇupūjā madyādviṣṇornniveditam \|*  
*dvādaśārṇaṃ japedviṣṇoraṣṭākṣaramanuṃ ca vā \|\| 20 \|\|*

2 One should enter a forest (forest-hermit’s life) with one’s wife, if she is agreeable in serving one’s self, is averse to objects of enjoyment, and likes to perform penance.

## \|\| 9.23.3 \|\|

*anyathā tu sutādibhyastasyāḥ poṣaṇarakṣaṇam \|*  
*ādiśya svayamekākī virakto vanamāviśet \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Otherwise, after ordering his sons and others for her maintenance and protection, he, being free from worldly attachment, should enter the forest alone.

## \|\| 9.23.4 \|\|

*nirbhayo nivasettatra taporuciratandritaḥ \|*  
*kuryāduṭajamagnyarthaṃ svayaṃ tu bahirāvaset \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Interested in performing penance and remaining vigilant, he should stay there fearlessly. He should construct a cottage for (sacrificial) fire, but should stay outside.

## \|\| 9.23.5 \|\|

*bhavetpañcatapā grīṣma udavāsaśca śaiśire \|*  
*āsāraṣāṭca varṣāsu jitakrodho jitendriyaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Having subdued his anger and sense-organs, he should perform the Pañcāgni-Sādhana (with four fires on four sides around him and the fifth fire, the sun, above) in Summer, stay in water during winter, and remain in showers in rainy season.

## \|\| 9.23.6 \|\|

*vāsaśca tārṇaṃ pārṇaṃ vā vasītājinavalkalam \|*  
*bhuñjīta ṛṣidhānyāni vanyaṃ kandaphalādi vā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He should wear garments made of grass or leaves or bark-garment or hide of a deer. He should eat corn prescribed for sages (i.e. which grows up naturally without tilling the soil) or bulbous roots or fruits grown in the forest.

## \|\| 9.23.7 \|\|

*agnipakvaṃ vārkapakvamapakvaṃ vāpi bhakṣayet \|*  
*abhāve tveṣa dantānāmaśmolūkhalakuṭṭitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He should eat food which is boiled on fire or heated in the sun, or not boiled at all. If that is not available, (he should eat it) powered in mortar of his teeth.

## \|\| 9.23.8 \|\|

*svayamevāharedannaṃ yathākālaṃ dinedine \|*  
*kāle parāhṛtaṃ vāpi gṛhṇīyānnānyadā kvacit \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. One should personally bring food everyday at the proper time. At (emergent) times, he may accept food brought by others, but never at any other time.

## \|\| 9.23.9 \|\|

*kālepi kṛṣṭapacyaṃ tu na gṛhṇīyādanāpadi \|*  
*vanyairevāgnikāryaṃ ca dhānyaiḥ kurvīta pūrvavat \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. When there is no emergency (i.e. normally), he should not accept corn from tilled soil. He should perform the religious worship of (sacrificial) fire with wild corn (grown naturally in a forest).

## \|\| 9.23.10 \|\|

*rakṣetkamaṇḍaluṃ daṇḍamagnihotraparicchadān \|*  
*keśaromaśmaśrunakhāndhārayenmalināndataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He should retain his waterpot of gourd, the (religious) staff and the articles required for maintenance of sacrificial fire. He should bear (grow) without cutting or trimming hair on the head and the body, mustaches, beard and nails and unscrubbed teeth.

## \|\| 9.23.11 \|\|

*aṃgānyamardayansnāyādbhūtale ca śayīta saḥ \|*  
*deśakāla balāvasthānusāreṇa tapaścaret \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He should bathe without massaging his limbs (for cleansing), and should sleep on bare ground. He should perform penance according to the exigencies of place, time, his power and state of health.

## \|\| 9.23.12 \|\|

*phenapāścaudumbarāśca vālakhilyāstathaiva ca \|*  
*vaikhānaseti kathitāścaturddhā vanavāsinaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Forest-hermits are spoken of as belonging to four classes, viz. Phenapa, Auduṃbara, Vālakhilya and Vaikhānasa.

## \|\| 9.23.13 \|\|

*yathāśakti dvādaśābdānaṣṭau vā caturo vane \|*  
*vaseddvāvekamevāpi tataḥ saṃnyāsamāśrayet \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. One should according to one’s (physical) capacity stay in the forest (i.e. continue to be a forest-hermit) for twelve, eight, four, two or one year, and then take to the stage of Saṃnyāsa (recluse).

## \|\| 9.23.14 \|\|

*yadi syāttīvravairāgyaṃ tarhi nyāso hitāvahaḥ \|*  
*vasettatraivā'nyathā tu yāvajjīvaṃ vane dvijaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. If one has intense Vairāgya (aversion against objects of worldly pleasures), the (adoption of) Saṃnyāsa is beneficial. Otherwise a Brāhmaṇa should stay in the forest (i.e. continue the stage of forest-hermit) throughout (the rest of) his life.

## \|\| 9.23.15 \|\|

*yathāvidhi kṛtatyāgasturīyāśramamāsthitaḥ \|*  
*sācchādanaṃ tu kaupīnaṃ kanthāmekāṃ ca dhārayet \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. After renunciation as per injunctions, one who has (entered and) established oneself in the fourth Āśrama (stage of life), he should wear a small piece (strip) of cloṃ to cover the privities, and a patched garment.

## \|\| 9.23.16 \|\|

*daṇḍaṃ kamaṇḍaluṃ cāmbugālanaṃ bibhṛyācca saḥ \|*  
*sadācāradvijagṛhe kāle bhikṣāṃ samācaret \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He should possess a (religious) staff, a waterpot of gourd and a piece of cloth for straining water.

## \|\| 9.23.17 \|\|

*na kuryātpratyahaṃ bhikṣāmekasyaiva gṛhe yatiḥ \|*  
*rasalubdho bhavenneva sakṛcca mitabhugbhavet \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. A recluse should not beg alms in the house of the same person everyday. He should never be longing for flavourous food. He should take food once (per day) and that too limited (in quantity).

## \|\| 9.23.18 \|\|

*vanasthāśramiṇo bhikṣāṃ prāyo gṛhṇīta bhikṣukaḥ \|*  
*tadandhasātiśuddhena śuddhyatyevā'sya yanmanaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. A mendicant should generally accept alms from a person who is a forest-hermit. His (mendicant’s) mind gets purified by the extremely pure food of the forest-hermit.

## \|\| 9.23.19 \|\|

*ghrāṇepi māṃsasurayoḥ pārākaṃ vratamācaret \|*  
*śaucācāraviśuddhaḥ syācchūdrādīṃścāpi na spṛśet \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Even if he has smelt meat and wine, he should perform the expiatory observance called pārāka. He should get purified by observing purificatory rites. He should not even touch Śūdras and oṃer (defiled) persons.

## \|\| 9.23.20 \|\|

*nityaṃ kuryādviṣṇupūjā madyādviṣṇornniveditam \|*  
*dvādaśārṇaṃ japedviṣṇoraṣṭākṣaramanuṃ ca vā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He should always perform the worship of Viṣṇu and eat what has been offered to Viṣṇu (i.e. offer that food first to Viṣṇu before eating it). He should mutter the twelve-syllabled (oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya) or eight-syllabled (oṃ nārāyaṇāya namaḥ) Mantra of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 9.23.21 \|\|

*asadvādaṃ na kurvīta vṛttyarthaṃ nācaretkathām \|*  
*asacchāstre na saktaḥ syānnopajīvecca jīvikām \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. He should not utter falsehood. He should not be a story-teller

for his livelihood. He should not be addicted to false (heretic) Śāstras or scriptures, nor should he follow a vocation for maintaining himself.

## \|\| 9.23.22 \|\|

*sacchāstramabhyaseccāsau bandhamokṣānudarśanam \|*  
*maṭhādīnnaiva badhnīyādahantāmamate tyajet \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. He should study true (non-heretic) scriptures which expound bondage and liberation. He should build a hut or a convent. He should give up the sense of ‘I’ and ‘my’ (personal pride and craving for possession).

## \|\| 9.23.23 \|\|

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye vanasthayatidharmanirūpaṇaṃ nāma trayoviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Except for the period of four months of rainy season (Cāturmāsya), he should not stay at one place except under duress or in emergency. He should realize by knowledge, the real form of his soul and that of Han.

## \|\| 9.23.24 \|\|

*kāmaṃ krodhaṃ bhayaṃ vairaṃ dhanadhānyādisaṃgraham \|*  
*naiva kuryātpālayeta yamāṃśca niyamānyatiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. A recluse (Yati) should never entertain desire, anger, fear, enmity and avoid storage of wealth, grains of com etc. He should practise moral restraints and observances.

## \|\| 9.23.25 \|\|

*tīvrajñānavirāgābhyāṃ saṃpannopi yatirdhruvam \|*  
*strīvittabhūṣāsadvastrasaṃsargādbhraṣṭatāṃ vrajet \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. A recluse though endowed with deep knowledge and intense aversion to objects of worldly enjoyment becomes fallen by contacts with a woman, wealth, ornaments, garments.

## \|\| 9.23.26 \|\|

*puṣpa candanatailādisugandhidravyavarjanam \|*  
*tyāgī kurvītānyathā tu bhaveddehātmadhīḥ sa vai \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. A renunciator (Saṃnyāsin) should give up (enjoyment of) flowers, sandal, oil and other fragrant materials; otherwise he will entertain the (mis-)conception of the identity of the body with the soul.

## \|\| 9.23.27 \|\|

*āhāro yasya yāvāṃstaṃ tāvānstrīkāma āviśet \|*  
*ato mitaṃ nīrasaṃ ca bhojanaṃ tyāgino hitam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The extent to which one takes food to that extent lust for women will take possession of him. Hence limited, tasteless meal is beneficial to a renunciator.

## \|\| 9.23.28 \|\|

*na śrāvyā grāmyavārttā ca mokṣasiddhimabhīpsatā \|*  
*naśyedyacchravaṇānnṝṇāṃ sadyo viṣṇukathā ruciḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Vulgar speech should not be heard by one who is desirous of attaining liberation. By hearing it liking for listening to the stories of Viṣṇu instantaneously disappears.

## \|\| 9.23.29 \|\|

*api citramayīṃ nārīṃ tyāgī nekṣeta na spṛśet \|*  
*stryākāradarśanādeva bhraṣṭā bhūri tapasvinaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. A renunciator should not see or touch the painting of a woman. Many ascetics have fallen by merely the sight of a woman’s form.

## \|\| 9.23.30 \|\|

*kuṭīcako bahūdaśca haṃsaḥ paramahaṃsakaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ caturddhā kathito yatirvairāgyabhedataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. According to difference in detachment Sannyāsins are classified as Kuṭīcaka\[7\], Bahūda\[8\], Haṃsa\[9\] and Paramahaṃsa.

## \|\| 9.23.31 \|\|

*kāṣāyavāsaso ye me bhaviṣyāḥ sādhavaśca taiḥ \|*  
*kāryaṃ madarthapākādi turyāśramasthitairapi \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Those who wear ochre-coloured garments and those who are future sages should perform work for me, including cooking etc., though they may be in the fourth stage (i.e. Sannyāsa).

## \|\| 9.23.32 \|\|

*śrīvāsudevabhaktā ye tīvravairāgyaśālinaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ dharmastu tatsevā proktāhassu ca rātriṣu \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The religious duty of the devotees of Śrī Vāsudeva endowed with intense aversion to objects of worldly pleasure is proclaimed as his (i.e. Vāsudeva’s) service, day and night.

## \|\| 9.23.33 \|\|

*ekopi ca kṣaṇasteṣāṃ jñānavijñānabhūyasām \|*  
*bhaktiṃ navavidhāṃ viṣṇorvinā vyartho na vai bhavet \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Not a single moment of those endowed with profound knowledge, both spiritual and secular, is vain (wasted) without being engaged in some form of devotion consisiting of nine types.

## \|\| 9.23.34 \|\|

*sarverguṇairupetopi bhagavadvimukho yadi \|*  
*svajanopi bhavettaṃ tu jahyureva hi vaiṣṇavāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The devotees of Viṣṇu should straightaway abandon a person who, though endowed with all good qualities, is averse to the Lord, even if that person happens to be a relative.

## \|\| 9.23.35 \|\|

*prāsādikaṃ harerannaṃ prokṣitaṃ tatpadāmbunā \|*  
*bhuñjīraṃstulasīmiśraṃ pratyahaṃ sātvatā janāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. People who are the followers of Kṛṣṇa should eat everyday the food which is offered to Hari, is sprinkled with the water with which his feet are washed, and mixed with leaves of Tulasī plant.

## \|\| 9.23.36 \|\|

*strīṇāṃ ca strīṣu saktānāṃ prasaṃgo viṣṇucintakaiḥ \|*  
*sarvathaiva parityājyo bhavettaddhyānamanyathā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Contact with women or those who are addicted to women, should be totally avoided by persons meditating on Viṣṇu. Otherwise they will be meditating on them (i.e. women).

## \|\| 9.23.37 \|\|

*bhagavantaṃ vāsudevaṃ vinaikamitaraḥ pumān \|*  
*kopi nāstyeva yo nārīṃ samīkṣya na vimuhyati \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. There is definitely no other man, except the venerable Lord Vāsudeva, who is not infatuated in looking at a woman.

## \|\| 9.23.38 \|\|

*yatra sthityā muhuḥ strīṇāṃ syātāṃ śabdaśrutīkṣaṇe \|*  
*tyāgī tatra vasennaiva vasandharmacyuto bhavet \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. A renunciator (i.e. a recluse) should never stay at a place by occupying which one frequently hears the speech and gets the sight of women. If he stays there, he falls from his religious duty.

## \|\| 9.23.39 \|\|

*kāmo lobho rasāsvādaḥ sneho mānastathā ca ruṭ \|*  
*ete tyājyāḥ prayatnena ṣaḍdoṣāḥ saṃsṛtipradāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Desire, greed, taste for flavours, affection, pride, anger—ṃese six defects should be avoided with special efforts; as they lead to Saṃsāra.

## \|\| 9.23.40 \|\|

*prokteṣu dharmeṣveteṣu yasyayasya cyutirbhavet \|*  
*yathāśakti yathāśāstraṃ kāryā tattasya niṣkṛtiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. If there be failure in observing any of the religious duties proclaimed here, it should be expiated to the best of one’s capacity as per religious injunctions.

## \|\| 9.23.41 \|\|

*itthaṃ caturṇāṃ varṇānāmāśramāṇāṃ ca nārada \|*  
*dharmāḥ saṃkṣepataḥ proktā vaiṣṇavānāṃ ca te mayā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Thus the religious duties of four Varṇas and Āśramas as well as those of Vaiṣṇavas have been briefly proclaimed by me, O Nārada.

## \|\| 9.23.42 \|\|

*varṇī yatiśca dharmastho brahmalokamupaiti vai \|*  
*ṛṣilokaṃ vanasthaśca gṛhasthaḥ svargamāpnuyāt \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. A religious student (Brahmacārin) and a Sannyāsin who are established in their (particular) religious duties go to Brahmaloka. Forest-hermits go to the world of Sages and householders to Svarga (heaven).

## Chapter 24 - The Nature of Knowledge (jñāna-svarūpa)

## \|\| 9.24.1 \|\|

*śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*atha jñānasvarūpaṃ te vacmi sāṃkhyena niścitam \|*  
*kṣetrādi jñāyate yena tajjñānaṃ hi nirucyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: This chapter gives a combination of the theistic Sāṅkhya theory of evolution of the universe as well as the Purāṇic concept of Viṣṇu creating Brahmā for the same.

Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:

1\. Now I shall relate to you the nature of knowledge (jñāna-svarūpa) as determined by Sāṃkhya, whereby Kṣetra and others are known. That knowledge is being explained.

## \|\| 9.24.2 \|\|

*vāsudevaḥ paraṃ brahma bṛhatyakṣaradhāmani \|*  
*ādāveko'dvitīyo'bhūnnirguṇo divyavigrahaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Vāsudeva is the Supreme Brahman in the great imperishable abode. At the beginning he was only one without a second and attributeless, with a divine (or refulgent) body.

## \|\| 9.24.3 \|\|

*sa kāryamūlaprakṛtiḥ sakālā'kṣaratejasi \|*  
*prakāśe'rkasya rātrīva tirobhūtā tadā'bhavat \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Just as night disappears in the light of the sun, so the Primordial Nature along with its evolutes and Time became invisible in his imperishable light.

## \|\| 9.24.4 \|\|

*sisṛkṣāthābhavattasya brahmāṇḍānāṃ yadā tadā \|*  
*sakālāvirbabhūvādau mahāmāyā tato hi sā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. When the desire to create cosmoses or universes occurred to him, then that great Māyā along with Time manifested herself at the beginning.

## \|\| 9.24.5 \|\|

*tāṃ kālaśaktimādāya vāsudevo'kṣarātmanā \|*  
*sisṛkṣayaikṣata yadā sā cukṣobha tadaiva hi \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Taking that power of Time, Vāsudeva with a desire to create, saw her with his Akṣara (imperishable) Self. Then she got agitated.

## \|\| 9.24.6 \|\|

*tasyāḥ pradhānapuruṣakoṭayo jajñire mune \|*  
*yujyante sma pradhānaiste puruṣāścecchayā prabhoḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. From her (Mahāmāyā) crores of Pradhānas (or Prakṛtis) and Puruṣas were born. Due to the will of the Lord those Puruṣas are united with Pradhānas (or Prakṛtis).

## \|\| 9.24.7 \|\|

*pumāṃso nidadhurgarbhāṃsteṣu tebhyaśca jajñire \|*  
*brahmāṇḍāni hyasaṅkhyāni tatraikaṃ tu vivicyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. In them Puruṣas deposited foetuses. From them were born innumerable Brahmāṇḍas (Cosmic Eggs). Out of them, one is described.

## \|\| 9.24.8 \|\|

*ādau jajñe mahāṃstasmātpuṃso vīryāddhiraṇmayāt \|*  
*ahaṅkārastatastasmādguṇāḥ sattvādayastrayaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. From the golden semen of the Puruṣa, at first (the principle called) Mahat was born (evolved). From it (i.e. Mahat) was evolved Ahaṃkāra (i.e. Cosmic Ego). From it (i.e. Cosmic Ego) were evolved the three Guṇas—Sattva etc.

## \|\| 9.24.9 \|\|

*tamasaḥ pañca tanmātrā mahābhūtāni jajñire \|*  
*daśendriyāṇi rajaso buddhyā saha mahānasuḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. From (Guṇa) Tamas five Tamātras (i.e. subtle elements) and gross elements were evolved. From (Guṇa) Rajas were evolved ten organs (of sense and action), the great (principle of) Life along with Buddhi (intelligence).

## \|\| 9.24.10 \|\|

*sattvādindriyadevāśca jāyante sma manastathā \|*  
*sāmānyatastattvasaṃjñā ete devāḥ prakīrttitāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. From (Guṇa) Sattva are born the deities presiding over the organs (of sense and action) and also Manas (mind). Ordinarily what are designated as Tattva (principles) are called (here) Devas.

## \|\| 9.24.11 \|\|

*preritā vāsudevena svasvāṃśairaiśvaraṃ vapuḥ \|*  
*ajījananvirāṭsañjñaṃ te carācarasaṃśrayam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Impelled by Vāsudeva, they gave birth to (i.e. created) a divine body called Virāṭ, by contributing their individual parts. That (Virāṭ) was the resort of the movable and immovable.

## \|\| 9.24.12 \|\|

*sa ca vairājapuruṣaḥ svasṛṣṭāsvapsvaśeta yat \|*  
*tena nārāyaṇa iti procyate nigamādibhiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. That Vairāja-Puruṣa slept on the waters created by him. Hence he is proclaimed as Nārāyaṇa by Vedas and such other (scriptural texts).

## \|\| 9.24.13 \|\|

*tannābhipadmādbrahmāsīdrājaso'tha hṛdambujāt \|*  
*jajñe viṣṇuḥ sattvaguṇo lalāṭāttāmaso haraḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. From the lotus (grown out) of his navel was born Brahmā, characterised by Rajoguṇa. Viṣṇu of Sattva character was born from the lotus of his heart. And Hara characterised by Tamas was born from his forehead.

## \|\| 9.24.14 \|\|

*etebhya eva sthānebhyastisra āsaṃśca śaktayaḥ \|*  
*tatrāsīttāmasī durgā sāvitrī rājasī tathā \|*  
*sāttvikī śrīśceti sarvā vastrālaṃkāraśobhitāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. From these very places three Śaktis were born. Out of them Durgā was characterised by Tamas, Sāvitrī by Rajas, Śrī is characterised by Sattva Guṇa. All of them are adorned with garments and ornaments.

## \|\| 9.24.15 \|\|

*tā vairājājñayā trīṃśca brahmādīnpratipedire \|*  
*durgā rudraṃ ca sāvitrī brahmāṇaṃ viṣṇumantimā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. By the order of Vairāja, they betook themselves to Brahmā and others. Durgā resorted to Rudra, Sāvitrī to Brahmā and the last (Śrī) to Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 9.24.16 \|\|

*caṇḍikādyāśca durgāyā aṃśenāsansahasraśaḥ \|*  
*trayīmukhyāśca sāvitryāḥ śaktayoṃśena jajñire \|*  
*dussahāpramukhāścāsannaṃśenaiva śriyo mune \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Thousands of Śaktis including Caṇḍikā were (born) from a part of Durgā; Śaktis of whom Trayī was prominent were born of part of Sāvitrī. Śaktis of which Dussahā was the chief one were born from a part of Śrī, O sage.

## \|\| 9.24.17 \|\|

*tatrādito yo brahmāsīdvairājanābhipadmataḥ \|*  
*ekārṇave tadabjasthaḥ sa kaścidapi naikṣata \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He who was Brahmā born of the navel-lotus of Vairāja and was staying in the lotus in that Ekārṇava did (could) not see (know) anything.

## \|\| 9.24.18 \|\|

*visargabuddhimaprāpto nātmānaṃ ca viveda saḥ \|*  
*kohaṃ kuta iti dhyāyannadidṛkṣatkajāśrayam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Not having acquired the knowledge of creation, he did not know himself. Meditating ‘who am I’, ‘whence have I come?’, he happened to see the Lotus which was his resort.

## \|\| 9.24.19 \|\|

*nālaṃ praviśyā'dho yātustanmūlaṃ ca vicinvataḥ \|*  
*saṃvatsaraśataṃ yātaṃ tasya nāntaṃ tu solabhat \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. A period of hundred years elapsed while he entered the stalk of the Lotus, and went downwards to discover the root (of the lotus), but he could not get at the end of it.

## \|\| 9.24.20 \|\|

*ūrdhvaṃ punarupetyā'tha śrāntaśca niṣasāda saḥ \|*  
*adṛśyamūrtirbhagavānūce tapatapeti tam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Coining up again and feeling exhausted, he sat down. The Lord in his invisible form spoke to him, “Perform penance; perform penance.”

## \|\| 9.24.21 \|\|

*tacchrutvā tatpravaktāramadṛṣṭvā ca sa sarvataḥ \|*  
*gurūpadiṣṭavattepe divyaṃ varṣasahasrakam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Having heard it and not being able to see the speaker anywhere, he performed penance for a period of one thousand divine years, as advised by the preceptor.

## \|\| 9.24.22 \|\|

*padme tapasyate tasmai tapaḥ śuddhātmane tataḥ \|*  
*samādhau darśayāmāsa dhāma vaikuṇṭhamacyutaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. To him who was performing penance in the Lotus and was of purified soul, Acyuta showed his place of residence (called) Vaikuṇṭha while he was in profound meditation.

## \|\| 9.24.23 \|\|

*prādhānikā guṇā yatra trayopi rajaādayaḥ \|*  
*na bhavantyalpamapi yatkālamāyābhayaṃ na ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. (Obscure) Where there are the three Guṇas, Rajas etc. evolved out of Pradhāna, there exists not the smallest, which has no fear from Kāla (Time, Death) and Māyā.

## \|\| 9.24.24 \|\|

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye jñānasvarūpanirūpaṇaṃ nāma caturviśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. In that refulgent light brilliant like the simultaneous rising of ten thousand suns, there he saw Vāsudeva of beautiful, lustrous, dark form.

## \|\| 9.24.25 \|\|

*caturbhujaṃ gadāpadmaśaṃkhacakradharaṃ vibhum \|*  
*pītāmbaraṃ mahāratnakirīṭādivibhūṣaṇam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. That Supreme Ruler had four arms holding (in each) an iron mace, a lotus, a conch and a discus. He wore a yellow garment and was adorned with a big crown set with jewels (and other ornaments).

## \|\| 9.24.26 \|\|

*nandatārkṣyādibhirjjuṣṭaṃ pārṣadaiśca caturbhujaiḥ \|*  
*siddhibhiścāṣṭabhiḥ ṣaḍbhirbaddhāñjalipuṭairbhagaiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He was resorted to by four-armed attendants like Nanda, Tārkṣya (Garuḍa) and others, by eight super-natural powers (like Aṇimā etc.) and by six types of good luck with their palms folded in reverence.

## \|\| 9.24.27 \|\|

*siṃhāsane śriyā sākamupaviṣṭaṃ tamīśvaram \|*  
*praṇamya prāñjalistasthau viriñco hṛṣṭamānasaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Bowing down to the great Lord who sat along with Śrī on the throne, God Brahmā, delighted in mind, stood before him with folded palms.

## \|\| 9.24.28 \|\|

*taṃ prāha bhagavānbrahmaṃstuṣṭohaṃ tapasā tava \|*  
*varaṃ varaya mattastvaṃ svābhīṣṭaṃ yatpriyosi me \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The Lord spoke to him: “O Brahman, I am pleased with you due to your penance. As you are dear to me, ask for any boon desired by you, from me.”

## \|\| 9.24.29 \|\|

*ityuktastena taṃ jānaṃstapasi prerakaṃ prabhum \|*  
*svaṃ ca viśvasṛjaṃ brahmā yayāce'bhimataṃ varam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Addressed by him thus, Brahmā knowing him to be his director to perform penance, entreated him (to grant) the boon desired by him regarding the creation of the universe.

## \|\| 9.24.30 \|\|

*prajāvisargaśaktiṃ me dehi tubhyaṃ namaḥ prabho \|*  
*tatrāpi ca na baddhyeyaṃ yathā kuru tathā kṛpām \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. “Obeisance to you, O Lord! Give me the power to create. Do also to me such favour as will not bind me in that (act of creation).”

## \|\| 9.24.31 \|\|

*tatastaṃ bhagavānūce setsyate te manorathaḥ \|*  
*vairājena mayātmaikyaṃ bhāvayitvā samādhinā \|*  
*prajāḥ sṛjā'tha svāsādhye kārye smaryohamiṣṭadaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Then the Lord said: “Your desire will be fulfilled. Create subjects by conceiving through meditation your identity with me, Vairāja. If any task is not possible for you to accomplish, I should be remembered. I am the donor of desired objects.”

## \|\| 9.24.32 \|\|

*ityuktvāntardadhe viṣṇurbrahmāpyekasamādhinā \|*  
*vairājenā'tha lokānprāglīnānsarvānsva aikṣata \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. After saying Viṣṇu vanished. Brahmā, by meditating on his identity with Vairāja, saw personally all the regions (or subjects) which were merged formerly.

## \|\| 9.24.33 \|\|

*visargaśaktiṃ saṃprāpya sa sargāya mano dadhe \|*  
*brahmajyotirmayastāvadādityaḥ prādurāsa ha \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Having secured the creative power, Brahmā set his mind on creation. In the meanwhile, Āditya (Sun-god) full of the lustre of Brahman, manifested himself.

## \|\| 9.24.34 \|\|

*sthāpayitvāṇḍamadhye taṃ tataḥ sa manasā'sṛjat \|*  
*tapobhaktiviśuddhena munīnādyāṃścatuḥsanān \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Having established him at the centre of Brahmāṇḍa (universe), he created by his mind which was extremely pure due to penance and devotion, the four primeval sages, the four Sanas (viz. Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatkumāra, Sanātana).

## \|\| 9.24.35 \|\|

*prajāḥ sṛjata cetyūce tāṃstadā te tu tadvacaḥ \|*  
*na jagṛhurnnaiṣṭhikendrāstebhyaścukrodha viśvasṛṭ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. He ordered them, “Create subjects”. Those who were prominent perpetual celibate (sages), did not accept his order. The creator of the universe got angry with them.

## \|\| 9.24.36 \|\|

*kruddhasya tasya bhālācca rudra āsīttamomayaḥ \|*  
*manyuṃ niyamya manasā prajeśānso'sṛjattataḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. From the forehead of angry Brahmā was born Rudra full of the Guṇa called Tamas. Controlling his anger, he mentally created Prajāpatis (presiders over the subjects).

## \|\| 9.24.37 \|\|

*marīcimatriṃ pulahaṃ pulastyaṃ ca bhṛguṃ kratum \|*  
*vasiṣṭhaṃ kardamaṃ caiva dakṣamaṃgirasaṃ tathā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. (They were as follow:) Marīci, Atri, Pulaha, Pulastya, Bhṭgu, Kratu, Vasitṣṭha, Kardama, Dakṣa and Aṅgiras.

## \|\| 9.24.38 \|\|

*dharmaṃ tataḥ sa hṛdayādadharmaṃ pṛṣṭhatastathā \|*  
*manasaḥ kāmamāsyācca vāṇīṃ krodhaṃ bhruvo'sṛjat \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. He created Dharma from his heart, Adharma from (his) back, sexual desire (Kāma) from (his) mind, Speech from mouth and Anger from his eyebrow.

## \|\| 9.24.39 \|\|

*śaucaṃ tapo dayā satyamiti dharmapadāni ca \|*  
*caturbhyo vadanebhyaśca catvāri sasṛje tataḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Then from his four faces (mouths) he created the feet of Dharma, viz. Purity, Penance, Compassion and Truth.

## \|\| 9.24.40 \|\|

*ṛgvedaṃ vadanātpūrvādyajurvedaṃ ca dakṣiṇāt \|*  
*sasarja paścimātsāma saumyāccātharvasaṃjñitam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. He created Ṛgveda from his eastern face, Yajurveda from the southern face, Sāmaveda from the western and Atharvan from the northern face.

## \|\| 9.24.41 \|\|

*itihāsapurāṇāni yajñānvipraśataṃ tathā \|*  
*vasvādityamarudviśvānsādhyāṃśca mukhato'sṛjat \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. From his mouth he created Itihāsa, Purāṇas, sacrifices, a hundred Brāhmaṇas, (gods such as) Vasus, Ādityas, Maruts, Viśvedevas, and Sādhyas.

## \|\| 9.24.42 \|\|

*bāhubhyaḥ kṣatriyaśatamūrubhyāṃ ca viśāṃ śatam \|*  
*padbhyāṃ śūdraśataṃ caitānsasarja saha vṛttibhiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. He created a hundred Kṣatriyas from his arms, a hundred Vaiśyas from his thighs and a hundred Śūdras from his feet—all along with their professions and modes of livelihood.

## \|\| 9.24.43 \|\|

*brahmacaryaṃ ca hṛdayādgārhasthyaṃ jaghanasthalāt \|*  
*vanāśramaṃ tathorastaḥ saṃnyāsaṃ śiraso'sṛjat \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. He created the (stage of life called) Brahmacarya (celibate-studentship) from his heart, householdership from his loins (genital organ?), forest-hermitship from his chest and Sannyāsa from his head.

## \|\| 9.24.44 \|\|

*vakṣaḥsthalātpitṛgaṇānasurāñjaghanasthalāt \|*  
*sasarja ca gudānmṛtyuṃ nirṛtiṃ nirayāṃśca saḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. He created a clan called Pitṛs (manes) from his chest, Asuras from his buttocks, the god of deaṃ, Nirṛti and hells from his anus.

## \|\| 9.24.45-46 \|\|

*gandharvāṃścāraṇānsiddhānsarpānyakṣāṃśca rākṣasān \|*  
*nagānmeghānvidyutaśca samudrānsaritastathā \|\| 45 \|\|*

*vṛkṣānpaśūnpakṣiṇaśca sarvānsthāvarajaṅgamān \|*  
*svāṅgebhya eva sosrākṣīdbrahmā nārāyaṇātmakaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. God Brahmā who thus identified his soul with Nārāyaṇa created from the limbs of the body the following: Gandharvas, Cāraṇas, Siddhas, serpents, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, mountains, clouds, lightnings, seas, rivers, trees, beasts (animals), birds and all movables and immovables.

## \|\| 9.24.47 \|\|

*sṛṣṭimetāṃ vilokyāpi nātiprīto yadā tadā \|*  
*hariṃ dhyātvā sa sasṛje tapovidyāsamādhibhiḥ \|*  
*ṛṣīnsvāyambhuvādīṃśca manūṃśca manujānapi \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. When he was not much pleased with this creation, he meditated on Hari and created with penance, learning and concentration, sages, Svāyaṃbhuva and other Manus, and human beings.

## \|\| 9.24.48 \|\|

*tataḥ prītaḥ sa sarveṣāṃ nivāsāya yathocitam \|*  
*svarlokaṃ ca bhuvarlokaṃ bhūrlokaṃ samakalpayat \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Then being satisfied, he created for their residence Svarloka (heaven), Bhuvarloka (the world above the earth) and Bhūrloka (earth).

## \|\| 9.24.49 \|\|

*yeṣāṃ tu yādṛśaṃ karma prākkālīnaṃ hi tānvidhiḥ \|*  
*saṃsthāpya tādṛśe sthāne vṛttīsteṣāmakalpayat \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. God Brahmā established them in places that they deserved by their Karmas in the previous Kalpa, and assigned to them their particular vocations.

## \|\| 9.24.50 \|\|

*devānāmamṛtaṃ nṝṇāmṛṣīṇāṃ cānnamoṣadhīḥ \|*  
*yakṣarakṣosuravyāghrasarpādīnāṃ surāmiṣam \|*  
*caklṛpe gomṛgādīnāṃ vṛttiṃ sa yavasādi ca \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. He assigned nectar (Amṛta) to Devas, food and (medicinal) herbs to men and sages, wine and meat to Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Asuras, tigers, serpents and others. For cows, bulls and deer he provided (grains of corn such as) barley etc.

## \|\| 9.24.51 \|\|

*sa devānāṃ tu viśveṣāṃ havyaṃ vṛttimakalpayat \|*  
*amūrtānāṃ ca mūrtānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ kavyameva ca \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. He fixed Havya (oblations in the fire) as the livehood for all Devas, and assigned Kavya to all embodied and non-embodied manes.

## \|\| 9.24.52 \|\|

*durgodbhavānāṃ śaktīnāṃ tadupāsanatatparaiḥ \|*  
*daityarakṣaḥpiśācādyairdattaṃ madyāmiṣādi ca \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. To the Śaktis born of Goddess Durgā, (he allotted) wine, meat etc. offered by Daityas, Rākṣasas, Piśācas and oṃers who eagerly engaged in propitiating them.

## \|\| 9.24.53 \|\|

*tathā sāvitryudbhavānāṃ śaktīnāṃ tadupāsakaiḥ \|*  
*dattamṛṣyādibhiryajñe munyannaṃ cānnamoṣadhīḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Similarly to the Śaktis created from Sāvitrī, (he allotted) eatables fit for sages, such as food and herbs offered in sacrifices by sages, the propitiators of those Śaktis.

## \|\| 9.24.54 \|\|

*śrījātānāṃ ca śaktīnāṃ tadupāstiparāyaṇaiḥ \|*  
*dattaṃ devāsuranaraiḥ pāyasājyasitādi ca \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. To Śaktis born of Śrī, (he fixed) Pāyasa (rice boiled in milk), ghee, radish etc. offered by Devas, Asuras and human beings who are engaged in propitiating them.

## \|\| 9.24.55-56 \|\|

*prajāpatīnāṃ sa patistataḥ prāhā'khilāḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*ijyā devāśca pitaro havyakavyātmakairmakhaiḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*iṣṭāḥ saṃpūrayiṣyanti hyete yuṣmanmanorathān \|*  
*etānye nārcayiṣyanti te vai nirayagāminaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. Then the Lord of Prajāpatis addressed all his subjects: “Devas and Pitṛs are to be worshipped by sacrifices consisting (of the offerings) of Havya and Kavya. These (deities) will fuffll all your desired objectives. Those who will not worship them will surely go to hell.”

## \|\| 9.24.57 \|\|

*itthaṃ kṛtā hi maryādā tena nārāyaṇātmanā \|*  
*daivaṃ pitryamato nityaṃ janaiḥ kāryaṃ yathāvidhi \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. In this way, the moral law was fixed by Brahmā, entered into by Nārāyaṇa. Hence ritualistic acts pertaining to Devas and Pitṛs should always be performed as per injunctions.

## \|\| 9.24.58 \|\|

*tato brahmā sa sarveṣāṃ dharmasetvavanāya ca \|*  
*tattajjātiṣu ye mukhyāstānmanūṃścāpyatiṣṭhipat \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Then Brahmā appointed the heads of those particular castes and categories as well as Manus for the protection of the bounds of moral law of all.

## \|\| 9.24.59 \|\|

*vāsudevecchayaivetthaṃ vairājādbrahmarūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*kalpekalpe bhavatyeva sṛṣṭirbahuvidhā mune \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. O sage! It is in this way that this diverse creation takes place in every Kalpa by Vairāja in the form of Brahmā, by the will of Vāsudeva.

## \|\| 9.24.60 \|\|

*prākkalpe yādṛśī saṃjñā vedāḥ śāstrāṇi ca kriyāḥ \|*  
*kalpe'nye tādṛśāḥ sarve dharmāḥ syuścā'dhikāriṇaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Just as the knowledge, Vedas, Śāstras and ritualistic rites were in the previous Kalpa, in the next Kalpa similar were all Dharmas and the persons authorized and functionaries.

## \|\| 9.24.61 \|\|

*viṣṇuryaḥ kathitaḥ sopi vairājapuruṣātmakaḥ \|*  
*poṣayatyakhilāṃllokānmaryādāḥ paripālayan \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. He who is called Viṣṇu is also of the nature of (possessed by) Vairājā-Puruṣa. He observes all the boundaries and sustains (by) nourishing all the worlds.

## \|\| 9.24.62 \|\|

*manvādibhiḥ pālyamānāḥ setavastvasurairyadā \|*  
*kāmarūpairvibhidyante vāsudevastadā svayam \|*  
*brahmādibhiḥ prārthyamānaḥ prādurbhavati bhūtale \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. When the limits (of moral behaviour etc.) which are being observed by Manu and others are broken (violated) by Asuras, who can assume any form they like, then Vāsudeva, being prayed to by God Brahmā and others, manifests himself on the earth.

## \|\| 9.24.63 \|\|

*avatārā bhagavato bhūtā bhāvyāśca santi ye \|*  
*kartuṃ na śakyate teṣāṃ saṃkhyāṃ saṃkhyāviśāradaiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. It is not possible to count the number of the Lord’s incarnations past and future even by experts in calculation.

## \|\| 9.24.64 \|\|

*saddharmadevasādhūnāṃ guptyai taddrohimṛtyave \|*  
*śreyase sarvabhūtānāmāvirbhāvosti satpateḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The manifestation of the noble Lord is for the protection of Saddharma (righteousness, moral order), Devas and saintly persons, for killing those who trouble them and for the welfare of all beings.

## \|\| 9.24.65 \|\|

*sa vāsudevaḥ prakṛtau puṃsi kāryeṣu caitayoḥ \|*  
*anvitaśca pṛthakcāste sarvādhīśaḥ svadhāmani \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. That Vāsudeva, the sovereign ruler of all, who is connected with Prakṛti, Puruṣa and all their products (evolutes) stays aloof from them in his own domain.

## \|\| 9.24.66 \|\|

*vyāpya svāṃśairimāṃllokānyathāgnivaruṇādayaḥ \|*  
*svastyāsate svasvaloke tathaiṣa bhagavānmune \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Just as Fire-god, Varuṇa and others permeate this world with their parts and stay happily in their respective regions, so does this Lord, O sage.

## \|\| 9.24.67 \|\|

*sargātprāksaccidānandaḥ śuddha ekaśca nirguṇaḥ \|*  
*yathāsīttādṛgevāsāvanvitopyasti nirmalaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Just as he was Existence, Consciousness and Bliss (incarnate), pure, one and attributeless before the creation of the universe, so he is of equal, unsullied, pure, nature though he is connected (with the universe).

## \|\| 9.24.68 \|\|

*vāyutejojalakṣmāsu tattatkāryeṣu khaṃ yathā \|*  
*anvīyāpyasti nirlepaṃ yathā pūrvaṃ tathaiṣa hi \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Just as sky, though permeating the products or effects of the (elements) wind, fire, water, earth, remains unsmeared by them, similarly he remains so (untouched and pure).

## \|\| 9.24.69 \|\|

*sarvopāsyo niyantā ca vyāpakaścaiṣa kīrtitaḥ \|*  
*ātyantike laye'thaiṣa bhavatyeva yathā purā \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. He deserves to be propitiated and to be worshipped by all. He is the controller. He is glorified as pervader (of the universe). Even in the final dissolution (of the world) he becomes as before (without any change).

## \|\| 9.24.70 \|\|

*vairājaḥ puruṣo yo'tra prokto'sāvīśvarābhidhaḥ \|*  
*jñeyaḥ svatantraḥ sarvajño vaśyamāyaśca nārada \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. He who is called here Vairāja Puruṣa, is designated as Supreme Ruler. He should be known as independent, omniscient and the controller of Māyā, O Nārada.

## \|\| 9.24.71 \|\|

*etasyaiva svarūpāṇi brahmaviṣṇuśivāstrayaḥ \|*  
*rajaādiguṇopetāḥ svaguṇānuguṇakriyāḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva, the three who are endowed with Guṇas like Rajas etc. and whose activities are in consonance with their Guṇas are nothing but forms of that (Lord).

## \|\| 9.24.72 \|\|

*brahmaṇo ye samutpannā devāsuranarādayaḥ \|*  
*te jīvasaṃjñā hyalpajñāḥ paratantrā bhavanti ca \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Devas, Asuras, human beings who are born of Brahmā are designated as Jīvas. They possess little knowledge and are dependent on others.

## \|\| 9.24.73 \|\|

*jīvānāmīśvarāṇāṃ ca tanavaḥ kṣetrasañjñakāḥ \|*  
*mahadāditattvamayyaḥ kṣetrajñākhyāstu tadvidaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. The bodies of living beings and Īśvarās are named Kṣetra. They are constituted of the principles like Mahat and oṃers. The knower of these (bodies) is called Kṣetrajña.

## Chapter 25 - Vairāgya (non-attachment) and Bhakti (devotion)

## \|\| 9.25.1 \|\|

*śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*vairāgyasyātha te vacmi lakṣaṇaṃ munisattama \|*  
*kṣayiṣṇuvastuṣvaruciḥ sarvatheti tadīritam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:

1\. O excellent sage, I shall now describe to you the characteristics of Vairāgya. It is complete disinterest in all perishable objects.

## \|\| 9.25.2 \|\|

*ārabhya māyāpuruṣātsarvā hyākṛtayastu yāḥ \|*  
*kālaśaktyā bhagavato nāśyante tāśca tadvaśāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Whatever forms there are, right from Māyā-Puruṣa, all of them are destroyed by the destructive power (Kāla Śakti) of the Lord, as they are subject to his control.

## \|\| 9.25.3 \|\|

*pratyakṣeṇānumānena śābdena ca vivekibhiḥ \|*  
*asatyatā kṛtīnāṃ ca niścitā satyatātmanām \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The unreality of created objects and the reality of souls have been determined by knowledgeable persons through direct perception, inference and scriptural authority.

## \|\| 9.25.4 \|\|

*nityena pralayenaiṣa kālo naimittikena ca \|*  
*prākṛtikena rūpeṇa caratyātyantikena ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Kāla (Death, god of destruction) moves in the form of Nitya (daily), Naimittika (periodical), Prākṛtika (of Prakṛti, Primordial Nature) and Ātyantika (final or absolute) Pralayas (destruction).

## \|\| 9.25.5 \|\|

*dehidehā ime nityaṃ kṣīyante pariṇāminaḥ \|*  
*krameṇa dṛśyate yatra bālyatāruṇyavārddhakam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. These bodies of souls which are subject to change and in which the stages of childhood, youth and old age are seen in that order, always go on decaying.

## \|\| 9.25.6 \|\|

*sūkṣmatvānnekṣyate tattu gatirdīpārciṣo yathā \|*  
*phalavṛddhirvā'nupadaṃ jāyamānā drume yathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The process of decay is not noticed as that of the flame of a lamp, or the growth and development of a fruit at every step on the tree, is not seen.

## \|\| 9.25.7 \|\|

*tasyāṃtasyāmavasthāyāṃ duḥkhaṃ ca mahadīkṣyate \|*  
*jāgradādiṣvavasthāsu duḥkhaṃ caiva punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. In its final stage, great grief is observed. In the stages of wakefulness and others (such as dream, sleep), there is frequent recurrence of grief.

## \|\| 9.25.8 \|\|

*duḥkhamādhyātmikaṃ bhūri dṛśyate cādhibhautikam \|*  
*ādhidaivikamapyatra duḥkhamevāsti dehinām \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Embodied beings suffer terrible misery and pain proceeding from bodily and mental causes and from elements (and oṃer beings) and caused by divine, planetary and supernatural factors.

## \|\| 9.25.9 \|\|

*hāhā mamāra matputro hā patnī mriyate mama \|*  
*tātaṃ me'bhakṣayadvyāghro daṣṭā sarpeṇa me vadhūḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. As a result of it, people lament like: “Alas! My son died; my wife is dying; a tiger ate up my father; my daughter-in-law was bitten by a snake.

## \|\| 9.25.10-14 \|\|

*mahāsaudhogninā dagdho hāhā sopaskaro'dya me \|*  
*svakuṭumbaṃ kathaṃ pokṣye nāvarṣatpākaśāsanaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*sasyaiḥ samṛddhaṃ matkṣetraṃ hāhā dagdhaṃ himāgninā \|*  
*hriyante taskarairgāvaḥ sarvasvaṃ mama luṇṭhitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*nṛpeṇa daṇḍito'tyarthaṃ śatruṇā hā'titāḍitaḥ \|*  
*kiṃ karomi ca kaṃ brūyāṃ mātā me vyabhicāriṇī \|\| 12 \|\|*

*viṣaṃ pāsyāmi hāhā'dya matpatnīṃ śatrurākṛṣat \|*  
*hā svasā me hṛtā mlecchairhāhā'riḥ prāpa marmabhit \|\| 13 \|\|*

*priye jvarātivyathayā yamadūtā ime hahā \|*  
*itthaṃ rorūyamāṇā hi dṛśyante sarvato janāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

10-14. Alas! all my belongings are burnt down in the great fire of my mansion. How can I maintain my family as God Indra did not shower rains? My farm was rich with crops, but Alas, it is blighted by the intensity of winter'. My cows are taken away by robbers! Everything in my possession (property) is plundered!

I am severely punished by the king! I am severely beaten by my enemy! What should I do? Whom can I tell that my mother was adulterous?

Alas, the enemy abducted my wife today! I shall drink poison. Alas, my sister is carried away (forcibly) by Mlecchas! Alas, my enemy, the penetrator of my weak points and secrets, has arrived!

I am dying of the excruciating pain of fever. Alas, these are the messengers of Yama, the god of Death!”

Everywhere people are seen lamenting like this.

## \|\| 9.25.15 \|\|

*avasthānāṃ śarīrasya janmamṛtyū pratikṣaṇam \|*  
*kālena prāpnuvadbhiḥ svaṃ prārabdhaṃ duḥkhamaśyate \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Every moment undergoing birth and death of their bodily states, in the course of time men suffer from pain originating from themselves (i.e. as a result of their own Karmas).

## \|\| 9.25.16 \|\|

*prārabdhānte mṛtyuduḥkhaṃ bhavatyapratimaṃ hi tat \|*  
*mṛtvāpi ca mahadduḥkhaṃ prāpyate yamayātanāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The pain of death at the end of the pre-destined period (of sufferings and life) is unparalleled. Even after death, extreme suffering—torture inflicted by the god of Death—is undergone.

## \|\| 9.25.17 \|\|

*tato jarāyujodbhijjasvedajāṇḍajayoniṣu \|*  
*bhūtvābhūtvā yathākarma mriyate duḥkhitaiḥ punaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Getting birth again and again in the species of beings such as viviparous, germinating ones (plants etc.), sweat-bom, egg-bom, according to one’s Karmas one dies with pain.

## \|\| 9.25.18 \|\|

*nityaḥ pralaya evaṃ te kīrttitaḥ sūkṣmayā dṛśā \|*  
*sa jñeyo'tha mune vacmi layaṃ naimittikābhidham \|\| 18 \|\|*

18a. Thus far the Nitya Pralaya (daily destruction) has been described to you with minute observation. You should understand it.

18b. Now, O sage, I shall describe to you the Pralaya called Naimittika (periodic).

## \|\| 9.25.19 \|\|

*nimittīkṛtya rajanīṃ bhavedviśvasṛjastu yaḥ \|*  
*naimittikaḥ sa kathito layo dainaṃdinaśca saḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The Destruction that is occasioned by the Night of the Creator of the universe (Brahmā) is called the Naimittika (periodic) Dissolution or Destruction. It occurs on everyday (of God Brahmā).

## \|\| 9.25.20 \|\|

*caturyugānāṃ sāhasraṃ dinaṃ viśvasṛjo mune \|*  
*niśā ca tāvatī tasya taddvayaṃ kalpa ucyate \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O sage, the day of the Creator of the universe consits of one thousand Caturyugas (groups of four Yugas). His night is also of that duration. Boṃ together (the day and night of Brahmā) are called Kalpa.

## \|\| 9.25.21 \|\|

*ekaikasmindine tasya caturdaśa caturdaśa \|*  
*bhavanti manavo brahmandharmasetvabhirakṣakāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. In each day of God Brahmā, there are fourteen Manus, the protectors of bounds of Dharma, O Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 9.25.22-24 \|\|

*ādyaḥ svāyambhuvastatra manuḥ svārociṣastataḥ \|*  
*uttamastāmasaścā'tha raivataścākṣuṣastataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*śrāddhadevaśca sāvarṇi bhautyo raucyastataḥ param \|*  
*brahmasāvarṇināmā ca rudrasāvarṇireva ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

*merusāvarṇisaṃjño'tha dakṣasāvarṇirantimaḥ \|*  
*caturdaśaite manavaḥ proktā brahmaikavāsare \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. The first Manu is Svāyambhuva, then (the next Manu is) Svārociṣa. Next to him (consecutively) are Uttama, Tāmasa, then Raivata and Cākṣuṣa, Śrāddhadeva (i.e. Vaivasvata), Sāvarṇi, Bhautya, Raucya, then (Manu) called Brahma-Sāvarṇi, Rudra-Sāvarṇi, then (Manu) named Meru-Sāvarṇi and the last is Dakṣa-Sāvarṇi.

## \|\| 9.25.25 \|\|

*iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye vairāgyabhaktinirūpaṇaṃ nāma pañcaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The period of each Manu is seventy-one Yugas. Twelve thousand years of Devas make one Yuga (= Mahāyuga).

## \|\| 9.25.26 \|\|

*caturdaśasyaiva manorantarentamupeyuṣi \|*  
*sāyaṃsaṃdhyā viśvasṛjo jāyate munisattama \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. At the end of the fourteen Manvantaras, the evening of the Creator of the universe sets in, O excellent sage.

## \|\| 9.25.27 \|\|

*dināvasāne vairājaḥ śaktīrākarṣati sthiteḥ \|*  
*vairājātmā tadā rudrastrilokīṃ hartumīhate \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. At the end of the Day (of Brahmā), Vairāja withdraws the powers that sustain the world. Rudra whose soul is Vairāja, then desires to destroy the world.

## \|\| 9.25.28 \|\|

*ādau bhavatyanāvṛṣṭiratyugrā śatavārṣikī \|*  
*tadālpasārasattvāni kṣīyante sarvaśo bhuvi \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. At first there is a terrific drought lasting for a hundred years. Then all living beings of meagre strength on the earth perish entirely.

## \|\| 9.25.29-30 \|\|

*sāṃvarttakasya cārkasya raśmayo'tyulbaṇā rasam \|*  
*āpātālātpibantyāśu dharaṇyāṃ sarvameva hi \|\| 29 \|\|*

*sārasaṃ caiva nādeyaṃ sāmudraṃ cāmbu sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*śoṣayitvā'khilāṃllokānso'rko nayati saṃkṣayam \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. Intensely powerful rays of the Saṃvartaka Sun drink up all liquid from the nether world. Having dried up quickly all water of the lakes, rivers and seas on the earth, the Sun leads all peoples (or regions) to destruction.

## \|\| 9.25.31 \|\|

*tato bhavati niḥsnehā naṣṭasthāvarajaṅgamā \|*  
*kūrmapṛṣṭhopamā bhūmiḥ śuṣkā saṃkucitā bhṛśam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Then the earth, bereft of all moisture and with all movables and immovables destroyed, becomes bald like the back of a tortoise, extremely dry and shrivelled.

## \|\| 9.25.32 \|\|

*kālāgnirudraḥ śeṣasya mukhādutpadyate tataḥ \|*  
*adholokānsaptabhūmiṃ bhuvaḥ svaśca dahatyasau \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Then Rudra in the form of destructive fire emanates from the mouth of Śeṣa, and it burns down the seven nether worlds, the earth, Bhuvarloka and Svarloka (the heaven).

## \|\| 9.25.33 \|\|

*nirdagdhalokadaśako jvālāvarttabhayaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*udvāsitamaharlokaḥ kālāgniḥ parivarttate \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The Kālāgni (‘the fire of world destruction’) which has burnt down the worlds and is terrible with its spiral flames, returns after devastating Maharloka.

## \|\| 9.25.34 \|\|

*gatādhikārāstridaśā bhuvaḥsvarganivāsinaḥ \|*  
*maharlokājjanaṃ yānti vahnijvālābhṛśārditāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Devas dwelling in the Bhuvar- and Svar-loka (the heaven), who are deprived of their posts and powers, become extremely tormented by the flames of that fire and proceed from Maharloka to Janaloka.

## \|\| 9.25.35 \|\|

*nivṛttidharmā ṛṣayaḥ prāptāḥ siddhadaśāṃ tu ye \|*  
*bhūtalāttepi tarhyeva ṛṣilokaṃ prayānti ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Sages, the followers of the path of Nivṛtti (‘abstaining’ from ritualistic acts—Karma) who attained state of Sidḍhas, go for the same reason from the earth to the world of Sages (Ṛṣiloka).

## \|\| 9.25.36 \|\|

*uttiṣṭhanti tato ghorā vyomni sāṃvarttakā ghanāḥ \|*  
*mahāgajakulaprakhyāstaḍitvanto'tinādinaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Then terrific clouds for destroying the world (called Saṃvartaka clouds) rise up in the sky. They look like a crowd of elephants. They are possessed of lightning, and thunder violently.

## \|\| 9.25.37 \|\|

*dhūmravarṇāḥ pītavarṇā kecitkumudasannibhāḥ \|*  
*lākṣārasanibhāḥ keciccāṣapatranibhāstathā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Some are smoke-coloured; some yellow-coloured. Some are white like night-lotus. Some are red like liquid lac; some like the wing of a blue jay.

## \|\| 9.25.38 \|\|

*śamayitvā mahāvahniṃ śataṃ varṣāṇyaharnniśam \|*  
*varṣamāṇāḥ sthūladhārāḥ stanantaste ghanā ghanāḥ \|*  
*brahmāṇḍasyāntarālaṃ ca pūrayanti dhruvāvadhi \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Extinguishing the great fire they shower with heavy torrents for a hundred years incessantly, day and night. Those thundering thick clouds fill up the interior of the Brahmāṇḍa up to the Polar Star.

## \|\| 9.25.39 \|\|

*ekārṇavajale tasminvairājapuruṣaḥ sa tu \|*  
*aniruddhātmakaḥ śete nāgendraśayane prabhuḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. In that vast sheet of water of that general inundation, on a bed of the (body of the) great Serpent, Lord Vairāja Puruṣa called Aniruddha lies (sleeps).

## \|\| 9.25.40-42 \|\|

*tadā devāśca ṛṣayo rajaḥsattvatamovaśāḥ \|*  
*ye te saha viriñcena svakīyaguṇakarṣitāḥ \|*  
*praviśya tasya jaṭhare śerate dīrghanidrayā \|\| 40 \|\|*

*ye tu brahmātmaikyabhāvā vaśīkṛtaguṇatrayāḥ \|*  
*nivṛttenaiva dharmeṇa vāsudevamupāsate \|\| 41 \|\|*

*maharādiṣu lokeṣu te caturṣu kṛtālayāḥ \|*  
*taṃ vairājaṃ saṃstuvanto nivasanti yathāsukham \|\| 42 \|\|*

40-42. Those who have realized the identity of Brahman and Self, and have brought under control the three Guṇas and propitiate Vāsudeva by Nivṛtti Dharma, make their residence in the four worlds of Mahar etc. and stay there as they please, praising Vairāja.

## \|\| 9.25.43 \|\|

*nārāyaṇaḥ sa bhagavānsvarūpaṃ paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*cintayanvāsudevākhyaṃ śete vai yoganidrayā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Lord Nārāyaṇa, meditating on the form of the Supreme Soul called Vāsudeva. lies absorbed in Yogic sleep.

## \|\| 9.25.44 \|\|

*niśānte brahmaṇā sākaṃ sarve te tasya jāṭharāḥ \|*  
*utpadyante yathāpūrvaṃ yathākarmādhikāriṇaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. At the end of (Brahmā’s) night, all those beings residing in his belly (during the Pralaya period) along with Brahmā are produced again as before, authorized for the same Karma as before.

## \|\| 9.25.45 \|\|

*evaṃ naimittiko nāma trilokīkṣayalakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*pralayaḥ kathitastubhyaṃ prākṛtaṃ kīrttayāmyatha \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. In this way, the Pralaya called Naimittika (‘periodic’) characterised by the destruction of the three worlds has been narrated to you. Now I shall describe the Prākṛta Pralaya (Destruction of Prakṛti or Primordial Nature).

## \|\| 9.25.46 \|\|

*ya eṣa kalpaḥ kathitastādṛśānāṃ śatatrayam \|*  
*ṣaṣṭyādhikaṃ ca yaḥ kālo vedhasaḥ sa tu vatsaraḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. What has been described (up till now) is a Kalpa. Three hundred and sixty periods of that duration constitute the year of God Brahmā.

## \|\| 9.25.47 \|\|

*pañcāśatā taiḥ parārddho brahmāyustaddvayaṃ matam \|*  
*parākhyakāle saṃpūrṇe mahānbhavati saṃkṣayaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Fifty of them (Brahmā’s year) constitute a Parārdha; two such Parārdhas constitute the life-span of Brahmā. When the period of time called Para (Brahmā’s complete span of life) is completed, there takes place a great annihilation.

## \|\| 9.25.48 \|\|

*saṃhārarudrarūpeṇa saṃhṛtya svaṃ virāḍvapuḥ \|*  
*svaparaṃ nirguṇaṃ rūpaṃ vairājo yātumicchati \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. After withdrawing his form called Virāj by the Rudra form of destruction, Vairāja desires to go (i.e. revert) to his supreme attributeless form.

## \|\| 9.25.49 \|\|

*tadā bhavatyanāvṛṣṭiḥ pūrvavacchatavārṣikī \|*  
*sāṅkarṣaṇaśca kālāgnirdahatyaṇḍamaśeṣataḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. At that time, there is a drought (a rain-less period) of a hundred years as before (at the time of Nitya Pralaya). The fire of destruction born of Saṅkarṣaṇa (Śeṣa) completely bums down Brahmāṇḍa (ṃe universe).

## \|\| 9.25.50 \|\|

*sāṃvarttakāstato meghā varṣantyati bhayānakāḥ \|*  
*śataṃ varṣāṇi dhārābhirmusalākṛtibhirmune \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Then the extremely terrible clouds called Saṃvartaka pour down torrents of water, (each) as big as a pestle, for a hundred years, O sage.

## \|\| 9.25.51 \|\|

*mahadādervikārasya viśeṣāntasya saṃkṣayaḥ \|*  
*sarvasyāpi bhavatyeva vāsudevecchayā tataḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Then by the will of Vāsudeva, there is a complete destruction of all the evolutes of Prakṛti beginning with Mahat and ending with Viśeṣas (i.e. peculiar attributes distinguishing Dravyas).

## \|\| 9.25.52 \|\|

*āpo grasanti vai pūrvaṃ bhūmergandhātmakaṃ guṇam \|*  
*āttagandhā tato bhūmiḥ pralayatvāya kalpate \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The (elemental) Water at first ‘swallows’ up smell (Gandha) which is a special quality of the (element) Earth. The Earth devoid of (its special quality) smell, becomes dissolved.

## \|\| 9.25.53 \|\|

*grasatembuguṇaṃ tejo rasaṃ tallīyate tataḥ \|*  
*rūpaṃ tejoguṇaṃ vāyurgrasate līyate'tha tat \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The (elemental) Fire swallows Rasa (liquid form), a special quality of Water, which thereby merges therein. The (elemental) Wind ‘devours’ Rūpa (colour), the special quality of Fire (Tejas) and it (the elemental Fire) merges therein.

## \|\| 9.25.54 \|\|

*vāyorapi guṇaṃ sparśamākāśo grasate tataḥ \|*  
*praśāmyati tadā vāyuḥ khaṃ tu tiṣṭhatyanāvṛtam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The (elemental) Ākaśa (Ether) then swallows up touch which is a special quality of Wind. Wind then calms down (and ceases to exist). Ether stands uncovered.

## \|\| 9.25.55 \|\|

*bhūtādistadguṇaṃ śabdaṃ grasate līyate ca kham \|*  
*indriyāṇi vilīyante taijasāhaṃkṛtau tataḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Bhūtādi (the origin of Bhūtas) swallows sound, the distinguishing quality of Ether and Ether merges therein.

The Indriyas (i.e. organs of sense and action) become merged in the Taijasa Ahaṃkāra.

## \|\| 9.25.56 \|\|

*ahaṅkāre vilīyante sāttvike devatā manaḥ \|*  
*yadyadyasmātsamutpannaṃ tattattasminhi līyate \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. In the Sāttvika type of Ahaṃkāra, the deities and manas get merged. That which is produced or evolved from a thing gets merged in that, i.e. its source of origin.

## \|\| 9.25.57 \|\|

*ahaṃkāro mahattattve trividhopi pralīyate \|*  
*tatpradhāne ca tatpuṃsi sa mūlaprakṛtau tataḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The three types of Ahaṃkāra (produced from the three Guṇas

i.e. Sattva, Rajas and Tamas) are dissolved in the principle called Mahat. That becomes merged in Pradhāna which in turn is dissolved in Puruṣa. It is then dissolved in the Mūla Prakṛti (Primordial Prakṛti).

## \|\| 9.25.58 \|\|

*eṣa prākṛtiko nāma pralayaḥ parigīyate \|*  
*tirobhavanti jīveśā yatrā'vyakte harīcchayā \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. This Pralaya called Prākṛtika is (thus) described. In this, by the will of Hari, the masters of living beings become concealed in Avyakta (i.e. the unmanifest primordial principle from which all the phenomena of the material world are developed).

## \|\| 9.25.59 \|\|

*yadā ca māyā puruṣau kālo'tyakṣaratejasi \|*  
*tadicchayā tiro yānti sa tveko vartate prabhuḥ \|*  
*tadā sa pralayo jñeyo nāradātyantikābhidhaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. When Māyā, Puruṣa and Kāla get merged in the imperishable refulgence by the Lord’s will, then the Lord alone exists (without a second). That Pralaya is called Ātyantika (Final or Absolute), O Nārada.

## \|\| 9.25.60 \|\|

*itthaṃ prabhoḥ kālaśaktyā layairetaiścaturvidhaiḥ \|*  
*asadbaddhvā'khilaṃ tatrā'rucirvairāgyamucyate \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. All this is rendered like Asat (non-being) by the four kinds of dissolutions by the power called Kāla (Time) of the Lord. Non-attachment or dislike of it is called Vairāgya.

## \|\| 9.25.61 \|\|

*vāsudevetarāndevānkālamāyāvaśīkṛtān \|*  
*viditvā teṣu ca prītiṃ hitvā tasyaiva nityadā \|*  
*gāḍhasnehena yā sevā sā bhaktiriti gīyate \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Knowing that all gods other than Vāsudeva are subject to Kāla (Destruction) and Māyā, and giving up liking (devotion) for them, continuous service with deep affection to him exclusively, is known as Bhakti (devotion).

## \|\| 9.25.62-63 \|\|

*śravaṇaṃ kīrtanaṃ tasya smṛtiścaraṇasevanam \|*  
*pūjā praṇāmo dāsyaṃ ca sakhyaṃ cātmanivedanam \|\| 62 \|\|*

*ityetairnnavabhirbhāvairyaḥ seveta tamādarāt \|*  
*ananyayā dhiṣaṇayā sa hi bhakta itīryate \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. He who serves him respectfully with his mind exclusively devoted to him, with the nine Bhāvas (‘types of devotions’), viz. listening (to the stories etc. of the Lord), glorifying (the Lord), remembering (him), bowing to the Lord’s fed, worshipping (him), paying obeisance (to him), servitude, (establishing) friendship with him and (complete) self-surrender, is called a Bkakta (a devotee).

## \|\| 9.25.64 \|\|

*tribhiḥ svadharmapramukhairyuktābhaktiriyaṃ mune \|*  
*dharma ekāntika iti prokto bhāgavataśca saḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The Devotion that is accompanied with three chief duties (dharma) of oneself is called Ekāntika Dharma. It is the Bhāgavata Dharma.

## \|\| 9.25.65 \|\|

*sākṣādbhagavataḥ saṅgāttadbhaktānāṃ ca vedṛśām \|*  
*dharmo hyekāntikaḥ pumbhiḥ prāpyate nānyathā kvacit \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. This Ekāntika Dharma is known by men by direct contact with the Lord or with his devotees of this (above described) nature, but never otherwise.

## \|\| 9.25.66 \|\|

*naitādṛśaṃ paraṃ kiñcitsādhanaṃ hi mumukṣatām \|*  
*niḥśreyasakaraṃ puṃsāṃ sarvābhadravināśanam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. To men who are desirous of Mokṣa, there is no other means like this, which brings the final beatitude to men, and is destructive of all inauspicious and evil things.

## \|\| 9.25.67 \|\|

*ekāntadharmasiddhyarthaṃ kriyāyogaparo bhavet \|*  
*pumānsyādyena naiṣkarmyaṃ karmaṇāṃ munisattama \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. For the accomplishment of Ekānta-dharma, he should devote himself to Kriyā Yoga. Thereby a man attains to the stage wherein one is exempted from the consequences of the Karmas, O excellent sage.

## \|\| 9.25.68 \|\|

*etanmayā vedapurāṇaguhyaṃ tattvaṃ paraṃ proktamaghaughanāśam \|*  
*ekāgrayā śuddhadhiyāvadhārya sacchraddhayā cetasi te maharṣe \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. This great doctrine (Tattva) kept as secret in Vedas and Purāṇas, which destroys the flood of sins, has been described by me. It should be attended to with concentration of mind, with pure intellect, and with ardent faith, O great sage.

## \|\| 9.25.69 \|\|

*na vāsudevātparamasti pāvanaṃ na vāsudevātparamasti maṅgalam \|*  
*na vāsudevātparamasti daivataṃ na vāsudevātparamasti vāñchitam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. There is nothing more sanctifying than Vāsudeva. Nothing is more auspicious than Vāsudeva. No deity is greater than Vāsudeva. There is nothing that is desired other than Vāsudeva.

## Chapter 26 - Eligibility for Kriyā-Yoga etc.

## \|\| 9.26.1 \|\|

*skanda uvāca \|*  
*ekāntadharmavivṛtiṃ śrutvā bhagavatoditām \|*  
*prahṛṣṭamānaso bhūyastaṃ papraccha sa nāradaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Skanda said:

1\. Having heard the exposition of the Ekānta Dharma as done by the Lord (Nārāyaṇa), Nārada, who was greatly delighted in mind, asked him again.

## \|\| 9.26.2 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*dharma ekāntikaḥ svāmiṃstvayā samyagudīritaḥ \|*  
*tamāśrutya mahānharṣo jātosti mama mānase \|\| 2 \|\|*

Nārada said:

2\. O Master, having heard the Ekāntika Dharma as has been excellently expounded by you, a great joy has been engendered in my mind.

## \|\| 9.26.3 \|\|

*siddhaye tasya bhavatā kriyāyogo ya ucyate \|*  
*tamahaṃ boddhumicchāmi bhagavaṃstava saṃmatam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. I wish to know the Kriyā-Yoga (‘the employment of means’) as approved by you, which is said to contribute to its accomplishment.

## \|\| 9.26.4 \|\|

*śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*pūjāvidhiḥ kriyāyogo vāsudevasya kīrttyate \|*  
*sa tu vedeṣu tantreṣu bahudhaivāsti varṇitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:

4\. Performance of worship as per injunctions is declared as the Kriyā-Yoga of Vāsudeva. It is described in different ways in the Vedas and the Tantras.

## \|\| 9.26.5 \|\|

*bhaktānāṃ rucivaicitryāttathā bahuvidhatvataḥ \|*  
*vāsudevasya mūrtīnāṃ bahudhā so'sti vistṛtaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Due to differences in tastes or desires of devotees and to diversity in the forms (i.e. icons) of Vāsudeva, it (i.e. Kriyā-Yoga) is vast and varied.

## \|\| 9.26.6 \|\|

*sākalyenocyamānasya pāro nāyāti tasya vai \|*  
*ataḥ saṃkṣepatastubhyaṃ vacmi bhaktivivarddhanam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Verily, there will be no end to it, if it were to be described in its entirety. Hence, I shall narrate to you briefly (ṃe Kriyā-Yoga) which enhances devotion.

## \|\| 9.26.7 \|\|

*prāptā ye vaiṣṇavīṃ dīkṣāṃ varṇāścatvāra āśramāḥ \|*  
*cāturvarṇyastriyaścaite proktā atrādhikāriṇaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Here (for this Kriyā-Yoga) those who have received initiation in Vaiṣṇava faith, whether men or women of the four castes or of the four stages of life (āśramas)—all are eligible.

## \|\| 9.26.8 \|\|

*vedatantrapurāṇoktairmantrairmūlena ca dvijāḥ \|*
